english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight to make food, which directly helps the tubers under the soil grow much larger.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Leaving too many shoots creates competition for water and soil nutrients, which results in smaller plantain bunches; keeping only two or three strong shoots yields bigger harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii ni jɛɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha yibii babaoo aba.

english: Extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer can stress the tomato plant, causing it to shed its flowers to save energy instead of setting fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ shwane mli Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa Aloo, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I water my pepper plants in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ nu shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering under intense sun causes fast evaporation, can heat up the soil and shock the roots, and leaves water droplets on leaves that act like small lenses, burning the plant.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ haa hulutsoo baa oya. Ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ akpokpo. ni eshiɔ nu ŋmɔtɔi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai bibii, ni baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally fix nitrogen from the air into the soil, restoring fertility for the next crop without needing to buy extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when the dry season sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because full direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out their soil. Planting plantain trees alongside cocoa provides natural shade umbrellas and keeps the soil cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo duɔ lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. When nitrogen is short, the corn plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ, Abele tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Fertilizers need moisture in the soil to break down so plant roots can absorb them. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can scorch plant roots without feeding the crop.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni egbɛ eshwa bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi lɛ ashã ni ahaaa tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I need to plant cassava stem cuttings at a slant instead of burying them flat under the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni aaafu amɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Slanted stem cuttings ensure the growth nodes face upward so branches grow quickly into sunlight, while allowing roots to spread easily into the soil to form thick tubers.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni niji lɛ ada oya yɛ hulu la mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines up onto tall wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking raises yam leaves off the wet ground into full sunlight, which prevents leaf decay and helps the leaves capture more sunlight to build bigger underground tubers.
ga: Staking baajie sweet potato baai lɛ kpo kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyashi amɛbaaná hulutsoo be fɛɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Extra suckers compete with the mother plant for food, water, and sunlight. Pruning weak suckers leaves more energy for the main stem to yield larger plantain bunches.
ga: Tso yibii krokomɛi kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ jwɛi wulu ko.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my growing tomatoes turning black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni midu lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani amɛshwereɔ po lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit. It often happens when soil moisture fluctuates heavily between rainy days and dry spells.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni shɛɛɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ gbii kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling tightly upwards and turning crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking plant juices and spreading viruses, which distorts leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ

english: Why do the center funnel leaves of my young corn plants look like they have holes eaten into them with fine dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ teŋgbɛ cone baa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ bu ko ni aye yɛ mli ni muji yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar hiding inside the growing center of the maize. The dirt is waste material left behind as the worm eats tender new leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Muji ji jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ beni ŋmeii yeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting groundnuts before maize makes the soil richer for the corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei dani adu ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmei kpakpa?

english: Groundnut plants are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in root nodules. When groundnut roots decompose, they leave free natural fertilizer in the soil for the next maize crop.
ga: Peanut tsei ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the center of my young maize plants and leaving holes in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ ni amɛshiɔ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the center whorl of maize. Catching them early and spraying neem leaf extract or approved insecticides prevents them from destroying the growing shoot and killing the plant.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ni amɛkafite tsei.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting stem cuttings from disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by local agricultural offices stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nibii ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ kɛhaa lɛ mli. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting up and shrinking into tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf twisting in pepper is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips. Spraying the undersides of leaves early with organic neem oil or soap solution protects the leaves so the plant can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ organic neem fɔ loo samla ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baashwie baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ebaabu baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They need shade trees or plantains planted next to them to act as natural sunshades until their stems become strong and mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade kɛyashi tso lɛ shishi lɛ baawa ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam plants need their leaves high up in full sunlight so they can make food to build large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the hot soil, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ hia baai kakadaji kɛ hulu ni eyi obɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛfee niyenii ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baa lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ koni akafoliar helai aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the root base encourages the flowers to stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Plantain roots are often eaten from the inside by microscopic worms called nematodes or banana weevil grubs. Dipping new suckers in hot water before planting kills these pests so roots grow deep and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana weevil lɛ yeɔ plantain shishifãi kɛjɛɔ emli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei heei wo nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani odu lɛ, ebaagbe nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. Shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize farm turning yellow while the top leaves stay light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves show that your soil is low in nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to make food. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure gives the crop the energy to turn dark green again.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkɛfee niyenii Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ.

english: How can I stop the ground around my vegetables from drying out quickly during the harmattan dry season?
ga: Mibaafee he ni ebɔle he lɛ Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-aduawai lɛ gĩii oya yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the bare soil with dry grass, leaves, or rice husks—a practice called mulching—locks water in the soil, blocks weed growth, and keeps roots cool during hot days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmãa ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ, nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why does my lowland rice crop grow poorly when the standing water in the field dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Lowland rice thrives when its roots remain flooded because the water carries nutrients to the plant and stifles weeds. Building earth walls around your field holds rainfall so roots stay submerged.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli lolo ejaakɛ nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa tso lɛ mli ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ naa. Shikpɔŋ gbogbo ni oootswa obɔle Oŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni abua nugbɔ nu naa. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ boteɔ nu shishi.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers alongside my newly planted young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under harsh, direct sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as a living umbrella, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines naturally need to climb to catch maximum sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground to prevent fungal rotting and allows the leaves to trap enough sunlight to grow big underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni fungal rot akafite. ni ehaa baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the key food it needs for healthy leaf growth. Heavy rains can also wash away this food or make the ground too soggy for roots to feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara waa Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Planting it continuously on the same spot wears out the soil's nutrients and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaafite niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to chew holes through the leaf funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the hatched worms hide deep inside the plant's central leaves to feed, which can ruin the crop if not treated early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ni woɔ wui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye nii. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and dry up during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and shady conditions. Rain drops splash the fungal spores from the soil onto lower pods, making them rot.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, fɔ́, shade shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. ha egbo

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves. As they suck the sap or spread viruses, the leaves become weak, deformed, and wrinkled.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ amɛnu nu mli nu loo amɛgbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã lɛ Baai lɛ baagbɔjɔɔ, amɛhe ejɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: High heat, dry winds, or over-watering can stress the tomato plant and make its flowers drop. If flowers drop before insects or wind can pollinate them, no fruit will form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ ni eha amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi. Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi dani kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ afee amɛ pollin lɛ, Yibii ko bɛ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts cracking open as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller every year on the same plant stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi yɛ tso kome nɔ lɛ?

english: When too many young shoots grow around the main plantain stem, they all fight for the same water and soil food. Pruning away extra shoots so that only two or three grow together will keep the bunches big.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ dara kɛbɔle tso wulu lɛ he tsɔ lɛ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ niyenii hu. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ pɛ koni ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ afee ekome kɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, no pɛ baaha ŋmeii agbo aba.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up during the sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh direct sunlight. Providing shade using temporary crops like plantains protects them from heat stress and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii kɛhaa hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas between my maize crop help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, which acts as natural food to help your maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmei lɛ ni edara waa ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why am I finding small holes in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ

english: Holes in young leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which feed on the growing heart of the plant and require early pest control to prevent crop loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni baa tso lɛ baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Ni esa akɛ atsu tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nii mra. Koni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce food for the tubers underground, while keeping the leaves off the damp ground prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni baa lɛ he helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil needed to support the growth of the fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai adalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my crop if I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin stems and a poor yield.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive; when heavy rain leaves the ground waterlogged for too long, it suffocates the roots and promotes fungus that causes rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ hela ni fiteɔ baa lɛ aba.

english: Why should I spread dry leaves and grass around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi mabɔle he lɛ? miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishitoo

english: Covering the soil around plants (mulching) prevents water from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps the roots cool, and reduces the growth of unwanted weeds.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ ha (mulching) lɛ, ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ hulu la lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: Why does cutting off small extra branches from my tomato plant make the remaining fruit grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Mɛni eshwɛ yɛ mi tomato tso lɛ mli ni haa aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ daraa?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary stems so the plant doesn't waste energy, allowing all available nutrients to go directly into producing larger and healthier fruit.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ. koni tsei lɛ akafite hewalɛ Enɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do weeds growing near my crops reduce the size of my final harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aha minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your main crops need to develop properly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei titrii lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is exhausted and cannot support crops anymore?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dɔŋŋ?

english: Exhausted soil usually turns hard, loses its rich dark color, and causes crops to grow slowly with pale, yellowing leaves even when there is enough water. When soil loses its organic matter and nutrients from overfarming, crops cannot get the food they need to thrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ. loses dark color Ni enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛnáa baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po yɛ jɛmɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ okwaayeli ni fe nine mli baa lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdu.

english: What can I do to bring my tired farm land back to life so I can get good yields again?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mikɛ miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ koni manyɛ maná sɛɛnamɔi kpakpai ekoŋŋ?

english: You can revive tired land by applying animal manure or compost, leaving crop remains on the field after harvest instead of burning them, and letting the land rest or planting cover crops like cowpea or groundnuts that naturally feed nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ aha hei ni etɔ lɛ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo edu ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: The weather in Ghana is getting hotter and rains are unpredictable this year, so how do I know when it is safe to plant my crop seeds?
ga: Ghana kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli miidɔ waa ni nugbɔ baanɛ afi nɛɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. No hewɔ lɛ te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ adu dumɔwui?

english: Instead of planting right after the very first rain, wait until the soil has soaked thoroughly from two or three consistent rains over a couple of weeks, ensuring the ground stays moist enough for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli lɛ sɛɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Which food crops can I plant that will still produce a harvest even if the rains fail or drought comes?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu ni mawo yibii lolo kɛji nugbɔ loo hɔmɔ bako po?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and sweet potatoes have deep roots or naturally low water requirements, making them tough enough to handle dry weather and poor rainfall far better than crops like maize.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo nu ni he hiaa lɛ faaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant are usually a clear sign that the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for green growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted chicken manure solves this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo tsina ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small harvests when I plant many seeds close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper spacing allows them to grow thick, strong, and produce larger yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehe awa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How does adding fertilizer actually help my crops produce a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for plants, supplying necessary nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that natural soil may be missing, allowing the plant to build strong roots, healthy leaves, and abundant fruits.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei aniyenii. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam. ni ekolɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ bɛ mli lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa, baai ni wa, kɛ aduawai babaoo.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, a destructive pest common in Ghana. You can control them by spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf water mixtures into the plant funnel early in the morning or late in the evening when the worms are active.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii babaoo yɛ Ghana. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ ni oookɛshwie tsei akui amli leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground. Rotating different crops, like switching between maize and legumes, keeps the soil healthy and pest numbers low.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ tsakemɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fioo pɛ yɔɔ nɔ.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant fail to come up out of the soil at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are damaged by insects, planted too deep in the soil, planted in dry ground without moisture, or buried in overly wet, waterlogged soil that rots them before they can grow.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji kooloi fite amɛ. adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Aloo fu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaagbo dani ebaanyɛ eda.

english: Wait for the first heavy rain that thoroughly soaks the soil about wrist-deep, rather than planting after a short shower. Planting too early in dry soil causes seeds to burn, while planting after proper rainfall ensures fast and healthy germination.
ga: Mɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baaha sũ lɛ ashɛ oniji ahe lɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo du ngɛ nu nɛ o pue be kuku ko se. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ashã. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni sa ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to protect themselves from intense heat. By rolling up, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, helping it hold onto water and survive dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛji okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ Tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: My family has always saved seeds from the last harvest to plant, so why should I buy improved seed varieties now?
ga: Miweku lɛ toɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ be fɛɛ be koni amɛdu. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ bianɛ?

english: Saved seeds gradually lose their strength over time and become easily damaged by pests and droughts. Improved seeds are specially developed to resist local crop diseases, grow faster with less rainfall, and produce much bigger yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baafite fiofio Hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hɔmɔ baafite amɛ oya Afee dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsei ahe helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Edaa oya kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo. ni ekɛ nibii babaoo ni anáa lɛ aha

english: My parents never used chemical fertilizers on cassava, so why is my cassava soil no longer producing big tubers on its own?
ga: Mifɔlɔi kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ tsuuu nii kɔkɔɔkɔ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ wooo bulbs wuji dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Continuous farming on the same plot of land removes natural nutrients from the soil over many years. While the soil was rich in your ancestors' time, modern soil often needs fertilizer to replace missing nutrients like potassium and nitrogen so cassava roots can grow large.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ afii babaoo mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ wɔblematsɛmɛi lɛ abeaŋ moŋ Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ shikpɔji lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni elaaje, tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen. Koni eha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ adara

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when I leave them under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight, which scorches their leaves and prevents them from making food. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa creates a canopy that protects young cocoa plants while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he waa. Enɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaaa amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This is a common sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies that feed on the plant's sap. The disease stops the leaves from trapping sunlight properly, which weakens the plant and reduces tuber growth.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ akɛ nɔ ni kɛ hela lɛ baa lɛ Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ amɔmɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any fruit appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is erratic watering during the flowering stage. Extreme heat causes stress, so the plant drops flowers to save its remaining energy and water.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: What happens to my crop if I plant my yam mounds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Placing yam mounds too close together forces the vines to block sunlight from one another and makes the roots fight underground for water and soil nutrients, resulting in very small tubers at harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ to he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha wain tsei lɛ atsĩ hulu lɛ naa kɛjɛ amɛhe. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ, amɛfeɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my sweet potatoes are fully ready for harvest without digging up the whole land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Watch the vines and leaves; when they naturally begin to turn yellow and dry up toward the end of the growing season, it indicates that the tubers underground have fully matured and are ready to be dug up.
ga: Kwɛmɔ wain tsei lɛ kɛ baai lɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ naagbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa.

english: Why should I trim off extra branches from my pepper plants if I want to get more peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ mli kɛji miitao pepper babaoo?

english: Trimming away non-fruiting lower branches directs the plant's water, food, and energy toward forming strong flowers and developing larger, healthier pepper fruits instead of wasting energy on useless foliage.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni wooo yibii lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nu, niyenii, kɛ hewalɛ lɛ yaa nɔ ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. ni amɛfee pepper aduawai lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ Yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from intense, direct sunlight. Planting shade trees or intercropping with fast-growing plantains creates a protective canopy that keeps young cocoa plants cool and preserves moisture in the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ loo akɛ dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ ŋmɔɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at a slant instead of flat or completely upright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ loo amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava stem cuttings at a 45-degree angle balances root depth and stem stability, giving tubers enough room to expand sideways in the soil while keeping the main plant firmly anchored against strong winds.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ ni ji 45-degree yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ amli kwɔ kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Enɛ haa tuber lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya afã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha tso titri lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to expose maximum leaf area to sunlight. When lifted on stakes, leaves produce more energy through photosynthesis, leading to larger, healthier tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ aya hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ awó nɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛtsɔɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves in a V-pattern indicate nitrogen deficiency in maize. Nitrogen is an essential food for crops, responsible for leaf greenness and overall stalk growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ feɔ V, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛ ji mɛi ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli kɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for future plantings.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why does putting a layer of dry grass or leaves around my crop roots help during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering soil with organic material, known as mulching, prevents soil moisture from evaporating rapidly under the sun, suppresses weed growth, and keeps plant roots cool.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why are small, window-like holes appearing in the young leaves inside my maize plants' center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Tamɔ samflɛ ko ni jeɔ kpo yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: This leaf damage is a classic sign of Fall Armyworm infestation. The caterpillars crawl into the central whorl of young corn plants to feed on soft new growth during cooler parts of the day.
ga: Nɛkɛ baa ni efite nɛɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm hela lɛ eba. Kplukai lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli koni amɛye ŋmãa heei ni eda yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering, which prevents successful pollination and halts fruit development.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination naa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ shweremɔ kpaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and turning small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or aphids, or viral infections spread by these insects that disrupt leaf expansion.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni baa mɔ nɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni tsiɔ baai lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ naa

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale and rot when rain water sits on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to live. Standing water fills soil air pockets, suffocating the root system so plants cannot take up food, leading to root rot and pale, wilting foliage.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aye niyenii. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and protect its root tubers underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my plantain plants die after producing just one bundle of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ beni amɛwo yibii akuu kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is structured to produce fruit only once in its lifetime, but it naturally grows young shoots called suckers around its base to continue the crop for the future.
ga: Ato plantain tsei lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Shi bɔ ni eji lɛ, tsei bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe. cones kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii wɔsɛɛ

english: Why do my oil palm trees take several years to bear fruit while maize yields in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋma lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Perennial tree crops like oil palm spend their first few years building deep root systems and strong trunks to support heavy harvests for decades, whereas short-term crops like maize focus all their energy on quick seed production.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ mu tsei lɛ kɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ maa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa koni amɛkɛye amɛbua ŋmaakpamɔ wuji afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ dumɔwui ni amɛwoɔ oya lɛ he nii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: High temperatures damage the flower's pollen, preventing pollination and causing the plant to drop the unfertilized flowers to save its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen. Etsiɔ pollination naa ni ehaa tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni pollination bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need plantains or shade trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ adu plantains loo shade tsei yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily in harsh sunlight, so shade plants act as living umbrellas, keeping the young trees cool and moist until they mature.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing new fruits after the first few harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ yibii heei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔi fioo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants exhaust the nutrients in the soil after bearing fruit; without fresh compost, fertilizer, or light pruning, the plant becomes weak and stops forming new blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo yibii sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni afoɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ekpa fɔfɔi heei feemɔ.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too tightly, the plants compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving little energy to develop large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ babaoo tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ aná koni akɛfee cob dumɔwui wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my young crops so heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha midumɔwui lɛ adalɛ miiba shi waa lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal essential water, light, and fertilizer from the soil before your young crops have a chance to feed.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani otsei bibii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛyeɔ nii.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting as a natural food source for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow deep into mounded soil instead of near the surface?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miiya shɔŋŋ kɛmiiya gɔŋji amli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaabɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally expand downward into loose, soft soil to seek moisture and store nutrients safely away from heat and surface pests.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ena ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ato he ko ni he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them directly under full sunlight without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and burn easily under strong heat. Shade plants like plantain or forest trees act like umbrellas, keeping the air humid and the soil cool until the cocoa plant's roots grow deep enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli baawo wu bɔ ni sa ni hulu la lɛ baashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: The very first rain is often a false start followed by a hot, dry period. If you plant right away, the seeds will sprout but then dry up and die before the actual rainy season begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ jɛɔ amale shishijee mli baa. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji be ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aba.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant steals food from its old bottom leaves and sends it to the top so new growth can survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye nitrogen. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛyaa ŋwɛi koni shweremɔ hee lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn weak and short even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ kuku kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants in your farm. They aggressively pull soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops, leaving your plants starved of the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ kɛ hiɛdɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa bo koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ otsei lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the tubers underneath are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibioo nɛkɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or foliage growth energy, the cassava plant puts all its strength into growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of storing food in the roots to make thick tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo hewalɛ babaoo tsɔ kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔlii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee tso ɔmɛ a mi mi wa.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper and tomato plants falling off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper fɔfɔii kɛ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Vegetable plants drop their flowers when they feel heat stress or don't get enough water. To protect itself from dying, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than spending food on making fruits.
ga: Aduawai baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnáaa lɛ hao amɛ. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ gbele he Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baatsu nii kɛfee aduawai.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing around the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, share food and water with the main mother stem. By cutting away the extra shoots and leaving just one strong replacement, all the food goes into making a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ jaa niyenii kɛ nu kɛ nyɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ. Afoɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ashiɔ tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ. Niyenii fɛɛ bafeɔ agbo ni etsii.

english: Yam leaves are tiny sun factories that need air and direct light to manufacture food for the tuber. Lifting the vines off the ground catches more sunlight and prevents soil diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato baai ji hulu nitsumɔhei bibii. No biɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ owó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ená hulu la babaoo, ni ebaaha helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why do Fall Armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the leaves of my maize plants during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Fall Armyworms dislike the hot daytime sun and naturally hide inside the cool, moist funnel of the maize leaves to avoid drying out or being eaten by birds, coming out to feed when temperature drops.
ga: Fall Armyworms sumɔɔɔ hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ. ni okɛ ohe awo ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ŋmeii ni mli ejɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ amli koni okpoi lɛ akagbi loo amɛkaye amɛ. Ni ebaaje kpo koni eyatao niyenii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them grow better during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, creates a protective blanket. It blocks direct sunlight from drying out the soil, keeps the root zone cool, and retains moisture for a much longer time.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni efee nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be babaoo

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top when nutrients in the soil run low.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛha shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ niyenii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii lɛ faaa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants with little caterpillars hiding inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. The caterpillars crawl into the central leaves (the funnel) of the maize plant during the day to feed on young tissue, leaving holes as the leaves expand.
ga: Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai (cones) lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛtsɔ bu ni ashiɔ yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and drying up right on the tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tso lɛ niji anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet, humid, and overly shady conditions. Rain drops splash the fungal spores onto the pods, causing them to rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ fungal spores shwieɔ pods lɛ anɔ. ha amɛgboi

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from dry weather, insect damage, or when there are not enough tiny midges in the soil leaf litter to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hao amɛ. Baai amli jwɛi ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Heavy rain fills all the small air spaces in waterlogged soil, suffocating the roots. Without air to breathe, the roots die and soil fungi quickly invade, causing soft rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha kɔɔyɔɔ kotoku bibioo lɛ nɔ. Fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni abaanyɛ amu Shishifãi gboiɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii baa oya. Ekɛ fitemɔ fioo baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines turning dark brown and drying up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: This is caused by Yam Anthracnose, a common fungal leaf disease spread by rain. It damages the leaf surface, preventing the vine from making enough food to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Anthracnose ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji fungal leaf hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni nugbɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Efiteɔ baa lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haaa wain tso lɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots. Tiny soil worms called nematodes or stem-boring insects damage the underground stem and roots, destroying the plant's anchor in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei kɛ shishifãi. Efiteɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling tightly upward and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe kɛtee ŋwɛi ni efee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by viruses spread by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips. The virus changes how the plant grows, causing leaves to twist and stunt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Virus tsakeɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when temperatures become too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing leaf growth instead of fruit growth.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ejaaa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why are my vegetable seeds failing to come up out of the soil after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep, if the soil dries out after watering, or if ants and subterranean insects eat the seeds before they can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi yɛ nu ni awo mli sɛɛ Aloo kɛji ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What is irrigation, and how does bringing a water system to my farm help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛni ji nu shwiemɔ? Ni te nu gbɛjianɔtoo ni mikɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Irrigation means bringing water directly to your farm using pipes, hoses, or pumps instead of waiting for rain. It ensures your crops get steady moisture, allowing you to grow and harvest vegetables all year round, even during the dry season.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ okɛ paipii, hose loo pɔmp baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ, moŋ fe ni ooomɛ nugbɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ po. Ehaa oduɔ ni okpaa aduawai afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli po

english: Is it better for me to pour water directly at the roots of my crops or spray it over the leaves?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔse nu yɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo mafɔse baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Pouring water directly at the base of the plant is better because roots absorb the water where it is needed most. Keeping the leaves dry also prevents fungal diseases that spread easily on wet leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu yɛ he ni ehe hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ aha baai lɛ agbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ oya lɛ naa.

english: Can I use water from a borehole or local stream directly on my crops without damaging them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ nubu loo maŋ lɛ mli faa mli lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: Yes, water from clean streams or boreholes is good for crops. However, if stream water is very muddy or salty, it can clog the soil or burn sensitive root systems over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli tse ni jɛɔ faa loo nubu mli lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi, kɛji nu ni yɔɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ ji muji loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo lɛ, Ebaanyɛ etsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa loo eshã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know if my maize crops are thirsty and need extra water during a dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kumai miiye mi-ŋma lɛ ni ehe miihia ni aha lɛ nu kroko yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: When maize plants do not get enough water, their leaves roll inward tightly like small tubes to save moisture. If you see this happen during the morning hours, your crop needs water immediately.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ mli shiŋŋ tamɔ ŋmãa bibii. koni ekwɛ koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi Kɛji ona akɛ eba mli leebi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia onibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt and sag in the afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, crops lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink from the soil. They droop to protect themselves from intense heat and usually stand tall again once the air cools in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛkotoɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ hulu lɛ enyɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops grow much slower in the dry season even when I give them water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kwraa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: In the dry season, hot temperatures and dry air force the plant to spend most of its energy cooling itself down rather than growing fast or producing heavy fruits.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha amɛhe ajɔɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ oya loo ewo yibii ni tsii

english: Can giving my pepper plants too much water kill them, or is more water always better?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛhaa pepper tsei fe nine lɛ baanyɛ agbe amɛ? Aloo ani nu babaoo hi be fɛɛ be?

english: Too much water can kill your pepper plants because roots need air to breathe. Excess water pushes air out of the soil, causing roots to rot, leaves to turn yellow, and the plant to die.
ga: Nu babaoo baanyɛ agbe o-pepper tso lɛ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni tsei lɛ gboiɔ.

english: Why does my soil dry out very quickly after rain while my neighbor's land stays moist for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni okutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large particles that let water drain away quickly, while soil mixed with organic matter holds moisture longer. Adding compost or animal manure to your soil helps it hold water like a sponge.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ nibii wuji ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli efutu mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nu tamɔ sponji.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass on the soil around the base of their crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ amɛtsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It shields the ground from hot direct sunlight, keeping the soil cool and stopping moisture from evaporating too fast.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ.

english: What time of the day is best for me to water my crops so the water doesn't dry up fast?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mawo mi tsei lɛ nu koni amɛkagbi oya?

english: The best time to water is early in the morning when the soil and air are cool. This allows plant roots to drink fully before the afternoon sun causes the water to evaporate.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo nu ji leebi maŋkpa be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani shwane hulu lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots spoil within a few days after digging them up, while they stay fresh if I leave them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ? Be mli ni eyɔɔ ehee lolo lɛ kɛji mishi yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots stop receiving water and nutrients once harvested, causing them to rapidly deteriorate within two to three days. Leaving them in the ground keeps them living and fresh until you are ready to harvest and sell them little by little.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛji akpa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi ni amɛfee ehee kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaakpa ni ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ kui bibii amli.

english: Why is it important for me to walk inside my maize field every few days instead of just looking from the roadside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabote ŋmãa ŋmɔ ko mli daa gbii fioo moŋ fe ni makwɛ kɛjɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide inside the leaf whorls of young maize plants where you cannot see them from a distance. Inspecting up close helps you detect pest outbreaks early before they spread and ruin your entire field.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli he ni onyɛɛɛ ona amɛ kɛjɛ shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ mra. Dani amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkpãtã okpokpaa muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: How do I know if my crop is stressed before the leaves start turning brown and dying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihao dani baai lɛ aje shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboi?

english: Plants show early signs of stress by drooping slightly in the mid-day sun, changing leaf color from dark green to pale green, or curling their leaves to conserve water before full drying occurs.
ga: Tsei jieɔ haomɔ he okadii mra kɛtsɔ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛshwieɔ shi fioo lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛyaa eŋɔli ni mli tse. Aloo tsɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni nu akafite dani amɛgbi kwraa.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and turn yellow when I pour too much water around their roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mikɛ nu babaoo wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just as much as they need water. Excess water drowns the root system, preventing it from taking up oxygen and food, which causes the leaves to yellow and wilt.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni tso shishifãi hu he hiaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ nu he hiamɔ Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli. Tsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why does my maize grow slow and turn yellowish-green instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miida blɛoo ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowish leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main nutrient crops use to build strong green leaves, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily scorch in hot, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants provide living canopy shade and retain moisture, giving young cocoa the protection it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ haa ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hebuu ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very thin with tiny cobs when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete against each other for light, soil nutrients, and water. Proper plant spacing ensures each stalk receives enough resources to grow thick and yield large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Tsoi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce less yield even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds often absorb water and fertilizer faster than crops do. If weeds are left in the field, they consume the nutrients intended for your crop, leaving the crop underfed.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji akɛ ashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Amɛbaaye niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant garden eggs on the exact same spot where I harvested peppers last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-egg lɛ yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ he ni mifo mi-peppers lɛ yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Peppers and garden eggs belong to the same crop family and share identical soil-borne diseases and pests. Planting them repeatedly in the same spot allows diseases lingering in the soil to immediately attack the new crop.
ga: Peppers kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ tsei aweku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha helai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atutua ŋmɔshi nibii heei oya.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, poor soil moisture, or an imbalance of fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot periods helps flowers develop into full fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kwraa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build leaves and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves the soil waterlogged, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma baai ni wa ni amɛdara. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have tiny root nodules that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them alongside maize naturally feeds the soil, giving your maize free nutrients to grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi bibii. No mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Na niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni ŋmãa bɛ mli mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, overly shaded farms. Pruning thick leaves and clearing heavy brush lets sunlight and air dry out the farm, stopping the disease from taking over.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Baai ni mli tse kɛ brɔshi ni mli tse ni afolɔ Ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni ekpa hela lɛ koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can draw it from the ground. If the plant revives by evening, it is temporary heat stress; using grass mulch around the base helps keep the soil moist and cool.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ ku esɛɛ eba wala mli ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa edɔɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil moisture steady and avoiding over-fertilization with nitrogen helps the plant keep its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa waa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava stems when setting up a new field?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu shikpɔŋ hee lɛ, te esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava stems should ideally be planted about 1 meter apart in all directions. Giving them enough space prevents their underground roots from competing with each other, allowing each plant to form big, heavy tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome yɛ he fɛɛ he. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛaaha lɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye akaŋ. Ha tso fɛɛ tso aná yitso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds early before my crops start growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔi shweremɔ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and water that your main crops need to get established. Clearing them early ensures your crops get full access to food and water during their most critical growing phase.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa otsei titrii lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu mli. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu kwraa yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yam plants make their food in their leaves using sunlight, which then travels down to feed the tuber in the ground. Staking gets the leaves up into the open air and sunlight so the plant can make maximum food to swell the yam tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ebaai lɛ feɔ niyenii ni ekɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii. No sɛɛ lɛ, fã gbɛ kɛba shi koni oyaye ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking kɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ baa ŋwɛi kɛyaa he ko ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ afee nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ebaanyɛ ni eha sweet potato tubers lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one plantain tree forces them to compete for the same food and water in the soil. Leaving only the main tree and one strong sucker ensures the plant has enough energy to grow a very large bunch.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu kome he Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso titri lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni eshwɛ koni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni etsɔ ŋmei agbo.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my harvested hybrid maize produce smaller crops when I plant them again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibioo ko beni miduɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two distinct parent varieties to produce high yield, but that special strength breaks down in the second generation. Seeds saved from a hybrid harvest lose their original strength, leading to smaller, uneven crops.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔɔ dumɔwui sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi nakai hewalɛ ni fa lɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛshishijee hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeee ekome.

english: Why can't I sell my harvest to international buyers in North America or Europe if I mix different varieties of the same crop together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ minibii lɛ maha majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ Amerika Kooyigbɛ loo Europa lɛ? Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli lɛ futu mli lɛ,.

english: International export markets require strict uniformity in crop size, color, taste, and variety so that all produce ripens at the exact same rate and meets standard safety regulations.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ jarayelihei biɔ ekomefeemɔ ni mli wa yɛ dalɛ, su, naa ŋɔɔ kɛ tsei srɔtoi. Bɔni afee ni nibii ni anáa lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ oyaiyeli ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ mli ni eshɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he mlai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do foreign buyers reject my vegetables if I spray crop chemicals right before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ shwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Chemical pesticides leave behind harmful chemical residues that take days or weeks to break down, making the harvest unsafe for consumers to eat according to export health laws.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shĩɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni heɔ gbii loo otsii babaoo dani amɛfiteɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha nihɔɔlɔi ni amɛyeɔ yɛ hewalɛnamɔ he mlai ni kɔɔ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ he lɛ naa.

english: How does insect damage on my produce prevent me from getting top market prices from large buyers?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi ni fiteɔ nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ minaa koni minine ashɛ jarayeli jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛ jarayelɔ wulu ko dɛŋ?

english: Insects leave physical scars and spread rot-causing bacteria on crops, which causes the produce to spoil faster during transport and leads buyers to reject them or pay lower prices.
ga: Kplukai shĩɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ ŋmeii ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ lɛ amɛshwãa. Enɛ haa nibii ni adu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. ni eha mɔ ni heɔ lɛ akpoo loo ewo jara ni baa shi.

english: What is the danger of planting random seeds bought from the local market instead of certified seeds from an extension office?
ga: Mɛni ji osharai ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ ema nɔ mi lɛ najiaŋ lɛ he?
