english: Market seeds often come from mixed, unverified plant strains that grow unevenly, give lower yield, and lack natural resistance against local diseases and pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. ni daa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: If I plant sweet corn right next to yellow maize, will it change the taste and color of my sweet corn?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni ji yellow ŋmãa lɛ masɛi Ani ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ baatsake yɛ ŋmãa loo ehiɛ su mli?

english: Yes, wind carries pollen between nearby fields, causing cross-pollination that mixes the genetic traits, color, and sweetness of the different maize varieties on the same cob.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ woɔ pollen kɛyaa kɛbaa yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa cross-pollination ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sui, su kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa srɔtoi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa kome nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Intercropping uses available soil space and sunlight efficiently while creating plant canopy coverage that keeps soil moist and suppresses harmful weed growth.
ga: Dumɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ baa.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, will I get a bigger total harvest from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo fɛɛ babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to compete with each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants with very small yields.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees needed to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni he hiaa koni akɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow and dry up early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient plants need to produce green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why does my land produce less harvest every year if I keep planting tomatoes on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu tomato yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows soil-borne diseases and pests targeted at that specific crop to multiply over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. Ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it important to loosen and level my land before I put seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mafee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds need soft soil to absorb water easily and push their tiny roots downward without fighting hard ground. Leveling the soil also prevents rainwater from washing your seeds away or drowning them in low spots.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ nu oya ni amɛtsi amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ kɛya shi ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ewuuuu. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ loo ekɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: What happens to my crop seeds if I leave them on top of the ground without covering them with dirt?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ sũ ehàaa nɔ?

english: Seeds left exposed on the surface will be eaten by birds and insects or dried out by the hot sun. Covering seeds with a thin layer of soil keeps them moist and safe until they sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ashi yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ, okpoi kɛ kooloi yeɔ amɛ loo amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni akɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my young crop shoots grow faster when the farm soil is broken into smooth, fine dirt instead of big hard rocks of dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ daraa oya kɛ́ akumɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ tɛi wuji ni wa amli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Fine, smooth soil wraps tightly around the seed, allowing it to draw in moisture evenly from all sides so the seed coat can soften and sprout quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ bɔleɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe waa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ he fɛɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Koni eha dumɔwu lɛ shishi afee blɛoo ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: How deep should I cover my seeds after planting so they don't get trapped under the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii agbe naa lɛ, te esa akɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashɛ he ko tɛŋŋ koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Seeds should usually be covered with soil that is roughly two to three times their own size. Planting them too deep wastes all their stored energy before the shoot can break through into the sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛdalɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ dani mfoniri lɛ anyɛ abote hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Why do crops grow better when I clear away all grass and roots before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mijie jwɛi kɛ shishifãi fɛɛ dani midu lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds and old roots removes competition. It leaves the soil open so your young crops don't have to fight for water, sunlight, and nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ shishifãi momo ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛyaa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tseɔ bɔni afee ni ehe ehiaaa ni odumɔwui lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow unevenly when some parts of my field are bumpier or higher than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo nɔ ni nɔ kwɔ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Uneven ground makes water flow away from high spots and collect in low spots, leaving crops on high ground thirsty while crops in low spots get too much water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ejaaa lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ ni efoɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa kumai yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ naa nu babaoo tsɔ.

english: Will my crops produce more if I use a planter to space them neatly instead of scattering seeds by hand?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii babaoo kɛji mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ tsu nii ni mikɛsaa he lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ minine baagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã?

english: Yes, planting seeds in neat, measured spaces ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and air to grow strong without overcrowding each other.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ fɛo, ni asusu he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃ ni eyeee dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kunim.

english: Why is it hard for my crops to grow if I plant directly into soil that has been walked on and stamped down hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃ kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛnyiɛɔ nɔ waa ni akɛnyiɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil lacks air pockets and blocks young root tips from expanding, which stops the crop from absorbing enough water to survive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni etsĩɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi.

english: How does well-prepared, plowed soil help my crops survive when the rain stops for a few days?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni asaa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ekpa gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Soft, properly loosened soil acts like a sponge, holding onto rainwater deep under the surface so crop roots can keep drinking even during brief dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni afee lɛ blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni emɔɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aya nɔ anu nu yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli po.

english: Why do young crop shoots die underground if heavy rain makes the surface soil bake into a hard crust?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ shã ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa lɛ?

english: A hard soil crust acts like a concrete slab that blocks weak young stems from reaching sunlight, trapping them until they bend and die underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kɔnkrit ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. ni awoɔ amɛ tsuŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know if a new crop variety will grow well on my farm before I plant my whole land with it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ hee ko baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can plant a small test patch on a section of your farm or talk to trusted local elders and farmers who have tried it first. Testing on a small area allows you to see how the crop behaves in your local soil and climate without risking your entire harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu kaa ŋmɔ bibioo ko. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ fã ko nɔ Aloo okɛ maŋ lɛ mli onukpai kɛ okwaafoi ni okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ ni eka amɛkwɛ dã lɛ agba sane. Kaa ni ooofee yɛ he bibioo ko lɛ haa ona bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ wooo oshara mli

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or the ground is holding too much water around the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers always tell us not to plant seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ akadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to build strong roots and grow larger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baa ni eha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ.

english: What causes my pepper plants to drop their flowers before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛwo yibii?

english: Plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or insect damage. The plant drops flowers to save its own energy when conditions are tough instead of spending energy to produce fruit.
ga: Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has become weak and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Weak soil shows when crops grow slowly, have pale leaves, or yield smaller harvests every year compared to the past. Adding animal manure, compost, or crop fertilizer puts essential food back into the soil for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ jieɔ ehe kpo kɛ́ tsei lɛ dara blɛoo, amɛbaa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo daa afi fe tsutsu lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and cooler soil they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crops wilt so fast even when it rained just a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Crops wilt quickly if their root systems are shallow or if the soil cannot hold moisture well. Covering the soil around plants with dry leaves or straw helps trap water in the ground so crops survive short dry spells.
ga: Tsei lɛ baagboi oya kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli.

english: Why do armyworms attack my maize leaves more during dry periods than during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi ŋmãa baai lɛ babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains physically wash young caterpillars off leaves and drown them, while dry weather allows them to hatch and multiply fast. Crops are also weaker during dry spells, making it easier for pests to feed on them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ahe ni ekɛ amɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ oya. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant fail to come out of the ground completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi yeee omanye kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep in the dirt, if the soil is too dry, or if insects eat them underground before they sprout. Planting at the correct shallow depth in moist soil ensures seeds sprout properly.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Aloo kooloi bibii yeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and thin if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee kuku ni efee mlɛo kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal the plant food, water, and sunlight from the soil before your crop can reach it. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow tall and produce well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open, sunny farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigboi beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulu la ni mli tse ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides essential shade, keeping the soil cool and moist while protecting the leaves from scorching.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa, yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and very small cobs instead of healthy, full grains.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa. Yɛ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for leaf growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn out thin and watery instead of big and starch-filled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni nu yɔɔ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛyɛ starch lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store food made by the leaves. If the farm has too many weeds competing for nutrients, or if the cassava is harvested too early during heavy rains, the roots won't store enough starch and will remain thin and watery.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ niyenii ni akɛ baai fee lɛ toɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi babaoo miitswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii loo kɛji akpa ŋmei mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ato ŋmei ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ebaaya nɔ ahi shi mlɛo ni efee nu.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms dry up and drop off without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plant retain its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ faaa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or viral diseases carried by insects. Neem oil sprays or recommended pest control can manage these bugs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋaa ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ atsa kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea pods get holes and black spots just before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmeii lɛ amli bu kɛ ŋmeii diji dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Holes and spots on cowpea pods are caused by pod-boring caterpillars and bugs that feed on the soft seeds inside. Timely spraying with natural extracts or approved treatments during early flowering prevents pod damage.
ga: Buji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cowpea ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite pod lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases tailored to that crop to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni etsɔ tso lɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ehaa helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ kpaa.

english: Why should I wait for two or three good rains before sowing my seeds at the start of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ kpakpa? Linei fioo komɛi dani adu dumɔwui yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: The very first rain usually moistens only the top surface, which dries out fast under the hot sun. Waiting for repeated steady rains ensures deep soil moisture so seeds can germinate fully without drying up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ pɛ. ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Emɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Kɛkɛ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make the energy needed to expand the tubers underground. Staking keeps the vines off the damp soil, preventing leaf diseases and giving the plant full exposure to light.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛkwɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking baaha wain tso lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ tso helai anaa ni ekwɛɔ koni tsei lɛ aná la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen fertilizer or the soil is too wet, forcing the plant to move nutrients up to keep the young upper leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eha ŋwɛi baai lɛ ahi shi bibii lolo.

english: When there is too much nitrogen in the soil, cassava puts all its energy into growing big stems and leaves on top instead of storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle full, harsh sunlight; they need shade trees to protect them from heat and retain moisture in the soil until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la fɛɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni amɛha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why does my crop growth slow down so much during the mid-season dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ waa yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants use soil water to dissolve nutrients and carry food through their stems; without moisture, the plant cannot absorb food from the ground even if the soil is fertile.
ga: Tsei kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii atsɔ amɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse po.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look twisted and tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni eyɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the sap and spreading viruses, which distorts the leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu lɛ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔi kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ adalɛ feɔ nɔ ni ejaaa.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over during light winds even when they have big bunches of fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyɛ aduawai babaoo moŋ.

english: Plantain roots are naturally shallow, and small soil pests like nematodes or weevils eat away the roots underground, leaving the heavy plant without a strong anchor.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo weevils baaye shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiiɔ ni ebɛ sɛkɛ ni wa.

english: Why do the flowers on my cowpea plants fall off before forming bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pea pods lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of rain, or flower-eating insects cause stress that makes the plant drop its blooms to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tsei shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he lɛ baa.

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when soil moisture goes from very dry to very wet too quickly.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake kɛjɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛtee nɔ ni mli edɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Lifting yam leaves off the wet ground lets them catch more sunlight to feed the tubers below, while keeping the leaves dry prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, gĩ baai lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds are asleep until they absorb enough water and feel warmth; if the soil is dry, the seed will either wait underground or die before it can shoot out leaves.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ kɛyashiɔ amɛnuɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ edɔ amɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baamɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo amɛbaagboi dani amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when the sun is very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them provides living shade and holds moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni yɔɔ ekãa ni haa hulutsoo baa oya lɛ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning pale yellow starting from the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's life will help the leaves turn dark green and produce full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves with little dark droppings inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ amli lɛ anɔ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that eats young leaves inside the stalk heart. Applying recommended organic sprays or clean wood ash directly into the plant funnel early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ organic spray loo tso sũ ni he tse ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ wo dumɔwui lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long in heavy soil. Planting your cassava stems on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with maize on the same piece of land without damaging my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas alongside maize is beneficial because cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, which helps the maize grow better without wearing out your land.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow forces them to compete with the mother plant for nutrients and water, resulting in small bunches. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures your main plant grows large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaanyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji niji bibii. Kɛ́ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ plantain jwɛi agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass on top of the soil around their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, protects the soil from hot sun, keeps rainwater from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the best time of the day for me to apply fertilizer or water to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo midumɔ nii lɛ amli loo mikɛ nu awo mli?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because the soil is cooler. Applying water or fertilizer during the hot afternoon sun causes quick evaporation and can burn the tender plant roots.
ga: Leebi loo shwane ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ. Nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ atsɔ oya ni ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme afternoon heat or irregular watering. Watering your plants consistently at the base helps the plant keep its flowers and produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ tomato.

english: How do weeds growing close to my crops prevent them from yielding a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops need to grow strong. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives your crop full access to food so it can produce plenty of yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, enyɛɔ efeɔ nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow root systems and soft leaves that burn easily. They require temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to keep the soil cool and moist until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaa bibii ni shãa oya. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Flower drop occurs when tiny pollinating insects are absent, or when the tree experiences stress from drought or sudden heavy rains that wash away pollen before fertilization can complete.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa trukaa. ni hoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli dani fɔmɔ nii lɛ baa naagbee.

english: High humidity and continuous moisture encourage the growth of a fungus that causes Black Pod disease. Excess shade and overcrowded branches trap damp air, allowing the disease to spread quickly across pods.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ haa ŋmei ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ daa. Shade babaoo kɛ tsei niji ni eyi obɔ lɛ baamɔmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa pod lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: What causes extra shoots to sprout near the base of my cocoa tree, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishigbɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mihe?

english: These side shoots, called suckers or chupons, grow naturally as a response to light or tree stress. They drain vital nutrients and water away from the main trunk and pods, so they should be pruned regularly.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo chupons. Edaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ la loo tsei ahe haomɔ hetoohamɔ mli. Amɛjieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ eshishifã lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ amli daa.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa tree growing with strange bumps and dark scars?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miida kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called mirids (or capsids) bite young cocoa pods to feed on sap. Their toxic saliva leaves dark, hard scars and deforms the pods as they try to grow.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids (loo capsids) lɛ ŋmɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii koni amɛye nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Amɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ poison lɛ shĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni wa. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: What does it mean when the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow from the middle?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the middle or tip usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient crops need to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ loo amɛnaagbee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei lɛ taoɔ koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will cutting off lower branches from my cocoa tree reduce my harvest?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mifo mi-kokoo tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: Pruning lower or overcrowded branches actually improves your harvest by opening the canopy to sunlight and airflow, reducing fungal diseases, and directing the plant's food towards pod production.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha okpamɔ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ ni ooogbele kɛha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha ŋmei helai aba shi, ni ebaaha tsei aniyenii lɛ aya pod feemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do crops planted too close together grow tall and thin with very tiny leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaai bibii waa lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, they compete intensely for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. The plants stretch upward quickly to reach sunlight, leaving them weak and spindly.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ nɔ ni he wa baa.

english: Why should I leave fallen leaves around the root base of my crops instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egbee shi lɛ mabɔle tsei lɛ ashishi moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: Dry leaves act as a natural blanket called mulch. They keep the soil cool, retain rain moisture, and slowly decompose into organic matter that feeds your crops naturally.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Ebuaa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ nugbɔ mli lɛ naa ni ejaraa mli fiofio ni etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts together with my main crops improve the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri ni miduɔ lɛ baadu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules, naturally adding free nutrients into the soil that surrounding crops can feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko fataa shikpɔŋ ni tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. baanyɛ afee ŋaa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient needed for green leaf growth. It can also happen when excessive rain waterlogs the soil, preventing the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ nu. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii

english: Why does my soil become hard and dry out so quickly after I burn the bush on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya beni mishã jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but it destroys the natural organic matter and beneficial organisms that act like a sponge to hold water and nutrients in the dirt.
ga: Shãa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse oya. Mohu ɔ, e kpataa adebɔ mi níhi nɛ a ngɛ mi kɛ níhi nɛ a he hia nɛ a peeɔ kaa sponji konɛ a kɛ nyu kɛ níhi nɛ ngɛ zugba a mi ɔ nɛ hi si ɔ a hɛ mi.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks very close to each other, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting too close forces the cassava plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin plants with very small roots instead of big, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shishifãi bibii waa yɔɔ mli lɛ baa yɛ bulb agbo ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: How long should I wait after the very first rain of the year before I plant my maize seeds?
ga: Yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady and reliable, usually after two or three good rainfalls. Planting right after the very first rain can cause seeds to dry up if a long hot dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ shiŋŋ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji akɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans in the same field alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which helps feed the maize and improves your overall soil fertility.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni aha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ afee fɛo.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall and thin without giving me many peppers under my large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ pepper babaoo wooo mi-pepper agbo lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need direct sunlight to manufacture the energy required for flowering and fruiting. Under heavy shade, they stretch upward searching for light instead of producing peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfɔ̃ ni amɛwo yibii. Yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ, amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛtaoɔ la moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do the black pods on my cocoa tree rot and spread to the healthy pods during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and shady conditions. It spreads when raindrops bounce off infected pods or soil onto healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔi shwie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛtee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, poor soil moisture, or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo kooloi ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce much less harvest even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa yibii fioo kwraa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops, so they steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops before your plants can use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ dani otsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so fast inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miifite oya yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest, exposed to hot sunshine after digging, or stored in a barn without good air circulation to keep them cool.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli beni akumɔ sɛɛ Aloo akɛto ŋmɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli koni eha edɔ.

english: How do I know if a sickness is spreading through my farm crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela miigbɛ eshwa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ amli?

english: Crop sickness often shows up as leaf yellowing, spots, or sudden wilting. Diseases can spread quickly between neighboring plants through wind, rain, or shared tools if infected plants are not removed or treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai jeɔ kpo akɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni baa trukaa. Helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ oya kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, loo nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ajieee tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ loo atsaaa amɛ mra lɛ,.

english: Why do my crops seem to fall sick more easily when weather conditions change?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ?

english: Changes in weather, especially increased moisture and humidity, create ideal conditions for fungi and bacteria to grow and infect vulnerable crops.
ga: kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ Titri lɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni baanyɛ atswa hela lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are all my plantain trees producing fruit at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Plantains planted during the same rainy period usually mature on the exact same schedule, resulting in a large, simultaneous harvest across your farm.
ga: Plantains ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome mli lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa akpaa ŋmaa babaoo yɛ be kome mli yɛ oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: How can I keep my harvested plantains fresh when I have a very large harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ahi shi ehee? Akɛni miyɛ ŋmaa babaoo hewɔ lɛ?

english: Store harvested plantains in a cool, shaded area away from direct sunlight, and leave them attached to the main stalk to slow down ripening and prevent early spoilage.
ga: Kɛ plantains ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulu la shɛɛɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. ni oshi lɛ ni ekɛkpɛtɛ tso titri lɛ he koni ekɛha eshweremɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo ni ekɛtsi fitemɔ naa mra.

english: Why do buyers pay less when there is a sudden flood of plantains in the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo beni plantains ba jara nɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: When many farmers harvest plantains at the same time, the market becomes crowded with produce. Because supply is higher than buyer demand, prices drop.
ga: Kɛ okwaafoi babaoo kpa plantains yɛ be kome mli lɛ Jarayelihe lɛ baayi kɛ nibii ni amɛbaakpa. Beni nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ taoɔ lɛ, jara baa shi.

english: Why is it important for me to sort and arrange my harvested crops neatly before taking them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Sorting crops by size and quality makes them look appealing to buyers, helps you spot spoiled items early, and allows you to command higher prices for prime produce.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli ni aaajara mli yɛ amɛdalɛ kɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ naa lɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔ amɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onaa nibii ni efite mra. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ nibii titrii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ajara ni yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: What should I do with diseased or damaged produce right after harvest?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni efite lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Separate damaged or sick produce from good crops immediately so that rot or mold does not spread to the rest of your clean harvest.
ga: Gbalamɔ nibii ni efite loo hela mɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmaa ni he tse lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ naa.

english: How does packing produce neatly prevent my crops from getting damaged during transport?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ kotoku mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite yɛ be mli ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ?

english: Arranging produce tightly and neatly stops items from bouncing and bruising against each other, which keeps the crop skin intact and delays rotting.
ga: Nibii ni afee lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo jogbaŋŋ kɛ fɛofeemɔ Tsĩ nibii anaa koni amɛkatswa amɛhe ni amɛkatswa amɛhe. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ hewolo lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha fitemɔ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: What brings produce buyers directly to our local collection points?
ga: Mɛni kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa wɔ maŋ lɛ mli hei ni akɛ nibii lɛ yaa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Buyers prefer collection points where large quantities of clean, well-sorted, and good-quality produce are brought together in one convenient place.
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi sumɔɔ hei ni abuaa nibii babaoo ni he tse, ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anaa yɛ he kome ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can organizing our harvest together with local elders improve our crop sales?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ wɔkɛ onukpai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ to ŋmaakpamɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni wɔŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ aya hiɛ?

english: Working together with experienced elders helps maintain quality standards, ensures neat presentation, and gives farmers better power to agree on fair selling prices with buyers.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni akɛ onukpai ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ tsuɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ahiɛɔ shishitoo mlai ni hi jogbaŋŋ amli. Ni ehaa okwaafoi lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baakpɛlɛ jarayeli jara ni sa nɔ.

english: How do I know when my oil palm fruits are mature enough to harvest from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-oil palm yibii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Oil palm fruits are ready for harvest when a few loose fruits naturally detach and fall to the ground, and the fruits on the outer layer of the bunch turn a bright reddish-orange color.
ga: Mu tso yibii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni yibii lɛ ateŋ fioo komɛi shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ni aduawai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli tse.

english: Why do we need to boil palm nuts soon after picking them instead of leaving them raw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔshãa palm ŋmeii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni wɔkpa amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni wɔbaashi amɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Boiling palm nuts softens the tough fruit pulp, stops natural enzymes from making the oil bitter or rancid, and makes it much easier to separate the oily fiber from the hard inner nut.
ga: Palm ŋmeii ni ashãa lɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli ŋmeii ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Ekpaa adebɔɔ mli enzymes ni haa fɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaagbala fɔji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ amli.

english: Why do some of my oil palm trees produce dry fruits that do not yield much oil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii ni egbi shi amɛwooo fɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Dry palm fruits usually occur when the tree experiences water stress during fruit development, lacks essential nutrients like potassium in the soil, or comes from an unselected wild seed variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, palm aduawai lɛ agbimɔ baa kɛji tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ akwɛmɔ be mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo kɛjɛ koo mli dumɔwui ni ahalaaa lɛ amli

english: What causes harvested palm nuts to spoil or turn sour if I wait too long before processing them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei yibii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ loo efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mikɛtsu nii?

english: Once palm fruit bunches are cut, natural fermentation and enzymatic breakdown begin immediately in the pulp. Storing them too long causes acid levels to rise rapidly, ruining the oil quality.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afolɔ tso yibii akui lɛ, adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ enzymatic mligbalamɔ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ loo lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha acid ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ oya. Ehaa fɔ lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is the purpose of the thick red fibers wrapped around the hard palm nut inside the fruit?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo ni yɔɔ tsɔji tsuru ni mli tse ni bɔleɔ ŋmei tso yibii ni wa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: The red fibrous pulp is where the oil is stored to protect the seed and nourish it during germination, while the hard inner shell shields the kernel from pests and drying out.
ga: Red fibrous pulp lɛ ji he ni akɛ mu toɔ koni ebu dumɔwu lɛ he ni eha lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni mligbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe, ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ.

english: How does a long dry season affect how my oil palm trees produce fruit bunches?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ saa mu tsei lɛ ayibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extended dry weather causes oil palms to produce fewer female flowers, leading to smaller fruit bunches or even aborted fruits several months after the drought ends.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa mu tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yei fioo ko pɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji aduawai bibii loo aduawai po ni ashɛrɛ ashwie nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ beni hɔmɔ lɛ ba naagbee lɛ.

english: Why are some palm nuts hard to crush with thin fruit flesh, while others have lots of flesh and thin shells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ akɛ amɛ aduawai ni mli tseee lɛ baatswa palm ŋmeii komɛi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi yɛ loo babaoo kɛ tsitsi ni mli tseee lɛ?

english: This comes down to the variety of oil palm. Wild types like 'Dura' have very thick shells with little flesh, whereas improved varieties like 'Tenera' have thin shells surrounded by thick, oil-rich pulp.
ga: Edamɔ oil palm henɔ lɛ nɔ Ko mli tso henɔi tamɔ ‘Dura’ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse waa kɛ loo fioo. Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ ‘Tenera’ lɛ yɛ tsitsi ni mli tse ni tsitsi ni mli edɔ ni fɔ eyi mli obɔ lɛ ebɔle he lɛ.

english: What nutrients do my oil palm trees need so that the fruits grow large and heavy with oil?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiaa mi-oil palm tso lɛ koni enyɛ ewo yibii wuji ni fɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palms need large amounts of potassium to build fat and oil in the fruit, along with nitrogen to keep the leaves broad and green enough to fuel fruit growth.
ga: Mu tso lɛ biɔ potassium babaoo koni ekɛfee fɔ kɛ fɔ ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Akɛ nitrogen fataa he koni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee eŋɔli bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai lɛ ada.

english: Why do young palm nuts sometimes drop off the bunch before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani amɛdaraa kwraa lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop can be caused by poor pollination during flowering, severe water shortages, or damage caused by pests like palm weevils and rodents feeding on the bunch stem.
ga: Nɔ ni baanyɛ aha aduawai lɛ agbo oya ji pollination ni ehiii yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. nu ni faaa waa loo nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmei tsei ahe ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛbaa.

english: How should I keep my harvested palm fruit bunches if I cannot process them on the same day?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-palm aduawai ni akpa lɛ ato? Kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ atsu he nii yɛ gbi kome nɔ

english: Harvested bunches should be kept in a cool, well-shaded, and ventilated place off the bare ground to prevent heat buildup, rot, and molding before you are ready to boil them.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ kpo nɔ koni hulutsoo akafee ekome. fitemɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ dani ofee klalo akɛ obaahoo.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing fewer pods compared to when my father farmed this same land many years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo kɛ akɛto be mli ni mitsɛ tsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Over many years of continuous farming, the soil naturally loses its vital nutrients and organic matter. Older cocoa trees also lose their vigor and become more vulnerable to pests and diseases, which causes pod yields to drop over time unless the soil is restored.
ga: Yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Cacao tsei ni egbɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛhe feɔ oya kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, ni baanyɛ aha pod yibii lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli. ja aku sɛɛ atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ

english: If I inherit an old cocoa farm, can I plant new cocoa seedlings in the exact same spot immediately after clearing the old trees?
ga: Kɛji akɛ miná kookoo ŋmɔ momo ko akɛ gboshinii Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie tsei momo lɛ?

english: It is better to rehabilitate the land first. Old cocoa soils often carry pests and fungal diseases from the old roots, and the soil nutrients are depleted. Clearing old roots, adding organic manure, and planting shade crops like plantains first will give new cocoa seedlings a better chance to survive.
ga: Ehi akɛ abaaku sɛɛ ato shikpɔŋ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Bei pii lɛ, kookoo shikpɔŋ momo lɛ hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shishifãi momo lɛ amli lɛ. ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa shishifãi momoi lɛ ajiemɔ Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli Ni aduɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shade tamɔ plantains klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ náa hegbɛ kpakpa ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: How do I know if the young cocoa seedlings in my nursery are healthy enough to be moved to the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu awo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Healthy cocoa seedlings have deep green, firm leaves without yellowing or leaf spots, a sturdy straight stem, and a strong root system that holds the nursery bag soil firmly together without root rot.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai ni mli tse, eŋɔli diŋŋ ni bɛ ŋmɔŋ loo baa he tsɔi. tso ni ja ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ grow bag lɛ mli lɛ shi shiŋŋ ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do some of my cocoa seedlings wither and die while they are still under the nursery shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Seedlings in a nursery usually die from either too much water which rots the roots, too little shade letting scorching heat in, or soil-borne fungi that attack young stems near the ground line.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ gboiɔ yɛ nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ hewɔ, ni no haa amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Shade fioo ko pɛ ni baaha la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aba mli. loo ŋmei ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tutuaa tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Can I plant tiger nuts on the same land where my mature cocoa trees are growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tiger nuts yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei ni eda lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Tiger nuts need full sunlight and loose, sandy soil to form good tubers. Mature cocoa trees create a dense canopy that blocks sunlight, so tiger nuts will not grow well under mature cocoa and should be planted in open, sunny areas instead.
ga: Tiger nuts lɛ he miihia hulu ni eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ koni ekɛfee bulbs kpakpai. Kokoo tsei ni edara lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, jata ŋmeii nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kookoo ni eda lɛ shishi. ni esa akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ moŋ

english: What kind of soil and weather conditions do tiger nuts need to produce good yields?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he hiaa tiger nuts lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Tiger nuts grow best in loose, well-draining sandy loam soil where their tubers can easily expand. They need moderate moisture during growth and lots of direct sunlight to develop healthy underground nuts.
ga: Tiger nuts lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni yitso lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo lɛ Amɛmiitao nu ni mli edɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ kɛ hulu la babaoo ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What simple maintenance steps should I carry out regularly to keep my cocoa farm healthy?
ga: Esa akɛ makwɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo komɛi anɔ. Mɛni mifeɔ daa koni mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Regularly weed around the tree bases, prune unwanted canopy shoots and diseased branches, remove black or damaged pods, and maintain good shade trees to protect cocoa from harsh sunlight and extreme dry winds.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ daa. Kpɔ̃ɔ yitsei kɛ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ ni ataooo lɛ. Jiemɔ ŋmeii diji loo ni efite lɛ. Ni okwɛ tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni oha hulutsoo kpakpa aha kookoo lɛ kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to cut off excess branches from our cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ wɔ kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning excess branches opens up the tree canopy to let in sunlight and fresh air. This reduces the dampness that encourages black pod disease and ensures the tree sends its energy into producing cocoa pods rather than extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa baa tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaha hulutsoo ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do older farmers say crops grew easily in their time without fertilizers, but today our crops struggle without care?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ kɛɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ? Shi ŋmɛnɛ lɛ wɔŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: In the past, forest soils were rich in natural nutrients and weather patterns were more predictable. Decades of land use, deforestation, and changing rainfall patterns mean today's soil needs extra care, organic matter, or fertilizers to support healthy crops.
ga: Be ko ni eho lɛ, koo mli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi baafee aha lɛ ji nɔ ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ kooi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ. kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni tsakeɔ yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amrɔ nɛɛ ehe miihia ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it safe to intercrop food crops with my cocoa plants, or will the food crops destroy the cocoa?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ baadu niyenii? Aloo ani niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ baafite kookoo lɛ?

english: Intercropping food crops like plantain, cocoyam, or cassava with young cocoa is actually beneficial because these food crops provide necessary shade and food during the first three years. However, once the cocoa canopy closes, food crops must be removed so they don't compete for light and space.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantain, cocoa, loo cassava ni akɛ cocoa bibii efutu mli lɛ dumɔ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ lɛ mli. Shi, kɛ́ kookoo ŋtayaa lɛ ŋmɛ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie Niyenii tsei lɛ. Bɔni afee ni akatswa la kɛ ŋwɛi he akaŋ

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs to build green leaves and healthy cobs. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the season helps keep the leaves green and boosts your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa lɛ afee baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is my crop yield getting smaller every year even though I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same soil year after year drains specific nutrients without giving the land time to recover. Rotating your main crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore essential soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is often caused by Fall Armyworms, which attack the growing tip of maize plants. Checking your farm early in the morning and applying recommended bio-pesticides or wood ash into the whorl can help control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tso mli sũ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids that feed on plant sap and spread viral infections. Spraying Neem oil solution or an approved insecticidal soap early helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Mra be mli ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my newly planted cocoa seedlings wither and dry up under full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate stems and leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside your cocoa creates a protective canopy that provides shade and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when temperatures get too high or when plants don't get consistent water during flowering. High heat stresses the flower buds, while uneven watering prevents proper nutrient uptake.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa lɛ tsiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete aggressively for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build strong stems, broad roots, and larger fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ aduawai wuji baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds blow during the fruiting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ yibiiwoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and heavy bunches of fruit make the tree top-heavy. Staking your plantain trees with strong bamboo poles or wooden forks provides external support to prevent wind damage.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni aduawai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ haa tso lɛ yiteŋ feɔ miitsii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei loo tsei ni wa ni akɛfee ŋmei lɛ du dumɔwui lɛ, ebaaha yelikɛbuamɔ ni jɛ kponɔgbɛ aba koni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite amɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess water causes waterlogging around the roots, leading to fungal diseases that rot the tubers. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your plants. Keeping your field clear of weeds, especially during the first few weeks after planting, gives your main crop a strong start.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli oya. Gbɛjianɔtoi ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ ni abaakwɛ nɔ Titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 2-3 ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni onibii titri lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct heat and strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or bananas next to them creates a protective canopy that shields the young leaves from scorching and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cassava stems at a slant rather than straight down in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni wɔɔdu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stem cuttings at a 45-degree angle encourages roots to develop evenly near the soil surface, which allows the tubers to grow larger and makes them much easier to dig up during harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ 45 degree angle mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ekomefeemɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaafo amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant is running out of nitrogen, which is essential for healthy leaf growth. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni he wa lɛ adalɛ Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does the soil in my vegetable bed get so hard and dry like rock after just a few days without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi aduawai aŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbi tamɔ tɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic material like decayed leaves or manure. Adding organic matter acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold onto water longer and stay soft so plant roots can breathe and grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi blɛoo. koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu ni amɛdara

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and get sticky during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and stickiness are usually signs of tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids sucking sap from the leaves. The sticky substance is sweet waste they leave behind, which can attract black mold if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ekpɛɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids miinu baai lɛ amli nu lɛ. Nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji jwɛi ni ŋɔɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbala ŋmɔtɔ diŋ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes into the leaves inside the center of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide and feed inside the central funnel of young corn plants where it is moist and safe. Checking the centers of stalks early helps you stop them before they ruin the grain head.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ateŋ he ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni okpa dani efite dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme sun heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist during hot weather helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la ni fa babaoo, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become woody and tough to cook if I leave them in the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tso ni ewaa akɛ abaahoo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava plants pass their ideal harvest age—usually around 9 to 12 months—the plant begins converting soft, starchy energy in the roots into hard woody fiber to help the plant survive longer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ shɛ amɛkpamɔ afii ni sa lɛ he Be ko sɛɛ (bei pii lɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12) lɛ, tso lɛ baabɔi ŋmei hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsakemɔ ni efee tso ni wa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my yam mounds with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, shields the soil from hot sun rays, reduces water evaporation, and keeps the soil cool so young yam vines can grow strongly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni sweet potato wain tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ada waa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds when they have a large bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ? Ani no yɛ sɛɛnamɔi wuji?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and no central deep taproot. When a large bunch of plantains grows, the tree becomes top-heavy, so supporting the main stem with wooden or bamboo poles keeps it stable.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛ taproot yɛ amɛteŋgbɛ. Beni plantains babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmei tsei fiɔ tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops turning yellow and dying even though I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ? Ni maha amɛ nu babaoo?

english: Too much water drowns the plant roots by cutting off their oxygen supply, causing roots to rot. Overwatering can damage your crops just as much as a severe drought.
ga: Nu babaoo baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ oxygen ni ebaafo mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Nu ni okɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afite onibii lɛ nakai nɔŋŋ. kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa

english: How can I tell if my crops actually need watering or if the ground is already wet enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ nu he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa?

english: Push your finger about two inches deep into the soil near the crop. If the soil feels dry and does not stick to your finger, your crop needs water; if it feels wet and sticks, do not add more water.
ga: Nyɛɛ onine nɔ aaafee inchi enyɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi ni ekɛ oniji kpaaa gbee Tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji enu he akɛ edɔ ni ekpɛtɛ ehe lɛ Ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ nu kroko afata he.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun, and should I water them immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ mawo nɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Crop leaves droop in strong heat to protect themselves from losing water too fast. If the soil underneath is moist, the plants will recover by evening, so you do not need to add more water right away.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu lɛ akafite oya tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ gbɛkɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afata he amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How can I make excess water drain out of my muddy farm so my crop roots do not rot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nu ni fa fe nine ni mikɛho kɛjɛ miŋmɔ ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli? Bɔni afee ni mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akagbo

english: Digging small drainage channels between your crop rows allows extra rainwater to flow away from the root zones, keeping the soil moist without soaking the roots.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ gbɛ bibioo ko ni afoɔ Yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ, nugbɔ nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ shishifãi lɛ akafɔ.

english: How do I stop heavy rain from washing away my topsoil and crop mounds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Planting cover crops like beans or placing dry grass mulch around your mounds slows down flowing rainwater and holds the topsoil in place.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baaha nugbɔ nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: What can I do to keep my crops alive during the dry season without buying expensive watering machines?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ni miheee tsɔne ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ nu mli?

english: Mulching—covering the soil around your plants with dry grass, leaves, or crop stalks—traps moisture in the ground for longer periods, reducing how often you need to water.
ga: Mulching—ni ji jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo tsei ashishifãi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ—haa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni afɔɔ lɛ shii abɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: What is a simple way for me to collect and store rainwater on my farm for dry periods?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni matsɔ nɔ mabua nugbɔ nu naa ni mikɛto miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can dig a small earth pond lined with a thick plastic sheet or direct rainwater from shed roofs into barrels to store water close to your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa muji bu bibioo ko ni akɛ plastic ni mli tse ebɔ he. Aloo tsɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli kɛyaa tanki mli koni akɛ nu ato he ni bɛŋkɛ onibii lɛ.

english: Can piling up dry grass and farm waste around my crops help them handle dry weather better?
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ ni atoɔ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkpeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, piling dry grass around crops keeps the soil cool and moist. As that waste decays, it breaks down into rich compost that helps the soil store even more water.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ni akɛ jwɛi fɔ̃ɔ he fɛɛ he. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ. Kɛ nakai jwɛi lɛ fite lɛ Egbɛɔ eshwaa ni efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu babaoo mli.

english: Why do my crops yield less every time I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?
