english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop loves. Switching to different crops, like legumes, helps refill those nutrients naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ edaa lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni tso lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. Ni aaatsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi, tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: When soil moisture changes drastically—going from very dry to suddenly flooded—the crop gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake kwraa—kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛyashi nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ lɛ—dumɔwui lɛ haoɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why do some new maize seed varieties produce bigger cobs than the traditional seeds I save from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi heei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmãa ni da fe blema dumɔwui ni mikɛhere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved or hybrid maize varieties are specifically bred by scientists to combine strong traits from different parent plants. This makes them more efficient at using nutrients and water to grow larger cobs, whereas saved seeds lose their vigor over time and give smaller yields.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi efɔ ŋmãa ni atsake lɛ, loo ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkɛ sui ni mli wa ni jɛ fɔlɔi tsei srɔtoi amli lɛ afata he. Enɛ haa etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu tsuɔ nii koni akɛdu ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: If I plant two different varieties of maize side by side on my land, will they mix and change each other?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ani ŋmãa lɛ baafutu ni ebaatsake?

english: Yes, maize plants pollinate through the wind carrying pollen from one plant's tassel to another's silk. If two varieties bloom at the same time near each other, cross-pollination will happen, which alters the seed quality and traits of the crop you harvest for the next season.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmãa tsei amli, ni ekɛ ŋmãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome tsitsii amli kɛyaa ekroko siliki mli. Kɛji fɔfɔi henɔi enyɔ fee ekome ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, Cross pollination baaba. Enɛ baatsake bɔ ni odumɔwui lɛ hi ha kɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni okpa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ baafee aha.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops wilting and turning yellow even though there is bright sunshine every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ egbo ni efee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ daa gbi lɛ?

english: Crops need sunshine to make food, but intense heat combined with dry soil causes plants to lose water faster than their roots can drink it. This heat stress damages the leaves, causing them to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Hulu la he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛfee niyenii. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ ni egbi he lɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ nɛɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Does the amount of sunlight my crops get during the daytime affect when they start flowering?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tso ko náa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ saa efɔfɔi lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, many crops depend on day length and light intensity to signal to the plant that it is time to move from growing leaves to producing flowers and fruits. Sufficient sunlight provides the energy needed to trigger flower development.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei babaoo damɔ gbi lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ kɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ etsake kɛjɛ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ kɛya fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ. Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baaha hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekanya fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do some demonstration farms cover the soil around crops with dry grass or sheets instead of leaving the dirt bare?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji komɛi ni feɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi ŋmɔji shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaashi muji yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, also known as mulching, shields the ground from hot direct sunlight so moisture does not evaporate quickly. It also keeps the soil cool, prevents weeds from taking over, and protects plant roots.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sɛɛ efooo oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaha tsei shishifãi ahe ni ebu amɛhe

english: Will putting paved tiles or hard stones near my crop nursery beds affect how my seedlings grow?
ga: Ani tile loo tɛi ni wa ni akɛaawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaná dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, hard surfaces like concrete or tiles block water from soaking deep into the ground and trap excessive heat from the sun. This hard boundary prevents roots from spreading outward naturally to find water and nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, hei ni wa tamɔ kɔnkrit loo tile baatsi nu naa koni ekabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni ehiɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ mli Husu ni wa nɛɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛyana nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my fruit trees drop most of their flowers before any actual fruit begins to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ yibii lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shi dani tso yibii diɛŋtsɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Fruit trees drop flowers when they experience stress, such as a lack of water, sudden high temperatures, or poor soil nutrients. The tree aborts the flowers to save its own strength when it senses it cannot support developing fruit.
ga: Tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ nu ni bɛ loo hulutsoo ni naa wa trukaa. loo niyenii ni esaaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli Tso lɛ baakpa fɔfɔi fɔmɔ koni ehiɛ ehewalɛ mli. Be mli ni onuɔ he akɛ onyɛɛɛ oha nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ.

english: How long will I have to wait for a newly planted fruit seedling to start giving me fruits?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ ni dumɔwui heei ni adu lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: It depends on how the plant was raised. Fruit trees grown directly from seeds can take 4 to 7 years to bear fruit, while grafted or budded seedlings can start producing fruit much earlier, usually within 2 to 3 years.
ga: Edamɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ tsei lɛ ahaa lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni woɔ yibii ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛwo yibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛwo tso mli loo ni akwɛ̃ lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa, bei pii lɛ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli.

english: How can keeping cattle on my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsinai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cows produce manure, which is a rich organic fertilizer that adds essential nutrients back to your soil and helps it hold water better. In return, crop leftovers like maize stalks can be fed to the cows.
ga: Tsinai feɔ ŋmɔshi nii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli. Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa tsei, aha tsinai.

english: Can I put fresh cow dung directly onto my growing crops right after collecting it from the animals?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mibua ŋmei lɛ naa lɛ?

english: No, fresh cow dung is too strong and releases heat and gas as it breaks down, which can burn plant roots and harm your crops. It must be dried or composted for a few weeks before applying it to your fields.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmei hee mli wa tsɔ ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi ni eye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui. Esa akɛ agbi loo afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ otsii 2-3 dani akɛwo oŋmɔji amli.

english: Why is it good for me to plant a little bit of plantain alongside my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantain bibioo ko yɛ kookoo tso ko masɛi lɛ?

english: Planting plantains alongside young cocoa trees provides crucial shade that protects tender cocoa seedlings from scorching sun while giving you quick food and income before the cocoa begins to produce.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa niyenii kɛ shika oya dani ajeɔ kookoo feemɔ shishi.

english: Can I grow food crops together on the same farm with my main cash crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu niyenii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mishika ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ?

english: Yes, mixing crops like plantain and food crops with young trees maximizes land use, protects the soil from drying out, and ensures you have food while waiting for long-term crops to yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsei bibii futu mli lɛ baaye abua ni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii babaoo. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni onáa niyenii yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How does planting shade crops like plantain help keep the soil on my farm healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Shade crops with large leaves block intense sunlight, keeping the soil moist, reducing weed growth, and preventing heavy rain from washing away fertile topsoil.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shade ni baai wuji yɔɔ mli lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Ha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni otsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different crop medicines together in the same sprayer to save time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ atsake yɛ tsɔne kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: No, mixing different farm chemicals without expert guidance can cause a reaction that destroys their effectiveness, damages your crops, or leaves chemical burns on leaves.
ga: Dabi, tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ŋaawoo ko bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha nibii ni fiteɔ bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ aba. kpatamɔ onibii lɛ ahiɛ loo shi tsofai yɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: Why did my crop medicine fail to work even though I sprayed it on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmɔshi tsofa lɛ tsuuu nii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛshwieɔ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ moŋ?

english: Crop medicines can fail if they are mixed with incompatible chemicals, diluted with dirty water, sprayed at the wrong time of day, or applied for the wrong disease.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee futu mli. Okɛ nu ni mli ewo muji awo mli. Ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa mli loo akɛ hela ni ejaaa tsuɔ nii

english: Can I use the same chemical medicine on my plantains that I use on my cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ kookoo lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛfee plantain?

english: Not necessarily; different crops react differently to chemicals, and some cocoa treatments are not safe or approved for food crops like plantain.
ga: nɔ ni he ehiaaa; Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi feɔ amɛnii yɛ tsofai ahe. Ni tsofai komɛi ni akɛtsaa kookoo lɛ bɛ shweshweeshwe loo akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ kɛha niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ plantain.

english: What happens if I apply too much chemical medicine to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai babaoo tsu nii yɛ cacao nɔ?

english: Overusing farm chemicals can burn crop leaves, damage the soil, harm beneficial insects that help your farm, and waste your money.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai, efite shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni efite kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔ lɛ. Ni ehaa ofiteɔ oshika.

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow roots and tender leaves that dry out easily under direct sunlight if they do not have taller shade plants like plantain protecting them.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ekãa ni buɔ ehe lɛ bɛ lɛ,

english: How do I know the right medicine to buy when my crops look sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mahe tsofa ni sa beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Before buying chemical treatments, show samples of the affected leaves or pods to an extension officer so they can properly diagnose whether it is a fungal disease, insect attack, or nutrient issue.
ga: Dani obaahe tsofafeemɔ Tsɔɔmɔ baai loo ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii otsɔɔ extension officer lɛ. Enɛ ji koni anyɛ ana pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛji eji tsɛŋemɔ hela, kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mɔ, loo niyenii mli naagba.

english: Why is it important to space out my plants when I am planting different crops together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mijara mi tsei lɛ agbɛhe lɛ mli beni mikɛ tsei babaoo feɔ ekome lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that crops do not fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, allowing both your food crops and cocoa trees to grow healthy.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe wooo hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii tsei kɛ cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some chemical sprays leave white marks on my crop leaves while other sprays leave no marks at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai komɛi ni akɛshwieɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ haa okadii yɛŋ feɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ? be mli ni sprays krokomɛi Eshiii okadi ko kwraa?

english: Different farm medicines are made differently. Wettable powder sprays leave visible powder residues on the leaves to deter insects, while liquid systemic sprays soak directly into the plant tissue without leaving any visible trace.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni afeɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai srɔtoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko. Pauda ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ pauda ni anaa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛtsi kooloi bibii anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni eshiuuu nɔ ko ni anaa.

english: Is the spray medicine I use on my farm strong enough to harm my crops if I apply too much?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji mikɛtsu nii babaoo?

english: Yes, farm chemicals are very strong poisons. Applying more than the recommended dose can burn the crop leaves, stunt the plant's growth, or even kill the crop completely.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔ mli tsofai lɛ yɛ gbeyei waa. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ni fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã. etsĩɔ tso lɛ dalɛ naa loo ehaa tso lɛ gboɔ kwraa po.

english: How long should I wait after spraying medicine on my vegetables before harvesting them to sell at the market?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa lɛ wo aduawai amli sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpã amɛ koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Every chemical medicine has a required waiting period called a pre-harvest interval. This gives the poison enough time to break down safely so the harvested food does not make consumers sick.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɛɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dani kpamɔ baa. Enɛ haa tsofa fɔŋ lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafite shweshweeshwe. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii ni akpaa lɛ haaa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ he ajɔ amɛ.

english: Why do I need to wear protective clothing when I am spraying medicine on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo atadei ni buɔ mɔ he kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa miifɔ cacao nɔ lɛ?

english: The spray is a powerful chemical poison that can soak into your skin or be inhaled into your lungs, causing immediate dizziness, skin rashes, or long-term health problems.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsofa nɛɛ ji tsofa ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni baanyɛ abote hewolo nɔ loo amu kɛya fɛ̃i mli. ni kɛ tsitsi ni tsɔɔ hewolo nɔ tsɔi loo helatsamɔ mli naagbai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and dry up after I spray them for pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf burning often happens if you spray during the hot sun, use a dosage that is too strong, or mix incompatible chemicals together, which causes chemical stress to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa shãa kɛji okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ yibɔ ni mli wa tsɔ atsu nii. aloo tsofai ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni akɛfutuɔ he ni kɛ tsofai ahe haomɔ baa tsei amli lɛ

english: Does rain wash away the spray medicine immediately after I apply it to my maize?
ga: Ani nugbɔ baajie tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmãa lɛ ewo nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Contact sprays that stay on the outside of the leaf can be washed away by rain, but systemic sprays enter inside the plant within a few hours and remain active even after heavy rain.
ga: Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ asɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Shi tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ boteɔ tsei lɛ amli yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli, ni eyaa nɔ etsuɔ ​​nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa po sɛɛ.

english: Can I mix homemade herbal medicines with store-bought chemical sprays to make them work better on my sick crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofa ni akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma fee yɛ shia lɛ afutu tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shwapo mli lɛ nɔ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mitsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: It is not recommended to mix traditional herbal concoctions with manufactured chemicals because they can react badly, reducing the effectiveness of the treatment or damaging your crops.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni afee lɛ futuɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ amli lɛ he ŋaawoo haaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ekolɛ nibii nɛɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Tsofafeemɔ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔtsemɔ loo oŋmɔshi nibii ni efiteɔ.

english: Why do insects keep attacking my crops even after I spray them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛtutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwieɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Pests can build up resistance if you use the exact same chemical spray repeatedly. Rotating between different types of crop medicines prevents insects from becoming immune.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛhe shi kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ. Tsofai ni atsakeɔ kɛtsaa tsei ahe helai srɔtoi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa kooloi ni yɔɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ akaná hewalɛ ni gbeɔ helai.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray medicine on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Spraying early in the morning or late in the evening is best because lower temperatures prevent the spray from evaporating quickly and reduce the risk of scorching the leaves in full sunlight.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi lɛ haaa nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsɔ oya, ni ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ baai lɛ shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if a spray medicine is safe to use on food crops like cassava and tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ hi akɛ akɛbaatsu nii yɛ niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tomato nɔ?

english: You must check the approved crop list on the chemical container's label or ask an agricultural officer, because medicines meant for non-food cash crops like timber or cotton can leave unsafe poisons in food.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ loo obi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko. Enɛ ji akɛ tsofai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee niyenii, tamɔ tsei loo ŋmɔji, baanyɛ aha tsofai fɔji ni ehiii kɛha niyenii aba.

english: How often should I use a water pump to irrigate my maize field during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ nu pɔmp atsu nii kɛfɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: During dry periods, maize needs deep watering about two to three times a week rather than light daily watering. Deep pumping ensures the water reaches lower roots, encouraging them to grow deeper and stronger.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ehe miihia ni afɔ ŋmãa nɔ nu waa shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli. Mohu ɔ, mo ha lɛ nu fioo daa ligbi. Nu lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shɛɔ shishigbɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe waɔ.

english: Why is it better to use siphon tubes instead of just pouring water directly onto my crop fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mikɛ sifon paipi baatsu nii moŋ fe ni mikɛ nu baashwie miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Pouring water directly can wash away topsoil and damage young stems. Siphon tubes deliver a smooth, controlled flow of water evenly across rows without eroding the soil.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ ashwieɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni efite tsei bibii lɛ. Sifon paipii lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ mlɛo, ni akudɔɔ, ni eyaa nɔ etsɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves turn yellow when I pump too much water into the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ akɛ nu babaoo wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much water drowns crop roots by pushing out oxygen from the soil. When roots cannot breathe, they rot and fail to absorb nutrients, which makes the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Nu babaoo haa tsei shishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu lɛ shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt as soon as I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ kɛji mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Young seedlings experience shock when suddenly exposed to full field sunlight and wind. Slowly introducing them to sunlight for a few days before transplanting helps them build strength to survive.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ahe baajɔ amɛ kɛ́ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo hulu la mli fiofio Gbii fioo komɛi dani abaawo amɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi.

english: Does the way I arrange my crop rows affect how much harvest I will get?
ga: Ani bɔ ni matoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ mihaa lɛ baaná nibii ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, proper row arrangement ensures every crop gets enough sunlight, airflow, and soil nutrients. Planting too close creates competition between plants, leading to small yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛkuu ni sa haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa tsei ateŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl and droop in heat to reduce water loss through evaporation. It is a natural defense mechanism, and the plant will recover once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Kasava lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ latsaa mli koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo. Ni tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the exact same spot after harvesting the old ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa tomato momo lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets soil-borne diseases build up. Rotating tomatoes with legumes or corn resets the soil and reduces pest problems.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai lɛ aba shi.

english: What can I spread on top of my soil to keep it from drying out so quickly in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛshwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi oya?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, leaves, or straw (mulch) acts like a blanket. It shades the soil, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and keeps the soil cooler.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo jwɛi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: How can I test if the seeds I saved from my last harvest are still good for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ sa lolo kɛha dumɔ?

english: Place your seeds in a container of water; healthy, dense seeds will sink to the bottom, while damaged or hollow seeds will float. Plant only the seeds that sink for good germination.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo nu tsɛnsi mli. Dumɔwui ni mli wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni efite loo ni mli ewo muji lɛ baaho. Dumɔ dumɔwui ni ebote mli pɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I remove infected leaves from my crops as soon as I notice them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ amli kɛji mina amɛ pɛ?

english: Infected leaves carry fungal spores or bacteria that spread quickly to healthy parts of the plant through wind and water. Removing them early stops the disease from taking over the entire crop.
ga: Baai ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ fungal loo bacteria spores ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛyaa tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu nɔ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my new cocoa seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and provide broad shade leaves that act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa plants from heat stress.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer pods now than they did years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their natural productivity drops and the soil beneath them loses key nutrients. Without regular pruning, soil replenishment, or replacing aged trees, pod yield naturally declines.
ga: Beni kookoo tsei yeɔ afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ewoɔ lɛ baa shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ eshishi lɛ mli niyenii titrii lɛ hu sɛɛ foɔ. Kɛji akɛ afolɔɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe, akɛ shikpɔŋ fataaa he, loo atsakeee tsei momoi lɛ Pod yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and falling off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, suffering from drought, or affected by a root disease. Ensuring good drainage and applying the right fertilizer helps keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni hɔmɔ miipiŋ lɛ. loo shishifã hela emɔ lɛ Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot whenever the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates high dampness that allows the black pod fungal disease to spread quickly. Pruning excess branches and weeding around the tree bases lets sunlight and air dry out the wet pods before the disease can attack.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni ehaa black pod fungus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ agbi dani helai abatutua amɛ.

english: Why do the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from severe heat, water shortages, or a lack of tiny insects that pollinate them. Keeping shade trees on your farm helps preserve humidity and encourages these helpful insects to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafite amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa miipiŋ amɛ. nu ni faaa loo kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ni bɛ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi ni ewoɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Pruning removes unnecessary water-sucking shoots and overcrowded branches. This allows air and light into the tree canopy, directing all the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa ni nuɔ nu kɛ tsei niji ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la boteɔ tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my land in the region is suitable for cocoa farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kpokpaa nɛɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good cocoa soil is dark, deep, loose, and drains water easily without turning into sticky mud. If water sits on top of the soil for days after rain, the cocoa roots will rot and struggle to grow.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ mli, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ oya ni etsɔɔɔ muji. Kɛji nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Cocoa shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni ebaawa akɛ amɛaadara.

english: Is it better to cut down my non-producing old cocoa trees or keep treating them with fertilizer?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaafolɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ amli loo aya nɔ awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If cocoa trees are extremely old or infected with diseases like swollen shoot, fertilizer will not bring them back to high production. Clearing the old farm and replanting with improved hybrid seedlings is the most effective way to restore income.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ egbɔ waa loo eyɛ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haŋ tso lɛ aku sɛɛ aba yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa shika ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji momoi amli ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ dumɔwui ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa shika ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes small dark spots on my young cocoa pods that make them shrivel up and die?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa? Mi kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ anɔ kɛyashi amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi?

english: These dark spots are caused by sap-sucking insects called mirids or capsids. They bite into young pods to feed, destroying the tissue and causing the pods to dry up before maturing.
ga: Koolooi ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids loo capsids lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛha niyenii. Enɛ fiteɔ fãji lɛ ni egbiɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds regularly ensures your crops get all the food and light they need to grow rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my crops grow greener and faster when I plant them close to the riverbank?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛshwereɔ oya kɛ́ midu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Land near rivers stays naturally moist even during hot spells and receives rich soil washed down from upstream, which gives crops a steady supply of nutrients and water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faai lɛ hiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli po. ni enine shɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii naa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu daa.

english: Why do my pepper plants turn yellow and drop leaves after water stands on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiiho baai beni nu ni damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do, so when water sits on the field for too long, the roots drown and rot, preventing the plant from feeding its leaves.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu, tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baagbo ni amɛbaagboi. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaha foliar niyenii.

english: Maize leaves curl up on hot days to hide part of their surface from the bright sun, which helps the plant reduce water loss so it does not dry out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛtee ŋwɛigbɛ fã ko kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do my vegetable plants grow very tall and skinny with few fruits when planted under thick shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ?

english: Plants need direct sunlight to make food. When shaded, they stretch rapidly upward to reach light, making them too weak to support heavy stems or fruits.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ eyɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Eshɛɔ oya kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyashiɔ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei loo aduawai ni tsii.

english: Yams produce underground tubers using sunlight captured by their leaves; staking keeps the leaves lifted and spread out to catch light while protecting them from ground rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes kɛ hulu la ni baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ woɔ amɛhe nɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛná la yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow plenty of tall leaves but produce small root tubers in very rich soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa kakadaji babaoo shi shishifãi bibii lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii waa nɔ?

english: Soil with too much nitrogen tricks cassava into spending all its energy building big green stems and leaves instead of storing food down in the root tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to plant crops without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ tsei anɔ ni mikɛyaaa laboratori?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels soft and crumbly in your hands, holds a bit of moisture without turning into sticky mud, and has earthworms living in it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ bɔdɔ nɛ e ngɛ tsɔe ngɛ nine mi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko hiɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ ni hiɔ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming tomatoes during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high or water is scarce, tomato plants shed their flowers to save energy and survive rather than trying to feed new fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu faaa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni okɛ aduawai heei aba

english: Why do my cowpeas produce fewer pods if I apply the same heavy fertilizer I use for maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni tsii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have tiny organisms on their roots that naturally trap plant food from the air, so adding too much external fertilizer makes the crop grow leaves instead of seed pods.
ga: Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ cowpeas mli. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, emɔɔ tso niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná baai yɛ dumɔwui ashishifãi najiaŋ.

english: Why do my plantain shoots take much longer to produce a bunch if I leave all the smaller stems growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji mishi tsei bibii ni bɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: The small stems surrounding a plantain tree steal food and water from the main mother stem, so removing extra suckers allows all energy to go into one strong, fast-yielding plant.
ga: Tso bibii ni bɔle plantain lɛ he lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ tso kome ni he wa ni woɔ yibii oya lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food plantains and maize need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plants regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa plantains Ni ehe miihia ni ŋmãa akwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the leaves grow tall and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together or have too much nitrogen in the soil, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of feeding the roots below. Proper spacing allows energy to reach the tubers.
ga: Beni tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa hewalɛ shɛɔ yitso lɛ he.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread diseases, or by extreme heat and lack of water. Keeping young plants protected and managing insects prevents the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa mli Tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ he kɛ kooloi bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa.

english: Why do white powdery spots spread across my vegetable leaves during rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-vegetable baa lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High air moisture creates a perfect environment for fungal diseases like powdery mildew to grow on damp leaves. Spacing plants farther apart allows wind to blow through and keep the leaves dry.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ powdery mildew, koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ baai ni mli edɔ nɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni eha baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil was watered?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni mikɛ nu efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Hot sun makes water evaporate from leaves faster than roots can drink it up, so plants temporarily wilt to protect themselves. Spreading dry grass mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and moisture steady.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛbu ehe. Mulch ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas on the same land after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu cowpea yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but legumes like cowpeas naturally trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth, restoring soil fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I let weeds grow near my young crop seedlings early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before seedlings can establish roots. Clearing weeds in the first few weeks gives your main crops full access to food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ shishifãi. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha otsei titrii lɛ aná niyenii babaoo.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to push out of the dirt after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ anyɛɛɛ ajie midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain can pack topsoil tightly into a hard crust or flood seeds, making them rot or preventing soft shoots from breaking through. Loosening the topsoil gently helps seeds sprout easily.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ekɛ nu abɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa egboɔ loo ehaaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ atsɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ blɛoo lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when heat is too high, when water is inconsistent, or when bees are not present to pollinate them. Regular watering and keeping flowering herbs nearby attracts bees to set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii Nu ni oooha kɛ tsofai ni fɔ̃ɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ Daa lɛ baaye abua ni egbala ŋmeii kɛba aduawai anɔ.

english: How do I know when groundnuts are fully grown and ready to pull out of the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the foliage turns yellow and dies down, and the inside of the harvested pods shows dark brown markings when you crack a few test pods open.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi. Ni ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpo kɛji ogbele kaa ŋmeii fioo komɛi.

english: Why should I plant moringa trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu Moringa tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moringa trees grow very quickly and produce leaves packed with rich vitamins and minerals. Feeding these leaves to your livestock helps build strong bones and improves their overall health.
ga: Moringa tsei lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni vitamini kɛ mineral babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ baai nɛɛ ha okooloi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛná wui ni wa ni eha amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Does moringa grow well in dry areas or poor soil?
ga: Ani moringa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ?

english: Yes, moringa is a very tough plant that survives well in dry weather and poor soils. Once planted, it continues to grow fast and produce nutrient-rich green leaves throughout the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, moringa ji tso ko ni wa waa ni hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Kɛ adu lɛ, edaa oya ni ewoɔ tsei eŋɔli ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How often can I cut fresh leaves from my moringa tree without damaging it?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ mafo Moringa tso lɛ baai heei ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: You can harvest moringa leaves every few weeks because the tree shoots back quickly. Cutting the branches regularly actually encourages the tree to grow bushier and produce even more leaves.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa moringa baai lɛ daa otsii fioo komɛi ejaakɛ tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tso lɛ he daa lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni eda ni ewo baai babaoo.

english: Is it safe to pluck tall wild grasses from outside my farm to feed my animals?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ majie koo mli jwɛi kakadaŋŋ ajɛ miŋmɔ lɛ kponɔ koni mikɛha kooloi lɛ niyenii?

english: Yes, tall wild grasses from uncultivated areas make excellent fresh food for small livestock like grasscutters and goats, providing them with natural energy at no cost.
ga: Hɛɛ, koo mli jwɛi kakadaji ni jɛ hei ni atsuuu nii yɛ lɛ ji niyenii hee jɛɛhe ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tooi. Ehaa amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛheee nɔ ko.

english: Why do some small farm animals prefer wild grasses over regular pasture grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi bibii komɛi sumɔɔ koo mli jwɛi fe jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Wild tall grasses growing in undisturbed bush areas are often softer and full of natural nutrients, making them a natural choice for animals like grasscutters that feed on lush forage.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei bibii ni nɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa lɛ amli lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa jwɛi nɛɛ feɔ nɔ ni kooloi, tamɔ jwɛi fɔlɔi, ni yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ halaa.

english: Can I grow wild pasture grass on my own farm plot for easy harvesting?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu koo mli jwɛi yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli koni ekpamɔ afee mlɛo?

english: Yes, you can cultivate forage grasses directly on a section of your land so you can easily pluck fresh green feed every day without walking far into the bush.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu jwɛi ni akɛyeɔ niyenii yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii hee, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ atsu nii daa gbi ni ehe ehiaaa ni onyiɛ shɔŋŋ kɛya jwɛi lɛ mli.

english: Can I mix poultry feed with fresh green crops when feeding my small farm animals?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi aniyenii afutu tsei ŋmɔji heei beni mikɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ nii lɛ?

english: Yes, combining a small amount of poultry feed—about a quarter of their daily food—with fresh wild grass and moringa leaves gives your animals a well-balanced diet for fast growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ kooloi aniyenii bibii (aaafee daa gbi niyenii lɛ mlijaa ejwɛ mli ekome) futu koo mli jwɛi heei kɛ moringa baai amli lɛ, ebaaha okooloi lɛ aná niyenii ni sa koni amɛdara oya.

english: Which farm plants help livestock develop stronger bones and bodies?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔ mli tsei yeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni amɛnáa wui kɛ gbɔmɔtsei ni wa?

english: Plants like moringa are very rich in calcium and essential vitamins. When fed to animals, these nutrient-dense leaves directly strengthen their bone structure and body frame.
ga: Tsei tamɔ moringa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ calcium kɛ vitamini ni he hiaa waa. Kɛ akɛ niyenii ha kooloi Nɛkɛ baai ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli nɛɛ woɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ wui kɛ fãji ahe hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Should I dry moringa leaves before feeding them to my livestock or give them fresh?
ga: Ani esa akɛ magbi Moringa baai lɛ dani mikɛha kooloi loo maha amɛ baai heei?

english: You can feed moringa leaves fresh directly after harvesting, or dry them in the shade to grind into powder and mix with regular animal feed for long-term use.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ moringa baai heei aha niyenii beni okpa lɛ sɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Aloo agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni atsɔ mli afee powda ni akɛ kooloi aniyenii fɛɛ afutu mli koni akɛtsu nii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I reduce the cost of animal feed using crops grown on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo niyenii he nyɔmɔwoo shi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ?

english: By growing nutrient-rich plants like moringa and harvesting local wild grasses, you can cover most of your animals' daily diet naturally and only buy small amounts of commercial feed.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli tamɔ moringa ni aduɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli koo mli jwɛi ni akpaa lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ daa gbi niyenii ni okooloo lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ mli babaoo awo mli. ni amɛheɔ kooloi aniyenii ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ fioo pɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plant turn yellow when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When rain waterlogs the soil, oxygen cannot reach the crop roots. Without oxygen, maize roots cannot absorb essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, causing the leaves to turn yellow and stunt growth.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ, Abɛi shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my maize cobs have missing grains instead of full rows of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ekomɛi amli ŋmeii ni elaaje yɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize cobs fail to fill completely when the crop suffers from heat stress or drought during its flowering stage, which prevents successful pollination of the corn silks.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ atsake ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ kɛji tso lɛ naa dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmãa siliki ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when planted in heavy clay soil that holds too much standing water, creating ideal conditions for fungal diseases to attack the swollen roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baatutua shishifãi ni efuu lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting shoots while sitting in my storage shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ beni mita mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living organisms that go through natural dormancy. Warm temperatures and high humidity in storage signal to the tuber that it is time to break dormancy and grow a new vine.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni wɔɔ. Nibii ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ bulb lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛfo wɔɔ ni amɛdu wain tsei heei.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from prolonged dry spells or when there are not enough tiny pollinating insects, like midges, present in the farm to fertilize the blooms.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ faaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: Why do young coffee seedlings wither when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔfe dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young coffee plants have shallow roots and delicate leaves that lose moisture faster than roots can absorb it under intense sun. They require shade trees during their early stages to survive.
ga: Kɔfi tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo mra he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and collapse around the trunk during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds pull moisture out of plantain leaves rapidly. The plant intentionally lets older leaves die back to conserve water in its main stem until the rains return.
ga: Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ plantain baai lɛ amli oya. Tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛhaa baai ni egbɔ lɛ gboiɔ koni amɛkɛto nu he yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my papaya trees shed their young fruits before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ miiho yibii bibii dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Papaya trees drop young fruit as a defense mechanism when they face irregular watering, nutrient shortages, or when the plant tries to carry more fruit than its roots can nourish.
ga: Papaya tsei shwieɔ amɛyibii bibii lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni ejaaa lɛ hiɛ. niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa Aloo kɛ́ tso ko bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die during the warm afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: This heat-of-the-day wilting often indicates a soil bacterial disease or root damage that blocks the plant's water-conducting stems, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, la ni tsoɔ daa gbi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa loo shishifãi ni efite ni miitsi tso lɛ shishifãi ni hiɛɔ nu lɛ anaa. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crop plants right after I clear the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil for years waiting for light. Clearing the land exposes these dormant seeds to sunlight and air, causing them to germinate faster than cultivated seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo, ni amɛmiimɛ la. Kɛ́ ajie he lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ akwɛ̃. Enɛɛmɛi nine shɛɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. Ehaa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender roots and leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight and intense heat. Planting shade crops like plantain or cassava next to them acts like a living umbrella, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stop growing even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores the nutrients your maize needs to develop properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen efo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa o-ŋmei lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops burn and die if I put chemical fertilizer right next to their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fata amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated salts. When placed directly against a stem or root, they suck moisture out of the plant instead of feeding it, causing the plant to dry up and die.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi loo shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Why are fall armyworms destroying my farm so much faster this year than before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ miifite miŋmɔ lɛ oya fe dani afi nɛɛ ba lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm multiply very fast during dry and warm weather conditions. If you plant the same crop in the exact same field every season, the pests stay in the soil and multiply, making each new attack much worse than the last.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ faa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ, Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛshwereɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tutuamɔ hee fɛɛ tutuamɔ hee mli wa kwraa fe nɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant cassava on the exact same piece of land three times in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava draws a massive amount of food out of the earth to grow its heavy roots. Planting it continuously drains the soil completely, leading to poorer harvests and allowing soil-borne diseases to build up.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eshishifãi ni wa lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu kwraa. Enɛ haaa yibii kpakpai aba, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ aba.

english: Why does covering my soil with dry leaves and grass help my vegetables grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, acts as a blanket. It blocks the hot sun from drying out the soil, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly breaks down into rich food for your crops.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ tsei ni egbi ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Etsĩɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye nɔ ni efiteɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha onibii lɛ fiofio.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds close together so I can fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in weak, thin stalks and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing any pepper when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani ewoɔ pepper kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, forcing them to drop flowers to save water and energy just to stay alive. Keeping moisture in the soil through shading and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛtsɔ shade kɛ mulching nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it better to water my vegetables early in the morning instead of at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔ aduawai anɔ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering at noon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can drink it. Morning watering allows the plants to soak up moisture before the heat of the day sets in.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ yeɔ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest produce less yield than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Seeds saved over many seasons lose their strength and can carry hidden pests and diseases from the old crop. Certified seeds are specially bred and tested to resist local diseases and yield larger harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsɛ mli lɛ aba. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Maize leaves roll up during peak heat as a natural survival mechanism to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun. This cuts down water loss through evaporation, helping the plant conserve moisture until the afternoon temperature drops.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ shwane mli latsaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does millet grow and produce grains in the dry Northern region, while plantain struggles to survive there?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ ni ewoɔ dumɔwui yɛ Kooyigbɛ ni nu bɛ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, plantains lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Millet has deep root systems and waxy leaf coatings that allow it to trap moisture and withstand prolonged heat. Plantain needs high rainfall, soft moist soil, and high air humidity, which makes it poorly suited for dry Northern climates without irrigation.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni tamɔ waxy ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni enyɛɔ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa be kakadaŋŋ. Plantains he miihia nugbɔshiimɔ babaoo, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa. Enɛ haaa amɛfee nɔ ni sa kɛha kooyigbɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi ni nu bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and fragile root systems that burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Shade trees block the harsh midday sun, lower the surrounding air temperature, and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane teŋ lɛ he hɔɔŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ nɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my yam crop yield very small tubers if I do not give the climbing vines wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji mihaaa amɛ tso kɛha wain tso lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose all their leaves to direct sunlight. When sunlight hits the leaves, the plant makes food that travels down to feed and swell the underground tuber; without stakes, lower leaves stay shaded on the ground and produce less food.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ hulu la lɛ tswa baai lɛ Tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eyaye ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaha shishigbɛ baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni niyenii fioo pɛ baaba.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil retains too much standing water during heavy rains. Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe, and waterlogged soil suffocates the roots and encourages fungal diseases that cause rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii helai ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push stem-like pegs back down into the dirt after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ eshishifãi ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: After a groundnut flower is pollinated above ground, it grows a long peg that bends down and burrows into the soil. The groundnut pod cannot form in the open air; it requires the dark, damp protection of the soil to grow into a pod.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Edaa ni etsɔɔ ŋmei kakadaŋŋ ni shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanut pods nyɛŋ afee yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ. Ehe miihia ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ abu ehe koni enyɛ eda ni etsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high, or when the soil experiences sudden drought or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Under heat or drought stress, the plant sheds its flowers to save energy and keep itself alive instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hɔmɔ ba trukaa loo akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli. yɛ latsaa loo hɔmɔ shishi Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei baawo yibii lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Pepper leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies sucking the sap from the underside of young leaves. This sap-sucking damages the leaf tissue as it grows, forcing the leaf to twist and wrinkle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ nu nɛɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji beni edaa lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap in half and fall over easily when strong rainstorms hit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ fãa enyɔ oya ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum ni naa wa ko mli lɛ?

english: A plantain trunk is not made of real wood, but of tightly wrapped leaf stems filled with water. As heavy fruit bunches grow at the top, the tree becomes top-heavy, making it vulnerable to snapping or uprooting in strong winds.
ga: Akɛ tso diɛŋtsɛ feeee plantain tsei lɛ. Shi baa tso lɛ ji nɔ ni akpɛtɛ he waa ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli shwereɔ yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ oshara mli akɛ amɛbaakumɔ loo amɛbaajie amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my rice plants turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmã tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen runs low, the plant mobilizes remaining nutrients from its older, lower leaves and sends them up to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ buaa niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛtsuɔ amɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: What do the numbers like 15-15-15 or 13-13-13 on a fertilizer bag actually mean for my crops?
ga: Mɛni yibɔi tamɔ 15-15-15 loo 13-13-13 ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kotoku nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: These numbers show the equal balance of three main nutrients: Nitrogen for leaf growth, Phosphorus for strong roots, and Potassium for fruit development and disease defense.
ga: Yibɔi nɛɛ tsɔɔ niyenii mli nibii titrii etɛ ni yeɔ egbɔ ni yeɔ egbɔ: Nitrogen kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Fosfɔs kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ potassium kɛha aduawai akwɛmɔ kɛ helai atsimɔ.

english: Other farmers tell me I am applying more fertilizer than the traditional amount, so how do I know the correct dosage for my land?
ga: okwaafoi krokomɛi Ekɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo miifata he fe bɔ ni mifeɔ daa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ male shika ni sa kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Using too little fertilizer starves your crops, while using too much burns the roots or wastes money. Following recommended officer guidelines for your specific soil type gives you maximum yield safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ loo ebaaha ofite shika. Kɛji onyiɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni amralo lɛ kɛha kɛha shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onine ashɛ yibii babaoo nɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize start turning pale yellow early in the season even when it rains well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are a clear sign that your crop lacks Nitrogen in the soil, which plants need to create healthy green foliage and convert sunlight into plant food.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛtsake hulu la lɛ amɛfee tsei aniyenii.

english: Why should I measure exact distances between my plants instead of just scattering seeds like we used to do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ he? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔɔgbɛ dumɔwui lɛ wɔshwã kɛkɛ tamɔ bɔ ni wɔfeɔ tsutsu lɛ.

english: Proper spacing ensures every single plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors, resulting in larger crops and higher overall yield.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ awuu Enɛ haa tsei wuji kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my field right when I plant seeds or wait until they sprout?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ loo mamɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Applying starter fertilizer at planting or shortly after germination helps young roots feed immediately, giving plants a strong head start before a second boost during flowering.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni jeɔ shishi yɛ dumɔ mli loo beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ yeɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ dani ekɛ hewalɛwoo ni ji enyɔ fataa he yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How do I calculate what a realistic harvest target should be for one acre of my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu nɔ ni esa akɛ ŋmaakpamɔ oti ni yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ afee kɛha miŋmɔ ni feɔ acre kome lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: Target yields are set by measuring recommended seed output under good care; if your harvest falls short of this mark, your farm likely needs improved seed varieties or better soil nutrition.
ga: Atsɔɔ yibiiwoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ dumɔwui yibiiwoo ni atsɔɔ akɛ abaawo yɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi lɛ susumɔ nɔ. Kɛji okpamɔ lɛ eshɛɛɛ nɛkɛ shishitoo mla nɛɛ he lɛ Ekolɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ he baahia oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred for uniform growth, pest resistance, and high yields, whereas saved seeds lose these strong traits in the second generation and produce far less.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛdara daa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why is it necessary to prune excess branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unproductive stems so the tree sends all its energy into growing big pods, while also opening the tree up to sunlight and air flow to prevent fungal pod diseases.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni wooo yibii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, gbelemɔ tsei lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry palm leaves help them grow during dry spells?
ga: Mulching around Te miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei baai ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: This practice, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from getting sunlight to grow.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aná hulu la

english: Why do weeds harm my cassava crop so severely even after the stalks have grown tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui waa eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkwɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water and fertilizer directly from the soil around cassava roots, which stops the plant from swelling and growing large, full tubers under the ground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afuu ni ekwɛɛɛ bulbs agboi ni eyi obɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks closer together, will I harvest more cassava tubers?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe Ani makpaa ŋmei shishifãi babaoo?

english: Planting cassava sticks too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Leaving adequate space around each plant allows the roots to expand fully underground, resulting in larger and heavier tubers.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ko ni bɛ nɔ ko ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ha tso fɛɛ tso nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi kwraa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ feɔ agbo ni etsiiɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their rich green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does mixing dried animal dung into my farm soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛfutuɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal dung acts like a sponge in the soil to hold rainwater longer and slowly breaks down to release essential plant food into the root zone over time.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ejie tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crop plants look small and weak even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crop roots. Even with good rain, weeds consume the food your crops need, leaving the main crop hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Jwɛi hu yeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ mɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing fresh shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or mites feeding on leaf sap, or by a plant virus. Controlling these insects early protects the leaves and keeps the plant growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ tso mli helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ Mra be mli ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ Ebaabu baai lɛ ahe ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in direct sunlight to manufacture energy for underground tuber growth. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, preventing leaf rot and maximizing sunlight exposure.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni oha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms keep falling off before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping soil moisture consistent prevents stress and helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ tsiɔ haomɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni shwereɔ.

english: Why do agriculture officers recommend planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen gas from the air and puts it naturally into the soil. This enriches the soil and helps neighboring crops like maize grow bigger.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele, ni amɛdaraa.

english: Is it safe to plant my maize seed right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular. Planting after just one early rain risks seed failure or seedling death if a dry period follows before the main rainy season fully establishes.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akafee nɔ ko loo dumɔwui lɛ agbele aba kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ je shishi kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that provide vital shade and moisture, protecting the cocoa plants during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if I am planting my cassava stem cuttings the right way up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miidu yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' where leaves used to grow on the stem. Make sure these buds point upward toward the sky before sticking the stem into the soil so it grows properly.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni be ko ni eho lɛ baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani okɛ ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.
