english: Why should I not plant my maize seeds very close together to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough food to produce larger, healthier cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen fertilizer or the soil is too wet. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops when the ground is dry or after it rains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist right after a rain. Moist soil helps the fertilizer dissolve quickly so the roots can absorb it, whereas dry soil causes the fertilizer to waste.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks in the soil for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tso kakadaŋŋ ko? kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight for making food. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground to avoid disease and allows the plant to produce much larger yam tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nihoomɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akamɔ tso lɛ ni eha tso lɛ awo sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crops' growth even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa oya eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops by stealing soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: What is making small holes in the middle leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Small ragged holes in maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the center of the plant. Spraying early with appropriate pest controls helps protect the harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni naa niyenii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Ni akɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baashwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu nibii ni adu lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl during intense heat to conserve moisture and protect themselves, but persistent curling can also be caused by insect-borne viruses. Consistent watering and pest control help reduce this.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa be mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe. Shi tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ kooloi amli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ aba. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaye abua ni naagba nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my pepper fruits rot and drop off the plant during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rainwater and high humidity create a perfect environment for fungal diseases to spread on wet peppers. Clearing weeds around the plants improves airflow and keeps the fruits dry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsɛŋemɔ helai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ajieɔ Tso lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Can crop diseases stay on my farm and affect my crops all year round from January to December?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ ahi miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ January kɛyashi December?

english: Yes, some diseases remain in the soil, fallen leaves, or wood throughout the entire year, coming out to attack your crops during different seasons whenever weather conditions favor them.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai komɛi hiɔ sũ lɛ mli, baai ni egbee shi, loo tsei amli yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Amɛtutuaa onibii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baaŋmɛ gbɛ

english: How can I tell if my mango trees are getting attacked by a fungus or disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela loo hela ko emɔ omango tso lɛ nɔ?

english: You will usually see dark brown or black spots on the leaves, flowers turning black and drying up, or young fruits developing dark rot spots and dropping off early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ obaana he ko ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ. Aloo aduawai bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni egbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Is it possible for my mango trees to suffer from more than one disease at different times of the year?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mi mango tso lɛ baaná helai ni fe ekome yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli?

english: Yes, a mango tree can be attacked by five or six different diseases throughout the year, such as flower rot during the rainy season and powdery mildew during drier months.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai srɔtoi baanyɛ atutua mango tsei. Helai enumɔ loo enumɔ baa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ, tamɔ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ. kɛ powdery mildew yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Will regular insect spray cure black spots and rot on my fruit trees, or do I need a specific fungicide?
ga: Kpoji ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ daa lɛ baatsa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi aduawai tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ni efiteɔ. Aloo ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko ni gbeɔ ŋmeii atsu nii?

english: Insect sprays only kill bugs and insects; they cannot stop rot or spots caused by fungi. You must use a specific medicine called a fungicide to kill fungal diseases.
ga: Insect spray lɛ gbeɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii pɛ. Enyɛŋ ekpa fitemɔ loo muji ni ŋmei kɛbaa lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ fungicide lɛ atsu nii ni okɛgbe tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ.

english: If a specific fungicide is recommended for my fruit disease, can I just buy any chemical spray from the market instead?
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsɔɔ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko ni gbeɔ ŋmeii kɛha mi tso yibii hela lɛ, Ani manyɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ yɛ jara nɔ moŋ?

english: No, using the wrong chemical will waste your money and leave your trees unprotected. Different diseases require specific active ingredients, so only the correct recommended fungicide will stop the disease.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni ejaaa ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaaha otsei lɛ akabu amɛhe. Helai babaoo biɔ nibii pɔtɛɛ ni tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofa ni ja ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛgbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ pɛ baaha hela lɛ akpa.

english: When is the best time for me to spray fungicide on my mango trees to protect my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii awo mi mango tso lɛ nɔ koni mikɛbu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: You should spray just before flowering begins and when fruits are small, because stopping the disease before it infects the flowers ensures your crop develops into healthy, full-sized fruits.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ dani fɔfɔi lɛ aba kɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ ji bibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ okpa hela lɛ dani ewo fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ni etsɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyi obɔ.

english: Should I wait until I see my fruits rotting before I apply fungicide medicine, or should I spray early?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni aduawai lɛ agbo dani mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ awo mli loo esa akɛ mafo mra?

english: It is much better to spray early as a preventive measure, because once fungal disease enters the flowers or young fruits, the damage is permanent and cannot be reversed.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshɛre mra. akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa Ejaakɛ kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai bote fɔfɔi loo aduawai bibii lɛ amli lɛ Nɔ ni efite lɛ hiɔ shi daa ni anyɛɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my mango flowers dry up and fall off before any fruits can form on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani aduawai baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is commonly caused by fungal attack during early bloom, which destroys the delicate stems holding the flowers, causing them to blacken and drop off before fruit forms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni baa mɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shishijee be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ tso ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni hiɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ diŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my mangoes get rotted spots even when the weather seems dry and good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mangoi lɛ yɛ hei ni egboi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Fungal spores can stay hidden in old branches and dried leaves on the tree from past rainy seasons, springing back to life and attacking green fruits whenever humidity rises.
ga: Fungal spores baanyɛ ahi tsei aniji momoi kɛ baai ni egboi ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ amli yɛ naagbee nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Ni ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa wala mli ni etutuaa aduawai eŋɔli be fɛɛ be ni hulutsoo be lɛ baaya hiɛ.

english: Do I still need to care for my mango trees during the months when they are not producing any fruits?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makwɛ mi-mango tso lɛ nɔ lolo yɛ nyɔji ni ewooo yibii lɛ amli?

english: Yes, pruning dead branches and clearing fallen leaves during the off-season removes the hiding places of diseases, ensuring your trees stay clean for the next harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei niji ni egboi lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni ajieɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ baaye abua ni ajie he fɛɛ he ni helai kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ, ni ebaaha otsei lɛ ahe atse kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Planting too early during light rains can cause seeds to dry up if a dry spell follows, while planting too late misses peak moisture. You should plant right after the soil receives a deep, soaking rain that thoroughly wets the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ Baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ ba. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni aduɔ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Esa akɛ odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni naa wa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What does it mean when someone tells me a maize seed variety takes three months to grow?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni mɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui heɔ nyɔji etɛ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: It means that from the exact day you put the seed into moist soil, the plant needs about 90 days of growth to complete its life cycle, form cobs, and be ready for harvest.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɛjɛ gbi ni odu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni tsei adara aaafee gbii 90 dani amɛgbe amɛwala be lɛ naa, amɛfee ŋmeii, ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How can I tell if my field is properly prepared and ready for planting maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ asaa he ni miyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Your land is ready when the soil has been cleared of thick weeds, loosened enough for seed roots to push through easily, and holds enough moisture to help seeds sprout within a week.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛji ajie jwɛi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ. Gbalamɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ abote mli mlɛo. Ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ otsi kome mli lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to save water and protect themselves from extreme heat. It reduces the leaf surface exposed to the sun so the plant loses less moisture.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni amɛkɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la ni baa baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu fioo.

english: How many days after planting should I expect to see my young maize plants coming out of the dirt?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu nii lɛ? Ani esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mana ŋmãa bibii ni miijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When there is good soil moisture and warm weather, healthy maize seeds will sprout and show green leaves above the ground between 4 to 7 days after planting.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kpakpa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ. Abele dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaaná baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 7 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers emphasize counting thirty-day intervals after planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa gbii nyɔŋmai etɛ ni aduɔ sɛɛ lɛ akanemɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Counting days helps you track key growth stages of the plant. At 30 days (one month), crops undergo a major growth spike, making it the ideal time for crucial tasks like top-dress fertilizing and weeding.
ga: Gbii ni akaneɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ tso lɛ dalɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ. Yɛ gbii 30 (nyɔŋ kome) sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ oya. Enɛ haa efeɔ be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nitsumɔi ni he hiaa tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young crop turn pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen nutrients in the soil or the ground is flooded with water, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii.

english: How can I tell whether my crop is struggling because of heat or because pests are attacking it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigba enaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ hewɔ loo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai miitutua lɛ?

english: Drought or heat stress causes whole rows of plants to wilt or curl evenly, whereas pest damage usually shows as visible holes, chewed leaf edges, or discoloration on specific plants.
ga: Hɔmɔ loo dɔlɛ he haomɔ haa tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛkpɛɔ amɛhe pɛpɛɛpɛ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo akɛ buji ni anaa. baai ni ashɛreɔ loo su ni tsakeɔ yɛ tsei komɛi anɔ

english: Why is it important to remove weeds within the first month after my crops sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: In the first month, young crop roots are weak and small. Weeds grow faster and will steal the soil's water, sunlight, and nutrients, which can permanently stunt your crop's final yield.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbaafee bibii. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha naagbee ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ afite kwraa.

english: What happens if I leave my mature maize in the field for a few weeks after it is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmãa ni eda lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli otsii fioo komɛi beni eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving mature maize in the field exposes the cobs to insect attacks like weevils, mold from unexpected rains, and damage from birds or rodents, which reduces both the quantity and quality of your grain.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni eda lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ mli baa lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ. kɛ nɔ ni okpoi loo ŋmeii fiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ayibɔ kɛ amɛhe ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow when there is heavy rainfall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ waa gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Too much water fills the air spaces in the soil, preventing root respiration and washing away essential nutrients like nitrogen that keep leaves green.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why does cassava manage to stay green and grow even during dry periods when other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli po beni tsei krokomɛi gboi lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep root systems that store water and nutrients underground, allowing it to survive long dry spells better than crops with shallow roots.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ.

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to absorb moisture before the hot sun evaporates it, giving plants the water they need for daytime growth.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa tsei lɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara yɛ gbi mli.

english: Why should I not plant my crop seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants with smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛshiɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb up instead of growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji ni ekwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb to expose more leaves to sunlight, which enables the plant to produce more energy and grow bigger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo. ni oha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their flowers without producing any fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High temperatures cause heat stress, leading the pepper plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy and survive rather than setting fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help improve my farm's soil for the next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have natural bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a free natural fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ baamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ehe lɛ

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster and stronger than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally hardy wild plants adapted to aggressively absorb water, nutrients, and sunlight faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why do insects seem to damage my crops more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During dry seasons, green farm crops are the primary source of moisture and food available, so pests congregate heavily on the few green crops left.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ji nɔ titri ni haa hulutsoo kɛ niyenii baa. No hewɔ lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa waa yɛ tsei fioo ni eshwɛ ni ji eŋɔli lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts are fully ready for harvest underground without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi kpamɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Groundnuts are mature when the leaves turn yellow and begin to shed, and the inside linings of harvested seed pods turn a dark brown color.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ mligbɛ fã lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an important nutrient in the soil. When soil runs low on nitrogen, maize cannot make enough green food for itself, so applying compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen faaa lɛ Abɛi nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that feed on nitrogen from the air and trap it in the dirt. When the plant finishes growing, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil and feeds whatever crop you plant there next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbe ekwɛ̃ naa Nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and high heat. They need temporary shade trees, like plantain or cassava, planted next to them to keep them cool and hold moisture in the air until they grow strong.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Ehe miihia ni amɛdu tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains loo yucca, ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛhe baajɔ amɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread dry fertilizer right before a heavy downpour of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away the topsoil along with the fertilizer before your plants' roots get a chance to drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist or during light rain so it dissolves directly into the root area.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does cassava stay green and alive during long dry seasons when other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli beni tsei krokomɛi gboi lɛ?

english: Cassava stores extra food and water deep underground in its large tubers and can drop its leaves to save water when weather gets hot, allowing it to survive tough droughts.
ga: Cassava kɛ niyenii kɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii agboi amli. Ni obaanyɛ oshɛrɛ baai oshwie koni okɛbu nu he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ. Ye obua lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: When temperatures get too high or the soil gets too dry, tomato plants get stressed and drop their flowers to save energy for survival rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: If too many small shoots grow at the base of a plantain tree, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Removing extra shoots leaves enough energy for the main stem to produce big, healthy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ lɛ Dalɛ babaoo yɛ plantain lɛ shishi. Nakai ŋmeii lɛ hu baatswa niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Yam vines need their leaves spread out high off the damp ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to grow big underground tubers and stay safe from soil rots.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ biɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛdu shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ lɛ he

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into small balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee bɔɔlu bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices out of the undersides of the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce small, weak yields if I leave them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ wooo yibii ni egbɔjɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the valuable water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops need to grow, effectively starving your plants and reducing the food they can make.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni niyenii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is even ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani abele lɛ po feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil has run out of nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the season keeps the leaves green so they can feed the growing cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa lɛ adara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ baa eŋɔli ni ekɛye ŋmãa ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and living organisms that make your soil naturally fertile. Clearing weeds and letting them rot back into the ground acts like free manure for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Jwɛi ni ooogbe ni oha amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote sũ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas in the same field with my maize help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots pull natural nitrogen out of the air and put it into the ground. This extra nitrogen stays in the soil to nourish your maize plants without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmãa kroko kɛfata he.

english: How do I stop my cassava roots from rotting in the ground when heavy rains start?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them in heavy soil. Planting your cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bote shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn dry during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling happens when tomato plants lose water faster than their roots can drink it from the hot soil. Placing dry grass around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and holds moisture longer.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ nu fite oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Hay ni akɛbaabɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when there is strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that cannot hold heavy fruiting stems in loose soil. Piling fresh dirt around the base of the plant as it grows helps anchor the roots firmly in the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ hee ni okɛtoɔ he lɛ Tso lɛ shishi be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by too much heat or lack of shade. Maintaining medium shade trees keeps the farm cool and protects the tiny insects needed to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo ebɛ hulutsoo. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be ni sa lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe. ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔii ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their leaves right after they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baa lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ebɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Leaf drop is usually caused by sudden dry spells or attacks by tiny pests like mites. Keeping your watering consistent and checking under leaves for insects helps the plant hold its leaves and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ baa. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ daa ni okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji kooloi yɛ mli lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ baai lɛ amli ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my yam vines grow very long with many leaves, but the tubers underground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough shade control, the yam plant spends all its energy making leaves instead of tubers. Staking the vines tall and using balanced nutrients encourages energy to flow down into the tuber.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni ebɛ shade ni fa bɔ ni sa Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ wain tso lɛ wo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ni okɛ niyenii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo hewalɛ hewalɛ ni eho kɛya bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and shriveling while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, dark farms. Pruning extra branches lets sunlight in and removing affected pods early keeps the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni edɔ mli lɛ amli. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fataa he koni hulu la babaoo abote mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni ena naagbai lɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the big trees away from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the surrounding soil. Leaving mature shade trees or planting plantains provides a shelter that protects the young cocoa from extreme heat until it matures.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu dumɔwui lɛ, ehaa enáa he ko ni buɔ kooloo tso bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ latsaa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ shweremɔ he.

english: Why should I plant my plantain suckers at the start of the rainy season instead of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli moŋ fe nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need constant moisture to establish strong underground roots. Planting at the beginning of the rains ensures the plant gets water daily to build roots before the dry season comes.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni wa. Nugbɔ ni duɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ nu daa gbi koni amɛwo shishifãi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant turn green and grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni ŋmeii lɛ waa.

english: Is it true that planting groundnuts in my field helps my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, groundnuts and other legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil nutrients through their roots, naturally enriching the ground for future crops like maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi. Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Curled and patchy leaves on cassava are caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried from plant to plant by small insects called whiteflies that feed on the sap.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe yɛ ŋmei nɔ ni ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛbaa. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ, ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil lacks water, or when the plant does not receive enough nutrients to support heavy fruit growth.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai babaoo ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll inward during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense against heat; by curling up, the leaf exposes less area to the sun, which keeps moisture trapped inside the plant during hot weather.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Curling baaha baai lɛ aná hulu la fioo. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and choke my crops when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? He ni tso lɛ yɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally have aggressive roots that steal water, light, and nutrients faster than young crops. Clearing them early prevents them from taking all the soil food away from your growing crops.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei bibii. Kpeemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkajie sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛ otsei ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, or when tiny pests called nematodes pierce the tuber, allowing damp soil fungi to enter and decay the yam.
ga: Tubers lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli. aloo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii Atsɛɔ amɛ tuber-bore nematodes. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa egboɔ.

english: How does burning the bushes on my farmland affect the soil before planting?
ga: Te jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ashãa lɛ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ he dani aduɔ nii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Burning clears the land fast and provides quick ash nutrients, but it destroys beneficial soil organisms, burns away organic compost, and dries out the soil structure over time.
ga: Shãa oya haa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Shi ebaakpãtã shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ. Shãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does my harvested cassava start to turn dark and spoil within just two days of pulling it out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ bɔi duŋ ni efite yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli beni mijie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain living tissue after harvest and react rapidly to oxygen once detached from the plant. This causes a natural chemical breakdown called vascular streak, which spoils the root unless it is processed, dried, or cooked right away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi akɛ fãji ni hiɛ ka yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii oya kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni fiteɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ atherosclerosis lɛ baa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ja atsu he nii, agbi, loo ahoo amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa beans need to be covered with plantain leaves and left in heaps for several days before I dry them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ plantain baai aha mi-kokoo yibii lɛ ahe ni ashi amɛ yɛ ŋtayaa mli gbii babaoo dani mikɛgbi lɛ?

english: Fresh cocoa beans undergo a natural fermentation process when wrapped under leaves. This process stops the bean from germinating, breaks down bitter compounds, and develops the essential chocolate flavor and rich color that buyers require.
ga: Cocoa yibii heei tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ko mli kɛ́ akɛwo baai shishi. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ. Efoɔ nibii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli ni ehaa tsokolate ni he hiaa lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ su ni mli wa ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize thoroughly in the sun before storing it or taking it to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛto loo mikɛwo jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize grains contain moisture that allows destructive fungi, mold, and insects to multiply rapidly. Sun-drying reduces moisture levels, causing the grain to harden and preventing spoilage during storage and transit.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni haa ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ feɔ babaoo oya lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni akpa ehee lɛ amli. Hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. Ehaa ŋmaa lɛ mli waɔ ni ehaaa efite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking crushed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni etamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually a defense reaction caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. As these insects feed on the undersides of young leaves, the uneven leaf growth causes them to curl and distort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies kɛbaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi. Baai ni kwɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ baaha amɛkpãtã ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems without forming any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes the pollen inside tomato flowers to become sticky or sterile, preventing proper fertilization. When a flower is not fertilized, the plant naturally drops the bloom to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ehiɛɛɛ fɔmɔ nii. Enɛ haaa aná fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi ko fɔ Tsei lɛ baafɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start growing green shoots even when I keep them inside a dark barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli moŋ.

english: Yam tubers enter a natural dormancy period after harvest, but as temperature and humidity change, internal hormones signal the end of dormancy. The tuber then uses its stored starch and water to push out new growth in preparation for a new season.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ boteɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ latsaa tsake lɛ, Endogenous hormones lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ wɔɔhe lɛ eba naagbee. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii kɛ nu ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛtsi ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ kɛje kpo kɛsaa amɛhe kɛha be hee lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leafy green branches but fail to produce pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ niji babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ ewo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: If cowpea plants receive too much nitrogen from enriched soil, they prioritize vegetative growth—producing leaves and stem vines—rather than shifting energy toward producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cowpea tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ, tamɔ baai kɛ wain tsei ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a jeɔ he wami ɔ kɛ yaa fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi a peemi mi.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow while the upper leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Because nitrogen moves easily within the plant, the maize draws this essential nutrient from its older bottom leaves to feed its rapidly growing top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nitrogen lɛ nyiɛɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli oya. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa gbalaa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida oya lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my plantain plant produce so many small suckers at the base, and should I leave them all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Lots at the base Ni ani esa akɛ mashi fɛɛ?

english: Plantain plants naturally produce shoots called suckers to propagate. However, if too many suckers are left to grow together, they compete with the parent plant for nutrients and sunlight, resulting in small, light bunches of fruit.
ga: Plantains woɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛfɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, Amɛkɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ hulu la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ daraaa ni etsiii.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work naturally with beneficial soil bacteria to absorb nitrogen gas from the air and store it in root nodules. When the plant dies, this nitrogen breaks down into the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛjie nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ fiteɔ kɛboteɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to grow strong green leaves, or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients out of the soil.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot and dry, or when there is too little water in the soil, which prevents the flower from completing its natural process of making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ atsu ebɔɔ su yibiiwoo nitsumɔ lɛ he nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants stay thin and small when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no plant with enough energy to build big tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náaa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee bulb agbo.

english: Why do I see holes eaten into my cabbage leaves when I cannot find any insects on them during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu ni ayeɔ yɛ kaabe baa mli lɛ? Be mli ni anaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Many crop-eating pests, like armyworms and caterpillars, hide under the soil or deep inside the leaves during the hot day and only come out to feed at night when it is cool.
ga: Nɔ ni fata kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ahe ji armyworms kɛ ŋmeii. Ehiɛɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo yɛ baai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbatao niyenii gbɛkɛ pɛ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop in the hot afternoon but look fresh again early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi lɛ?

english: Plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink during hot afternoons. Drooping is the plant's natural defense to reduce surface area and save water until the air cools down.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Drooping ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛbu nu he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do crops grow faster with store-bought chemical fertilizer than with regular animal manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shwapo mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ tsu nii fe kooloi ashishifãi ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are like fast food that gives crops quick, concentrated nutrients right away, whereas animal manure breaks down slowly over time to feed the plant and improve the soil gradually.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tamɔ niyenii ni ayeɔ oya ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii amli hewalɛ ni mli wa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kooloi ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛha tsei niyenii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ fiofio.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally built to survive tough conditions, so their roots absorb water and plant food from the soil much faster than cultivated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni adebɔɔ fee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee.

english: Why did the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout when I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can die if they are stored in warm or damp places, or if tiny insects ate the living part hidden inside the seed while it was in storage.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ agbo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii Yeɔ wala yibii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the tubers of my yam plants rot in the ground when heavy rain sits on the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like humans do. Waterlogged soil drowns roots by blocking oxygen, which causes them to die and allows harmful rot organisms in the mud to decay the yams.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. ni haa amɛgboiɔ ni ehaa nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ oshara ni yɔɔ muji lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How often should I go to check on my farm during the growing season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Visiting your farm regularly, at least two to three times a week, helps you catch pest invasions, leaf diseases, or water issues early before they destroy your entire crop.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, shii fioo komɛi yɛ otsi mli ni oooyasara oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua bo ni oyoo tsɛŋemɔ helai, tsei amli helai, loo nu he naagbai mra. Dani ebaakpãtã onibii fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I stop visiting and working on my farm for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikpa saramɔ kɛ nitsumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi?

english: When a farm is neglected, weeds quickly grow and steal light, water, and nutrients from your crops, while unmonitored pests and diseases can spread unchecked and ruin your yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aku hiɛ ashwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell if wild animals or pests are coming onto my farm at night?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji koo mli kooloi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui miiba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ?

english: You can detect pests or animals by checking your farm early in the morning for chewed leaves, trampled stems, droppings, or footprints left in the soft soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona tsɛŋemɔ helai loo kooloi kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oookwɛ leebi koni ona baai ni ashɛre lɛ nɔ. Tsoi ni atswa, kooloi afɔfɔi, loo naji ahe nibii ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I see certain insects and animals on my farm at the exact same time every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi komɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Many pests follow seasonal weather patterns, appearing when rain creates young, tender leaves or during dry spells when they move to crop fields searching for water and food.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo nyiɛɔ be mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi asɛɛ. Ejeɔ kpo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ, ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe feɔ blɛoo. loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni amɛfãa kɛyaa ŋmɔji amli koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Is it safe to keep farm animals like goats or sheep near my crop field?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahã ŋmɔ mli kooloi, tamɔ tooi loo tooi ahi miŋmɔji ni miduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Raising animals near your field provides valuable manure for crop nutrients, but you must fence your farm properly so the animals do not eat or trample your crops.
ga: Koolooi ni oookwɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ oŋmɔji lɛ baaha oná ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei lɛ amli niyenii. Shi esa akɛ okɛ gbogbo awo oŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni kooloi akaye loo amɛkanyiɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I inspect my plants carefully to identify a pest before buying chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ mitsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ koni mana nɔ ni yeɔ amɛ awui dani mahe tsofai?

english: Different pests and diseases require specific treatments; identifying the exact issue first prevents you from wasting money on the wrong chemical that could harm your crops.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai Ehe miihia ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ oyɔse naagba lɛ diɛŋtsɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaatsi bo gbɛ koni okafite shika yɛ tsofai ni ejaaa ni baanyɛ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and wilting like they are sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are a common sign of crop distress caused by plant diseases, lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or poor watering.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe naagbai ni tsei ahelai kɛbaa lɛ ahe. Nibii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes dark spots to appear on the leaves of my plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: Dark spots on leaves are usually fungal or bacterial diseases that develop when plants stay wet for too long or when there is high humidity in the air.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ loo hela ko ni baa kɛji tsei lɛ hi shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I protect leafy green vegetables from pests without making the leaves unsafe for my family to eat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-green lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe? Ni mikɛ baai lɛ efeee nɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha miweku lɛ ni amɛye?

english: You can use natural protection like neem leaf extracts, wood ash, or manual pest removal to control leaf-eating insects safely without relying on harmful chemicals.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu tamɔ neem baa mli nu, tso sũ, loo DIY tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nibii atsu nii. Koni akudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ shweshweeshwe ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my plant's poor growth is caused by soil problem or a crop disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ naagba loo tso hela hewɔ ni mitso lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soil nutrient problems usually affect entire rows of plants evenly with light green or yellow leaves, while crop diseases often start on individual plants with spots, mold, or unusual leaf shapes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he naagbai saa tsei akuu muu lɛ fɛɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Eko fɛɛ eko yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo baai lɛ ahe mfoniri ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil around their small roots. Keeping some big shade trees or planting plantains next to them protects the cocoa from harsh heat and keeps the ground moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe lɛ agbi. Ha tsei wuji lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ baabu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Plantain trees have roots that grow shallow near the top of the soil, making them top-heavy when they carry a large bunch of fruit. Mounding soil deep around the base and supporting heavy bunches with bamboo poles prevents wind from pushing them over.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ́ amɛmiiwo aduawai akui wuji. Okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ abɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he shɔŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmeii afi tsei niji ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa amɛnɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or compost early in the season restores their health and increases crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rain floods my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water sits in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots and attracting fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight, which the leaves turn into food to grow big tubers underground. Staking also lifts the leaves off wet soil, preventing fungal diseases from spreading.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Baai lɛ bafeɔ niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains all the specific nutrients maize needs and gives soil pests a permanent place to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea restores nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ babaoo kɛya naanɔ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and growing tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat stress. Spraying neem oil to control whiteflies and providing steady water helps keep tomato leaves normal and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛɔ haomɔ ni jɛɔ la ni naa wa mli baa lɛ mli Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ koni akɛkudɔ whiteflies lɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tomato baai lɛ feɔ nɔ ni sa ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from high temperature stress, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer which pushes leaf growth instead of fruit growth. Regular watering and balanced fertilizer encourage flowers to turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni tsirɛɔ baai lɛ koni amɛdara yɛ aduawai lɛ najiaŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil water, and fertilizer nutrients. Clearing weeds early in the planting season ensures your crops get all the food and water they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, sũ mli nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwereɔ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away into gutters and streams before the plant roots have time to drink it. Applying fertilizer when the soil is slightly damp—but not right before heavy rain—ensures the crop actually absorbs the food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo—shi jeee dani nugbɔ ni naa wa baanɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ—baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa seedlings the shade and soil moisture they need during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can capture direct sunlight to make energy for tuber growth. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also reduces the risk of fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulb lɛ dalɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Pale yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or waterlogged roots that cannot absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas or beans in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting beans or cowpeas alongside maize improves the soil because legumes naturally capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, feeding the maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛye ŋmãa.

english: Why is it risky to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that crop to build up in large numbers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa babaoo.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the plant sap, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when soil moisture fluctuates sharply, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like calcium during the flowering phase.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ oya loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium bɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why do some of my tiny cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mine lɛ tsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi lɛ. Ni kookoo ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ lolo?

english: Small cocoa pods shrivel either due to cherelle wilt, where the tree naturally sheds pods it cannot support, or due to black pod disease caused by excessive moisture and fungi.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ cherel ni shwieɔ lɛ hewɔ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ eshishifãi ni enyɛŋ eye ebua lɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. aloo yɛ black pod hela ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ

english: Why should I construct soil ridges across a slope instead of planting straight down the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu gɔŋ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ

english: Building ridges across a slope slows down rainwater runoff, preventing topsoil and fertilizer from washing away down the hill during heavy rains.
ga: Kɛ́ afee ŋshɔkei ni tsɔɔ ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkaho kɛjɛ gɔji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Can I still get a good yield if my farm size is only half an acre?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná yibiiwoo kpakpa lolo kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ ji acre fã pɛ?

english: Yes, even a small plot of 0.5 acres can produce a profitable harvest if you practice proper crop spacing, use high-quality seeds, and maintain good soil fertility through composting or fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni dalɛ ji acre 0.5 po baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛji okɛ otsei lɛ to he ko jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ atsu nii Ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooofee lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it good to join two or three small pieces of land together to grow one type of crop?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafee shikpɔji bibii ni akɛfee ekome? Parcel enyɔ loo etɛ ni akɛfee ekome koni akɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii kome?

english: Combining adjacent small plots helps you manage inputs like seeds and fertilizer more efficiently, though you must ensure the soil fertility across all pieces is treated equally so the crops mature at the same time.
ga: aggregation of small plots Adjacent lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni akwɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ amli lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ moŋ. koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ be kome too mli

english: Why do some crops require manual harvesting with hands or cutlasses instead of machines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ niji loo dade kpalaa ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ tsɔne najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Crops like cocoa, cassava, or delicate fresh vegetables grow in ways that machines can easily damage. Hand harvesting allows you to select only mature fruits and harvest roots without bruising them.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo, ŋmei loo aduawai heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni tsɔnei baanyɛ afite amɛ oya nɔ. Nine ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ pɛ ni okpaa shishifãi lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔlɔ etswaaa.

english: How can I tell if a crop will demand too much labor before I commit to planting it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ko heɔ nitsumɔ babaoo tsɔ dani madu?

english: Evaluate the harvesting and weeding requirements of the crop. Crops that need constant hand-picking or heavy manual digging require high labor; if you work alone and cannot hire farm labor, lower-maintenance crops may be better.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ he nibii ni he hiaa lɛ mli. Tsei ni biɔ ni akɛ niji atsu nii daa loo akɛ niji atsa shi waa lɛ heɔ nitsumɔ babaoo. Kɛji okome too otsuɔ nii ni onyɛɛɛ otsu ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ he nii lɛ Ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Which food crops are easiest for a single farmer to harvest without extra help?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni okwaafonyo kome pɛ baanyɛ akpa ni yelikɛbuamɔ kroko fataaa he?

english: Grains like maize or pulses like cowpea are generally easier for one person to harvest gradually compared to crops like cassava or fresh tomatoes, which require intensive digging or quick picking before spoilage.
ga: Nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa bei pii lɛ fiofio Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ mɔ kome baakpa kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo tomato hee he. Enɛ biɔ ni atsa shi waa loo ajie oya dani efite.

english: Why do young cocoa trees turn yellow and wither when exposed to full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate intense heat. They need temporary shade plants like plantains to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up in the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves during peak heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and preserve moisture; they usually recover when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ dɔlɛ be mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni eha fɛ̃i ahi shi. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why does my maize grow slowly when I plant it right next to cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants have large leaves and aggressive root systems that steal light, water, and soil nutrients from neighboring maize, causing the maize to grow poorly.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ yɛ baai wuji kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmãa lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do groundnut flowers blossom above the ground but the nuts grow under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Once the groundnut flower is pollinated, the plant grows a long stem called a peg that pushes itself downward into the soil, where the nut pod can safely expand underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ shwere lɛ Tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bean pods lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do cassava roots start rotting if heavy rain stays on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil starves cassava roots of air, causing the tubers to suffocate and allowing soil fungi to quickly rot the crop before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akashɛ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akpaa.

english: Leaves yellowing from the bottom up is a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need for green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure feeds the plant so it can stay green and produce big ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛha baai eŋɔli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha tsei lɛ aná niyenii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛ toi wuji.

english: Covering soil with dry plant leaves—called mulching—acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground during hot days, keeps the soil cool, and stops weeds from growing and stealing food from your crops.
ga: Mulching kɛ tso baai ni egbi (Atsɛɔ enɛ mulching.) Etsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and pull it into the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps the maize grow stronger without you having to buy as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni egbalaa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli babaoo.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and sticky dirt in the middle of the stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu kɛ muji ni shwieɔ shi lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by a caterpillar called the Fall Armyworm, which eats deep inside the heart of the maize plant. Spraying safe bio-pesticides or putting clean wood ash inside the plant's funnel early in the morning kills the pest before it destroys your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ji ŋmei ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ nii kɛyaa ŋmei tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie shi loo okɛ tso sũ ni he tse fata tsei lɛ ahe leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and making the branches look stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni ehaa eniji lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling happens when tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feed on the leaves and spread a plant virus. Removing infected plants quickly and spraying mild soapy water or neem oil helps stop the insects from spreading it to healthy peppers.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni akɛ samla ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their tiny flowers before they turn into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani ebaatsɔ pod ni eyi obɔ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry spells, poor soil, or insect attacks, as a way to save energy. Providing shade trees, protecting the farm from capsid insects, and maintaining moist soil helps the tree keep its flowers and yield heavy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji hɔmɔ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo kooloi tutuamɔ hao amɛ. Bɔni afee ni akafite hewalɛ lɛ, hulutsoo ni akɛhaa lɛ buɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ capsid kooloi ahe. Ni kɛ́ tso lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food and grow large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread, and spreads the leaves out to catch as much sunlight as possible.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Ni okɛ baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni onine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ bɔ ni ooonyɛ.

english: Black rotted bottoms—known as blossom-end rot—happen when the plant cannot draw up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering. Watering your tomatoes steadily so the soil stays evenly moist prevents this rot from forming.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji diŋ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ blossom end rot Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Okɛ nu awo otomatoi lɛ amli daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni amɛkafite.

english: How do I know when it is safe to sow my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until your land receives at least two or three heavy rains that thoroughly wet the soil. Planting in dry soil after just one small shower can cause seeds to sprout and then die if dry heat returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baashɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji latsaa ni egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up for market?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ aya jara nɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open as the tubers swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmei lɛ mli shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: How long does it typically take for cassava to grow before I can harvest it?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ, ŋmei fɔɔ shweremɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Most improved cassava varieties in Ghana take between 9 to 12 months to fully mature, though some early-maturing varieties can be harvested as early as 6 months after planting.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ akpa ŋmei henɔi komɛi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ nyɔji 6 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ moŋ.

english: How do I know when my yams are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam plants show maturity when the leaves turn yellow and the vines dry up, which usually happens around 6 to 9 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wain tso lɛ gĩɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa aaafee nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 9 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ
