english: Can a plantain sucker really produce a full bunch of fruit within one year?
ga: Ani banana tsei lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli?

english: Yes, with good soil fertility and sufficient water, a plantain sucker will flower within 8 to 10 months and produce a mature bunch ready for harvest by 12 months.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni baa nii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Sucker dumɔwui lɛ baawo fɔfɔi yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 10 mli ni amɛbaadara ni abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 12 mli.

english: Is it true that I can harvest sweet potatoes in less than six months?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ manyɛ makpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ ni shɛɛɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli?

english: Yes, sweet potatoes are fast-growing root crops that are typically ready for harvest in just 3 to 4 months after planting the vines.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni shwereɔ oya ni bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ sɛɛ beni adu wain tso lɛ, efeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Which crops can I plant if I need to harvest and sell within three months?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ makwɛ kɛji ehe bahia ni akpa ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli?

english: Fast-maturing crops like cowpeas, tomatoes, leafy vegetables, and short-duration maize varieties can all be harvested within 60 to 90 days.
ga: Abaanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ tsina ŋmei, tomato, aduawai ni baa yɔɔ mli, kɛ ŋmãa ni shwereɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 mli.

english: How soon after transplanting should I expect my pepper plants to start giving fruit?
ga: Beni mikɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ adu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Pepper plants usually start flowering around 60 days after transplanting, and you can begin picking the first harvest within 2 to 3 weeks after flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi aaafee gbii 60 sɛɛ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ. Ni obaanyɛ oje klɛŋklɛŋ aduawai lɛ anaabuamɔ shishi yɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni fɔfɔi lɛ ewo lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How many years after planting will my hybrid cocoa trees start bearing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni mi hybrid cocoa tso lɛ baaje shishi ewo ŋmeii?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties start flowering and producing pods within 2 to 3 years, unlike traditional varieties that take up to 5 years.
ga: Kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni esoro no kwraa yɛ blema kookoo henɔi ni heɔ afii enumɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my pawpaw tree produce fruit within a year while my mango tree takes much longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya tso lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi mango tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo lɛ?

english: Pawpaw is a fast-maturing herbaceous plant that fruits in 8 to 12 months, whereas mangoes are large woody trees that require 3 to 5 years to build strong branches before supporting fruit.
ga: Pawpaw ji jwɛi tso ko ni daa oya ni ewoɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli, yɛ be mli ni mango ji tso agbo ko ni yeɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani efeɔ niji ni mli wa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my maize plants already flowering when they are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miikwɛ momo lɛ? Ani no ji kuku kwraa lolo?

english: Maize plants flower early or stay short when they experience stress, such as dry spells or poor soil nutrients, which forces the plant to reproduce early to survive.
ga: Abɛi fɔɔ mra loo ehiɛɛɛ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛji akɛ haomɔ, tamɔ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛfɔ oya bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do some of my crops produce plenty of flowers but no fruits develop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fail to turn into fruit mainly due to a lack of water, missing soil nutrients, extreme heat, or a lack of insects like bees to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee aduawai, titri lɛ yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops produce small ears on my land, but grow very large on my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ toi bibii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ni eda waa yɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Different soil types have different nutrients. If your soil lacks essential food like nitrogen, even good seeds cannot express their full potential and will give poor yields until you improve the soil.
ga: Sũ henɔ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ yɛ niyenii mli nibii sɔrɔtoi. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Dumɔwui kpakpai po nyɛŋ ajie amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kpo ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo ja otsake shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some cassava varieties suffer from leaf disease while improved varieties nearby remain healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi yeɔ foli helai yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni bɛŋkɛ ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Certain crop varieties carry natural internal defenses against diseases. Improved cassava breeds are developed to resist viruses, whereas vulnerable local varieties get easily overwhelmed and fail.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ helai ahe. Afee ŋmei henɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛte shi ewo hela nɛɛ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa henɔi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ nɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ omanye.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my hybrid maize harvest give me weak plants when I replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛji midu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds only keep their strong, high-yielding traits for one generation. The seeds saved from that harvest lose those good characteristics, resulting in weak plants and tiny yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ hiɛɔ amɛ su ni wa, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ yinɔ kome pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nikpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui kpakpai lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Will planting cassava closely together with my pepper plants harm the peppers?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni mikɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ duɔ lɛ baaye pepper lɛ awui?

english: Cassava has strong, aggressive roots and broad foliage that steals light, water, and nutrients from shorter crops. This aggressive growth will starve and shade out your peppers.
ga: Yucca yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni feɔ basabasa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni juɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei kukuji amli. Nɛkɛ shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ waa nɛɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye o-peppers lɛ ni amɛgboi.

english: If I plant my yam mounds very close together, will I harvest more yams from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmeii ni abua naa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani makpa ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight each other underground for space and food. This competition causes the plant to produce many tiny, poor-quality tubers instead of large ones.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko kɛ niyenii. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ ha nitsumɔhei fee ŋmeii bibii ni jara waaa babaoo yɛ ŋmeii wuji najiaŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my young crop seedlings after the rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe dumɔwui bibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds naturally adapt quickly to grab water and soil nutrients before young farm crops can. You must clear weeds early so your crops do not get starved out.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani okwaayeli mli ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baanyɛ afee nakai. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra. koni hɔmɔ akaye onibii lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants react badly to intense heat and burn easily in full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and provide living shade umbrellas that protect cocoa seedlings until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ efeee nɔ ko jogbaŋŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛhaa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves turn yellow and drop off at the start of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their leaves as a survival reaction to save water during dry heat. Providing shade and keeping organic mulch around the base helps them hold moisture and stay green.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi akɛ nɔ ko ni amɛfeɔ koni amɛhi shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ́ aha amɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛshishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dying from soil sickness when I plant them in the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ hela mli beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ saatso kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Pathogens build up in the soil when the same crop is grown repeatedly. The soil retains these diseases from previous seasons, attacking new seedlings immediately unless you rotate with a different crop type.
ga: Helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baahiɛ helai nɛɛ kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui heei ni oootutua amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ Ja okɛ tsei srɔtoi krokomɛi tsake amɛhe.

english: Why should I cut off extra stems and side branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ amɛsɛɛ niji lɛ?

english: Tomato plants naturally send energy into growing excess leaves and stems instead of fruit. Cutting off extra branches forces the plant to direct all its food into growing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni amɛdaraa lɛ nɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni eye nii kwraa koni ekwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I still grow healthy food crops on farmland that was previously used for mining?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lolo yɛ okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtaoɔ shika tsuru lɛ nɔ?

english: Mined land usually loses its fertile topsoil and can contain harmful chemicals or heavy metals. Before planting food, the soil needs to be tested for toxins, treated, and rebuilt with organic manure and fresh soil to make it safe for crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni atsa lɛ nɔ sũ ni baa nii lɛ fiteɔ, ni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo dade ni tsii baanyɛ ahi mli. dani adu niyenii Esa akɛ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akwɛ kɛji eyɛ tsofai fɔji, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni afee lɛ ehee ekoŋŋ koni efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and dying even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen or the soil is too acidic or waterlogged. When soil nutrients are washed away or damaged, the plant cannot absorb food through its roots even if water is present.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi kɛ acid tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ho loo efite Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛŋɔ niyenii kɛji nu yɛ po.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing huge leafy stems above ground but producing tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ ni baai wuji yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or experiences unexpected heavy rainfall, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves instead of storing starch in its underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni akpaaa gbɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ starch baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep falling off before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, dry soil, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil moist with mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo fɔfɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tuber underground. Staking lifts the vines toward the sun and keeps the leaves off the wet ground where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning heavy tree branches lets sunlight and fresh air reach the pods, which stops the fungus from growing.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. niji ni tsii ni afoɔ Enɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why do armyworms suddenly attack my young maize field all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn ŋmɔji lɛ trukaa lɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay hundreds of eggs on tender green leaves during dry spells right after early rains. When the eggs hatch, caterpillars emerge together and eat the leaves rapidly unless controlled early.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ wɔji lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ oya. ja akudɔ lɛ oya

english: Why is it important to space my plantain suckers far apart rather than planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ agbala plantain tsei lɛ amli moŋ fe ni aaadu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that each plantain tree gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. When planted too close, the crops fight each other for food, resulting in small bunches.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛji adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa niyenii he akaŋ. Enɛ haa anáa kuu bibioo ko.

english: How can I prevent my topsoil from washing away into streams during heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ koni ekaho kɛya faai amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Planting cover crops like groundnuts or constructing soil ridges along the slopes reduces the speed of rainwater, trapping the rich topsoil and plant nutrients on your farm.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ loo shikpɔŋ ŋmeii ni afee yɛ gɔŋji lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ nu lɛ aya oya. Ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ.

english: How do traditional crop seeds slowly disappear from our local farming communities?
ga: Kusum tso dumɔwui lɛ ji fiofio Te efee tɛŋŋ elaaje kɛjɛ wɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli akutso lɛ mli?

english: When farmers switch completely to hybrid seeds or when extreme weather destroys native crops repeatedly, farmers stop saving local seeds, leading to the gradual loss of old crop varieties.
ga: Beni okwaafoi tsakeɔ kwraa kɛyaa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ anɔ loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa fiteɔ maŋ lɛ mli tsei lɛ shii abɔ lɛ. Okwaafoi lɛ baakpa dumɔwui ni amɛbua naa yɛ amɛmaŋ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni egbɔ lɛ miiho fiofio.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing nitrogen, a crucial nutrient they need to grow. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help the leaves turn green again and increase your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts before planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii dani midu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and leaves it in the soil. Planting them first enriches your farm naturally so your next maize crop grows better.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ odu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaagbe oŋmɔ lɛ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, o-maise ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water in your field, the roots drown from a lack of air and wet rot sets in, so building mounds or ridges helps water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni etse lɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko lɛ, ebaaye ebua nu lɛ ni eho kɛya.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes split open while they are still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miitswa be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they receive a sudden splash of water after a long dry period. The inside of the tomato expands faster than its skin can stretch, so maintaining regular, light watering during dry spells prevents splitting.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛji akɛ nu shwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni egbi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, nu fioo ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ baaye abua ni akafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my corn seeds failing to sprout after I put them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need water to activate their growth process. If you plant them in dry soil without rain or irrigation, the seeds stay asleep or dry out and die before they can push through the ground.
ga: Nu he hia dumɔwui koni ekanya amɛ dalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nugbɔ loo nu shwieee nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baawɔ loo amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to use wooden stakes to train my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso tso he hiaa mi koni mikɛtsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that feeds the growing tuber beneath the dirt. Staking lifts the leaves into the sun and keeps them off damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ ni ehaaa amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ji he ni helai shwereɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Plantains have shallow roots near the surface and heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. Supporting the main stem with a bamboo or wooden prop keeps the tree standing until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni aduawai akuu ko ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. make it top heavy Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei loo tsei fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting shade plants like plantain alongside young cocoa protects them from heat stress while they get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get too hot or don't get enough water. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the roots helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo ahaaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ sũ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so small even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than your crops can. Removing weeds early ensures all the nutrients you add go directly into feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni okɛfataa he lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Is it good to plant plantains on the same farm with my young cocoa plants?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ plantains yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, planting plantains with young cocoa is very helpful because the large plantain leaves provide shade to protect delicate young cocoa seedlings from the harsh sunlight while giving you food and income before the cocoa matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni akɛ dumɔwui duɔ lɛ he waa ejaakɛ plantain baai wuji lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa niyenii kɛ shika dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How do I know when my plantain bunch is ready to be harvested from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains are ready to harvest when the fingers become full and rounded, and the sharp ridges on the fruit start to smooth out. Harvest them while they are still deep green so they remain firm during transport to the market.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ niji lɛ eyi obɔ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ehaa Harvest feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo koni ehi shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my green plantains bruise and rot quickly after I carry them from the farm to the roadside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain eŋɔli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ oya beni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee gbɛjegbɛ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Plantain skin damages easily when bunches are thrown, dropped, or stacked directly on top of each other. The pressure breaks the peel tissues, which speeds up ripening and rot before the crop reaches the buyer.
ga: Plantain hewolo lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashɛrɛ ashwie tɛ̃ɛ, ashɛrɛ ashwie, loo abua naa yɛ kui amli. Nɔnyɛɛ lɛ gbáa ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli fãji lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ oya ni efiteɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: How can I stop my harvested green plantains from turning yellow too fast while waiting for trucks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-plantain eŋɔli ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya tsɔ beni mimɛɔ lɔle lɛ?

english: Keep your harvested plantain bunches in a cool, shaded shed out of direct sunlight. Do not keep them close to already ripe fruits, as ripe fruits release natural gases that cause green plantains to ripen much faster.
ga: Kɛ plantains ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulu la shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kaakɛto he ko ni bɛŋkɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ni ji gas lɛ kpo. Enɛ baaha plantains eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃ oya kwraa.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain trees turn yellow when water settles on my farm after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu gbee miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots cannot breathe when soil remains flooded for days. When the roots drown in standing water, they stop taking up nutrients, causing the plant leaves to turn yellow and growth to slow down.
ga: Plantain shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ bote nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ shishifãi lɛ baakpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rainstorms when they have big bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli eyɛ mli akɛ miyɛ jwɛi agbo lolo moŋ?

english: Plantain plants have very shallow root systems that do not dig deep into the ground. When a heavy fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for strong winds to pull the roots out unless you support the stem with a bamboo or wooden prop.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa ni eboteee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu agbo ko da Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ baagbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Ja okɛ ŋmei loo tso ko tsu nii kɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my plantain stems produce very small bunches while others give large bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ ekomɛi daa bibii waa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi haa tsei wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain stems produce small bunches when too many sucker shoots grow around one main stem. The suckers steal water and food from the mother plant, so you should prune away extra suckers to keep only one or two per plant.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii 1-2 pɛ ahi tso kome mli.

english: How do I choose the right plantain suckers to plant when starting a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni sa ni madu kɛji mije ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Select sword suckers, which have a broad base and thin, spear-like leaves. These suckers grow stronger, produce deep roots faster, and yield healthier bunches than water suckers that have broad leaves early on.
ga: Halamɔ klante tsei ni yɔɔ shishi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baafee nɔ ni wa. Shishifãi lɛ daa oya. ni amɛwoɔ aduawai akui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe ŋmeii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ mra.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain plants getting black spots and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Sigatoka, a fungal leaf disease that spreads rapidly in warm, humid weather. Cutting off heavily infected leaves and spacing your plants properly helps air circulate and keeps the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Black Sigatoka, ni ji fungal leaf hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afo baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ amli ni ashi tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ hela lɛ mli lɛ, ni ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: What causes holes and weakness at the bottom stem of my plantain plant near the ground?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu kɛ hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by plantain stem borers or weevils. Their grubs tunnel into the bulb base and weaken the plant, which can cause the stem to snap easily near the ground level.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei loo plantain ŋmeii. Eŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ bulb lɛ shishi ni amɛhaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ akumɔ oya yɛ he ni ebɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient in the soil. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer gives the maize the food it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the surrounding maize plants and keeps the soil rich.
ga: Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ niyenii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot survive sitting in stagnant water for too long because they need air to breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the roots safe from rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ ahi shi kɛji amɛtara nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛkɛmu. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry palm fronds or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Nibii ni akɛ ŋmei baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ewo mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material acts as a protective blanket. It keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating under the hot sun, and keeps the soil moist for your crops.
ga: Akɛ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs maximum daylight to manufacture food for its underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch full sunlight and stay free from rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkafite.

english: What will happen to my harvest if I plant my seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Giving each plant enough space allows it to grow full and yield a larger harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the plant and spreading diseases. Spraying neem oil or soapy water helps clear the pests so healthy leaves can sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden heatwaves or irregular watering. Providing consistent moisture at the base of the plant helps keep the flowers healthy so they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, tamɔ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ ha fɔfɔi lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa aahu akɛ amɛbatsɔmɔɔ tomato.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to produce much smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ awo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing weeds early ensures that your crops get all the nourishment they need to produce large, healthy yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop yields keep dropping every year when I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull specific nutrients from the soil to grow. When you plant the same crop in the exact same soil year after year without feeding the land manure or fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted, causing the crops to produce smaller harvests.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Kɛ́ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi fioo.

english: Why is it bad for my crops if I burn the dry bush on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mishã tsei ni egbi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter and beneficial soil organisms that feed your crops. It leaves the soil exposed to the hot sun and rain, which washes away topsoil nutrients needed for healthy plant roots.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ehi hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my old farmland is tired and needs a break before planting again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ momo lɛ etɔ ni ehe miihia ni majɔɔ mihe dani madu nii ekoŋŋ?

english: If your crops stay stunted, leaves turn pale, weeds like spear grass take over, or harvest amounts drop significantly despite good rains, the soil is telling you its nutrients are depleted and it needs rest or organic fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ, ni baai lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, jwɛi tamɔ spear grass lɛ yeɔ nɔ. aloo nikpamɔ lɛ falɛ baa shi waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ miikɛɛ bo akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ etã, ni ehe miihia ni ekɛ ehe ajɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli atsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. It can also happen when the soil is waterlogged and roots cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge leafy branches but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruits when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause heat stress, which prevents successful pollination inside the flower. Without pollination, the plant drops the flower to save its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ Tsei baajie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees grow better when I plant plantains right beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large broad leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist around the cocoa roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle kookoo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas together with my maize help my crops?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil food through their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them survive dry periods?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass—called mulching—acts like a blanket. It shades the soil from the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and keeps crop roots cool and moist.
ga: Hay ni aduɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and crowd out my main crops right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are wild, hardy, and sit dormant in the soil ready to germinate instantly at the first drop of rain. They naturally absorb nutrients and water faster than cultivated crops, which is why early clearing is critical.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ basabasa, amɛhe wa, ni amɛhiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ. Amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: If I plant maize and cassava together on the same land, won't one crop steal all the food from the other?
ga: Kɛ́ midu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, Ani tso kome ejuŋ niyenii fɛɛ kɛjɛ ekroko dɛŋ?

english: Maize grows quickly and feeds mostly near the surface of the soil, while cassava grows slower and roots deeper. Planting them together allows them to share space and light without fighting for the exact same nutrients at the same time.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni eyeɔ nii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Cassava daa blɛoo ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Hefatalɔi adumɔ haa tsei lɛ jaa he ko kɛ la ni amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves stay green during dry spells while the maize on the same plot turns brown and dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi.

english: Cassava roots go deep into the soil to reach underground moisture, making it resistant to drought. Maize has shallow roots and relies heavily on regular rainwater, so it dries out much faster when rains fail.
ga: Cassava shishifãi boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Ehaa enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni edamɔ nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, egbiɔ oya kwraa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Can I harvest quick food from my plot while waiting for a long-season crop like cassava to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpã niyenii ni ayeɔ oya kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni mimɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ ŋmei?

english: Yes, planting short-term crops like maize alongside cassava allows you to harvest maize in three to four months for immediate food, while the cassava slowly grows and matures over a full year.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa kɛha niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ baada fiofio ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ afi muu kome mli.

english: What is the main difference between using fertilizers and just farming naturally like my family has always done?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ okwaayeli yɛ adebɔɔ naa tamɔ bɔ ni miweku lɛ feɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ teŋ?

english: Traditional farming relies only on whatever nutrients are already in the soil, which slowly run out over time. Fertilizer directly adds essential plant foods like nitrogen and phosphorus to feed the crops for bigger harvests.
ga: Kusum okwaayeli damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ, ni fiofio lɛ, sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus fataa he tɛ̃ɛ. koni tsei lɛ aná yibii babaoo

english: Why do my crops grow much faster and greener when I apply fertilizer compared to when I don't?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe be mli ni mikɛwooo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer provides concentrated nutrients that act like a quick food boost for crops, helping them build strong stems and leafy green leaves much faster than unfertilized soil can support.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni mli wa ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ.

english: Will using chemical fertilizers spoil my soil over time compared to traditional methods?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ akɛto blema gbɛi ahe?

english: Fertilizers feed plants but do not build long-term soil structure. If used correctly with proper plant care, it raises yields, but using only chemical fertilizers without adding organic matter like manure can make soil hard and tired over time.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii shi etswaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsei akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ Ebaaha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ. Shi kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ tsu nii ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii fataaa he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa ni efite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What actually happens to my farm if I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up, leading to weaker crops and smaller harvests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shi, ni ŋmaa hu baa shi.

english: How does changing the type of crops I plant on my plot each season help my harvest?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ ni mitsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi yɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Different crops feed on different soil nutrients and attract different insects. Rotating crops lets the soil rest and rebuild missing nutrients naturally while breaking pest life cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yeɔ niyenii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛgbalaa kooloi srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ wala shihilɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency, meaning the crop is starving for the main nutrient it needs to build green leaves and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: How do legumes like beans help improve the growth of other crops planted after them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii haa tsei krokomɛi ni aduɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Beans and similar plants take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, that stored food remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant, like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ tsei ni tamɔ nakai lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Is it safe to spray my crops with chemicals when the fruits are already fully grown?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai baashwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji aduawai lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ pɛ?

english: Yes, but you must use specific approved chemicals designed for mature fruits and wait for the recommended 'pre-harvest interval' so the spray degrades and becomes safe before consumption.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ okɛ tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni afee aha aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ atsu nii ni omɛ ‘be ni akɛbaakpa nii’ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ dani tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ akumɔ ni efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe dani oye.

english: How do I know if a pesticide I spray on my fruits will make people sick when they eat them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ aduawai anɔ lɛ baaha mɛi aná hela kɛ́ amɛye?

english: Every approved pesticide has a safe waiting period written on its label; as long as you wait the correct number of days between spraying and harvesting, the chemical breaks down and the fruit becomes safe to eat.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be ni esa akɛ amɛmɛ ni aŋmala awo nɔ. Shii abɔ ni obaamɛ gbii ayibɔ ni sa ni ka shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ teŋ lɛ. Tsofai lɛ fiteɔ ni aduawai lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: Can I remove chemical sprays from my harvested fruit just by washing them with clean water?
ga: Ani manyɛ majie tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai ni akpa lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni mli tse ni mikɛbaafɔ he lɛ nɔ?

english: Washing removes chemical residues sitting on the outer skin, but it cannot remove chemicals that have been absorbed inside the fruit, which is why waiting the proper safe period before harvesting is essential.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ he lɛ, ebaajie tsofai fɛɛ ni eshwɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ. Shi enyɛŋ ejie tsofai ni shwieɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛ be ni sa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe dani akpa ŋmaa lɛ.

english: Will applying a higher amount of chemical protect my mature crops better and faster?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe jogbaŋŋ ni ebaatsu nii oya?

english: No, using more chemical than recommended can burn your crop, leave toxic chemical residues on your food, waste your money, and cause pests to become resistant to the treatment.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni fa fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ okɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã onibii. Tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni ashiɔ yɛ niyenii mli lɛ fiteɔ shika, ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsa amɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray chemical medicine on my fruit crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ mi tso yibii lɛ anɔ?

english: The best time is early morning or late afternoon when the sun is mild and winds are calm, preventing the heat from evaporating the chemical or the wind from blowing it away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu efee dioo, ni no haaa dɔlɛ akafee tsofai loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa amɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why do insects attack my fruits right when they are mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi yibii lɛ trukaa beni edara kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Mature fruits contain high amounts of natural sugars, moisture, and nutrients, making them an attractive and easy food source for insects and diseases just before harvest.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli sugars, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ aduawai ni edara lɛ amli. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha kooloi kɛ helai dani akpaa.

english: Why do some chemical sprays damage my plant leaves while trying to protect the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai komɛi ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ fiteɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ be mli ni mibɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni mibu aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plants can be damaged if you use the wrong type of chemical, spray during hot sunshine, or mix the wrong dosage, which burns the delicate plant tissues.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ afite kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni ejaaa tsu nii. Okɛshwie hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. loo akɛfutu mli yɛ bɔ ni esaaa mli Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right chemical spray to keep my ripe fruits from rotting on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ koni aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akafite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should show a sample of the damage to an extension officer to identify the exact disease or pest, then select a chemical registered specifically for that crop and problem.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nɔ ni efite lɛ he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ atsɔɔ extension official lɛ koni ena hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, halamɔ tsofa ko ni aŋmala awo wolo nɔ pɔtɛɛ kɛha nakai ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ naagba lɛ.

english: Why are my fruit trees dropping their fruits before they get fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso yibii lɛ miiho yibii dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fruits drop early due to heavy pest or disease attack, lack of adequate water, or poor soil nutrients that prevent the plant from supporting the heavy weight of growing fruits.
ga: Yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ahewɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Aloo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa kwraa bɔ ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ yibii ni miida lɛ ni tsii lɛ nɔ.

english: Are there safe ways to protect my mature fruits from pests without using chemical sprays?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni matsɔ nɔ mabu mi yibii ni miida lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, you can use insect traps, net bags around individual fruits, or natural biopesticides like neem oil extract to protect fruits without leaving harmful chemical residues.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ bug zapper atsu nii. Mesh kotokui abɔle aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he loo okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ atsu nii. Bɔni afee ni abu aduawai lɛ ahe ni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui akashi.

english: Can I grow plantain and cocoa together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantain kɛ cocoa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting plantain alongside young cocoa trees is very beneficial. The fast-growing plantains provide essential shade to shield delicate young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight while giving you food and income before the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani cacao tsei lɛ daa.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and high sunlight. Without shade from larger crops like plantains or shade trees, the seedlings lose moisture too quickly, leaf burns occur, and many will die before establishing strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo bɛ kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei adɛŋ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ, baai lɛ shãa, ni mɛi babaoo baagboi dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa.

english: How long after planting cocoa can I expect to start harvesting pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ beni midu kookoo lɛ manyɛ mabɔi ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years before yielding a full harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cocoa henɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema cocoa henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛshɛɔ ŋmaa lɛ he.

english: Why does maintaining a cocoa farm require so much hard physical work throughout the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔ nɔkwɛmɔ biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa requires continuous labor such as clearing aggressive weeds, pruning overgrown branches, removing infected pods, and manual harvesting to prevent diseases and ensure high pod quality.
ga: Cocoa biɔ nitsumɔ daa, tamɔ jwɛi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ajiemɔ. pruning overgrown branches Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛ niji ni akɛkpaa koni hela akashɛ nɔ ni akwɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing far fewer pods than they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their natural vigor declines, their root systems become less efficient at absorbing nutrients, and they become more susceptible to diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei ye afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ baa shi. Amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ni helai yeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Will planting plantains next to my cocoa trees steal all the nutrients from the soil?
ga: plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ani mi-cocoa tso lɛ baaju niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems compared to cocoa trees, so they do not heavily compete for deep soil nutrients. Furthermore, decaying plantain leaves and stems form organic mulch that enriches the soil for the cocoa.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ akɛto cacao tsei ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ babaoo he akaŋ. Kɛfata he lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛha kookoo dumɔ.

english: How can I earn money from my farm while waiting for new cocoa trees to yield pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni mimɛɔ cacao tsei heei ni baawo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Planting food crops like plantain and cassava alongside young cocoa allows you to harvest and sell produce within 9 to 12 months, providing regular income while your cocoa trees grow.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava ni ooodu yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli, ni ehaa onáa shika daa be mli ni okookoo tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: What happens to cocoa plants if I do not prune their branches regularly?
ga: Mɛni baaba kookoo tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mifolɔɔɔ lɛ daa?

english: Unpruned cocoa trees become overcrowded with leaves, blocking sunlight and air flow. This creates a dark, humid climate inside the canopy where fungal diseases like black pod thrive.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ eyi kɛ baai. Etsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli edɔ baa ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ daa yɛ.

english: What kind of soil is best for starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishijee?

english: Cocoa grows best in deep, well-drained loamy soil rich in organic matter that can hold moisture during dry periods without staying waterlogged.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast under young cocoa trees and slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ashishi ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have small leaves that let sunlight hit the soil, encouraging weed growth. These weeds steal valuable water, nutrients, and sunlight from the young cocoa plants.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii. ni haa hulu la shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ehaa jwɛi lɛ daa Jwɛi nɛɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli.

english: Why am I getting smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same way I always do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ nibii babaoo nɔ daa afi lɛ? Ni miduɔ nii yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: Over time, planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil. Combined with changing weather patterns and rising temperatures, crops produce lower yields unless soil nutrients are restored and planting dates are adapted.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ekwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ latsaa ni yaa hiɛ lɛ fata he lɛ, Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo ni baa shi aba. Ja aku sɛɛ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba ekoŋŋ ni atsake gbi ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Trees drop young pods (known as cherelle wilt) when they experience stress from heat, sudden dry spells, or a lack of nutrients. The tree sheds part of its load to save enough water and energy to stay alive.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ cherelle wilt) kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Gbimɔ trukaa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Tsei lɛ laajeɔ amɛjatsu lɛ eko koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: What causes the main rainy season in Ghana to start later and end earlier than it used to?
ga: Mɛni haa Ghana nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ mli ni egbeɔ naa mra fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Global climate patterns are shifting, altering West Africa's rainfall cycles. Higher temperatures change how clouds form and move, resulting in shorter rainy seasons and unpredictable dry spells.
ga: Jeŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi miitsake. Afrika Anaigbɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ miitsake. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baatsake bɔ ni atatui lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa kɛ bɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe amɛhaa lɛ. Enɛ haa nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ feɔ kuku, ni nugbɔshiimɔ be ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa.

english: How does intense sunlight and heat affect my crops during their flowering stage?
ga: Te hulu ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extreme heat dries up pollen and damages delicate flower parts, preventing proper pollination. This leads to poor fruit formation and empty grains on crops like maize.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ agbiɔ ni efiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa aduawai gbohii kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko baa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my soil has lost its power to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ?

english: Tired soil shows clear signs: crop leaves turn pale or yellow despite rain, plants remain stunted, topsoil forms a hard crust, and your total harvest declines year after year.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo: tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Tso lɛ kã he eji nɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa. ni okpamɔ fɛɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen, which plants need to build food. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient away, or poor soil drainage can prevent roots from taking it up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ. Aloo nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ lɛ.

english: Why does adding compost help my farm withstand dry spells better than chemical fertilizer alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni enyɛɔ edamɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi anaa jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Compost acts like a sponge in the soil, holding onto rainwater and releasing it slowly to plant roots during hot days, whereas chemical fertilizer only supplies plant food without improving water retention.
ga: Kompost tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu ni emɔɔ ni ejieɔ lɛ fiofio lɛ nɔ. Koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii pɛ ni ehaaa nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops wither quickly even when rain fell just a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: When air temperatures are very high, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it from the ground. Soil with low organic matter also loses moisture to evaporation very quickly.
ga: Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔji ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ hu fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ la ni hoɔ oya lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in warm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds require both moisture and moderate soil temperature to germinate. If the soil becomes too hot and dry right after planting, the seeds lose internal water and die before popping up.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ fɛ̃i kɛ sũ mli dɔlɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why does my farmland flood easily during heavy rain but dry up completely a day later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi egbiɔ kwraa yɛ gbi kome sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Hard, degraded soil loses its structure and cannot absorb rainwater quickly. Water runs over the top, causing flooding and erosion, instead of soaking deep into the ground for plants to use later.
ga: Shikpɔji ni wa ni efite lɛ fiteɔ amɛhe oya, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nugbɔ nu. Nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ekɛ nu afua kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi baa. Mohu ɔ, e pueɔ zu ɔ mi wawɛɛ konɛ tsehi nɛ a kɛ tsu ní pee se.

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. They need shade from larger trees or plantain plants to protect their tender leaves and keep the soil moist while their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli koni amɛbu baai bibii ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plant leaves use to stay green. The plant is moving its limited nutrients to the newer leaves at the top to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei ahe baai kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tso lɛ miitsi niyenii fioo ko kɛmiiya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ehi shi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When the cowpea roots rot, they leave behind natural plant food that your maize can drink up to grow strong.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni egbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji cowpea shishifãi lɛ egbo Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni o-corn lɛ baanyɛ anu koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam plants produce very small tubers if I do not provide sticks for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji akɛ mikɛ niji haaa wain tso lɛ ni ekwɔ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the underground tuber using sunlight. When vines climb tall sticks, their leaves spread out to catch maximum sunlight, but when vines lie on the ground, leaves shade each other and produce less food.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kwɔ nine ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ, baai lɛ baaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over during big storms when they are bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni tsii lɛ gbee shi yɛ ahum wulu ko mli beni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry a lot of water weight in their stems. When the heavy bunch forms at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wet soil and strong winds to pull the roots out of the ground unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ nu babaoo yɛ amɛtso lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmeii ni tsii fee yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baagbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ja akɛ tso nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard, woody, and watery when I delay harvesting them past their time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa, amɛfeɔ tsei ni nu yɔɔ mli beni mikpaa amɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch for the plant to use. When the roots stay in the ground too long, the plant starts using up that stored starch to survive dry seasons, leaving behind tough plant fiber and water.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch toɔ koni tso lɛ kɛtsu nii. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baabɔi amɛ ŋmeii ni amɛto lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Eshiɔ tsei ahe tsɔi ni mli wa kɛ nu.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme hot weather, prolonged dry spells, or sudden flooding. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo flash flood Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tso tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni ehi wala mli.

english: This black rot at the bottom of tomatoes is caused by uneven watering. When soil quickly switches between being too dry and too wet, the plant cannot move calcium to the growing fruit, causing the bottom cells to collapse.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ tsɔ teŋ. Tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: The first rain often wet the hot ground without fully cooling it down, and dry spells usually follow immediately. The seeds absorb water and hot soil heat, causing them to spoil before they have a chance to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa hei ni mli edɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ehaaa amɛhe ajɔɔ kwraa. ni bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ dɔlɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛnaa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crop plants to stay thin and small even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops. They drink the soil water and eat up fertilizer before your crop roots can reach them, leaving your crops hungry and thirsty.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. Amɛnuɔ sũ mli nu ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ kɛ kumai baaye onibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my yam setts too close to the top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When yam seed tubers are planted too shallowly, direct heat from the sun can dry them out, scorch young shoots, or attract pests, preventing the tubers from developing deeply and healthy in the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbi, ashã ŋmeii bibii, loo egbala ŋmeii kɛba. Etsiɔ tubers naa koni amɛkakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: What causes my growing yams to push out slightly above the soil surface, and how do I fix it?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato lɛ yaa ŋwɛi fioo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: As yam tubers expand, hard soil or shallow mounds force them upwards toward the surface. Covering exposed tubers with loose soil or dried leaves prevents sunburn and keeps them growing large and healthy.
ga: Kɛji sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛ Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo gɔji ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baatsi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse loo baai ni egbi ha bulb lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu lɛ akaha amɛ, ni ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops producing a lower harvest this year compared to the good harvest I got last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afi nɛɛ kɛ akɛto yibiiwoo kpakpa ni miná nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Changes in rainfall timing, unexpected dry spells, or soil nutrient loss from continuous farming can lower harvest yields even if you farm the same land using the same methods.
ga: Be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ tsakemɔ Loo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi. Kɛji akɛ okɛ gbɛi kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ po.

english: Why do crops like yam and cassava produce bigger tubers when planted on raised soil mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ sweet potatoes kɛ cassava woɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ?

english: Raised mounds loosen the soil, making it easier for root crops to spread and swell freely while protecting the roots from getting soaked and rotting during heavy rains.
ga: Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee mlɛo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛha tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfuu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How can I protect my young crop seedlings when the rains stop earlier than expected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the base of your plants with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, traps moisture in the soil longer and keeps the ground cool during dry periods.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa tso shishi lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow plenty of green leaves but produce very small tubers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi bulbs loo aduawai bibii waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages lush stem and leaf growth at the expense of root or fruit development; crops need balanced nutrients, including potassium, to form full fruits and tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii kɛ baai lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa shishifãi loo aduawai lɛ daraa. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. ni potassium fata he koni akɛfee aduawai kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ emuu

english: Why are the lower leaves on my crops turning yellow early in the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves early in the season often mean the soil lacks essential plant nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is sitting around the roots and choking the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ekɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa.

english: What causes seed tubers to rot in the soil before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui ayitsei fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Planting in excessively wet soil or buried under heavy, unventilated soil starves the seed of air and allows fungal rot to attack before the sprout can push through.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fe nine nɔ loo afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye dumɔwui lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ atutua amɛ dani dumɔwui lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do my crops look weaker when I plant the exact same crop on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets plant-specific pests build up in the soil, which reduces plant strength and yield over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛ gbɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense against extreme sun heat; by rolling its leaves, the plant reduces its surface area to slow down water loss.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ koni nu lɛ aya hiɛ fiofio lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Planting shade trees or fast-growing plantains around them creates a protective cover that keeps the soil cool and prevents the leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni daa oya ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Tsei lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa baa lɛ shãaa.

english: Why are there small holes and light grey patches appearing on my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse je kpo yɛ mi-abele baai bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: This pattern of leaf damage is usually caused by fall armyworm caterpillars feeding on the crop. Identifying them early lets you treat the plants with safe control methods before the caterpillars ruin the whole harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyɔsemɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ tsei ahe nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe nɔ, ni akudɔɔ amɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay thin and yield very small cobs when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in the same spot, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting fewer seeds per hole with proper spacing gives each plant the room it needs to yield large, heavy cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui babaoo tsɔ ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔwui fioo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa tsu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmei agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to stick tall wooden poles next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Keeping the vines off the wet soil also protects the foliage from rotting and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛaatsi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why are the bottoms of my young green tomatoes turning dark black and rotting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ashishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often due to uneven watering. Maintaining steady moisture in the soil helps the plant transport calcium properly to the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, drain valuable water and soil nutrients away from the main stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant gets enough strength to produce a massive bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ jieɔ nu ni jara wa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ plantains babaoo baa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my maize help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmã duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food inside the soil. This naturally enriches the soil, feeding the neighboring maize plants without relying entirely on chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ niyenii ni okɛ ohe akafɔ̃ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves in dry weather as a survival strategy to prevent water loss through evapotranspiration. The root tubers remain healthy underground, and fresh leaves will quickly sprout once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛhi shi koni nu akafite kɛtsɔ evapotranspiration nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off instead of forming hot peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when plants face high heat stress, extremely dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and using balanced fertilizer helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
