ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I tell if my crops need nitrogen fertilizer without paying for a soil test?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia mitsei lɛ ni miwooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa he nyɔmɔ?

english: A clear sign of nitrogen shortage is when the lower leaves of your crops start turning pale green or yellow from the tips inward. Nitrogen is essential for leafy growth, so yellowing leaves indicate the crop needs extra feeding.
ga: Okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa ji be mli ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ emligbɛ. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii kroko he miihia tso lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. They require shade crops like plantains or cassava planted alongside them during their first 2 to 3 years to act as living umbrellas, protecting their young leaves and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka. Ebuɔ baai bibii ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of the stalk usually indicate that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green again and supports crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava cuttings when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ ahi ŋmei niji lɛ ateŋ?

english: Cassava cuttings should ideally be planted about 1 meter apart. Giving them enough space ensures that the underground roots have room to expand into large tubers without competing with nearby plants for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu tsei ni afo lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ha lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii wuji. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔi akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes in the ground for my yam leaves to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves off the ground into direct sunlight. Leaves exposed to sunlight produce more food for the plant, which results in larger and healthier yam tubers under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛhaa tso lɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have beneficial bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. This naturally enriches the land with nutrients, reducing the need for chemical fertilizers for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ atsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans breaks disease cycles and restores soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ, fiteɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are weeds around my young crops causing them to grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni bɔle mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛdaraa blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, sunlight, and essential soil nutrients away from your crops. Removing weeds early allows your main crop to consume all the food and moisture it needs to grow quickly and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otso titri lɛ niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ewo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from excessive heat, dry soil, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting in places with good air movement helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What is causing holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the top funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They nest inside the central leaves of young maize to feed and must be treated early using recommended biological extracts like neem or approved control measures before they ruin the plant's growth point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛfeɔ amɛshĩa yɛ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii ni esa akɛ akwɛ amɛ mra. kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ atsuɔ he nii tamɔ neem loo gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. dani efite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops early in the morning or during the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo aduawai anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water your crops early in the morning. Morning watering allows the soil to absorb moisture before the hot sun causes fast evaporation, giving the plant the water it needs to withstand the heat of the day.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu leebi. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be lɛ naa nakai gbi lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje ŋmãa shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: Wait for the first two or three steady, heavy rains of the major season so the soil holds enough moisture. Planting too early in dry soil causes the seeds to dry out and fail to germinate.
ga: Mɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ bei fioo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa, ni nɛɔ daa yɛ be titri lɛ mli lɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛkwɛ̃ŋ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees growing so much slower than my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miida blɛoo kwraa fe mi cassava tsei lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that spends its early years establishing deep roots and strong trunks, while cassava is a seasonal tuber crop built to grow rapidly and produce yields within a single year.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ daa. koni akɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni mli wa Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, Cassava ji be mli nibii ni aduɔ ni ama koni eda oya ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aba yɛ afi kome mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are overcrowded, they shade each other from sunlight and compete for soil nutrients. The plant drops its lower leaves to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛhaa amɛhe shade ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsei shiɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: What causes my maize leaves to roll up into tight tubes during hot sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli?

english: Maize leaves roll up naturally during intense heat to reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun, helping the plant save moisture and prevent drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli. Koni akɛba he ni baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by severe heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Giving the soil steady moisture and organic manure helps keep the flowers on.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaawo mli be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do plantain suckers grow tall and thin when planted under large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Plantains need direct sunlight to build thick stems. Under heavy shade, they stretch upward searching for light, which makes them tall, weak, and easy for wind to blow down.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee tsei ni mli tse. Yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ, amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛtaoɔ la. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛɔ, amɛhe waaa, ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are fully mature under the soil and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and vines stop growing and naturally dry up or turn yellow, showing that the plant has finished sending stored food down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes shɛɔ dalɛ he kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ kpa dalɛ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe loo amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni ato lɛ kɛmajemɔ shi kɛtee bulb lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why does my land give me smaller crop yields every year even though I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni midu yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Crops consume nutrients from the ground every season. Without adding compost, animal manure, or fertilizer to replenish the soil, the land becomes tired and produces smaller harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii daa be. Ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni ewooo yibii babaoo.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by heat stress or tiny insects like whiteflies that spread viruses. Providing light shade and checking for small pests under the leaves helps identify the issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo loo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. La ni tsoɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni ana naagba lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings wilt and die right after I move them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants suffer transplant shock when moved into strong sunlight without preparation. Transplanting in the cool late afternoon and watering immediately helps their weak roots adjust without dying.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ naa amanehulu kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni asaaa he. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli ni awo lɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why do the leaves on my young oil palm trees turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the tree is hungry for essential soil nutrients like nitrogen or potassium. Applying the right fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the base of the tree helps restore its rich green color and improves overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni bɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha edalɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant my oil palm trees very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu mu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planted too closely, oil palms fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the trees to grow tall and thin while producing fewer, smaller fruit bunches because they cannot capture enough sunlight.
ga: adu ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Mu tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ni efeɔ bibii ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do some of the fruit bunches on my palm tree rot before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ anɔ yibii lɛ ekomɛi miifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Fruit rot often happens when leaves around the tree crown are overcrowded, trapping excess moisture and blocking fresh air. Pruning dead or overcrowded leaves allows sunlight and air to reach the fruits, preventing fungal rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai fitemɔ baa kɛji baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fite. Tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ mli ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa. Kɛ́ afo baai ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ aduawai lɛ ahe. Ebaanyɛ etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Does removing old fronds from my palm tree help it bear more fruit?
ga: Ani kɛ́ ajie tɛŋ tso ko he baai momo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, carefully cutting off old or dying fronds stops the tree from wasting energy on non-productive parts. It also opens up space for flowers to pollinate properly and gives growing fruit bunches room to expand.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ baai ni egbɔ loo ni miigboi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ hei ni wooo yibii lɛ anɔ. Ehaa gbɛ hu haa fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai akuu ni miida lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my young oil palm trees during their early stage?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mu tsei ateŋ shishijee mli?

english: Yes, intercropping with short-term crops like maize or cassava is safe during the first two to three years. Just make sure to leave a clear circle around each palm tree base so the food crops do not choke the young palms.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ kɛkɛ akɛ oshi kooloo ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni obɔle he. Tso fɛɛ tso shishi Koni niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ akatsi tsei bibii lɛ anaa

english: Is it bad practice to mix damaged or bruised palm fruits with fresh ones when selling to buyers?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ akɛ ŋmei yibii ni efite loo egbɔjɔ lɛ baafutu ŋmei yibii heei beni ahɔ̃ɔ ahaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ?

english: Yes, mixing bruised or decaying fruits with fresh ones speeds up spoilage and reduces the overall quality of the palm oil produced. Sorting your harvest by quality helps you command higher prices for prime produce.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ aduawai ni egbo loo egbo lɛ futu aduawai heei amli lɛ, ebaaha efite oya, ni ebaaha ŋmei fɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ fɛɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni akwɛɔ mli lɛ amlijaa yɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ naa lɛ haa okɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ haa nibii titrii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest an oil palm bunch?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa mu tsei akui lɛ?

english: A fruit bunch is ripe and ready for harvest when two to five loose, bright orange fruits naturally break off and fall to the ground. Harvesting too early means getting less oil, while waiting too long causes the oil quality to drop.
ga: Yibii akuu lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni yibii enyɔ kɛyashi enumɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli gbala yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ mu faaa. Yɛ be mli ni mɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha mu lɛ mlihilɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my palm fruits lose their oil quality if I keep them on the ground for days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm yibii lɛ amli fɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ mli gbii babaoo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Once harvested, palm fruits begin a natural chemical process that rapidly increases their acidity. Leaving harvested bunches in the heat or rain for days spoils the oil taste and reduces its market value.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa Palm yibii lɛ jeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔ nifeemɔ ko shishi ni haa acidity lɛ yaa hiɛ oya. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ latsaa loo nugbɔ mli gbii babaoo lɛ, efiteɔ mu lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ, ni ehaa jara ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds around the base of my oil palm slow down how fast the tree grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ mu tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ haa tsei lɛ daa blɛoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive competitors that drink up the moisture and eat the soil nutrients intended for your tree. Clearing a clean ring around the trunk ensures the palm gets all the water and plant food it needs.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei, ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ mli lɛ. Ajieɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni he tse ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa tso lɛ nu kɛ tsei niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if an oil palm seedling will produce plenty of oil before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ baajie fɔ babaoo dani adu?

english: High-yielding oil palm varieties, such as the Tenera type, are bred to have thick fruit flesh and small shell seeds. The best way to be sure is to buy certified seedlings from registered government nurseries rather than raising wild seeds.
ga: Mu tso henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo, tamɔ Tenera henɔ lɛ, yɛ aduawai loo ni mli edɔ kɛ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ ana nɔmimaa ji ni ahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ nɔyeli dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ko ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ koo mli dumɔwui lɛ

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice so the grains do not break during milling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ akakumɔ yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Harvest your rice when about 80% to 85% of the crop heads turn golden yellow. Delaying the harvest makes the grains overly dry and brittle, which causes them to crack easily when processed by milling machines.
ga: Kpãa o-rice lɛ be mli ni aaafee 80% kɛyashi 85% ni ji tubers lɛ etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Nikpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ mli egbiɔ tsɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fãa oya kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii.

english: Why do my young rice plants turn yellow when there is standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nu ni damɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Even though rice needs water, completely flooding young plants or having poor drainage starves the roots of air. This prevents the roots from taking up nitrogen from the soil, making the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia ŋmãa moŋ Shi kɛ́ nu eyi tsei bibii amli loo nu hoɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I harvest more grain from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani makpa dumɔwui babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together causes plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and smaller cobs, actually reducing your total harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why does my land produce less yield every year even though I plant the same crop at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every season drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to replenish. Rotating different crops or adding manure restores soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ Loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants showing ragged holes and small black droppings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in leaves with dark droppings inside the leaves are usually caused by pests like fall armyworms feeding on the young crop. Clearing weeds early and applying appropriate pest control protects the plants.
ga: Bu ko ni etse ehe yɛ baa ko mli ni ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɔɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ tsei bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ni akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa baatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu tsei ahe.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil, which causes stress and forces the plant to drop its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efoɔ shi.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick leaves but producing very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer or very rich leaf growth makes the cassava plant send all its energy into developing branches and leaves instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo loo baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine lɛ haa yucca tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei niji kɛ baai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Leaf rolling during hot afternoons is a natural defense mechanism pepper plants use to conserve moisture and reduce water loss under intense sunlight.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ waa lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni pepper tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted food crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants with deep, aggressive root systems naturally adapted to absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated food crops, making early weeding essential.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji maŋ tso ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ basabasa. Amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ. Ha efee nɔ ni abaanyɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. lɛ he miihia

english: Why do my stored cowpea beans get filled with tiny holes and turn to powder after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Storage insects called weevils lay eggs on the beans, and their larvae eat the insides of the seeds. Thoroughly drying your beans and storing them in airtight containers stops these insects from surviving.
ga: Picker kooloi ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. ni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ogbala o-beans lɛ ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akajo foi.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries up the soil moisture before their roots grow deep enough to find water.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni egbiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛnaa nu.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that carry very heavy tops, so if pests like root nematodes weaken the base, the plant easily loses its grip in the soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ root nematodes lɛ ha shishitoo lɛ gbɔjɔ lɛ, ewaaa akɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, a vital plant food that easily washes away from the soil during heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves instead of sweeping it clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? ŋmɔshi nibii ni baai egbi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaatsumɔ he

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves acts like a blanket that traps water in the soil, keeps the roots cool, and slow-releases nutrients as the leaves rot.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ekɛ nu mɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii fiofio kɛji baai lɛ fite

english: Why is it harmful to throw dry fertilizer on my crops when the ground has no water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be mli ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops can only drink nutrients when they are dissolved in water; putting dry fertilizer on dry ground burns the plant roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ amɛwo nu mli pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaashã tsei shishifãi moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground before it is time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles in heavy soil without draining away properly, creating wet conditions where underground fungi destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch full sunlight, which allows the plant to produce enough energy to grow big underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaji lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars hide inside the center leaves of my corn plants during the early rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of young corn because it provides tender food while protecting them from rain, birds, and sprays.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa amɛyeɔ niyenii ni mli jɔ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ, okpoi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field make my maize grow better in the next farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts extract nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for whatever crop you plant there afterward.
ga: Akpɔlɔi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ jɛmɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat stress, lack of soil water, or when bees are absent to help pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo ŋmeii ni baaye abua ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ haa amɛhaoɔ.

english: How should I position cassava stems in the soil when I am planting them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Plant cassava stems slanting at about a 45-degree angle with the growing buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them this way helps the plant establish deep roots quickly and produce bigger tubers.
ga: Aduɔ cassava tsei lɛ yɛ koŋ ni miihe ashɛ digrii 45 nɔ, ni ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ tso lɛ daa yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni etswaa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ oya ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Should I cut off the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain crop?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi plantain tsei titrii lɛ miida?

english: Yes, keep only 2 or 3 shoots per stand—the main mother plant, one medium shoot, and one small sucker. Removing extra shoots ensures the main plant gets enough water and plant nutrients to produce large bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, ha ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ahi shidaamɔhe fɛɛ shidaamɔhe, tamɔ tso nyɛ titri lɛ, ŋmeii 1 ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ, kɛ ŋmeii bibii 1. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa nu kɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam plants are vines that need tall sticks so their leaves can spread out and reach sunlight. The sunlight gives the leaves energy, which flows down to build thick, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni ehe hia niji kakadaji koni ebaa lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni emɔ hulu la lɛ. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn lacks nitrogen food in the soil or the ground is soaked with too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or improving field drainage will make the leaves green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my crop after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Apply the first round of fertilizer about two weeks after planting when young roots appear, and a second round when the crop begins flowering or fruiting to give it strength to produce good yield.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ beni shishifãi bibii jeɔ kpo lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ afata he kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɔi fɔfɔi loo amɛwoɔ yibii koni amɛhe awa ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How do I test if my field soil has enough moisture for planting after the rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: Scoop a handful of dirt and squeeze it into a ball; if it holds shape but breaks apart easily when touched, it is ready. If it turns into sticky mud, wait a few days for the ground to drain excess water.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ muji ko ni okɛmimɔ mli ni efee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli shi efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ ata he lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo. Kɛji etsɔ muji ni shwieɔ shi lɛ Mɛɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ajie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my young corn leaves and green powder inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ powda eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which feed on young corn leaves. You can control them by spraying approved crop protection products early in the morning or applying neem leaf liquid directly into the leafy funnel.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ leebi lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ nu ni jɛ neem baai lɛ amli lɛ awo funnel lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and drying up on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, which spreads during wet, cool seasons. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets sunlight reach the tree trunk and drying up wet conditions helps prevent the disease.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji black pod hela, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ fɛ̃i bei amli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ amli, ni aha hulu la lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni aha shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the sunny afternoon even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Midday drooping in moist soil is often caused by root rot or soil wilt disease affecting the plant's water pipes. Planting on raised soil beds and rotating crops every season keeps roots healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni egbo loo shikpɔŋ ni egbo ni saa tso lɛ nu paipii lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ yibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ daa be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: How can I stop insects from eating my harvested dried corn while stored in bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Ensure the corn grains are dried completely until hard, clean the storage area, and store the grains in airtight hermetic bags to prevent insects from breathing and damaging your harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ agbi kwraa ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsumɔ he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ he Ni okɛ ŋmãa awo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli koni kooloi akamu ni amɛkafite onibii lɛ.

english: What is this 'mulch' that other farmers are talking about, and how does it help my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘mulch’ nɛɛ ni okwaafoi krokomɛi wieɔ he lɛ ni te eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Mulch is simply a layer of organic material, such as dry grass, straw, or fallen leaves, placed over the surface of the soil around your plants. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps moisture inside the soil, stops weeds from growing, and shields the earth from the harsh sun.
ga: Mulch ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi, loo baai ni egbee shi kɛkɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he

english: Why does the dirt around my crops dry out so quickly after rain during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ muji ni ebɔle mihe lɛ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: When soil is left bare, the direct heat of the sun causes the moisture inside it to evaporate rapidly into the air. Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or grass blocks the heat from reaching the earth, trapping the water underneath so your crops can drink longer.
ga: Beni ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Hulu lɛ mli la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dɔlɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni emɔɔ nu yɛ shishi koni onibii lɛ anu nu be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I keep my vegetable soil moist when there is no rainfall for a few days?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-vegetable shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko gbii fioo komɛi nɛ?

english: You can cover the bare ground around your crop roots with dry plant leaves or straw. This material acts as a barrier that prevents the sun from baking the soil, helping the earth hold onto water longer so your plants do not wilt.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni tso baai loo jwɛi ni egbi yɔɔ mli. Nibii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela koni hulu lɛ akashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ gbooo.

english: Can the strong afternoon sun actually damage the soil on my farm?
ga: Ani shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, strong direct sunshine bakes bare soil, drying out all the water and damaging the healthy soil environment. Placing a protective cover of plant material like mulch over the ground prevents the sun rays from striking the soil directly.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha nu lɛ fɛɛ agbi. ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ kpakpa lɛ Tsei ahe nibii, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is there a simple way to stop weeds from popping up around my crops without using a hoe every week?
ga: Gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni oootsɔ nɔ oha jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Ani manyɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni mikɛ tsɔne tsuuu nii daa otsi?

english: Yes, you can spread a thick layer of dry grass or leaves over the soil around your crops. This layer covers the ground so that weed seeds cannot get sunlight, which prevents them from sprouting and growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni mli edɔ ashwã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akashɛ hulu la he. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Why did my neighbor's field have almost no weeds after he covered the ground with dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eshwɛ fioo ni jwɛi ko bɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni ekɛ baai ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The dry leaves form a protective shield over the soil that cuts off light from reaching weed seeds hidden in the earth. Without sunlight, those seeds cannot germinate, leaving the crop field mostly free of weeds.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haa la shɛɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Kɛ hulu la bɛ Nakai dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃. Ha jwɛi akafee he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ fa ko.

english: Will covering the ground around my crops with dry plant materials actually give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani tsei ni egbi ni mikɛha he ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa babaoo diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, because it protects the soil from losing water and keeps weeds from stealing plant food and nutrients. When your crops do not have to compete with weeds or suffer from dry soil, they grow much stronger and produce a higher yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he, ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aju niyenii kɛ niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ amli hewalɛ. Be mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ jwɛi akaŋ loo amɛna shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he amanehulu. Tsei baakwɛ̃ waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does soil under a thick cover of leaves feel cool while bare ground feels very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa.

english: The cover of leaves acts like an umbrella, blocking the hot rays of the sun from hitting the bare earth. This keeps the root area under the ground cool and comfortable for your crops.
ga: Baa lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i kɛha onibii.

english: What happens to my plants if the ground gets too hot from direct sun exposure?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔ tsɔ kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli?

english: When the ground becomes overheated from direct sunshine, plant roots struggle to soak up water and food, which can cause the crop to grow slowly or wither. Shielding the soil keeps the temperature lower so the roots can function properly.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ. Tse shishifãi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei adara blɛoo loo amɛgbi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa hulutsoo baa shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I use dry grass cut from my farm land to protect my vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni afolɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ abu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, gathering clean dry grass and spreading it around the base of your vegetables creates a great layer of mulch. This grass cover keeps the soil moist, shields it from direct sunlight, and stops weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni he tse ni ooobua naa ni okɛshwã o-vegetables lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye obɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient plant need to grow. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer gives the maize the food it needs to stay green and yield big cobs.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji tso ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmãa wuji.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that spread viruses, or by extreme heat and drought stress. Controlling pests early and keeping the soil moist helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ mli. Mra Be mli Kooloi ni Yeɔ Nibii Amli Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry out and die when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have very tender leaves and roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting plantain trees alongside them provides living shade that keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ Cacao tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Why do the roots of my crops turn soft and rot after heavy rains leave standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa nu ni ekã shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crop roots need to breathe air in the soil just like humans do. When water sits on the field for days, it blocks air from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei shishifãi amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ nu lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Kɔɔyɔɔ baatsi enaa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni efiteɔ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from evaporating water out of the soil, keeping moisture near the roots for much longer.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to stick tall wooden poles next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers. Lifting their vines onto tall poles exposes all their leaves to sunlight, which allows the plant to produce more energy and grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ etso lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Too many young shoots fight with the main tree for water and soil nutrients. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough food to produce a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ baawu koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before they can grow into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant suffers from sudden water stress, high temperatures, or pest damage. Ensuring consistent watering and protecting the buds from insects keeps flowers attached so fruit can form.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni okɛ nu awo mli daa ni obu ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he koni aduawai aba.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so thin and weak if I leave them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that quickly steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds early allows your crops to get all the nutrients they need to grow thick and strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛha onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Cassava plants show they are mature when their bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil at the base of the trunk begins to crack from swollen tubers underneath.
ga: Cassava tso tsɔɔ akɛ eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Shi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni efuu lɛ mli.

english: How do I choose the best seeds or seedlings to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui loo dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for healthy, strong parent plants that produce a lot of fruit and do not get sick easily. Using seeds or cuttings from these top-performing plants ensures your new crops will grow strong and give you a good harvest.
ga: Taomɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni hela mɔɔɔ lɛ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ nɛɛ amli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ daa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: Is it better to plant seeds from any healthy tree I see, or should I pick specific ones?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ madu dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mina lɛ amli? Aloo esa akɛ mahala tsei lɛ pɛ?

english: You should always select seeds from specific 'mother trees' that consistently show great qualities, like high yields or pest resistance. Picking seeds randomly can lead to weak crops with unpredictable harvests.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala dumɔwui kɛjɛ ‘nyɛ tso’ pɔtɛɛ ko ni ejie sui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kpo be fɛɛ be, tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa loo nɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Dumɔwui ni ahalaa trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ aba.

english: What does it mean when extension officers talk about choosing a 'good mother tree' for planting?
ga: Nɔyaa he nitsulɔi wieɔ halamɔ lɛ he Mɛni ‘nyɛ tso kpakpa’ tsɔɔ kɛji adu?

english: A mother tree is an outstanding tree on a farm that has exact qualities a farmer wants—such as fast growth, big fruit, or disease resistance. Farmers collect seeds or cuttings from this tree to grow new trees with those same great qualities.
ga: Tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ ji tso ni yeɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni yɔɔ sui ni okwaafonyo lɛ sumɔɔ, tamɔ dalɛ oya, yibii wuji loo helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ helai. Okwaafoi buaa dumɔwui loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ tso nɛɛ mli koni amɛkɛdu tsei heei. ni yɔɔ sui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ

english: Why do some cocoa trees produce bigger pods than others on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji fe ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Every tree inherits specific traits from its parent plant. Some trees naturally carry superior qualities, like growing larger pods or surviving dry seasons better than neighboring trees.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso náa sui kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Tsei komɛi yɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmeii ni daraa loo amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why are some of my mango trees full of fruit every season while others barely produce anything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii daa afi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni eshwɛ fioo ni tsei komɛi wooo yibii kwraa lɛ?

english: Trees carry different natural characteristics. Some are naturally heavy producers, which is why farmers look for those specific trees and propagate them so their new farm will be equally productive.
ga: Tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli sui srɔtoi. Henɔi komɛi ji adebɔɔ mli nibii wuji ni feɔ nibii. Nɔ ni haa okwaafoi taoɔ nakai tsei pɔtɛɛi lɛ ni amɛfɔɔ amɛ koni amɛŋmɔji heei lɛ awo yibii tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can I make sure all the fruit trees I plant yield sweet fruits like the best tree on my neighbor's farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ aduawai tsei ni miduɔ lɛ woɔ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ tamɔ tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can achieve this by taking seeds, shoots, or cuttings specifically from that sweet-fruit tree. Selecting planting materials from trees with proven good qualities guarantees that your new trees will share those same traits.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni oookwɛ kɛjɛ nakai tso pɔtɛɛ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni ahalaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni ana he odaseyeli, ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Akɛ nɔmimaa haa akɛ otsei heei lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ kome.

english: Why should I look for disease-resistant trees when selecting materials to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ otao tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ beni ohalaa nibii ni okɛbaadu lɛ?

english: Trees that naturally fight off diseases pass those protective traits down to their young plants. Planting from disease-resistant trees saves you money on agrochemicals and protects your entire farm.
ga: Tsei ni kɛ helai wuɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ kɛ nakai sui ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ haa tsei bibii. Tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ amli ni oookwɛ lɛ haaa okɛ shika akafite yɛ okwaayeli tsofai ahe, ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ he.

english: Why should I throw away weak-looking seedlings in my nursery before taking them to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi dumɔwui ni tamɔ nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weak seedlings often carry poor traits or hidden diseases that will prevent them from fruiting well. Sorting them out early ensures only strong, high-quality plants use up your farm space and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ sui kpakpai loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni haaa amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ. Mligbalamɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaakwɛ koni tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni hi jogbaŋŋ pɛ kɛ oŋmɔ mli he kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ atsu nii.

english: Can I just buy any crop seeds from the local market to start my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ koni mikɛje miŋmɔ lɛ shishi?

english: Seeds from the open market often come from mixed crops with unknown qualities. It is safer to use certified seeds or seeds carefully selected from proven, high-performing plants for reliable yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni jɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ jɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni aleee bɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ha lɛ amli. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase loo dumɔwui ni ahala jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ tsei ni ana he odaseyeli ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ baatsu nii koni anyɛ ana yibiiwoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: How does spending time to select good planting materials save me money in the long run?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ be ni ooohala nibii kpakpai ni okɛbaadu nii lɛ baanyɛ aha okɛ shika akafite yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Starting with carefully chosen, high-quality planting material reduces crop loss from pests and ensures higher harvests. This means you spend less money on farm inputs like chemicals and earn more from sales.
ga: Je shishi kɛ nihalamɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ okɛ shika fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii tamɔ tsofai ahe ni onáa shika babaoo kɛjɛɔ jarayeli mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cashew trees inside my house compound in the village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ cashew tsei yɛ tsũi ahe yɛ akrowai amli lɛ?

english: Cashew trees develop very wide branch canopies and extensive root systems that can crack building foundations, damage walls, and block light. They need wide, open farm fields to spread out without destroying property.
ga: Cashew tsei yɛ niji ni mli kwɔ waa kɛ shishifãi babaoo ni baanyɛ afite tsui ashishitoo. Akɛni amɛfiteɔ gbogboi ni amɛtsiɔ kane naa hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔlɔ ni agbele naa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfiteee nibii.

english: Why should I buy grafted cashew seedlings instead of just planting seeds directly from raw cashew nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe cashew nut dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu cashew ŋmeii ni ahoo lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛkɛ lɛ.

english: Grafted seedlings join a strong root system with a stem from a high-producing tree. This allows the plant to bear fruit much faster—in about 2 to 3 years instead of 5—and guarantees bigger nuts with higher market value.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ tsa shishifãi ni mli wa ni shishifãi ni jɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ yibii oya kwraa—yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ afii 5 najiaŋ—ni ehaa anáa ŋmeii wuji kɛ jarayeli jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: How close to my farm boundary line am I allowed to plant permanent crop trees like cashew?
ga: Te aŋmɛ mi gbɛ ni madu tsei ni hiɔ shi daa tamɔ cashew ŋmeii lɛ ebɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he eha tɛŋŋ?

english: It is best to plant large trees at least 3 to 5 meters away from your property boundary line. This prevents your tree branches and root systems from spreading into your neighbor's land and causing boundary conflicts when harvesting.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu tsei wuji kɛ hoo lɛ mitai 3 kɛyashi 5 kɛjɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ line lɛ he. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ niji kɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã okutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ béi baa husui amli kɛ́ akpa.

english: How do I know which parts of my farmland are best suited for growing cashews?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha cashew ŋmeii akwɛmɔ?

english: Cashews prefer deep, well-drained sandy loam soil where water does not settle. Areas of your farm that get waterlogged or flooded during heavy rains are unsuitable because wet soil rots cashew roots.
ga: Cashew ŋmeii sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu hiɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Hei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu shwieɔ nɔ loo nu shwieɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ esaaa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ haa cashew nut shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How many cashew trees can I safely plant on one acre of land?
ga: Cashew tsei enyiɛ manyɛ madu shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ?

english: The standard recommended spacing for cashews is 10 meters by 10 meters, which allows about 40 trees per acre. Spacing them properly prevents mature trees from shading each other out, ensuring maximum fruit production.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ esa akɛ akɛto cashews he lɛ ji mitai 10 x 10, ni haa aaafee tsei 40 yɛ acre kome mli. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei ahe lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkatsi amɛhe naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa nibii babaoo.

english: Why do some parts of my farm produce better yields than other spots on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo fe hei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Differences in soil depth, nutrient levels, and water drainage across your land cause varying yields. Soil in lower or richer pockets of your farm naturally holds nutrients better, leading to healthier trees and higher yields.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ Nutrient level Kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei srɔtoi lɛ haa yibiiwoo srɔtoi baa. Shikpɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shishi loo ni yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ hiɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cashew trees start losing their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ baai lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves during the dry season is a natural survival defense. The tree sheds leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation, conserving its internal moisture until rain returns for flowering.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛhaa wala. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛlaaje kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛtsɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baafɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my cashew tree growing lots of green leaves but failing to produce nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewooo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Excessive leaves with low nut production usually mean the tree is getting too much nitrogen or insufficient sunlight due to overcrowding. Pruning lower branches lets light reach the canopy to stimulate flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai babaoo kɛ ŋmeii fioo ni ajieɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ naaa nitrogen babaoo loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni afoɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ haa la shɛɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ he koni ewo fɔfɔii ahe hewalɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my young cashew trees while they are small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava loo ŋmãa yɛ cashew tsei ateŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping food crops like maize, legumes, or cassava between young cashew trees is recommended for the first 3 years. It gives you early food and income while keeping weeds suppressed until the cashew trees grow large.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ adu niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa. loo cassava Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 ni cashew tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ be mli ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ shi kɛyashiɔ cashew tsei lɛ daraa.

english: How many years can a cashew farm continue producing nuts after planting?
ga: Afii enyiɛ cashew nut ŋmɔ ko baanyɛ aya nɔ awo ŋmɔshi nibii beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A well-maintained cashew farm can remain productive for 30 to 40 years or more. Keeping the farm clear of weeds, pruning dry wood, and protecting it from bushfires ensures long-term annual income.
ga: Cashew ŋmɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Ni jwɛi akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni egbi ni afoɔ Kɛ koo mli la hebuu yeɔ ebuaa ni anáa shika ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ daa afi.

english: Does taking care of my crops every day really make a big difference in how much yield I get?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ daa gbi lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ kpele baa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, regular care allows you to spot pests, diseases, and weed competition early, preventing loss before it ruins your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, daa kwɛmɔ yeɔ ebua bo ni ona kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, helai kɛ jwɛi akaŋshii mra. Tsi nibii ni afiteɔ lɛ naa dani efite onibii.

english: What makes one farmer's cocoa farm produce more than a neighboring farm with the same soil?
ga: Mɛni haa okwaafonyo ko kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni shikpɔŋ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Differences in daily management—such as timely weeding, proper pruning, shade control, and regular pest management—greatly affect final harvest size.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ daa gbi nitsumɔ mli, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa jwɛi ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ daa Enɛ náa naagbee ŋmaa lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ waa.

english: How do I know if my crop leaves are turning yellow because of poor soil or a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo hela hewɔ?

english: Soil nutrient deficiency usually makes older leaves turn yellow evenly, while fungal or viral diseases cause irregular yellow spots, patches, or leaf curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ amɛhe. yɛ be mli ni fungal loo virus helai haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni ejaaa.

english: Can old, neglected cocoa trees produce well again if I start taking good care of them now?
ga: Ani cacao tsei ni egbɔ ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee shweremɔ ekoŋŋ kɛji wɔbɔi amɛkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ bianɛ?

english: Yes, by pruning dead branches, clearing surrounding weeds, opening up sunlight, and applying fertilizer, old cocoa trees can recover and produce high yields again.
ga: Nakai eji, kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ, hulu la ni akɛhaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, cacao tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is shade important for young cocoa plants but harmful to full-grown ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo be he hiaa cacao tsei bibii shi eyeɔ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun and need shade to survive, but full-grown trees need plenty of direct sunlight to bloom and bear heavy pods.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi ni ehe hiaa hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Shi tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛná ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: How many years does it take for a newly planted cocoa seedling to start bearing fruits?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwu ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing fruit in 2 to 3 years, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why do cocoa flowers fall off my tree without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off due to a lack of tiny pollinating insects, prolonged dry weather, or damage caused by pests like capsid bugs.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pollinators ni bɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hewɔ. loo nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛbaa

english: How much hard physical labor is really needed to start a brand new crop farm in Ghana?
ga: Nitsumɔ ni wa enyiɛ ehe hiaa dani anyɛ aje ŋmɔshi nibii heei ashishi yɛ Ghana?

english: Starting a farm requires intensive work like clearing heavy bush, digging proper planting holes, and frequent weeding during the early months to ensure crop survival.
ga: Okwaafoi ashishijee biɔ nitsumɔ ni mli wa, tamɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ajiemɔ. Bu ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ shii abɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji lɛ amli Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do young crop seedlings die quickly if the soil around their stem gets packed down hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwu bibioo ko gboɔ oya kɛji shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ fee ais lɛ?

english: Hard, packed soil prevents air and water from reaching the seedling's delicate young roots, suffocating the plant and stopping root growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni etsilɛ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu naa koni ekashɛ dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe. Ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ekpaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings look weak and stunted even during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛhe efee shoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Too much rain can flood the soil, driving out air from the roots and washing away essential plant food from the soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu. Ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ekɛ tsofai ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and build large, full ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi agboi ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that dry out easily under harsh heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa protects them from direct hot sun and dry winds.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ, ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upward and turning yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on tomato plants are often caused by a plant virus spread by tiny whiteflies. Clearing weeds around your farm helps reduce whitefly populations.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ajiemɔ Okwaafoi lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii yɛji ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Alternating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Should I sow my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until rainfall becomes consistent. The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can scorch sprouted seeds in hot soil.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Should I apply my fertilizer directly touching the stem of my plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly against the plant stem can burn the crop. It is best to dig a small ring or hole a few inches away from the plant so the roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsa ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko. loo bu ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the pods and reduce mold growth.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I see small holes and powdery dirt inside the central leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ni muji ni tamɔ powder lɛ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding on the fresh growing leaves. Checking your farm weekly allows you to catch and treat the caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai heei ni miida lɛ. Otsi fɛɛ otsi ni oookwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ ŋmeii ni otsaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and visible cracks appear in the soil around the base of the plant stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kwraa beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ je kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Weeds act as competitor plants that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and underground soil food away from your crop roots before your plants can use them.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ ashishifãi amli dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do the young cocoa pods on my trees turn black and dry up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Black, dried-up cocoa pods are usually caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, overly shaded farms. Pruning thick tree branches to let in sunlight and airflow helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa diŋ ni egbi lɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. niji ni mli tse ni afoɔ Enɛ haa hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide living shade and moisture, protecting the young cocoa during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow maize leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crop leaves need to stay green and healthy. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like NPK will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛya nɔ amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves early in the season?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli

english: Ragged holes inside the funnel of maize leaves are caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the plant leaves to feed, but can be managed by early hand-picking or applying recommended crop sprays.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ahe ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ahe baai amli koni amɛye nii. Shi abaanyɛ atsu he nii kɛtsɔ onine ni ooohala mra lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso nɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii.

english: Curled and yellow-patched leaves on cassava are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural offices is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava tsei ni helai ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ etsɔɔ mli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot so quickly after I harvest them and put them away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mifolɔ amɛ ni mikɛto he ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot easily if they get cut or bruised during harvest, or if they are stored in hot, enclosed spaces. Storing undamaged yams on raised wooden racks in a cool, well-ventilated barn keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni atsĩ naa lɛ To sweet potatoes ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he lɛ ahe yɛ tsei ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dry weather, causing it to save water instead of making fruit. Mulching the soil with dry grass and watering consistently early in the morning helps prevent this.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa. Ehaa nu baa shi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ ni okɛ nu wo mli daa leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why does my pepper plant produce lots of green leaves but very few pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pepper yibii fioo pɛ?

english: Excess green leaves with few fruits happen when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer but lacks phosphorus. Nitrogen builds big leaves, while phosphorus helps the plant produce strong flowers and plentiful fruit.
ga: Baai eŋɔlii ni fa fe nine kɛ aduawai fioo baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo shi phosphorus bɛ mli. Nitrogen lɛ feɔ baai wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, fɔsfɔs yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni mli wa kɛ aduawai babaoo.

english: Why does stubborn spear grass keep growing back so fast after I clear my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ akpɔlɔ ni yitsoŋ wa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Spear grass has deep, tough roots underground called rhizomes that remain alive even after you cut the grass above the soil. To stop it, you must dig up the underground roots completely or treat the patch with appropriate weed control.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes. Eyaa nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni ofolɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ po sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni okpa lɛ Esa akɛ Ofo shishifãi lɛ amli kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo okwɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does the rain wash away the top layer of my soil whenever it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away bare soil that has no plants or cover to hold it together. Planting cover crops like cowpeas or leaving crop residues on the ground protects the topsoil from being washed away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni tsei loo nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ nɔ ni baaha ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ he lɛ kɛtee. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ loo nibii ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he koni nu akahoo.

english: Why do my maize crops grow weaker if I plant them on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛji midu yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil consumes all the specific nutrients maize needs without giving the soil time to recover. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and keeps it fertile.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ biɔ niyenii ni he hiaa abele lɛ pɛ ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is essential food for growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ baai ni etsɛ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ tomato lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their blossoms to save energy instead of producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or thrips that spread viruses, or by severe heat stress and irregular watering.
