ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater collects in the soil without draining away, it starves the roots of air and encourages fungal rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ewo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my yam plants even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa mi sweet potato tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with yam vines for sunlight, ground space, and soil nutrients. Even with adequate rain, weeds steal the essential food the yam needs to form large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ sweet potato wain tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ hu juɔ sweet potato lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide broad leaves that create living shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when the heavy bunches start to mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and become top-heavy when carrying large bunches. Strong winds easily push them over unless you support the main stem with strong wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛhiɛ ŋmeii wuji. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa mlɛo. Ja okɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ fi tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Planting too closely causes overcrowding, forcing plants to compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and poor yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo baa. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough for planting right after the first rain of the season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain often only wets the surface. Soil is ready for planting when moisture has soaked down to at least the depth of your hand, ensuring seeds do not dry out after sprouting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ beni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ebote mli kɛyashɛ kɛ hoo lɛ nine mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akagbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on the same piece of land where I want to grow cassava next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni misumɔɔ ni madu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts add natural nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil. Rotating your cassava onto that land allows it to feed on those leftover nutrients, leading to a healthier crop without tiring out the soil.
ga: Peanuts kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ o-cassava lɛ tsɔ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni enáa niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ kpakpa ni sũ lɛ nijiaŋ ejeee wui.

english: Why does my farm yield fewer crops every year even when I work hard on the land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be moŋ.

english: Soil gets exhausted when the same crop consumes the exact same soil nutrients year after year. Allowing the land to rest or changing the crops you grow helps the soil rebuild its natural strength.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii afi fɛɛ afi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha ejɔɔ ehe loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ ato najiaŋ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ tsutsu lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How many times in a year am I supposed to spray chemical medicine on my cocoa trees?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔse kookoo tsei anɔ yɛ afi mli?

english: Chemical treatments should only be applied at specific times during the pest cycle—usually 3 to 4 times per year. Spraying excessively wastes money and can damage the blossoms on your trees.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsaa helai lɛ atsu nii yɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli pɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli, bei pii lɛ shii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ afi mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ fe nine lɛ, eji shika fitemɔ, ni ebaanyɛ efite fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: If I add more farm medicine to my knapsack sprayer than recommended, will it kill pests faster?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai babaoo fata sɛɛgbɛ tsofa ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ nii lɛ he fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ Ani ebaagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui oya?

english: Using more chemical than instructed can burn your plant leaves, contaminate your soil, and waste your money. Following exact measurements ensures pests are controlled safely without hurting your crop.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baai ashã. fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni efiteɔ shika Susumɔi pɔtɛɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa anyɛɔ akudɔɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ shweshweeshwe ni eyeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: When plants are crowded, they compete like too many children fighting over one plate of food. Giving crops proper space allows each plant to get enough light, air, and water to grow big produce.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ tamɔ gbekɛbii akuu ko ni miiye niyenii kome he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛduɔ nii babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow and thin when the field is crowded with weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that quickly steal water and fertilizers from your maize. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get the food they need to stay green and thick.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do some improved maize seeds handle dry weather better than the seeds I saved from last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni miŋmala he saji yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are bred specifically to withstand harsh conditions like short droughts or local diseases, whereas saved seeds gradually lose their strength over generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shihilɛi gbohii tamɔ hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli loo maŋ lɛ mli helai anaa. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ fiofio kɛjɛ yinɔ kome mli kɛya yinɔ kroko mli

english: Why do some of my planted seeds rot in the soil before sprouting while others sprout strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot if they are planted too deep, buried in waterlogged soil, or infected by seed-borne fungus. Planting healthy seeds at the correct depth in well-drained soil lets them sprout easily.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni dumɔwui kɛbaa lɛ emɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kpakpai ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my pepper plants struggle to produce leaves when I grow them under large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ baai beni midu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants rely heavily on direct sunlight to make their food. Dense tree shade prevents sunlight from reaching the leaves, slowing down plant growth and reducing yields.
ga: Pepper tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ waa koni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Tsei lɛ ahe hɔɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ haaa hulu la lɛ ayashɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ha tsei lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni oha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do officers advise me to cover the bare soil around my plants with dried leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔi lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dried leaves keeps the ground cool, locks in moisture during dry days, and prevents rainwater from washing away your good topsoil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli Ni etsĩɔ nugbɔ nu naa koni ekafɔ oshikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato plants need much more daily attention than my oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ daa gbi fe mi-oil palm tsei lɛ?

english: Vegetables grow very quickly and have soft stems and shallow roots, making them sensitive to heat, pests, and drought. Tree plantations like oil palm grow slowly, develop deep roots, and can withstand changing conditions once established, requiring a less frequent care schedule.
ga: Aduawai lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Enɛ haa nɛkɛ aduawai nɛɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ hɔmɔ he waa. Gbɛjegbɛi tamɔ mu tsei lɛ daa fiofio. eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ shihilɛi ni tsakeɔ lɛ anaa kɛji agbe naa pɛ. Ebiɔ be ko ni akɛkwɛɔ lɛ shii abɔ.

english: How do I set up a proper feeding schedule for my maize crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato niyenii ni sa kɛha mi-abele tsei lɛ?

english: A good crop schedule matches fertilizer timing with the plant's growth stages. Maize needs an initial feeding at planting to build strong roots, followed by a second feeding when the plant reaches knee-height to support rapid leaf growth and cob development.
ga: Dumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa haa fɔmɔ be lɛ kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be lɛ kpãa gbee. Abele biɔ klɛŋklɛŋ niyenii yɛ dumɔ mli koni shishifãi ni wa ama shi. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji niyenii ni ji enyɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe koni eye ebua baai lɛ adalɛ oya kɛ cob lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need to be spaced much further apart than my garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie kookoo tsei kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ nɛkɛ?

english: Cocoa trees grow large, heavy branches and wide roots over many years, requiring wide spacing so air and sunlight can reach them to stop fungal diseases. Garden eggs are smaller, short-term crops that can be planted closer together to make full use of garden space.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ daa niji wuji ni tsii kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Esa akɛ akɛ he ko ni jɛkɛ waa atsu nii koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la akpa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ji tsei bibii ni hiɔ shi be kukuoo ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni akɛ abɔɔ mli he lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt and droop so fast during the dry season heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetable leaves are soft and lose water rapidly through evaporation during hot afternoons. Establishing a routine watering schedule in the cool early morning helps the plants retain enough moisture to survive the peak heat of the day.
ga: Aduawai ahe baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya yɛ la ni hoɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ ato nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ he gbɛjianɔ daa yɛ leebi maŋkpa ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why does it take years for my citrus trees to produce fruit while my okra yields in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni mi-okra lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Perennial plantation crops like citrus invest their early years into building strong trunks and deep root systems to produce fruit for decades. Short-term crops like okra are programmed to mature, flower, and produce fruit quickly within a single season.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ citrus lɛ heɔ be fioo dani amɛdaraa yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli. Koni afee tsei ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baaha ewo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Atoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ okra lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛshwere, amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii oya yɛ be kome mli.

english: Can I follow the same watering and spraying routine for both cabbage and cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo nu ni mikɛshwie cabbage kɛ cassava fɛɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ?

english: No, different crops have different schedules. Cabbage has soft leaves that easily attract insects and dry out, requiring frequent checks and watering. Cassava is much hardier, holding water in its roots and requiring far less intervention to thrive.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ be srɔtoi ni akɛbaagbe naa. Kaabaji yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni gbalaa kooloi oya ni amɛgbiɔ, ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ mli shii abɔ ni awo amɛ nu. Cassava wa fe no kwraa. Amɛtoɔ nu yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛbiɔ ni akɛ he awo mli babaoo dani amɛshwere.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open after a heavy rain comes following a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ tswaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa ni nyiɛɔ hɔmɔ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When a dry plant suddenly receives a huge burst of water, the inside of the fruit swells faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to crack. Following a consistent, regular watering plan prevents this sudden shock.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ egbi lɛ, ná nu babaoo. Yibii lɛ amli fũuɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mligbalamɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni afeɔ daa kɛ daa lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ baaye abua ni akatswa tsɔne ni tswaa trukaa lɛ.

english: When is the best time in the season to prune my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tree crops should be pruned immediately after the major harvest or just before the main rainy season. This timing removes dead wood and helps the tree direct its energy into healthy new shoots when the rains begin.
ga: Esa akɛ afo tsei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ wulu ko sɛɛ loo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba. Be nɛɛ jieɔ tsei ni egboi lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ amli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ je shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my vegetable plants turning yellow even though I give them water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much water smothers the roots and prevents them from breathing or absorbing nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. A balanced schedule gives plants enough moisture without drowning their roots.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ayi obɔ kɛ mumɔ loo enyɛŋ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛjianɔtoo ni ja haa tso lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieee nu mli.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young plantains more often than around my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ bibii fe hei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Kookoo tso ni eda kwraa?

english: Young plantain suckers have shallow roots that easily lose sunlight and soil nutrients to aggressive weeds. Mature cocoa trees create a dense canopy of leaves that blocks sunlight from hitting the ground, naturally slowing weed growth.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hulu la kɛ sũ mli niyenii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛyaa jwɛi ni baa amɛŋɔɔ lɛ anɔ. Kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ feɔ baai ni mli eyi obɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekatswa shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die off whenever the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be ni Harmattan hulutsoo be lɛ baaje shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have thin leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under intense sun and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living canopy that protects the seedlings and keeps soil moisture from evaporating.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and rolling up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow and curl inward, the plant is trying to save water and is likely lacking nitrogen. Applying NPK fertilizer at the right time helps the plant stay green and build large corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔle amɛhe kɛtee mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ miitao ni amɛbu nu he ni ekolɛ nitrogen bɛ amɛmli. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli yɛ be naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody even after spending a full year in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ be mli ni mikɛ afi muu fɛɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, well-drained soil and direct sunlight to expand. If planted in hard, compacted clay soil or shaded by large trees, the plant wastes its energy growing top leaves instead of storing starch in the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli tse. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ni baaha egbɛ eshwa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atswa nɔ waa mli loo yɛ tso agbo ko shishi. Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛkwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ starch ato tuber lɛ mli.

english: Is it better to plant seeds saved from my last maize harvest or buy certified seeds from the agriculture office?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli loo aaahe dumɔwui ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ ema nɔ mi?

english: Certified seeds are bred to resist local pests, withstand unpredictable rains, and give uniform yields. Saved seeds lose their vigor over generations, resulting in weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Edamɔɔ nugbɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ naa. ni amɛfeɔ nibii ni yaa nɔ daa Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why does my tomato field produce smaller fruits every year if I keep planting them in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ woɔ yibii bibii daa afi kɛji mikɛdu yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes in the same soil continuously drains specific nutrients and allows soil-borne pests and diseases to build up. Rotating tomatoes with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally replenishes soil nitrogen and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake tomato. Ebaaha nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaakpa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: What is chewing tiny holes in my cabbage leaves, and how can I stop it without buying costly chemicals?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kaabii baai amli lɛ ni ayeɔ ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa?

english: Tiny caterpillars like the Diamondback Moth larvae eat cabbage leaves. Spraying an extract made from crushed neem leaves and water repels these pests naturally without harming your soil or crop quality.
ga: Kplukai bibii, tamɔ diamondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ kaabeji baai. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa lɛ fee lɛ kɛ nu shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaashwie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efiteee oshikpɔŋ loo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Maintaining steady soil moisture and balanced feeding keeps flowers attached so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ eyaaa nɔ be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni ja ni akɛhaa lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my yam sprouts right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to capture moisture and nutrients immediately after rain. Because yams take longer to sprout leaves, weeding early prevents wild grass from choking the young yam vines.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛmɔmɔ fɛ̃i kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, sweet potato heɔ be babaoo dani baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa koo mli jwɛi akayeɔ sweet potato wain tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested sweet potatoes rot and turn soft so quickly in my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miifite ni miifee blɛoo oya yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes rot quickly if bruised during harvest or kept in hot, unventilated rooms. Curing them in a dark, cool, and airy space for a few days toughens their skin and prevents fungal rot during storage.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ atsa lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha hewolo lɛ mli awa. ni atsĩ fungal rot naa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ

english: Why should I bury fertilizer in small holes near my plants instead of scattering it across the soil surface?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ bu bibii amli lɛ? ni bɛŋkɛ tsei moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Placing fertilizer near the roots allows the plant to absorb nutrients directly. Broadcasting it on top allows heavy rains to wash it away or sunlight to evaporate the nutrients before the plant roots reach them.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ. Aloo hulu la lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. This often happens when the soil is worn out or after heavy rains wash away the nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ejie niyenii mli nibii ni haa tsei lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy and humid weather. Removing affected pods early and pruning tree branches to let sunlight in helps keep the trees healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ mra Ni afoɔ tsei lɛ aniji koni hulu la abote mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem. This typically happens between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni amɛshi shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and small cobs with very few grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii kɛ dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars or beetles. Checking under leaves early in the morning and spraying with organic neem extract or recommended remedies helps protect the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaaba baa mli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi leebi ni okɛ organic neem extract loo tsofa kroko ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling in heat is the plant's natural defense to save water and prevent drying out. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down or after watering, the plant is simply coping with the afternoon sun.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi loo beni awo lɛ nu sɛɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eshɛ shwane hulu lɛ he.

english: Can I save seeds from my current hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ hybrid ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is better to buy fresh certified hybrid seeds each season. Grains saved from hybrid harvests will grow into weaker plants with lower yields because the strong hybrid qualities only work in the first generation.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmaa ni akɛfee nibii sɔrɔtoi amli lɛ daa kɛfeɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo baa shi. Enɛ ji akɛ, hybrid nibii ni mli wa lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ.

english: Why do weeds always grow back faster and stronger than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions. They absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, which is why clearing them early gives your crops a fair chance.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie amɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa.

english: How can I stop my harvested yams from rotting quickly in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when exposed to damp ground, direct sunlight, or physical cuts. Storing them off the ground in a shade-covered, well-ventilated yam barn keeps them dry and extends their shelf life.
ga: Sweet potato yibii fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛ tee hei ni efɔ, hulu la tɛ̃ɛ, loo gbɔmɔtsoŋ piŋmɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes shwie shikpɔŋ yɛ sweet potatoes ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young maize leaves early in the season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by fall armyworm caterpillars. Checking your farm early allows you to catch them before they destroy the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ feɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ. Okwaafoi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni omɔ amɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ yitsei lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves. Spraying with neem oil or mild insecticidal soap can help clear them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni waaa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni efɔ amɛhe.

english: Why should I alternate planting beans with my maize instead of growing maize every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ moŋ fe ŋmãa ni miduɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the ground, while leguminous crops like beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and add it back into the soil, keeping your land fertile.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii

english: How can I tell if my crop land needs fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu?

english: If your previous harvest gave very low yields, or if your previous crops showed pale yellowish leaves despite getting enough water, the soil is low in nutrients and needs manure, compost, or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji okpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ wo yibii ni baa shi kwraa Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okpa tsutsu lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni oná lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells to save water and stay alive. Once the rains start again, the plant will sprout new green leaves and continue growing its roots.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi wala mli. Kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni eŋɔli ni shishifãi lɛ baaya nɔ ada.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop in the afternoon heat even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon sun makes plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it up. If your tomato plants stand back up by morning, they are fine and just reacting to afternoon heat.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛji akɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ damɔ shi leebi lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa shwane mli latsaa lɛ hetoo kɛkɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and moisture while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my young crops as soon as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni mi dumɔwui lɛ adara kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ.

english: Young crops grow slowly and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Removing weeds early gives your crops a strong head start.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems. Piling extra soil around the base (mounding) and supporting fruit-bearing stems with wooden bamboo props prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Shikpɔŋ krokomɛi ni akɛbaabɔle shishigbɛ (pile) lɛ he kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛfiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahe lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaje shishi.

english: Why do many of my cocoa flowers fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ babaoo miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small portion get pollinated by tiny insects or receive enough nutrients to become full pods. High shade or low soil moisture can also cause flower drop.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii pɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ lɛ pollin. loo nine ashɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ ni baaha etswa ni etsɔ dumɔwui akui ni eyi obɔ Shade ni nɔ kwɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How long does a plantain crop usually take from the day I plant it until I can harvest the fruit?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani akwɛɔ plantains kɛjɛɔ gbi ni miduɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni abaanyɛ akpa aduawai lɛ?

english: Plantains generally take about 11 to 15 months to produce mature fruit from the time you plant a healthy shoot, depending on rainfall, soil richness, and how well you care for the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains heɔ aaafee nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni oduɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Edamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ bɔ ni okwɛɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ ohaa lɛ nɔ

english: How does a plantain plant reproduce itself, and can I use the small shoots around the main stem to start a new farm?
ga: Te dumɔwui fɔɔ bii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ? Ni manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii bibii atsu nii. Abɔle tso wulu lɛ he koni aje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Plantain plants multiply by growing small shoots called 'suckers' from an underground stem base. You can carefully dig up these healthy suckers and replant them on fresh land to grow new plantain trees.
ga: Agbɛɔ dumɔwui ashwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘ŋmeii’ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nɛkɛ tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ ahe nii ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ koni ona plantain hee.

english: What happens if I plant my plantain suckers too close to one another on my plot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If plantain suckers are planted too close together, their large leaves block sunlight from each other, causing the plants to grow tall and weak while producing much smaller bunches of fruit due to competition for light and nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai wuji lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛwoɔ aduawai akui bibii kwraa yɛ akaŋshii ni amɛfeɔ kɛha la kɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ hewɔ.

english: Plantains have very wide leaves and shallow roots, which cause them to lose moisture rapidly in hot weather. When the soil dries out, the plant sheds or yellows its lower leaves to save water and keep the main stem alive.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ lɛ, tso lɛ baashwie eshishi baai lɛ loo ebaafee ŋmɔŋ koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha eshishifã titri lɛ akafite.

english: Why do plantain trees fall over so easily when a strong wind blow through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have a long taproot going deep into the earth; instead, they rely on a bunch of shallow roots near the surface. When a tree carries a heavy bunch of fruit, top-heavy wind pressure can easily pull its shallow root system out of wet soil.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ e hɛ fɔ sisi nɛ mi kuɔ we nɔ. ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ moŋ Beni tso lɛ woɔ aduawai babaoo Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Ejeɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ mlɛo

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my young plantains slow down their growth so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? Mi plantains lɛ miiha amɛdalɛ miiba shi babaoo?

english: Young plantains have roots close to the surface that share the exact same soil depth as weeds. Weeds aggressively steal the water and soil nutrients meant for the plantain, causing the young plant to grow much slower.
ga: Plantain bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ tamɔ jwɛi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha plantains lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ daraa blɛoo kwraa.

english: What type of land or soil is best for growing plantains successfully?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha plantains ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ omanye?

english: Plantains thrive best in soft, deep, black or dark soils rich in decomposed plant matter that stay moist but do not flood, as water standing around the roots for long periods causes them to rot.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni ji ediŋŋ, loo ni mli edɔ ni tsei ni egbo ni hiɔ shi ŋmɔtɔ shi nu afuaa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni ta shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha amɛgboi.

english: Can I plant other crops like vegetables or beans alongside my young plantains, or will it harm the plantain?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii yɛ mi plantains bibii lɛ ahe? Aloo ebaaye plantains lɛ awui loo ebaayeee amɛ awui?

english: You can safely grow short-term crops like beans or leafy vegetables between young plantains. These companion crops shade the ground to reduce weeds and can even add nutrients back into the soil while the plantain trees are still small.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu be kukuoo mli nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai ni baai yɔɔ mli. shweshweeshwe yɛ plantains bibii ateŋ Nɛkɛ nanemɛi tsei nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ koni jwɛi lɛ aba shi. Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ hu aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: How do I know that my plantain plant is about to start producing a bunch of fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-plantains lɛ miibɔi aduawai akui fɔmɔ?

english: Before fruiting, the plant stops producing new full-sized leaves and shoots out a large, reddish-purple bell-shaped bud from the center of the top leaf canopy, which opens up over time to reveal fingers of plantain.
ga: dani ewoɔ yibii Tso lɛ kpaɔ baai heei ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu lɛ feemɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii agboi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɛlɛ ni tamɔ ŋmɛlɛ kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ baagbele yɛ be ni sa mli koni ejie plantain niji lɛ akpo.

english: Does a single plantain tree continue to produce fruit year after year, or does it die after harvest?
ga: Ani dumɔwu kome pɛ yaa nɔ ewoɔ yibii afi fɛɛ afi loo egboɔ yɛ nikpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: A single plantain stem produces fruit only once in its life and dies after harvest. However, new suckers continuously grow at the base of the old stem to take over and produce future harvests.
ga: Dumɔwu kome woɔ yibii shikome pɛ yɛ eshihilɛ mli, ni egboɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, dumɔwui heei baaya nɔ akwɛ̃ yɛ tso momo lɛ shishi koni amɛye nɔ ni amɛwo wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I let cleared weeds rot on the land instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ miha jwɛi ni ajie lɛ gboi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic plant food in the soil and kills helpful soil organisms. Letting cleared weeds rot down slowly turns them into natural manure, keeping the dirt moist and fertile for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei aniyenii ni fa babaoo lɛ, ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Ni aaaha jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ afite fiofio Enɛ baaha amɛfee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha muji lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha onibii.

english: Why should I make raised ridges or mounds before planting my yams instead of planting on flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ dani madu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand easily under the ground. Mounds loosen the soil so the roots grow long and fat, while also preventing heavy rains from standing around the seeds and causing rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi mlɛo. Gɔji lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ asɛɛ atsɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekadamɔ shi ebɔle ehe. dumɔwui kɛ fitemɔ

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava cuttings too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other and their roots fight for food in the dirt. Spacing them properly allows each plant to build large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Baai lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do many farmers plant beans or cowpeas in the same farm with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo duɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans have a special ability to capture nitrogen plant food from the air and put it back into the soil. This naturally feeds the heavy-eating maize plants and keeps the soil healthy without extra costs.
ga: Beans yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni ekɛmɔɔ nitrogen tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni tsii lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow from the tip inwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiya mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a cry for help showing that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores the green color and helps the plant produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Does leaving tall grass and weeds around my young pepper plants really affect how much pepper I harvest?
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji kɛ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi-pepper tso bibioo lɛ saa pepper ni mikpaa lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, weeds act like thieves that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your pepper plants get full energy to grow many strong flowers and fruits.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ mli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha o-pepper tso lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the tiny flowers on my tomato plants fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from water stress during hot sun or when small sucking insects damage the stem. Regular watering at the root level and protecting the blossoms helps them turn into juicy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa, ni abuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi ni mli edɔ.

english: Watering early in the morning allows moisture to soak deep into the soil before the sun gets hot. Afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani hulu lɛ haa edɔɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my oil palm bunches to get good quality oil for market buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa mu tsei akui koni maná mu ni hi jogbaŋŋ aha mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: The best time to harvest is when a few ripe fruitlets naturally detach and fall to the ground. Harvesting too early yields thin, low-quality oil, while harvesting too late makes the oil sour and watery, lowering its market value.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa ji be mli ni aduawai fioo komɛi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha mu lɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii ni ebaafee mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa fɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha fɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji jarayeli jara ni baa shi.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize grains thoroughly before putting them into sacks for storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ dani mikɛwo kotokui amli koni mikɛto lɛ?

english: Damp maize creates the perfect environment for destructive molds and insects to breed and ruin the grain. Drying the maize until it is hard and dry keeps it fresh for months and attracts higher prices at the market.
ga: Abɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ koni amɛfɔ ni amɛfite ŋmaa lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ebaawa ni egbi lɛ, ebaaha ehi shi nyɔji babaoo. ni egbalaa jarayeli jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why should I cut off leaves and healthy-looking branches from my crops when they are growing so well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai kɛ tsei niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ? Beni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cutting off excess leaves and branches, known as pruning, helps the plant direct its food and water into growing bigger, healthier fruits and tubers instead of wasting energy on useless green leaves.
ga: Baai kɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛɔ niyenii kɛ nu nɔ koni amɛfee aduawai kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I allow all the side branches and suckers to grow wild?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ? Akɛni miha tsei lɛ aniji kɛ amɛsɛɛ tsei lɛ dara yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe hewɔ lɛ.

english: Extra suckers and dense branches block sunlight from reaching the trunk and steal nutrients from the tree, which reduces pod growth and creates a damp environment where diseases like black pod thrive.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi kɛ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aba shi. ni efee shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli.

english: If I pluck off some of the weak flowers from my crop, won't that reduce my harvest?
ga: Kɛ mijie fɔfɔi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ Ani no haŋ nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: No, removing extra or weak flower buds allows the plant to channel its full energy into the remaining flowers, producing larger, heavier, and better-quality fruits that yield a higher market value.
ga: Dabi, fɔfɔi krokomɛi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa fɔfɔi ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai ni dara, ni tsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa. ni haa jara nɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ

english: Is it better for me to put all my energy into properly caring for one main plot, or should I spread my effort across several small farms?
ga: Ani ebafeŋ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛ mihewalɛ baakwɛ shikpɔŋ titri kome nɔ jogbaŋŋ? Aloo esa akɛ magbɛ mimɔdɛŋbɔɔ lɛ mashwa ŋmɔji bibii babaoo amli?

english: Focusing completely on one well-managed plot usually yields far more food and income than spreading your effort thinly across multiple neglected fields where weeds and pests can destroy your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kome ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛjwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ lɛ baaha aná niyenii kɛ shika babaoo fe mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔji babaoo ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ amli. he ni jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ afite onibii lɛ

english: Why do some farmers in my community get much higher crop yields even though we farm on the same soil type?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ wɔtsuɔ okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Higher yields often come from fully committing to best practices—such as proper spacing, timely weeding, and full fertilizer application—rather than doing only half of the required field operations.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nitsumɔ ni nɔ kwɔ jɛɔ hetuu-kɛhamɔ ni yeɔ emuu kɛha nifeemɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ, tamɔ gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, atsu ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ni he hiaa lɛ fã pɛ.

english: What happens if I leave part of my weeding work until the next farming season instead of finishing it now?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mishi mi jwɛi ŋmɔmɔ nitsumɔ lɛ eko kɛyashi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafee amrɔ nɛɛ hu?

english: Leaving weeds to mature allows them to drop seeds and multiply, while also harboring pests over the dry season, making your field much harder and more expensive to clear during the next planting season.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, ehaa amɛduɔ nii ni amɛshwereɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa oŋmɔji lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa waa ni ejara wa waa kɛha jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Can I save half of the recommended fertilizer for my maize crop to use on next year's farm instead?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ fã ato koni mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli afi ni baa lɛ moŋ?

english: Crops need a specific amount of nutrients at critical growth stages; giving them only half starves the current crop during its growth period, and saved fertilizer can lose its potency over time.
ga: Tsei biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ amɛdalɛ bei ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. Hɔmɔ aye amɛ be lɛ fã yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baanyɛ akatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds early in the rainy season instead of waiting until my crops are tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mamɛ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Young crops are delicate and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, so clearing weeds early gives your main crop the strongest start possible.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ.

english: Why should I follow every step of a recommended planting method instead of just picking one or two steps to try?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ mli gbɛ fɛɛ gbɛ nɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo bɔ mɔde nɛ o hla blɔ kake loo enyɔ pɛ.

english: Good farming practices work together like a complete system; skipping steps like proper spacing or timely feeding can spoil the whole yield, even if you did the other parts correctly.
ga: Okwaayeli nifeemɔi kpakpai feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni yeɔ emuu. Nibii tamɔ gbɛ ni sa loo niyenii ni akɛhaa yɛ be naa lɛ ni aaatsɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛji ofee fãi krokomɛi po Kɛji eja po

english: Why are we advised to completely remove and destroy diseased plants immediately instead of leaving them until harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔjie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni wɔfite amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni wɔɔshi amɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Diseased plants act as breeding grounds that quickly spread infection to surrounding healthy crops through wind, rain, and insects, so removing them right away saves the rest of your field.
ga: Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kɛ kooloi anɔ, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ojie amɛ oya lɛ, ebaahere he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ yiwala.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, a vital nutrient for leaf growth. It can also happen when excess rainwater washes nutrients away from the roots. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the crop dies and decomposes, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crops you plant, such as maize or cassava.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbo ni egbo lɛ, Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Heavy rain can saturate flat soil, filling up all the tiny air pockets with water and suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the tubers stay dry enough to grow healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. fɛɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a shield against the harsh sun, keeping the soil cool and moist for longer so you do not have to water as often, while also stopping weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni okɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ gãimlibi ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why are there small holes and sawdust-like waste inside the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni ŋmeii lɛ yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the fall armyworm, a small caterpillar that hides deep inside the leaf funnel of the corn plant to feed on tender green shoots. Applying safe bio-pesticides or clean neem leaf extract early in the morning into the center of the plant can eliminate them.
ga: Fall armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ baai amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni he tse wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up when the wet season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This issue is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in damp, shady weather. Pruning extra branches from your cocoa trees allows sunlight and fresh air to dry out the farm canopy, preventing the fungus from multiplying.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kookoo tsei lɛ aniji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋwɛitsu lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkafee babaoo

english: Why do my corn plants grow thin, tall, and weak when I sow seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete aggressively with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and soil water. Proper spacing gives each crop its own area to absorb nutrients, allowing stems to grow thick and stalks to produce large, full ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ waa. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa baaha tso henɔ fɛɛ henɔ aná hegbɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyɛ tsei lɛ agboi kɛ baai ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce the food energy needed to form large underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves high in the sun and off the wet ground, which also protects the plant from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ hulu lɛ mli ni amɛjeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my pepper plants fall off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, poor soil moisture, or a sudden change in weather. Giving your plants consistent moisture during dry periods keeps the flowers healthy so they can turn into pepper fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi trukaa Kɛ́ afee tso lɛ ŋmɔtɔ daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛtsɔ aduawai ni mli edɔ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and sunken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efo mli lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot. It happens when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium during fruit development, usually caused by irregular watering that makes it difficult for roots to absorb soil nutrients continuously.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli, ni haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛ baa ŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ daa.

english: Why do my crops yield so much produce during certain months of the year but stop producing in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli shi amɛkpaa ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Crops respond to natural environmental signals like rainfall, daylight hours, and temperature. During rainy seasons, plants receive maximum water and nutrients to produce flowers and fruits in abundance, while in dry periods, they conserve energy to survive.
ga: Tsei hereɔ shihilɛ mli okadii tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ, hulutsoo be, kɛ dɔlɛ nɔ. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, tsei lɛ naa nu kɛ niyenii babaoo ni haa amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai babaoo. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, tsei toɔ hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my fruit trees produce a massive harvest one year and very little fruit the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ wo yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: This behavior is known as alternate bearing. A bumper harvest drains the tree's stored nutrients, so the plant needs the following year to rebuild its reserves before it can produce a large harvest again.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ fallback gbɛtsɔɔmɔ. Nikpamɔ ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ mli niyenii ni ato lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná be yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli koni amɛsaa amɛhe nibii ni amɛto lɛ ekoŋŋ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii babaoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do crop fruits mature faster and drop off the plants when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya ni amɛgbee shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High temperatures speed up a plant's internal chemical processes, forcing fruits to ripen quickly. Extreme heat also causes water stress, making the plant drop its fruit early to save water and keep itself alive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ yaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa hu kɛ nu he haomɔ baa. Ha tso lɛ ajie eyibii lɛ oya koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha ehi wala mli.

english: How do I know the exact time my tomatoes are ready to be harvested from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni tomatoi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Tomatoes show clear signs of maturity when their skin changes from green to light pink or red, the fruit feels slightly soft to a gentle squeeze, and it separates easily from the stem with a gentle twist.
ga: Tomato jieɔ dalɛ he okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛ́ ehewolo lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee pinki loo etsuru ni mli tse mli. Yibii lɛ baanu he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ fioo kɛji akɛ ota he, ni ebaatse ehe kɛjɛ tso lɛ he oya kɛtsɔ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ lɛ blɛoo nɔ.

english: How do changes in the timing of the rainy season affect when my crops will be ready for harvest?
ga: Te tsakemɔi ni baa nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ saa be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops depend on water to fuel their growth stages. Delayed rains postpone flowering and fruiting, while early or heavy rains speed up growth, making accurate harvest timing dependent on when the rains actually start.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ nu nɔ koni eha amɛdara. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baaha fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha ekwɛ̃ oya. Enɛ haa kpamɔ be pɔtɛɛ lɛ damɔ be ni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the best way to store my harvested maize so it doesn't spoil or get destroyed by insects?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maha mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ akafite loo ŋmeii akafite lɛ?

english: Maize should be dried thoroughly until the grains are hard, cleaned of all field dust, and stored in airtight hermetic bags or elevated, ventilated cribs treated with approved grain protectants to keep moisture and weevils out.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nyɛjiea sũ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ. ni akɛtoɔ kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo tsɔne ni kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli waa ni akɛ nɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ mli.

english: How can I prevent my cassava roots from rotting if I cannot harvest them all at once?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite kɛji minyɛɛɛ makpa amɛ fɛɛ shikome?

english: Cassava roots can safely remain stored underground in the living plant for up to two years, provided the field is well-drained and free from waterlogging or root diseases.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei shishifãi ato shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe yɛ tso ko ni hiɛ ka mli kɛyashi afii enyɔ. Kɛji akɛ nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni nu loo shishifã hela bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: What should I do to keep my harvested yams fresh for many months without them decaying?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ahi shi nyɔji babaoo ni efiteee?

english: Yams must be handled carefully during harvest to avoid cuts, cured in a shaded area for a few days to harden their skins, and kept off the ground inside a well-ventilated yam barn protected from direct sunlight.
ga: Esa akɛ akwɛ sweet potato nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli koni akafolɔ mli. Okɛwo he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ gbii fioo komɛi koni hewolo lɛ afee shiŋŋ. ni okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ato ŋmeii atsu ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Buu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Is it possible for me to grow crops like watermelons during the dry season when there is no rain?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ watermelon yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Yes, you can grow crops during the dry season by using irrigation systems like drip lines or by planting in low-lying valley bottoms where the soil retains moisture throughout the dry months.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi tamɔ drip line nɔ, loo kɛtsɔ dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baahiɛ nu yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔshiimɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do food prices drop so low in the market whenever all farmers harvest at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii jara baa shi yɛ jara nɔ be fɛɛ be ni okwaafoi baakpa nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When many farmers bring crops to market simultaneously, supply exceeds buyer demand. Because fresh produce spoils quickly, farmers lower prices to sell their goods fast before they decay.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo kɛ amɛŋmɔshi nibii baa jara nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ. Nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hɔlɔ lɛ taoɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai kɛ aduawai ni afee ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ okwaafoi baa jara shi koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ amɛnibii lɛ oya dani nibii lɛ fite.

english: Why should I use wooden frames or stakes to spread out the main branches of my young trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ trellis loo tsei atsu nii kɛgbɛ midumɔwui lɛ aniji titrii lɛ ashwã?

english: Spreading out the main branches on a frame helps sunlight and fresh air reach every part of the plant, encouraging the tree to grow balanced and produce flowers evenly.
ga: Niji titrii lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How do I decide which main branches on my tree to keep and which ones to remove?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ mitso lɛ niji titrii ni esa akɛ mahi shi kɛ nɔ ni majie kɛjɛ mli lɛ he?

english: You should keep strong branches that grow outwards at wide angles and remove branches that rub against each other, grow straight down, or block light from reaching the middle.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ ahi he ko ni da. Ni jiemɔ tsei niji ni shwieɔ amɛhe, ni daa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shi, loo ni tsiɔ la naa koni ekashɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ohe.

english: Why does my tree suddenly sprout many small green shoots very quickly after I trim its upper branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ miikwɛ̃ trukaa lɛ? Mɛi babaoo oya beni mifo tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When top branches are removed, the tree uses energy stored in its roots to rapidly grow new leaves so it can continue making food from sunlight.
ga: Kɛji ajie ŋwɛi niji lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai heei oya koni amɛya nɔ amɛfee niyenii kɛjɛ hulu la mli.

english: What is the difference between light trimming and cutting off big branches on my farm trees?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsei ni afolɔ fioo kɛ tsei ni afolɔ wulu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Light trimming just removes small dead twigs to keep the tree tidy, while heavy pruning cuts larger main branches to open up the canopy and restart fresh growth.
ga: Niji bibii pɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ jieɔ tsei lɛ. Jiemɔ he ni egbo lɛ koni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni afolɔ waa lɛ jieɔ tsei niji wuji lɛ koni egbele tso lɛ shishi ni ebɔi dalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to cut major branches off my cocoa trees during the dry season in December?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji agboi yɛ December mli nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Cutting heavy branches in the dry season can be risky because the harsh sun can burn the exposed bark and dry out the tree when water is scarce.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashã hulu lɛ, ni eha tsei lɛ agbi kɛ́ nu faaa.

english: What is the best time of year for me to trim back my trees so they recover fast?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafolɔ mitso lɛ koni ehiɛ aya nɔ oya?

english: The best time to trim trees is usually right after harvest or just before the main rains start, so the rainfall helps the tree quickly grow back healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afo tsei ji beni akpa tsei lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ loo dani nugbɔ lɛ baabɔi nɛmɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛná baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ oya.

english: If I cut off too many branches from my crop at once, will it damage or kill the tree?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mifolɔ niji babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be kome mli hu? Ani ebaafite tso lɛ loo ebaagbe lɛ?

english: Yes, taking off too many branches at once shocks the plant because it loses the leaves it needs to feed itself, which can delay fruiting or stunt growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji babaoo ni afolɔ shikome lɛ baaha tso lɛ he akpokpo. Ejaakɛ baai ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ena lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii lɛ laajeɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha aduawai lɛ asɛɛ afo loo amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut off healthy-looking leaves and branches from our crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ baai kɛ tsei niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ wɔŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Removing excess branches directs the plant's food and energy away from useless leaves and straight into growing bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: How does clearing out the crowded branches inside my tree stem help protect it from diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mitso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akamɔ mi?

english: Crowded branches trap moisture and humidity, which creates a home for black pod and fungal diseases; opening up the branches allows wind and sun to dry the plant.
ga: Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni no haa ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ helai feɔ shĩa. Tso lɛ niji lɛ ni agbeleɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa tso lɛ gĩɔ.

english: Will cutting back my crop's branches reduce the total amount of harvest I get at the end of the season?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: No, while it looks like you have fewer branches, the tree actually produces larger and better-quality fruit because all nutrients go into the remaining branches.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni obɛ niji fioo moŋ, shi yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, tso lɛ woɔ yibii wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ baaya tsei niji ni eshwɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates a cool environment and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baadara ni enyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ.

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in high humidity and wet conditions. Pruning excess leaves to let in sunlight and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm and keeps the pods dry.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni ajie jwɛi lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ amli gbiɔ.

english: What is eating small holes through the leaves of my young maize plants and hiding inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Kɛtsɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai anɔ ni akɛtee ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant during the day and eat the leaves; applying safe, recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening targets them effectively.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii shweshweeshwe leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatswa ehiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my maize farm so it grows tall and yields big cobs?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni tsei lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛwo ŋmãa wuji?

english: Maize needs fertilizer at two key stages: a small amount at planting or two weeks after germination to help roots develop, and a second boost when the plant reaches knee-high height to support stem growth and grain filling.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛi titrii enyɔ nɔ: fioo ko yɛ be mli ni aduɔ loo otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shii enyɔ nɔ beni tso lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe koni eye ebua tso lɛ shishifã lɛ dalɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground when I harvest them after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ akpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when left in waterlogged soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away from the roots, preventing rot during wet seasons.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa yɛ nugbɔ be mli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to build large, healthy yam tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛbai lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but the blossoms drop off without producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi efoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms often drop off due to extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Ensuring regular watering during hot weather and avoiding excessive nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant hold its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii hewɔ. Kɛ́ oha otso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni okɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otso lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards, shrinking, and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is typically caused by a viral infection spread by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids. Controlling these pest insects early with proper sprays prevents them from spreading the virus across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil. When you rotate or mix them with maize, they naturally feed the soil and make it richer for your crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmãa tsake loo okɛfutu lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhaa efeɔ nii babaoo kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I choose which new plantain shoots to keep around my main stem and which ones to remove?
ga: Mahala tsei heei ni mikɛbaahi shi. Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ajie tso titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni ajie lɛ

english: Keep shoots with narrow, spear-like leaves because they grow fast and produce strong bunches. Cut away shoots with broad, wide leaves close to the ground, as they drain nutrients away from the main plant without yielding good fruit.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya ni amɛfeɔ kui ni mli wa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni ekɛ yibii kpakpai ko baaa.

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing moisture during hot weather. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss until cooler evening temperatures or rain arrive.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni ŋmɔtɔ akaje mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni haa nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ loo nugbɔ baashɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers during extremely hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants and dries out pollen, preventing fruit formation. The plant drops flowers to conserve its remaining water and energy until weather conditions cool down.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ aduawai anaa Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without ever turning into cocoa pods?
