ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee kookoo ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small portion turn into pods. The tree drops extra flowers if it lacks sufficient soil moisture or energy, or if midge insects are not present to pollinate them.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ E pɛ ebafeɔ pod. Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi krokomɛi kɛji ŋmɔtɔ loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ midge kooloi bɛ ni baanyɛ afee pollination

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully matured and ready to harvest so I do not dig them up too early?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ oyaiyeli tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. Look for the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, along with visible cracks forming in the soil around the base of the main stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Taomɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ ŋmeii ni anaa ni feɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can capture direct sunlight. Maximum exposure to sunlight allows the leaves to make more food, which fuels the growth of larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo lɛ haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. ni ji tsofa ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ daa lɛ

english: Why does my plantain sucker take more than a year before it starts showing a fruit bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain sucker lɛ heɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani ebɔi aduawai akui fɔmɔ?

english: Plantains require 12 to 15 months to build a sturdy trunk, produce large leaf canopy leaves, and establish deep roots. The stem needs to store enough energy before it can support a heavy stalk of fruit.
ga: Nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 he miihia plantains dani enyɛ efee ŋmeii ni wa. Ewoɔ ŋmeii agboi ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ baa Esa akɛ tso lɛ ato hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa dani enyɛ eye ebua aduawai tso ni tsii lɛ.

english: Why do my bean seeds fail to sprout when I plant them deep inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛdu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: If planted too deeply, bean seeds run out of stored energy before the shoot can break through the soil to reach sunlight. Beans should be planted shallowly so the tender shoots can emerge quickly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, Bean dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hulu la. Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ anyɛ ajie oya.

english: Yellow bottom leaves indicate that the soil is low in nitrogen. The corn plant copes by shifting nitrogen from its older lower leaves to feed the newly growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei tsuɔ enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Will planting cowpeas together in the same field with my maize harm my crops?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: No, planting cowpeas alongside maize is helpful. Cowpeas cover the soil to keep it moist and cool, and their roots fix nitrogen from the air into the soil, which feeds the maize plants.
ga: Dabi, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he. Cowpeas haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ. Ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmeii tsei lɛ náa niyenii.

english: Why do black spots appear and spread on my cocoa pods during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa yɛ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates high humidity, which helps the black pod fungal disease grow and spread rapidly. Pruning excess branches and clearing farm weeds improves air circulation, keeping pods drier and safer.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni no yeɔ ebuaa black pod fungus hela lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizers like urea or ammonium sulphate early in the plant's growth will help the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ammonium sulfate wo tso lɛ shishijee be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes, meaning they have a special ability to trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them with maize naturally enriches your soil and helps your maize grow better without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛmɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ni eye ebua oŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the plants grow very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ waa moŋ?

english: If cassava plants are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, causing them to put all their energy into growing tall leaves instead of tubers. Spacing them about one meter apart gives the roots enough room and food to grow big.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa akɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛwo baai kakadaji yɛ bulbs najiaŋ. Aaafee mita kome ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara.

english: Plantain trees naturally grow many young shoots called suckers around their base, which steal water and food from the main stem. Cutting away the extra suckers and leaving only two or three strong ones allows the main plant to direct its energy into producing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, plantains yɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers, ni bɔleɔ amɛshishigbɛ, ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ ni ekɛfee fɔfɔii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves up high to catch as much sunlight as possible, which helps the plant manufacture food to grow a large tuber underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni ekɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and thin stems that easily burn and dry out under direct, intense heat from the sun. Keeping larger shade trees or planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides a cool umbrella that protects the seedlings while they get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ tsei bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akwɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha aná hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛmaa shi lɛ.

english: Curled and twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves. Spraying your pepper plants with neem oil extract or a recommended organic pesticide gets rid of these pests and allows new leaves to grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni eha baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rot before they can turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani efeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when watering is uneven or the soil is too dry. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil prevents this rotting.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Ehe miihia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ lime loo tso sũ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni enɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers keep falling off the plant without forming any bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop when tiny insects called flower thrips attack and feed on the blossoms before they can set pods. Spraying a mild, safe insecticide just as the plant starts producing buds protects the flowers so they can turn into full pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii ni ale amɛ akɛ fɔfɔi thrips lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ dani amɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie nɔ beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ fɔfɔii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing big loose leaves instead of forming a hard, tight ball in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Agbo moŋ fe ni eeefee nɔ ko ni wa yɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form solid heads if the weather gets too hot, if they do not get enough steady water, or if they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer late in their growth. Regular watering and using a balanced fertilizer helps the plant roll its center leaves into a tight, solid head.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni wa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ onine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ aná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ daa blɛoo lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ ni efeɔ bulb ni mli wa ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and lose water quickly. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade that keeps the soil cool and protects the seedlings until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni nu lɛ hu sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow from the bottom up even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the base of the maize helps the plant regain its dark green color and grow healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he Abɛi shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aná eŋɔlii ni tsuɔ waa lɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha toi lɛ afee hewalɛ.

english: Should I apply chemical fertilizer on my farm at the same time I put the seeds in the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ be kome too mli? Kɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo daabi?

english: Putting chemical fertilizer directly on seeds before they sprout can burn the seeds and destroy them. It is best to wait about one to two weeks after the seeds sprout so the young roots are ready to absorb the food without getting damaged.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui lɛ ni egbe amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ koni shishifãi bibii lɛ afee klalo ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground through their roots. Planting them alongside or after maize naturally enriches the soil so future crops grow bigger without needing as much store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ wɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ daa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Planting cassava sticks about one meter apart gives each stem enough space underground to spread its roots and swell into big tubers. If you plant them too close together, the roots will fight for water and food, resulting in small, thin cassava roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛgbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ashiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ

english: When too many young shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they steal nutrients and water from the mother plant. Cutting away extra shoots and leaving only two or three strong ones allows the main tree to devote its energy to producing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ, ŋmeii nɛɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ashi niji fioo komɛi pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ baatsu niji agboi ni tsii ni efee lɛ he nii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the sunlight so their leaves can make food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the ground exposes them to sunlight and airflow, which feeds the growing yam tuber under the soil and prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Yɛ hulu la mli bɔni afee ni akɛ ebaai lɛ atsu nii akɛ niyenii aha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa amɛnɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aha sweet potato ŋmeii ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii, ni ebaatsi foliar helai anaa.

english: Why does my soil become hard and cracked just a few days after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture quickly under the sun because there is nothing to trap the water inside the dirt. Covering the ground around your crops with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks direct sunlight, stops the soil from baking hard, and keeps it moist longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la shishi ejaakɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni hiɛɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my crop seeds rot in the soil when I plant immediately after the very first rain in April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ April mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by several hot, dry days before the regular rains actually settle in. Planting too early means seeds absorb water, start to open, and then bake in the hot, drying soil before the next rain comes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baa. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baaŋɔ nu, amɛbaabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ, ni amɛbaashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dust inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: Ragged leaves with saw-dust-like dropping in the funnel are signs of the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. These pests hide inside the plant to eat the fresh leaves, so catching them early and applying approved treatments inside the leaf funnel protects your crop yield.
ga: Baai ni ekpɔtɔ ni ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei amli koni amɛye baai heei. No hewɔ lɛ, mɔmɔ amɛ mra. Ni kɛ okɛ tsofafeemɔ gbɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce large leaves that provide living shade and moisture, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to survive full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enáa hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I leave space between my cassava stems when planting them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that each plant's roots have enough room under the soil to expand into large tubers without competing with neighboring plants for nutrients and sunlight.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso shishifãi náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ akaŋ yɛ niyenii kɛ hulu la he.

english: Why is it better to plant my maize at the very start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting early allows crop roots to grow deep into the soil using initial moisture, helping the plants build strong stalks before heavy downpours or dry mid-season spells occur.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛtsɔ shishijee nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa amɛshishifãi ni wa dani nugbɔ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ be teŋgbɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why do many of my cocoa flowers dry up and drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need pollen from other flowers to form pods. In nature, tiny insects do this work, but if there are few insects or poor air movement, the unpollinated flowers simply drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia pollen ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi amli lɛ koni amɛfee pods. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, kooloi bibii tsuɔ nitsumɔ nɛɛ, shi kɛji kooloi fioo pɛ yɔɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries out the pollen inside the flowers, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gĩɔ. Ha tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite.

english: How do bees and tiny insects actually help my crops yield more produce?
ga: Wuobii kɛ kooloi bibii Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: As insects search for nectar, they carry pollen dust from one flower to another. This movement fertilizes the flower, which is necessary for the plant to form fruit and seeds.
ga: Beni kooloi bibii taoɔ fɔfɔi amli nu lɛ Amɛwoɔ pollen sũ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Nɛkɛ nyiɛmɔ nɛɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi, ni he hiaa koni tso lɛ awo yibii kɛ dumɔwui.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for leaves, or that waterlogged soil is preventing roots from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni sa.

english: How does removing weeds from around my crops help them grow bigger fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii wuji?

english: Weeds act as thieves that steal light, water, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing them leaves all the nourishment for your crops to build healthy leaves and fruit.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ baai kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp conditions with little airflow. Heavy rain splashes the fungal spores from the soil onto lower pods, spreading the rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo pɛ tsɔɔ mli lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. ni ehaa helai fiteɔ

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, or viruses spread by these insects that drain the plant's sap and stunt its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli nu lɛ hoɔ ni ehaaa eda.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow so slowly when I first put the seeds in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: At the beginning, seeds put most of their energy into growing strong roots deep underground to search for water and food. Once those roots are established, the crop will start growing much faster above the ground.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, dumɔwui kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ shishifãi ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ nakai shishifãi lɛ ema shi pɛ lɛ, Nibii ni adu lɛ baabɔi dalɛ oya kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to leave proper space between my seeds when I am planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii?

english: Leaving space gives each crop enough sunlight, fresh air, and room in the soil for its roots to spread. If crops are planted too close together, they fight for food and stay small.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ he lɛ to he ko lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la. kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa Ni gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii he akaŋ ni amɛji bibii.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for plant food like nitrogen in the soil. Healthy leaves need nutrients from the earth to stay green and make food for the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye oŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops curl up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up to protect the crop from losing too much water in the hot sun. It is a natural way for the plant to save its moisture until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Flowers drop when the crop is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Without enough water and proper pollination, the plant cannot support turning flowers into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo amɛmli lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ pollination ni sa bɛ lɛ, Tsei nyɛŋ aye abua ni amɛtsake fɔfɔi lɛ amɛfee aduawai.

english: Why do weeds in my field make my main crops produce a very small harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haaa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. Because weeds grow fast, they starve your plants of the food needed to grow big leaves and heavy fruits.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. Ehaa otso lɛ náaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai wuji kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants produce big tubers while others right next to them stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiwo ŋmeii wuji lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: Plants produce uneven harvests when soil nutrients are not spread evenly or when some plants are shaded by trees or choked by weeds. Every plant needs the same amount of light and soil nutrients to yield well.
ga: Tsei woɔ yibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛji akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa. aloo kɛ́ tsei eha tsei komɛi ahe ŋmɔlɔ loo jwɛi ehà amɛhe. La kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei fɛɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why does growing a different crop on my land next season keep my plants healthier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kroko ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ baaha mitsei lɛ aná hewalɛ kpakpa lɛ?

english: Changing crops breaks the life cycle of pests and diseases that hide in the soil waiting for their favorite food. It also gives the soil a chance to rebuild different nutrients naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni miimɛ niyenii ni amɛsumɔɔ waa lɛ wala shihilɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu naa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. ebaa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: How do I know if my crops are high enough quality to be sold to buyers for export?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ maha mɔ ko ni kɛ nibii majeɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Export crops must be healthy, uniform in size, fully mature, and completely free from insect damage, diseases, or chemical stains. Buyers look for clean produce that will not spoil during long transport.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ ahi hewalɛ, amɛdalɛ afee ekome, amɛdara, ni kooloi akafite amɛ, helai loo tsofai ahe muji bɛ amɛhe. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ nibii ni he tse ni efiteee yɛ be mli ni akɛ nibii majeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil or get insects when I store them in my house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo ŋmeii yɔɔ mli kɛ́ mikɛto shĩa mli lɛ?

english: Harvested grains still contain hidden moisture inside them. If they are not completely dried in the sun before storage, mold will grow and insects will be attracted to the damp seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee mli lolo. Kɛji akɛ agbiko yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, Fungus baakwɛ̃ ni kooloi baagbala dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the plantain fingers on my farm growing very small and thin instead of getting fat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli plantain niji lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ fɔmɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Plantains produce thin fingers when the soil lacks essential nutrients like potassium or when the crop doesn't get enough water during the flowering stage. Adding well-rotted manure around the base of the plant helps the fruits swell properly.
ga: Plantains baakwɛ niji bibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium, loo kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nibii ni egbo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛfuɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plantains are ready to harvest when the individual fingers lose their sharp angular edges and become plump and rounded, and the flower parts at the tips of the fingers rub off easily.
ga: Plantains efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji nineshi nine fɛɛ nine ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo ni ebatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni abaanyɛ ashɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni yɔɔ niji ahe lɛ he mlɛo.

english: Why do some fingers on my plantain bunch rot while still hanging on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi plantain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ fite beni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Rotting fingers on a growing bunch are often caused by fungal infections that thrive in high humidity and poor airflow. Pruning dry, hanging leaves around the bunch improves ventilation and keeps the fruits clean.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ niji ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Baai ni egbi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni afolɔ Ashwie shi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ ahe tseɔ.

english: Why does my plantain stool stop producing big bunches after a few harvest cycles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmei lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii wuji ni akpaa yɛ ŋmaa fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Over time, plantain stools produce too many side shoots (suckers) that compete for nutrients, light, and water. Trimming extra suckers so that only two or three strong shoots remain per stool keeps fruit yields high.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Plantain ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, la, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ amli bɔni afee ni tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmei kome mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my young plantain trees to turn yellow and dry up early?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi plantain baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi oya?

english: Early leaf yellowing is usually caused by dry soil, poor soil fertility, or leaf spot diseases like Black Sigatoka. Mulching around the base retains soil moisture and protects leaves from drying out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra. Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo baa mli helai tamɔ sigatoka diŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Plantains have shallow roots, and heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy. Root damage from soil pests can also weaken the plant, so supporting fruiting stems with wooden stakes prevents wind damage.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni aduawai akuu ni tsii lɛ haa efeɔ tsii. Shishifãi ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsei fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite amɛ.

english: Why does it take longer for my plantain trees to flower during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains rely on consistent soil moisture to build the stem strength needed for flowering. Low rainfall slows down internal plant processes, delaying the emergence of the flowering heart until moisture returns.
ga: Plantains kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa lɛ nɔ koni ekɛma tso lɛ shishi hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔi lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ haa tsei amli nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ baa shi. Tsɔ fɔfɔi tsui lɛ kwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How does water standing in my farm affect the growth of my plantains?
ga: Te nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While plantains need water, standing water chokes the roots by blocking oxygen, causing root rot and stunted growth. Constructing simple drainage channels allows excess water to flow away safely.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni plantains he hiaa nu lɛ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my green plantains ripen too quickly before I can transport them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains eŋɔli lɛ miikwɛ̃ oya tsɔ dani abaanyɛ akɛya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight, heat, and skin damage cause green plantains to release natural gas that speeds up ripening. Storing harvested bunches in a cool, shaded area and handling them carefully delays ripening.
ga: Hulu la, dɔlɛ, kɛ hewolo ni fiteɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ oya lɛ kpo. Kɛ tsei ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni shade yɔɔ. ni kɛ́ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why do plantain fingers bruise and turn black easily after transport?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain niji lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ amɛ tee tsɔne mli lɛ?

english: Plantain skin is sensitive to pressure and friction during transport. Cushioning bunches with leaves or transporting them upright in padded crates protects the fingers from bruising and discoloration.
ga: Plantain hewolo lɛ nuɔ nɔnyɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ he yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai wo nɔ loo akɛwo adeka ni akɛ tsɔne wo mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu niji ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni tsakeɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do yams seem to grow so easily on my land compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ waaa kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Yams thrive in deep, loose, and well-drained soils rich in organic matter. If your land naturally has these soil conditions, yams will easily establish strong root systems and grow healthy tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ shihilɛi Sweet potatoes baafee shishifãi ni mli wa oya ni ebaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will yams produce a good harvest anywhere I plant them, or do they need specific conditions?
ga: Ani sweet potatoes baawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ he fɛɛ he ni madu amɛ yɛ? Aloo esa akɛ shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahi shi?

english: While yam vines will sprout in many places, producing large tubers depends heavily on good soil texture and surrounding environmental conditions like proper sunlight, moisture, and temperature.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei babaoo moŋ, shi Tubers wuji lɛ afeemɔ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kpakpa kɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ tamɔ hulu la, hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni sa nɔ.

english: How do I know if a piece of land is naturally suitable for growing yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji he ko ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Land suitable for yams typically has soft, fertile soil that isn't heavy clay or overly rocky, allowing the tubers to expand underground without waterlogging.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha sweet potato lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni baa nii ni etsiii tsɔ loo tɛi bɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni nu shwieee amɛnɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if the rains do not come at the normal time of the year?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei ni sa mli?

english: When rainfall timing changes, crops may experience water stress during critical growth stages like germination or tuber formation, which can delay growth and reduce your final harvest yield.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tsake lɛ, Dumɔwui baanyɛ ana nu he haomɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa tamɔ shweremɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii afeemɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha edalɛ aya hiɛ ni eha naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why does unpredictable rain affect my yam crop so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛ ni mikpaaa gbɛ lɛ ná mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ hewalɛ waa lɛ?

english: Yams need steady moisture during their early growth and tuber formation stages. Late or irregular rains can cause the plants to stall or produce small, underdeveloped tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes biɔ nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra kɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ tuber lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ blɛoo loo ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ awɔ loo ewo bulbs bibii ni edako.

english: How can I protect my crops when the rainfall pattern in my village keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ yaa nɔ etsakeɔ lɛ?

english: You can protect your crops by practicing mulching to retain soil moisture, clearing land carefully to preserve soil water, and adjusting your planting dates based on local weather forecasts.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ mulching ni ooofee koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko lɛ nɔ. Tsumɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu akafite. ni otsake gbi ni abaadu lɛ mli yɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do surrounding trees and vegetation affect how well my crops grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kɛ tsei ni ebɔle mihe lɛ No hewɔ lɛ enaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Nearby trees and bush create a microclimate by providing shade, reducing strong drying winds, and helping the soil hold moisture, which directly impacts crop health.
ga: Tsei kɛ tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ feɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni amɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crops perform differently on two parts of the same farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsu nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli hei enyɔ lɛ?

english: Even within the same field, surrounding conditions like tree shade, soil depth, hill slopes, and wind exposure vary, causing crops in one spot to grow better than in another.
ga: Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ po lɛ, shihilɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ tsei ahe ŋmɔlɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, gɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ hu yɛ srɔtoi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kome fe hei krokomɛi.

english: Does the environment around my farm matter as much as the fertilizer I apply?
ga: Shihilɛ ni ebɔle Miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia nakai nɔŋŋ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Yes, surrounding conditions like temperature, sunlight exposure, and natural rainfall timing work together with nutrients in the soil; fertilizer cannot fully make up for severe heat or lack of water.
ga: Hɛɛ, shihilɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ latsaa, hulu la ni shɛɔ mɔ nɔ Kɛ be ni adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ekome. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ atsu dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ he nii kwraa.

english: Why does my neighbor's farm yield better yams than mine even though we planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu amɛ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Differences in soil looseness, surrounding tree shelter, moisture retention, and micro-location can give your neighbor's land better growing conditions for yam tuber development.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ etse lɛ mli He ni ahiɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli Fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ mli kɛ hei bibii Ebaanyɛ eye ebua okutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ená shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha sweet potato tuber lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Officer, why are my cocoa trees producing so many flowers, but very few of them turn into pods?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi koko tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers rely on tiny midges to spread pollen. If insect numbers are low, flowers drop off without forming pods. Hand pollination can be done to manually transfer pollen to make sure the flowers set into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi bibii. yɛ pollen mlijaa mli Kɛji kooloi fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii. Abaanyɛ akɛ niji afee pollination koni akɛ pollen lɛ aya kɛtsɔ nine nɔ koni fɔfɔi lɛ afee pods ni mli wa.

english: What is the right time of day for me to carry out hand pollination on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafee nine nɔ pollination yɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Hand pollination is best done in the early morning between 6:00 AM and 10:00 AM. This is when the cocoa flowers open, the pollen is fresh, and the heat of the sun has not yet dried out the flower parts.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ niji feɔ pollination yɛ leebi maŋkpa yɛ ŋmɛji 6:00 AM kɛ 10:00 AM teŋ, be mli ni cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi fɔfɔi, pollen lɛ mli ewo ehee ni hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ egbiko fɔfɔi lɛ fãi lɛ lolo.

english: Do I need to hire extra labor when doing specialized treatments like hand pollination on my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mahe nitsulɔi krokomɛi beni mifeɔ helatsamɔi krɛdɛɛi tamɔ nine ni akɛwoɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Because flowers open for a short time in the morning, having a small group of trained farm workers helps you cover a large number of trees quickly before the morning pollination window closes.
ga: Akɛni fɔfɔi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ be kukuoo ko leebi hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oyɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi akuu bibioo ko Tsei ni atsɔse amɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oha tsei babaoo ahe oya dani leebi fɔfɔi lɛ fɔmɔ samflɛ lɛ agbe naa.

english: How do I know the best season to start major treatments on my cocoa crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ maje kookoo tso wulu lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ shishi?

english: Major treatments are tied to natural rainy and dry cycles. Pollination treatments and flower boosters are timed just before or at the start of the rainy season when trees naturally prepare to flower.
ga: Tsamɔ titri lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ tsakpaa. Pollination kɛ fɔfɔii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ ahe tsofafeemɔi yaa nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Be nɛɛ ji be ni tsei saa amɛhe koni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do some of the tiny young cocoa pods on my trees turn shriveled and black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ, yɛ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ, egbo ni etsɔ ediŋŋ dani eda.

english: This is often caused by Cherelle Wilt, a natural process where the tree sheds pods it cannot afford to feed, or by Black Pod disease caused by excess moisture. Proper pruning and soil feeding reduce this loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Cherelle Wilt, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni haa tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii ni nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ black pod hela ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛbaa lɛ mli Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ nɔ ni laajeɔ nɛɛ aba shi.

english: How can working in a farmer group help my cocoa trees thrive better than working alone?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafoi akuu mli nitsumɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikome too mitsuɔ nii?

english: Farmer groups allow members to share farm tools, learn new field methods together, and pool labor to complete time-sensitive tasks like pruning and pollination far faster than a single farmer can.
ga: Okwaafoi akui ŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛmli bii lɛ aja okwaafoi adɛŋdadei. Kasemɔ gbɛi heei kɛfata he ni okɛ nitsumɔi afee ekome kɛtsu nitsumɔi ni heɔ be tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni okwaafonyo kome pɛ baanyɛ afee.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn yellow early while they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya be mli ni amɛji bibii waa lolo lɛ?

english: Early yellowing in small pods usually means the plant lacks essential nutrients or water, or that the pod was not fully pollinated during flowering.
ga: Yellow yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishijee Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa loo nu. aloo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛɛɛ amɛhe kwraa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why does my cocoa farm yield less cocoa when the tree canopy becomes too thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ kookoo fioo be mli ni tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ?

english: Overly thick canopies block sunlight and trap humidity, creating a breeding ground for fungi like Black Pod. Pruning lets sunlight reach the branches and promotes healthy flower development.
ga: Tsu yiteŋ ni mli tse tsɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii tamɔ black pods lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji ahe ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa waa.

english: How does shade from bigger trees affect how my cocoa crop behaves?
ga: Te hulutsoo ni jɛɔ tsei wuji amli lɛ saa bɔ ni miduɔ kookoo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa needs heavy shade to avoid leaf burn, but mature cocoa needs balanced shade (about 30-50%) so it gets enough sunlight for photosynthesis while staying cool.
ga: Cocoa bibioo he miihia hulutsoo ni mli wa koni ebaa lɛ akashã. Shi kookoo ni eda lɛ he miihia ni ená hulutsoo be ni sa (aaafee 30-50%), no hewɔ lɛ enáa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha fotosintɛsis be mli ni edɔ lolo lɛ.

english: When is the correct time to apply fertilizer so my cocoa flowers don't drop off?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi?

english: Fertilizer should be applied at the onset of the rains when the soil is damp. Applying it during deep dry spells can scorch the roots and cause flowers to drop off.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow before the crop even produces leaves at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ po woɔ baai yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top, showing that it needs fertilizer like Urea or NPK.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK awo mli.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer to my crop fields when the soil is completely dry and no rain is coming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fataaa miŋmɔji lɛ ahe beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops cannot absorb solid fertilizer directly; they can only take in nutrients when dissolved in water. Without soil moisture or rain, the fertilizer sits unused on top of the soil and can even burn the roots.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ pɛ kɛji akɛ amɛwo nu mli. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ Fɛ̃i lɛ ta shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuuu nii ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after I apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive, wild root systems that absorb nutrients faster than cultivated crops. If you do not clear the weeds before applying fertilizer, the weeds will eat the plant food instead of your crops.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei, ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaye tsei niyenii yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Large trees provide shade that protects young cocoa leaves from scorching and helps keep essential moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni amɛbuɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã amɛ. ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil gets dry suddenly. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to shed its blossoms to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩ trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Ha efɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite ni ehi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever a strong wind blows through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots near the surface of the soil. Without mounding topsoil around the base or pruning extra suckers, the heavy fruit bunch at the top easily pulls the root system out of the ground during strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Yibii akui ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli ni ekɛ ŋwɛi sũ etooo shishigbɛ lɛ he loo efolɔko ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into tight cups and stopping the plant from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekadara lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the underside of leaves and spreading viruses, which prevents healthy leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni haaa baai lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my cowpea pods look healthy on the outside but end up full of small holes and tiny worms inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, bu nyafii kɛ ngmlɛfia nyafii ngɛ mi.

english: Insects like pod borers lay invisible eggs inside the flowers or young pods. When the eggs hatch into worms, they feed on the developing seeds inside the pod where you cannot see them.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ pod borers lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa yɛ fɔfɔi loo pod bibii amli. Beni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ Ebaaye dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ni onyɛɛɛ ona.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot underground when there is too much rain during harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills up air pockets in the soil, starving the cassava roots of oxygen. Without air, fungal diseases quickly attack the waterlogged roots and cause them to rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ bɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Fungal helai tutuaa shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ oya ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting leaves in my barn even when I haven't planted them in soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduuu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Yam tubers go through a natural sleeping period after harvest called dormancy. Once that natural period ends, warm air signals to the tuber that it is time to start growing a new vine.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Kɛ nakai adebɔɔ mli be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ bulb lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ aje wain tsei heei shishi.

english: How do I know if the pest spray I used on my crops is actually effective or harming the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ loo eyeɔ baai lɛ awui?

english: Effective spraying kills the pests within a day or two while leaving the plant green. If leaf tips turn yellow, brown, or burnt immediately after spraying, the mixture was either too concentrated or applied during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaagbe tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli, ni ebaaha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ŋmɔŋ, loo shãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ashwie nɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ loo akɛwo mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe to spray my vegetable crops right before it rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ nu dani nugbɔ anɛ?

english: No, rainfall will wash the chemicals off the leaves before the plant or pests can absorb them. This wastes your input costs and leaves your crops unprotected against insects and diseases.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ ahe dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ shika ni okɛfeɔ nii lɛ. Ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi kɛ helai ahe.

english: Why are my young cassava plants dropping their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells to conserve internal water and survive heat. Once the rains return, the plant naturally shoots fresh green leaves from its stem.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baajie baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kɛjɛ eshishifã lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up into tight balls when the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl to protect themselves from intense sunlight and reduce water loss. However, if leaves remain tightly curled after watering, it usually means sucking pests like mites or a plant virus are affecting the leaves.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nu ni awo amɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni nuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmei loo tso mli hela ko miigba baai lɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and thin with small ears when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ toi bibii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, crops compete for sunlight and soil nutrients, forcing them to stretch upward instead of growing thick stems. Proper spacing allows each plant to get enough light and nutrients to form large ears.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛshwere yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaana ŋmeii ni mli tse. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ toi wuji.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce many flowers but very few actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi anɔkwa ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Flowers fall off if the soil lacks nutrients like phosphorus or if the tree experiences water stress. Lack of pollinating insects or damage from mirid pests can also prevent flowers from forming pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛji tso lɛ naa nu he haomɔ. Pollinators ni bɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii fioo lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee pods.

english: Will planting cowpeas alongside my maize help or hurt my maize yield?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye miŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ awui?

english: Cowpeas help maize by capturing nitrogen from the air and enriching the soil. As long as the cowpea vines do not climb over and smother the maize stalks, growing them together improves crop yields.
ga: Cowpeas yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni emɔɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni cowpea wain tso lɛ ekwɔɔɔ ni efolɔɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ, Dumɔ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ baaye abua ni yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt and droop immediately after moving them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings go through shock when tender roots are disturbed or exposed to direct heat. Transplanting in the cool late afternoon and watering immediately helps the plants settle into the soil without wilting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe feɔ amɛ yaa kɛji akɛ agba shishifãi bibii lɛ anaa loo akɛ amɛ wo la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ shwane ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni awo lɛ nu oya lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbooo.

english: How can I tell underground yam tubers are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up completely. Dying foliage above ground shows that the tuber underground has stopped growing and is ready to harvest.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Baai ni egboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why are the bottom parts of my vegetable stems turning black and soft near the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Soft, black stems near the soil level are caused by fungal stem rot, which thrives in overly wet, soggy soil. Improving field drainage and clearing dense weeds around plant bases keeps stems dry and healthy.
ga: Stem rot fungus ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ fe nine nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsei diji, bibii ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baa. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight and harsh heat. Without shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees to cover them, the sun scorches the leaves and dries up the plant's moisture before its roots can establish deep in the ground.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ shishi. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ lɛ, Hulu lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ mli nu lɛ gĩɔ dani shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves is usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for plant growth. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant takes whatever nitrogen it has left in its lower leaves and sends it up to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Abɛi tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛye ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with thick green leaves, but giving me small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, cassava plants put all their energy into growing leaves and stems above ground. Because the plant is busy growing tall, it does not store enough starch underground, resulting in small or thin tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ejaakɛ tsei lɛ daraa babaoo No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛ ŋmei ni fa bɔ ni sa ato shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo loo eyɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do my young maize plants have ragged holes in the leaves and dark powder inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ yɛ bu yɛ ebaa lɛ mli kɛ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar hides inside the center of the young maize leaves to protect itself from heat and birds, chewing on the tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ okpoi ahe. Kɛtsɔ baai bibii lɛ ni oooye dani amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from heat stress or irregular watering. When temperatures get too hot or the soil dries out completely, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and water so it can survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and fall over when I plant four or five seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ ebɔ he yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted in the same spot, the seedlings compete with each other for water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil. This forces them to stretch thin for sunlight, making their stems weak and easy for wind to knock down.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ, Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my yam plants help them stay healthy when the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, covering the soil like a blanket. It shades the soil from direct heat, keeping it cool and trapping moisture underground so the roots can still drink water even when it does not rain.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ atade Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu nu lolo kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: Why does planting cowpea or groundnut on my farm make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots that work with beneficial organisms to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When the plants die, this natural fertilizer remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi ni kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and choke my young crops during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛtsiɔ midumɔwui lɛ anaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have wild, hardy seeds that germinate quickly and take immediate advantage of sunlight and rainfall. Because young crops grow slowly at first, weeds quickly steal the nutrients, water, and space before the crop's roots can fully spread.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ koo mli dumɔwui ni mli wa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ekɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bibii baakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ shishijee mli. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii, nu kɛ he oya dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot from the bottom during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains create damp, humid conditions that encourage a fungal disease called Black Pod to spread. Raindrops splash fungal spores from the wet soil onto low-hanging pods, causing them to turn black and rot if they remain continuously wet.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ he hewalɛ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛji amɛtee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which gives plants their green color, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even though the leaves above ground grow big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lack of potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing branches and leaves instead of storing food in the tubers underneath.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha niyenii ahi oyitso shishi lɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees take so long to produce fruit when I leave all the young stems growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii beni mikɛ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ shwieɔ lɛ? nakai tsei lɛ

english: Multiple suckers growing around one main plantain stem steal water and food from each other. Removing extra suckers leaves more energy for the main stem to fruit faster.
ga: Tsobii babaoo ni miida kɛbɔle ehe. Tso titri kome pɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ awo yibii oya, ni ebaaná hewalɛ babaoo.

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads fast in damp, shaded farms during the rainy season when air cannot flow freely between trees.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ amli. he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ oya lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines curl up and turn pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or viruses they spread, which suck nutrients out of the leaves and slow down the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo virus ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do pepper plants drop all their leaves suddenly after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, pɛpɛɛpɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots suffocate and rot when water sits around them for too long, causing the plant to drop its leaves out of stress.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa pepper tso lɛ jeɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ haomɔ he.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when temperatures get too high or when they don't get consistent water, as the plant tries to save water to stay alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu daa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have adapted to quickly grab light, water, and food from the soil before crop seeds even finish germinating.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛŋɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani dumɔwui lɛ agbeɔ kwɛ̃mɔ naa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my maize seeds at the start of the rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔ lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to plant after two or three good rains when the topsoil stays moist, ensuring seeds get enough water to sprout without drying up during a short dry spell.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii 2-3 sɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli edɔ lolo. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi yɛ be kukuoo ni nu bɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my land feel hard and dry quickly even after rain falls on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa ni egbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Soil loses its ability to hold water when it lacks organic matter like decayed plants or manure, which acts like a sponge to keep moisture near the crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ nu kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ tsei loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni eha nu ahi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow root systems that lose water rapidly under direct sun. They need shade crops like plantains to shelter them and retain moisture until their root systems grow strong enough to withstand full heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ amli baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat or sudden dry spells. The heat damages the pollen, preventing the flower from getting fertilized to form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ loo ŋmɔlɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ kpataa pollen ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛɛɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize crop turning light green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient the plant uses to build green leaves and process sunlight for growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hia ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛtsuɔ hulu la he nii koni amɛdara.

english: Why is my cassava producing huge leafy foliage above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ baai wuji yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excessive organic foliage growth, the cassava plant directs all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing energy underground in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo bɔɔ nii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ babaoo. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ebaa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeekɛto shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm makes the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acts as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee tsei kakadaji koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to swell and grow large yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbai lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi ni efuɔ ni edaraa ni efeɔ sweet potato tuber agbo ko

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, space, and essential soil nutrients away from your crops, effectively starving the main plant.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, ŋwɛi, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the underside of leaves, or by viruses transmitted to the plant by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same place drains specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the land.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my citrus trees produce a sudden burst of new flowers right after the dry season ends and rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee ni nugbɔ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: The dry season puts the tree in a resting state, and the arrival of the first heavy rains signals to the tree that water is abundant, triggering flowering hormones.
ga: Hɔmɔ be lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ woɔ hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli. Ni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baa lɛ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ. Ehaa fɔfɔii ahe tsofai lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Why are my maize leaves curling up like tight tubes during hot sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ paipii ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense to protect themselves from losing water in intense heat. By rolling up, the leaf reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and wind, saving moisture inside the plant until temperatures cool down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe Baai lɛ haa he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How can my cassava plants stay alive and green even when there is no rain for months?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli kɛji nugbɔ enɛko nyɔji babaoo po?

english: Cassava plants store large amounts of water and starch in their thick underground tubers. During dry spells, the plant relies on these stored food reserves and drops some upper leaves to conserve moisture until rain returns.
ga: Cassava tsei toɔ nu kɛ starch babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli tse amli. yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ niyenii ni ato nɛɛ anɔ ni amɛshiɔ amɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do yam tubers manage to grow so big underground when the top soil feels hard and dry?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nɛkɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa ni egbi lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their vines and leaves to capture energy from sunlight and send that energy down into underground tubers. The tubers grow downward into deeper soil layers where moisture remains, expanding by storing water and nutrients.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ wain tsei kɛ baai tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbua hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ naa ni amɛkɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ majeɔ shi kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ amli. Tubers lɛ daa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni ehiɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting when the rain is very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen from air pockets in the soil to sprout. When heavy rains flood the soil, water fills all the air spaces, effectively suffocating the seeds and causing them to rot before roots can form.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the roots are getting too much water and cannot breathe, or that the soil lacks essential nitrogen. Overwatering washes nutrients away from roots and prevents the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiná nu babaoo ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ Nu ni awoɔ fe nine lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli, ni ehaaa tso lɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.
