english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or drought stress. The plant senses that it does not have enough water or strength to support fruits, so it drops the flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ he. Tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ nu loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baanyɛ aye abua aduawai lɛ. Ejieɔ fɔfɔii koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees scorch and die if I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ shã ni egbo kɛji mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight because they lose moisture faster than their small roots can drink. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping young cocoa cool and preserving soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Akɛni amɛfiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ anu lɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow very tall and thin with weak stems when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When planted too closely, plantains compete for sunlight. Instead of building strong, thick stems, they waste energy stretching quickly upward to catch light, making them weak and easy for wind to knock down.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dare ni eju hulu la lɛ Moŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei ni mli wa ni mli tse lɛ feɔ tsei. Amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛgbalaa amɛhe oya koni amɛmɔ la. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ amɛtswaa amɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow many green leaves but very few bean pods during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much water and nitrogen in the soil encourage cowpea plants to focus on vegetative growth—producing leaves and branches—rather than reproductive growth, which produces flowers and bean pods.
ga: Nu kɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ cowpea tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama tsei ni shwereɔ lɛ anɔ. ni ji baai kɛ tsei niji abɔɔ Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, fɔmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni no haa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my cassava sprouts after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe mi-cassava lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds produce aggressive, fast-germinating seeds adapted to seize early moisture and surface nutrients rapidly, whereas crop plants like cassava take longer to establish strong roots and leaf systems.
ga: Jwɛi woɔ dumɔwui ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. ni tsakeɔ ehe oya kɛhaa shishijee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii tamɔ ŋmei heɔ be babaoo ni ekɛmaa shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your rice crop is hungry for nitrogen or standing in water that lacks nutrients. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea at the right stage helps the leaves regain their green color so the crop can produce heavy rice grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-rice tsei lɛ miiye nitrogen loo amɛyɛ nu ni niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ urea fata he yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmaa ni tsii.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into straws during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to save water when heat and sunshine are high. It reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, helping the plant hold onto its moisture until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he kɛji dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la fa babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with lots of green leaves, but the tubers under the ground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When cassava has too much nitrogen in the soil or is planted too close together, it puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy foliage instead of developing roots. Giving plants enough space and balanced soil nutrients encourages energy to go down into building thick cassava roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei yɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ moŋ fe ni eeefee shishifãi. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaawo hewalɛ ni amɛná koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii shishifãi ni mli tse.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? Ni okɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward the sun to make food through their leaves. Staking keeps the leaves high above ground weeds, exposed to sunlight, and safe from soil fungal diseases, which allows the plant to build much larger tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ amɛfee niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ fe sũ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ, hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ, ni amɛhe bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my small green cocoa pods turn black, rot, and dry up right on the branch during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ji Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, egboɔ ni egbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads quickly in wet, shaded conditions. Pruning overgrown cocoa branches allows air and sunlight into the farm, drying out dampness and protecting young pods from the fungus.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kookoo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. shwiemɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni obu ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ he

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the stems carry heavy bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be mli ni tso lɛ yibii babaoo yɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain stems fall over mainly because tiny pests called nematodes or root borers weaken their root systems, making them lose their grip in wet soil. Using clean planting suckers and propping up heavy bunches with sturdy wooden poles prevents plants from toppling.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi babaoo yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ahewɔ. Ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ, ni amɛhaa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli nibii ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii ni he tse tsu nii ni akɛ tsei ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni wa wo mli lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off before turning into actual pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by intense heat or sudden periods of dry soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots during the flowering stage prevents flower drop and allows healthy peppers to form.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Roots lɛ he lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and sunken as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ehaa shwieɔ shi beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This condition is known as Blossom End Rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit while it develops, often due to uneven watering. Keeping soil moisture steady with regular watering allows tomato roots to continuously draw up calcium for healthy fruit development.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli beni edara lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ haa tomato shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛjieɔ calcium kɛhaa aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my soil dry out and turn hard like rock shortly after the heavy rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kpa pɛ kɛkɛ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni ewa tamɔ tɛsaa lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like dry leaves, straw, or manure. Adding compost or leaving crop residues on top of the farm acts like a blanket, keeping soil soft, cool, and capable of holding water much longer after rainfall ends.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egbi, jwɛi loo ŋmeii bɛ mli. Kompost ni akɛfataa he loo tsei amli nibii ni eshwɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli be babaoo beni nugbɔ lɛ egbe naa lɛ.

english: Why does my maize grow much better when I plant groundnuts on the farm before planting the maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally extracts nitrogen from the air and leaves it in the soil through its roots. When you plant maize in that same soil afterward, it uses that free left-over nitrogen to grow faster and produce bigger ears.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ tsuɔ nii koni eda oya ni ená toi wuji.

english: Why should I trim or remove some of the leaves from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo majie mi-cacao tso lɛ baai lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Trimming unnecessary leaves, or pruning, helps the cocoa tree direct its food and energy to developing flowers and cocoa pods rather than wasting energy on extra leaves. It also allows sunlight and air to reach the inner branches, keeping the tree healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ loo afolɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa cacao tso lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ cacao fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu shɛɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. ha tsei awa

english: Does cutting crowded branches help prevent black pod disease on my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ black pod hela naa yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cutting away overgrown branches allows breeze and sunlight to flow through the tree canopy. This dries up excess moisture on leaves and pods, making it much harder for fungal diseases like black pod to grow and spread.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ shweremɔ kɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ wa waa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need tall shade trees growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he hiaa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baabɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Tall trees protect young and mature cocoa trees from severe sun heat and strong winds. They create a cool, moist environment that mimics the natural forest, preventing cocoa leaves from scorching and keeping soil damp longer.
ga: Tsei kakadaji buɔ kookoo tsei bibii kɛ mɛi ni eda lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Amɛhaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ ni kaseɔ adebɔɔ mli koo. Ehaa kookoo baai lɛ shãaa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does a cocoa tree decide where to send the food it creates?
ga: Te cacao tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛkpɛɔ amɛyiŋ yɛ he ni amɛkɛ amɛ niyenii lɛ baatsu nii yɛ?

english: The cocoa tree uses sunlight and soil nutrients to make food in its leaves, and it naturally sends this food to areas with active growth. When cocoa pods are developing, the tree prioritizes sending most of its food directly to those pods and flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei kɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ niyenii yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Ni ebaatsu niyenii nɛɛ kɛya hei ni aduɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ afee kookoo ŋmeii lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa amɛ niyenii lɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛmajeɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my cocoa trees help the trees grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Cocoa yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds steal water and soil nutrients that your cocoa trees need to grow. When you clear weeds away, all the food in the soil goes straight to your cocoa tree's roots so it can produce stronger branches and more pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ mli. Kɛji ojie jwɛi lɛ Nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni ená niji ni wa kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How does adding fertilizer help my cocoa trees make more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer supplies vital nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium to the soil. The roots absorb these nutrients so the leaves can manufacture more food, which fuels the tree to grow healthy flowers and bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hia tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ gbalaa niyenii nɛɛ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni mli wa kɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do leaves play such a big role in keeping my cocoa tree healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai tsuɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ ko ni he hiaa waa yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves act as the plant's kitchen. They trap sunlight and air to prepare food (sugars) for the rest of the tree. Healthy green leaves are necessary to feed the trunk, roots, flowers, and cocoa pods.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ kpataashi. Amɛmɔɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛkɛsaa niyenii (sugar) amɛha tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ. Baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he hia kɛha kookoo tsei, shishifãi, fɔfɔi, kɛ tsei adalɛ.

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but it cannot feed all of them. If the tree lacks nutrients, water, or proper pollination from tiny insects, it drops extra flowers so it can save its strength for the remaining pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi jeee fɛɛ abaanyɛ atsɔse amɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa, nu, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii amli lɛ, Ebaashwie fɔfɔi krokomɛi koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli hewalɛ ahi shi.

english: What causes small, young cocoa pods to turn shriveled and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt, which happens when the tree does not have enough food or water to support all the developing pods at once. The tree naturally sacrifices smaller pods to ensure larger ones survive.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ fɛɛ shikome. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, tsei kɛ ŋmeii bibii shaa afɔle koni ŋmeii wuji lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does an older cocoa tree produce fewer pods than it used to when it was younger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe beni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 years, their internal systems for moving water and food slow down. While proper pruning and fertilizer can help, old trees naturally produce fewer flowers and pods over time.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tso ko eye fe afii 20 lɛ, emli gbɛjianɔtoi ni haa nu kɛ niyenii yaa lɛ baa shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua moŋ, Shi tsei ni egbɔ lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the cassava tubers I harvested this season so much smaller than the ones I harvested last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni mikpa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ faaa kwraa fe ŋmeii ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers stay small when the soil lacks sufficient nutrients or when there is not enough rainfall during their growing phase. Adding compost or manure before planting restores soil fertility so the roots can swell properly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ afuu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing smaller pods now compared to when the farm was young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii fe beni amɛji gbekɛbii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older, their natural ability to transport food from the soil to the branches slows down. Regular pruning to remove unproductive branches and applying fertilizer can help older trees produce large pods again.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ Amɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛjieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ ni afoɔ amɛ daa koni ajie amɛ niji ni wooo yibii lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei ni edara lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ekoŋŋ.

english: How come some cobs on the same maize plant grow big while others remain tiny and undeveloped?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso kome nɔ lɛ daraa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛdarako lɛ?

english: Maize plants need a strong supply of water and nutrients right when the silks appear. If the plant experiences drought or poor soil at that moment, it only puts energy into feeding the top cob, leaving the lower cobs small.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii babaoo he miihia ŋmã tsei kɛji amɛfee siliki pɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ na hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii pɛ koni amɛkɛye ŋmei lɛ yiteŋ. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ ŋmei lɛ ni oooshi lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my plantain bunches turn out small when I plant the suckers close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantain suckers are planted too close, their roots fight underground for food and water, while their large leaves block sunlight from each other. Giving each plant enough spacing ensures every sucker gets what it needs to produce a large bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. yɛ be mli ni baai wuji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaha mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni nuɔ nu lɛ aná nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni efee kuu agbo.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, a key plant nutrient, or that the roots are sitting in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving soil drainage will restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ Aloo akɛɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ mli su kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from intense heat or uneven watering. Keeping the soil continuously moist with mulch protects the plant from stress so the flowers can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ haomɔ he. koni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ tomato

english: Why does my yam vine dry up and die off after a few months of growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ gĩ ni egbo yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: This is a natural stage in the yam plant's life cycle called die-back. The plant intentionally stops growing leaves above ground so it can transfer all its energy down into swelling the tuber below the soil.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛhe ko yɛ sweet potato tso lɛ wala shihilɛ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ dieback. Tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekpa baai lɛ adalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ aya shikpɔŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions during the rainy season. Pruning extra shade leaves lets sunlight and air dry out the farm, preventing the fungus from ruining the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni afoɔ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akafite ŋmeii lɛ

english: Why does my maize grow tall and green in one part of my land, but short and weak in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miida ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ? shi eyɛ kuku ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fã kroko mli

english: Soil nutrition is rarely uneven across a farm because rainwater often washes topsoil away from higher ground into lower spots. Spreading organic manure on the weak spots helps balance out soil fertility across your whole farm.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli nibii lɛ jeee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ fɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kɛyaa hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Organic fertilizer ni ooogbɛ ashwã hei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are my rice plants forming heads that are empty with no rice grains inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ yitsei efee efolo ni ŋmãa ŋmãa ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty rice grains, often called chaff, happen when the plant lacks water right at the flowering stage. Without enough moisture during flowering, the grains fail to fill up with food.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ omɔ ŋmeii Baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Dumɔwui nyɛŋ afee niyenii ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer (like urea) helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii (tamɔ urea) fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but leguminous crops like beans and groundnuts do the opposite—they grab nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally restoring the land's fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii feɔ nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ nakai Amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small saw-dust like dirt in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Tamɔ muji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on the soft growing tip of the plant. Spraying approved organic or chemical control measures early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out will protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking the juice out of young leaves, or by a virus spread by those insects. Clearing weeds around the farm and controlling these tiny insects early helps keep leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Okwaafoi kɛ kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and can easily burn or dry out under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large broad leaves that act like umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil cool for the young cocoa plants.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã loo amɛgbi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi oya. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ.

english: The first rain often heats up dry soil without thoroughly soaking it, which can trigger seeds to sprout and then wither if the rain stops for a week or two. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular and the soil is deeply moist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome loo enyɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ eba ekoŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa.

english: Why do I have to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam vines as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Sweet potato wain tso beni ebɔi edamɔ

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves high into the sunlight to make energy. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases live, allowing the plant to capture light and grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Atomɔ tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ bɔni afee ni ená hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ hiɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ emɔɔ la ni ekwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant feels stressed, most commonly from extreme heat, irregular watering, or soil drying out completely. Mulching the soil and keeping it evenly moist helps the plant keep its flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Nɔ ni kɛbaa babaoo ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Mulching kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛtsɔ yibii.

english: When cassava roots mature underground, the lower leaves of the plant naturally turn yellow and begin to fall off. You can gently dig up the soil near the base of one test plant to inspect root size before harvesting the whole plot.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi kwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi. Obaanyɛ Ofo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso kome ni akaa lɛ shishi lɛ fiofio koni okwɛ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ dani okpa shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What benefit do I get if I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ maná kɛji mikɛ sũ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ebɔle ehe lɛ wo mli? ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ jwɛi ewo mli

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that stops the hot sun from drying out the earth, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall without any corn ears showing yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miida ni ŋmãa toi ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Maize plants build strong stalks and wide leaves first to gather sunlight and nutrients. The corn ears develop internally before emerging, so growth happens inside long before you see the actual ear on the stem.
ga: Abɛi tsei feɔ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛkɛbua hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa. Abɛi toi lɛ daa yɛ mli dani ejeɔ kpo. No hewɔ lɛ, mligbɛ dalɛ baa be kakadaŋŋ dani onaa toi diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are growing well under the soil when the plant above looks unchanged?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi? Beni tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee?

english: As cassava roots swell beneath the ground, you will notice small cracks forming in the soil around the base of the stem, showing that the plant is building tubers unseen.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ Obaana ŋmeii bibii. ni baa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miifee ŋmeii ni anaaa.

english: How do I know if my groundnut plants are successfully forming pods under the earth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-peanut tso lɛ eye omanye ni ekɛfee pods yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they drop their petals and send small pegs growing downward into the soil, where the pods develop beneath the surface.
ga: Beni ekɛ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ ebɔi pollination sɛɛ lɛ, ebaajie efɔfɔi lɛ ni ebaatsu ŋmeii bibii. ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their early flowers without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi oya ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees often drop their initial flowers because the tree is not yet strong enough to support heavy pods, holding back its strength until it reaches full maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛ shishijee fɔfɔi lɛ ejaakɛ tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ fɔfɔi ni tsii lɛ anɔ lolo. ni ehiɛ ehewalɛ mli kɛyashi ebaada kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce many blossoms, but only a few turn into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi tsei fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Plants shed extra blossoms if they experience heat stress or lack water, keeping only the number of fruits they have enough water and nutrients to feed.
ga: Tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ waa kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli. Amɛkpaa aduawai ni nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: How do I know the exact time my plantains are ready to cut before they spoil on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaafo dani amɛgboi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Plantain fingers are ready for harvest when they plump up, lose their sharp outer edges, and the dried flower tips at the ends break off easily.
ga: Plantain niji lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kponɔgbɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ laaje. Ni fɔfɔii ni egbi ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ baakumɔ oya.

english: How can I tell if my crops need water before their leaves start curling and drying up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani baai lɛ aje shishi amɛfo ni amɛgbi?

english: Dig a few inches into the soil near the root zone; if the earth crumbles completely dry in your hand without clumping, the roots need water even if the leaves look fine.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni shɛɔ inchi fioo komɛi yɛ he ni shishifã lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ onine mli lɛ mli egbi kwraa ni ekɛ ehe ebɔko he lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baahiɛ nu kɛji akɛ baai lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Why do my yam vines grow plenty of green leaves but produce very small yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi sweet potato ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes yams put all their energy into leaf growth above ground instead of sending food down to grow big tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii feɔ ŋmeii ni ekɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu niyenii kɛya shi koni amɛkwɛ bulbs yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Why is it better for all farmers in my village to plant our maize at the same time after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ okwaafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ baadu ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting together distributes pest pressure across all farms instead of letting insects destroy one early field, and ensures all crops make the most of the short rainy season.
ga: Hefatalɔi dumɔ gbɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha kooloi bibii afite he kome, ni okwɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ana sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛjɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my soil is moist enough to apply fertilizer so my crops can use it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve into a form that roots can drink; if the ground is completely dry, the fertilizer sits on top and can burn the plant roots when rain finally comes.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ nɔ ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ, Fertilizer ta nɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi kɛji naagbee lɛ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: What is the main difference between using local seeds from my harvest and buying improved agricultural seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni jɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛ okwaayeli dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ ahemɔ teŋ?

english: Local seeds are saved from previous harvests and are adapted to the area, but improved agricultural seeds are specially developed by scientists to yield more produce, mature faster, and resist common pests and diseases.
ga: Ahereɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli, ni atsakeɔ amɛ kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Shi jeŋ nilelɔi efee okwaayeli dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, amɛshwere oya ni amɛte shi amɛwo helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni afɔɔ namɔ.

english: How can I know if the seeds I am about to plant are a local variety or an improved agricultural variety?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miitao madu lɛ ji maŋ lɛ mli loo okwaayeli mli dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ?

english: Improved agricultural varieties are usually sold in sealed, labeled packages from certified agricultural officers or input dealers, while local seeds are typically bought loosely in open markets or saved from a neighbor's farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ okwaayeli mli tsofai srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ kotokui ni akɛwo mli ni aŋmala nɔ nii lɛ amli kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ loo nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe nitsulɔi adɛŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, aheɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni bɛ mlɛo. yɛ jara nɔ loo abua naa kɛjɛɔ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli

english: Is it risky for me to plant local crop seeds given to me by a friend without knowing the exact variety?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ ooodu maŋ lɛ mli tsei ahe dumɔwui ni onaanyo ko kɛha bo lɛ ni oleee henɔ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, it is risky because unknown local seeds may carry hidden seed-borne diseases, have poor germination rates, or produce very low yields compared to certified varieties.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni aleee lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli kɛbaa lɛ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. eyɛ shweremɔ ni baa shi loo ewoɔ yibii ni baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto henɔi ni awo he odase lɛ ahe

english: Why should I come and consult an agricultural extension officer before I start planting on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko agba sane dani obɔi dumɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extension officers have updated technical knowledge about seed varieties, climate patterns, and crop care that isn't written on seed packages, helping you avoid costly planting mistakes.
ga: Mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ eha ŋaa nilee ni kɔɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ahe lɛ etee hiɛ. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ ni atsɔɔɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ahe tɔmɔi ni jara wa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do elders in my village advise us to be careful about which seed variety we select before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkwɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔwui ni wɔhalaa dani wɔduɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Elders know from experience that planting the wrong seed variety for your specific soil or rainfall pattern can lead to crop failure, wasted labor, and financial loss for your household.
ga: Onukpai le kɛjɛ niiashikpamɔ mli akɛ, kɛ́ odu dumɔwui srɔtoi ni ejaaa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ loo bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafee nɔ ni ehiii. Nitsumɔ ni afiteɔ kɛ shika ni afiteɔ yɛ oshia lɛ mli.

english: Why can planting the wrong crop variety cause severe trouble on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ naagbai ni mli wa aba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Each crop variety requires specific soil types, rainfall, and care; if you plant a variety unsuitable for your area, it may fail to germinate, get destroyed by local insects, or yield almost nothing.
ga: Tso henɔ fɛɛ tso henɔ biɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ, kɛ kwɛmɔ. Kɛji odu tso srɔtoi ni esaaa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Ekolɛ enyɛŋ ekwɛ̃. Kplukai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ loo eshɛɛɛ ni ewoɔ yibii ko kwraa

english: Do improved agricultural crop varieties take the same time to grow as our traditional local crops?
ga: Ani okwaayeli mli ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ heɔ be ni fa tamɔ wɔ maŋ tsei lɛ nɔŋŋ dani amɛdaraa?

english: No, many improved agricultural varieties are bred to grow and mature faster than traditional local crops, allowing you to harvest earlier and escape dry spells at the end of the rainy season.
ga: Dabi, atsɔ okwaayeli mli tsei srɔtoi babaoo ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛshwere oya fe tsutsu maŋbii tsei. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii mra ni ojoɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naa foi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee.

english: Will planting improved agricultural seeds guarantee that I get more bags of harvest from my field?
ga: Ani okwaayeli dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha maná ŋmaakpamɔ kotokui babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli?

english: Improved seeds have the potential to produce much higher yields, but they must be combined with good farming practices like proper spacing, timely weeding, and adequate soil fertility.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaawo yibii babaoo. Shi esa akɛ akɛtsu nii kɛfata okwaayeli nifeemɔi kpakpai tamɔ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa he. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa

english: Why do improved agricultural seeds need different fertilizer and care compared to local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kwɛmɔ srɔtoi kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ahe lɛ?

english: Because improved varieties are engineered to produce much higher yields, they feed more aggressively and need proper nutrients and care to reach their full harvest potential.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, afee tsofai srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ amɛyeɔ nii babaoo ni amɛbiɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa koni amɛshɛ amɛhewalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee lɛ he.

english: Why do my traditional local crops seem to catch diseases more easily nowadays than before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni helai yeɔ mimaŋ tsei lɛ waa yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ?

english: Over time, crop diseases and weather patterns change, and old local seed varieties lose their strength against new diseases, whereas agricultural researchers continually update new varieties to resist modern threats.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi miitsake. ni maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui momo lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛkɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai heei lɛ baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni baanyɛ adamɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbeyeishemɔi anaa.

english: This usually means your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build green leaves. When the plant cannot get enough nitrogen from the ground, it pulls the nutrient from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ana nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Egbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. As these insects suck the plant juice, the leaf deforms and curls up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ tsei amli nu. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or water early in its growth, it spends all its energy growing leaves above the ground instead of storing food in the roots. Ensuring balanced nutrients and proper plant spacing helps the crop send energy down to build big tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli. Niyenii ni sa kɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ni abaakwɛ koni tsei lɛ akudɔ hewalɛ kɛya shi koni amɛfee bulbs agboi.

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need to lift their leaves up into full sunlight to produce food efficiently. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents fungal diseases and helps the plant produce larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni amɛná niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which works together with beneficial soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut crop is harvested, that extra nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen from flower to flower. If the air is too dry, if there is no shade, or if strong chemicals kill these insects, the unpollinated flowers cannot form pods and will simply drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen ajɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, hulutsoo be bɛ, loo tsofai ni mli wa gbe nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ, Fɔfɔi ni bɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily once the heavy bunch starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii wuji je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy weight above ground. Putting a strong Y-shaped wooden pole against the stem (propping) gives the plant structural support so wind does not snap the stem or pull up the roots.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua muji ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y lɛ fĩ tso lɛ shishi (fiɔ sɛɛ) lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye ebua tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ. Enɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa koni ekafo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ loo egbala shishifãi lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by soil-borne bacteria or fungi entering the root system. The disease clogs the tiny water pipes inside the stem, so even though the soil has water, the plant cannot transport it up to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ nu paipii bibii anaa. yɛ tso lɛ mli No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu po lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ amɛ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya baai lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if the ground has received enough rain for me to safely plant my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui shweshweeshwe?

english: You should wait until the rain has soaked deep enough into the soil—at least hand-length deep (about 15 to 20 cm)—and when heavy rains fall consistently for several days. Planting after just one light shower can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ—kɛ hoo lɛ, aaafee ŋmei kome (aaafee sɛntimitai 15 kɛyashi 20)—kɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni naa wa lɛ etee nɔ enɛ gbii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Weed seeds sit hidden in the soil in large numbers, waiting for clearing and sunlight to sprout. Because wild weeds are naturally tough and well-adapted to local conditions, they germinate rapidly and compete with your young crops for water, light, and soil nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo. Ni amɛmiimɛ ni hulu lɛ atse ni hulu la atsɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, koo mli jwɛi lɛ wa yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛkɛ onibii bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow weak and yellow when weeds are growing close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive unwanted guests at a food table. They quickly take up the soil nutrients and water meant for your maize, leaving your crop with very little food to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni ataooo amɛ ni yɔɔ basabasa yɛ gbɛkɛ niyeli okpɔlɔ lɛ nɔ. Amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli kɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ oya. Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii fioo pɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds early instead of waiting until my crops are big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ mra? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mamɛ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara?

english: Crops need the most nutrients during their early growth stage. Clearing weeds early ensures all the soil food goes to your crop when it needs it most, preventing early damage to your expected harvest.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia tsei fe fɛɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee be mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa onibii amli yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ. Tsi nibii ni baafite mra yɛ kpamɔ ni okpaa gbɛ lɛ naa.

english: Will my farm produce any reasonable harvest if I leave weeds to grow alongside my crops?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ baawo yibii ni sa? Ni kɛji akɛ mishi jwɛi komɛi koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛfata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe hu?

english: You will likely get little to no harvest. Weeds naturally grow faster than farm crops, so they will take over the land, capture all the soil nutrients, and choke your crops before they can bear fruit.
ga: Ekolɛ obaaná ŋmaa fioo ko pɛ loo obaakpa nɔ ko kwraa. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbaaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mɔ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ofite onibii dani amɛwo yibii.

english: What happens if I plant my crop seeds too close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight with one another for the same limited soil nutrients and water. This competition causes all the plants to remain small and produce poor yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Can I grow two different crops together in the same field without them fighting for soil food?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni amɛkaaa niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, if you choose crops that use different nutrients or help each other. For example, planting legumes like cowpeas alongside maize works well because cowpeas add nitrogen back into the soil, feeding the maize instead of stealing from it.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi srɔtoi tsuɔ nii loo ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe lɛ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. ni amɛye ŋmãa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaju kɛjɛ mli

english: When soil food is low, plants show warning signs such as yellowing leaves, stunted growth, thin stems, or shedding flowers early instead of producing healthy fruits.
ga: Beni niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo, loo fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ mra yɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ najiaŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year if I keep farming it without adding manure or fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ mitsu nii yɛ nɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they take away nutrients from the soil. If you do not replace those nutrients with manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil food runs out and future crops will starve.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeee nakai niyenii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaho aya ni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ.

english: Why did my field stop giving good yields after years of producing big harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔji lɛ ekpa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai awomɔ yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛkpa nii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous farming without giving the land a rest or adding nutrients drains the soil's natural food reserve completely. Once the soil food is exhausted, crops can no longer thrive there.
ga: Okwaayeli ni ayaa nɔ ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ewo mli ekoŋŋ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afiteɔ. Beni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ efo lɛ Dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops stay small and thin when large trees are shading them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ be mli ni tsei wuji miitsi amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight alongside soil food to produce their food. Large trees block sunlight and their big roots drink up most of the soil water, leaving your crops hungry and shaded.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛná niyenii. Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ nuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ babaoo. Ha hɔmɔ kɛ hulutsoo aye onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants dry up faster when wild grasses are growing next to them during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya beni koo mli jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Wild grasses have tough, wide root systems that pull up available moisture in the ground very fast, leaving no water in the soil for your tender vegetable plants to drink.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa. ni gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli oya ni eshiii nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anu.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, offering the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips and moving down the center in a V-pattern indicates nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is essential for green growth, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help restore healthy growth.
ga: Yellow jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaagbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I know if my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up all the plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efoŋ?

english: Cassava plants show maturity when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts cracking. You can carefully remove a bit of soil at the base of one plant to check if the roots are thick enough.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ sũ aha tso kome shishi jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dry conditions. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and putting dry grass mulch around the base will cool the soil and reduce flower loss.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Curled or wrinkled leaves in pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites. Spraying the plants early with recommended insecticides or organic neem oil mixtures helps eliminate these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle loo ekpɔtɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Okɛ tsei lɛ afɔ mra. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he akɛ akɛtsu nii loo ni akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ ohe.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch direct sunlight, which fuels the growth of big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves dry and reduces fungal diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni ji tsofa ni haa bulbs wuji lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it helpful to cut off the dry leaves from my plantain stems?
ga: Ani eyeɔ ebuaa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egbi lɛ kɛjɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, trimming dead or diseased leaves prevents fungal diseases and insect pests from spreading. It also improves air circulation and sunlight exposure throughout your farm, helping your fruits grow larger.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ afo baai ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akagbɛ ashwã. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la hu yaa hiɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa oyibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my garden vegetables with dry dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool under hot sunlight, traps moisture so you water less often, and stops weeds from sprouting and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: What is eating holes in my young maize leaves and leaving tiny green powder inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni ashiɔ powda bibii ni ji eŋɔli yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, and the green powder is their waste. You need to apply recommended control sprays early in the morning or late afternoon, directing the treatment right into the center funnel of the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ni powda ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ji amɛ jwɛi. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii leebi loo shwane. Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my oil palm trees producing very small fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Small bunches occur when oil palms lack adequate potassium, water, or light. Pruning old, dead fronds allows sunlight to reach the crown, while applying potassium-rich fertilizer improves bunch size and oil yield.
ga: Kuu bibii baa kɛji mu tsei lɛ bɛ potassium, nu loo la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Fern tsei ni egbɔ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni ehaa fɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen fertilizer, or the soil has too much water which stops the roots from taking in nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why does my farm soil turn hard like a brick after a few harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ brikii yɛ ŋmaa fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil becomes hard when it loses its organic matter from continuous farming; adding animal manure or compost helps keep the soil soft so plant roots can breathe and grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jɛɔ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ fiteɔ. Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my cowpea and groundnut plants grow well even without adding chemical nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea kɛ peanut tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ tsofa ni ji nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts have special bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and feed the plant naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha tsei

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil, so when water stays on the farm for too long without draining, fungi grow and cause the roots to spoil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ hia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Fuji lɛ daa ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves get full of tiny holes during the warm dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Small caterpillars, such as the diamondback moth, hatch in large numbers during warm weather and feed on the tender cabbage leaves.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ Diamond Moth Amɛfɔɔ babaoo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. ni oye kaabeji baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily in full sunlight, so fast-growing plantain leaves act like big umbrellas to give them shade and moisture during their first years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantain tso lɛ baai ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather is too hot or when they lack water, as a way to save energy to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu bɛ. Bɔni afee ni akɛ hewalɛ ato shihilɛ mli

english: Why must I tie my yam vines to wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to catch more sunlight to feed the growing tuber underneath, while keeping leaves away from wet soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni ekɛhaa ŋmeii ni miida yɛ shishi lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I change the crop I plant on my field every season instead of planting maize every time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting different crops breaks the life cycle of pests that target one plant, and helps keep the soil from losing all its nutrients.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ ashihilɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ akalaaje.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the tomato plant does not get enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: What is the difference between planting my seeds in a nursery bed and using polybags?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ poly bags ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ teŋ?

english: A nursery seedbed allows you to plant directly into the ground, while polybags hold soil in individual plastic bags. Both methods help nurse seedlings, but polybags make it easier to transfer plants to the farm without disturbing their roots.
ga: Dumɔwui ashishi haa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, poly kotokui lɛ hiɛɔ sũ ni yɔɔ plastic kotoku fɛɛ kotoku mli lɛ. Gbɛi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛkwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Shi poly bags lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie tsei kɛya ŋmɔji amli ni agbalaaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I water the nursery bed before I put my seeds or plants in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mi-nursery saatso lɛ nɔ nu dani mikɛ dumɔwui loo tsei afata he lɛ?

english: Watering the soil base beforehand ensures the ground is soft and sufficiently moist, which helps the tender young roots establish quickly and prevents transplant shock.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni edɔ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ feɔ oya, ni ehaaa shoofeemɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ mli baa lɛ naa.

english: Is it better to grow my seedlings in polybags before taking them to the main field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui awo poly bags amli dani adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Using polybags is a great option because it protects the root system inside the bag when moving crops to the farm, though planting directly in a seedbed is also a valid, traditional method.
ga: Poly bags ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebuɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ ahe kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui adumɔ tɛ̃ɛ hu ji kusum gbɛ ni abaanyɛ atsɔ nɔ atsu nii moŋ.

english: Can I uproot seedlings directly from a nursery bed to plant on my main farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbala dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni mayadu yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Yes, this is a one-stage process where seedlings are carefully uprooted from the initial nursery bed and transplanted straight to the farm field.
ga: Hɛɛ, enɛ ji gbɛ kome ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishijee ŋmɔ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ amɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Are there different options for how I can start growing my new seedlings?
ga: Ani gbɛi srɔtoi yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajeɔ dumɔwui heei ashishi?

english: Yes, you can choose between two main methods: planting directly into a watered seedbed, or nursing each seed individually inside a plastic polybag.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ohala gbɛi titrii enyɔ ateŋ: Okɛdumɔ awo dumɔwui ni awo mli nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. aloo ni adu dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko srɔtoi yɛ plastic polybag mli

english: How long does the nursery stage usually take before crops are ready for the farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ heɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Depending on the crop, the process of raising seedlings in a nursery bed or polybag until they are ready for the main farm takes about six months.
ga: Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli loo polybags amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔ wulu lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ. Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: How long should I expect to wait from planting my crop process until it matures on the farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: For many crops following this cultivation approach, the cycle from early propagation to full growth or transplant readiness takes around six months.
ga: Yɛ tsei babaoo ni nyiɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ asɛɛ lɛ agbɛfaŋ lɛ, Be ni amɛshwereɔ mra kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa loo amɛsaa amɛhe kɛha tsei krokomɛi lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ.

english: What does a one-stage planting process mean for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nibii amli yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: A one-stage process means growing seedlings in one place and then uprooting them directly to take them straight to your farm, without moving them through multiple container stages.
ga: Gbɛ kome ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ tsɔɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he kome. No sɛɛ lɛ, jiemɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni okɛya oŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni otsɔ tsɛnsii babaoo amli

english: How does keeping the base of the plant wet help during transplanting?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni aaawo lɛ nu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua yɛ tso kroko ni aaawo lɛ mli?

english: Moistening the soil around the base provides essential water for the root system, reducing stress on the plant when it is moved or planted.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ ni afee Shishitoo ni mli efɔ lɛ baaha nu ni he hiaa kɛha shishifãi lɛ aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa haomɔ ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ baa shi kɛ́ amɛmiiya loo amɛmiidu.

english: Where can I learn proper techniques for nursing and planting my crops?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ makase ŋaai ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ?

english: Agricultural extension agents and agricultural training programs teach farmers practical skills like choosing seedbeds, using polybags, and proper watering techniques.
ga: Okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛ okwaayeli he tsɔsemɔ gbɛjianɔtoi tsɔɔ okwaafoi lɛ nibii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii, tamɔ dumɔwui ashikpɔji ni ahalaa. Poly bags kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ŋaai ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, harsh sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil, or the soil is too waterlogged and drowning the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen niyenii bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ miiho. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stems at an angle instead of straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafee nɔ ni ja?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slanting angle helps the roots spread out evenly near the surface, making it easier for the plant to form bigger tubers and yield a better harvest.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes weak, thin stalks that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why are my pepper flowers dropping off the plants before producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant suffers heat stress, irregular watering, or poor soil fertility. Keeping the soil consistently moist and rich in organic matter prevents flower drop.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the same spot where I just harvested peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato lɛ yɛ he ni mifo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same plant family and attract the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them in the same spot repeatedly allows pests in the soil to easily destroy the new crop.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei akuu kome mli ni amɛgbalaa helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ni ooodu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha efee mlɛo aha kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii heei.

english: Watering early in the morning allows roots to absorb water before the hot sun evaporates it, keeping the leaves cool and hydrated throughout the heat of the day.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to grow healthy tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good soil for tomatoes feels crumbly, drains excess water easily so roots don't rot, and is rich in dark organic matter like manure or compost.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha tomato lɛ mli etse. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ mlɛo No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbooo. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my watermelons turning black and rotting while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ beni eyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This black rot at the bottom is caused by calcium deficiency, which happens when the plant experiences irregular watering during fruit formation.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi nɛɛ jɛɔ calcium ni faaa lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to be dug up from the farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the base of the main stem thickens, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is waterlogged and preventing roots from breathing. Adding compost or manure feeds the soil and restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli obɔ ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I drop fertilizer directly against the main stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mitso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer right against the stem causes direct chemical burns to the plant's skin and roots. Spreading it in a small ring around the plant allows roots to reach out and safely absorb nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha tsofa ashã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ agbɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai bibii ashwã tso lɛ he lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he shweshweeshwe ni amɛŋɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive harsh, direct sunlight during their first years. Leaving canopy trees or planting plantains provides shade and keeps the soil cool and moist for the seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii loo dumɔwui lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ kɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into tight rolls during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl as a natural defense to trap moisture and stop water loss under intense sun, but continuous curling can also mean tiny insects like mites or aphids are sucking sap from the underside of the leaf.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekpa nu ni hoɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ. Shi ŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli nu

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without ever producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when extreme heat or drought stresses the plant, stopping pollination. Keeping soil moisture steady with mulching helps flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao. ni akpa pollination Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ mulching nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller maize cobs when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ be mli ni adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and ground water, resulting in thin stems and small ears. Proper spacing gives each plant the room it needs to yield full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ toi bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa tsu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo tso lɛ mli ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant cowpeas or beans inside my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans naturally pull nitrogen out of the air and fix it into the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for the maize. In return, tall maize stalks provide structural support for bean vines to climb.
ga: Beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ koni amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: What causes holes in the fresh leaves of my young maize plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bulɛ baa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai heei lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding inside the central whorl. Spotting them early allows you to control them before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Ni ooona amɛ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ amɛnɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally hardier and better adapted to native soil than domesticated crops, allowing them to drink water and take nutrients instantly. Clearing weeds early keeps them from starving your crops.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ anɔ fe shia tsei. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi hɔmɔ ni yeɔ onibii lɛ anaa.

english: How can I keep my harvested yams from turning soft and rotting in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafee blɛoo ni efite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when exposed to direct heat, darkness, or stagnant air. Storing them on elevated bamboo shelves inside a cool, well-ventilated shade barn allows fresh air to keep tubers dry and sound.
