ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo dɔlɛ, duŋ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni ekã shi. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ni yitsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep drooping during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up during peak afternoon heat. As long as the soil has moisture and the plants bounce back in the evening, this midday wilting is just a temporary defense mechanism to conserve water.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ lɛ, Nɛkɛ gbi mli ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji be kukuoo mli hebuu gbɛ ko kɛkɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he.

english: Why do my hot pepper seeds take almost two weeks to sprout while my maize sprouts in just three days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hot pepper dumɔwui lɛ he nɔ ni miihe ashɛ otsii enyɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni mi-corn lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ gbii etɛ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds have tough, thick outer coats and need continuous warmth and moisture to break that coat down, whereas maize seeds absorb water rapidly and have softer seed coats that allow quick sprouting.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui yɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni wa, ni mli tse. Ni ehe miihia ni ená hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be koni enyɛ efo nakai ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ nu oya, ni eyɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: I want to start growing swamp rice to sell, but why does rice need standing water to grow when my maize rots in water?
ga: Miisumɔ ni madu ŋmãa ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ. Shi mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ be mli ni ŋmãa fiteɔ yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes in their stems that carry oxygen down to their roots under water. Maize roots lack these air channels, so standing water cuts off their oxygen and causes the roots to decay.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Abele shishifãi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off when there are no bigger trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Without shade plants like plantains or shade trees to shelter them, the heat damages the leaves, causing them to turn yellow and drop off to protect the main stem.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ lɛ baafite baai lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he.

english: Why are my sweet orange trees dropping small green fruits onto the ground long before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ekwɛ̃?

english: Fruit dropping happens when a tree faces stress from irregular watering, poor nutrients, or heat. The tree sheds excess fruit it cannot support so it can save enough energy to keep the rest of the plant alive.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Niyenii ni esaaa loo dɔlɛ baaha tso lɛ awo yibii babaoo ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ ato hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize field have small, neat holes in them overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Agbe naa nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed deep inside the rolled-up leaves during the cool night. As the leaf grows and unfolds, the small chew marks expand into visible lines of holes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ baai ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Beni baai lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ŋmɔtɔ he okadii bibii lɛ Ebaagbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ bu ko ni anaa.

english: If I plant cowpeas together in the same field with my maize, will the cowpeas steal food from the maize plants?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli Ani tsina ŋmãa baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa tsei amli?

english: No, cowpeas actually feed the soil. As legumes, cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer through their roots, which actually helps neighboring maize grow stronger.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Taakɛ eji ŋmãa lɛ, Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni edaraa waa.

english: My cassava plants are growing very tall with bushy green leaves, so why are the tubers under the ground so small?
ga: Mi yucca tso lɛ daa waa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive water, it spends all its energy producing leaves above ground instead of storing starch below. Reducing nitrogen forces the plant to send its energy down into expanding the tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu babaoo nɔ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmãa baato shishi. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi lɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ bulbs lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: A plantain stem is biologically built to flower and fruit only once. After harvesting, the main stem naturally dies back so its remaining nutrients can feed the young shoots (suckers) growing at its base for the next harvest.
ga: Akɛ wala yibii fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ. kpamɔ sɛɛ Tso titri lɛ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam leaves and vines dry up completely at the start of the dry season while the yam tuber under the ground stays fresh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes kɛ wain tsei lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ ehee lolo lɛ

english: Yam vines naturally wither to enter a resting state called dormancy during dry weather. The plant preserves itself by storing all water and food underground in the tuber until the next rain season arrives.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛboteɔ shihilɛ ni bɛ mli mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli. Tso lɛ kwɛɔ ehe nɔ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ bulb lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: If my cocoa tree is sick with swollen shoot disease, why can't I just spray it with chemicals instead of cutting it down?
ga: Kɛji akɛ hela mɔ kookoo tso lɛ ni eshishifãi efuu lɛ Mɛni hewɔ okɛ tsofai shwieee nɔ moŋ fe ni ooofolɔ amɛ?

english: The swollen shoot virus lives deep inside the sap system of the tree where chemical sprays cannot reach. Cutting the infected tree completely is the only proven way to stop the virus from spreading to the rest of your healthy farm.
ga: Bud swollen virus lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni abaafolɔ amɛ kwraa lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. ni ji oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli

english: Can a sick cocoa tree pass its disease to the healthy trees planted next to it?
ga: Ani cacao tso ni hela mɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, insects like mealybugs carry the virus from infected trees to healthy ones, and the roots of touching trees can also transfer the sickness underground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs lɛ hiɛɔ helai kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Ni tsei shishifãi ni taa amɛhe lɛ baanyɛ agbala helai ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If I cut down a sick cocoa tree, do I also need to dig out the roots underground?
ga: Kɛ́ ofo kookoo tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ, ani ehe miihia ni otsa shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yes, because the virus can stay alive in the active root system for months. If left in the soil, infected roots can pass the sickness to newly planted seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shishifã ni tsuɔ nii mli nyɔji babaoo. Kɛji ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shishifãi ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela lɛ ashwã dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ anɔ.

english: How does cutting down my diseased cocoa trees benefit my farm in the long run?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cacao tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: While it feels like losing your farm today, cutting infected trees stops the disease from destroying your entire crop. Replanting with healthy, modern cocoa varieties gives you much higher yields and profits in the future.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ onuɔ he tamɔ nɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ elaaje moŋ. Shi tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ haaa hela lɛ akpata onibii fɛɛ ahiɛ. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha oná yibii babaoo kɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees stop producing many pods even when I clear the weeds and apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ ekpa ŋmeii babaoo ni ewoɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni mikɛwo mli lɛ ewo mli moŋ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 25 to 30 years, their internal transport system slows down, making them less efficient at absorbing nutrients and producing pods regardless of how much fertilizer you use.
ga: Beni cacao tso lɛ yeɔ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ emli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmeii fioo pɛ feɔ. Ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii ohaa.

english: Will a new cocoa seedling grow properly if I plant it in the exact spot where I cut an old diseased tree?
ga: Ani cacao tso hee lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu yɛ he ni afo tso momo ni hela emɔ lɛ yɛ lɛ?

english: You must wait for the old roots to rot completely and prepare the soil properly; otherwise, remnants of the disease in the old roots can infect the new seedling.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni shishifãi momo lɛ agbo kwraa ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, helai ni eshwɛ yɛ shishifãi momoi amli lɛ baanyɛ atswa dumɔwui heei.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that lose water very quickly in direct heat. They require shade crops like plantains during their first few years to protect them from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ shɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he.

english: How long does a newly replanted hybrid cocoa tree take to start bearing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Unlike older traditional cocoa varieties that took 5 years, modern hybrid cocoa trees usually start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years if properly cared for.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ cacao tsei ni etsɛ, ni ji kusum nifeemɔi, ni yeɔ afii enumɔ lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cacao tsei ni akɛ tsofa ebɔ he lɛ baaje shishi amɛwo ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the branches on my cocoa trees swelling and turning misshapen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mikooko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efuu ni efite lɛ?

english: Swollen branches are a classic symptom of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which causes abnormal cell growth in the tree before reducing its pod production and eventually killing it.
ga: Niji ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ he okadi ni ale waa, ni haa tsei amli wala yibii lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. dani ebaa pod ni afeɔ lɛ shi ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbe lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, overly shaded environments with poor airflow between trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi fe nine. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward to protect themselves from losing too much water during hot dry spells. It is a natural survival mechanism to conserve moisture until the next rain comes.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crop flowers keep falling off before turning into fruits when the dry spell starts early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi mra lɛ?

english: When plants do not get enough water from rainfall, they experience extreme stress and shed their flowers to save energy to stay alive, which stops fruits or pods from forming.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ mli Amɛkɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpeɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli. Enɛ haa aduawai loo pod feemɔ kpaa.

english: What will happen to my seeds if I plant them in dry soil while waiting for the rains to start?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi?

english: Seeds buried in dry soil can rot if they get only a tiny splash of rain, or they can be eaten by insects and birds before steady rains come to help them germinate properly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu yɛ sũ ni egbi mli lɛ baanyɛ agbo kɛji nugbɔ fioo po nɛ. Aloo kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi baanyɛ aye lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be koni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which crops can survive better on my farm if the rains are not regular this year?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ afi nɛɛ mli?

english: Drought-tolerant crops like sorghum, millet, and cassava have deep root systems or efficient water usage, allowing them to handle irregular rainfall much better than crops like maize.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa Eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo ekɛ nu tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ ekpeɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How can I keep moisture in my soil for my crops when the rains stop suddenly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Covering your farm soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground and prevents the harsh sun from drying out crop roots quickly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa ni ehaa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haaa tso shishifãi lɛ agbi oya.

english: How does adding animal manure help my crops survive dry breaks between rainy days?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ gbii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Manure acts like a natural sponge in the soil, soaking up water when it rains and holding onto it for a long time so your crops can keep drinking during long dry spells.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ni ekɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni onuɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow after I applied fertilizer during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need soil moisture to safely absorb fertilizer. Applying fertilizer to dry soil without rain can burn the plant roots and cause the leaves to yellow or stunt plant growth.
ga: Tsei lɛ hia ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ loo tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why did my groundnuts produce many leaves but very few pods this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ miiwo baai babaoo shi pods fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts need steady rain specifically during their flowering and pod-forming stages. If rain fails during this critical period, the plant puts energy into leaves rather than developing underground pods.
ga: Nugbɔ he miihia ŋmeii daa, titri lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli lɛ Tsei tsɔɔ hewalɛ mli kɛyaa amɛbaai lɛ amli moŋ fe ni amɛaafee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is too much rain late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall fills all the air spaces in the soil with water, suffocating root crops and creating a wet environment where soil fungi quickly decay the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ehaa shihilɛ ko ni mli efɔ ni sũ mli ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: Is it better to water my vegetables in the hot afternoon sun or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai ni hulu egbi lɛ nu shwane loo leebi?

english: Watering early in the morning gives plants time to absorb moisture before the sun heats up, preventing rapid water loss through evaporation and protecting leaves from heat stress.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa be ni ekɛnuɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ haa edɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ nu ni laajeɔ oya lɛ naa kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and turn yellow when I remove all the tall shade trees from the plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally thrive under partial canopy cover because direct, intense tropical sun scorches their tender leaves and dries out topsoil moisture. Without shade trees to filter sunlight, the young plants suffer heat stress and cannot retain water properly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baatsi hulu la lɛ naa lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava right next to my young cocoa trees to feed my family while the cocoa grows?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ahe koni mikɛha miweku lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Planting cassava too close to young cocoa is risky because cassava has heavy tuberous roots that aggressively strip water and nutrients from the soil, while its broad leaf canopy can block light from young cocoa plants. Crops like plantain or cocoyam provide better companion shade without overwhelming the cocoa.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo bibii lɛ tsɔ lɛ yɛ oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni tsii ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa. yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛitsu lɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ la ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ naa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ plantain loo kookoo baaha hulutsoo kpakpa aba ni eyeee kookoo lɛ nɔ kunim.

english: If I cut off the vertical shoots growing straight up from my cocoa branches, will it damage the tree?
ga: Kɛ mifo tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo nine lɛ mli lɛ, Ani ebaakpãtã tsei ahiɛ?

english: Cutting off vertical shoots, known as chupons or water shoots, actually helps the tree. Removing them stops the tree from wasting food on excessive upward stem growth and redirects energy into healthy side branches where cocoa pods develop.
ga: Afoɔ tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ, ni ale amɛ hu akɛ chupons loo nu mli tsei. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei diɛŋtsɛ Amɛjiemɔ haaa tso lɛ akafite niyenii kɛtsɔ tso lɛ shishifã ni kɛlɛ fe nine lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ hewalɛ lɛ yaa niji ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ he ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the tiny cocoa pods on my trees turning black and shriveling before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mitsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Small pods often turn black due to a condition called cherelle wilt or fungal attacks like black pod disease. Cherelle wilt occurs naturally when the tree cannot support all the pods it started growing, but excessive wetness and poor airflow can cause fungal infections that kill healthy young pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherel’s wilt lɛ hewɔ. loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tamɔ black pod hela lɛ, Cherelle wilt baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai fɛɛ ni ebɔi shweremɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ. Shi hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aba.

english: Will burning the cut bush before planting make my crops grow faster and stronger?
ga: Ani mi tsei lɛ ni mikɛshãa dani miduɔ lɛ baaha mitsei lɛ adara oya ni amɛhe awa?

english: Burning offers a quick temporary burst of nutrient-rich ash, but it destroys essential organic matter and soil micro-organisms needed for long-term crop health. Over time, burned soil loses its ability to hold water, making roots dry out much faster.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ haa sũ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ tswaa oya yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni eshã lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ nu dɔŋŋ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kwraa.

english: Why do some timber trees in my farm help cocoa produce more pods while other trees seem to kill the cocoa around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mikoo lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi feɔ nakai lɛ? Etamɔ nɔ ni efite kookoo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: Certain indigenous trees drop leaves that rot into rich organic manure and fix nutrients in the soil, helping nearby cocoa thrive. Other tree species have shallow, aggressive root systems or toxic leaf litter that rob cocoa roots of water and plant food.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ shiɔ amɛbaai ni egboi lɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo ni amɛhiɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kookoo lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ. Tsei krokomɛi Eyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni mli wa loo baai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers during heavy rain seasons instead of forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ fɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and high humidity make it difficult for tiny insects, like midges, to move around and pollinate cocoa flowers. Without pollination, unfertilized flowers naturally fall off the branches, and excess moisture can lead to fungal flower drop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa kooloi bibii tamɔ midges fãa kɛyaa he fɛɛ he. ni ewa akɛ abaafee pollination yɛ cocoa fɔfɔii amli Kɛji pollination bɛ Fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛjɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni hulutsoo be babaoo baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: If I plant my cocoa trees very close together, will I harvest more cocoa pods from my small farm?
ga: Kɛ midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ mibaakpa kookoo ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: Planting too densely causes trees to fight each other for limited sun, soil food, and underground moisture. Overcrowded trees grow tall and thin with fewer pod-bearing branches, and the trapped damp air makes it easier for diseases to spread.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ he akaŋ. Tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi lɛ baafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛbaafee mlɛo ni amɛniji fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are getting too old to produce good harvests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: As cocoa trees pass 25 to 30 years of age, their trunks become gnarled, trunk branch growth slows down, and pod yields drop significantly. Older trees also become more susceptible to pests and diseases like swollen shoot virus.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko ye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, eshishifã lɛ feɔ ŋmeii. Tso lɛ niji lɛ adalɛ baa shi. ni pod yibiiwoo lɛ ba shi kwraa. Tsei ni edara lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai tamɔ bud swelling virus.

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning pale yellow after planting them in soil that has grown cocoa for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee beni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ kookoo yɛ nɔ afii babaoo lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cocoa trees absorb large amounts of essential plant nutrients like nitrogen and potassium over their lifespan. When you plant food crops in old cocoa soil without adding organic compost or manure, the new crops starve from missing soil nutrients.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium, yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli. Beni oduɔ niyenii yɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ momo nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he. Tsei heei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Planting maize in straight, spaced rows gives every single plant enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients to grow big ears, while making it much easier for you to weed and apply fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ toii wuji akwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short and bent instead of growing long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle shi moŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eja lɛ?

english: Yams bend and stay short when the soil under them is too hard or stony. Creating tall, loose soil mounds allows the tubers to push down easily into the ground without hitting hard obstacles.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee kuku kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ tɛi tsɔ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni afee lɛ haa yitso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo ni ekɛ gbɛtsii nii ni wa etswaaa.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay near the top of the ground. When the soil becomes soft from rain and the fruit heavy at the top, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the earth.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ efee blɛoo kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni aduawai lɛ tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving black powder inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii diji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that hides deep inside the center of the young maize leaves and feeds on the plant as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni teɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning yellow with white spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ-ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that suck sap from the underside of the leaves.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi ni cassava mosaic hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing big leaves and instead grow lots of tiny, clustered pale leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ekpa baai wuji ni ewoɔ baai bibii ni mli tse babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: This is called pepper leaf curl virus, which is transmitted by small insects like thrips or aphids. The virus stunts the plant's normal development, preventing it from bearing big peppers.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ pepper baa hela. Kplukai bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ hela lɛ baa. Virus gbalaa tsei adalɛ ni sa lɛ mli. Tsi ŋmɔtɔi wuji anaa koni amɛkafee.

english: When temperatures get extremely hot, tomato flowers cannot fertilize properly. The plant drops the dried flowers to save its water and energy until the weather cools down.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ aná ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi ni egbi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on my farm right after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mikpa ŋmãa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of food from the soil, but beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen naturally from the air and store it in their roots, which restores rich food back into the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni okɛ niyenii ni jara wa aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Groundnuts are ready when the leaves turn yellow and dry out, and when you open a test pod, the inside wall of the shell has dark brown or black markings.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Ni kɛ́ ogbele kaa pod lɛ Akɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ ekadi ŋmeii lɛ amli gbogboi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize turn yellow when it rains continuously for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excessive rain washes away nitrogen from the soil and drowns plant roots, preventing them from breathing or absorbing nutrients properly, which makes the leaves turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when there are constant rain clouds and very little sun for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ be mli ni atatui yɔɔ be fɛɛ be ni hulu la fioo pɛ yɔɔ nyɔji babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need sunlight to make food through a process called photosynthesis. Even with plenty of water, without enough sunshine, plants cannot produce energy to grow quickly.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la koni amɛ fee niyenii kɛtsɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Kɛ nu babaoo po Shi hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Tsei nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ ni baaha amɛdara oya kɛkɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting during this prolonged heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rainfall and high humidity create the perfect environment for a fungus to spread and cause Black Pod disease. Pruning tree branches lets air flow through and reduces excess moisture.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ekɛ blackpod hela baa. Tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ baa shi.

english: What makes the stems of my tomato plants go soft and rot after days of non-stop rain?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbii babaoo ni ekpaaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Too much water on the stems and leaves allows fungal and bacterial diseases to attack the plant. Staking tomato plants keeps them off wet ground and lowers the risk of rot.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ bacteria helai atutua tso lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ wo ŋtayaai amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ anaa, ni ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ amɛbaafite lɛ baa shi.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if rainwater sits on my farm for a long time?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Cassava roots will rot quickly if they remain submerged in wet soil because they need well-drained ground to stay healthy. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ baagboi oya kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ ejaakɛ ehe miihia ni amɛná he ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why does the dark top layer of soil wash off my farm whenever heavy rains last for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsuɔ waa lɛ hoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Unprotected soil easily gets carried away by heavy flowing rainwater through soil erosion. Planting cover crops like leguminous plants helps bind the soil and protect it from heavy rain.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni abuuu he lɛ oya kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: How do I know if it is safe to plant my seeds when the heavy rains start earlier in the year than expected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Wait until the soil is consistently moist across several days rather than planting right after the first heavy rainfall, as early unusual rains can stop abruptly and cause young seedlings to dry out.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii komɛi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra ni bɛ daa lɛ baanyɛ akpa trukaa ni eha tsei bibii lɛ agbi.

english: Which crops survive best in farmland that stays flooded or very wet during long rain periods?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ okwaayeli hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Crops like swamp rice and cocoyam thrive in extremely wet soils, whereas crops like groundnuts or cowpeas prefer dry, well-drained soils and will spoil in waterlogged conditions.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ marsh rice kɛ cocoa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni ebaagbo yɛ shihilɛi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops while the heavy rainy season is at its peak?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: It is best to wait for a break in heavy rain, as constant downpours will wash the fertilizer away into streams before the plant roots can soak it up.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛya faa lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after months of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyɔji babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong root systems that absorb excess water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to take over quickly during wet periods.
ga: Weed ji koo mli tso ko ni shishifãi ni mli wa waa yɔɔ mli. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ nɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil that plants use to make food and stay healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛhaa amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli.

english: Planting tomatoes repeatedly in the same soil drains specific nutrients and allows tomato-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, weakening future yields.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tomato nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ wɔsɛɛ lɛ baagbɔjɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess water fills the air spaces in the soil, drowning the roots and encouraging fungal diseases that cause rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main mother plant, causing the main plant to produce smaller bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Ha tso titri lɛ awo plantains bibii bibii.

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to produce energy for the underground tubers to grow big. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground and spreads them out to catch full sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ adara. Staking baabu tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe ni ebaagbɛ eshwa koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ.

english: Why should I leave proper spacing between my pepper plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ abɔ he ni sa moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crowded pepper plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, and their close leaves trap humidity, making it easy for fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Pepper tsei ni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Baai ni agbe naa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves dry up and fall off during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds rapidly strip moisture from young cocoa leaves. The trees drop their leaves as a protective instinct to preserve water inside their stems.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai bibii amli oya. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛto nu he yɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that provide essential shade and keep the soil cool and moist for young cocoa.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛha kookoo bibii.

english: Why do weeds on my farm make my crops stay small even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops before your crops can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft, tender inner leaves of young maize plants where moisture accumulates, feeding heavily during early growth stages.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ buaa ehe naa ni eyeɔ nii babaoo yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee be mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sun during the dry season (Harmattan) burns their delicate leaves and strips them of moisture. Planting shade trees or plantains around them keeps the soil moist and protects them from severe sun heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli (harmattan) lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛmli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off when the rainy season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during dry periods to save water and protect itself from drought. The plant is not dead; as soon as the rains return, it will grow fresh green leaves again.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baafee ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiye mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are fall armyworms, a common pest that attacks maize. They hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of the plant, so spraying early in the morning or late evening directly into the center funnel is necessary to reach and control them.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ji cutworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmãa. Akɛ amɛ etee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, leebi loo gbɛkɛ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsɔnei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he miihia koni anyɛ ashɛ amɛhe ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting while still growing on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa lolo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium, which is usually caused by irregular watering where the soil dries out too much between rainfalls.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ lɛ.

english: Why does the chemical spray I bought fail to clear the pests on my farm even when I use a lot of it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ shi ni mihe lɛ ejieee kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtsuɔ nii babaoo moŋ.

english: Pesticides only work if they match the specific pest and are mixed at the correct strength. If a chemical has been improperly diluted, stored poorly, or is the wrong type for that insect, adding more of it will still not work and may burn your crop leaves.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii pɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ kooloi pɔtɛɛ lɛ kpãa gbee ni akɛfutu mli yɛ bɔ ni sa mli. Kɛji akɛ tsofa lɛ mli ewo nu mli jogbaŋŋ, akɛtooo jogbaŋŋ, loo kɛji akɛ kooloo lɛ ji nɔ ni ejaaa lɛ, Tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛbaafata he lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ni ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer near the root zone of my crop instead of scattering it everywhere on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ moŋ fe ni magbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli he fɛɛ he?

english: Placing fertilizer close to the roots ensures your crop absorbs the nutrients directly before rain washes them away or wild weeds take them up first.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ dani nugbɔ shwieɔ amɛ loo koo mli jwɛi yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and have to support heavy fruit bunches. If you do not prune extra suckers growing around the main stem or support the tree with wooden props, strong winds will easily tip them over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Kɛji ofolɔɔɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ, Akɛ tso nibii fiɔ tso lɛ shishi loo tso lɛ shishi titri lɛ sɛɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baaha amɛku amɛsɛɛ oya.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small harvests when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni eji ŋmaa bibioo beni midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough space to build thick stems and large fruits.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei ashishifãi ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why does grass grow back so fast after I cut it down on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mifo jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Many grasses have strong roots and underground stems that stay alive even after the top part is cut off. To stop grass from returning quickly, you need to dig up the root systems or clear them before they set seeds.
ga: Jwɛi babaoo yɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni hiɔ shi kɛ́ afo amɛyiteŋ po. Enɛ haaa jwɛi lɛ aku esɛɛ oya. Esa akɛ otsa shishifãi lɛ loo ojie mli dani okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo mli.

english: Why do some of my saved maize seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds stored in damp or hot places lose their strength or get eaten inside by insects like weevils. Drying seeds thoroughly and storing them in airtight containers protects their ability to germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ loo hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii baaye amɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ agbimɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsinsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their leaves burn easily under full sunlight. Keeping larger shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains protects the cocoa seedlings and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa bushes grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo be kukuoo mli tsei tamɔ kookoo plantains ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make healthy green leaves. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and share the same pests and soil diseases. Planting them in the same spot season after season allows these pests and diseases to build up in the soil, so alternating with crops like maize or beans breaks the disease cycle.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ tsei aweku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome. Tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ haa nɛkɛ kooloi kɛ helai nɛɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the land for too long, water fills all the tiny air spaces in the dirt and starves the roots of air, causing them to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli ni ehaa ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in standing water while my maize plants drown in the same swampy land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ? Be mli ni mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miiho yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal tubes in their stems that act like tiny pipes, carrying air from above the water down to their roots. Maize plants do not have these air tubes, so their roots choke when buried in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ mligbɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔnei bibii. Ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ nu lɛ yiteŋ lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Abɛi tsei bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ afu amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: Having too many shoots around one plantain stem creates competition for light, water, and soil nutrients. Pruning extra shoots leaves only two or three strong suckers, which ensures the main plant gets enough strength to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Ni aaana plantain tsei ahe tsei babaoo kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ mli tsei 2-3 pɛ ahi shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it necessary to put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines use their leaves to catch sunlight and produce the food that grows the underground tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground away from heat and mud, allowing them to capture maximum sunlight to feed bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛhe hulu la lɛ ni amɛwo niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajie kɛjɛ latsaa kɛ muji lɛ he. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛná hulu la babaoo koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii wuji lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before turning into pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by intense heat, drought, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and covered with mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do groundnut plants need loose, soft soil around them after they finish flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he hiaa ŋmei tsei lɛ? Beni fɔfɔi lɛ etse sɛɛ

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they grow long stems called pegs that must push downward into the dirt to form the pods. Soft, loose soil makes it easy for these pegs to bury themselves and grow full groundnuts.
ga: Beni afee ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ, atsɛɔ ŋmei tsei kakadaji lɛ akɛ pegs. Esa akɛ ashɛ enɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee pod. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ amɛaafu amɛhe ni amɛdu ŋmeii.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly and stop the plant from growing big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Curled tomato leaves are usually caused by a plant virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Clearing weeds around the farm where whiteflies live and using proper insect management stops the virus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso hela ko ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ajiemɔ Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ whitefly gbɔi kɛ kooloi akwɛmɔ ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need to grow strong, or that the soil is holding too much water around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Aloo eji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔ?

english: Why should I leave proper space between my maize plants instead of planting them close together to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and tiny cobs instead of large, healthy ones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. This results in small, weak stems and cobs instead of large, strong branches.

english: Why is it dangerous for my maize field to dry out when the plants start producing flowers at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi beni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: The flowering stage is when the maize plant forms its grains. If it lacks water during this period, the cobs will end up with missing kernels or remain completely empty.
ga: Fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ ji be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ woɔ dumɔwui. Kɛji nu faaa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Cob lɛ bɛ dumɔwui loo ebaafee efolo kwraa.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily when a strong wind blows through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over if the seed was planted too shallow, if the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium, or if insects have damaged the roots and stem base.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium loo kɛji kooloi fiteɔ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my maize to grow slowly even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ be mli ni awo mli ŋmãa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than maize and steal the nutrients, water, and light meant for your crops, effectively starving your maize despite the fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa ni ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ o-corn lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii po.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my maize leaves and tiny caterpillars inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Yɛ tso lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli

english: That is damage from pests like Fall Armyworms. They feed on young leaves, and catching them early with proper treatment prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: No ji nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii. kɛ amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, abaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers advise me to plant beans or groundnuts on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, but legumes like beans and groundnuts naturally take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring its strength for the next season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ejɛɔ adebɔɔ mli ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ

english: Why should I add animal manure or compost to my soil instead of using only chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he moŋ fe ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ baatsu nii?

english: Chemical fertilizers feed the plant, but manure and compost build up the soil itself, helping it hold moisture longer during dry spells and keeping it healthy over many years.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ maa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ afii babaoo.

english: It is best to wait until the soil gets a few steady, deep soaking rains so that the ground stays moist enough for seeds to sprout and build strong roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fioo. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize cobs completely before putting them into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ kwraa dani mikɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Damp maize grows mold and attracts insects like weevils quickly in storage, whereas properly dried maize stays fresh and safe to eat or sell for many months.
ga: Abɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ shwereɔ oya ni egbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni agbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baakã he ahi shi ehee ni ehi akɛ aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Wait until the soil stays consistently moist for a few days after the first rains. Planting during initial, sudden showers can cause seeds to dry up and die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji hɔmɔ shihilɛi nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops look withered even when it rained heavily just a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo lɛ? Ni nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ?

english: Heavy rain often runs off dry, hard ground without soaking deep into the soil. Adding organic manure helps the soil hold onto water like a sponge so roots can drink longer between rains.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa nɔ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efɔɔɔ shi tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli tamɔ sponji. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if there is too much rain during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Excessive rain can cause waterlogging, which cuts off oxygen to the roots and causes root rot. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away safely.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha nu abɔle he. Enɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow after long periods of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous rain washes essential nutrients like nitrogen deep out of the root zone, leaving the plant hungry and turning its leaves yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa tso lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do leaf diseases seem to spread much faster on my farm when it rains constantly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kwraa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Fungal and bacterial diseases thrive in high humidity and moisture, and splashing raindrops physically spread disease spores from leaf to leaf.
ga: Fungal kɛ bacteria helai yaa hiɛ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Ni nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ gbɛɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ.

english: How can I protect my crop roots from drying out when the rain suddenly stops for a week?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa otsi kome lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dry grass or leaves (mulching) traps moisture in the soil and prevents the sun from drying out the root area.
ga: Mulch ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) shwieɔ tso lɛ he lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa hulu la lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops right before a big downpour comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?

english: No, heavy storms will wash the fertilizer away into streams before plants can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but torrential rain is not expected.
ga: Dabi, ahum ni naa wa waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ faai amli dani tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi akpaaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants during heavy rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Strong rains physically damage delicate blossoms and prevent insects from pollinating them, causing the flowers to drop off before setting fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kpataa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahiɛ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ, ni ehaaa kooloi bibii afee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it important to clear and loosen my soil before the wet season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajie lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Preparing the ground early allows the soil to immediately trap and absorb the first rains, giving your crops a soft, moist bed to grow quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ amɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni eŋɔ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ náa he ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni baakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rain completely floods the ground, it pushes all air out of the soil. Without air, seeds suffocate and rot before they can sprout into plants.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ kɛyashi ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei.

english: Why does milling my harvested corn into flour help it last longer before spoiling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ni ashwieɔ lɛ ni efeɔ ashikishaŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ dani efiteɔ lɛ?

english: Milling removes the outer surface where insects like to lay eggs, and proper drying before milling removes moisture that mold needs to grow. Stored in clean, sealed containers, processed flour or grist stays usable far longer than raw grain.
ga: Miling jieɔ kponɔgbɛ he ni kooloi sumɔɔ ni amɛwo amɛwui lɛ yɛ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ agbi jogbaŋŋ dani aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ adara lɛ kɛyaa. Akɛtoɔ tsɛnsi ni mli tse ni aŋã mli jogbaŋŋ mli. Ashikishaŋ ni afee lɛ loo ni agbɛlɛ lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ fe ŋmaa ni ahoko lɛ.

english: Does processing my surplus corn into flour or feed make it easier to sell to buyers far away?
ga: Ani mi-abele ni fa fe nine lɛ ni mikɛfeɔ ashikishaŋ loo kooloi aniyenii lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ maha mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, processing crops reduces their weight and volume, prevents them from spoiling during transport, and opens up new markets like bakeries, households, and livestock farms that need ready-to-use ingredients.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni atsu he nii lɛ baaye abua ni eha shwiili lɛ shwiili kɛ shwiili lɛ shwiili lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa yɛ gbɛfaa mli. kɛ jarayeli hei heei tamɔ aboloofeemɔ hei, shia kɛ kooloi alɛɛhei ni he hiaa nibii ni afee klalo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ agbelemɔ.

english: What causes my stored maize cobs to turn into dust and get full of small insects after a few months?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ sũ ni ŋmeii bibii eyi mli obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Storage pests like maize weevils burrow inside dry grains to feed and lay eggs. If the grain is not dried properly or stored in insect-proof bags, these pests multiply rapidly and eat the crop from the inside out.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii amli tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli koni amɛye niyenii ni amɛwo ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo akɛtooo kotokui ni kooloi nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ faa oya ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why does my corn rot or smell bad when I put it into bags immediately after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa kɛ́ mikɛwo kotoku mli beni akpa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested corn holds natural moisture inside the grain. Trapping wet corn in sealed sacks creates heat and moisture, which causes mold, fungi, and bacteria to grow quickly and ruin the harvest.
ga: Abele ni akpa ehee lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Abɛi ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Enɛ haa ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ muawai shwereɔ oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my stored grains spoil much faster during the rainy season than during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli fe harmattan be lɛ?

english: Rainy weather makes the air humid, and dry grains absorb moisture directly from damp air. This added moisture reactivates dormant mold spores and encourages insects to breed.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ni ŋmaa ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɛkɛ fɛ̃i ni akɛfata he nɛɛ tsirɛɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ nitsumɔ lɛ. ni ekanyaa kooloi bibii lɛ koni amɛshwere ekoŋŋ

english: Why do some of my corn varieties rot on the cob while still in the field before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele henɔi lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ beni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo dani mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Corn varieties with short or loose husk leaves allow rain and insects to enter the top of the cob. Varieties with tight husks that cover the tip completely protect the kernels from water damage.
ga: Abele henɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai kukuji loo ni etse amɛhe lɛ haa nugbɔ kɛ kooloi nyɛɔ amɛboteɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Henɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmei ni mli wa ni haa amɛhe lɛ buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kwraa koni nu akafite amɛ.

english: Why do my corn plants produce small, weak cobs even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize needs nutrients like nitrogen from healthy soil or fertilizer to build big cobs. Rain helps plants drink, but if the soil lacks food, the crop remains small and weak regardless of water.
ga: Niyenii nibii tamɔ nitrogen ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he miihia abele koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji. Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnuɔ nu. Shi kɛji niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakã he afee bibioo ni egbɔjɔ ekɔɔɔ he eko nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know my corn is dry enough for long-term storage or milling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ loo atsɔ mli?

english: You can test grains by biting one; if it cracks hard without denting, or if you shake dry salt with the grain in a jar and the salt stays loose without sticking, the corn is dry enough.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ŋmaa okwɛ kɛtsɔ amɛ ni oooye lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efo waa ni efeee ŋmeii Aloo kɛji okɛ ŋmei ni egbi lɛ kɛ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ tɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ŋmei lɛ jeɔ kpo lolo ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa.

english: How do weevils get inside my stored corn bags even when I keep them inside my room?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ko bote ŋmãa kotoku ni mikɛto lɛ mli? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ amɛ toɔ mitsu lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Weevil eggs are often laid on the corn cobs while the crop is still standing in the field before harvest. When you bring the corn indoors, the eggs hatch into visible insects inside the warm bags.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmeii awoɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii anɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo dani akpaa ŋmãa lɛ. Kɛ okɛ ŋmãa ba shĩa lɛ Wɔɔji lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni anaa yɛ kotoku ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I store my extra harvest safely when market prices are too low to sell right away?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ato shweshweeshwe? Beni jara lɛ baa shi tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Drying your grain thoroughly and storing it in airtight (hermetic) bags or sealed containers prevents oxygen from letting pests survive, allowing you to hold your crop until market prices go up.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nibii krokomɛi ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ toɔ kɛyashiɔ jara nɔ jara lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and burning under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu lɛ etswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as umbrellas and protect their leaves until they grow older and stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. To act as an umbrella and protect the leaves until they get older and stronger.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow healthy green leaves. Adding well-decomposed organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. This is the main food plant needed to grow healthy, green leaves. Adding organic fertilizer or well-degraded nitrogen fertilizer will restore the green color.

english: Is it safe for me to put fresh chicken droppings directly onto my growing crop fields?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee baafata midumɔ saatsoi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is too strong and generates heat that can burn young crop roots. You should dry and rot (compost) the manure for a few weeks before applying it to your crops.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ baa. Esa akɛ okɛ o-manure (compost) lɛ agbi ni okɛwo mli otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛwo onibii amli.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground right around the base of the stem starts to crack open as tubers expand underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baabɔi mligbalamɔ be mli ni yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences drought stress. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching around the roots helps save the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ aya nɔ ahi shi.

english: Why does my plantain plant produce so many extra shoots around the bottom, and should I cut them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ shishi lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ mafo mli?

english: Plantains grow side shoots called suckers, but if too many grow at once, they steal nutrients from the main plant. Trimming away extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong ones leads to bigger fruit stems.
ga: Plantains yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii. Shi kɛji odu babaoo shikome lɛ Feemɔ ekãa ni oju niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ agbo.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight for building big tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off the damp wet ground, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs agboi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi baai helai anaa.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper bushes to curl tightly upward and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni ekpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juice from the undersides of leaves. Spraying early with neem extract or soap solution helps clear these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ neem mli nu loo samla baashwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which hide in the central whorl of maize plants to feed on new leaves. Applying recommended neem-based treatments or approved pest solutions directly into the funnel kills them.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai heei. Kɛ́ akɛ neem tsofa loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ wo tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because roots absorb water before heat causes evaporation, giving plants the strength to stay hydrated through the afternoon heat.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shwane lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does my crop dry up so quickly when I plant in sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large particles with big gaps between them, which causes rainwater to drain away rapidly instead of staying near the roots where your crops can drink it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ. ni haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya Moŋ lɛ, ebɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ he ni onibii lɛ baanyɛ anu nu yɛ lɛ.

english: What can I mix into dry, sandy soil to help it hold water longer for my crops?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛfutu ŋã shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli koni eye ebua ni nu lɛ ahi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Mixing organic materials like rabbit manure into sandy soil helps bind the loose soil grains together so it acts like a sponge, holding moisture around your crop roots for a much longer time.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋshɔŋlooi afɔfɔi, ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii bibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ afee ekome. No hewɔ lɛ etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ahi otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my crops wither quickly in sandy farm areas even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ ŋã ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Sandy soil loses moisture very fast through quick drainage and evaporation; adding rich organic animal manure helps lock that rainwater in place so your crops stay hydrated.
ga: Shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔ nu ni hoɔ oya kɛ lasu ni hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Koolooi a-organic ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ nu lɛ ahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does rabbit manure help my crops grow better during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Rabbit manure adds rich organic matter to the soil that absorbs water and releases nutrients slowly, keeping the ground damp and feeding your crops when rainfall is scarce.
ga: Kpɔŋɔ fɔmɔ nii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni no gbalaa nu ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fiofio. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ.

english: Is animal manure better than chemical fertilizer for keeping moisture in my soil?
ga: Ani kooloi ashishifãi hi fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli ni haa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, for soil structure. Chemical fertilizers feed plants directly but do not hold water, whereas organic manure like rabbit manure physically improves the soil so it captures and retains water.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ shishitoo. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ shi amɛhiɛɛɛ nu mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ koni enyɛ ehiɛ nu mli ni ehiɛ mli.

english: Should I mix rabbit manure into the soil before planting or just leave it on top?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu loo mashi yɛ nɔ?

english: It is best to mix rabbit manure thoroughly into the sand or soil around the crop roots so it can immediately improve water retention and feed the plant roots evenly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔtɔ afutu ŋã loo sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni eha nu lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ niyenii pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: What makes rabbit manure useful for improving dry farmlands?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ feɔ nɔ ni he hiaa kɛha okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔyaa?

english: Rabbit manure breaks down easily, adds essential plant nutrients, and creates a spongy soil layer that greatly improves water holding capacity without burning your crops.
