ga: Kpɔŋɔi afɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ oya. Akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa fataa tsei ahe ni ehaa sũ ni mli ewo muji ni haa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: How do I stop rainwater from draining away too fast in my sandy soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha nugbɔ nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Integrating decomposed animal manure into the sand increases organic matter, which slows down water movement and holds moisture right in the root zone.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo ni akɛfataa ŋã lɛ he lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ yaa oya ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Will mixing animal manure into sandy soil hurt my crop seeds when they sprout?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni mikɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ baaye midumɔwui lɛ awui kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃?

english: No, rabbit manure is mild compared to some other manures; when mixed with sand, it creates a gentle, moist environment that protects sprouting seeds.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli jɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔtɔi krokomɛi ahe. Kɛ akɛ ŋã futu mli lɛ Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli jɔ ni mli edɔ baa. Koni akɛbu dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ ahe

english: How long will animal manure keep working to hold water in my soil for my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsu nii koni ekɛ nu ahi sũ lɛ mli kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Once well mixed into sandy soil, animal manure continues to improve soil texture and retain rainwater throughout the entire growing season.
ga: Kɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ futu mli lɛ, Koolooi ashishifãi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: If maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and thin with very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛhe tseee ni amɛmli ŋmeii bibii waa loo amɛhe bɛ ŋmeii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp wet ground, which prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baa helai anaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for green growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why shouldn't I spread dry fertilizer on my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the roots can absorb it. Putting dry fertilizer on dry soil can burn the crop's roots and waste your money because the plant cannot drink it in without water.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika ejaakɛ tsei nyɛŋ anu nu kɛji nu bɛ mli.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetables with dried leaves help them grow?
ga: Mulching around Te mi aduawai ni baai egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dried leaves or grass acts like a protective blanket. It stops the bright heat from drying out the ground too quickly, keeps the roots cool, and reduces how often you need to water.
ga: Akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ la ni naa wa lɛ, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu ni afɔɔ lɛ shii abɔ lɛ baa shi

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings rot in the dirt while others grow into strong plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa?

english: Cassava cuttings rot if they are taken from old or diseased plants, or if they are planted in waterlogged soil that doesn't drain well. Healthy cuttings from strong stems planted in moist, loose soil will sprout roots quickly.
ga: Cassava tsei ni afo lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni egbɔ loo helai emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu shwieee nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afolɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni mli ejɔ nɔ lɛ baawo shishifãi lɛ adalɛ oya he hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot, when the plants don't get steady water, or if bees are not visiting to pollinate them. Watering regularly and providing shade during very hot afternoons helps flowers stay on.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Be ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa Aloo kɛji ŋmeii baaa koni amɛbafee pollination. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my pepper plants lower the amount of pepper I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiha pepper ni mikpaa lɛ miiba shi?

english: Weeds act like thieves in your farm—they steal the water, sunlight, and soil food meant for your pepper plants. Without these resources, your pepper plants become weak and produce fewer fruits.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-pepper tsei lɛ amli lɛ mli. Kɛji nibii nɛɛ bɛ O-pepper tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Small ragged holes inside the young leaves are usually caused by tiny caterpillars like fall armyworms. They hide inside the center of the plant during the day and feed on the fresh leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ fall flukes ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ teŋ yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ.

english: Can I use garlic on my cocoa farm to keep insects away without hurting the cocoa beans?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ galiki atsu nii yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli koni mikɛshwie kooloi bibii ni miyeee kookoo yibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, garlic contains natural compounds that repel insects and control fungi. When applied correctly as a dry powder or natural mixture, it protects the tree without leaving harsh residues or damaging the development of the cocoa beans.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, galiki yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni eshwieɔ koolooi ni eyeɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Kɛ akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ akɛ powda ni egbi loo adebɔɔ mli nibii. Ebuɔ tso lɛ he ni eshiuuu nɔ ko ni mli wa loo efiteee kookoo yibii lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do natural herbal mixtures take longer to kill insects on my cocoa trees compared to chemical sprays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani egbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ fe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays work by poisoning insects instantly, while natural herbal mixtures usually work by repelling insects, disrupting their feeding, or preventing them from laying eggs. This means they protect your crops gradually without harming the soil or beneficial insects.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fɔɔ nitsumɔ kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii ni agbalaa mɔ naa loo ni tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkawo ŋmeii Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbuɔ onibii ahe fiofio ni amɛyeee shikpɔŋ lɛ loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ awui.

english: Can I make my own herbal pest spray using local plants to protect my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni mikɛbu mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, grinding local plants like garlic, neem leaves, or hot peppers into fine powders or steeping them in water creates natural sprays that effectively repel common farm pests without expensive store-bought chemicals.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ atsɔ maŋ lɛ mli tsei tamɔ galiki, neem baai loo chili ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ afee powda kpakpa loo akɛwo nu mli lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni shwieɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni jara wa ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: How do powdered plant treatments protect cocoa leaves from getting leaf diseases?
ga: Te tso mli powda ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ buɔ kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛɔ foliar helai ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When fine plant powders or natural extracts are sprayed on cocoa leaves, they form a protective coating that prevents fungal spores from sticking to the leaf and taking root when it rains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ tso mli powda kpakpa loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ miifɔ kookoo baai lɛ anɔ lɛ Amɛfeɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haaa fungal spores lɛ akpɛtɛ baai lɛ ahe ni amɛkawo shishifãi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Will applying strong-smelling herbal mixtures to my cocoa trees ruin the taste of the chocolate made from my beans?
ga: Ani tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni akɛfutuɔ mi-cacao lɛ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ waa lɛ baafite tsokolate ni akɛ mi-beans lɛ fee lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ?

english: No, applying dry herbal powders or natural treatments to the growing tree leaves early in the season will not change the bean flavor. Cocoa beans only absorb strong smells during the post-harvest drying and fermentation stages.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni egbi loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai wo tsei ni miida lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, etsakeŋ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ. Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ pɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ be mli ni akpaa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods usually turn black due to Black Pod disease, a fungus spread by rain and high humidity. Clearing weeds and applying natural protective plant mixtures early in the rainy season helps stop the fungus from attacking the young pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ tsu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akatutua ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress, extreme heat, or damage from tiny insects called thrips. Ensuring good shade and protecting trees from insects allows flowers to stay on the branches and develop into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji nu mli haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii fite amɛ. Atsɛɔ nakai hela lɛ akɛ thrips. Kɛ́ afee hulutsoo kpakpa ni abu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tsei aniji ahe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are some herbal farm treatments given to us as powders or capsules instead of liquids?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsofai komɛi ni jɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa wɔ yɛ powda loo capsule mli yɛ nu najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Powdered and encapsulated herbal treatments stay dry and last much longer in tropical heat without spoiling. Liquid remedies break down quickly, whereas dry mixtures can be stored safely until you are ready to mix them with water for spraying.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfee powda kɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hiɔ shi ni egbiɔ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni efiteee. Tsofa ni ji nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ akɛ tsofa ni egbi lɛ ato shweshweeshwe kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ okɛ nu baafutu koni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ.

english: Is it safe to mix dry plant powders into the soil around the roots of my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tso ni egbi lɛ mli powda baafutu shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli? Mikoo tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi

english: Yes, mixing dry organic powders into the soil provides slow-release nutrients and helps suppress harmful soil fungi without burning the delicate roots of young cocoa trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni akɛfutuɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jeɔ kpo blɛoo lɛ baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa ni eshãaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: How should I store dry herbal crop treatments so they don't lose their strength before I use them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma tsei ni egbi lɛ ato koni amɛhewalɛ akafite dani mikɛtsu nii?

english: Dry herbal powders should be kept in airtight containers, stored off the ground, and kept away from direct sunlight and moisture. When kept dry, they retain their strength to protect your crops for a long time.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni egbi lɛ ato nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli, yɛ shikpɔŋ, ni hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni egbi lɛ Amɛbaahiɛ amɛhewalɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu onibii ahe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants drop off during the long dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods to save water. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation, allowing the roots underground to stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ haa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and curl up when there is no rain for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have huge leaves that lose water rapidly under intense heat. Leaf curling and browning is the plant's natural defense to reduce sunlight exposure and conserve moisture inside its soft trunk.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe koni ekɛba hulu la shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On hot afternoons, tomatoes lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. This temporary wilting protects the plant, and it usually recovers by evening as the air cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomatoi shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tso lɛ ni egboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why am I finding tiny holes in my young maize leaves shortly after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny ragged holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on the soft tender leaves inside the central whorl of the plant before the ears form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli dani toi lɛ feɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes showing yellow patches and growing in twisted shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow, twisted leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that carry a virus from infected plants to healthy ones while feeding on plant sap.
ga: Baai ni etse amɛhe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Whiteflies bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni hiɛɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli be mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall with green leaves but fail to produce big ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli shi enyɛɛɛ ewo abele toi wuji lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen, which encourages leaf growth, but lacks phosphorus and potassium, which are the essential nutrients plants need to form strong flowers and big corn ears.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. ni haa baa lɛ daa Shi ebɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potassium. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni wa kɛ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why do farm extension officers advise planting cowpeas or groundnuts before planting maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii dani adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, they naturally fertilize the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ fite lɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn weak and yellow so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops, so they steal essential soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crops need to stay healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa waa, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to direct sunlight for energy production and keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing bigger tubers to develop underground.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. ni etsĩ sweet potato baai lɛ anaa koni ekahi hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ Tsɔ fungal helai anaa ni eha bulbs wuji shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings burn and die if I remove all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. Planting them under shade trees creates a cooler microclimate that retains moisture and protects tender cocoa leaves from sun scorch.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be shishi lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni mli ejɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ baa, ni ebuɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: How does growing vegetables inside a greenhouse make them produce more than open field farming?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo yibii babaoo fe okwaayeli ni agbeleɔ naa lɛ?

english: A greenhouse protects crops from heavy rains, harsh sunlight, and destructive insects. Because the environment inside stays controlled, plants spend less energy fighting off stress and weather, allowing them to grow faster and produce much higher yields on less land.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ koolooi ni fiteɔ nii ahe. Akɛni akudɔɔ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ lɛ No hewɔ lɛ tsei kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwuɔ ashiɔ nɔnyɛɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ he ko ni faaa.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant takes the remaining nutrients from its oldest bottom leaves and sends them to the top to keep new growth alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my garden egg plants produce plenty of big green leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ baai agboi babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer without enough phosphorus, they focus all their energy on leaf and branch growth instead of producing flowers and fruits. Balancing your fertilizer encourages the plant to set fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo tsei amli ni phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ niji ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, shady conditions. Rain droplets splash fungal spores from the soil onto lower pods, and high moisture allows the rot to spread rapidly across the tree.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ agbɛ ashwã tso lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects. Once infected, the plant's internal system gets blocked, causing leaves to twist and stopping fruit from growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, atsĩɔ tso lɛ mli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa aduawai lɛ adalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why does striga weed keep attaching itself to my sorghum and making the crop wilt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ striga jwɛi lɛ miikpɛtɛ mi-sorghum lɛ he ni eha tsei lɛ miigbo lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic plant whose roots grow directly into the roots of your sorghum underground. It steals water and nutrients straight from the sorghum plant, causing it to look starved even if you apply fertilizer.
ga: Striga ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa o-sorghum lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni hɔmɔ miiye lɛ kɛji okɛ fɔ wo mli po.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds neighboring crops like maize and leaves the soil richer for the next farming season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aye nii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha okwaayeli be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need room underground to swell and form thick tubers. If planted too close, the roots fight each other for moisture and nutrients, resulting in thin, woody roots instead of heavy tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ shishi he ko koni amɛfu ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Yɛ yitso ni tsii najiaŋ

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off before setting any small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai bibii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or dry soil. Dropping flowers is the plant's natural defense mechanism to save water and energy so it can survive harsh weather.
ga: Pepper tsei baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ato. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting quickly after I place them in the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya beni mikɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot easily if their skins are scraped or cut during harvesting. Bacteria and moisture enter through these small wounds; drying and curing yams in a shaded, well-ventilated space after harvest helps wounds heal and prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atsɔ hewolo nɔ loo afo lɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Muawai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ pilamɔi bibii nɛɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi sweet potatoes yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni pilamɔ lɛ tsaa ni ehaaa efite.

english: The bottom leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern when the plant is hungry for nitrogen. Maize naturally moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop a black, sunken spot at the bottom end before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni ebote shishigbɛ lɛ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil into the fruit, which usually occurs during dry spells or irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ agbala calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo be mli ni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like drinking straws during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi ni anuɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the maize plant's survival trick against intense heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to hold onto water.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji teemɔŋ sane ni haa ŋmãa tsei nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei baa amɛhe nɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their tiny flowers without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Bei pii lɛ, efeee pods kwraa?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed flowers they cannot feed. Excessive flower drop happens when there are not enough midges (tiny insects) to pollinate them, or when the tree lacks water and nutrients.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. (kooloi bibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ loo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cowpeas put energy into leaf growth instead of flowers. High temperatures can also cause the flowers to fall off before forming pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo dani pods aba.

english: Why are the young leaves on my pepper bushes curling upward and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a leaf curl virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ leaf curl hela ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the soil during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because they cannot breathe. Excess standing water suffocates the roots and allows soil fungi to enter and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt in the hot sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gboɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it up. If they recover by evening, it is just heat stress; if they stay wilted, soil bacteria or fungi may be blocking water movement inside the stem.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Kɛji amɛhe wa amɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Eji heat stress kɛkɛ. Kɛji amɛgbo lolo lɛ Sũ mli helai loo ŋmeii baanyɛ atsĩ nu ni nyiɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over completely when the heavy bunches start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ fɛɛ miiho lɛ? He ni jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains fall easily because they have shallow roots that can be damaged by underground pests like nematodes and root borers, leaving the heavy top unsupported against wind.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ nii baanyɛ afite. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi fã ni mli tse ni tsii lɛ náaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my stored yams starting to sprout long shoots in the barn before planting time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii kakadaji kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani dumɔ be shɛɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally break dormancy when storage areas get warm and humid. The rising temperature acts as a natural signal telling the tuber it is time to grow.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ fiteɔ wɔɔhe yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ tsei lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛdara.

english: Why did some of the maize seeds I bought fail to sprout even after I planted them in moist soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ni miheɔ lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds can fail to sprout if they are past their expiry date or were stored in hot, humid conditions. When a seed gets too old, the tiny living embryo inside dies, so it can no longer grow into a healthy shoot.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji be ni esa akɛ amɛfite lɛ eho loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Beni dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ tsɔ lɛ, fɔmɔ kotoku bibioo ni hiɛ ka Mɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baagbo. No hewɔ lɛ, enyɛŋ eda ni etsɔ tsei ni he wa dɔŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the crop seeds I bought from the dealer are still good before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ hi dani miduɔ?

english: Good seeds should look uniform, dry, and free of tiny insect holes or mold. You can test a small sample by putting ten seeds in a wet cloth for a few days—if at least eight sprout, the seed batch is healthy and good for planting.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ afee ekome, amɛgbi ni kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii buji akafee amɛ. Obaanyɛ oka nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko okwɛ. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii 2-3 lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɛ hoo lɛ, dumɔwui 8 kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ dumɔwui akuu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ehi kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my corn plants produce smaller cobs when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving less energy for each individual plant to build full-sized cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náaa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaawo ŋmei ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plants lack nitrogen, which is the essential plant food needed to build green leaves. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep out of the reach of young roots.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my cowpea plants make small round bumps on their roots, and are those bumps damaging my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ni ani ŋmeii lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Those bumps are healthy, not damaging. They contain beneficial soil bacteria that help cowpea plants pull nitrogen food straight out of the air, which actually enriches your soil for future crops.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ, jeee nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara. Shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa cowpea tsei lɛ ni amɛgbalaa nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ, ni no haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii diɛŋtsɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to protect itself from losing precious water through evaporation. The plant rests above ground while keeping its energy safely stored in the roots below.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni jara wa ni elaaje kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Akɛ tsei woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Under extreme heat and water stress, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ shishi lɛ Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Wrinkled and curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaves, or by viruses transmitted by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ

english: Why do my rice stalks fall flat on the ground right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔɔ be shɛɔ lɛ?

english: Rice stalks fall over—a problem called lodging—when the stalks become too thin and weak to hold up heavy grain heads. This usually happens if plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or are sown too close together.
ga: Toi ni shwieɔ shi - naagba ko ni ale lɛ akɛ lodging - beni ŋmaa lɛ feɔ mlɛo tsɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ aha tsei lɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct sunlight. Leaving taller shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the cocoa from sunburn and keeps moisture in the soil during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo he kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni edara mra lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source for plants. Adding rich compost, well-rotted manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore green leaf growth and boosts crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii jɛɛhe titri kɛha tsei Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo woɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ Loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baaye abua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my maize crop produce smaller cobs every year when I plant it on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps put essential nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots for days, it smothers them and allows soil fungi to cause root rot. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ he fɛɛ he. shishifãi gbii babaoo Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agboi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why does swamp rice survive sitting in water while my vegetables die under the same conditions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nu mli yɛ be mli ni mi-vegetables lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni tamɔ nɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have natural air tubes inside their stems that carry oxygen down to their roots even when submerged in water. Vegetables lack these hollow tubes, so standing water drowns their roots and stops them from breathing.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛji akɛ amɛbote nu mli po. Aduawai bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei ni mli ewo muji nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa mumɔ.

english: Plantain plants have very shallow root systems near the top of the soil. As their heavy fruit bunches grow, the plant becomes top-heavy, so propping them with strong wooden bamboo stakes prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei ni mli wa wo nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekaje shishi.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to feed the growing tubers underground. Lifting the vines off the ground using tall stakes exposes the leaves to light and prevents soil-borne diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli, ni ehaaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ akatutua baai lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa tso lɛ dalɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mites or aphids living under the leaves. Applying neem oil or appropriate organic sprays controls the insects so new leaves can grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi lɛ koni baai heei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when temperatures get too high or when water supply drops suddenly. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ba shi trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster and bigger than my planted crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ dara oya ni amɛdara fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with seeds that can lie dormant in the soil for years waiting for rain. Because they absorb food and water faster than cultivated crops, early weeding is necessary to give your young crops room to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa. Dumɔwui komɛi yɛ ni baanyɛ aka shi ni amɛhiɛ aka shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛmɛ nugbɔ afii babaoo Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛheɔ niyenii kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehe miihia ni oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ adara.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, giving the young cocoa trees the protection they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ buɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are missing essential nutrients in the soil like nitrogen, or the soil is waterlogged. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua jwɛi lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rains start?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: You should plant your maize after the first one or two heavy rains have thoroughly soaked the soil. Planting too early during light early showers can cause the seeds to dry up and die before they fully germinate.
ga: Esa akɛ odu ŋmãa beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ kome loo enyɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ fioo nɛɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why are holes on my cassava leaves reducing the size of the tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves trap sunlight to make food for the roots. When insects eat and damage the leaves, the plant cannot produce enough energy to grow big cassava tubers underground.
ga: Shi hulu la lɛ koni eha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Kɛji kooloi yeɔ ni amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why will planting my cocoa trees too close together reduce my total harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Trees planted too close together fight for light, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight and air movement, which reduces black pod disease and allows trees to yield more pods.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa black pod hela lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ pods babaoo.

english: Can I put fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn and damage the plant. It is best to place fertilizer in a small ring a few inches away from the stem so the roots can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shãa aba ni efite tso lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli. Inchi fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water and nutrients from the main plant. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main plantain tree receives enough food to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwu titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after clearing the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to grow aggressively in poor conditions. Clearing land exposes hidden weed seeds to sunlight and rain, allowing them to sprout and steal nutrients before your planted crops fully take root.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. He ni ajieɔ lɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ naa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ. Enɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani otso lɛ shishifãi kwraa.

english: Why is my harvested maize spoiling and molding inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ miifite ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grains spoil when they are stored with too much moisture or in humid spaces. Sun-drying your maize until the kernels are completely hard before storage prevents mold and keeps insects from destroying your grain.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa fiteɔ kɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ loo hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa dani akɛto lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa kɛ kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Watering your plants consistently and mulching the soil keeps the roots cool so flowers can set into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: What causes my harvested cocoa pods to rot quickly if I cannot sell them immediately?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Harvested cocoa pods continue to breathe and lose moisture. If they are left piled on the damp ground or under hot sun without proper air circulation, fungi and rot-causing bacteria quickly invade, spoiling the seeds inside.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋtayaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ loo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kɛ Rot baa lɛ boteɔ mli oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How long can I safely leave fully ripe cocoa pods on the tree before they start going bad?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ mashi kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe dani ebɔi fitemɔ?

english: Ripe cocoa pods can safely remain on the tree for about two to three weeks. Leaving them longer causes the seeds inside to begin sprouting or attracts diseases like black pod, which ruins their market value.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baanyɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe aaafee otsii enyɔ loo etɛ. Kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo ebaagbala helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji, ni no baafite jara ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do crops refuse to grow properly on land that was previously used for illegal mining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mining strips away the rich topsoil where plants get food, packs the ground too tight for roots to breathe, and often leaves toxic heavy metals behind that poison young plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni tsei naa niyenii yɛ nɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Paki shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu. Ni bei pii lɛ, eshiɔ dade ni tsii ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ amli.

english: How does water mixed with mud and mining chemicals affect the growth of my crops?
ga: Te nu ni akɛ muji kɛ tsofai ni jɛɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔji amli lɛ efutu mli lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Muddy, chemical-filled water clogs the tiny passages in roots, preventing plants from drinking clean water or absorbing nutrients, which eventually starves the plant and turns leaves yellow.
ga: Nu ni muji kɛ tsofai eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ gbɛi bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ anaa, ni no haaa tso lɛ anu nu ni mli tse loo enyɛŋ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ yɛ naagbee ni ebaa lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is it bad to clear all large trees off my land before planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ majie tsei fɛɛ ni eda kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu kookoo lɛ?

english: Large trees act as windbreaks and giant umbrellas. Removing them completely leaves young cocoa vulnerable to direct burning sun and allows heavy rains to wash away the valuable topsoil.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei wuji kɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Kɛ́ ajie fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ waa. ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni jara wa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves in dry weather to conserve moisture. Providing a steady water source during dry spells helps the tree hold its leaves and keep producing flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu jɛɛhe ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni eyaa nɔ ewoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting too much water from my watering system?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ mi nu ni mikɛhaa lɛ mli?

english: Too much water drowns the roots by cutting off air underground. When this happens, leaves turn soft and yellow before falling off, and the plant stops growing new shoots.
ga: Nu babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ enɛ ba lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛgbeeɔ shi. Ni tso lɛ baakpa ŋmeii heei ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers fall off without turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the tree feels stressed by heat, lack of water, or poor nutrients, or when there are not enough beneficial insects like midges in the farm to pollinate them.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ, nu ni faaa, loo niyenii ni esaaa. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: What makes black pod disease spread so fast across my cocoa farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Black pod is a fungus that thrives in wet conditions. Rain splashes the fungal spores from the soil onto low pods, and humid air helps it quickly jump from pod to pod across the farm.
ga: Black pod ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli. Nugbɔ haa ŋmeii ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni efoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa pod kroko mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale yellow even when the rainy season is active?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli po lɛ?

english: Excess rain can wash essential plant foods like nitrogen deep into the soil past the roots' reach, or cause waterlogging that stops the roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ afɔ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he. Aloo ekɛ nu ni hoɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa.

english: Why are the young leaves on my cocoa seedlings scorching and turning brown during the dry afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under direct sunlight. They require shade trees or fast-growing nurse crops like plantains to block harsh sunlight, keep the soil cool, and protect their delicate leaves until they are mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni amɛjeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the leaf center starting from the tip signals a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen keeps leaves green, and when soil nutrients run low, the plant draws remaining nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli. ni kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce plenty of bushy green leaves but very few pods after I added chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi pods fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo mli sɛɛ.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull their own nitrogen from the air into the soil. Adding high-nitrogen fertilizer tricks the crop into spending all its food energy on leafy growth instead of making flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ lakaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ atsu nii yɛ baai lɛ adalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting up with yellowish-green patches and keeping the roots small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yellow-green ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects or infected stem cuttings. The virus damages the plant's leaves, preventing them from catching sunlight to make food for the roots.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ Virus lɛ kpataaa tso lɛ baai lɛ ahiɛ. Buu he kɛjɛ hulu la he koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my young maize leaves with brownish dirt inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide inside the center funnel during the day to eat tender leaves and leave behind waste that looks like wet sawdust.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii ni amɛshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efɔ lɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling upward into tiny cups and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Upward curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like mites or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, which damages leaf tissue and stunts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ehaa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my main plantain trees produce small bunches when I let all the young shoots grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ feɔ kui bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ be mli ni miha ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ Nakai plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ

english: All the young shoots (suckers) share water and soil nutrients with the main tree. Removing extra shoots and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main stem gets enough food to build big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii fɛɛ (tsei lɛ) kɛ tso titri lɛ jaa nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight without shading each other. Maximizing sunlight allows the leaves to make the heavy starch needed to feed and swell underground tubers.
ga: Staking baaha ajie sweet potato baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni eyi obɔ ni tsiii enaa lɛ aná. Hulu la ni yaa hiɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmei ni tsii ni he hiaa koni ekɛ niyenii aha lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off without forming any tomatoes during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato pollen to become dry or sterile, preventing pollination. Without successful pollination, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ loo ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. tsiɔ pollination naa Kɛji pollination lɛ yeee omanye Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why does holding standing water in my lowland rice field help the rice grow while killing weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mikɛtoɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ hu ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Kɛ jwɛi nɔyeli?

english: Rice plants have special internal air passages that allow their roots to breathe underwater, whereas most common weed seeds and roots suffocate and rot when trapped under standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni haa amɛshishifãi lɛ muɔ yɛ nu shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ shishifãi ni afɔɔ naa waa lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight because strong heat scorches their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Keeping or planting shade trees like plantains creates a cool environment that helps young cocoa survive its early years.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ loo adumɔ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food maize plants need to stay green. The plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer top leaves, showing it needs organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛyaha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, leaving just a cluster of leaves at the top of the stem. You can also dig around the base of one plant to check if the tubers are thick enough before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Baai akuu pɛ eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli hu. Tso lɛ yitso kome ni akɛkwɛɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa dani akpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when insects damage the stems. Keeping the soil moist and giving the plants enough water during dry spells helps flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ooohã tso lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Is it helpful for my farm if I plant cowpeas together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsina ŋmãa fata ŋmãa he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and naturally feed the soil. This extra food in the soil helps the maize grow better while giving you two different harvests from one farm plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa sũ lɛ niyenii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni akɛfataa he nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekɛ yibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ baa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why should I remove extra small shoots growing around the stem of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ mi plantain lɛ tsei lɛ.

english: When too many shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they fight over water and nutrients in the soil. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring the main plant gets enough food to grow large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids that hide under leaves and suck out the plant juices. Spraying the plants early with neem leaf extract or recommended organic solutions controls these insects and lets the leaves open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ mra Kɛtsɔ Neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni eha baai lɛ agbele.

english: Why do my crops rot and turn yellow when rain water sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans do. When heavy rain sits on the farm without draining, water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, causing the roots to drown, rot, and stop feeding the plant.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛkpaa tso lɛ niyenii hamɔ.

english: Why do I need to put long sticks next to my yam vines as soon as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei niji kakadaji awo he kroko lɛ? Sweet potato wain tso kɛji ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ pɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb tall sticks so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves make the food that flows down to swell and grow large yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efuɔ ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it bad to put chemical fertilizer on dry soil when it hasn't rained?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baafata he be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can drink it up safely. Applying fertilizer to dry soil leaves concentrated chemical salts around the roots, which can burn and damage the plant instead of feeding it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia nu koni amɛtsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsofai ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ ekome, ni no baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ ni egbe lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do many of my cocoa flowers fall off the tree without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage turn into pods. Factors like dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or a lack of tiny pollinating insects cause the tree to shed excess flowers to save energy.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ bafeɔ pod. Nibii tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo pollinators ni bɛ Ha tsei lɛ afɔlɔ fe nine koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants curling inward during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot hours to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This is the plant's natural way of saving water and preventing itself from drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he ni ehaaa egbi.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight. The plants put all their energy into growing taller to reach the light rather than growing fruits or pods.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛná la. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ aduawai loo ŋmeii

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo abɔle kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Shade plants act as natural umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my soil is tired and needs plant food or manure?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehe miihia ni aye tsei aniyenii loo ŋmeii?

english: Tired soil shows signs like light green or yellow leaves, slow plant growth, thin stems, and low yields even when there is good rainfall.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baajie okadii tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kpo. Tso lɛ daa blɛoo, eyɛ tsei bibii, ni yibiiwoo faaa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Why does cutting off unnecessary extra branches from my cocoa tree help it bear more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi cacao tso lɛ niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or extra branches so air and sunlight can reach the center of the tree. This stops fungal diseases from breeding and directs the plant's food to pod growth.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa ni eha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: This is Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady, and overly wet conditions, especially during the heavy rainy season.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, hɔɔŋ, kɛ hei ni edɔ fe nine lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my farm crops after rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants natively adapted to the local environment, meaning they absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and watery if I leave them in flooded ground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ he ko ni nu eyi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in flooded soil cuts off air to the cassava roots, causing the tubers to absorb too much moisture and rot quickly in the waterlogged ground.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ foɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ oya yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: Why is proper fermentation of cocoa beans necessary before selling them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsɔ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ jogbaŋŋ dani ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation kills the germ inside the bean, develops the chocolate flavor, and builds the natural oil content needed to produce goods like cocoa butter.
ga: Fɛ̃i gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. ni kɛ tsokolate mli ŋmɔlɔ baa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee nibii tamɔ kookoo bɔta lɛ baa.

english: Is it safe to apply fertilizer into the soil at the very same time I am planting my seeds?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ be kome too mli ni aduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yes, it is safe as long as the fertilizer is placed slightly to the side or below the seed. This gives the seedling immediate access to food as soon as roots sprout without burning the delicate seed.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo dumɔwui lɛ afã loo amɛshishi fioo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa niyenii kɛji shishifãi lɛ shwere pɛ ni amɛshãaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: What happens to a crop seed if chemical fertilizer touches it directly inside the ground?
ga: Mɛni baa dumɔwui anɔ kɛji tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Direct contact can burn the seed because fertilizer salts draw water away from the seed, preventing it from germinating or killing the tender young root as it tries to emerge.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ ehe wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui lɛ ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃ loo amɛkagbe shishifãi bibii beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize plants grow faster when starter fertilizer is put in the ground right at planting time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ daraa oya kɛ akɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Early fertilizer gives the seed an immediate food boost, allowing it to grow strong roots and leaves quickly so it can outgrow weeds and handle dry spells better.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná niyenii babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛhe wa oya. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛye jwɛi lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsu hulutsoo be lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will using a planting machine change how deep my crop seeds stay in the soil compared to planting by hand?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baatsake bɔ ni midumɔwui lɛ mli kwɔ ha yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto nine ni akɛduɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, a planter places every seed at a precise, uniform depth across the entire field, unlike hand planting where some seeds end up too shallow or buried too deep.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaafoi kɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu woɔ he ko pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ nine ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ he ni dumɔwui komɛi mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ he.

english: How does planting seeds at the exact same depth across my field help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kome mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: When all seeds are planted at the same depth, they receive equal warmth and moisture, causing them to sprout and rise out of the soil at the same time for an even harvest.
ga: Beni aduɔ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shishigbɛ kome mli lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ baaná dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ebaakwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome too mli. amɛfee ekome kɛha kpamɔ ni yeɔ egbɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce bigger yields when they are planted in straight, well-spaced rows instead of scattered?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni amɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ dumɔwui ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Proper row spacing ensures each crop gets its fair share of sunlight, air, and ground water without fighting neighboring plants for nutrients.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ akaŋ

english: Why is it important for me to start planting my crops immediately after the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabɔi tsei adumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Early rains release trapped nitrogen in the warm soil, giving newly planted seeds the perfect combination of moisture and natural nutrients to jumpstart growth.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ kpo. Ehaa dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yeɔ emuu koni ekɛje dalɛ shishi.

english: How does moist soil make a dry crop seed wake up and start growing?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ teɔ shi ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Water softens the hard outer skin of the seed and activates internal food stores, signaling the embryonic plant to break open the shell and send out roots.
ga: Nu haa dumɔwu lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ekanyaa niyenii ni akɛtoɔ emli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso bibioo lɛ leɔ akɛ ebaafo ehewolo lɛ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my crop seeds take longer to come up if I bury them deep in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry a fixed amount of stored energy. If buried too deep, the young shoot burns up all its energy trying to push through heavy soil before reaching the surface light.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ daa. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ shãa amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli dani amɛshɛ la ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he.

english: How long does a maize seed usually take to sprout out of the ground after planting in warm soil?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmãa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: In warm, moist soil, a healthy maize seed usually sprouts and shows green shoots above the ground within 4 to 7 days after planting.
ga: yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛnáa ŋmeii eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii 4 kɛyashi 7 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ.

english: Why should I leave part of my farmland to rest for a few seasons before planting on it again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi midumɔi lɛ ekomɛi koni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe be fioo dani madu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving land to rest, or fallow, allows the soil to naturally rebuild nutrients, organic matter, and moisture that previous crops used up, leading to better harvests when you plant again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ashiɔ koni ejɔɔ ehe loo ehi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ nu ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii tsutsu lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmaa kpakpa baa kɛji odu ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if soil that has been farmed for many years is exhausted and needs help?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ ni odu nɔ afii babaoo lɛ efo ni yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia bo?

english: Exhausted soil often turns pale, gets hard to clear, or loses water quickly. If your crops stay small, turn pale yellow, or yield poorly despite good rainfall, the soil lacks essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu efite lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ewa akɛ abaajie, loo nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ tsakemɔ kɛya ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse Aloo yibiiwoo lɛ ehiii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ kpakpa nɛɔ moŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings shade and keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ hulutsoo. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Can I plant cassava together with maize on the same piece of land without them damaging each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ he kome ni amɛfiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows fast and is harvested in three to four months, leaving the cassava to spread out and mature over the rest of the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Ha ni ŋmei lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.
