english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help the next crops I put on my field?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When they decay, this built-in fertilizer feeds the next crop, like maize or yam.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni efiteɔ Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo mli nɛɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is essential for green leaf growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tso lɛ. ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha eŋɔli lɛ su lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no winds or bees to help transfer pollen inside the blossom.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo ŋmeii bɛ ni baaye abua ni ajie pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots for too long, the roots drown and rot. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ashiɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids. Spraying neem oil solution or soapy water controls the pests so healthy green leaves can sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ koni baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning overhead branches, clearing weeds, and removing infected pods early stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Niji ni yɔɔ yiteŋ lɛ afolɔ jwɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct, harsh sunlight. If they do not have enough shade trees or plantains planted around them, the intense sun burns their leaves and turns them yellow.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Kɛji amɛbɛ tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã ebaa lɛ ni eha amɛfee ŋmɔŋ.

english: This is usually caused by Fall Armyworms. The caterpillars feed on the young leaves inside the central whorl of the plant, which stunts the corn's growth if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Enɛ haaa ŋmãa akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ mra.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet, and shaded conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning dense branches allows air and sunlight to dry the pods and reduce the disease.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai ni baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my maize plants weak and light green even though there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Rain alone is not enough if the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Light green leaves usually mean the soil is exhausted, and adding compost, manure, or fertilizer will help the crop grow dark green and strong.
ga: Nugbɔ pɛ faaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efo. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, tall stalks with very small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni dumɔwui bibii bibii yɔɔ mli loo ni bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, or when the soil goes from extremely dry to suddenly very wet, causing the plant to shed its blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Ha tomato tsei lɛ agbo.

english: Why must I clear weeds while my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have weak roots and will easily lose the fight against fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and plant food. Early weeding gives young crops the space and energy to build strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛbaaye kunim yɛ ta ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ mli oya koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ hegbɛ kɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves into the sunlight, which allows the plant to make food and grow large tubers under the ground while keeping leaves away from ground diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni adu bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ ehaa baai lɛ tsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant groundnuts between my cassava rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally pulls nitrogen gas from the air and puts it back into the soil, feeding the cassava crop while giving you an extra food harvest.
ga: Peanuts ji legume weku lɛ mlinyo ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmei tsei lɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ niyenii krokomɛi hu baa.

english: Can I put manure from my animals directly on my young maize crops to make them grow faster?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi a-ŋmei tsei lɛ awo mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara oya?

english: Fresh manure is too hot and strong for young crops and can burn their roots. You should dry or compost the manure first by letting it sit mixed with dry grass for a few weeks before spreading it near your plants.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ tsɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ ogbi loo okɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ kɛtsɔ jwɛi lɛ ni oooha ekɛ jwɛi lɛ afutu mli otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛgbɛ ashwã tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the food plants need to build green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer around the roots will bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baafata he Shishifãi lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy clay or flooded soils. Planting your cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep wilting and dying suddenly even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in tomatoes often comes from soil diseases that attack the roots and block water from going up the stem. Rotating your land by planting maize or cassava in that spot for a season starves out the disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa nu nyɛɛɛ aya ŋwɛi shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato mli shwiemɔ baa trukaa. Kɛ́ otsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔ be kome lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akabote mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ egbo beni mijieɔ tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that get scorched under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa gives them living umbrellas that keep the air cool and soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Young cocoa masɛi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa hulutsoo ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely between waterings. Covering the soil around the plant with dry leaves helps keep the roots cool and moist so flowers stay on.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ. Mulching around Dumɔ kɛ baai ni egbi yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: If I am moving my farm to a new piece of land, how can I tell if the soil is good for planting?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ tee shikpɔŋ hee nɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha okwaayeli?

english: Good farming soil feels dark and crumbly in your hand and holds some moisture without turning into sticky mud. You can also look at the natural vegetation—land where wild grasses and shrubs grow thick and green usually has fertile soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ baanu he akɛ eyɛ duŋ ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ oniji amli. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli Obaanyɛ ona adebɔɔ mli tsei lɛ hu. Enɛɛmɛi ji hei ni jwɛi kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni bei pii lɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii yɔɔ nɔ.

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to sprout after I planted them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to come up if they are buried too deep, eaten by soil insects, or if the soil hardens like a crust after heavy rain. Planting seeds at a shallow depth of about two thumb-joints makes it easy for young shoots to break through.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kplukai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ lɛ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ aaafee thumb joints 2 haa tsei bibii boteɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I put many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space lets its roots spread out and receive enough light to produce heavy yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛnáa la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkpa nii babaoo.

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves on the plant start turning yellow and dry up. You can pull up one sample plant to test—if the inside of the pods has dark brown markings instead of remaining white, the crop is ready.
ga: Beni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ, no mli lɛ ŋmeii efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ. Obaanyɛ ogbala tso ko he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ni okɛka lɛ okwɛ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ efee klalo.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their tender leaves burn easily. Without shade trees or plantains planted nearby to filter the heat, the plant loses too much water, the leaves scorch yellow, and growth stops.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni akɛjie la lɛ bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baafite nu babaoo tsɔ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shãa. ni dalɛ baakpa.

english: Why are there small holes appearing in my young maize leaves like something is eating them from the inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Etamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko miiye nii kɛmiijɛ mligbɛ?

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They crawl inside the central leaves (the funnel) of the young maize plant during the day to feed on tender tissue, which weakens the crop if you do not catch it early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai (cones) lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji omɔɔɔ lɛ mra.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many green leaves but leave me with small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants receive too much nitrogen or are planted too close together, the crop spends all its energy producing leaves and stems instead of underground roots. Proper plant spacing and balanced soil nutrients help force the crop to send energy down into building bigger tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ baai kɛ tsei yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ najiaŋ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo awo bulbs wuji afeemɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants instead of letting the vines spread across the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ masɛi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha wain tsei lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to make food for the heavy roots underneath. Staking also keeps the leaves off the warm, damp ground, preventing soil diseases from rotting the leaves and stems.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛha shishifãi ni tsii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaatsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni ekahi hei ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Koni helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akafite baai kɛ tsei lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Too many young suckers attached to one plantain stem will fight with the main mother plant for food and water in the soil. Cutting off extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main tree gets enough nourishment to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo ni akɛkpɛtɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do extension officers tell me that planting groundnuts or cowpeas helps make my soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔ ko kɛɔ mi akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that stored nitrogen remains in the dirt, acting as natural fertilizer for nutrient-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni he hiaa niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off without forming fruit when temperatures become extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. Keeping soil moisture consistent and providing light shade during peak heat helps the flowers stay attached and produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛ la ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass or dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with organic matter (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation from the hot sun, and stops weeds from taking over the bed.
ga: Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ Nibii ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii yɛ mli (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaha saatsoi lɛ anɔ

english: How do I know if the very first rainy day of the season is enough for me to start planting my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔwui dumɔ?

english: A single rainy day often only wet the very top layer of dry earth. If you plant immediately, the seeds might sprout and then wither when dry days follow; it is best to wait until the rain wets the soil down to about the depth of your hand so the seeds have lasting moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbi kome ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi be mli ni gbi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashɛ he ni onine lɛ mli kwɔ. Koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and weak even when I apply water to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo ŋmɔji lɛ amli po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that act like extra straws in the ground, drinking up the water and sucking up the plant nutrients long before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nourishment they need.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ jwɛi krokomɛi ni fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Tsei nuɔ nu ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aná. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: I heard people put medicine directly inside tree trunks instead of spraying the leaves. How does medicine travel inside a tree to protect it?
ga: Minu akɛ mɛi kɛ tsofa woɔ tsei akutsei amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafɔ̃ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Te tsofa lɛ yaa tso lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ koni ebu ehe?

english: Trees have internal channels that act like blood vessels. When you inject medicine into the trunk, the tree naturally draws the liquid upward along with water and sap, carrying it to the leaves, branches, and fruits to fight pests and diseases from the inside.
ga: Tsei yɛ mligbɛ gbɛi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ lá fãji. Kɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ wo tso lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ gbalaa nu lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛfataa nu lɛ kɛ nu lɛ he. Taakɛ eji lɛ, akɛyaa baai, tsei aniji, kɛ aduawai amli koni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai awuu kɛjɛ mli.

english: If I inject chemical treatments directly into my cocoa tree to kill pests, will it poison the cocoa beans?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Ani ebaafee nɔ ni gbeɔ kookoo yibii lɛ?

english: Approved injection treatments break down naturally within the tree's tissues over a specific timeframe. They kill the target pests while leaving the harvested cocoa beans completely safe for consumption, provided you observe the recommended waiting period before harvest.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli. Amɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛshiɔ kookoo yibii ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni aye. Esa akɛ onyiɛ be ni akɛbaamɛ ni akɛwo ŋaa lɛ sɛɛ dani okpa ŋmaa lɛ.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer in the soil around a tree's base or apply liquid nutrition directly into the trunk?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafata shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he loo akɛ niyenii ni ji nu baawo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Soil fertilizer nourishes the roots and improves long-term soil quality, but trunk injection places liquid nutrients straight into the tree's circulation system. Direct injection gives fast results when roots are damaged by disease or when the soil is too dry for roots to take up nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Shi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni ji nu lɛ baaya tso lɛ mli lá ni hoɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baa oya kɛ́ helai efite shishifãi lɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani abele lɛ afee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Leaves turn yellow early primarily when the crop lacks essential nitrogen in the soil or when heavy rains soak the roots and stop them from breathing. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the crop regain its green color and feed the developing ears.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkpaa mumɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha toi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die so quickly during the dry sun season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow root systems and delicate leaves that lose moisture quickly under direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates living shade that protects young trees until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ, amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: My cassava plants are growing very tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers underground remain small. Why is this happening?
ga: Mi yucca tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo. Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraaa lolo. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil makes cassava spend its energy building tall stems and leafy foliage instead of storing food in the roots. Balancing the soil with potassium encourages the plant to direct its energy downward to expand the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ potassium to shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkudɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs.

english: How does black pod disease spread so fast from one cocoa tree to another across my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus whose tiny spores are carried by rain splashes, wind, insects, and unwashed pruning tools. In cool, wet weather, these spores easily land on healthy pods and infect them.
ga: Fungi ko ni spores bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ pods diji baa. Nugbɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni ahooo lɛ woɔ amɛ kɛyaa. Yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ kpɛtɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya.

english: Why does cutting off extra branches and leaves help my fruit tree produce larger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii wuji lɛ?

english: A tree has a limited amount of water and food to share. When you prune unproductive branches, the tree stops wasting energy on useless foliage and redirects those nutrients straight into swelling the remaining fruits.
ga: Tsei bɛ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ hewalɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ, ni ekɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ koni eha yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why doesn't regular chemical spraying kill the stem borers inside my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi daa lɛ egbeee stem borers ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Stem borers tunnel deep inside the stem where external chemical sprays cannot reach them. To control them, you need systemic treatments that are absorbed into the plant's sap or preventative treatments applied before the larvae bore into the stalk.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi boteɔ tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he koni ekɛkudɔ amɛ Ohe miihia ni okɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ko atsu nii, ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli, loo tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa dani ŋmeii lɛ aboteɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do crops like sorghum survive long periods without rain while my maize wilts quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ oya lɛ?

english: Sorghum has an extensive, deep root system that can reach hidden water deep underground, and its leaves roll up to trap moisture. Maize has shallower roots and broad leaves that lose water rapidly in dry weather.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he. Ni ebaai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant on the same piece of land every single year without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he kome daa afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Just like a human body gets weak without rest, soil loses its natural plant food (nutrients) when crops are grown continuously. Leaving the land to rest (fallowing) allows natural vegetation to decay and restore organic matter and nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Taakɛ adesa gbɔmɔtso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni hejɔɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii (nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ) be mli ni tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe (egbee shi) lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I dig up and turn over my soil completely before planting, or is it better to leave the ground undisturbed?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ dani madu nii? Aloo ani ehi akɛ aaashi sũ lɛ ni nɔ ko akagbala lɛ?

english: Disturbing the soil too much breaks its natural structure, dries out stored moisture, and kills beneficial soil life like earthworms. Minimal tilling or clearing only the planting spots helps the soil retain water and protects it from being washed away by heavy rain.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbala shikpɔŋ lɛ naa tsɔ lɛ, ebaafite bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ. Gbimɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebua naa lɛ. ni efite shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ atsu nii loo ajie fioo pɛ yɛ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli, ni ebaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie lɛ.

english: Why does planting leguminous crops like beans or groundnuts after harvesting maize help my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii? Beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eye ebua mishikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Different crops feed on different soil nutrients. Legumes have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that enriches the land for the next crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yeɔ niyenii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Legumes yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Will my crops produce more yield if I flood my farm with water as often as possible?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii babaoo kɛji mikɛ nu wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli shii abɔ bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Crop roots need oxygen to breathe just as much as they need water. Flooding or over-watering suffocates the roots, causing them to rot and turning the leaves yellow.
ga: Dabi, tsei ashishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni tsei ashishifãi hu taoɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ nu he hiamɔ Nu afua loo Nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do the roots of my tomato plants turn soft and rot when rainwater sits on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ gbii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When standing water remains on the field, it blocks air from reaching the roots and creates a humid environment where soil fungi thrive. These fungi attack the weakened roots and cause root rot.
ga: Kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni efee shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetables so they do not dry out quickly?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ nu koni amɛkagbi oya?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening gives the soil time to absorb the moisture. Watering under the hot mid-day sun causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can drink it.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: What can I mix into my sandy soil so that water does not sink through it too fast?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛfutu ŋã sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo mli oya tsɔ?

english: Adding decomposed livestock manure, compost, or dry plant matter acts like a sponge in sandy soil. It traps rainwater near the surface where crop roots can easily reach it.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei ni egbi ni egboi baafata he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ ŋã sũ mli. Emɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he oya lɛ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer pods now compared to when I planted them almost twenty years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo fe beni midu lɛ aaafee afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As tree crops age, their root systems become less efficient at absorbing soil nutrients, and their branches become more vulnerable to diseases and pests. Pruning old wood or gradually replanting aged trees helps refresh the farm’s productivity.
ga: Beni tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ daraa lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni amɛniji lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ oya. Kpɔ̃ɔ tso momo loo tso ni afo blɛoo. Tsei momoi ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a defense mechanism. By curling its leaves, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing water from evaporating too fast from its leaves while it waits for rain.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ beni emɛɔ nugbɔ lɛ.

english: Why do crops like sorghum stay green during dry periods while my maize dries up completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gĩɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Sorghum has a deep and extensive root system that can reach underground water reserves, along with leaves that naturally trap moisture. Maize has shallower roots that depend heavily on surface water, making it dry out faster when rainfall stops.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhei ahe. Kɛfata baai ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ he. Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni damɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ waa. Egbiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Why should I plant two or three maize seeds per hole instead of just one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ bu kome mli moŋ fe ekome pɛ?

english: Not every seed will germinate, and insects or heavy rains can destroy young sprouts. Planting extra seeds per hole ensures that at least one solid, healthy plant survives to give you a full harvest.
ga: Jeee dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu baakwɛ̃. Ni kooloi bibii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ akpata tsei bibii lɛ ahiɛ. Dumɔwui krokomɛi ni ooodu yɛ bu fɛɛ bu mli lɛ haa kɛ hoo lɛ, tso kome ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baahi shi ni eha bo ŋmaa ni fa.

english: Why do some of my yam setts fail to sprout after planting them under the mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko shishi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam setts can rot from waterlogging, get eaten by soil insects, or dry out during heatwaves. It is normal to lose a small percentage of setts, which is why farmers prepare extra mounds to protect their total output.
ga: He ni sweet potato lɛ yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite kɛjɛ nu afua mli. Kplukai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ loo amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa akɛ jwɛi fioo ko ni ato lɛ baafite. Nɔ ni haa okwaafoi saa gɔji krokomɛi koni amɛkɛbu amɛŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do some pepper seeds take much longer to sprout than others planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper dumɔwui komɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ?

english: Pepper seeds naturally germinate at different speeds depending on seed coat thickness, planting depth, and local moisture. This natural variation helps protect the crop so that a sudden hot spell does not destroy all young seedlings at once.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Edamɔ dumɔwui lɛ atsɔne lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ nɔ. dumɔ mlibotemɔ kɛ he ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ tsakemɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo be ni naa wa ni baa trukaa lɛ kpataaa tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ shikome.

english: How do I calculate how much maize I will actually harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa ni makpa diɛŋtsɛ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You estimate your harvest by multiplying your total crop count by the average ears per plant, and then subtracting about 10 to 20 percent to account for unexpected losses from dry weather, pests, or animal damage.
ga: Obuɔ okpamɔ lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni okɛtoɔ toi ni yɔɔ tso kome mli lɛ mlijaa mli lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, jiemɔ aaafee oha mlijaa 10 kɛyashi 20 kɛjɛ mli koni okɛwo nibii ni elaaje ni akpaaa gbɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii loo kooloi ni efite lɛ mli lɛ he nyɔmɔ.

english: How can I protect my farm income if pests kill part of my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shika ni mináa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ kpata miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi ahiɛ?

english: Experienced farmers plan their target income based on lower crop survival rates rather than perfect conditions. Planting a slightly larger area ensures that even after natural crop losses, your remaining harvest will still cover your costs and bring a solid profit.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ toɔ amɛ shika ni amɛtaoɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohi shihilɛ ni yeɔ emuu mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni da fioo ni ooodu lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ sɛɛ po lɛ, Okpamɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ baaya nɔ ekɛ shika ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ aba ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce smaller fruits towards the end of the harvesting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: As tomato plants get older, they drain the nutrients in the soil and exhaust their internal strength. The later fruits receive fewer nutrients from the plant, causing them to develop into smaller sizes than the early harvest.
ga: Kɛji tomato tsei lɛ dara lɛ Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaho ni ebaafite emli hewalɛ. Yibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ baaná niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo kɛjɛ tsei amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo fe shishijee ŋmaa lɛ.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition makes them grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in small fruit or poor grain yields overall.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, akaŋshii nɛɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛwoɔ yibii bibii loo dumɔwui fɛɛ ni ehiii lɛ baa.

english: Why is it necessary to pull out some healthy seedlings from a crowded hole after they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ bu ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli beni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Removing extra seedlings, known as thinning, leaves only the strongest plant in the hole. This ensures that the remaining plant gets all the light, water, and nutrients needed to produce a large, high-quality harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni fa fe nine lɛ ajiemɔ Atsɛɔ lɛ thinning. Tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi yɛ bu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ naa la, nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops drop many of their flowers before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo dani amɛfee pods lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants shed extra flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or water shortages. The plant drops flowers naturally so it can direct its limited water and energy into bringing the remaining pods to maturity.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi titri kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa mli baa lɛ kpe. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔi ni eshwɛ lɛ amli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry spells to save water and protect its underground roots. Once the rains return, the plant will shoot out fresh green leaves and continue growing steadily.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be baa koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baatswa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and easily scorch under intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and feature broad leaves that provide vital shade and hold moisture in the soil, protecting the young cocoa until it is mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhiɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets the growing tip of maize plants. Applying organic remedies like neem extract or approved treatments early in the morning or late evening destroys the pests before they kill the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakpata tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛgbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava crop have tall stems and lots of green leaves, but very tiny roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen, cassava plants spend all their energy growing stems and leaves instead of roots. Avoiding nitrogen-heavy fertilizers and maintaining proper planting distance encourages the plant to store energy underground in large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi kɛ baai amli yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ he ni sa ni akɛduɔ lɛ baaye abua tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ bulb agboi amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying balanced nitrogen fertilizers like NPK or adding well-decomposed manure gives plants the essential nutrients they need to keep leaves green and support grain growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tamɔ NPK tsu nii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ, ni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why are the blossom ends of my ripening tomatoes turning black and rotting before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani akpa lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by calcium deficiency combined with irregular soil moisture. Keeping soil consistently moist through regular watering and adding calcium sources, such as wood ash or lime to the soil, keeps tomato fruits healthy and firm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ calcium jɛɛhe tamɔ tso sũ loo lime ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni eha tomato yibii lɛ mli awa ni ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I have to heap topsoil into tall mounds before planting seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔbua sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ naa wɔwo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ mli dani wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Mounding creates loose, uncompacted soil that allows yam tubers to expand easily without resistance. Mounds also elevate the plants above waterlogged ground, preventing seed yams from rotting during heavy rains.
ga: Mounding haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ oya ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa lɛ baa. Gɔŋ lɛ hu woɔ tsei anɔ kɛyaa ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ akafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and wrinkling, preventing flowers from opening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Tsi fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkakwɛ

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking leaf sap and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early with neem oil or recommended sprays helps leaves stay flat and flower normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Excess suckers compete directly with the main stem for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, resulting in small fruit bunches. Keeping only the main stem alongside one medium and one small sucker concentrates resources to yield large, healthy bunches.
ga: Suckers babaoo tsɔ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai bibii bibii. Ni akɛ tso titri lɛ pɛ toɔ he kroko Sucker medium kome kɛ sucker bibioo kome Ebaabua nibii ni he hiaa lɛ anaa koni ená kuu agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why does spreading dry straw around my vegetable plant roots help them stay green during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa mi-vegetable shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: Spreading dry straw acts as mulch, covering the bare soil to shield it from direct sunlight. This slows water evaporation from the ground, suppresses competitive weeds, and maintains cool soil temperatures for the roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shi lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la akashɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Tsi jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ naa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i ahi shi kɛha shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for two or three steady rains before planting my seeds at the beginning of the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani madu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting after just one isolated rain is risky because the soil can dry out quickly if rains stall, causing sprouted seeds to wither and die underground. Waiting for steady rainfall ensures sufficient moisture for seedlings to establish strong roots.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ be kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mɛmɔ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting companion crops like plantain gives them natural shade and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow mature enough to tolerate full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Hefatalɔi tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow starting from the tips instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the maize plant rebuild healthy green leaves to feed itself.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛwo baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in flat or poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain off, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like aphids or thrips under the leaves. Spraying organic solutions like neem oil or appropriate pest treatments clears these insects so new leaves can expand properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni jɛ wala mli tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. koni baai heei lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the fruit is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees tumble when small soil pests called nematodes damage their roots, weakening their anchor in the ground. Propping heavy stems with wooden poles and using healthy sucker planting material prevents trees from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ kpata amɛshishifãi lɛ ahiɛ. ni ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ Akɛ tsei ni tsii tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni akɛ nibii ni akɛduɔ nu ni mli wa tsuɔ nii koni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my harvested seed yams start sprouting early in the barn before the rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ ba lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break dormancy and shoot sprouts when they feel warm temperatures in storage. Storing seed yams in a shaded, well-ventilated barn keeps them cool and delays sprouting until planting time.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo shihilɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛnu he akɛ amɛhe edɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ to ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo kɛyashi be ni esa akɛ adu lɛ baashɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete fiercely for water, sunlight, and soil food. Spacing seeds out according to recommended distances gives each plant enough room to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or irregular watering. Applying dry grass mulch around the base keeps the soil moist and cool, allowing flowers to set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Mulch ni egbi ni bɔleɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa edɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal the nutrients and water meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life ensures your plants get the full benefit of fertilizer and rain.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ogbeɔ yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ haa otsei lɛ náa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nugbɔ lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small cocoa pods on my trees turn black and shrivel up shortly after forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ beni ebɔi feemɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This shriveling, known as cherelle wilt, happens when the tree cannot support all its young pods or when pests attack them. Proper pruning to let in light and feeding the soil helps the tree retain more growing pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ shwiemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherel shwiemɔ. Ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ lɛ. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua amɛ. Tso lɛ ni afolɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni la atsɔ mli ni eha sũ lɛ niyenii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ayibɔ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have weak root systems and limited energy storage. Planting them under shade crops like plantains protects them from harsh sunlight while their roots establish enough capacity to survive on their own.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ adu tsei nɛɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ plantains lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops look yellow and weak even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Rain provides water, but plants also need food from the soil to create energy. Yellow leaves mean the soil lacks nutrients (low capacity), so adding compost or fertilizer gives the plants the strength they need to grow.
ga: Nugbɔ haa nu, shi tsei hu taoɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee hewalɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ (nibii ni haa mɔ he waaa), no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: No, because a piece of land has limited nutrient and water capacity. When plants are crowded, they fight for energy, resulting in weak, stunted crops with poor yields.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ kuku ko bɛ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo. Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaawuu koni amɛná hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping allows fast-growing maize to finish using the soil's early energy before the slow-growing cassava expands, allowing both crops to share land capacity without burning out early.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ heɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shishijee mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ mli lɛɛɔ. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ jaa he ko ni amɛshãaa oya.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and droop during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's way of conserving energy and water during peak heat to prevent drying out; once the afternoon heat reduces, the plant recovers.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ akagbi Beni shwane mli latsaa lɛ ba shi lɛ Tso lɛ he wa lɛ.

english: How does covering the ground around my plants with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Mulching acts as a protective shield that prevents moisture from evaporating, helping the soil hold water energy longer so plants don't get exhausted during hot days.
ga: Mulching tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nu hewalɛ toɔ be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ ahe ejɔɔɔ amɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my young orange tree before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tso bibioo lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Young trees often do not have enough energy or root capacity to support fruit yet. They drop their flowers to save their strength for growing bigger and stronger first.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ahewalɛ loo nyɛmɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaaye amɛbua aduawai. Amɛshiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu amɛhewalɛ he koni amɛdara ni amɛhe awa klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the low branches and extra shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning redirects the plant's limited energy away from unnecessary leaves and sends it straight into growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ fioo lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe. ni otsɔɔ lɛ gbɛ kɛya aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant yam on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmeii yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Yam drains a lot of nutrients from the soil, leaving it tired and weak. Rotating with legumes restores nutrients and gives the soil time to rebuild its capacity.
ga: Atomɔ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa be ni ekɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do we start delicate vegetable seeds in a shaded nursery before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔjeɔ wɔ aduawai dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shishi yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ amli dani wɔkɛyaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery provides a controlled environment with gentle sun and water, giving young seedlings time to gain strength and experience before facing the harsh conditions of the open field.
ga: He ni akwɛɔ gbekɛbii yɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ ni hulu la ni mli tse kɛ nu yɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui bibii ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛ niiashikpamɔ dani amɛkɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kpeɔ.

english: Why should I buy improved or grafted rubber seedlings instead of just planting seeds I pick under an old tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe rɔbɔt dumɔwui ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo ni akɛwo mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu lɛ yɛ tso momo ko shishi

english: Grafted seedlings are cloned from high-producing parent trees, which guarantees they will grow uniformly, resist common trunk diseases, and yield significantly more latex than wild seeds collected from the ground.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ he mfoniri kɛjɛ nyɛ tso ko ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli. Enɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ amɛbaadara daa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tso lɛ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ni ekɛ latɛs babaoo baa fe koo mli dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting my young rubber tree before it starts producing latex?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du rɔbɔt tso bibioo ko sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani ebɔi latɛs feemɔ?

english: Rubber trees require about 6 to 7 years of growth before they mature enough to produce latex. During these early years, the tree spends its energy developing a strong trunk and deep root system.
ga: Rɔba tsei he miihia aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 ni amɛdara dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee latɛs. Yɛ shishijee afii nɛɛ amli lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tso ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: How do I know that my rubber tree trunk is thick enough for me to start tapping it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-rɔba tso lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi tswamɔ?

english: A rubber tree is ready when its trunk circumference reaches about 50 centimeters (roughly the size of a grown person's wrist to forearm wrapping around) measured at one meter from the ground.
ga: Rɔba tso lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ feɔ aaafee sɛntimita 50 (aaafee mɔ ko ni eda nine kɛyashi ehiɛ) ni akɛsusu mita kome kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do all the leaves on my rubber trees turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi rɔba tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This natural process is called wintering. The tree deliberately sheds its leaves during dry periods to conserve water, and it will flush with fresh green leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ fɛ̃i be. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does rain make latex harvest difficult or stop the tree from dripping properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ haa latex ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa loo ehaa tsei shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rainwater dilutes the latex and causes it to overflow the cut channels on the trunk rather than trickling into your collection cup, and wet bark increases the risk of fungal infections in the tree cut.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ haa nu lɛ mli nu lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaa etsɔɔ gbɛi ni afo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeho kɛya nu ni abua naa lɛ kɔɔpoo lɛ mli Ni tso lɛ yibii ni efɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa tsei ni afo lɛ amli lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava or plantain in between my young rubber trees while waiting for them to grow big?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava loo plantains yɛ rɔbɔt tsei bibii ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛdara?

english: Yes, during the first 2 to 3 years when the rubber trees are small, intercropping with short-term food crops is beneficial because it provides food and income without blocking light from the young trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli beni rɔba tso lɛ ji bibioo lɛ. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛduɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ ejaakɛ ehaa niyenii kɛ shika ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ haaa tsei bibii lɛ.

english: What happens to my crop if I plant rubber trees too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu rɔbɔt tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: If planted too close, the trees fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and groundwater, causing them to grow thin trunks that produce very little latex.
ga: Kɛji adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛmli nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why does a rubber tree produce that thick white liquid when the bark is cut?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ afo rɔba tso lɛ he lɛ, nu ni mli tse ni yɔɔ futafuta baa lɛ?

english: Latex is the tree's natural defense mechanism. When the outer bark is cut, the tree releases latex to seal its wound and protect itself against insects and fungal attacks.
ga: Latex ji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe. Kɛji akɛ afo kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ Tso lɛ jieɔ latɛs ni ekɛtsiɔ pilamɔi anaa ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why has the bark on my rubber tree dried up and stopped leaking liquid when I tap it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-gum tso lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mita he lɛ?

english: This condition is known as Tapping Panel Dryness, which occurs when a tree is over-tapped or cut too deeply, causing stress that shuts down the latex vessels in that section.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ slit panels lɛ ni egbi. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ atswa tso lɛ tsɔ loo afo lɛ tsɔ. Enɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni haa latɛs tsɔne lɛ ŋmɛɔ yɛ nakai fã lɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Can rubber trees grow and yield well in every part of Ghana, or do they prefer specific areas?
ga: Rɔba tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ Ghana hei fɛɛ. Aloo tamɔ kpokpaa pɔtɛɛ ko?

english: Rubber trees require consistently high rainfall, warm temperatures, and deep acidic soils, which makes them thrive best in the wet forest zones of the Western, Central, and Eastern regions.
ga: Rɔba tsei biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni yaa nɔ daa. hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa ni haa ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ anaigbɛ, teŋgbɛ kɛ bokagbɛ kpokpai lɛ amli lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and scorching during the sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from taller crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them from direct sunlight. Without shade, the hot sun burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil before their roots can reach deeper water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ dani shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are small cocoa pods on my trees turning black and shriveling up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in wet, dark conditions. Removing affected pods immediately stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is losing its nutrients and needs fertilizer for my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efo mli ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛha mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: When soil becomes weak, maize leaves will turn light green or yellow starting from the tips, and the stems will grow thin and short instead of strong and dark green.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo lɛ, Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi. ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ kuku yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ.

english: Will planting legumes like cowpeas between my maize rows steal nutrients away from my main crop?
ga: Ani ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ baaju niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa titri lɛ mli?

english: No, legumes actually feed the soil. They trap nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the earth, providing free nutrient food that helps your maize grow stronger.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ji niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni edara waa lɛ jɛɛhe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava crops right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry out young stems. Waiting for the main rainy season ensures the soil stays wet enough for the roots to establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: If I cut branches off my cocoa tree, won't that cause me to harvest fewer cocoa pods?
ga: Kɛji mifo kookoo nine lɛ Ani no baatsɔɔ akɛ mikpaa kookoo ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Pruning actually increases yields because it lets sunlight and air pass through the canopy. This prevents fungal diseases from breeding in damp dark spots and helps the tree send energy into growing pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ahaa etsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: What causes white, sticky spots under my cassava leaves and causes the leaves to curl up?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii yɛŋ ni ŋmɔɔ yɛ ŋmei baai lɛ ashishi lɛ baa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi?

english: These spots are caused by tiny insects called mealybugs that suck the juice out of the leaves. Removing infected leaves or spraying soapy water helps protect the plant.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ ojie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ loo okɛ nu ni mli edɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous crop yield less grain than certified seeds from an extension officer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mitsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo fe dumɔwui ni extension agent lɛ etsɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests and diseases and produce high yields, whereas saved seeds lose their strength and quality over generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli.

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Covering the ground around the plants with dry leaves keeps the soil cool and retains moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ baai ni egbi baatsu nii ni akɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Weed seeds are tough and remain hidden in the soil for years waiting for rain. Clearing weeds while your crop seedlings are still young keeps the weeds from stealing the crops' light, water, and food.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo, ni amɛmɛɔ nugbɔ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju la, nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Standing water chokes crop roots by cutting off oxygen in the soil. This causes the leaves to turn yellow, roots to rot, and plant growth to stop. Digging small drainage channels allows excess water to flow away safely.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ fiteɔ tsei shishifãi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tsei lɛ kpaa dalɛ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ bibioo ko ni aaatsɔ mli Enɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Is heavy rainfall bad for my farm, or is it only a problem when water stays pooled on the ground?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ náa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii? Aloo kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eji naagba pɛ?

english: Rainfall itself provides essential water for crop growth, but pooled or standing water is harmful because it suffocates root systems and breeds fungal diseases. Well-drained soil lets plants benefit from rain without rotting.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ ji nu jɛɛhe ni he hia kɛha tsei adalɛ. Shi nu ni abua naa loo ni ekã shi lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei náa nugbɔ he sɛɛ ni amɛgbooo.

english: How can I prevent heavy rainwater from washing away my topsoil on a sloping farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni etse ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Digging simple contour trenches across the slope and planting deep-rooted grass along the edges slows down rushing water, allowing it to soak into the ground gently without carrying your fertile topsoil away.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi ni mli kwɔ ni aaatsɔ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ ahe kɛ jwɛi ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ aya hiɛ blɛoo. Ha ni ekɛ ehe awo sũ lɛ mli blɛoo ni ojieee sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ.

english: Why do my unripe cocoa pods keep falling off the tree onto the ground before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmeii ni edako lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛmiiba shikpɔŋ dani amɛdara kwraa lɛ?

english: Premature pod drop, often called cherelle wilt, happens when trees get stressed by sudden excess moisture, poor soil nutrients, or insect damage. Proper shade management and drainage help the tree retain its pods.
ga: Pod ni shwieɔ shi oya, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ Cherelle Wilt lɛ baa kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine trukaa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni fiteɔ lɛ Shade ni sa kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and drooping right after the heavy rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Yellow, drooping leaves during heavy rains are usually a sign that roots are sitting in waterlogged soil and cannot breathe or absorb nutrients. Planting on raised soil mounds helps keep roots above flooded soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. ni enyɛɛɛ emu loo eŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Dumɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do diseases like black pod spread so fast among cocoa trees during long rainy spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo tsei ateŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fungi thrive in wet conditions, and heavy rain splashes disease spores from infected leaves and soil onto healthy pods. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm faster.
ga: Fungus lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ oya.

english: Why do my fruit trees drop their flowers when unseasonal rain falls in February during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ February mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sudden rain during a dry month triggers rapid sap movement in the tree, which can shock fragile flowers and cause them to drop before they turn into fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli lɛ woɔ tsei lɛ amli nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ he hewalɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akpokpo ni amɛgbee shi dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai.

english: What causes my tomatoes to split open on the vine after a sudden heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato niji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa trukaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when plants absorb a sudden rush of water after a dry period. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the fruit wall to burst.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛ́ tso lɛ ŋɔ nu ni hoɔ trukaa yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Ehaa aduawai gbogboi lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting quickly when I store them after harvesting on a wet day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikpa amɛ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ yɛ gbi ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Trapped moisture on harvested tubers creates ideal conditions for rot and fungus to grow during storage. Always air-dry harvested roots in a shaded, well-ventilated space before storing them.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ahe lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii adalɛ kɛ fitemɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, aŋmɛɔ shishifãi ni akpa lɛ gbɛ koni amɛgbi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ dani akɛtoɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has too much water before I plant cassava cuttings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli nu fa tsɔ dani madu ŋmei?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil into a ball; if water drips out easily or it forms a sticky, wet lump that stays muddy, the ground is too wet and fresh cuttings are likely to rot before taking root.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo ko mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji nu hoɔ oya loo efee ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni tsei niji heei baanyɛ agbo dani amɛwo shishifãi.

english: What is the benefit of digging small channels or ditches across my crop field?
ga: Bu bibioo ko ni afoɔ Aloo mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ bu ni tsɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Channels help control water flow—they direct water evenly to your crop roots during dry periods and allow heavy rain to drain away so your plant roots do not rot from sitting in standing water.
ga: Funnels yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ nu lɛ yaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni oha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ mli Enɛ baaha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ akafite kɛjɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense to protect themselves from intense sun and reduce water loss; it shows the plant is stressed by heat and will need rain or irrigation soon.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ko ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa mli. Ni nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he baahia lɛ etsɛŋ.

english: Why does crops planted closer to riverbanks usually stay greener than those on high ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ faai ahe lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ fe nɔ ni yɔɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Land near riverbanks retains deep soil moisture longer and often contains rich silt deposited by water, providing crops with a steady supply of moisture and nutrients even in dry weather.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ naa lɛ hiɛɔ sũ mli nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nu lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai daa, yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi po mli.
