english: How do I know if I am planting my crops too close together in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, thin plants with poor yields rather than short, sturdy plants with full crops.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo faaa. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso kpiti nɛ e he wa nɛ e woɔ yiblii tsuo.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my young crops early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi awo midumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are tougher than farmed crops, so clearing them early prevents them from stealing vital sunlight, fertilizer, and soil moisture from your growing plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju hulu la, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni yɔɔ otsei ni miida lɛ amli lɛ.

english: As cassava plants mature, older lower leaves yellow and drop so the plant can direct its nutrients into expanding its root tubers or supporting fresh top leaves, though extreme leaf drop can signal drought.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cassava tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ baafee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa shishifãi lɛ akwɛ loo eyeɔ ebuaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ hɔmɔ moŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers but no actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when temperatures are too high, when there is insufficient water, or when there are no insects like bees around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu faaa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ he fɛɛ he. koni akɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings look long, pale, and weak instead of short and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni kɛlɛ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ kuku kɛ eŋɔli najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch out and become weak and pale when they do not receive enough direct sunlight, as they are spending all their energy reaching upward towards light.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe ni amɛbaafee gbɔjɔmɔ ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛshɛ ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ he.

english: Repeatedly growing the same crop drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground; changing crops keeps the soil balanced and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni efiteɔ helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does water sit on top of my soil instead of soaking down to the crop roots after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha tsei shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When topsoil is exposed to intense heat, it forms a hard crust that repels water; gently loosening the soil surface with a hoe allows rain and irrigation water to sink deep into the root zone.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa he lɛ Kpãa ni wa ni shwieɔ nu lɛ baafee. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋtayaa shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ blɛoo lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow before the corn even grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani abele lɛ po eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps the plant grow strong ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmãa toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the tree branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that spreads easily during cool, wet weather. Pruning excessive shade leaves lets sunlight and air into the farm to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ shade baai babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Koni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why is it necessary for me to put wooden stakes next to my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ko ama sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to produce food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground and allows the plant to send more energy into growing big tubers under the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni ehaa tso lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Curled, sticky cassava leaves are often caused by tiny insects like mealybugs or whiteflies that suck the sap from the plant. Planting bug-resistant cassava varieties or clearing infected leaves helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni wa lɛ baa. Kasava henɔi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ loo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ simɔ.

english: Why does my plantain tree bend and fall over right when the fruit bunch starts getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni aduawai akutsei lɛ feɔ shwiili lɛ?

english: Plantain trunks are soft and filled with water, so heavy fruit bunches pull them down easily. Propping the trunk with a sturdy, fork-shaped wooden stick gives it the support it needs until harvest.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ahe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ajieɔ aduawai ni tsii kɛyaa shi oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa ni tamɔ fɔk tsu nii kɛfi tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efi shi kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same plot of land three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the dirt and allows pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans naturally restores nitrogen to the land.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when the roots don't get consistent water. Covering the soil with dried leaves or straw helps keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm soil richer for my other crops?
ga: Cowpeas loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná minɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have helpful bacteria on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it directly into the dirt, acting like a natural fertilizer for surrounding crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground instead of sprouting after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when planted in soil that stays soaked with water for too long or when buried too deep. Plant seeds at the proper depth when the rain is steady but the soil drains well.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nu ewo mli be kakadaŋŋ loo ni afu mli tsɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ he ni sa be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does rice grow so well in low, watery valley bottoms where my maize plants die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ shishigbɛ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli, he ni mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ gboi yɛ lɛ?

english: Rice roots are built to breathe and thrive in standing water, whereas maize roots drown and rot if submerged. Lowland valley bottoms naturally retain the water rice needs to mature.
ga: Abɔ ŋmãa shishifãi koni amɛmu ni amɛdara yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni amɛbaafite kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu mli. Jɔɔ lɛ shishi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ toɔ nu kɛhaa ŋmãa ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How long do I need to wait to harvest and eat my crops after spraying them with insect killer?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie shi lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni maye?

english: Every farm chemical has a required waiting period before harvest, called a pre-harvest interval. For most insecticides, you must wait about 2 weeks to 21 days after spraying before picking and eating the produce so the chemical breaks down safely.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ ni amɛmɛ be dani akpa. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ be ni tsɔ nikpamɔ hiɛ lɛ. Kɛha tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi babaoo lɛ Esa akɛ omɛ aaafee otsii 2 kɛyashi gbii 21 yɛ tsofa ni okɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani okɛ tsofai lɛ ato ni oye koni tsofai lɛ akumɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it unsafe to pick and sell my vegetables immediately after applying pesticide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ebɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ mi-vegetables lɛ ato ni mahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ?

english: Chemicals remain active and toxic on or inside plants for several days. Picking crops right after spraying leaves dangerous chemical residues on the food that can make buyers and your family sick.
ga: Tsofai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛtsuɔ nii ni amɛfeɔ awui yɛ tsei anɔ loo amɛmli gbii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii to amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afɔse tsofa lɛ, eshiɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ niyenii lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ oweku lɛ aná hela.

english: What does 'pre-harvest interval' mean when using farm chemicals?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘dani kpamɔ’ tsɔɔ kɛ akɛ tsofai miitsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Pre-harvest interval is the mandatory number of days you must wait between the last chemical spray and the day you harvest your crop to ensure the produce is safe for human consumption.
ga: Be ni tsɔ ŋmaa lɛ hiɛ lɛ ji gbii ayibɔ ni esa akɛ omɛ yɛ naagbee tsofai ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ kɛ gbi ni obaakpa onibii lɛ teŋ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesa niyenii.

english: How long do strong insecticides stay inside a plant after I spray them?
ga: Be enyiɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli wa lɛ baahi mitsei lɛ anɔ beni mikɛshwie amɛnɔ sɛɛ?

english: Strong systemic insecticides absorbed by the plant usually remain high in concentration and active for about 14 to 21 days before they naturally break down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni he wa ni tsei shwieɔ lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shweremɔ babaoo mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii aaafee gbii 14 kɛyashi 21 dani efiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can I spray my fruit trees for pests even when the fruit is almost ready to be picked?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ koni mikɛjie tsɛŋemɔ helai? Eyɛ mli akɛ eshwɛ fioo ni abaakpa aduawai lɛ moŋ

english: You can spray, but you must ensure there are at least 2 to 3 weeks left before harvest. If you pick the fruit earlier than that, the chemical residue will still be present on the fruit.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ. Shi esa akɛ okwɛ akɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, eshwɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 dani obaakpa. Kɛji ogbala aduawai lɛ mra lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ashwɛmɔ baakã aduawai lɛ anɔ.

english: How many months does it take for a mango to mature and ripen on the tree?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango shwereɔ yɛ tso nɔ?

english: From the late development stage until the fruit fully ripens on the tree, mangoes typically take about 5 months to complete their natural cycle.
ga: Kɛjɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shwereɔ lɛ naagbee kɛyashi be mli ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ shwereɔ kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ mangoi aaafee nyɔji 5 dani amɛgbeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ naa.

english: Does spraying insecticides make mangoes ripen faster?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa mango lɛ shwereɔ oya diɛŋtsɛ?

english: No, insecticides only protect the fruit from insect damage. Mangoes follow a natural growth timeline and take about 5 months to mature and ripen regardless of chemical sprays.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ buɔ aduawai lɛ ahe kɛkɛ koni kooloi akafite amɛ. Mango lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ aaafee nyɔji 5 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ kɔɔɔ he eko.

english: When should I stop spraying insecticide on my mango tree before picking the fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ makpa tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ mango tso lɛ nɔ dani makpa aduawai lɛ?

english: You should stop spraying at least 21 days (3 weeks) before you harvest your mangoes to allow enough time for the chemical strength to disappear.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa tsofa lɛ shwiemɔ kɛ hoo lɛ gbii 21 (otsii 3) dani okpa mango lɛ koni eha be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni tsofa lɛ hewalɛ lɛ afite.

english: How do I know if produce from my farm is safe to cook and eat after pest treatment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mahoo ni maye beni migbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ?

english: Produce is safe to eat once you have passed the chemical's required safety waiting period, which is usually 14 to 21 days after your last application.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ kɛji otsɔ tsofa lɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ be ni ataoɔ lɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ gbii 14 kɛyashi 21 sɛɛ beni akɛtsu nii naagbee kwraa lɛ.

english: Why do different crop chemicals have different waiting times before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi amli lɛ yɛ be srɔtoi ni amɛkɛmɛɔ dani akpaa nii lɛ?

english: Different chemicals disappear at different speeds. Mild sprays wash off quickly, while stronger insecticides stay in the plant longer and require up to 3 weeks to break down completely.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi laajeɔ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Spray ni mli tse Efɔ oya. Shi tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ be babaoo ni amɛheɔ otsii 3 dani efiteɔ kwraa.

english: Cocoa pods change color when they are ripe—green pods turn yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange or yellow-orange. Harvesting them when they reach this color change ensures the seeds inside have fully developed the sugar and flavor needed for good processing.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baatsake ni efee ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ su tsakemɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ sugars kɛ flavours ni he hiaa kɛha nitsumɔ kpakpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many harvest seasons does a cocoa tree have in a single year in Ghana?
ga: Be enyiɛ yɔɔ kɛha kookoo tsei yɛ afi mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Cocoa trees in Ghana typically yield crops twice a year: the major harvest season, which runs from October to March with higher yields, and the minor harvest season (mid-crop), which runs from May to August.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ woɔ yibii enyɔ daa afi: kpamɔɔ be titri, ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ October kɛyashiɔ March lɛ ji nɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo. kɛ kpamɔ be ni ji enyɔ (teŋgbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii) ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ May kɛyashiɔ August lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop because only a small fraction are pollinated by tiny insects called midges. If the tree lacks water, nutrients, or proper shade, it will also shed flowers to save its energy for overall survival.
ga: Kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii ji mɛi ni feɔ pollin lɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu, niyenii loo hulutsoo ni sa lɛ, Tsei hu shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha wala fɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my tiny, young cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ egbo ni etsɔ ediŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the tree thins out extra fruit it cannot afford to feed. However, if too many pods die, it can be a sign of drought stress, nutrient shortage, or insect damage.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ Cherelle Wilt, ni tsei shwieɔ aduawai ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ pods babaoo gboi lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee hɔmɔ he haomɔ he okadi. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii

english: Why are my full-grown cocoa pods turning black and rotting while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni eda lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy, cool, and overly shady conditions. Pruning thick branches to let in sunlight and harvesting ripe pods promptly helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ, fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni mli wa koni hulu lɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akpamɔ baaye abua ni akpa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees look eaten and covered in fine webs during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni aye ni ŋmeii kpakpai ehà amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: This damage is often caused by pests like cocoa mirids (capsids) or mites, which multiply during hot, dry weather and feed on young shoots and leaves, causing them to dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cocoa myrids (capsids) loo mites, ni yaa hiɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ baai ni haa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight and dry winds. Fast-growing plantain trees act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist while the young cocoa roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Will planting cassava in the same field harm my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaye mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, cassava grows rapidly and aggressively competes for soil nutrients and water, which can starve nearby young cocoa seedlings. It is safer to plant plantains or temporary shade trees instead of cassava right next to cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei daa oya ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha cacao tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli moŋ fe ni aaadu ŋmei yɛ kookoo masɛi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stall in growth when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Excess rain waterlogs the soil, pushing out oxygen that roots need to breathe and washing away nitrogen. Without nitrogen and healthy roots, maize leaves lose their green color and growth stops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni shishifãi lɛ taoɔ koni amɛmu lɛ kɛjeɔ kpo ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji nitrogen kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa bɛ lɛ, Abɛi baai lɛ hu baafite amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ni amɛbaakpa dalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become light and watery if I harvest them during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: During heavy rains, the cassava plant absorbs excess water and directs its energy into growing new stems and leaves rather than storing starch in the roots, making the tubers soft and watery.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai heei. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ starch ato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Ha yitso lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or standing in waterlogged roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving water drainage helps the leaves regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he loo oha nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during harsh sun helps fruit form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni eyɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do small caterpillars suddenly appear inside the central leaves of my maize after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii baa trukaa lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, which hatch rapidly from eggs laid by moths during warm, rainy weather. Checking the center of your plants early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts right into the funnel stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii shwieɔ amɛwui amli oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ ateŋ mra. ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ awo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are big enough to harvest without digging up the whole stem?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava shows it is mature when its lower leaves naturally dry up and fall off, and the soil right around the base of the main stem begins to crack upwards as the tubers swell below ground.
ga: Cassava jieɔ bɔ ni edara ha lɛ kpo kɛ́ eshishi baai lɛ gĩ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do tiny black insects start eating my harvested grains even after I dried them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji bɔi niyenii ni mikpa lɛ yeli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ hulu lɛ shwie nɔ moŋ?

english: Sun drying removes wetness from the surface, but insect eggs can stay hidden inside the grain kernels and hatch later. Storing fully dried grains in airtight bags or mixing them with safe storage dust suffocates the insects and protects your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ nɔ. Shi ekolɛ kooloi bibii akui lɛ baanyɛ ahi dumɔwui amli ni sɛɛ mli lɛ amɛfɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmaa ni egbi kwraa wo vacuum kotokui amli loo okɛ sũ ni akɛto shweshweeshwe lɛ futu mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebu onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do dark spots start spreading on my tomato leaves after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii diji jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa tomato baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes mud carrying fungal spores onto lower leaves, where wet conditions allow disease to spread. Staking your tomato plants off the ground and trimming leaves near the soil line keeps air moving and prevents the leaves from rotting.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ muji ni hiɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Dumɔ o-tomato lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ofolɔ baai lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha baai lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and weak with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ mli tse ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each crop enough room to build strong stems and feed full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Legume plants like cowpeas work with beneficial soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots, acting like a free natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo sũ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cut seed yams rot in the soil before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mifo lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Freshly cut yam pieces rot easily if exposed to wet soil bacteria before the cut surface has hardened into a protective skin. Rubbing dry wood ash over the raw cuts and letting them dry in the shade before planting prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni afo ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpe dani nɔ ni afo lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa ni etsɔ hewolo ni buɔ mɔ he. Kɛ́ okɛ tso sũ ni egbi lɛ shwie tsei lɛ ahe ni oha amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani odu lɛ, ebaatsi fitemɔ naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my garden egg plants curl up and wilt during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Garden egg leaves curl up in strong afternoon heat to reduce surface area and slow down moisture loss through evaporation. As long as they stand back up in the cooler evening or morning, the crop is managing the heat normally.
ga: Eggplant baai ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛha nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi fiofio kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni amɛteɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ loo leebi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baatsu latsaa lɛ he nii bɔ ni sa.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective leafy canopy that shelters the cocoa leaves from scorching while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kookoo baai lɛ akashã yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to put up tall sticks for my yam vines to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need plenty of sunlight to photosynthesize and build big underground tubers. Staking lifts the vine leaves off the dark, wet ground into the air where they can catch maximum sunlight and stay safe from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee fotosintɛsis ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking woɔ wain tsei anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. He ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually indicate that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its bright green color and continue growing strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli tse ekoŋŋ ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara waa.

english: How does planting groundnuts in the same field alongside my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes with special root systems that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. This naturally enriches the soil, sharing extra nutrients with nearby crops like maize without needing extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛ ko ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jaa niyenii mli hewalɛ krokomɛi, ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why is it a bad idea to put fertilizer on my fields right before a heavy downpour of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer off the surface of the soil before the roots can absorb it. It is better to apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp or just before a soft rain so the nutrients dissolve gently into the root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo fioo dani nugbɔ anɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aha fiofio. shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishifã lɛ he

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants start to curl up and twist tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating the crop early with neem oil or appropriate sprays stops these insects before they stunt the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ neem fɔ loo spray ni sa. Ekpaa nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ dani tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are small holes appearing all over my maize leaves just a few weeks after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-abele baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Small ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like fall armyworms eating the tender central leaf whorl. Catching them early through routine field checks allows you to apply recommended pest controls before they ruin the entire field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ fall armyworm, ni yeɔ baa bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛ ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Gbɛjianɔtoo mli kwɛmɔi ni ooofee daa lɛ baaha okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite jɛmɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to turn soft and rot in the soil during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots starve of air and rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience extreme daytime heat or sudden changes from dry to very wet soil. This temperature or water stress prevents proper flower pollination, causing the plant to drop its blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo be mli latsaa ni naa wa loo tsakemɔ trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa nɔ. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo loo nu mli haomɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ naa. ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing around the main trunk of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water, light, and nutrients away from the main mother plant. Pruning away all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant gets all the energy it needs to produce large, heavy bunches of plantains.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ amli, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves usually means your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the crop's growth fixes this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ mli mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under full sun and cannot hold water well. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantain beside them provides living shade and keeps the air cool until the cocoa stems grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛhiɛɛɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu nurse tsei ni yɔɔ ekãa ni shwereɔ oya yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ mli baawa.

english: If I plant my cassava cuttings very close together, will I harvest more tubers?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa Ani mana yitsei babaoo?

english: No, planting cassava too closely causes the roots to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows the underground roots enough room to swell into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or dry soil, which prevents pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching around the roots helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. ni tsiɔ pollination naa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: It is better to apply fertilizer after the rain when the soil is already damp. Applying fertilizer right before heavy rainfall causes the water to wash your expensive nutrients away into streams before the plant roots can soak them up.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ faa lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Curling leaves are usually a reaction to tiny pests like aphids or thrips hiding underneath, sucking out the plant's sap. Spraying the undersides of the leaves with neem oil or targeted insecticides stops these pests and lets new leaves grow flat again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛtsɔ tsei amli nu ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akɛtaoɔ kooloi amli lɛ baashwie baai lɛ ashishi. Ekpaa nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ ni ehaa baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like stone shortly after I water my vegetable garden?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ beni mikɛ nu wo mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil becomes hard when it lacks organic matter like well-rotted animal manure or compost. Adding compost breaks up hard soil, acting like a natural sponge that holds water and makes it easier for roots to spread.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaagbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃.

english: Why are my maize plants growing extremely tall and thin, but producing tiny cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ŋmei bibioo ko yɛ.

english: Maize grows tall and weak when it gets too much nitrogen without enough phosphorus and potassium, or when planted too tightly together. A balanced fertilizer gives the plant strong stems and the right energy to fill out fat cobs.
ga: Abɛi daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji enine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shikpɔŋhosomɔ ni ja yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ waa ni ehaa hewalɛ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmei ni eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are dark spots spreading across my plantain leaves and turning them brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ miigbɛ eshwa mi plantain baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots on plantain leaves are typically caused by leaf spot diseases like Black Sigatoka, which spread in damp weather. Cutting off damaged leaves and clearing weed cover improves airflow to keep the remaining leaves dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ plantain baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa, tamɔ black sigatoka, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Baai ni efite lɛ ni aaafolɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni akɛhaa amɛhe lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ Enɛ baaha baa ni eshwɛ lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do I tell if my cassava is mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and shed, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the base begins to crack open as the swelling tubers push against the upper soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni eshiɔ tso ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baabɔi mligbalamɔ be mli ni ŋmei ni efuu lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Is it a good idea for me to plant coconut trees alongside my other crops?
ga: Eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa kɛha mi akɛ makwɛ ŋmei tsei kɛfata ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: Yes, intercropping coconut trees with other crops is a great way to maximize your land use and secure extra income without risking your main crop, as coconuts provide long-term yield and don't easily fail once established.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei tsei ni akɛ tsei krokomɛi duɔ. Eji gbɛ kpakpa ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii babaoo ni oná shika kroko ni okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ akawo oshara mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii woɔ yibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, ni amɛfiŋ mlɛo. Beni adu lɛ

english: Why do farmers say that growing coconut trees is a low-risk investment for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei tsei akwɛmɔ ji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli ni oshara bɛ mli kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Coconut trees are very resilient once established, require relatively low maintenance compared to seasonal crops, and provide continuous harvests for many years, ensuring you don't lose your investment.
ga: Kokoo tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe waa kɛji adu amɛ pɛ. Amɛbiɔ saamɔ fioo ko kɛ akɛto be mli tsei ahe. ni ofee nibii ni yaa nɔ afii babaoo Kwɛmɔ ni okɛ shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ akafite.

english: Will planting large trees like coconuts take away nutrients from my short-term crops?
ga: Ani tso agbo ko ni tamɔ ŋmei ni miduɔ lɛ baajie niyenii ni haa mitso lɛ yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ?

english: If spaced correctly, deep-rooted trees like coconuts draw nutrients and water from deeper soil layers, leaving topsoil nutrients for shallower crops while providing light shade and wind protection.
ga: Kɛji akɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ja Tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli. Shi niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni mli tse kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he.

english: How do coconut trees behave during the dry season compared to short-term vegetables?
ga: Te ŋmei tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli kɛ akɛto aduawai ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ ahe?

english: Coconut trees have extensive, deep root systems that allow them to tap into underground moisture, helping them survive dry spells far better than seasonal crops that dry up quickly.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ ni haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni yɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ.

english: Why should I mix different types of crops on my land instead of planting just one crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi afutu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ tso kome pɛ

english: Mixing crops spreads your financial risk so that if one crop fails due to bad weather or market price drops, the other crop can still provide you with income and protect you from total loss.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ haa oshika he osharai feɔ srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii loo jarayeli jara ni eba shi lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu baanyɛ aha oná shika ni ebu ohe kɛjɛ nɔ ni baafite kwraa lɛ he.

english: How long does it usually take to start getting returns when I plant new tree crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mijeɔ nyɔmɔwoo shishi kɛji midu tso hee?

english: Most permanent tree crops like coconuts take about 3 to 5 years to start producing fruit, but once they start, they yield consistently for decades with very low ongoing costs.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmeii, heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi kɛ́ aje shishi lɛ, ebaaha afee nibii ni yaa nɔ daa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ yɛ shika ni baa shi waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can adding permanent trees to my farm help protect my soil from heavy rain?
ga: Ani tsei ni hiɔ shi daa ni mikɛbaafata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Yes, the strong root systems of long-term trees bind the soil together, preventing heavy rainwater from washing away valuable topsoil and plant nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ashishifãi ni wa lɛ haa sũ lɛ feɔ ekome. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ tsei amli niyenii.

english: How do I know if a new farming method or crop scheme being introduced to us is safe to try on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ okwaayeli gbɛ hee loo ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni wɔkɛhaa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni maka yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can safely test a new method by dedicating a small section of your land to it first to see how it performs before committing all your land and money.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka gbɛi heei okwɛ shweshweeshwe kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni ooojɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. onɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii eha. Dani okɛ oshikpɔŋ kɛ oshika fɛɛ baaha

english: What should I consider before trying out a new intercropping arrangement on my land?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ masusu he dani maka ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo hee makwɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should check plant spacing so crops do not choke each other out, soil fertility, water needs, and ensure the crops mature at different times to give you steady cash flow.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ bɔ ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kɛjɛ he. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii nu he hiamɔ nii Ni okwɛ koni tsei lɛ ada yɛ bei srɔtoi amli koni eha bo shika ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: What kind of care do young tree crops need during their first few years in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔ he hiaa dumɔwu ko yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni ekɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: Young tree crops need regular weeding, protection from stray animals, and water during dry periods until their root systems grow deep enough to survive independently.
ga: Tsei bibii ahe miihia ni ajie jwɛi daa. Tsi kooloi ni elaaje kɛ nu yɛ hɔmɔ be mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to measure my land properly before buying my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ dani mahe dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Measuring your land helps you calculate the exact amount of seed, fertilizer, and water you need so you do not waste money or overcrowd your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ osusu he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni he baahia bo lɛ he akɔntaa pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bɔni afee ni okafite shika loo okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii akawo mli fe nine.

english: Why should I clear and prepare my land long before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni asaa he dani nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Early land preparation gives the soil time to loosen up and allows cleared grass to rot into natural manure before seeds are planted.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛshwieɔ shi. ni ehaa jwɛi ni he tse lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani aduɔ dumɔwui.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close together on a small plot?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko bibioo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak plants and small harvests.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast on land that I leave empty without crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mishiɔ amɛ ni amɛduuu nii lɛ?

english: Bare land absorbs direct sunlight and moisture, which causes wild weed seeds hidden in the soil to sprout rapidly to cover the open ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ ŋmɛɔ hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa koo mli jwɛi dumɔwui ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛha hei ni agbele naa lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it good practice for me to let my farm land rest without planting anything for a season?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ maha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe ni miduuu tsei komɛi? Kɛha be kome?

english: Yes, letting land rest allows the soil to naturally rebuild its nutrients and organic matter, making it stronger for your next planting season.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaaha ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa enyɛɔ etswaa niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa enáa hewalɛ babaoo kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What can I plant on my field during the off-season so the soil does not stay unused?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akatsu nii?

english: You can plant cover crops like cowpeas or beans, which protect the soil from sun damage and put natural nitrogen back into the ground.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii. Enɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la he, ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does tired soil take a long time to start producing good crop yields again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai afeemɔ shishi ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soil loses its plant food over time when crops eat from it, and it takes time for natural microbes and organic waste to break down and rebuild that food supply.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ tsei amli niyenii yɛ be mli ni tsei yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni eheɔ be babaoo dani adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛsaa nakai niyenii jɛɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my young crops grow very slowly during their first few weeks in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In the beginning, seedlings put most of their energy into growing strong underground roots to find water before they start growing fast above the ground.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, dumɔwui kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni wa koni amɛtao nu. dani eda oya kɛho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How can I grow more food if I only have a small piece of land available?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu niyenii babaoo kɛji shikpɔŋ bibioo ko pɛ miyɔɔ?

english: You can practice intercropping by planting two complementary crops together, like maize and cassava, to make the best use of space and sunlight.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ intercropping akase kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Koni akɛ ŋwɛi kɛ hulu la lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I get a large crop yield from a small plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná nibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ?

english: Yes, by giving plants proper spacing, adding good compost, and keeping weeds away, a small plot can produce a very high harvest relative to its size.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, shikpɔji bibii baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo waa kɛha amɛdalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which the crop needs to build green foliage. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii awo baai eŋɔli yɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses, or by severe heat stress when the soil dries out completely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my cassava under the ground is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack from the swelling roots below.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the middle of the day even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it up. They temporarily wilt to conserve moisture and usually recover once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Amɛbaagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe baajɔ amɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why did my seeds fail to grow after planting them right after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni adu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain packs the soil tightly and fills all the tiny air pockets with water, which can drown seeds or prevent them from getting the oxygen they need to break open and sprout.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ nu woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ atsɔ nu mli loo etsĩ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress, as the plant drops blossoms to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Planting cassava repeatedly in the same spot drains specific plant nutrients from the soil and allows root-damaging pests and diseases to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ajieɔ niyenii ni haa tsei pɔtɛɛi lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What is the white powder showing up on the leaves of my garden plants during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni ji powda yɛŋ ni jeɔ kpo yɛ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: That white coating is powdery mildew, a plant fungus that spreads quickly in warm, humid air. Spacing out your plants helps air flow freely and reduces the spread.
ga: Nakai nɔ ni yɔɔ futafuta lɛ ji powder mildew. Enɛ ji tso mli ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. He ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa gbɛfaŋnɔ baa shi.

english: Why are my young crop seedlings growing tall and thin instead of short and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ miidara ni amɛmiifee shwiili yɛ kukuji ni amɛmiifee shwiili lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch tall and weak when they are not receiving enough direct light, as they are reaching out toward the sun to get the energy they need to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛji amɛnaaa la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. beni amɛshɛɔ hulu lɛ he koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛshwere lɛ.

english: How can I keep my crops alive when the rains stop completely during the farming season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahi shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli?

english: You can use simple irrigation methods like drip pipes or bucket watering directly at the base of plants early in the morning or late evening. Covering the soil around plants with dry leaves or straw (mulching) also stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu shwiemɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi loo baagi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulching) shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu la lɛ mli.

english: I hear farmers in dry places can grow corn without rainfall, so how does drip irrigation actually work?
ga: Minu akɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ adu ŋmãa ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, te nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Drip irrigation uses thin plastic hoses with small holes placed along your plant rows to drop water directly onto the roots slowly. Because water goes straight to the roots without spilling on empty soil, almost no water is wasted through evaporation.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ plastic paipii bibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ tsei amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi fiofio kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu hoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ ni eshwieee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, eshwɛ fioo ni nu ko kwraa laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up into tight tubes when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the leaf area exposed to the strong sun. This helps the plant trap moisture inside and stop water from evaporating too quickly during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha he ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ baa lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ emli lɛ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How does excessive sunshine and heat affect the way my crops produce fruits and seeds?
ga: Te hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine kɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ saa bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extreme heat stresses plants, causing them to spend energy trying to cool down instead of growing. Very high temperatures can cause flowers to dry up and fall off before forming fruits, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei yeɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbi ni amɛgbee shi dani amɛwo yibii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: What is mulching, and how does putting dry grass on my farm help my crops during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni ji mulching? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Mulching means covering the bare soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves. It acts like a protective blanket that shades the soil from hot sunshine, keeps the ground cool, and keeps soil moisture from drying out.
ga: Mulching tsɔɔ akɛ abaaha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai aha onibii ahe. Amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he, ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi

english: Why does my soil become hard like concrete after a few days of hot sun, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit yɛ gbii babaoo ni mikɛhi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter and loses all its water. Mixing animal manure or compost into your soil adds rich organic material that helps the ground hold onto water like a sponge and stay soft under heat.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli, ni nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ futu mli lɛ, ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli tamɔ sponji lɛ fataa he. ni ehaa ehe feɔ blɛoo kɛ́ edɔ lɛ

english: Are there special seeds I can buy that grow better and produce yield when there is very little rainfall?
ga: Ani dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ mahe ni daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ?

english: Yes, agricultural officers offer 'drought-tolerant' or early-maturing crop varieties. These seeds are bred either to grow deep roots that search for underground water or to mature quickly before dry spells hit.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli he onukpai kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni ‘nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa’ loo tsei ni kwɛɔ mra lɛ haa. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui nɛɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛtao shikpɔŋ shishi nu loo amɛkwɛ̃ oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Can planting taller crops next to my shorter crops help protect them from intense sunshine?
ga: Ani tsei kakadaji ni aduɔ yɛ mitsei kukuji lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Yes, this is called intercropping. Planting taller crops like cassava or plantains near shorter, tender crops creates natural shade, lowers ground temperature, and protects sensitive plants from scorching heat.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ intercropping. Tsei kakadaji tamɔ cassava loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ tsei kukuji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ baa shi ni ebuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni shãa mɔ lɛ he.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize now that the rain patterns keep changing every year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ daa afi?

english: Rather than relying only on traditional calendar months, wait until the soil receives two or three heavy, deep-soaking rains before planting, and check local farm weather advisories for seasonal rainfall updates.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ kusum kalanda nyɔji pɛ anɔ lɛ, Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ dani odu nii. Ni okwɛ akutsoŋ ŋmɔ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he ŋaawoo kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be mli tsakemɔi.

english: Is it safe to apply fertilizer to my crops when the soil is very dry and the sun is hot?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: No, applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil in hot weather can burn and kill crop roots. Always apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist or when you are able to water the crops immediately after.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo beni obaanyɛ okɛ nu awo tso lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants drying up and turning brown in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides essential cover and keeps the soil cool while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi. Ebaaha nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ aha nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce enough food to grow large underground tubers. Lifting the vines on stakes helps the leaves catch maximum light while keeping them off the damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa la babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ji he ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers or well-rotted manure helps the maize plant regain its rich green color and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔshi tsei lɛ ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa.

english: Cassava roots suffocate and rot when trapped in waterlogged soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows heavy rain to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ he. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests to build up. Rotating your land with beans or cowpeas returns nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. Checking your field early and spraying recommended organic mixtures or insecticides directly into the center of the plant can control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli mra. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛfutuɔ nibii loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye enɛɛmɛi anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on young leaves. Using insecticidal soaps or neem tree extract helps get rid of these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso mli nu tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ajie kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience extreme heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by watering regularly and using grass mulch helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ebɔi yibii womɔ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and struggle to hold up the heavy weight of a fruit bunch, especially in strong winds. Supporting the main trunk with a propping pole or forked stick keeps the plant standing.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ, titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli loo tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔɔ shi.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crop seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for the same sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to grow larger and yield more food.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo niyenii babaoo.

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away nutrients or swamp the soil so roots cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii loo nu ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aahu akɛ ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow plenty of leafy green branches, but the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ niji babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When yam plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below. Using balanced fertilizers helps energy move down to the tubers.
ga: Kɛji sweet potato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii, moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato bulbs ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua hewalɛ lɛ ni eya shi kɛya bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl tightly upwards and stop the plant from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekadara lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny sucking insects called whiteflies. It can also happen as a natural defense when the plant suffers from extreme heat or sudden dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Ebaanyɛ eba hu akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my groundnut leaves getting small dark spots and dropping off before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii diji lɛ? ni amɛgbee shi dani kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease commonly called leaf spot (Tikka disease). High humidity and rain help the fungus spread, which weakens the plant and reduces the number of nuts it can produce.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni afɔɔ lɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ leaf spot (tikka hela) kɛ enɛ baa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ afee lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Cassava root rot happens when water stays trapped around the roots for too long, allowing soil fungi to enter and decay the roots. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small green pods before they grow into full cocoa fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani ebaada ni etsɔ kookoo aduawai ni eyi obɔ

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees naturally drop extra young pods that they cannot feed when there is drought, low soil nutrients, or damage from mirid insects.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii kɛji hɔmɔ ba. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo naakpɛɛ kooloi bibii efite

english: Why do my pepper plants produce many flowers, but the flowers fall off without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjieee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa?

english: Pepper flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. When the plant experiences stress, it drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ tsei kɛ haomɔ kpe Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he koni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed underground by tiny worms called nematodes or stem weevils. Without healthy roots to grip the soil, top-heavy plants easily blow over unless supported by wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem weevils lɛ baanyɛ afite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Tsei ni amɛyitsei tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. ja tsei ni akɛfiɔ sɛɛ lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do my cabbage plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Wilting during hot hours happens because the broad leaves lose water faster than the roots can pump it up. If they do not recover in the cooler evening, soil diseases like bacterial wilt may be blocking the stem.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa ejaakɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu lɛ. Kɛji amɛjieee amɛhe yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ helai tamɔ bacteria wilt baanyɛ atsĩ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do the heads on my rice plants turn white and empty instead of filling up with rice grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee futafuta ni efee efolo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmãa ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Empty rice heads, often called 'chaffy heads,' happen when insects like stem borers bite into the base of the stem, cutting off the supply of food to the developing grains during flowering.
ga: Omɔ yitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘chaff yitsei’ lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii, tamɔ stem borers, ŋmɔ tso lɛ shishi, ni amɛfo niyenii ni akɛhaa dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers lay black plastic sheets on the soil around their crop rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ plastic diji fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The black plastic cover, known as plastic mulch, prevents weeds from growing and stealing crop nutrients. It also keeps the soil damp and warm, which helps plant roots grow faster and stronger.
ga: Plastic diŋ ni akɛhaa nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ plastic shikpɔŋ nɔ hamɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛju tso lɛ mli niyenii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why should I start my pepper seeds in black plastic polybags before transferring them to the open farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi pepper dumɔwui yɛ plastic kotokui diji amli dani mikɛya ŋmɔ ko ni agbele mli lɛ mli?

english: Young seedlings are delicate and easily killed by heavy rainfall, hot sun, or pests. Nursery polybags allow you to protect and water young plants until their roots are strong enough to survive on the main field.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ gboiɔ oya. hulu la ni mli edɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Nursery poly bags lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ tsei bibii ahe ni ohaa amɛ nu kɛyashiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I plant them in an open field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains grown beside them to act as natural sunshades during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Why do the leaves of my maize crop curl up into tight tubes during hot dry afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni edɔ ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves inward to protect themselves from losing water through evaporation when the afternoon heat becomes too intense.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu akaje mli kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ.

english: How can I tell if grain seeds I bought at the local market are good enough to grow well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can test seed quality by dropping a sample into a bucket of clean water. Healthy seeds are heavy and sink to the bottom, while dead or insect-damaged seeds float to the top.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka dumɔwui lɛ ahe okwɛ kɛtsɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko ni oookɛwo nu ni mli tse baagi mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsii ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni egbo loo kooloi efite lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: When crops lack enough food in the soil—especially nitrogen—they pull stored nutrients out of their older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top, causing the old leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli titri lɛ nitrogen Amɛgbalaa niyenii ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai momo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do weeds sprout up on my land almost immediately after the first rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi shwereɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aaafee yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds remain alive but asleep in dry soil through the hot season. As soon as rain touches them, they wake up and sprout much faster than most planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui yɛ wala mli lolo shi amɛkã shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni amɛteɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kwraa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo.

english: Why are my garden egg plants dropping their flowers before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Vegetable crops drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden hot spells, lack of water in the soil, or a shortage of plant nutrients like calcium.
ga: Aduawai shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ latsaa trukaa, nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo tso mli niyenii tamɔ calcium ni bɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing long stem branches and big leaves, but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ niji kakadaji kɛ baai wuji shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?
