english: If the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or if the ground is too hard, the plant spends all its energy growing leafy tops instead of swelling its roots underground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai bibii amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with maize make the maize stalks grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du cowpea lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli tsei lɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that gather nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil through their roots, providing natural food that neighboring crops like maize can feed on.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmei tso ko ni buaa nitrogen gas naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ aye.

english: Why does my local millet grow much better in dry areas compared to maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ hei ni egbi lɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Millet has a deep, efficient root system and small leaves that conserve water, allowing it to survive hot, dry conditions where maize roots would dry out and wither.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ baai bibii. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shi Eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Abɛi lɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbi.

english: How deep should I plant my millet seeds in the soil during planting season?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Millet seeds are very small, so you should plant them shallowly—about 2 to 3 centimeters deep. If planted too deep, the young seedling will run out of energy before it reaches the surface.
ga: Millet dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ odu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ, aaafee sɛntimitai 2 kɛyashi 3. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, Tsei bibii lɛ ahewalɛ baaho dani amɛyashɛ nu lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my millet plants turn yellow and stop growing when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sorghum tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Millet prefers dry soil and gets stressed when its roots sit in soaked, watery soil. Waterlogged soil prevents the roots from breathing air, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Sorghum sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli kɛ́ eshishifãi lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni nu ebɔle he lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Which crops can I farm on my land if I want to produce cooking oil?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni maná fɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii?

english: In Ghana, the best crops for extracting cooking oil are oil palm, groundnuts (peanuts), sesame seeds, sunflowers, and soybeans. Each crop requires different processing equipment to press the oil.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛjieɔ fɔ ni akɛhooɔ nii lɛ ekomɛi ji oil palm, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmei (shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmei), sesame dumɔwui, hulutsoo fɔfɔi, kɛ soybean. Tsei srɔtoi biɔ nibii srɔtoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛjie mu lɛ.

english: How do I know when my oil palm fruits are ripe enough to press for palm oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-oil palm yibii lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ majie palm oil lɛ?

english: Oil palm bunches are fully ripe when the fruits change to a bright reddish-orange color and a few outer fruits naturally start falling to the ground. Pressing them at this stage gives you the highest oil yield.
ga: Oil palm tsei akui lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ aduawai lɛ batsɔ tsuru-ŋmei ni kpɛɔ. Ni kponɔgbɛ yibii lɛ ekomɛi baaje shishi amɛgbee shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ onyɛ amɛnɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oná mu babaoo.

english: Why do my groundnuts give very little oil when I press them after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii lɛ amli fɔ fioo pɛ baa kɛji mimimɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts need to be fully mature and thoroughly dried before pressing. Harvesting them too early or processing wet nuts leads to low oil yield and poor oil quality.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahoo jogbaŋŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa dani atswa amɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa mra tsɔ loo ŋmãa ni mli ewo muji lɛ he nitsumɔ lɛ, ebaaha fɔ ni anáa lɛ aba shi, ni fɔ lɛ hu baafee nɔ ni ehiii.

english: Why do some of my millet grains fail to sprout when I soak them to prepare pito?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-millet dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni mikɛwoɔ nu mli koni mikɛsaa pito lɛ?

english: Millet seeds will not sprout if they were dried at very high temperatures, stored for too long, or damaged by pests. Only fresh, healthy seeds that were dried in the shade germinate well for brewing.
ga: Sorghum dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ agbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa mli. ni akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efiteɔ Dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ pɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛha dãafeemɔ.

english: Can I sell any variety of millet to local pito brewers, or do they prefer a specific type?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi. Ani abaanyɛ akɛha Pito dãafeelɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Aloo amɛbaanyɛ amɛhɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ ko?

english: Brewers prefer specific local red or white millet varieties because they sprout uniformly and produce the right sweetness and color needed for good pito.
ga: Mɛi ni feɔ dãa lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa tsuru loo ŋmãa yɛŋ henɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Ejaakɛ ekwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔ kɛ su ni sa kɛha pito kpakpa.

english: How should I store my dried crop stalks if I want to use them for fuel to light farm fires?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsei ahe tsei ni egbi lɛ ato? Kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛtsu nii akɛ fuel ni okɛje la shishi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Keep dried stalks elevated off the wet ground on wooden racks and cover them with a tarpaulin to protect them from rain, mold, and termites so they stay dry and burn cleanly.
ga: Okɛ tsei ni egbi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ yɛ tso shĩa ko nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ tarp aha nɔ koni ebu he kɛjɛ nugbɔ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahe koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛshã jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will growing millet on the same piece of land every year spoil my soil?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ baaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: Yes, millet uses up a lot of nutrients from the upper soil layers. To keep your soil healthy, rotate millet with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts, which put nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Enɛ haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an important nutrient for healthy growth. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves regain their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eha dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas in the same field alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for maize while covering the soil to reduce weed growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni ehaa ŋmãa ni haa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves dry up and drop off, leaving only a cluster of leaves at the top of the main stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Baai akuu pɛ eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa tree blossoms falling off before developing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience water stress, extreme heat, or attacks from pests like mirids. Maintaining adequate shade trees and protecting plants from sap-sucking insects helps flowers stay on the tree.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ nu mli haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ atatu ni tswaa lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ afee tso lɛ he hulutsoo jogbaŋŋ ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into small tightly rolled shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe bibii ni ebɔle ehe shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is commonly caused by small insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking plant juice and spreading viruses. Managing these insects early protects the leaves and keeps fruit yields steady.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaabu baai lɛ ahe ni eye ebua ni aná yibii.

english: Why do my yam setts rot in the soil before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam setts rot when planted in waterlogged soil or when the cut surfaces are not treated with wood ash or fungicide to protect them against soil fungi and bacteria.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ akɛ tso sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii tsuuu he ni afo lɛ koni ebu he kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli helai ahe.

english: Why do my maize crops produce small, weak cobs when planted very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for sunlight, ground moisture, and nutrients, leaving less energy for each individual plant to build big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii haa tso fɛɛ tso náaa hewalɛ fioo ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋshɔŋlooi wuji.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my garden crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the soil moist during hot weather, suppresses weeds, and breaks down over time to enrich the soil naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can dry out and kill fragile germinating seedlings. Waiting until rains become regular ensures continuous soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ agbi ni efite dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain plants turn brown and droop early in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water rapidly in dry, windy weather. Clearing weeds, applying mulch around the base, and watering helps the plant hold moisture through dry periods.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ amli. weeding Mulching ni bɔleɔ shishitoo lɛ he Ni nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Pale yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. As the plant grows, it pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore healthy green foliage.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛye ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same soil drains specific nutrients and allows pests that feed on maize to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like beans or peanuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and scorch when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense direct sunlight because excessive heat damages their delicate foliage. Planting shade plants like plantains nearby provides a natural umbrella that protects the young cocoa leaves while keeping the soil cooler.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ fiteɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Nibii ni haa hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around my crops help them survive when rain is scarce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ Miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi beni nugbɔ faaa lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or mulch acts as a blanket that blocks direct sunlight from drying out the earth. It lowers soil temperature and holds moisture in the ground for longer so plant roots stay hydrated between rains.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shishifãi hiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water blocks air from reaching the roots, causing decay and fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rain to drain away easily from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli oya.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes extremely hot or when watering is irregular. High heat stops proper pollination, causing the plant to drop unpollinated flowers to conserve its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa pollination ni sa lɛ kpaa. Enɛ haa tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my farm even after I clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mijie amɛ po lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil for long periods and germinate as soon as rain and sunlight hit them after clearing. Planting cover crops or spreading dead leaf mulch shades the ground and prevents weed seeds from getting the light they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ba pɛ kɛkɛ ni ajie amɛ. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ aná la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which attack the tender central leaves where the plant grows. Applying recommended biological treatments or neem extract into the center whorl early in the morning destroys the pests before they kill the main shoot.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛgbe ŋmeii titrii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji mishi tsei bibii komɛi ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ he lɛ

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one or two ensures the main stem gets enough food to produce a large, heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Tsobii bibii babaoo (tsots) kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots and dead branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ ahe tsei ni egboi kɛ tsei aniji lɛ?

english: Removing unwanted shoots and dead branches opens up the cocoa tree canopy so air and sunlight can pass through. Good airflow reduces humidity that causes black pod disease and allows the tree to focus its energy on growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ ŋmeii kɛ eniji ni ataooo lɛ, egbeleɔ kookoo tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Sir, why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ shi ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: When the lower leaves of maize turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, it means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for green growth. The plant is forced to move nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the young leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa shishi baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei yeɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Anyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛjie nitrogen kɛjɛ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Please, why do experienced farmers say I should plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting my maize?
ga: Ofainɛ, mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Crops like maize exhaust the soil's strength. Legumes such as groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny nodes on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and put it back into the earth, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha okpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to intense heat and light. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them during their first few years to block direct sunlight and keep the surrounding air cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa amɛnɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Koni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ

english: Sir, why do my cassava roots rot underground when the heavy rains start?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot breathe when they sit in soaked, standing water for too long. If the soil lacks good drainage, excess rainwater suffocates the roots, causing fungal rot; planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛji amɛtara nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu kpakpa Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ha ŋmeii lɛ agbo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Please, why do some tomato farmers cover the ground around their crops with dry grass?
ga: Ofainɛ, mɛni hewɔ tomato okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It prevents the hot sun from evaporating water out of the soil, keeps the roots cool, and blocks sunlight so weeds cannot easily grow.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa hulu la shɛɛɛ amɛhe, no hewɔ lɛ jwɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo.

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When crowded, individual plants remain weak and produce tiny fruits or grains, resulting in a smaller total yield than properly spaced crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Beni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ Tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii bibii loo dumɔwui. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni abaaná lɛ baafee bibioo fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Sir, why should I cut off the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ? Mi plantain shishitoo lɛ hu je kpo?

english: A plantain mother tree shares its food and water with all the young shoots growing around it. By cutting away extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones, the main tree keeps enough energy to produce a large, heavy cluster of plantains.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ jaa niyenii kɛ nu kɛ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ ni ashiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ. Tso titri lɛ baato hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: How do weeds growing near my cassava actually harm the crop if they aren't directly touching it?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cassava lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ cassava lɛ kpaaa gbee tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water and fertilizers from deep inside the soil before your cassava roots can reach them. They also shade small crop leaves from getting sunlight and provide hiding places for harmful insects.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kaaha hulu la lɛ miishɛ ehe. Ni eji he ko hu ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ.

english: Please, what causes small holes in the fresh leaves inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Ofainɛ kadimɔ, mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ baai heei lɛ amli, yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli

english: Holes and saw-dust-like waste in the central funnel of maize are classic signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the rolled leaves during the hot day and chew on the soft growing tissues of the plant.
ga: Bu kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadii ni ale waa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni amɛye tsei lɛ amli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ

english: Sir, why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off to the ground without making any peppers?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme stress, such as severe heat, lack of water, or soil that has too much nitrogen and not enough phosphorus. Without steady moisture and balanced nutrition, the flowers fall off before fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni naa wa, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ nɔ ni phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni sa bɛ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when I wait too long to put fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji akɛ awo mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Just like a person gets weak and hungry when they go unpaid and cannot buy food, maize plants starve without nutrients like nitrogen. When feeding is delayed, the plant pulls food from its old leaves to survive, causing them to turn yellow.
ga: Taakɛ bɔ ni gbɔmɛi gbɔjɔɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ kɛ́ awooo amɛ nyɔmɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii lɛ. Hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmã tsei hu kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen bɛ amɛhe. Kɛji niyenii hamɔ sɛɛ tsɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their blossoms without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: When a plant lacks enough water or food in the soil, it panics and drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival, similar to a person cutting back on extra spending when money runs out.
ga: Kɛ tsei bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ebaafee gbeyei ni ekɛ fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni ekɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala. Etamɔ bɔ ni mɛi jieɔ shika babaoo kɛjɛɔ amɛshika mli kɛ́ amɛshika fite lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year when I plant the same crop over and over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull specific food out of the soil to grow. If you keep planting the same crop without giving the soil a rest or adding manure, the soil runs out of that food, leaving future crops to starve.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ohaaa sũ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, Nakai niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaho aya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii baafite.

english: In intense heat, plants lose water quickly through their leaves. Drooping is the plant's way of reducing its exposure to the sun to save water until the soil gets moist again.
ga: Yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Drooping ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbaa hulu la ni amɛnaa lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground after too much heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil for too long, the roots drown and begin to decay.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛje shishi amɛgboi.

english: Why do my maize crops produce tiny cobs when I plant many seeds very close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight with each other for the limited water and food in that spot. Because no single plant gets enough food, none of them can form full, heavy cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaawuu yɛ nu kɛ niyenii fioo ni yɔɔ nakai he lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso ko bɛ ni baanyɛ awo ŋmeii ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are weeds able to choke and stunt my young cassava plants so easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miitsi mi yucca tsei lɛ anaa oya ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the food, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. If weeds take the resources first, your cassava plant goes hungry and stops growing.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛji jwɛi yeɔ nibii klɛŋklɛŋ O-cassava tsei lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛbaakpa dalɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce a very small bunch when there are many suckers growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ niji bibii waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ? mi plantain lɛ

english: The young shoots growing around the main stem act like extra mouths to feed. They steal water and nutrients away from the mother plant, leaving less energy to fill out the fruit bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Tso titri lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ naabu krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ ayeɔ nii. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛbaawo aduawai akuu lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and burn when I clear away all the big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and cannot handle direct sunlight all day. Shade trees protect them from overheating while their roots grow deep enough to collect water.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhiɛ nu mli lɛ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my weak and poorly fed crops more than my healthy ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ahaaa amɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ fe miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Healthy plants produce natural defenses to fight off insects. When a crop is weak or starved of nutrients, it loses those defenses, making it easy prey for pests.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ maa adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ helai anaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ hewalɛ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ lɛ Ebaafee nɔ ni buɔ ehe. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui.

english: Why do my rice leaves turn yellow shortly after I transplant them into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Transplant shock causes temporary yellowing as the roots adjust to new soil. It can also mean the crop lacks nitrogen or needs better water management in the field.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he gbeyeishemɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko mli beni shishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo ehe miihia ni akwɛ nu nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Does my rice crop always need to stay completely underwater to grow well?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ ahi nu shishi kwraa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, while lowland rice thrives in flooded fields, upland rice varieties grow in regular moist soil. Even flooded fields need periodic draining so plant roots can breathe.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa folo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli moŋ. Shi ŋmãa henɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Gbɛjegbɛi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ po he miihia ni nu atsɔ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: How do I know when my grains are ready for harvest so I do not pick them too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmaa lɛ eshɛ nikpamɔ? Bɔni afee ni okabua naa oya tsɔ?

english: Grains signal maturity when about 80 percent of the head turns golden brown and hard, while the lower leaves begin to dry naturally.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida beni ŋmeii lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 batsɔ shika tsuru ni amɛhe wa lɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops curling up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism crops use to protect themselves from heat by reducing moisture loss through evaporation.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why did some of the seeds I buried in the dirt fail to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mifu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛko lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep, if the soil is dried out or flooded, or if insects damaged the seeds before sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi loo nu eyi mli obɔ loo kɛji kooloi bibii kpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What will happen if I plant my crops too close together to save space in my field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ koni mikɛ he ko akafee nɔ ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crowding forces plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, weak stems and small, poor yields.
ga: Nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Weeds are hardy wild plants adapted to quickly steal water and nutrients from the soil, which is why early clearing gives your main crop a fair chance.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni kɛ́ ojie lɛ mra lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni sa lɛ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes dark spots to spread across my crop leaves after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ?

english: Rainwater splashes fungal spores from the wet soil onto plant leaves, where warm and damp conditions encourage diseases to spread.
ga: Nugbɔ nu shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tsei baai anɔ. Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ woɔ helai srɔtoi ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil or attract insects even after I dry them under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo egbalaa kooloi kɛbaa amɛmli eyɛ mli akɛ migbiɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ?

english: If grains retain hidden moisture deep inside or are stored in unsealed bags, mold can develop and hidden insect eggs can hatch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmaa to ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee mli shɔŋŋ loo akɛto kotokui ni atsĩ mli lɛ amli lɛ, Fungus baanyɛ aba ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ awui baanyɛ afɔ.

english: If the rains start falling in March, does that mean I should start planting my crops immediately?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ March mli Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Not always. Early March rains can be brief 'false rains' followed by dry spells. It is best to wait until the soil stays consistently moist over several days so your newly planted seeds do not dry up and die.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be, March shishijee nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee ‘amale nugbɔ’ kuku ni hulutsoo be nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ gbii babaoo. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do some regions in Ghana get two rainy seasons in a year while other parts get only one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Ghana kpokpai komɛi anɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni hei krokomɛi Nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Southern Ghana experiences a bimodal rainfall pattern, meaning it gets two distinct rainy seasons (major and minor), whereas Northern Ghana has a unimodal pattern with only one long rainy season before the dry season begins.
ga: Ghana wuoyigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ bei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ yɔɔ (shishijee kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ), yɛ be mli ni Ghana kooyigbɛ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kome ni nugbɔ be kakadaŋŋ kome pɛ yɔɔ mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: What happens to my maize if I plant it too late in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji midu lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Late-planted crops run out of water before they finish growing. If the rains end while the maize is flowering or forming grains, the plants will produce smaller ears or fail completely.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ nu baaho dani amɛgbe amɛdumɔ naa. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi loo eedu dumɔwui lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baatsɔ bibii loo ebaagbee shi kwraa.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough water after the first rains for me to start planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui?

english: You can dig a small hole about hand-depth into the soil, grab a handful, and squeeze it. If it forms a loose ball without water dripping out, the moisture level is just right for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa bu bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha ekwɔ tamɔ onineshi. Kɛkɛ ni ekɔ nine kome ni ekɛmimɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etse ehe ni nu ejɛɛɛ mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ sa kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops start turning yellow when there is too much rain on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive water fills up all the small air spaces in the soil, drowning the roots. Without oxygen, the roots cannot absorb nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow and droop.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How can I protect my crops from drying out if the rains suddenly stop for a few weeks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa otsii fioo komɛi?

english: You can practice mulching by covering the bare soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves. This acts as a blanket that traps moisture in the soil and keeps root temperatures cool.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mulching atsu nii kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni oooha ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai ŋmɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni haa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow so much faster during the early rainy season compared to when I water them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Kɛ akɛto nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Rainwater contains natural nitrogen absorbed from the atmosphere, which acts like a mild natural fertilizer, prompting rapid leaf and stem growth.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo Haa baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ daa oya

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my farm right before a heavy rain comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, heavy rainfall will wash the fertilizer off the field before the plant roots can absorb it. It is better to apply fertilizer after light rain when the soil is already damp.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow faster than my main crops as soon as the rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep root systems that react immediately to rain, allowing them to steal water and soil nutrients much faster than young crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni wa ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why do pests and insects suddenly increase on my crops during the warm, rainy months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo trukaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures combined with high moisture create the perfect environment for insect eggs to hatch quickly, while tender new leaves provide abundant food for them.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo fataa he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi akui lɛ baanyɛ afɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa amɛ niyenii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. They need shade from bigger trees or plantains to keep the air cool and soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my growing maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil that helps crops stay green and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni wa.

english: Why do people tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for crops like maize that need a lot of soil food.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni he hiaa shikpɔŋ mli niyenii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I put four or five maize seeds in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ wo bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing stalks fight each other for water, light, and nutrients, resulting in thin plants with small or no corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsoi ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la kɛ niyenii, ni no haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa bibii loo ŋmãa ko kwraa baa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible, which gives the plant energy to build large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or dry, or if the soil lacks consistent moisture, causing the plant to drop blossoms to save water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ Gbalamɔ tomato tsei lɛ koni nu akafite.

english: Why do my mature cassava tubers begin to rot if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei ni eda lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in the soil starves the underground cassava roots of air, encouraging fungi to grow and cause root rot.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii yɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on tender young leaves in the funnel of the maize plant, which can destroy the crop if not treated early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why do weeds in my pepper farm cause the pepper fruits to stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ pepper aduawai bibii lɛ dalɛ baa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizers, and sunlight away from your pepper plants, leaving the crop stressed and lacking energy to make large, healthy peppers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛnáaa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why should I spread dry grass on top of the soil around my garden crops in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi mashwã shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Dry grass acts as a blanket (mulch) that shades the soil, keeps moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, and keeps root zones cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. (Mulch) Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ latsaa be mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and die when I carry them from the nursery to my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings lose water quickly through their leaves and suffer severe stress when exposed to wind and hot air during transport. Keeping their roots moist and covered during the journey prevents them from drying out.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛnaa haomɔ ni naa wa kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛkɛ amɛ yaa lɛ. Kɛ́ aha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni aha nɔ yɛ gbɛfaa mli lɛ, ehaaa amɛgbi.

english: Why do some farmers put young seedlings inside plastic bags with water before moving them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ dumɔwui bibii woɔ plastic kotokui amli ni nu yɔɔ mli dani amɛjieɔ amɛ kɛyaa he kroko lɛ?

english: The plastic bag traps moisture around the roots, creating a humid environment that keeps the plant hydrated and prevents the root system from dying while being moved to the field.
ga: Plastic kotokui mɔ̃ɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni haa tsei lɛ náa nu, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ gboiɔ beni ajieɔ amɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I leave my crop roots exposed to open air and sunshine before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tso shishifãi lɛ woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli dani miduɔ lɛ?

english: Tiny root hairs absorb water for the plant, and exposing them directly to heat and wind dries them out within minutes, making it hard for the plant to survive once planted.
ga: Shishifãi bibii lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛhaa tso lɛ. Ni kɛ́ okɛwo dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha yitsɔi lɛ agbi yɛ minitii fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso lɛ akɛ ebaahi shi kɛji adu lɛ pɛ.

english: Is it good to let my seedlings rest in a shaded spot before I plant them into the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaaha dumɔwui lɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Yes, giving seedlings a break in a cool shade lets them recover from the shock and physical stress of transportation before they face the hard soil environment.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ hejɔɔmɔ ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shoofeemɔ kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ haomɔ ni jɛɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ lɛlɛ mli kɛbaa lɛ mli dani amɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and yellow for a few days after I move them to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock. The roots are temporarily disturbed and cannot absorb nutrients properly, but the plant will bounce back once new root tips start growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Akɛ shishifãi lɛ haoɔ be kukuoo ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shi tso lɛ baaku esɛɛ kɛji shishifãi heei bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves to hide from the harsh sun and reduce the surface area exposed to heat, which helps them hold onto water and avoid drying out.
ga: Tso lɛ shwieɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛtee ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni eha he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ aba shi Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaaa amɛgbi.

english: How does keeping water at the bottom of a transport container help a seedling stay fresh?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akɛtoɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ lɛlɛ mli lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: The water creates constant humidity around the roots, allowing the seedling to keep drawing up moisture to replace what is lost through evaporation.
ga: Nu lɛ haa hulutsoo be fɛɛ be bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ gbalaa hulutsoo kɛbaa koni ekɛye nɔ ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa and vegetable plants need shade when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei kɛ tsei bibii he hiaa hulutsoo beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Young plants have delicate leaves that burn under direct tropical sunlight. Shade trees or covers keep the environment cool and retain soil moisture while the plants build strength.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shishi. Tsei haa hulutsoo loo wɔɔhe, amɛhaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ maa hewalɛ emaa shi lɛ.

english: Why do seeds grow faster in small nursery bags than when I plant them straight into the big farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli lɛ daa oya fe be mli ni miduɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ agbo ko mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Nursery bags keep rich soil, fertilizers, and water concentrated around the young roots while protecting them from weed competition and soil pests.
ga: Grow bags haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ nii, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni bɔleɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ akaŋshii ni jɛɔ jwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops stop growing when the ground gets dry, even if the leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo moŋ.

english: Plants rely on water pressure inside their stems to stretch their cells and grow taller; when soil moisture drops, cell growth stops until the plant gets water again.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ koni amɛha amɛmli wala yibii lɛ asɛɛ atsɛ ni amɛdara. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi lɛ, wala yibii lɛ adalɛ kpaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ naa nu ekoŋŋ.

english: If my crops fail this season after I spent money on fertilizer, will my land still be good for planting next year?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite yɛ be nɛɛ mli beni mifite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ hu? Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi lolo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, your land remains usable. Fertilizer nourishes the soil for the active crop, but even if the harvest fails due to low rain, nutrients and organic matter remain in the soil to assist your next crop cycle.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii lolo. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi kɛji akɛ kpamɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aya nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ hewɔ lɛ, Nutrients kɛ organic matter baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua bo yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: What happens to my soil if I leave the farm to rest for a season after a bad harvest?
ga: Mɛni baa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be ko yɛ kpamɔ ni ehiii sɛɛ?

english: Leaving land to rest (fallowing) allows wild plants and soil organisms to naturally restore nitrogen, organic matter, and moisture back into the ground, making it richer for future planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe (ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ) lɛ haa koo mli tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa nitrogen, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa efeɔ nɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛha wɔsɛɛ dumɔ.

english: Why do crops grow very well on one section of my farm but do poorly on another section of the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli lɛ? Shi ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ fã kroko mli.

english: Soil properties vary across the same farm. Some sections hold water better, while sloped parts lose topsoil and fertilizer nutrients to water runoff during heavy rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. Hei komɛi hiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ laajeɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ koni amɛho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Fertilizer acts like food for plants by supplying essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that soil lacks, helping plants build strong roots, greener leaves, and larger fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ lɛ ni ekɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni shishifãi ni wa, baai eŋɔli, kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Will applying fertilizer guarantee me a big harvest even if the rains are small?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa anáa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ po?

english: No, fertilizer requires water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. If rainfall is too low, plants cannot use the applied fertilizer effectively, which limits crop growth.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ nu koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ faaa tsɔ Tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ afee mlɛo.

english: How long after spreading fertilizer on my field should I see changes in my plants?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mana tsakemɔi yɛ mi tsei lɛ amli beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You will usually see plants turn greener and show faster growth within 1 to 2 weeks after fertilizer application, provided there is enough moisture in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, obaana tsei ni etsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara oya yɛ otsi 1 kɛyashi 2 mli yɛ be mli ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my maize is fully matured and ready to harvest before all the leaves dry up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa dani baai lɛ fɛɛ agbi?

english: Peel back the green husk and check the grains. If pressing a grain with your fingernail leaves a firm mark and a small dark spot (black layer) appears at the base of the kernel, the maize is mature.
ga: Gbalamɔ hewolo ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ni okwɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ onineshi nibii nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa okadii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii (black layers) jeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce small yields even when I use good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kpakpai tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Good seeds need adequate soil nutrients, proper spacing, weed management, and sufficient water. If any of these elements are missing, the plant cannot reach its full yield potential.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai hia niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. jwɛi ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ ni sa kɛ nu ni fa Kɛji nibii nɛɛ bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ajie amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kpo.

english: If I do not have enough money for full fertilizer, should I put a little bit on my whole farm or full strength on a small area?
ga: Kɛji akɛ obɛ shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ani esa akɛ okɛ fioo afata ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ he loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ afata he bibioo ko?

english: It is better to apply the correct full dose on a smaller area. Spreading too little fertilizer over a large area means no plant gets enough nourishment to yield properly.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ dalɛ ni ja lɛ awo he ko bibioo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ wo he ko ni da lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I protect my farm from heavy financial loss if the rain fails during the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ shika babaoo ni baafite kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ mli?

english: Reduce risk by planting crop varieties that tolerate drought, mixing different crops together (intercropping), and staggering planting dates so a single dry spell does not destroy your entire investment.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ oshara ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shi kɛtsɔ tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Futumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii (ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsakeɔ) ni okɛ gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ atsake bɔni afee ni hulutsoo be kome pɛ akafite oshika fɛɛ ni okɛwo mli lɛ.

english: How long will it take for my new cashew trees to start producing fruit after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-cashew tso hee lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cashew trees are relatively fast-yielding tree crops. With proper care and improved varieties, a young cashew tree usually starts bearing its first fruits within 2 to 3 years.
ga: Cashew tsei ji tsei ni woɔ yibii oya. Kɛtsɔ kwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ srɔtoi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei bibii jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli.

english: How do I know if my land is good for growing cashews?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha cashew ŋmeii akwɛmɔ?

english: Cashews prefer well-drained sandy or loamy soils and warm weather. They thrive very well in the transition and savanna zones of Ghana where there is a distinct dry season.
ga: Cashew ŋmeii sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã loo sũ yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni edɔɔ lɛ. Ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ghana hei ni hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: What is the very first step I should take before I start planting cashew seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ ni esa akɛ mafee dani mabɔi cashew dumɔwui dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should clear the land, mark out proper spacing—usually 7 to 10 meters apart—and dig planting holes enriched with topsoil and compost before bringing seedlings to the field.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Kadimɔ he ni sa akɛ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 7 kɛyashi 10—ni otsa dumɔwui ni akɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efata he lɛ mli dani okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Does growing cashew require a lot of hard daily labor once the trees grow big?
ga: Ani cashew ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ ni wa daa gbi kɛji tsei lɛ dara pɛ?

english: No, mature cashew trees are hardy and low-maintenance. Once established, your main tasks will be seasonal weed control, light pruning of dead branches, and protecting the farm from dry-season fires.
ga: Dabi, cashew tsei ni eda lɛ wa ni amɛhe ehiaaa ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji ato shishi pɛ Onitsumɔ titri ji ni okwɛ jwɛi ni baa be mli lɛ anɔ. Niji ni egboi lɛ ni afolɔ fioo kɛ ŋmɔji ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ la he yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Yes, intercropping with food crops like maize, cowpeas, or groundnuts works well during the first 2 to 3 years while the cashew trees are small, giving you food and income while keeping weeds under control.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni cashew tsei lɛ ji bibii. Ha niyenii kɛ shika kɛ agbɛnɛ hu jwɛi akudɔmɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cashew plants turning yellow and dropping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal water stress—either waterlogging around the roots from poor drainage or extreme dry spells—or a lack of key soil nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ nu mli haomɔ. Kɛji eji nu ni ahiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa lɛ hewɔ. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen

english: Why do my young cashew seedlings grow very slowly even though I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cashew nut tsei lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛdaraaa moŋ? Ni mikɛ nu ewo mli?

english: Slow growth happens if the soil is too hard for roots to push through, if the seedlings are planted in shade instead of full sunlight, or if weeds are competing with them for nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wa tsɔ ni shishifãi nyɛŋ akwɛ̃. aloo kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ fe ni amɛaana hulutsoo be fɛɛ. Aloo kɛji jwɛi kɛ amɛ miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of my cashew flowers dry up and drop without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flower drop is mostly caused by insect pests like tea mosquito bugs, fungal diseases during foggy mornings, or severe water stress right when the tree starts flowering.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ Aedes ŋmeii, tii ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii helai yɛ afua be mli leebi. loo nu he haomɔ ni naa wa beni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi lɛ.

english: How do I protect my young tree crops from bushfires during the harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ koo mli la he yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli?

english: Create a wide firebreak by clearing a strip of bare land around the boundary of your farm, and keep weeds cleared from the base of each tree before the dry season starts.
ga: Bɔɔ la line ni mli kwɔ kɛtsɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ ni oootsi lɛ nɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ husui ni ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ tso fɛɛ tso shishi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: How can I tell when the cashews on my tree are fully ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ cashews ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ eshɛ he kwraa kɛha kpamɔɔ?

english: Cashews are mature when the fruit apple turns bright yellow or red and naturally drops to the ground. You should pick up the fallen fruit promptly so the nuts do not spoil.
ga: Cashews lɛ eda kwraa kɛ́ apple lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni egbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Esa akɛ oŋɔ aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Is it better to give my crops liquid fertilizer through their water or use solid fertilizer on the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ matsɔ nu nɔ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu loo mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa baatsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Liquid fertilizer mixed with water is absorbed by plant roots much faster than solid fertilizer, giving young crops immediate food to grow strong.
ga: Nu ni akɛfutuɔ nu mli lɛ, tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Can I give my young seedlings a small amount of liquid fertilizer every day, or will it burn them?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha dumɔwui bibii lɛ nu fioo ko ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii daa gbi? Aloo ebaashã?

english: Giving seedlings a very weak, diluted liquid fertilizer daily provides a steady supply of nutrients without burning or damaging their delicate young roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni bɛ hewalɛ waa ha dumɔwui lɛ daa gbi lɛ, ebaaha amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ daa ni amɛshãaa loo amɛfiteee shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: How does using a water tank to feed my nursery plants help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli ni mikɛhaa midumɔwui lɛ niyenii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: A water tank allows you to mix liquid fertilizer evenly so every single seedling gets the exact same amount of food and water every day.
ga: Nu tsɛnsi lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ futuɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, no hewɔ lɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu nine shɛɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ daa gbi.

english: Why is it important to pull out tiny weeds as soon as they sprout around my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi bibii lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ? Beni eda ni ebɔle mi tso bibioo lɛ he pɛ kɛkɛ

english: Tiny weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from your crops right when they are weakest, so removing them immediately gives your crops full access to nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi bibii juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛshɛɔ he ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will weeds really harm my young crops if I wait a few weeks before clearing them?
ga: Ani jwɛi lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ kɛji mimɛ otsii fioo komɛi dani mikɛjie?

english: Yes, weeds usually grow faster than crop seedlings and will quickly shade your plants from the sun and drink up all the soil moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi daa oya fe tsei dumɔwui. Ni ebaaha otsei lɛ afee hulutsoo oya ni ebaaŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just plant my crop seeds directly into the main field instead of using a nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe baatsu nii?

english: A nursery protects delicate seeds and small sprouts from harsh sun, heavy rains, and pests until they grow strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: How long should my young seedlings stay in the nursery before I move them to the farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Most crop seedlings need about two to three months in a nursery to build a sturdy root system and strong stem before facing field conditions.
ga: Tso dumɔwui babaoo he miihia aaafee nyɔji enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli koni amɛto shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa ama shi dani amɛyaje ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi amli.

english: How do I know when my seedling has reached its 'true leaf' stage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midumɔwui lɛ eshɛ ‘anɔkwa baa’ lɛ he?

english: The very first leaves that sprout are simple seed leaves; true leaves appear right after them and look like smaller versions of the full-grown crop's real leaves.
ga: Baa klɛŋklɛŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ ji dumɔwu baa ni sa. Anɔkwale baai jeɔ kpo yɛ amɛsɛɛ ni amɛtamɔ tsei bibii ni eda lɛ ahe baai diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why should I wait until my seedlings grow true leaves before transplanting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni midumɔwui lɛ aná baai diɛŋtsɛ dani mikɛ amɛ awo he kroko?

english: Plants with true leaves have developed strong roots and can create their own food through sunlight, which helps them survive being moved.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ baai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjoɔ tsɔne ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ naa foi.

english: Why do my young plants sometimes wither and die right after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock when moved; waiting until they reach the proper leaf stage and keeping them well-watered helps them survive the move.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ naa piŋmɔ kɛjɛɔ transplant shock mli kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ tee. Kɛ́ amɛmɛ kɛyashi amɛshɛ baa lɛ fã ni sa lɛ he, ni oooha amɛ nu bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ shimɔ lɛ mli.

english: How many years do I have to wait after planting a mango seedling before the tree starts giving fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ odu mango dumɔwu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Grafted mango seedlings usually start bearing fruit within 3 to 4 years, whereas trees planted directly from seed can take 7 to 10 years. Grafted seedlings reach maturity much faster and guarantee high-quality fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 7 kɛyashi 10. Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ daa oya kwraa ni ehaa yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my fruit trees very close to each other on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ aduawai tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting trees too closely makes them fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, weak trees that produce small harvests and spread diseases easily between branches.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa onáa tso kakadaŋŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa niji ateŋ oya.

english: Why do small mango fruits drop off my tree before they are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Young fruits drop off mainly when the tree lacks water, faces pest attacks, or lacks proper soil nutrients. Giving the tree sufficient water during dry spells and protecting it from pests keeps the fruit on the tree until harvest.
ga: Yibii bibii babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu bɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ kpeɔ loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why does my fruit tree bloom with many flowers, but very few of them turn into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso yibii lɛ miifɔ kɛ fɔfɔii babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Heavy rain or intense heat during flowering can damage pollen, and a lack of bees or insects prevents flower pollination. Without proper pollination, flowers dry up and fall off without producing fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo latsaa ni naa wa waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afite fɔfɔi lɛ. Ni ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii ni bɛ lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ anaa. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Do mature mango trees need water during the dry season, or can they rely on rain alone?
ga: Ani mango tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli loo amɛbaadamɔ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ?

english: While older mango trees have deep roots to survive dry periods, watering them when flowers and young fruits are forming prevents fruit drop and ensures bigger, juice-filled fruit.
ga: Mango tsei ni edara lɛ po yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Shi nu ni oooha fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ darako lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ akagbee shi ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ adara ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ nu.

english: What simple steps can I take to make sure my crops produce high yields that fetch good market prices?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii babaoo ni maná jara kpakpa?

english: Pruning dead branches to let in sunlight, removing weeds regularly, controlling pests, and applying manure or fertilizer at flowering time ensures your trees produce large, healthy fruits that sell at premium prices.
ga: Niji ni egboi lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la atsɔ mli Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa. pest control Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Enɛ baaha otso lɛ awo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ.

english: Why is it important to cut off some branches from my fruit trees, and when should I do it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ niji komɛi lɛ? Ni mɛɛ be esa akɛ mafee?

english: Cutting off unwanted branches, known as pruning, lets air and sunlight flow through the tree. This prevents fungal diseases and directs the tree's energy into growing fruit rather than excess leaves. It is best done right after harvest.
ga: Niji ni ataooo lɛ ni afoɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ewo yibii moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ baai babaoo. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ afee yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can I plant crops like maize or vegetables between my young mango trees while waiting for them to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai yɛ mi mango tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, this is called intercropping. Planting low-growing crops like legumes or vegetables between young trees gives you food and income while the trees mature, without harming the fruit trees as long as you keep a small space clear around each trunk.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ intercropping. Nibii ni shwereɔ fioo tamɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai adumɔ Yɛ tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ obaaná niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ. ni oyeee aduawai tsei lɛ awui Shii abɔ ni okɛ he bibioo ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ bɔleɔ tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he lɛ.

english: What causes dark spots on my mangoes while they are still on the tree, and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa mango nɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ? Ni te ooofee tɛŋŋ otsĩ naa?

english: Dark spots are usually caused by fungal infections like anthracnose, which thrive in high humidity and shade. Pruning branches to improve airflow and clearing fallen leaves from the farm floor prevents fungi from spreading to the fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ anthracnose, ni yaa hiɛ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ baa. Tsei ni afoɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya mli jogbaŋŋ, kɛ baai ni egbee shi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã aduawai amli.

english: If your plant leaves turn yellow, growth seems slow, or fruit production drops despite good weather, your soil is running low on nutrients and requires organic manure or chemical fertilizers to rebuild its strength.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ Eyaa hiɛ fiofio loo ebaa shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ hi po. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ awo mli koni enyɛ etswa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tree crops taking so long to bear fruit when my neighbor's maize was ready in just three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa lɛ eshɛɔ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different crops have different growth speeds. Fast crops like maize or vegetables finish their life cycle in a few months, while tree crops like cocoa, citrus, or palm build strong trunks and deep root systems first, which can take several years before they can produce fruit.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai baagbe amɛwala shihilɛ naa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei tamɔ kookoo, citrus, loo palm lɛ feɔ tsei ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ ahe afii babaoo dani ewo yibii.

english: Can I do anything to make my slow-growing crops bear fruit in six months instead of waiting for years?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee nɔ ko koni mitsei ni miida blɛoo lɛ awo yibii yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli moŋ fe ni mamɛ afii babaoo?

english: You cannot bypass a plant's natural growth period. While good water and soil nutrition can keep a plant healthy and growing at its best speed, perennial crops naturally require one to three years or more to reach maturity.
ga: Onyɛŋ otsi tso lɛ dalɛ be lɛ naa. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ nu mli niyenii kpakpai yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛdaraa oya moŋ, shi tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ biɔ afii kome kɛyashi etɛ loo nɔ ni fe nakai yɛ adebɔɔ naa dani amɛshɛɔ dalɛ he.

english: Why do my crops seem to stop growing during the dry season even when I water them occasionally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu yɛ bei komɛi amli moŋ lɛ?

english: Plants need continuous moisture, moderate temperatures, and nutrients to grow quickly. During dry spells, intense sun and dry soil force the plant to enter a survival mode, slowing its growth to save energy until good rain or moisture returns.
ga: Tsei lɛ hia ŋmɔtɔ daa. Temperature ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baakwɛ̃ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Hulu babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Dalɛ blɛoo koni akɛto hewalɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ loo fɛ̃i baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What does it mean to feed my crops well before I expect a big harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ mahã miŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ dani makpa ŋmaa babaoo gbɛ?

english: Feeding crops means giving the soil enough food—such as animal manure, compost, or chemical fertilizer—so roots can absorb essential nutrients. Just like farm animals need food to grow fat, crops need rich soil to grow strong leaves and heavy fruits.
ga: Tsei niyenii tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Taakɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi he hiaa niyenii koni amɛná fɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why should I add manure or fertilizer to the soil before planting instead of waiting until the crops appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: Adding nutrients to the soil before planting ensures that as soon as the young roots sprout, they immediately find food. If you wait too long, young plants can become weak or stunted in their early weeks, which delays their growth later.
ga: Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani aduɔ lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ pɛ kɛkɛ ni amɛna niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji omɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ekolɛ tsei bibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ loo amɛbaagbɔjɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha sɛɛ mli lɛ, edalɛ aya hiɛ blɛoo.

english: How is feeding plants with fertilizer similar to feeding livestock on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa lɛ tamɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii?
