english: Farm animals need regular balanced food to build meat and milk, and plants operate the same way. When you give plants proper soil nutrients, they build strong stems, healthy leaves, and disease resistance needed to produce high crop yields.
ga: Niyenii ni ja ni ŋmɔ mli kooloi yeɔ daa koni amɛná loo kɛ mliki. Ni tsei hu feɔ amɛnii nakai nɔŋŋ. Kɛji okɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ha tsei lɛ Tsei lɛ baaná ŋmeii ni wa, baai ni wa kɛ helai ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: If a crop has stopped growing for months and looks weak, can it still be saved or is it a complete loss?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpa shweremɔ nyɔji babaoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ Ani abaanyɛ abu he loo ebaafee nɔ ni elaaje kwraa?

english: If a crop is stunted simply because of poor soil food or temporary dry weather, adding fertilizer and water can revive it. However, if the plant is severely ruined by root disease or bad breeding, it may be a total loss and should be replaced.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛkɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ shishifãi hela loo fɔmɔ ni ehiii lɛ efite tso lɛ waa. Ekolɛ elaaje kwraa ni esa akɛ akɛto najiaŋ.

english: If some of my young plants look sickly while others are growing well, should I clear the weak ones away?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi miida jogbaŋŋ lolo hu? Ani esa akɛ majie tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe?

english: Yes, if weak plants show signs of disease or pest infestation, removing them protects the remaining healthy crops from catching the same sickness. It also allows you to focus your water and manure on the healthy plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ jie hela loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe okadi kpo. Nakai tsei lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe koni amɛkaná hela kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebua bo hu ni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ maa onu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning pale yellow and failing to expand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the crop is hungry, usually lacking nitrogen in the soil, or that the roots are drowning in too much water or dried out from drought. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer usually helps green them up.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ ebote nu babaoo mli loo amɛgbi yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Is it better for my farm income to plant crops that mature quickly or crops that take years to grow?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔ mli shika lɛ akɛ makwɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo tsei ni heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Mixing both is usually best. Quick crops like maize, cassava, or vegetables give you food and fast cash within months, while long-term crops like cocoa, cashew, or oil palm take years to start but provide steady income for decades.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nibii enyɔ nɛɛ ni akɛfutuɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo aduawai baanyɛ aha oná niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo kɛ cashew nuts loo palm oil Heɔ afii babaoo dani ejeɔ shishi shi ehaa shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why should I leave wide space between my cassava mounds instead of packing them closely together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ ato he kome ni ebɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need room to expand underground, and leaves need sunlight to make food. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough light, air, and soil space to produce large tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia he ko ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni hulu la he miihia baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs agboi.

english: Why do my crops grow well in the first year after clearing the bush, but get weaker every year after that?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni mijie ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ? Shi ani egbɔjɔɔ daa afi yɛ no sɛɛ?

english: Plants consume nutrients from the soil like food. Continuous planting without adding compost or fertilizer drains the soil of its nutrients, making subsequent crops weak.
ga: Tsei heɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tamɔ niyenii pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ baaje mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do officers recommend that I plant beans or groundnuts in my field before planting maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu ŋmeii yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they naturally fertilize the soil for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ bii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do some farmers cover the ground around crop roots with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa he ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating, and protects topsoil from being washed away by heavy rain.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsi nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akaho.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look yellow and small even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. If weeds are not removed early, they steal the food your crops need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Trimming unnecessary side leaves stops the plant from wasting energy on foliage, allowing it to direct its food and water into growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ, no haaa tso lɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ niyenii kɛ nu woɔ yibii wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of just saving seeds from last harvest to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni madu?

english: Certified seeds are developed by agricultural scientists to resist common local diseases, survive tough weather, and yield more food compared to saved seeds that lose strength over time.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi efee dumɔwui ni aŋmala he odaseyeli lɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Hiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa mli ni ewo yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ato ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does my maize fail when the rain stops unexpectedly, and how can science help?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jeŋ nilee baanyɛ aye abua?

english: Maize requires water at critical growing stages like flowering. Improved seed varieties developed through science mature faster and tolerate dry spells, helping crops survive sudden changes in rainfall patterns.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa yɛ dalɛ bei titrii tamɔ fɔfɔii amli. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔ jeŋ nilee nɔ afee lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi trukaa tsakemɔi yɛ nugbɔ henɔi amli.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to suddenly eat holes through all my young maize leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye buji kɛyashi amɛbaayi mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm lay hundreds of eggs that hatch quickly and feed voraciously on young leaves. Checking your farm regularly allows you to catch and treat them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ ni fɔɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii kɛ ŋmiŋmi. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ daa lɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ amɛ ni otsaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa creates a canopy that protects tender cocoa trees from harsh sun and keeps soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do I need to make big soil mounds before I plant my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa shikpɔŋ ŋmɔ agbo dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth so they can expand easily deep underground. High mounds provide well-drained, uncompacted soil for root growth and prevent heavy rainfall from waterlogging and rotting the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ oya. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ. ni etsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha nu afua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ egbo.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away, or the soil may be exhausted from continuous planting without adding manure or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afite kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience temperature or water stress, such as when the weather is too hot or the roots are either too dry or flooded with too much water.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be loo nu mli haomɔ he, tamɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Aloo shishifãi lɛ egbi tsɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ mli.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which crawl deep into the central funnel of the maize plant where the youngest, softest leaves are protected from heat and birds while they feed.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni abuɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ okpoi ahe be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller harvests even if there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the plant food, water, and sunlight that your crops need. Even with good rain, crops cannot grow big if neighboring weeds are taking away nutrients from the soil.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsei lɛ aniyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Shi Dumɔwui hu nyɛŋ adara babaoo kɛji jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ miihe niyenii kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, which naturally feeds and fertilizes nearby maize plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa amɛmli ŋmãa

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even after growing for over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛji bibii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ nɔ ni fe afi eho kɛjɛ be mli ni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot expand in hard, packed soil or when planted too closely together. If cassava plants compete for light and space, energy goes into growing top leaves instead of thick tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ loo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei kɛ amɛhe miitswa la kɛ ŋwɛi he akaŋ lɛ Hewalɛ yaa ŋwɛi baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ mli yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant maize on the exact same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot exhausts the exact nutrients maize needs and allows specific pests and diseases that target maize to build up in the soil year after year.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baafite. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why did the seeds I stored in a sack from my last harvest fail to grow when planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kotoku lɛ mli kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can die if exposed to damp air or excessive heat during storage, or if invisible weevils damaged the seed embryo inside before planting day.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ agbo kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ mli loo dɔlɛ ni fe nine mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmei ko ni anaaa lɛ fite dumɔwu lɛ mli fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ dani gbi ni akɛduɔ lɛ shɛ.

english: Cabbage needs cool temperatures, steady water, and the right soil nutrients to form tight heads. Giving the plant too much nitrogen fertilizer late in its growth causes it to keep producing loose leaves instead of closing into a solid head.
ga: Kaabaji he miihia hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ, nu ni damɔ shi, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa koni ekɛfee yitsei ni mli edɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná baai ni etsilɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee mɛi ni bɛ jwɛŋmɔ lɛ,.

english: Why is my lettuce growing very tall and flowering, and why does it taste bitter now?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-lettuce lɛ daa ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ amrɔ nɛɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ?

english: When the weather gets too hot or water is low, lettuce tries to produce seeds quickly before it dies. This process makes the stems stretch upwards and fills the leaves with a bitter sap, showing the crop is past its fresh eating stage.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ, Lettuce baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ dumɔwui awo oya dani egbo. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛyiɔ baai lɛ amli kɛ nu ni mli edɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ etsɔ niyeli hee gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: In high sun, vegetable leaves lose water through evaporation faster than their roots can drink it from the ground. Covering the soil around the crops with dry grass or leaves keeps the roots cool and holds moisture in the ground longer.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, aduawai ahe baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ŋmɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cabbage and lettuce turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage kɛ lettuce baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which gives leafy vegetables their green color, or that too much water around the roots is suffocating the plant so it cannot absorb plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni haa aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo nu ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii.

english: What happens to my cabbage and lettuce if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cabbage kɛ mi-lettuce lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When leafy vegetables are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients. This struggle leaves all the crops small, weak, and more likely to get sick or attacked by pests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ta nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo, egbɔjɔ, ni hela baamɔ amɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baatutua amɛ.

english: Why do my lettuce seeds take much longer to sprout during the hot dry season than during cooler months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-lettuce dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nyɔji ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Lettuce seeds naturally go dormant and refuse to germinate when the soil gets too hot. Shading your nursery bed with palm fronds and watering regularly keeps the soil cool enough for seeds to wake up and grow.
ga: Lettuce dumɔwui lɛ yaa wɔɔ ni amɛkpooɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsei wo ŋmei saatso lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ ateshi ni amɛdara.

english: What causes small round holes in my cabbage leaves, and how does it hurt my crop yield?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ baa? yɛ mi-cabbage baa lɛ nɔ Ni te enaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes are usually made by caterpillars or small beetles eating the foliage. Leaves act as the plant's food factories using sunlight, so losing leaf area slows growth and makes the cabbage look unappealing to market buyers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa. Baai tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei aniyenii nitsumɔhei ni kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, baa lɛ he ni elaaje lɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Ni enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔɔ kaabii.

english: Why are the stems of my young vegetable seedlings rotting right at the soil level and falling over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miifite kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: This condition is caused by soil fungi that thrive in overly wet soil with poor airflow. Keeping the seedling nursery moist but not waterlogged helps protect delicate stem tissues from rotting.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ jɛɔ sũ mli ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sũ ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ aya mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ahã dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i shi nu ehiɛɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ shishi fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my cabbage heads so they do not spoil quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kaabe yitsei lɛ koni amɛkafite oya?

english: A cabbage head is ready to pick when it feels firm and dense when squeezed gently. If left in the farm field too long after reaching full maturity, the head will split open and begin to rot.
ga: Kaaba yitsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛnu he akɛ amɛhe wa ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ ashɛ amɛhe blɛoo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ. Tubers lɛ mli baagbala ni amɛje shishi amɛgboi.

english: Why do my leafy vegetables grow smaller every season when I plant them on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ feɔ bibii daa be mli beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same vegetable continuously drains the specific soil nutrients that crop needs and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the earth. Swapping leafy greens with beans or groundnuts restores soil strength.
ga: Aduawai henɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do many farmers in Ghana tell me that cassava is a good crop for making money?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miikɛɛ mi akɛ ŋmei ji ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni akɛnáa shika lɛ?

english: Cassava is highly profitable because every part of the harvest can be sold, and it can be processed into shelf-stable food like gari, which sells for a stable price all year round.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi babaoo yɛ cassava he ejaakɛ abaanyɛ ahɔɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fã fɛɛ fã. Ni abaanyɛ afee niyenii ni anyɛɔ akɛtoɔ adeka mli, tamɔ gari, ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: If I want to produce gari to sell, what kind of cassava should I plant?
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni ofee curry ni ohɔ̃ɔ. Mɛɛ ŋmei esa akɛ madu?

english: You should ask extension officers for improved, high-starch cassava varieties, as these produce a much higher weight of gari after peeling and grating compared to standard water-heavy varieties.
ga: Esa akɛ obi extension officer lɛ ni eha bo ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni starch babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmei nɛɛ haa kari ni tsiimɔ fa babaoo baa yɛ be mli ni ajie amɛhe ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ ni nu babaoo heɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why is selling processed gari better for my income than selling fresh cassava tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ curry paste ni afee lɛ srɔtoi lɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ hi kɛha mishika fe ŋmei shishifãi heei ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Fresh cassava roots rot within a few days after harvest, forcing you to sell fast at cheap prices, whereas gari can be stored for months without spoiling until market prices go up.
ga: Kasava shishifãi heei lɛ baagboi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ oya ni jara waaa. Yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ akɛ gari ato nyɔji babaoo ni efiteee kɛyashi jara nɔ jara lɛ baaya hiɛ lɛ.

english: How long can cassava stay unharvested in the ground without going bad?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteee?

english: Cassava is unique because the roots act like living underground storage; they can safely stay in the soil for months until you are ready to harvest, process, or sell them.
ga: Cassava yɛ srɔto ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nibii ni akɛtoɔ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaakpa, otsu he nii, loo ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Can I plant maize on the same piece of land where my cassava is growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop maize with cassava because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, leaving space for the slow-growing cassava to expand later.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa gbɛ haa ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa sɛɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to grow both maize and cassava on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Growing both crops gives you double protection: maize provides quick food and early income in the season, while cassava provides a reliable, long-term food supply and income reserve.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa mɔ he buɔ shii enyɔ. Abele haa niyenii oya ni ehaa anáa shika yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei haa niyenii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛ shika ni akɛtoɔ he.

english: How do changing rainy and dry seasons affect maize compared to cassava?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hɔmɔ be ni tsakeɔ lɛ saa ŋmãa he ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he?

english: Maize is sensitive to dry weather and needs steady rain early on, whereas cassava is very hardy and can survive extended dry spells once its roots are established.
ga: Abɛi nuɔ he waa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa mra. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei wa waa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛji eshishifãi lɛ ema shi pɛ.

english: What should I plant if I want a quick harvest while waiting for long-term crops to mature?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ madu kɛji miitao nikpamɔ oya yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Maize is an ideal quick crop because it matures in about three to four months, giving you fast food and cash flow while longer-term crops like cassava take up to a year.
ga: Abele ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni kwɛɔ oya ejaakɛ ekwɛɔ yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Ehaa bo niyenii oya kɛ shika ni hoɔ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ baahi shi kɛyashi afi.

english: As a newcomer farming in this area, how do I know if my land is suitable for cassava?
ga: Ákɛ okwaafonyo hee yɛ nɛkɛ he nɛɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei?

english: Cassava grows well in most Ghanaian soils as long as the ground is well-drained and does not flood, because standing water causes the tubers to rot.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana shikpɔji lɛ ateŋ babaoo nɔ, kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ. Ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Which crop is safest to rely on if the weather becomes bad and rain is irregular?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ akɛ he afɔ nɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ mli wa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: Cassava is one of the safest crops during bad weather because its deep roots extract moisture from dry soil, securing your farm's food supply when other crops fail.
ga: Cassava ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli lɛ ateŋ ekome. Akɛni eshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ hewɔ lɛ, egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Koni okwɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ehiii.

english: Why do my crops die completely after I cut them back instead of growing fresh leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboi kwraa beni mifo mli yɛ baai heei ni makwɛ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Some crops store food reserves in their roots to sprout back after cutting, while others need their main stem and green leaves intact to produce energy. If you cut certain crops too close to the ground or at the wrong time, they lose all their energy reserves and die.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi kɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ beni amɛfo lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi biɔ tso titri kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji ofo ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni obɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔ loo yɛ be ni esaaa mli lɛ Tso lɛ laajeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ni egboɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is dying from too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii miigboi yɛ nu babaoo loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa hewɔ?

english: When crops do not get enough water, their leaves wilt, turn dry, and feel crisp to the touch. When they get too much water, the leaves turn yellow, soft, and the stem or roots may rot because excess water drowns the air in the soil.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baagboi, amɛbaagbi, ni amɛbaanu he akɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ amɛta he. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛbaafee bɔdɔɔ, ni shishifãi lɛ loo shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ afite be mli ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some new crop varieties survive dry heat while my local crops wither and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei No hewɔ lɛ tsei srɔtoi komɛi hiɔ shi yɛ latsaa kɛ hɔmɔ mli yɛ be mli ni mimaŋ tsei lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Drought-resistant crop varieties are specially bred with deeper roots, thicker leaves, or the ability to close their leaf pores during the hottest part of the day to hold onto moisture, allowing them to withstand harsh sun better than traditional seeds.
ga: Atsɔse tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, baai ni mli kwɔ, loo amɛnyɛ amɛŋa baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ fe dumɔwui krokomɛi.

english: Why do my plants sprout well at first but then suddenly collapse and die midway through the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishijee mli, shi trukaa lɛ efoɔ ni egboɔ yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This often happens due to soil-borne diseases or root rot. In the early stages, the plant uses energy stored in the seed to grow, but once the roots try to pull nutrients from infected or poorly drained soil, the damaged root system fails and the plant dies quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ hewɔ ni enɛ baa lɛ. Yɛ shishijee mli lɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ amɛdumɔwui amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara. Shi kɛ́ shishifãi bɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbala niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ loo ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Shishifãi ni efite lɛ baafee nɔ ni esaaa ni tso lɛ baagbo oya.

english: Is it better to water my crops a little bit every day or give them a lot of water once in a while?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu fioo daa gbi loo mahã amɛ nu babaoo? Bei komɛi?

english: It is generally better to water deeply once in a while because it encourages plant roots to grow deep into the soil looking for moisture. Shallow daily watering keeps roots near the surface where the sun quickly dries them out.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, nu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛhaa Bei komɛi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ daa gbi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ he ni hulu la baanyɛ aha amɛgbi oya lɛ.

english: How does hard or dry soil affect how my plants absorb water and nutrients?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ saa bɔ ni tsei lɛ nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ amɛhaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Hard, compacted soil prevents water from sinking in and stops young crop roots from spreading. Adding organic compost or farmyard manure softens the soil, making it act like a sponge that holds water and nutrients for roots to drink.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa nu abote mli, ni ehaa tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ afee blɛoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ enii tamɔ sponji ni kɛ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai toɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Which crops can regrow after I harvest them, and which ones do I have to replant completely?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ beni mikpa nii lɛ sɛɛ? Ni mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu ekoŋŋ fɛɛ?

english: Crops like cassava, sugar cane, and certain grasses can regrow from stumps or stem cuttings because they store food in their lower tissues, whereas annual crops like maize must be replanted from seeds every season after harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ jwɛi komɛi baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ehee kɛjɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ amli. Enɛ ji akɛ amɛ toɔ niyenii yɛ amɛ shishi fãji lɛ amli. yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ekoŋŋ daa afi ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa, daa be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ.

english: How do I choose the right crop variety to plant if my farm suffers from unpredictable rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei ni sa ni madu? Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ na nugbɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ hu?

english: Look for early-maturing or short-duration seed varieties. These varieties are developed to grow fast and produce yields before the rainy period ends, reducing the risk of crop failure during dry spells.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo ni hiɔ shi be kukuoo. Afee nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba naagbee. Enɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my young crops turn yellow and brown during the hot dry afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso ni nu egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme sun causes crops to lose water faster through their leaves than their young roots can pull from the soil. This heat stress damages leaf tissues, causing them to scorch, turn brown, and dry up.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ nɛɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. kɛ shãa baa Etsɔ blɔfo ni egbi

english: What can I put on my farm soil to stop water from drying up too fast in the heat?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves, straw, or grass—a practice called mulching—blocks direct sunlight, keeps the soil cool, and prevents water from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi ha onibii ahe—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient crops need for healthy green foliage. Applying compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer around the root area restores plant strength and boosts crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɔle Shishifã lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn under harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or leaving shade trees provides a natural canopy that shields young plants from heat and helps the soil retain moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ tsei bibii loo shade tsei ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli shade ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: What is eating small holes into the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ye bu bibioo ko ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, caterpillars that hide in the growing center of maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended organic remedies or targeted sprays directly into the leaf funnel prevents severe crop loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ waa lɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell if I am planting my cassava stem cuttings the right way into the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the tiny buds along the stem; they must point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down forces the plant to waste energy growing around itself, resulting in poor root growth and smaller yields.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Cassava ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛkwɛɔ ehe lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why does the soil around my vegetable garden dry out and crack so quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ he lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil cracks when direct sunlight bakes the bare ground and evaporates moisture rapidly. Covering the soil with a layer of dried leaves or dry grass acts as a protective blanket, keeping the soil cool and moist for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbo loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into any fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures stress tomato plants and destroy the pollen inside the flowers before fruit can form. Giving plants adequate water at the root level and providing light afternoon shade keeps them cool enough to produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ hulutsoo yɛ shwane mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my stored bean seeds get filled with tiny holes and dust before the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ sũ dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba

english: Insects called seed weevils lay eggs inside stored beans and eat their way out as they grow. Storing thoroughly dried seeds in airtight containers or mixing them with clean wood ash keeps oxygen out and stops pests from damaging the seeds.
ga: Kpluka ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ seed moth lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ amli ni eyeɔ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo akɛ tso sũ ni he tse futu mli lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ he, ni ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin with tiny ears when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɔɔ toi bibii beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving crops proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow thick stalks and produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants mature and decompose in the field, they release this natural fertilizer back into the soil for future crops to use.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔji amli Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do weeds make my cassava plants produce very small tubers even if I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi yucca tsei lɛ miifee ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, sunlight, and underground nutrients that your cassava roots need to expand. Regular weeding during the first few months allows the cassava plant to direct all its strength into growing large, healthy tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii ni he hiaa ni o-cassava shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ oya. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmei wuji ni mli wa ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or nurse crops like plantains to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni woɔ amɛbii, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. kɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed new growth at the top, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with thick green leaves but leaves me with tiny tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi kɛ́ akpa lɛ, eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are planted too close together, cassava spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the roots below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔ starch kɛ toɔ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why is it beneficial for my farm if I plant groundnuts in the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ he ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When planted alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil and make the maize grow better.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or irregular watering. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and keep itself alive.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ na tso lɛ he amanehulu. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛha amɛhe ahi wala mli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards and look wrinkled during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips that thrive in dry weather. Their feeding twists the leaves and can also transmit leaf-curl viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Amɛ niyenii lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ baa lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ eshwa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight gives the plant energy to make food, which travels down to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la haa tsei hewalɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding deep inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms. They crawl deep into the central leaf funnel because the tender growth inside is soft to eat and protects them from heat, rain, and predators.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Asraafoi ŋmeii. Amɛshwereɔ kɛyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni ayeɔ ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ, nugbɔ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the broad leaves on my plantain trees tear into narrow ribbons during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ gbálaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves tear along natural structural lines so that strong winds can pass right through them. This prevents the heavy wind from snapping the trunk or pulling the whole plant out of the soil.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ gbálaa yɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha lɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa atsɔ mli. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akatswa tso lɛ shishi loo ekagbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my rice crop need standing water in the field to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he hiaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Standing water acts as a natural barrier that chokes out weeds competing with the rice. It also keeps the soil temperature stable and ensures the roots always have moisture to uptake nutrients.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ jwɛi ni kɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ akaŋ lɛ anaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why should I water my crop nursery early in the morning or late in the evening instead of during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mibii akwɛmɔhe lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ moŋ fe shwane?

english: Watering during the cool parts of the day allows the crop roots to absorb the water fully. In the intense afternoon sun, most of the water evaporates before roots can drink it, and hot water drops on leaves can burn the tender plant.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ shwane hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Nu lɛ mli babaoo shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are suffering from drought or if they are getting too much rain water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hɔmɔ miipiŋ mi-ŋmãa lɛ loo nugbɔ miinɛ babaoo?

english: When maize lacks water, its leaves curl inward like tubes and turn dry at the edges to save moisture. When soil has too much water, the leaves turn pale yellow and look soft because flooded roots cannot breathe.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ ŋmãa lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli tamɔ tsɔne ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo ejaakɛ shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my tomato plants help them stay healthy during dry weeks?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like an umbrella for the soil. It traps moisture beneath it so the sun cannot dry out the earth quickly, keeping root zones cool and hydrated.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings wither and die even when the ground feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have delicate stems and small roots that cannot handle full, direct heat from the sun. Without temporary shade, intense light causes the leaves to lose moisture faster than small roots can pull it from the ground.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii. ni nyɛŋ aná dɔlɛ kɛjɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ Kɛji akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo bɛ La ni naa wa haa baai lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. koni enyɛ egbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants droop down during the hottest part of the afternoon and stand back up in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yucca tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛteɔ shi gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during midday to reduce the surface area exposed to direct heat, which prevents water loss. Once the air cools down in the evening, the plant recovers and lifts its leaves back up.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi aaafee shwane mli koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni ebaawo baai heei.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and thin with very small tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they struggle against each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Instead of putting energy into growing thick tubers underground, the plant wastes its strength growing high to reach sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei kɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ bulbs ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdaraa lɛ shaa afɔle koni amɛná hulu la.

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my farm every morning to inspect my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa leebi koni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Checking your field every morning helps you catch early signs of pest attacks, leaf diseases, or lack of water before they spread across the whole farm. Early action saves your harvest from destruction.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ daa leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ebatutua bo, tso lɛ mli hela, loo nu bɛ mli mra. dani egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Nifeemɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaahere onibii kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ.

english: Why do cowpea flowers open in the early morning but close up by midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii fɔ̃ɔ leebi shi amɛkpaa shwane mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants open their flowers in the cool morning to attract bees and insects for pollination when those insects are active. They close up during the harsh midday heat to protect their delicate flowering parts from drying out.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli koni amɛkɛgbala ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni haa ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ kɛ amɛmiitsu nii. Amɛŋmɛɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my crops when the ground is moist rather than dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Crop roots can only drink in food dissolved in water. Applying fertilizer to dry earth leaves the chemicals sitting on top, which can burn root tips and waste nutrients until rain eventually falls.
ga: Abaanyɛ anu tso shishifãi yɛ niyenii ni nu shwieɔ mli pɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baashi tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni efite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛyashi naagbee lɛ nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in the same farm with maize make my maize grow greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally captures nitrogen food from the air and fixes it into the soil. The nearby maize roots drink this natural fertilizer, making their leaves deep green and strong.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛsu mli amɛmɔɔ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nuɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Officer, how do I know how many weeks or months a new crop needs before it is ready for harvesting?
ga: Nitsulɔi Te mafee tɛŋŋ male otsii loo nyɔji enyiɛ tso hee ko baahe dani efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Every crop variety has a specific maturity period listed on seed packets or provided by extension officers. You count from the day of planting or transplanting; for short-duration crops, harvesting can start in as little as 10 weeks, while other crops take several months or years.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni amɛdaraa taakɛ aŋmala yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe wolo lɛ nɔ loo mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ kɛhaa lɛ. Okaneɔ kɛjɛɔ gbi ni adu loo atsakeɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛha tsei ni be kukuoo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ, Nikpamɔ baanyɛ aje shishi yɛ otsii 10 pɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi Eheɔ nyɔji loo afii babaoo.

english: When an extension agent tells me a crop takes 10 weeks to yield, how many months is that in normal farm counting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ he najiaŋdamɔlɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ heɔ otsii 10 dani ewoɔ nii lɛ, nyɔji enyiɛ ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ akane?

english: Ten weeks equals two months and two weeks (two and a half months). Counting in weeks gives you a more precise schedule for watering, fertilizing, and preparing for harvest than just counting in whole months.
ga: Otsii nyɔŋma kɛ nyɔji enyɔ kɛ otsii enyɔ yeɔ egbɔ. (Nyɔji enyɔ kɛ fã) Otsii ni oookane lɛ haa onáa gbɛjianɔtoo ni ja jogbaŋŋ kɛha nu ni oooha, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hesaamɔ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ. Nɔ ni fe nyɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ ni akaneɔ

english: My crop is at 8 weeks and has not produced any flowers or fruits yet, does this mean my field has failed?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eye otsii 8 ni ebɛ fɔfɔi loo aduawai lolo. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ efite?

english: Not at all. At 8 weeks, many crops are still growing leaves and strong stems. Flowering and fruiting often start around 10 weeks, so your crop is likely just following its natural growth timeline.
ga: Jee nakai kraa. Beni shɛɔ otsi ni ji 8 lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lolo. Fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo jeɔ shishi aaafee otsii 10, no hewɔ lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni onibii lɛ baanyiɛ ebɔɔ su dalɛ be lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Is flowering the same as fruiting, or do I have to wait after flowers appear before I can harvest?
ga: Ani fɔfɔii afeemɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ji ekome loo esa akɛ mamɛ beni fɔfɔii lɛ efɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani akpa?

english: Flowering comes first so bees and wind can pollinate the plant. Fruits form inside or behind the flower after pollination, so flowering is the signal that fruit development and harvest will follow shortly.
ga: Esa akɛ fɔfɔi aba klɛŋklɛŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ aha tsei afee ŋmeii. Yibii baa yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli loo amɛsɛɛ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔii ni baa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ etsɛŋ ni hiɛyaa kɛ aduawai akpamɔ baanyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do some crops flower very quickly in a few weeks while others take many months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi fɔɔ fɔfɔi oya, yɛ otsii fioo ko pɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi heɔ nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Different crops are bred for different life spans. Short-season crops are designed to complete their cycle quickly to beat dry weather, while long-season crops spend extra time growing larger roots and stems before flowering.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ shihilɛ mli shihilɛi srɔtoi amli. Afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ koni amɛgbe sɛɛkuu lɛ naa oya koni amɛye shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anɔ kunim. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ baahe be kroko koni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ adara dani amɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: If my crops start flowering at 10 weeks, does that mean I can start harvesting on that exact same day?
ga: Kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi beni eye otsii 10 lɛ, ani no tsɔɔ akɛ manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Flowering is the beginning of the harvest stage. While some vegetable crops yield harvestable parts as soon as 10 weeks, full fruit development usually requires a few extra days after the flower opens.
ga: Fɔfɔii ni shwereɔ lɛ ji kpamɔ be lɛ shishijee. Eyɛ mli akɛ aduawai komɛi woɔ amɛkpamɔ lɛ yɛ otsii 10 mli pɛ moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni yeɔ emuu lɛ heɔ gbii fioo krokomɛi kɛfataa he beni amɛfɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I plan my planting date so that my crops are ready to harvest before the heavy rains end?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato midumɔ gbi lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee klalo kɛha nikpamɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba naagbee?

english: Count backward from the end of the rainy season using the crop's maturity period. If a crop takes 10 weeks (2.5 months) to harvest, plant it at least two and a half months before the rains are expected to dry up.
ga: Kanemɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ be lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ otsii 10 (nyɔji 2.5) dani akpaa lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, dumɔ nyɔji enyɔ kɛ fã dani nugbɔ lɛ agbi.

english: Once my crop reaches its expected harvest time at 10 weeks, do I harvest the whole farm at once or bit by bit?
ga: Kɛ́ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛ otsii 10 ni mikpaa gbɛ akɛ ebaakpa lɛ he lɛ, ani makpã ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo makpã mli fioo fioo?

english: For most flowering crops, harvesting is a gradual process that starts at maturity (e.g., week 10) and continues over several weeks as new flowers continuously develop into mature fruits.
ga: Kɛha tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo lɛ, Kpamɔ ji nifeemɔ ko ni yaa nɔ fiofio ni jeɔ shishi yɛ be mli ni amɛdara (ni ji otsi 10) ni eyaa nɔ otsii babaoo be mli ni fɔfɔi heei yaa nɔ amɛdaraa kɛfeɔ aduawai ni eda lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my crop is truly mature and ready to harvest without picking it too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛkpaaa mra tsɔ?

english: Besides tracking the recommended growth time (like 10 weeks), look for physical signs such as changes in fruit color, firmness, drying of outer leaves, or full size development.
ga: Kɛfata be ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ lɛ nɔ (tamɔ otsii 10) lɛ he lɛ, taomɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii tamɔ aduawai lɛ ahe su tsakemɔi, amɛhewalɛ, kɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ ni egbi. loo shweremɔ ni fa babaoo

english: At what stage in the crop's growth cycle should I give fertilizer to help it produce plenty of flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa awo mli koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai babaoo?

english: Apply growth fertilizer early in the first few weeks for strong leaves, and switch to flowering fertilizer just before the expected flowering time (around week 6 to 8) so the plant has energy to flower and fruit by week 10.
ga: Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ mra lɛ atsu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli koni eha baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. ni otsake kɛya fɔfɔi ahe ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani fɔfɔi be ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ aba. (Aaafee otsii 6 kɛyashi 8) koni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii yɛ otsi ni ji 10 lɛ mli.

english: How do liquid chemicals actually protect my cocoa trees from dying?
ga: Te tsofai ni ji nu lɛ baanyɛ abu mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Liquid chemicals, like systemic insecticides or liquid fertilizers, are sprayed onto cocoa leaves or trunks. They either kill damaging pests directly on contact or get absorbed into the tree so insects die when they try to feed on the plant.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni ji nu tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ kookoo baai loo tsei lɛ anɔ. Amɛgbeɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he loo amɛboteɔ tso lɛ mli bɔni afee ni kooloi bibii lɛ agboi kɛ́ amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye tso lɛ.

english: Can applying too much chemical harm my cocoa crop instead of helping it?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye mi cacao tsei lɛ awui moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ?

english: Yes, using too much chemical can burn the leaves, destroy young flowers, and stress the tree. Always follow the correct mixing instructions so you protect your yield without hurting the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai, egbe fɔfɔi bibii, ni eha tso lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, nyiɛmɔ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni ja ni kɔɔ futumɔ he lɛ sɛɛ koni obu onibii ahe ni okɛyeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different liquid chemicals together in the same spray tank?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai enyɔ ni ji nu baafutu yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli?

english: Not all chemicals can be safely mixed. Combining incompatible liquids can make them stop working entirely or create a mixture that burns your cocoa leaves, so always check with an extension officer before mixing.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛ tsofai komɛi afutu jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛkpa nitsumɔ kwraa loo amɛfee nɔ ko ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni shãa kookoo baai lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ extension officer lɛ agba sane dani okɛfutu.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet and humid conditions. Spraying approved fungicides helps protect healthy pods from being infected.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: What causes small insects to suck the life out of my young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii shwieɔ wala kɛjɛɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ amli?

english: These insects are usually mirids (capsids), which pierce young cocoa shoots and pods to feed on the sap, causing the branches to dry up. Regular spraying with recommended insecticides keeps them away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji mirids (capsids), ni tsɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei niji ni egbi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ he.

english: Why should I avoid spraying chemicals on my cocoa trees right before it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ kookoo tsei anɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ he?

english: If rain falls shortly after you spray, it washes the chemical off the cocoa leaves before the tree or pests can absorb it, wasting your effort and money.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni afɔse tsofai lɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ Tsofai lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai lɛ amli dani tso lɛ loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ shwieɔ amɛ. Ehaa ofiteɔ hewalɛ kɛ shika.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are hungry for extra nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii kpakpai krokomɛi he miihia mi-kokoo tso lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees lack nutrients, their green leaves turn pale or yellow, growth slows down, and they produce smaller pods. Applying liquid fertilizers helps restore their health and boosts production.
ga: Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ Ebaai eŋɔlii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dalɛ baafee mlɛo. ni ebaana pod bibioo ko Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛnamɔ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when they are damaged by pests like mirids, lack proper nutrients, or suffer from heat stress. Protecting the tree with proper treatments allows the flowers to stay on and grow into pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids lɛ fite amɛ ni amɛnáaa niyenii ni sa. loo hulutsoo he haomɔ ni enaa Kɛ́ obu tso lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsamɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray chemicals on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ kookoo ŋmɔ ko nɔ?

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cooler. Strong afternoon heat causes the chemicals to evaporate before they can do their job.
ga: Be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves curl up and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees curl their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and prevent drying out. Providing shade crops like plantains and keeping the soil covered helps reduce water stress on the trees.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii haa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni tsii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and grow strong. Applying the right nitrogen fertilizer or compost will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara waa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains water easily. When water sits in the ground for too long, it smothers the roots and causes fungal rot, which ruins the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Ebaakpã shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo. ni baanyɛ akpata yitso lɛ hiɛ

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my farm so it doesn't wash away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii koni ekaho?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a gentle light rain. Avoid applying it right before heavy rains, as flooding will wash the nutrients off the farm before plants can drink them.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni okɛbaatsu nii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu afua lɛ baajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani tsei lɛ anu.

english: What is eating the soft middle leaves inside my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni ji teŋ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli lɛ yeli?

english: That damage is caused by fall armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. Checking your farm early and using recommended biopesticides or insecticides inside the plant leaves will stop them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji cutworms. ni ji kooloi ni fɔɔ baa yɛ Ghana Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa loo kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slow and look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Keeping your farm clean lets your crops get all the food they need.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die if I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn under full direct sunshine. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains provides a cooling cover that keeps the cocoa trees alive while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ fɛ̃i ni haa kookoo tso lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ oblahiiaŋ ŋmɔnɔ beaŋ lɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for water, food, and light. Giving crops proper space helps every single plant grow big and produce a higher total yield.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ la he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edara ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight and make food. Lifting the leaves off the ground also prevents wet soil diseases and helps grow larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛhoo nii. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ekɛtsiɔ helai anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific soil pests to build up. Switching to beans or groundnuts feeds the soil and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmeii loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni ekpa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Consistent watering during dry spells helps flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or are drowning in too much wet soil. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow leaves, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ miiye nitrogen loo amɛbote shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ babaoo mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava stems when putting them in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, te esa akɛ amɛdu amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava stems should generally be planted about one meter apart from each other in all directions. Giving them enough space prevents the roots from fighting for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, allowing the cassava tubers underground to grow large and thick.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome yɛ he fɛɛ he. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are all the blossoms falling off my cocoa trees before turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as strong sun heat, prolonged dry spells, or poor soil fertility. Maintaining good shade trees, mulching around the roots to keep the soil cool, and feeding the soil helps the flowers stay on and develop into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ayeɔ niyenii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my ripening tomato fruits turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo lɛ?

english: This black rotting on the bottom of tomatoes is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the growing fruit, often triggered by irregular watering. Watering your tomatoes regularly and evenly helps the plant absorb calcium smoothly from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo tomato nɔ daa kɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Beans and cowpeas are leguminous plants that have special root systems capable of pulling nitrogen gas from the air and storing it in the soil. This natural nitrogen feeds the nearby maize crops, acting like a free fertilizer to make the soil richer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛ ko ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: What is causing ragged holes in the middle leaves of my maize plants, and how does it hurt my crop?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei tso baa lɛ mli bu lɛ baa? Ni te eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Ragged holes inside the central leaves of maize are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating their way through the growing tip. If left untreated, these worms destroy the leaf structure, which prevents the plant from absorbing sunlight to make food, drastically reducing your grain yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ. Enɛ haaa tsei aŋɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmaa ni anáa lɛ ba shi kwraa.

english: How does spreading dry grass or palm fronds on the soil help my garden crops during hot days?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei tsei ni mikɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Spreading dry organic matter on top of the soil is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps the sun from drying out the soil too quickly, smothers weeds so they cannot sprout, and slowly rots over time to feed the soil with rich organic nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfite yɛ be ni sa mli koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni fa babaoo.

english: Why is it necessary to tie my tomato vines to wooden sticks as they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-tomato wain tso lɛ akpɛtɛ tso he beni edaa lɛ?

english: Staking tomato plants lifts the heavy stems and fruits off the damp ground, keeping them away from soil-borne diseases and pests. It also opens up the plant to sunlight and fresh air, making the fruits ripen better and easier for you to harvest without breaking the main branches.
ga: Tomato tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei kɛ aduawai ni tsii kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ anɔ. Etsiɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa Ehaa tsei lɛ hu naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaakpa ni ogbeee niji titrii lɛ.

english: Why do some of my planted pepper seeds fail to come up out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if the soil is buried too deep, gets too dry, or is too packed for tender sprouts to break through. Planting seeds shallowly, keeping the top layer of soil moist like a squeezed sponge, and shading the nursery bed gently will encourage uniform germination.
ga: Dumɔwui ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ, egbi tsɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni mli ekɔɔɔ nɔ lɛ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ sponji ni ashɛre. ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ shwieɔ ŋmɔ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ blɛoo Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ daa.

english: When is the correct time to apply my granular fertilizer during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ okɛ granular fertilizer awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but not during heavy, continuous downpours. A light rain or moist soil helps dissolve the fertilizer granules into liquid form so the roots can drink it up, whereas heavy downpours will wash expensive fertilizer off your land before plants can use it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ he. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nu ni shishifãi lɛ anu. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei kɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why do different varieties of maize take different numbers of days to grow before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi lɛ heɔ be srɔtoi dani amɛdaraa dani akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred for different weather conditions and farmer needs. Fast-growing varieties mature early to beat short rainy seasons, while longer-growing varieties spend more time absorbing nutrients to build larger yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi kɛ okwaafoi ahiamɔ nii anaa. Henɔi ni daa oya lɛ daa oya koni amɛye nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ nɔ kunim. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni amɛná yibii babaoo.

english: Which maize seed should I buy if I need a quick harvest in less than three months?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmãa esa akɛ mahe kɛji miitao ni akpa oya yɛ nɔ ni shɛɛɛ nyɔji etɛ mli?

english: You should look for short-duration varieties like Wagnata, which reach full maturity in about 85 to 90 days, allowing you to harvest food quickly before the dry season starts.
ga: Esa akɛ otao ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ wagnata, ni shwereɔ yɛ aaafee gbii 85 kɛyashi 90 mli, koni onyɛ okpa niyenii oya dani hulutsoo be lɛ aje shishi.

english: What is Obatanpa maize, and how long does it take from planting to harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji obata ŋmãa? Ni be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ nikpamɔ mli?

english: Obatanpa is an improved, high-protein maize variety commonly grown in Ghana that takes about 110 days (around three and a half months) to mature fully.
ga: Obatanpa ji ŋmãa ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ protein, ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni afɔɔ dumɔ yɛ Ghana. Eheɔ aaafee gbii 110 (aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛ fã) dani eshɛɔ dalɛ he.
