english: How long will I have to wait to harvest if I plant Aburokyini maize?
ga: Kɛji odu Aborokin ŋmãa Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ?

english: Aburokyini is a longer-duration maize variety that usually takes between 115 and 120 days (about four months) to fully mature in the field.
ga: Aburokyini ji ŋmãa henɔ ko ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee gbii 115 kɛyashi 120 (aaafee nyɔji ejwɛ) dani eshɛɔ dalɛ he yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to plant short-season maize or long-season maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa ni yeɔ be kuku loo ŋmãa ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: It depends on your local rainfall; short-season maize is best if rains are brief or unreliable, while long-season maize is better if you have steady rainfall and want higher grain yields.
ga: Edamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. loo ŋmãa ni anyɛɛɛ ahe aye yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ daa ni oosumɔ ni ŋmãa babaoo aba.

english: How can I plan my farm so I do not harvest all my maize at the exact same time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni mikakpa mi-ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli?

english: You can plant different varieties with different growth periods—such as a 90-day variety alongside a 120-day variety—on the same day so they mature a few weeks apart.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu srɔtoi srɔtoi. kɛ dalɛ bei srɔtoi, tamɔ gbii 90 henɔi ni akɛ gbii 120 henɔi ebɔ he yɛ gbi kome nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛdara yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ateŋ.

english: How do I choose the right maize variety based on the rain patterns in my region?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmãa ni sa yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ naa?

english: If your area gets short or erratic rains, choose early-maturing varieties (85–90 days). If your area gets long, stable rainy seasons, choose medium to late-maturing varieties (110–120 days) for maximum production.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Halamɔ tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra (gbii 85–90) kɛji akɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni yaa nɔ daa. Halamɔ henɔi ni shwereɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ kɛyashi sɛɛ mli (gbii 110–120) kɛha yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: How do I calculate the approximate week my crops will be ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu otsii ni asusuɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baafee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You count the expected maturity days specified for your seed variety starting from your planting date, and convert those days into weeks to estimate your harvest period.
ga: Okaneɔ gbi ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ ebaakwɛ ni aŋmala aha odumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ kɛjɛ gbi ni adu lɛ nɔ. ni otsake nakai gbii lɛ owo otsii amli koni okɛbu okpamɔ be lɛ he akɔntaa.

english: Will bad weather make my maize take longer to mature than the seed package says?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii baaha mi-ŋmãa lɛ ahé be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ fe bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ awo mli lɛ?

english: Yes, factors like poor rainfall, extreme heat, or poor soil nutrients can slow down crop development, causing the plant to take longer to reach full maturity.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii tamɔ nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa kwraa.

english: What happens if I leave my mature maize in the field long past its maturity date?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmãa ni eda yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛho be ni esa akɛ ekwɛ lɛ he?

english: Leaving dry maize in the field past its maturity period increases the risk of damage from pests, weevils, mold, unexpected rainfall, and field fires, which lowers your crop quality.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmãa ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni eho be ni ekɛdaa lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha oshara ni jɛɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, ŋmeii, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ, kɛ la ni baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni no baaha onibii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant beans together with my trees on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mikɛ mitsei lɛ baadu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting beans alongside trees helps cover the soil to keep it moist, prevents weeds from taking over, and adds useful nutrients back into the ground to help your trees grow better.
ga: Beans ni aduɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ koni eye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can growing bean crops close to tree roots cause any damage when there is heavy rain?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ baanyɛ afite nii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: If beans are planted too close to trees in very wet areas, they can trap excess water around the tree trunk, which creates damp conditions that make the tree roots rot.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ tsɔ yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ waa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. tso shishi Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my crops die after heavy rain leaves standing water on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboi beni nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ shi nu yɛ miŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water sits on your farm for too long, it cuts off air to the plant roots under the ground, causing the roots to drown, rot, and eventually kill the crop.
ga: Kɛ nu hi oŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛdu shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How does heavy rainfall and flooding destroy my farmland?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ nu afua fiteɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Floodwater washes away the good topsoil containing plant food and leaves behind overly wet, packed soil that makes it hard for crops to grow strong.
ga: Nu afua lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kpakpa ni tsei aniyenii yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa. ni oshɛrɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ashwie Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: What can I do when rainwater always gathers in the lower part of my farm?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shishi be fɛɛ be?

english: You need to dig simple water channels or drainage ditches so excess water can flow off your farm easily instead of sitting there to damage your crops.
ga: Esa akɛ otsa nu gbɛ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ mli bɔni afee ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ anyɛ ajɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootara jɛmɛ kɛkɛ ni ofite onibii lɛ.

english: Is standing water on my farm able to cause sickness in my plants?
ga: Ani nu ni damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha hela aba mitsei lɛ amli?

english: Yes, too much standing water creates warm, wet conditions that allow fungal diseases and root rot to develop rapidly and spread through your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa onibii fɛɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and droop after a flood even though there is plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nu afua sɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ?

english: Flooding damages the roots so badly that they can no longer suck up nutrients from the soil, making the plant look sick and starved despite being surrounded by water.
ga: Nu afua fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ waa aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ lɛ ni hɔmɔ miiye lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ebɔle ehe moŋ.

english: How can I check if excess water has rotted the roots of my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ miiha mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miifite?

english: Carefully dig up one affected plant and look at the roots; if they are dark, soft, and bad-smelling instead of firm and light-colored, water damage and disease have set in.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ tso ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okwɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛji amɛji ediŋŋ, amɛhe jɔ, ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ, Moŋ lɛ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nu kɛ hela eba.

english: Should I clear and replant new seeds immediately after floodwater leaves my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni madu dumɔwui heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nu afua lɛ eshi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, you must allow the soil to dry out and the old diseased plants to wither completely, otherwise the sickness left in the wet soil will attack your new seeds.
ga: Dabi, ehe miihia ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni tsei momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ agbi kwraa. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, helai ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatutua odumɔwui heei lɛ.

english: What should I do with crops that have been spoiled by water disease in my field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee ŋmɔshi nibii ni helai ni jɛɔ nu mli baa lɛ efite yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: You should let the sick plants dry out and wither completely, then remove and destroy them so the disease does not stay in the soil to infect your next planting.
ga: Esa akɛ oha tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kwraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, jiemɔ nakai tsei lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ. Enɛ baaha hela lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hela aba odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my groundnuts so I do not leave half of them buried in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? koni akashi ŋmeii lɛ fã yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Groundnuts are ready when the leaves turn yellow and the inside of the shells show dark brown markings; digging too late causes the stems to weaken, leaving the pods trapped in dry soil, while harvesting too early leaves you with shriveled nuts.
ga: Peanuts lɛ efee klalo kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Kɛ́ atsa shi blɛoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ha ŋmeii lɛ akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha okɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ ahi ohe.

english: Why do my harvested groundnuts develop black mold and go bad inside the storage bags after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nitoo kotoku lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storing groundnuts before they are thoroughly sun-dried traps moisture inside the bag, creating a damp environment where mold grows and spoils the nuts.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii to dani ogbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii awo kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa ni ŋmeii lɛ daa yɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means the maize plant lacks nitrogen, so it pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ egbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green bushes on top but gives me very small cassava roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ jwɛi agbo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi? Cassava shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shishi?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer or planting cuttings too close together makes the cassava plant spend all its energy growing leaves instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ Enɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the large shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight because their delicate leaves scorch easily and their shallow roots dry out without shade trees to protect them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa oya, ni eshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baagbi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo hebuu bɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain suckers droop and dry up during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmatta be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water very quickly in hot, dry winds, so the plant naturally lets its outer leaves dry up to conserve water inside its main stem.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei haa kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ gĩɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni nu ahi tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato plants drop their flowers before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plants drop flowers when they experience stress from intense heat, lack of soil moisture, or irregular watering, which prevents the flowers from forming fruits.
ga: Tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do I need to raise stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei anɔ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to spread their leaves in the sunlight to make food for big tubers, while vines lying on damp ground are easily attacked by pests and diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tsei kakadaji ni amɛkɛbaagbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛha amɛ bulbs wuji lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, wain tsei ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ helai tutuaa amɛ oya.

english: Why does weed growth during the first month hurt my maize crop much more than weeds growing later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ awui fe jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young maize roots are small and weak, so early weeds easily steal all the water, fertilizer, and sunlight before the maize can establish itself.
ga: Baby corn shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi ni baa mra lɛ baaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ ama shi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in tiny knots on their roots, which naturally fertilizes the soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: Can leftover weed killer in my spraying machine harm my pepper plants if I use it to spray for insects later?
ga: Ani tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni eshwɛ yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye mi-pepper tsei lɛ awui? Kɛ mikɛtsu nii kɛshwie ŋmeii sɛɛ mli.

english: Yes, even a small amount of weed killer left in your spraying tank can scorch, stunt, or kill your pepper plants. You must thoroughly wash out the spraying machine with clean water before putting in a new crop medicine.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa fioo ko po ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi nɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã, efo loo efite o-pepper tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani okɛ tso tsofa hee awo mli.

english: How many times should I rinse my knapsack sprayer before switching from weed control to treating vegetable leaves?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafɔ misɛɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ he dani matsake kɛjɛ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛyaa aduawai ahe tsofafeemɔ nɔ?

english: You should rinse the sprayer tank, hose, and nozzle thoroughly with clean water at least three times to remove all traces of the previous chemical so your crops do not get burnt.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ spray tanki, hose, kɛ nozzle lɛ he jogbaŋŋ kɛ hoo lɛ shii 3 koni ojie tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ. Koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akashã

english: How can I be sure I am mixing the right amount of medicine for my cocoa trees if I cannot read the label on the bottle?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni sa miifutu mi-cacao tsei lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ makane nɔ ni aŋma yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu?

english: You should ask the chemical seller to explain the exact measurements to you at the store, or ask a family member or extension officer to read the instruction paper inside the box for you before you start mixing.
ga: Esa akɛ obi mɔ ni hɔ̃ɔ tsofa lɛ ni etsɔɔ bo bɔ ni tsofa lɛ dalɛ ji ha lɛ mli yɛ shwapo lɛ mli. Aloo bi oweku lɛ mlinyo loo mɔ ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ekane gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ adeka lɛ nɔ lɛ eha bo dani obɔi tsɔne lɛ mlifu.

english: What should I do if I forget the right steps for applying my crop medicine after getting home from the market?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mihiɛ kpa gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii beni miku misɛɛ kɛjɛ jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look for the paper leaflet that comes inside or attached to the bottle package, or ask your local extension officer for guidance so you do not apply the wrong mix and damage your crops.
ga: Taomɔ wolo bibioo ko ni yɔɔ mli loo ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ tɔ lɛ he. Aloo bi ŋaawoo kɛjɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ extension nitsulɔ lɛ dɛŋ. Enɛ ji koni okɛ nibii ni ejaaa akafutu ni ofite onibii.

english: Will putting extra medicine in my spraying tank protect my crops better from pests?
ga: Ani tsofa krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛbaawo tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli lɛ baabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: No, putting too much chemical can poison your crops, causing leaves to dry up and reducing your harvest. Always use the exact dosage recommended on the product leaflet.
ga: Dabi, tsofai babaoo ni okɛbaafata he lɛ baanyɛ afite oŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ yibɔ pɔtɛɛ ni atsɔɔ yɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe wolo lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why did my maize leaves turn brown after I mixed two different crop medicines together in the same tank?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ tsei ahe tsofai enyɔ futu baagi kome mli lɛ?

english: Some crop chemicals react negatively when mixed together, creating a harsh liquid that burns plant leaves. Unless the instructions specifically say two medicines can be mixed, apply them separately.
ga: Tsofai komɛi ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ amɛ futu mli. Enɛ haa nu ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ashã tsei baai lɛ baa. Ja gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ tsɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ akɛ abaanyɛ akɛ tsofai enyɔ afutu. Okɛ tsofai lɛ atsu nii srɔtoi.

english: Why did my tomato leaves wilt after I sprayed them with a new chemical product I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mikɛ tsofa hee ni mihe lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves can wilt if the chemical is too strong, mixed incorrectly, or combined with residues of an old chemical left inside an unwashed spraying tank.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ baanyɛ agbo kɛji tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Akɛ tsofai momo ni eshwɛ yɛ spray tanki ni ahooo lɛ mli lɛ futuɔ loo akɛfataa he yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ

english: Can using the wrong chemical spray in my soil prevent my yam seeds from sprouting?
ga: Ani tsofa ni ejaaa ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃?

english: Yes, harsh chemicals or bad mixtures can remain in the soil and damage young seed eyes or tender roots, preventing your yams from sprouting properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa loo nibii gbohii baanyɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli ni amɛfite dumɔwui bibii loo shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops get stressed when I spray them during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haoɔ beni mikɛ nu shwieɔ amɛnɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Under strong heat, crops open their pores wide and absorb chemicals too quickly, which causes heat stress and leaf burning. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when it is cool.
ga: yɛ la ni naa wa shishi Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagbele ŋmeii wuji ni amɛbaaŋɔ tsofai oya tsɔ. Enɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ baa shãa baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why did the crop medicine stop protecting my cabbage from insects after I left the bottle open in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso tsofa lɛ kpa mi-cabbage lɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ahe beni mishi tɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight and high heat break down the active ingredients in farm medicines, making them weak or useless. Store your farm inputs in a cool, dark place with the lid tightly closed.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji bɔjɔmɔ loo sɛɛnamɔ ni bɛ Okɛ oŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni duŋ ewo mli ni okɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ naa lɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plant need for growth. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves up to feed the newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very small yields when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, leaving none of them with enough strength to produce big fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli, bɔni afee ni dumɔwui ko bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji loo bulbs.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge, bushy leaves above ground but tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Having too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus all its energy on growing thick green leaves instead of storing energy in the underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ

english: Why do caterpillars attack the center leaves of my young maize plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm prefer eating soft, young shoots, and warm, moist rainy weather allows their eggs to hatch faster and spread rapidly.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmeii bibii. ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni wɔji lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl upward during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural shield to reduce leaf surface area so it loses less water through evaporation under hot afternoon sunshine.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛha baa lɛ hiɛ he ni baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, nu fioo pɛ laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ tomato yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme hot temperatures cause stress to the plant and dry out flower pollen, preventing proper pollination and causing the flower to drop off.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ pollination ni sa naa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans together with my cassava make the soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots, which naturally enriches the soil and provides food for nearby crops.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the surface, so as heavy fruit bunches grow, the top becomes too heavy for the shallow roots to anchor in the soil.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aduawai akuu ni tsii lɛ dara lɛ, Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baafee tsiimɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I saved from last harvest fail to sprout when planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds fail to sprout if they were stored with too much moisture, damaged by weevils, or dried under extreme heat that destroyed the living embryo inside.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Akɛ ŋmeii efite loo egbiɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, ni fiteɔ fɔmɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ wala mli ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops right after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie jɛmɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil for years and wake up instantly when land clearing exposes them to direct sunlight and rainwater.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛteɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ ha hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ pɛ.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with plenty of leaves, but the roots under the ground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa lolo.

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, cassava plants use all their energy to grow big top leaves instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai wuji lɛ amli moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Staking spreads out yam leaves so they can catch direct sunlight to make food for the tubers, while also keeping the leaves off wet soil to prevent rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Staking gbɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛha bulb lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ koni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akafee nɔ ko.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their roots are not deep enough yet. Shade trees act as living umbrellas that keep the air cool and soil moist while the cocoa grows.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain stem for water and soil nutrients. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, which ensures the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow fast, or the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. loo shishifãi ni ebote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli

english: If I plant groundnuts on my plot this year, why will my maize grow much better in that same spot next year?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli afi nɛɛ Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the groundnut crop is finished, that left-behind nitrogen serves as free fertilizer for the next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ agbe ŋmeii adumɔ naa Nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ baafee ŋmeii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no bees or wind to shake the pollen inside the flower so fruit can set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen lɛ mli koni eha aduawai lɛ akã shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up like small cups and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of young leaves, which damages the leaf tissue and can pass diseases to the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ baa fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ hela eshwa tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer directly against the main stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mitso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is very strong salt; touching the stem directly will burn the plant's skin and roots. Fertilizer should be placed a few inches away where the feeder roots spread out.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei fa babaoo waa. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko, ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my seeds fail to germinate even after the first big rainfall of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ po sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often wet only the top layer of dirt while the deep soil stays dry. Seeds need steady moisture over several days to swell up and sprout, so planting after just one isolated rain can cause seeds to dry out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he egbi Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be gbii babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛshwere ni amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted nearby to protect them from the sun's heat and keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the center funnel of the maize plant during the day and feeds on soft leaves, which can severely ruin your harvest if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni eyeɔ baai bibii, ni baanyɛ afite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow, twisting up, and staying very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛmiifee bibii waa lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies or spread by using infected stems for planting. You should remove sick plants and plant disease-resistant cassava stem varieties next season.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ amɛ loo amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ ojie tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛ ŋmei henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping all their blossoms instead of growing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛmiikwɛ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely between waterings, or when the plant lacks nutrients. Consistent watering and balanced fertilizing help the plant hold its flowers and produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli ni amɛwoɔ tomato.

english: How do I know if my crops need chemical fertilizer or farm animal manure to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsofai loo ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia mitsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crops grow slowly, look pale green, or have yellow leaves, your soil is short on nutrients. Animal manure builds long-term soil moisture and health, while chemical fertilizers provide quick food to growing plants, so using both gives the best results.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ loo eyɛ kaadi ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ náa hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baa.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by a long dry stretch before the main rainy season sets in. If seeds sprout after one rain and receive no follow-up rain for weeks, the young roots will dry up and die in the hot earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ ni amɛnáaa nugbɔ ni yaa nɔ otsii babaoo. Shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to use wooden sticks to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread across the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei duɔ sweet potato wain tsei moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up toward the sunshine so the plant can catch light and make food. That food is sent down into the ground, resulting in much larger, healthier yam tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ la lɛ ni efee niyenii. Akɛ niyenii lɛ maje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger in my farm field than my planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to aggressively take over space, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing food and water away from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni sa akɛ amɛyeɔ he ko, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why shouldn't I collect and plant seeds from the harvest of hybrid pepper seeds I bought from the agro-store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mibuaa dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid pepper dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ okwaayeli shwapo lɛ mli lɛ anaa ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only in the first generation. Seeds collected from that harvest will produce weak plants with mixed qualities and much lower pepper yields.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ nibii ni efutu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi kwraa lɛ aba.

english: Why are tiny insects making powder out of my dried maize grains inside my storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii lɛ fee powda kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni egbi ni yɔɔ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These insects are grain weevils that lay eggs on dry corn. To stop them, your maize must be dried completely until hard before bagging, and stored in airtight bags or treated with approved grain-storage protectants.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji dumɔwui amli kooloi ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi nɔ. Koni okpa o-corn lɛ Esa akɛ egbi kwraa kɛyashi ewa dani awo kotoku mli. ni akɛtoɔ kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo akɛ nɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtoɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ ewo nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them in an open field without any larger plants around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni cacao tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa from harsh sunlight and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛitsu ko ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines so they can grow upward on sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso nɔ koni enyɛ eda yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines that need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch direct sunlight for energy. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and spreading fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni shwieɔ amɛhe ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛkafiteɔ ni amɛkagbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn ears have formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the key food it uses to stay green. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has from older leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ Kɛ́ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni edara yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like pencils during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ pensil yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot hours as a protection mechanism. By rolling up, the leaf reduces its exposure to the sun and wind, helping the plant conserve water so it does not dry out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ hebuu gbɛ. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he koni amɛkagbi.

english: Wrinkled and curling pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juices from the underside of new leaves, or by viral diseases spread by whiteflies that distort leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge bushy leaves above ground, but the roots under the soil stay very tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ji bibii kwraa lolo?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in extremely loose topsoil, it directs its energy into growing thick stems and leaves instead of storing energy underground in the tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni etse ehe waa lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ oyitsoŋ lɛ najiaŋ

english: Tomato flowers drop without fruiting when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save its strength for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni ewooo yibii kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do tiny cocoa pods on my tree shrivel up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Ani mitsei lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This behavior, called cherelle wilt, happens because the tree naturally thins out excess young pods it cannot feed due to limited nutrients, shade stress, or dry spells, focusing its strength on the remaining pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ subaŋ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilt lɛ baa ejaakɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii lɛ. yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ hewɔ lɛ Shade strain, loo dry spell lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ lɛ maa ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when many young suckers are left growing around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni ashiɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers compete directly with the main stem for water, sunlight, and soil food. Cutting away extra suckers lets the main plant channel full energy into making a larger bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aha hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfee tsei akui wuji.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings collapse and rot at the stem base just a few days after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This condition, known as damping-off, is caused by soil fungus that attacks tender stems when nursery beds are kept too wet, densely packed, or shaded without enough fresh airflow.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ damping off lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tutuaa tsei bibii lɛ amli kɛ́ ŋmei saatso lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ kwɔ. loo hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up like tubes during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing moisture to the sun. It is a natural way for the plant to save water until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be ni hulu lɛ shwieɔ amɛ lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i baa.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning or during the midday sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the soil is cool and allows the roots to absorb the water deeply. Watering at midday causes most of the water to evaporate in the heat before the roots can drink it.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la yɛ latsaa be mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from too much water rather than dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii miigboi yɛ nu babaoo hewɔ moŋ fe kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves dry out, turn brown, and feel crisp. When crops get too much water, the soil stays soggy, roots rot, and the leaves turn soft, limp, and yellow.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ tsei lɛ, baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ asarasu. and feels crispy Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to dig and loosen hard soil before planting my cassava cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ ni wa mli dani madu ŋmei niji lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil allows the roots to spread easily underground, which helps the cassava form large tubers. Hard soil blocks root growth and causes rainwater to wash away without soaking in.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni enáa yitsei wuji. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ ni eboteee mli.

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural plant nutrients and acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold onto water longer so your crops stay nourished during dry periods.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa sũ lɛ kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ, ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct harsh sunlight burns their leaves faster than their small root systems can absorb water from the ground.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very leafy and tall, but not producing flowers or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ baa ni kɛlɛ waa lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo aduawai bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: When tomato plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing stems and leaves instead of developing flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛji tomato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over whenever a strong wind blows across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay near the top of the soil. If the roots are damaged by pests or the soil is too loose, the heavy top part of the tree easily pulls the roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii efite shishifãi lɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse tsɔ. Tso lɛ yiteŋ ni tsii lɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do tiny insects always gather under the bottom of my pepper leaves instead of on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ ashishi moŋ fe nɔ ni amɛbaabua amɛhe naa lɛ?

english: Insects hide under leaves to shelter from hot sunlight and heavy rain while sucking the plant's sap in a safe, cool spot.
ga: Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ashishi koni amɛná he ko kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni jɛmɛ ejɔ.

english: Why are the stems of my maize plants breaking in half just when the ears are ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fãa enyɔ beni amɛtoi lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Stalk borer caterpillars tunnel inside the maize stem and eat it from the inside, leaving the stem hollow and weak so it snaps under the weight of the corn.
ga: Borer worms lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli. Ashiɔ tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛkuɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ tsiimɔ shishi.

english: When the lower leaves of maize turn yellow starting from the tips in a V-shape, it means the plant is starving for nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newer upper leaves to survive, leaving the old bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ, no lɛ nitrogen ni faaa lɛ miipiŋ tso lɛ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli koni ehi shi. Ha shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of green leaves and flowers, but the flowers just fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit mainly due to extreme heat stress or too much nitrogen fertilizer. High heat dries out the flower pollen so it cannot fertilize, and too much fertilizer makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Nɔ titri ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni yibii bɛ mli lɛ baa ji dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha pollen lɛ agbi bɔni afee ni enyɛŋ ekɛ fɔmɔ nii awo mli. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow and droop even when the soil is very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked with water for too long, the plant roots drown because they cannot breathe in air. Drowned roots begin to rot and can no longer drink water or absorb food, causing the leaves to yellow and wilt as if the plant were dry.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ. Shishifãi ni miiho nu mli lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛnu nu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ tamɔ nɔ ni tso lɛ egbi.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very thin and fall over when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, the crowded plants compete aggressively for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. They stretch upward quickly to reach the sun, making their stems tall, thin, and weak.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni mli wa Amɛshwereɔ oya koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Ehaa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ, eyɛ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge stems and leaves above ground but very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava plants put all their energy into leafy top growth when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or excess rain early in the season. Because the plant uses its food to grow leaves, it has very little energy left to store in the underground roots.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛdaraa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ niyenii tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai. No hewɔ lɛ, hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ eshwɛ ni abua naa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my garden egg plants get dark spots and die after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Raindrops splashing on bare soil pick up fungal spores and land on the lower leaves of the plant. The wet leaves provide the perfect environment for these spores to sprout, leading to leaf spot disease that browns and kills the leaves.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ holeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ni egbeeɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Baai ni efɔ lɛ ji he ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ kɛ leaf spot hela ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbeɔ baai lɛ baa.

english: Why do my yam setts rot in the mound before they even sprout shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miifite yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Yam setts rot when planted in soil that is wet and unventilated, or if the cut surfaces of the seed tubers were not properly dried in the shade before planting. The moist environment allows soil fungi to invade the cut tissue before the plant can grow roots.
ga: Sweet potatoes baa fite kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ nɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ ayitso lɛ nɔ ni afo lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani adu. Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ fãji ni afo lɛ amli dani tso lɛ shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cowpea plants curling up tightly and becoming sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and stickiness on cowpea plants are caused by tiny insects called aphids. Aphids suck the sap from the underside of leaves, causing them to curl, and they secrete a sweet, sticky liquid called honeydew as they feed.
ga: Kplukai bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ cowpea tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ aphids Aphids lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli. ha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni amɛjieɔ nu ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kpo. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nectar lɛ jeɔ kpo beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crop right after I clear and till the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie jwɛi lɛ ni mikɛtsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant in the soil for years and are built to sprout immediately when exposed to sunlight and air after tilling. Crops take longer to germinate and establish roots, giving the wild weeds a head start in growth.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. ni ebaakwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛ enɔ beni etsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Tsei heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi. Enɛ haa koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the food the plant needs to stay green and build big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛma ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them after maize naturally restores nutrients to your field so your next crop grows better without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni ooodu yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why should I spread dry grass around my pepper plants instead of burning it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi abɔle he lɛ? Pepper tso yɛ shãa najiaŋ?

english: Covering the ground around plants with dry grass keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, traps moisture so you water less, prevents weeds from growing, and rots into rich plant food over time.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbɔleɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli babaoo Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkafite ni amɛtsɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, scorching sunlight. Big trees act as natural umbrellas that shade the seedlings, keep the air cool and humid, and protect the soft leaves while the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa dumɔwui lɛ hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ ni edɔ. ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ

english: Black pod is a water-loving disease that spreads fast in wet, dark conditions. Pruning excess cocoa branches lets sunlight and fresh air flow through your farm, which dries out the moisture and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod ji hela ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo nu ni mli ewo duŋ mli. Cocoa niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the fresh top leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai heei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide in the deep center of the corn plant where leaves grow. Treating them early with recommended pest controls keeps them from destroying the main leaf whorl and ruining your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Amɛtsamɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni awieɔ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite baai wuji lɛ ahe ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to reduce water loss during intense heat, but curling can also mean tiny insects like whiteflies are spreading a plant virus. Keeping the roots watered and controlling small flies helps the leaves stay flat.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Shi curling lɛ hu tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies miigbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã tsei anɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔkwɛmɔ Ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from the main mother plantain tree. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main tree grows thick and produces heavy, large plantain bunches.
ga: Tsofai ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni ewo plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to stretch their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off damp ground to stop rot and disease, helping the plant convert sunlight into big, healthy underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akpã amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekpa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ hulu la lɛ amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei agboi ni mli wa.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower stem leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: How far in advance should I start clearing and preparing my land before the rainy season starts?
ga: Te esa akɛ oje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ kɛ ehe saamɔ shishi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba?

english: You should start preparing your land at least a month before the rainy season begins. Clearing early gives weeds time to dry out, allows you to enrich the soil, and ensures your farm is ready for planting as soon as the first steady rains arrive.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ aje shikpɔŋ he saamɔ shishi nyɔŋ kome dani nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ aje shishi. Ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ mra Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ be ni amɛgbiɔ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ohaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ohaa oŋmɔ lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔwui kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil needs fertilizer or manure before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu?

english: Signs like pale or yellowing leaves, slow plant growth, or thin stalks indicate poor soil. Adding organic manure or recommended fertilizers during land preparation restores nutrients so young crops grow strong from the very beginning.
ga: Okadii lɛ ekomɛi ji baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ dalɛ blɛoo loo eshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛfataa he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ be mli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ adara waa kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: What basic management practices should I teach my caretaker to keep my farm healthy while I am away?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee gbɛjianɔtoo he nifeemɔi esa akɛ matsɔɔ koni mi-ŋmɔ mli nine lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ be mli ni mibɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: A caretaker should be trained in regular weeding schedules, proper pruning, spotting early signs of pests or diseases, and correct harvesting techniques so the crops remain productive year-round.
ga: Esa akɛ atsɔse mɛi ni kwɛɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ daa lɛ he. proper pruning Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo helai ahe okadii ni anaa mra kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ ahe ŋaai ni ja koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to prune the extra branches off my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ kookoo tsei aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to reach the lower trunk. This reduces fungal diseases like black pod and helps the tree focus its energy on producing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle and die when planted in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in full sun. They require temporary shade from tall crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their leaves and retain soil moisture during their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni abu baai lɛ ahe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ shishijee be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, overly shaded farms. Removing affected pods immediately and clearing excessive shade helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How long should I keep cocoa seedlings in the nursery before moving them to the main field?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛwo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa seedlings generally stay in the nursery for 4 to 6 months until they develop a strong root system and multiple mature leaves, which helps them survive the transition to the main farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji 4 kɛyashi 6 kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ náa shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ baai babaoo ni eda. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ yeɔ wala yɛ tsakemɔ ni yaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes the seeds inside to sprout or rot, destroying bean quality and attracting pests and diseases that can harm future harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. efiteɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni egbalaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baanyɛ aye ŋmeii ni abaakpa wɔsɛɛ lɛ awui lɛ kɛbaa.

english: How does clearing weeds early in the season help my crops yield more?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Weeds compete with young crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing them early removes this competition, allowing your main crop to establish a deep root system and produce better yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Jiemɔ amɛ mra. Enɛ baajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. Ha onibii titrii lɛ afee gbɛjianɔtoo ni shishifãi yɔɔ mli ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Can I plant cassava alongside my young cocoa trees, or will it harm them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe? Aloo ebaaye kookoo tso lɛ awui?

english: Cassava grows rapidly and consumes significant nutrients and sunlight, which can choke young cocoa seedlings. It is better to use plantains or food crops that provide high shade without overcrowding the cocoa.
ga: Cassava daa oya ni eyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la babaoo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ plantains loo niyenii tsei krokomɛi ni haa hulutsoo ni nɔ kwɔ atsu nii ni akɛwooo kookoo lɛ mli tsɔ.

english: How should I cut my cassava stems when preparing them for planting so they grow well?
ga: Te esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ oha tɛŋŋ beni osaa ohe koni odu amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems should not be cut carelessly or bruised. Making clean, angled cuts with a sharp tool ensures the stem buds stay healthy, helping the cutting sprout strong roots quickly without rotting in the soil.
ga: Esaaa akɛ afoɔ ŋmei tso lɛ shishi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo atswaa lɛ. Nibii ni he tse, ni akɛ dɛŋdade ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni afo lɛ koni amɛwo shishifãi ni wa oya ni amɛfiteee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some farmers graft fruit trees instead of just planting seeds directly in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ aduawai aniji shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds can give unpredictable results, but grafting uses skilled cutting techniques to attach a high-yielding branch to a strong root base. This guarantees the tree produces sweet, high-quality fruit much faster.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie yibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei ahe lɛ kɛ ŋaa ni akɛfoɔ tsei niji ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ fĩɔ shishitoo ni wa he. Enɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ tso lɛ baawo yibii ni ŋɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ oya kwraa.

english: Is there a right way to prepare sugar cane cuttings before putting them in the ground?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni ja ko yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa ŋmei ni afoɔ lɛ dani aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Yes, cutting the cane properly at the internodes without splitting the stem protects the growing eyes. Clean cuts keep moisture inside the stem so the plant sprouts evenly across your field.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ ni akuuu tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe. Kpojiemɔ ni he tse yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ada pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just chop off any branch I want from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ kookoo tso lɛ niji ni misumɔɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning requires proper care because cutting the wrong main branches can reduce your pod yields or harm the tree frame. Removing only dead or overcrowded shoots lets air and sunlight reach the trunk, which prevents pod diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ afo tso lɛ nine lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ kɛ́ afo tso lɛ nine titri ni ejaaa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha pod yibiiwoo aba shi loo eye tso lɛ fã lɛ awui. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akabote ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: What happens if I cut down an old cocoa tree to stump it at the wrong angle?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji ofo kookoo tso momo ko bɔni afee ni eshishifã lɛ ahi he ni esaaa?

english: If a stump is cut flat, rainwater collects on top and rots the wood down to the roots. Cutting at a smooth, sloping angle allows water to run off, helping healthy new shoots sprout from the base.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ Nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ tso lɛ kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ́ afo yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etse ehe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei heei ni he wa lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ shishi.

english: Why do I need to be careful when trimming extra suckers from my plantain plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ mihe nɔ jogbaŋŋ beni mifoɔ mi plantains lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Hacking out suckers roughly can damage the main plant's underground corm. Using the proper cutting motion keeps the mother plant healthy so all its energy goes into producing a heavy bunch.
ga: Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ Ebaanyɛ efite tso titri lɛ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni afo lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso ni ji nyɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: What is the correct way to cut a plantain bunch off the tree without ruining the next crop?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ plantains kuu ko kɛjɛɔ tso ko nɔ ni afiteee ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting too deep into the main stem can kill the follower shoots beneath it. Cutting cleanly just above the fruit stalk leaves the rest of the plant stable so the next shoot can grow well.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha sɛɛnyiɛlɔi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ agboi. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii lɛ nɔ ni he tse lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. koni tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ

english: How can I harvest my cassava roots without causing them to spoil quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa ŋmei shishifãi ni mikɛhaaa amɛgboi oya?

english: Hitting or cutting into the tuber skin with a cutlass leaves open wounds where rot sets in. Digging carefully around the roots and cutting the main stem slightly above the ground protects the cassava so it stays fresh longer.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei gbá ŋmei shishifã lɛ loo ofo lɛ, ebaaha pilamɔ ko ni mli tse ni ŋmei baanyɛ atsɔ mli abote mli lɛ ahi shi. Kɛji akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ tsu nii kɛbɔle he lɛ Shishifãi kɛ tso titri lɛ ni ooofo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmei lɛ he koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to keep my farm cutlass sharp when working on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔ mli tsɔnei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miitsu nii lɛ?

english: A blunt cutlass crushes plant stems instead of slicing them, creating ragged wounds that attract insects and fungi. A sharp blade creates a smooth cut that heals fast, protecting your crops from sickness.
ga: Kakla ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ baakumɔ tso lɛ shishi moŋ fe ni eeefolɔ mli. Enɛ haa fãji ni gbalaa kooloi kɛ ŋmeii baa. Lade ni naa wa lɛ feɔ pilamɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsaa oya. Buu onibii ahe kɛjɛ hela he.

english: Can using an unwashed cutlass to cut my crops spread diseases across my farm?
ga: Ani dade ni afɔɔɔ he ni mikɛfoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Yes, plant diseases travel on sap left on cutlasses. Cleaning your blade between cutting different trees or fields prevents you from accidentally transferring diseases from a sick plant to healthy ones.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ahe helai fãa gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ nu ni ashiɔ yɛ dade lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei loo ŋmɔji ni afoɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ ahe saamɔ Enɛ baatsi bo gbɛ koni okagbɛ hela kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ oshara mli.

english: Planting cassava and maize together lets you harvest maize early for quick food and income while the slow-growing cassava continues to mature underneath, helping you make the best use of your land.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome lɛ, onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa mra kɛha niyenii kɛ shika oya. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ yaa nɔ edaa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni oná he sɛɛ babaoo.

english: When plantains are planted too close together, their roots and large leaves compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to thin stems and smaller bunches of fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi wuji kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni aduawai lɛ feɔ kui bibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl during intense heat to reduce water loss through evaporation, but if they remain tightly curled all day, it is usually a sign of insect attack or a plant virus.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Shi kɛji akɛ ehi shi ni ebɔle ehe shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi loo tso mli hela ko ebatutua lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off the trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from water stress during dry spells, lack proper shade, or when tiny pollinating insects are missing from the farm.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Shade ni sa ni bɛ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollinate lɛ laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Yam plants naturally climb toward sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers, and lifting their leaves off the damp ground prevents leaf fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛfee hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ owó baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa baai lɛ amli lɛ anaa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the ground is flooded with excess water that prevents roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu ni fa fe nine ni haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow heavy green leaves but produce very few flower pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔlii ni mli tse shi ewoɔ fɔfɔii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen from enriched soil or fertilizer, they use all their energy growing stems and leaves instead of flowering and producing food pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔi ni ekɛ niyenii ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ

english: Why are my harvested cassava roots hard and woody inside instead of soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfee tso yɛ mligbɛ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become woody when the soil is packed too hard for roots to expand properly, or when the crop is left unharvested long after the dry season begins.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bafeɔ tso kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ. aloo kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaaa be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ shishijee sɛɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my tomato plants dry up and turn brown starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni amɛjeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This happens when rain splashes soil-dwelling fungi onto the lowest leaves, causing a common plant disease that slowly works its way up the stem if not managed.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ shwie ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ baa ni fiofio lɛ ekwɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii.

english: Why do I find small powdery holes in my stored maize grains after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa powda buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Powdery holes are caused by tiny insects called grain weevils, which hatch from eggs laid inside the seeds and feed on the inside of the maize during storage.
ga: Kplukai bibii ji mɛi ni kɛ powder bu lɛ baa. Atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmãa ŋmei ŋmei. Amɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ amli amɛyeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn yellow instead of staying dark green?
