ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow strong and green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore their dark green color and increase yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This natural fertilizer feeds the soil and helps your maize crop grow better in the next season without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli babaoo.

english: What is eating holes in the leaves and stems of my young maize crop, and how do I stop it?
ga: Te eji tɛŋŋ akɛ aye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a major pest in Ghana. You can manage them by applying recommended bio-pesticides early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed, or by dropping clean wood ash into the plant whorls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei wulu ko ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ eje kpo amɛmiitao niyenii lɛ atsu nii kɛkwɛ amɛnɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tso sũ ni he tse ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei ashishi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the ground is well watered?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by bacterial wilt, a disease that lives in the soil and blocks water from moving up the plant stems. Rotating your tomatoes with non-solanaceous crops like maize or cassava helps break the disease cycle in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa nu aya tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Tomatoi ni akɛ nibii ni jeee mono-ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa helai ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with tiny fruits when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ yibii bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and resources to grow thick stems and produce big, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni mli tse ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct sunlight because their root systems are still small and fragile. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the young seedlings from heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa lolo ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one high-yielding crop cycle. If you plant the saved seeds, the new plants will grow unevenly, produce smaller cobs, and yield much less grain than the original seed.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ato lɛ Tsei heei baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Ha cob lɛ afee bibioo. ni ehaa dumɔwui fioo kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting and turning soft inside if I delay digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛji mifo amɛ blɛoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots reach full maturity at a specific time depending on the variety, and leaving them in the ground too long makes them susceptible to rot organisms and loss of starch content, especially after heavy rains.
ga: Kɛjɛ ŋmei srɔtoi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli. Ni kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe oya, ni amɛmli starch lɛ hu baa shi. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: How do I know that the rain is strong enough for me to safely sow my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ miinɛ waa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui shweshweeshwe?

english: You should wait until the soil is consistently moist to a depth of about a palm's length after a major rain, rather than planting after the very first light shower, so your germinating seeds do not dry out.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛyashɛ aaafee tso kome mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do weeds in my crop field make my harvest so small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mikpamɔ lɛ faaa nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the first four weeks of crop growth ensures your plants get all the nourishment they need to yield heavily.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How long does it usually take for crops to fully mature before I can harvest and sell them?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii ko shwereɔ dani manyɛ makpa ni mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Most medium-term crops require about 5 to 6 months after planting to reach full maturity and peak weight before they are ready for market.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be teŋgbɛ lɛ ateŋ babaoo biɔ nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ dani amɛshɛ shweremɔ kɛ shwiili ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaaya jara nɔ.

english: Does my crop gain much size and weight during its final month in the farm?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ayibɔ kɛ amɛhewalɛ tee hiɛ waa yɛ amɛnaagbee nyɔji ni amɛye yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: Yes, the period between the fifth and sixth months is critical because crops do most of their bulking and weight gain during this final maturation stage.
ga: Hɛɛ, be ni kã nyɔji enumɔ kɛ ekpaa lɛ teŋ lɛ he miihia. Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baafee babaoo ni amɛbaaná muji yɛ naagbee dalɛ be nɛɛ mli.

english: What happens if I harvest my crops early at 4 months instead of waiting for 5 months?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mra yɛ nyɔji 4 mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mamɛ nyɔji 5?

english: Harvesting too early prevents the produce from reaching its full weight and size, resulting in smaller yields that sell for lower prices.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ kɛ elɛɛmɔ fɛɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa nibii ni afee lɛ faaa, ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ.

english: Why are some crops on my field bigger than others even though I planted them all on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dara fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ.

english: Variations in soil nutrients, sunlight, and water cause crops to mature into a sequence of different sizes—some reaching top grade while others stay medium or small.
ga: Tsakemɔi ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei daraa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Ekomɛi ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi hu kã he amɛji mɛi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ loo bibii.

english: How much weight should a healthy medium-sized produce item have at harvest time?
ga: Te esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ lɛ agbɔjɔ enyiɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: A healthy, medium-grade produce item typically weighs between 500 to 600 grams when properly cared for up to maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsiimɔ ji gram 500 kɛyashi 600 kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do market buyers group harvested produce into size one, size two, and size three?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ buɔ amɛkpamɔi lɛ anaa yɛ dalɛ kome, enyɔ, kɛ etɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grading crops into size categories helps buyers easily price produce, as larger sizes command higher market rates than smaller ones.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo yɛ amɛdalɛi srɔtoi anaa Eyeɔ ebuaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ni amɛleɔ amɛnibii lɛ ajara yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsɔnei wuji lɛ biɔ jarayeli nyɔmɔwoo ni nɔ kwɔ fe tsɔnei bibii lɛ.

english: What does it mean if my crop harvest is categorized as size two?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akɛ size 2?

english: Size two usually refers to medium-grade produce weighing around 500 to 600 grams, which is a popular standard for everyday buyers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Size 2 lɛ tsɔɔ nibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni tsiimɔ aaafee gram 500 kɛyashi 600, ni eji nɔ ko ni mɛi ni heɔ nii daa gbi lɛ sumɔɔ waa.

english: Why is it useful for me to weigh my harvested crops before taking them to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ masusu mikpamɔ lɛ he dani mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Weighing your produce helps you know the exact grade of your crops so you can set fair market prices and avoid being underpaid by traders.
ga: Kɛ́ osusu nibii ni oduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni oyɔseɔ bɔ ni onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ji lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oto jara ni sa. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ jarayelɔi ni woɔ bo nyɔmɔ fioo lɛ ahe

english: How can I make sure consumers in Ghana like the crops I bring to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ Ghana lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Ghanaian consumers prefer clean, fully matured produce, so allowing your crops to grow to their proper weight over 5 to 6 months ensures strong market demand.
ga: Ghana jarayelɔi sumɔɔ nibii ni he tse, ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ oha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara kɛyashɛ amɛhe ni sa yɛ nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 mli lɛ, no haa jarayeli nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ baaná nɔmimaa.

english: What steps should I take to get my crops ready for sale once they reach 5 months of age?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni masaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni mahɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛye nyɔji 5?

english: Once your crops hit the 5-to-6-month mark, inspect them, sort them by size sequence, and weigh them so you can present organized grades to buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛ nyɔji 5 kɛyashi 6 he okadi lɛ, kwɛmɔ amɛ, ni oto amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ bɔ ni amɛdalɛ ji lɛ naa. ni asusu he koni onyɛ okɛ grades ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their tender leaves lose moisture quickly and burn. They need nurse crops like plantains or shade trees to filter the sunlight and keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ koni ekɛjie hulu la lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. To survive heat stress, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy and water.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I harvest more corn from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani minyɛŋ makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely actually reduces your total yield because the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Overcrowded maize plants grow tall and weak, producing small, poorly filled ears.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Abɛi tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, toi lɛ daraaa, ni baai eyi mli obɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which plants need to build strong, green leaves. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting cowpeas in the same field as my maize help my crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which means their roots work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that nourishes both the cowpeas and the nearby maize.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ ŋmãa weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwo sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ fɛɛ hewalɛ.

english: Extra suckers act like competing mouths, stealing food and water from the main mother plant. Removing all but the strongest shoot directs all the plant's food into growing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ, ni amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ adara ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes split open right after a heavy rain comes after a dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ otsi kome ni hɔmɔ eho lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When a dry tomato plant suddenly gets a lot of rain, its roots take up water very fast, causing the inside of the fruit to swell quickly. The outer skin cannot stretch fast enough to hold the extra water, so it cracks open.
ga: Kɛ́ tomato tsei ni egbi lɛ ná nugbɔ ni naa wa Eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu oya. Ehaa aduawai lɛ amli shwieɔ oya. Hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ ehe oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ahi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ba.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetable crops look pale and stunted so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-vegetables lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that drink up water and fertilizer faster than your crops can. They also block sunlight, depriving your vegetables of the food and light they need to grow green and strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni baanu nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Etsiɔ hulu la hu naa. Enɛ haa aduawai náaa niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my yam mounds with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks direct hot sun from drying out the dirt. It holds moisture in the root zone, keeps the ground cool, and protects rich topsoil from washing away in heavy rains.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni eha muji akagbi. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishifã lɛ he. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akaho.

english: Why did my vegetable leaves burn and wither after I poured chemical fertilizer right against their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable lɛ baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are strong salts that burn plant roots and stems when they touch directly. Instead of feeding the plant, contact with concentrated fertilizer draws water out of the roots, causing the plant to dry up and die.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ shãa tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha tsei lɛ niyenii lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ kpe lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How can I tell if my maize is fully ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Look at the leaves and husks—when they turn brown and dry up, and the kernels become hard with a small dark spot at the base, your maize is mature and ready to harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhewolo lɛ—beni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni wa ni ŋmeii diji bibii yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-ŋmei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: How do I know when my rice crop is mature enough to cut?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-rice tsei lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafolɔ?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80% to 85% of the grains on the plant turn from green to a bright golden-yellow color and the heads begin to droop slightly.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ beni aaafee 80% kɛyashi 85% ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ni mli tse mli. ni yitso lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ fioo

english: Why do my rice grains keep breaking into pieces when I take them to the mill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice grains crack and break during milling if they are dried too quickly in hot sun or milled when they are either too wet or overly dry. Drying grains evenly in thin layers reduces breakage.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ baagbala ni amɛbaakumɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛmiitswa lɛ kɛji amɛgbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. loo pɛnte kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo egbi tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ agbimɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fãji lɛ baa shi

english: Why is it bad to store my harvested rice or corn while it is still a little damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ baato be mli ni edɔ fioo lolo lɛ?

english: Damp grains attract mold and fungi, which cause the crop to rot, smell bad, and produce dangerous toxins that ruin the food and reduce its market value.
ga: Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ, amɛfuɔ, ni amɛjieɔ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni fiteɔ niyenii ni ehaa jara ni akɛheɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes my growing corn leaves to turn yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged, which stops the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ mumɔ ni amɛkpaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops even when I clear the land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jɛmɛ dani midu nii moŋ.

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong, aggressive roots that adapt quickly to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your planted crops can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni wa, ni yɔɔ basabasa. Amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani otsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Rice plants have shallow root systems adapted to wet soils, and flooded water helps supply nutrients easily while preventing weeds from growing and competing with the rice.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni nu afua lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni anáa lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ akaye akaŋ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my field right before a heavy rain comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, heavy rain will wash the fertilizer off the field before your crops have a chance to absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but heavy rain is not expected.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi akpaaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and small, empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How do I prevent insects from eating up my corn after I store it in bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa lɛ beni mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Dry the corn thoroughly until the kernels are very hard, clean the storage area well, use airtight bags or clean storage drums, and keep the bags off the bare floor.
ga: Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Tsumɔ he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ vacuum kotoku loo nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli ni he tse atsu nii. Ni ha baagi lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ be ehi akɛ aaawo sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist, usually shortly after the rains begin and plants are actively growing, so the roots can safely absorb nutrients without getting burned.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ni tsei lɛ daraa oya lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛshãaa.

english: How do I know if my crop actually needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia mi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: If your crops grow slowly, produce small yields, or have weak, pale leaves, it usually means the soil lacks essential nutrients that fertilizer can replenish.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo Ehaaa yibii fioo loo eyɛ baai ni bɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it bad if I put fertilizer on my crops during a hot, dry period?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yes, applying fertilizer to dry soil without enough water can burn plant roots and waste nutrients, so it is always best to wait until the soil has sufficient moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning red after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso baai lɛ feɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ kɛji adu lɛ?

english: Leaves turning red can be caused by plant diseases such as amewaam or severe nutrient deficiencies in the soil, both of which prevent the plant from developing healthy green foliage.
ga: Tso hela ko, tamɔ amoeba, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee etsuru. Nibii enyɔ nɛɛ fɛɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What is amewaam disease and how does it affect my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji amoeba hela? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Amewaam is a crop disease that causes abnormal discoloration like reddening in plants, weakening their growth and reducing harvest yields if left untreated.
ga: Amewaam ji tso hela ko ni haa tsei lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, tamɔ tsei lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ. Nibii ni akpaa lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can a plant disease like amewaam spread to my whole farm if I leave it alone?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai tamɔ amoeba baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛji mishi amɛ pɛ?

english: Yes, crop diseases can easily spread from a few affected plants to your entire field through wind, rain, insects, or tools if not addressed early.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ tsei ni ena hela fioo lɛ amli kɛya he ni okwɛɔ lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kooloi bibii, loo nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ anɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ ajajeee mra

english: Why is it risky for me to try treating a serious crop disease alone without advice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni mikome too matsa tso hela ko ni naa wa ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Trying to manage a complex disease on your own can lead to using the wrong treatment, which wastes your money and can destroy your entire harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ obɔ mɔdɛŋ ni otsu hela ko ni mli wa he nii yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ ohe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha okɛ tsofafeemɔ ni ejaaa atsu nii. Enɛ fiteɔ shika ni ebaanyɛ efite nibii fɛɛ ni ofeɔ lɛ.

english: Where can I go to get expert advice when my crops have a problem?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana ŋaawoo ni jɛ ŋaalɔi adɛŋ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ naagbai miikpe lɛ?

english: You can visit a local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) office or speak with an agricultural extension officer in your district who can assist you with farm issues.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ loo okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ awie ni baanyɛ aye abua bo yɛ okwaayeli he saji amli.

english: What kind of guidance can agricultural officers give me about crop fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋaa okwaayeli he nitsulɔi baanyɛ awo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he?

english: Agricultural officers can inspect your farm to advise you on the exact type of fertilizer your soil needs, how much to apply, and the correct timing for application.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔi baanyɛ akwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛwo bo ŋaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, bɔ ni esa akɛ okɛwo mli lɛ falɛ ni sa kɛ be ni esa akɛ okɛwo mli lɛ he.

english: What should I do if I see strange symptoms on my crops that I do not understand?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina okadii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ? On a crop that I don't understand?

english: You should bring a sample or description of the affected crop to a local agricultural expert or extension officer so they can identify the cause and show you how to treat it.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ena naagbai lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii loo amɛhe saji aya okwaayeli he nilelɔ loo sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nɔkwɛlɔ ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ. Enɛ ji koni amɛna nɔ ni kɛbaa lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ bo bɔ ni ooofee otsa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to grow green and strong, or the soil has too much standing water suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Aloo nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking sap from the leaves, which can also spread diseases that stunt the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ lɛ ashwã

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from taller trees because strong direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil before their roots can spread.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji adɛŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do I need to put long sticks for my yam plants to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi niji kakadaji koni sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to make energy. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum light, leading to larger yams underground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, keeping the soil cool and moist during hot days while stopping weeds from stealing water and plant food.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of regular watering, or poor soil nutrients needed to support fruit development.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa daa loo sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ adalɛ ni bɛ

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves turn yellow and fall off. Harvesting at this time prevents roots from becoming hard and woody.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee nɔ ni wa ni amɛfee tso.

english: Why do my groundnut pods snap off and stay buried when I pull the plants out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut ŋmɔtɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfuɔ amɛhe kɛ́ mijie tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pods snap off if the ground is too dry and hard during harvest or if you wait too long after maturity when the stems connecting the pods to the plant weaken.
ga: Pods lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni ewa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Aloo kɛji omɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni edara sɛɛ beni tso lɛ shishifã ni kɛ tso lɛ yibii lɛ tsaa lɛ egbɔjɔ lɛ.

english: Why do buyers demand that I ferment and dry my cocoa beans before selling them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miisumɔ ni mafee kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni migbi dani mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation and drying develop the rich chocolate flavor inside the bean, stop mold from growing, and allow the cocoa to be stored safely without spoiling.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli ni agbiɔ lɛ haa kookoo yibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Etsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ naa ni ekɛ kookoo toɔ shweshweeshwe ni efiteee

english: Why do my harvested onions start rotting quickly when I pile them together in a warm room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Onions hold moisture and need cool, circulating air after harvest to cure properly. Storing them in hot, closed spaces creates damp conditions that cause rot.
ga: Sabolai lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehe miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ abɔle ehe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ aha edɔ ni aŋmɛ lɛ, ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize turn yellow from the bottom up when they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. The crop moves whatever nitrogen it has left to its newer, top leaves to keep growing, causing the older leaves at the bottom to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. Enɛ haa baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What will happen to my crop if I put three or four maize seeds in one planting hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa yibii etɛ loo ejwɛ wo ŋmãa bu kome mli?

english: Putting too many seeds in one spot forces the young plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because of this competition, the plants grow tall, weak, and thin, leading to very small ears or no grain at all.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ he kome lɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Yɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ daa, egbɔjɔɔ, ni egbɔjɔ, ni no haa efeɔ toi bibii waa loo ebɛ dumɔwui kwraa.

english: Cowpeas work as natural soil improvers. They capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil to feed the cassava, while their broad leaves cover the ground to keep the soil moist and stop weeds from taking over.
ga: Cowpea tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛdu ŋmei. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even when I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mi lɛ shwieee lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can pull water up from the soil. The plant wilts on purpose to shrink its leaf surface and conserve water, usually recovering once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Tsei gboiɔ kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ amɛbaagbɔjɔ baa lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaakwɛ nu nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi pɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes get more diseases when I plant them on the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ náa helai babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Diseases and pests specific to tomatoes survive in the soil long after harvest. Planting tomatoes in the same spot continuously allows those soil pests to build up in high numbers, whereas changing to a non-related crop like maize starves them out.
ga: Helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tomato nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ oya nɔ adu tomato yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo abua shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ amɛtsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe bɛ tsakpaa, tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye amɛ.

english: How do weeds hurt my yam crop if they are growing next to it?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ baaye mi sweet potato tso lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ sweet potato lɛ masɛi?

english: Weeds act like thieves by taking away the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your yams need to build tubers. If weeds grow unchecked early in the season, the yam plant loses its main growing window and will produce small, light tubers.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa sweet potatoes koni bulbs lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni atsaaa amɛ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, Sweet potato tsei lɛ baafite amɛ shishijee dalɛ gbɛhe lɛ, ni amɛbaawo ŋmeii bibii ni tsiimɔ waaa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant drops its blossoms to save energy and protect itself rather than trying to feed developing peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Mohu ɔ, bɔ mɔde kaa o maa ha nihi nɛ a ngɛ wae ɔ niye ní.

english: Does cutting off some of the healthy green leaves from my tomato plants help them produce more fruit?
ga: Ani mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, trimming off lower leaves and non-fruiting side stems prevents the plant from wasting food on unnecessary foliage. This forces the crop to direct all its water and nutrients straight into growing bigger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishigbɛ baai kɛ sɛɛ tsei ni wooo yibii lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akafite niyenii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ koni ekwɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekwɛ̃ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why did my bean seeds rot under the soil instead of sprouting after the heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep or planted in waterlogged soil, air cannot reach them. Without oxygen to breathe, the seeds weaken and soil fungi quickly cause them to rot before they can push shoots above the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Anyɛɛɛ ashɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he. Kɛji oxygen bɛ ni akɛmuɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ oya dani amɛtsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my sweet potato vines growing lots of heavy leaves but producing very small potatoes under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ baai ni tsii waa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: This happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, often from using the wrong fertilizer. High nitrogen tricks the plant into spending all its energy building lush top vines rather than storing starch in the roots.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ lakaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plant turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow strong and green. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves regain their green color and produce larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔi wuji.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily and leaves the soil weak. Beans and groundnuts are special crops that pull food out of the air and put it back into the dirt, naturally fixing the soil so your next crop grows better.
ga: Abele haa kooloi babaoo niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Ebaafi shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots for days, it suffocates them and allows water-loving germs to quickly rot the crop underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ashiɔ nu ni ebɔleɔ he. shishifãi gbii babaoo Ebaaha egbɔjɔ ni eha helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ afite shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔshi nibii oya.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off during very hot days without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: When the sun gets extremely hot, pepper plants get stressed and lose too much water. To protect themselves, they drop their blossoms instead of spending energy to grow fruits until the weather becomes cooler.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Pepper tsei lɛ baaná haomɔ ni nu babaoo baaje amɛdɛŋ. koni obu ohe he Amɛfɔ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: On scorching afternoons, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to conserve moisture, but it usually stands back up when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ, amɛdamɔɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to survive if I clear away all the big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi kɛji mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees on your farm creates a cool environment and protects the young leaves until the cocoa is mature enough to withstand full heat.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ fe hulutsoo lɛ to oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high in the air to catch full sunlight, which helps the plant create energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the hot ground where diseases easily spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni mli edɔ yɛ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: If too many young shoots grow around the main plantain, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Removing extra shoots ensures the main plant gets enough nourishment to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ he lɛ, amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops suffer so much more when the rain stops for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa amanehulu babaoo kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the little water left in the soil long before your crops can reach it. Clearing weeds gives your crops full access to every drop of moisture stored underground.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu fioo ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ayashɛ he. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nu ni mli ewo muji fɛɛ ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he gbɛ kwraa.

english: Why do worms attack my maize plants mostly in the early morning or evening instead of during the hot day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-abele tsei lɛ babaoo yɛ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ mli moŋ fe gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Most caterpillars and crop worms dislike the intense heat and sunlight of midday, so they hide deep inside the plant stem or soil. They only come out to feed when the air cools down in the morning, evening, or night.
ga: Kplukai kɛ tsei amli ŋmeii babaoo sumɔɔɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ shwane mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye niyenii pɛ kɛji hulu lɛ miitso waa leebi, gbɛkɛ loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant food that keeps leaves green and helps the crop grow strong before producing grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ dani amɛwoɔ dumɔwui.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall but only produce small, weak cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, causing them to grow tall and thin instead of putting energy into filling out big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii wuji amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow big leafy branches but give me very small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi shishifãi lɛ daraaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Too much leaf growth with tiny roots happens when the soil has too much nitrogen but not enough potassium. Potassium is the specific nutrient that helps underground roots swell and grow heavy.
ga: Baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine kɛ shishifãi bibii Ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Potassium ji niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiimɔ baa shi.

english: Yams rot underground when water collects in the soil mound without draining, or when small soil insects bite the yam skin and let waterborne rot fungi enter the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ gɔji ni nu bɛ mli lɛ amli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ ŋmɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ fite yɛ nu lɛ mli kɛbote ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat or dry soil. When the plant feels it does not have enough water to support fruit, it drops flowers to save its own life.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ bɛ Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi ashwie shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up during the hot afternoon even if I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Leaf curling in the heat is a defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves to expose less surface area to the hot sun, preventing water from evaporating faster than the roots can drink it.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe fioo. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ.

english: Why does cutting off side branches from my tomato plant make the fruits bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ haa aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches prevents the plant from wasting food energy on unnecessary leaves and redirects all the nutrients straight into growing larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Kpojiemɔ kroko ni fata he lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. ni okɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ lɛ aya tso yibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the tree branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, damp, and shady weather. Pruning heavy shade trees helps air and sunlight dry the pods and stop the fungus.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli. Tsei ni afoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni etsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the bunches start getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ mli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not go deep into the ground. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, strong winds can easily pull the roots out of moist soil unless the trunk is supported with a wooden pole.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ da waa lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ oya. ja akɛ tso ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant them immediately after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season usually only wets the surface and warms up the hot soil, which tricks the seed into opening but leaves it without enough steady water to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ pɛ mli dɔɔ. Enɛ lakaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛtswaa shi ehaa amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why are the maize seeds I bought from the agro-dealer failing to sprout after planting them in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ŋɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ beni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds can fail to sprout if they were stored in hot or humid conditions before sale, if they are past their expiration date, or if they were planted too deep in the soil where they cannot get enough oxygen to wake up.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni edɔ loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ dani ahɔ̃ɔ. Kɛji akɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii lɛ eho Aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ he ni enyɛŋ ená kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛte shi.

english: Why do crops grown from seeds saved from my previous harvest yield much less than fresh certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii ni faaa kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strength and disease resistance in the second generation. Certified seeds are specially produced under strict conditions to ensure every seed has maximum vigor and high yield potential.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he hegbɛ lɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa shishi koni dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu aná hewalɛ babaoo kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants scorch and burn after I apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo mli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated salts. If you apply them directly onto plant leaves or put them too close to the stem during hot sunlight, they suck water out of the plant tissue and cause leaf burn. Fertilizer should always be applied to moist soil near the root zone.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãji amli ni ehaa baai lɛ shãa. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do insect pests return to destroy my cabbage farm just a few days after spraying pesticides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaafiteɔ mi-cabbage ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Many contact pesticides only kill the adult insects present on the day of spraying, but leave unhatched eggs unharmed. Once those eggs hatch a few days later, a new generation of insects appears to feed on the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtswaa mɔ he lɛ babaoo gbeɔ kooloi ni eda ni jeɔ kpo yɛ gbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ. Shi shimɔ ŋmeii ni afɔko lɛ ni akaye amɛ awui. Beni nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, Etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii ayinɔ hee ko hu miiye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does weedicide kill grass weeds in my farm but leaves my cassava crop healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shi ehaa mi-cassava tsei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Selective weedicides are formulated to target specific plant body types, like narrow-leaf grasses, while broad-leaf crops like cassava remain unharmed as long as the chemical is applied correctly.
ga: Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahala koni akɛtutua tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ jwɛi ni baai lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ, tamɔ yucca lɛ, ehiii kwraa kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tube shapes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism. The maize plant rolls its leaves to shrink the surface area exposed to the hot sun, stopping water from evaporating out of the leaves so the plant can survive heat stress.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ afee bibioo. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ baai lɛ amli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ adamɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers before any tomatoes start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or insect attacks. The plant drops its blossoms to conserve energy and stay alive rather than spending resources on developing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baatsu nii koni akɛfee aduawai lɛ

english: Why are my cassava tubers very small and thin when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct, bright sunlight on its leaves to make food through photosynthesis. When shaded by big trees, the plant cannot make enough food energy to store underground in thick tubers.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Beni yɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse amli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot so fast when the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that multiplies rapidly in cold, wet weather. Raindrops splash fungal spores from the soil onto low-hanging cocoa pods, causing them to turn black and decay.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves turn yellow and stop growing when rainwater collects in my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the soil for too long, the roots drown, rot, and can no longer absorb nutrients, causing the plant leaves to turn yellow and starve.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboɔ, ni amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛmɔmɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ dɔŋŋ. Ehaa tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape from the tip, it usually means the plant is starving for nitrogen. The crop moves whatever nitrogen it has to the top leaves to keep growing, leaving the bottom leaves to yellow and die.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni baai lɛ aya nɔ ada. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very big and bushy with dark leaves, but produce almost no flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii ko kwraa bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing green leaves and stems instead of setting fruit. They need phosphorus and potassium to trigger healthy flowering and fruit production.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii. Amɛhe miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai kpakpai.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my maize seeds closer together in the row?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu mli?

english: No, crowding seeds together causes the plants to fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks with very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Dabi, kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni amɛbuaa naa lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Ayɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo ŋmeii bɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their young flowers before they turn into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi bibii lɛ fɛɛ dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by intense heat, drought, or when tiny beneficial insects called midges are not present to pollinate them. Moderate shade trees help keep the temperature cool so flowers can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ baaa koni ebafee pollination. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do small worms appear inside my tomatoes just as they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-tomato lɛ mli kɛ́ amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Moths lay invisible eggs on the blossoms or young tomato fruits. When the eggs hatch, tiny caterpillars bore directly inside the fruit to feed, which becomes visible only when the fruit begins to ripen.
ga: Kpɔŋɔ lɛ woɔ wɔji ni anaaa lɛ yɛ tomato fɔfɔi loo aduawai bibii anɔ. Kɛ́ wɔɔji lɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛbatsɔmɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. Ebaabote aduawai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni ena niyenii. Anaa enɛ pɛ kɛji aduawai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔmɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the same piece of land where I harvested pepper last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously in the same soil allows crop-specific diseases and pests to build up in high numbers. Rotating with a different crop family, like maize or cassava, starves those pests out.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ kɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo ni kɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaaha hɔmɔ aye nakai kooloi lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy or flat soil, cutting off oxygen and allowing rot fungi to attack. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni oha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: How can I tell if my vegetable crops are dying from lack of water or too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-vegetables lɛ miigboi yɛ nu ni bɛ loo nu ni fa fe nine hewɔ?

english: Plants lacking water will wilt and curl their leaves during the heat of the day to save moisture. Plants sitting in too much water will develop pale, yellowing leaves that look limp even when the soil is completely wet.
ga: Tsei ni nu faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaabɔle amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛbu nu he. Tsei ni yɔɔ nu babaoo mli lɛ baaná baai ni baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaafee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kwraa po.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to the local climate, so their seeds germinate instantly and absorb available water and plant food faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii oya fe dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: What makes my plantain trees fall over easily when wind blows, even before the bunches are mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa? Dani tsei niji lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can easily be weakened by tiny soil pests called nematodes or by heavy fruit bunches that make the stem top-heavy. Supporting the stems with strong forked wooden poles prevents them from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ oya. ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo kɛtsɔ tso yibii ni tsii ni haa tso lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to harsh sunlight and dry winds. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants suddenly full of ragged holes with tiny caterpillars hiding inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe baai eyi kɛ ŋmeii bibii? ni akɛtee mli

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on young maize leaves. Catching them early and spraying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts into the plant centers can save your crop before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni ajieɔ yi lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ehere onibii lɛ ayiwala dani efite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up, look twisted, and show yellowish spots?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnáa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers is the best way to keep your farm safe.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies loo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ena lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tips down the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ baa lɛ naagbee kɛmiiya teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the middle of the leaf means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for the plant to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea at the right time turns the leaves green again.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa waa koni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my plot after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and leave it in the ground, naturally enriching the soil for the next crop without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant gets inconsistent water, or when there isn't enough phosphorus in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly damp and applying balanced fertilizer helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náa nu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo be mli ni fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa awo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know the right time to dig up my yams so they do not rot in the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ otsi ŋmɔtɔ koni ekafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams are ready for main harvest when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up naturally. Harvesting when the plant stops growing keeps the tubers healthy and allows them to last longer in storage.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ be mli ni ekpa shweremɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni bulb lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and black when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ nii waa kɛ ediŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus that thrives in dark, wet conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air into the tree canopy, drying out moisture so the fungus cannot spread easily.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ni sumɔɔ nu ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ewo duŋ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ tso lɛ shishi. gĩ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ Fungus nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: Is it better to burn the bushes on my plot or clear them and leave the vegetation on top of the ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo majie amɛ ni mashi tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving cleared grass on top of the ground acts like mulch, keeping the soil cool and moist while breaking down into free plant food. Burning destroys organic nutrients and leaves the soil exposed to hot sun and heavy rain.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni ekɛ tsei aniyenii shwieɔ shi lɛ. Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from a recognized store instead of planting leftover seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ shwapo ko ni ale lɛ mli? Mohu ɔ, nyɛɛ du wuhi nɛ piɛ ngɛ ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Certified seeds are specially selected to give higher yields, resist common local pests, and tolerate short droughts. Seeds saved from past harvests slowly lose their strength, resulting in weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Eteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ be kukuoo he gbɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi fiofio, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do my maize plants dry up and die right after they produce cobs, even if there is still rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo ŋmãa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize is an annual crop with a fixed lifespan. Once it produces cobs and seeds, its life cycle comes to a natural end, and the plant directs all remaining energy into maturing the grain rather than keeping itself green.
ga: Abɛi ji tso ko ni yeɔ daa afi ni ehiɔ shi be fɛɛ be. Beni ewoɔ ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui lɛ Eshihilɛ be lɛ baagbe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eŋmaa lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ ehe eŋɔli.

english: Why do some varieties of maize mature in three months while others take four months to complete their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi komɛi heɔ nyɔji ejwɛ dani amɛshɛɔ amɛdalɛ he lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have different internal biological clocks. Early-maturing varieties complete their life cycle quickly to survive shorter rainy seasons, while longer-season varieties spend more time growing to yield larger cobs.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ mligbɛ wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswai srɔtoi. Tsoi srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ gbeɔ amɛshihilɛ be lɛ naa oya koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni efee kuku lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How does my yam plant know when it is time to stop growing leaves and start forming tubers underground?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni sweet potato tso ko leɔ be ni eshɛ ni esa akɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ebɔi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: Yam plants react to daylight length and seasonal humidity changes. As the season progresses, internal signals tell the plant to shift its energy away from growing vine leaves and start storing food underground in the tuber.
ga: Atomɔ tsei hereɔ hulu la kɛ be mli tsakemɔi yɛ fɛ̃i mli. Beni be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, okadii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛɛ tso lɛ akɛ ejie hewalɛ kɛjɛ wain tso lɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli. ni ebɔi niyenii toomɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eyitso mli

english: Why are my young tomato plants wilting and dying before they even produce flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei bibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigboi dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi po lɛ?

english: When crops die early, it is usually caused by stem rot, soil pests, or a lack of water and nutrients. Plants need proper root protection and soil care to complete their growth cycle and reach flowering.
ga: Be ni tsei gboi oya Bei pii lɛ, stem rot ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ Tsei lɛ ahe miihia ni abu amɛshishifãi ahe jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbe amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa ni amɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees produce pods for decades while others weaken and stop bearing fruit early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo tsei komɛi gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo oya.

english: Cocoa trees can naturally live for decades, but their productivity depends on continuous care. Trees that are pruned, protected from pests like capsids, and given adequate shade live longer and stay productive compared to neglected ones.
ga: Cacao tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Shi nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ damɔ kwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ nɔ. tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi Buu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ ahe ni oná hulutsoo ni sa. Amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai fe tsei ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow and dying early while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When the soil lacks sufficient nutrients like nitrogen, the plant prioritizes new growth. It pulls nutrients out of its older, bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to age and die early.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ baama shweremɔ hee nɔ. Egbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ daa ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why is it dangerous for me to plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell before the main rainy season truly starts. Seeds planted too early will germinate but then dry up and die because the soil loses moisture before the steady rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is mature enough to harvest, or if it has stayed too long in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa? Aloo ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Cassava is mature when lower leaves turn yellow and drop, usually between 9 to 12 months. If left in the ground too far past maturity, the roots become woody, fibrous, and lose their cooking quality.
ga: Cassava eda kwraa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtekeɔ bɔ ni edara ha. Shishifãi lɛ bafeɔ tso, amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni amɛhoomɔ sui lɛ baa shi.

english: If my plantain stem dies after harvesting the bunch, does that mean the whole plant is dead for good?
ga: Kɛji mi plantain tsei lɛ gboi yɛ be mli ni akpa ŋmeii lɛ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwu muu lɛ fɛɛ gbo?

english: The main plantain stem naturally dies after bearing fruit, but the plant leaves behind underground suckers. Cutting down the dead stem allows the young sucker at the base to grow into a new, productive plant.
ga: Plantain titri lɛ tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni ewo yibii sɛɛ. Shi tso lɛ baashi eshishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni egboi lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tso bibioo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ada ni etsɔ tso hee ni woɔ yibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my hot pepper plants curl up during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in hot afternoon sun is a defense behavior. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing excess moisture loss during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Baai ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji subaŋ ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni baa shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green, or that heavy rains have washed the food too deep into the soil where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before making small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop because of poor insect pollination or a process called cherelle wilt, where the tree intentionally drops extra flowers and small pods that it does not have enough water or food to support.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kooloi bibii ni bɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahewɔ loo gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilt lɛ hewɔ. he ni tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ shi He ni eshwɛ lɛ he ni nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot underground mainly when water collects in the soil without draining properly, which suffocates the roots and causes fungal diseases to build up.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses to the plant, or by extreme heat stress where the plant curls to protect itself from losing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni kɛ helai baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa tsei shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over so easily during rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains fall over because tiny pests called nematodes eat their underground roots, leaving the heavy stem without a strong anchor in the soil.
ga: Mifee ekãa ni migbee shi yɛ kooloo bibioo ko ni ebote mihe lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni yeɔ nii ni ji nematodes. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii lɛ bɛ ŋwɛi ŋta yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my yam leaves showing dark brown spots and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads rapidly across yam leaves during hot, high-humidity weather when rain splashes from leaf to leaf.
ga: Fuji hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose kɛ enɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ sweet potato baai lɛ amli fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ mli. Beni nugbɔ lɛ jɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ

english: Pepper blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by irregular watering, excessive heat during the day, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil during flowering.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi kɛji tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni fe nine yɛ gbi lɛ mli Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce empty shells with no seeds inside?
