ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'blind nuts,' happen when the soil lacks calcium during pod formation or when the ground becomes too dry while nuts are developing.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘blind peas’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ pod feemɔ be mli loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ be mli ni pea lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow slower when planted near large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daa blɛoo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ahe lɛ?

english: Large trees block the direct sunlight that vegetables need to make food, and their large root systems steal water and nutrients away from your crops.
ga: Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa aduawai kɛha nihoomɔ lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ. Ni amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dried grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot sun to keep moisture in, cools down plant roots, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and short roots that cannot absorb water fast enough to replace what burns off in direct sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a protective canopy until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛye shãa ni hulu la tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ najiaŋ. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam vines produce leaves that act like solar panels to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves lifted off the damp ground so they can catch maximum sunlight without rotting or catching soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ baai ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli nibii ni akɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛgbooo loo helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akamɔ amɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant takes whatever food it has left in its older, bottom leaves and moves it to keep the fresh top leaves growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni etsiɔ lɛ koni eha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: Groundnut plants have special bacteria living in their roots that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and turn it into natural soil fertilizer. When you harvest the groundnuts, that extra plant food stays behind in the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa ŋmeii Nakai tso niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it risky to sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often heats up the dry soil without soaking deep underground. If you plant immediately, seeds may sprout, but a few days of heat afterward will dry out the topsoil and kill the young seedlings before deeper rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaaa edɔ waa. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Shi yɛ gbii 2-3 ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɛ́ɔ ni tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny cobs when I sow the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing strong, all the plants remain thin and hungry, leaving them without enough energy to grow big cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ hewalɛ babaoo lɛ, tsei lɛ fɛɛ egbɔjɔ lolo ni hɔmɔ miiye amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ebɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: This black patch, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot pull up enough calcium to build the fruit. It is usually caused by irregular watering, where the soil switches suddenly between being very dry and very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fã diŋ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by excessive heat, lack of soil moisture, or heavy pest attacks. The plant sheds its flowers to save water and energy just to survive until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui waa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up, shrinking, and turning yellowish-green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus distorts the leaves so they cannot catch sunlight properly, which stops the root tubers from growing large.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ haa baai lɛ tsakeɔ bɔni afee ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ hulu la jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi shishifã lɛ naa koni ekadara.

english: Why is the inner leaf shoot of my young maize drying up while the outer leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ mli tsei lɛ egbi yɛ be mli ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ kã he amɛji eŋɔli lɛ?

english: This problem, known as 'deadheart,' happens when small stem borer caterpillars chew their way inside the main stalk. Because they eat the inner pathway that carries water up from the roots, the newest center shoot starves and dies first.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘tsui gbele’ lɛ baa kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii titri lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ mligbɛ gbɛi ni holeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ dumɔwui heei lɛ ni amɛgboiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as the main food for green leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away nutrients or when roots are trapped in waterlogged soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ daa lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo shishifãi lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts have special root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that helps your maize grow stronger without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops so the rain doesn't waste it?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii koni nugbɔ akafite?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing, but avoid doing it right before heavy downpours or during dry spells. Heavy rain washes fertilizer away, while dry soil prevents the plant roots from taking it in.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida lɛ. Shi kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa loo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsei shishifãi anaa koni amɛkabote mli.

english: Cassava roots need enough underground room to expand without fighting neighbor plants for water and nutrients. Planting cuttings about one meter apart gives roots the space they need to grow thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ewuuuu kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die if I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mifo cacao tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees or planting plantains around them creates a protective umbrella that keeps the air cool and holds moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Tsei lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Having too many shoots around one plantain stem causes them to steal food, water, and light from each other. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots, allowing the main plant to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ oyɛ plantain tsei ahe tsei babaoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha amɛye niyenii, nu, kɛ la ni jɛ amɛhe lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become extremely high or when they lack sufficient water. Heat stress stops flower pollination, so the plant sheds them to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe. Dɔlɛ haomɔ haa fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ lɛ kpo koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines up on tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tso yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce energy for growing big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they can catch sunlight easily and avoid soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni eshɛ amɛbaa lɛ he koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la lɛ oya, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ yeɔ amɛhe.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the underside of leaves, or by a plant virus. Removing sick plants quickly stops these insects from spreading the problem to healthy ones.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amli Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya lɛ haaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ agbɛ naagba lɛ amɛshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Does my paddy rice field need to be covered in standing water all the time to give a good yield?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ nu ni damɔ shi aha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: While lowland rice loves wet soil, it does not always need deep standing water to thrive. The key is keeping the soil continuously damp so the shallow roots can easily absorb food while preventing weeds from taking over.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ moŋ, shi jeee be fɛɛ be ehe hiaa nu ni mli kwɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Ehe hia ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii oya ni amɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted around them to block harsh sun and keep the soil moist during their first few years of growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves starting in a V-shape at the tips usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for deep green leaves and strong vegetative growth.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi efeɔ V yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni haa tsei lɛ daa waa.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil, giving nearby maize extra food without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii kroko ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmãa kroko.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after a light rain. If you put it down when the soil is completely dry, plants cannot drink it up, and heavy rains will wash it away before roots can catch it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kɛ okɛwo shi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ, Tsei nyɛŋ anu. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rains fall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Too much water standing in flat soil starves cassava roots of oxygen, allowing fungal diseases to multiply. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily so roots stay healthy.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off without producing any tomatoes during hot dry winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme dry heat dries out the sticky pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When a flower is not fertilized, the plant sheds it to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi ko Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the same land where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa tomato kɛkɛ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same plant family and suffer from the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them back-to-back lets pests multiply in the soil and attack your new crop much faster.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei akuu kome mli, ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa onibii heei lɛ oya kwraa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wood instead of leaving them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves up onto stakes catches maximum sunlight for energy and keeps leaves off damp soil where fungal leaves rot, leading to much bigger tubers under the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛtee tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ kɛha hewalɛ. ni etsĩ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ he ni baa lɛ fiteɔ fungus Enɛ haa yitso ni da kwraa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why does letting weeds grow in my farm cause my maize cobs to remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni shwereɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds eat the soil fertilizer, drink the groundwater, and block sunlight faster than your crops can. Clearing weeds early ensures all water and food in the soil goes directly to feeding your crop.
ga: Jwɛi yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nuu shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni otsĩ hulu lɛ naa oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do sword suckers grow into stronger plantain trees than broad-leaved water suckers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ klante tsei lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni he wa fe nu tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ?

english: Sword suckers grow from a strong, food-filled underground corm with thin spear leaves, while water suckers grow broad leaves early because they lack strong underground roots and food reserves.
ga: Sword suckers lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli wa ni niyenii eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ lanceolate Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ oya ejaakɛ amɛbɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ niyenii ni amɛtoɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from companion crops like plantains or shade trees because direct sunlight burns their young leaves and dries out essential moisture in the topsoil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ nanemɛi tsei, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbi.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crop plants compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak stems and smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground with stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight to make food, which grows larger tubers underground and prevents ground rot.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso wo sweet potato baai anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Enɛ baaha bulb lɛ adara babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akafite.

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a nitrogen deficiency in the soil, which happens when nutrients are exhausted or washed away by heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ eho loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hole amɛ.

english: How does adding dried animal manure help my land before I plant?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloo ŋmei ni egbi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ dani aduɔ nii?

english: Manure improves soil texture, helps the soil hold moisture longer during dry periods, and slowly releases essential nutrients to support crop growth.
ga: Manure yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ adalɛ fiofio.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my farm so it is not wasted?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii koni ekafite?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing, avoiding hot dry days or times right before heavy downpours that wash nutrients away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ gbii ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ loo bei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ he koni ekɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii.

english: What is eating holes in the center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the plant funnel and can be managed using neem extracts or recommended insecticides.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa, ni abaanyɛ akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu he nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground after long rain showers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil starves cassava roots of oxygen and promotes soil-borne fungi that cause the tubers to decay underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, inconsistent watering, or a lack of specific soil minerals like calcium.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium.

english: How do weeds harm my farm crops if I am already watering the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ mikɛ nu miifɔ tsei lɛ anɔ momo?

english: Weeds steal vital soil nutrients, space, and light away from your main crop, and they often harbor harmful insect pests and plant diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋwɛi kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ ahe. ni bei pii lɛ, amɛji he ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai baa.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves turn yellow and drop off when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan season, dry winds cause cocoa trees to lose moisture faster than their roots can drink it. Shedding leaves is the tree's natural defense mechanism to conserve water and survive the drought.
ga: Yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-decayed manure helps restore their rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ afee tamɔ bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally replenishes nitrogen back into your soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni amɛfɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack from swelling roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ yɛ shishifãi ni efuu lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into full sunlight, allowing the plant to make more energy. This extra energy goes down into the roots, producing much larger and healthier yam tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ babaoo. Hewalɛ ni fa nɛɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any fruits can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when soil moisture is inconsistent. Extreme heat stresses the plant and prevents proper flower pollination, causing them to drop off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or aphids, or by viral diseases spread by these insects as they feed on young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because roots absorb moisture before the sun gets hot, while leaves dry quickly during the day, reducing the chance of fungal diseases developing.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hegbɛ ni yɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Having too many shoots around one stem forces them to compete for water and nutrients. Keeping only two or three strong suckers allows the main plant to yield large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛyɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni bɔle tso kome he lɛ, ehaa amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tsei babaoo ni tsii.

english: Placing raw chemical fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the delicate outer tissue of the plant due to high salt concentrations. Placing it a few inches away in a circle lets roots absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ asɛɛ fãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Okɛ amɛ ato he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi yɛ kooyigbɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, a key soil nutrient. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and improves grain production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha dumɔwui lɛ afeemɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that pull nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the dirt. This leaves rich, natural fertilizer in the soil for whatever crop you plant there next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop during the middle of the day when it is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants fold or droop their leaves in intense afternoon sun to prevent water from evaporating too quickly. As long as the leaves bounce back in the evening, it is just the plant's natural way of protecting itself from drought.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛjieɔ amɛ yɛ shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he kɛkɛ.

english: How do I know when my yams are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and vines stop growing green, turn yellow, and dry up naturally. This yellowing shows that the plant has finished sending all its energy into growing the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kwraa kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ kpa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. turn yellow and naturally dry Nɛkɛ ŋmɔŋ su nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulb lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa.

english: My tomato plants have plenty of flowers, but why are the blossoms dropping off without producing fruit?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and shade helps the plant hold onto its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get more harvest from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani manyɛ makpa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔji amli?

english: Planting too close actually reduces your harvest because the crops will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to grow larger and produce more yield.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aba shi ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ agbo ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I just save maize from my regular harvest to use as seed for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni jɛɔ ŋmãa ni akpaa daa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Grains saved from high-yielding hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation, leading to smaller, uneven plants. Buying fresh certified seed each season ensures strong growth and the highest possible yield.
ga: Ŋmãa ni ahereɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛwoɔ yibii babaoo amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeee ekome. Dumɔwui heei ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the extra suckers growing on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Removing side suckers prevents the tomato plant from wasting its energy on extra leaves. This directs all the plant's food straight into growing bigger, healthier fruits that sell for better prices.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ tsiɔ tomato tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ yaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara kpakpa nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do armyworms seem to attack my maize leaves mostly during the night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi-corn baai lɛ fe fɛɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hide inside the stalk or under soil during the hot day to protect themselves from sunlight and predators. They come out at night when it is cool to feed on the soft leaf tissues.
ga: Fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei amli loo shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ koni amɛbaye baai bibii amli fãji.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops much more when the crops are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui fe tsutsu lɛ beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, weak roots that easily lose the struggle against aggressive weeds for water and plant food. Clearing weeds early gives young plants the uninterrupted space they need to build strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ta ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni mli wa lɛ nɔ oya koni amɛná nu kɛ tsei aniyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my crops grow small and yellowish even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daraaa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Plants turn yellow and stay small when the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Adding compost, animal manure, or the right fertilizer restores the soil's strength so crops can grow green and strong.
ga: Tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How can I make my tired farmland fertile again without buying expensive chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: You can restore tired soil by planting leguminous crops like groundnuts or beans, which naturally put nitrogen back into the dirt, and by plowing crop residues back into the field.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni akuɔ sɛɛ ashɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ

english: Why do groundnut plants push stems down into the ground after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛyaa shi beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants produce flowers above the ground, but once pollinated, they grow stems called 'pegs' that burrow into the soil so the actual peanut pods can grow and mature underground.
ga: Peanut tsei woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ amɛwo pollination Amɛyɛ tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my groundnuts rot in the dirt before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut pods rot when soil remains waterlogged for long periods or when harvesting is delayed. Planting in well-drained, loose soil and harvesting as soon as the inner pod shells show dark brown markings prevents rot.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo kɛ́ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ. Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Ni kpamɔ be mli ni pod lɛ mli lɛ ná okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni akafite.

english: Maize leaves roll up during extreme heat as a survival mechanism to reduce leaf surface area, which slows down water loss through evaporation until temperatures drop.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ baa lɛ hiɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi fioo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, drought, or heavy nitrogen fertilizer, as the plant gets stressed and cannot successfully pollinate its blossoms.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni naa wa he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ miihao ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wrinkle and curl up tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni amɛkpãa amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites, or viruses spread by whiteflies, which damage the growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa Enɛ haa baai ni miida lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Intercropping cassava and maize maximizes space and labor because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, leaving the slow-growing cassava to take over the field for the rest of the season.
ga: Cassava kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa gbɛ kɛ nitsumɔ yaa hiɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Ha ni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ aŋɔ dumɔwu lɛ nɔ yɛ be muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds always grow much faster than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to local conditions, allowing them to suck up water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crop varieties.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛheɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my stored harvested grains get destroyed by insects even after drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii fiteɔ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ eshɛ amɛnɔ po lɛ?

english: Sun-drying kills adult insects and reduces water, but microscopic insect eggs can survive inside the grains and hatch later in storage if the grains are not stored in airtight containers or treated with safe protection powders.
ga: Hulu ni shɛɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni eda lɛ ni ehaa nu lɛ baa shi. Shi kooloi bibii bibii babaoo baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli ni amɛfɔ koni akɛto sɛɛ mli. Kɛji jeee nakai lɛ, too dumɔwui lɛ yɛ tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo okɛ powda ni buɔ mɔ he ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe atsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees drying up and turning brown in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside them creates shade and holds moisture in the air, protecting the delicate leaves until the cocoa canopy matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Buu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up into tight tubes when the sun is hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant slow down water evaporation and survive dry spells.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why is my cassava crop growing tall with huge leaves, but giving me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or fertilizer added at the wrong time, the plant spends all its energy developing leaves and stems instead of storing food in its tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be ni esaaa mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ niyenii ato oyitsoŋ lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I plant four or five maize seeds together in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ feɔ ekome yɛ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to fight each other for water, light, and soil food. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough space to build thick stalks and produce larger cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do my garden egg and tomato plants drop their blossoms before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-egg kɛ tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Consistent watering and protecting soil with mulch help keep the soil cool so flowers can set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ miigba tsei anaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why does my plot of land yield less food every time I plant cassava on it year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmei, afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating with nitrogen-fixing leguminous crops like cowpeas restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nitrogen-fixing legumes tamɔ cowpea ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do fall armyworms destroy my maize leaves mostly during the night while hiding during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ fiteɔ mi-corn tsei lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ, ni amɛteɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Armyworms avoid the high day heat and predators like birds by hiding deep inside the central whorl of the leaf during the day, coming out to feed in the cool evening and nighttime.
ga: Armyworms tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi tamɔ okpoi ahe kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛhiɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi mli ni amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛyatao niyenii yɛ gbɛkɛ kɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines turning yellow before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Early yellowing in yam leaves usually means the roots are suffering from soil waterlogging, fungal rot, or a lack of essential soil nutrients needed during the tuber expansion stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra. This means that the roots have water retention in the soil, fungal rot, or lack of essential nutrients in the soil during the bulb expansion stage.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds when my crops are still tiny seedlings?
ga: Mɛni he je nɛ e he hia kaa wa je jwɛi ɔmɛ a he ɔ? Be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji dumɔwui bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, weak root systems. Weeds grow much faster and will steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before the young seedlings can establish themselves.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa ni ebaaju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ ama shi.

english: Why do my pepper bushes stop bearing fruit after two harvests, and how do I bring them back?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpa yibiiwoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔi enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maná ekoŋŋ?

english: Pepper plants slow down production when old stems exhaust their nutrients. Cutting back old branches and feeding the soil encourages fresh stems to shoot up and start flowering again.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ haa amɛfeɔ nii fioo be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hu faaa lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji momoi lɛ amli ni akɛ sũ ha amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei heei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛje fɔfɔii ashishi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees perform better when I plant plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa seedlings cool and preserving soil moisture during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily during strong windstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that need healthy soil to anchor firmly. If the soil is too hard, poorly drained, or infested with root-eating pests like nematodes, the root system remains weak and cannot support the heavy top weight of the plant.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni wa koni enyɛ ehi shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ Nu ni hoɔ oya loo kooloi ni yeɔ shishifãi tamɔ nematodes yɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ shwiili lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when the soil is ready for planting after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ he kɛha dumɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain, as the ground is still hot and dry below the surface. Wait until the soil stays continuously moist down to a depth of about four inches so your seeds do not dry out and die after germinating.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛyashɛ aaafee 4 inch bɔni afee ni odumɔwui lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge leafy stems but produce very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai wuji shi eshishifãi bibii waa lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of root tubers. Balanced nutrients, especially potassium, are needed for the plant to send energy downward to expand the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. niyenii ni ja titri lɛ potassium Ehe miihia ni tsei atsu hewalɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and curling tightly during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism maize uses to reduce surface area and slow down water loss in hot weather. The yellowing indicates water stress or a lack of nitrogen, which the roots cannot absorb easily without moisture.
ga: Leaf curling ji hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Yellow tsɔɔ nu mli haomɔ loo nitrogen ni faaa. ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ mlɛo kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during cold, damp, and overly shaded conditions. Rain droplets splash the fungal spores from infected pods, soil, or farm tools onto healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulutsoo fe nine mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli, shikpɔŋ, loo okwaayeli nibii amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. Severe heat stress prevents successful pollination, so the plant drops the unpollinated flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from around my yam mounds regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ato daa.

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your yam plants. Removing them reduces competition so the yam vines can photosynthesize efficiently and build larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-sweet potato tsei lɛ amli lɛ waa. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei baanyɛ afee fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛfee yitsei ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of small holes and powder when I store it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛto?

english: Insects called weevils lay eggs inside stored maize grains, especially if the corn was not dried completely before storage. The hatching larvae eat the grain from the inside out, creating holes and leaving behind fine powdery dust.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Lala ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Ehaa buji feɔ ni eshiɔ sũ bibii yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give maximum yield only in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their special traits, leading to uneven growth, smaller cobs, and lower yields in the next planting season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a vital soil nutrient, or that the soil has too much water, which suffocates the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ lɛ mli nu babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Beans naturally pull nitrogen into the soil. Adding extra nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend energy growing extra leaves instead of producing flower pods.
ga: Beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai krokomɛi amli moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔii ashishifãi.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and thin even though the stems and leaves look tall and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Cassava puts energy into stem and leaf growth instead of root development when the soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are planted too close together.
ga: Cassava haa hewalɛ kɛha tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ. Yɛ shishifãi ni baa lɛ najiaŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa wala yibii lɛ fa babaoo loo kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ.

english: It is best to wait until the rain has soaked the soil deeply at least two or three times so the ground remains moist enough for seeds to germinate without drying out.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ hoo lɛ shii enyɔ loo etɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any fruits begin to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by severe dry heat, sudden changes in watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakemɔ trukaa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato fruits get soft black spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Yɛ shishigbɛ dani ahoo?

english: This is blossom end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by inconsistent watering patterns.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot while still hanging on the trunk?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, heavily shaded conditions with high humidity and poor air flow.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tiny holes are usually caused by insects like caterpillars feeding on the leaves, which damages the plant and prevents it from forming a firm head.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii baa. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ ni ehaaa ewa.

english: Weed seeds lay dormant in the soil for long periods. Clearing the ground exposes these seeds to sunlight and rain, allowing them to sprout faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui nɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ. Ehaa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and dry up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by leaf spot diseases or underground pests like nematodes attacking the tubers, preventing nutrients from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbimɔ oya ji leaf spot hela loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ayashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: How long does it take for a cocoa tree to complete its growth cycle before harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tsei lɛ shwereɔ dani akpaa amɛ?

english: A full cocoa production cycle usually takes around 9 to 10 months from flower initiation through pod development until the pods are fully ripe and ready for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo lɛ feemɔ be fɛɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 10 kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔii ni baa lɛ anɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kwraa ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa harvest happen at a different time of year compared to my maize or vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa yɛ afi lɛ mli be kroko mli fe mi-ŋmãa loo aduawai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a perennial tree crop that requires almost a full year of pod growth and maintenance, whereas crops like maize mature in just three to four months.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni yeɔ daa ni heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi dani edaa ni ekwɛɔ etsitsii lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji etɛ loo ejwɛ pɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to thoroughly clear my farm before the cocoa harvest begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani kookoo kpamɔ lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds and underbrush before harvest makes it easier to move through the farm safely, reduces hiding spots for snakes and pests, and prevents pods from getting damaged during collection.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii dani akpa amɛ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe. Tsɔɔmɔ hei ni onufui kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teɔ shi yɛ lɛ shi. ni etsĩɔ pods lɛ anaa koni ekafite yɛ be mli ni abua naa lɛ.

english: How often should I clear the weeds on my cocoa farm during the growing season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ?

english: You should clear weeds 3 to 4 times a year, ensuring a thorough clean-up right before the major harvest season to keep the soil healthy and make harvesting smooth.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii shii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ afi mli, ni okwɛ koni otsumɔ mli jogbaŋŋ dani kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ aba. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ koni kpamɔ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: What happens to my cocoa pods if I allow weeds to grow very high around the trees?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji miŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi lɛ shwere waa yɛ tso lɛ he?

english: High weeds create high humidity around the tree trunks, which encourages fungal diseases like black pod disease and attracts pests that destroy ripe pods.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. tso shishi Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ he hewalɛ ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why is cocoa harvesting usually done with a group of people rather than by one person alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, afeɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kui amli moŋ fe ni afeɔ amɛkomekomei lɛ?

english: Cocoa harvesting involves several heavy tasks—plucking, gathering pods, breaking them open, and carrying wet beans—which are done faster and better when family or group labor is organized together.
ga: Cocoa kpamɔ biɔ nitsumɔ ni wa babaoo, tamɔ ŋmeii ni ajieɔ, ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ anaabuamɔ, ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ agbelemɔ kɛ amɛyaa he kroko. Afeɔ enɛ oya ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ato nitsumɔ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ wekui loo kui amli.

english: How do I know the right time to pluck cocoa pods from my trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Pods are ready to harvest when their color changes completely—usually turning yellow or orange depending on the variety—showing that the beans inside are fully mature.
ga: Pods lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji amɛhe su tsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ bɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers but only a few turn into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi fioo pɛ tsɔɔ fɔfɔi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Many flowers fall off naturally because they are not pollinated by insects, or because the tree drops extra flowers to save water and energy for the pods it can support.
ga: Fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ejaakɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Aloo akɛni tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi koni ekɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha ŋmeii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do some of my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young pods dry up due to cherelle wilt, a natural process where the tree thins out excess pods, or due to black pod disease caused by too much moisture and shade.
ga: Pods bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ cherelle lɛ ni egbo lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ejieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ. aloo yɛ black pod hela ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry weather to reduce water loss through their foliage, helping the tree conserve moisture and survive until the rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to stay healthy and green. It can also happen when the ground gets waterlogged, preventing roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the earth time or different plant types to recover.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ loo tsei srɔtoi lɛ be ni amɛkɛbaatsa amɛhe.

english: Why do the green pods on my cocoa trees turn black before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease known as Black Pod, which spreads quickly in very wet and shady conditions when air cannot flow freely through your farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli oya lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves get sticky and covered in dark spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ wa ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called aphids are feeding on your plants and producing a sweet waste liquid. This liquid attracts a dark mold that grows over the leaves.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ aphids lɛ miiye tsei ni amɛmiifee nu ni ŋɔɔ. Nu nɛɛ gbalaa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my cowpea pods when I open them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Be ni migbeleɔ lɛ?

english: Insects called pod borers lay eggs on the cowpea flowers, and when the young caterpillars hatch, they chew inside the pods to eat the growing seeds.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ pod borers lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ tsina fɔfɔi anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni eye dumɔwui ni miida lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains leave the ground flooded for days, the roots suffocate from a lack of air and start to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ.

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to push through. If the soil is too hard, stony, or dry, the tuber cannot grow straight or expand fully.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛtsɔ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo egbi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ adara tɛ̃ɛ loo amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kwraa.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or too much fertilizer, choosing to save energy rather than grow fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ooohala akɛ oookɛto moŋ fe ni ooodu aduawai lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Cocoa tso bibioo daa?

english: Weeds grow faster than young cocoa trees and steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crop, which slows down cocoa growth or kills the tree.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe kookoo tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ baaha kookoo lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo loo ebaaha tso lɛ agbo.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the surface. When the bunch of fruits grows heavy, the tree becomes top-heavy and can easily be pulled out of the ground by wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji aduawai akuu lɛ mli wa lɛ Tso lɛ bafeɔ ŋwɛi tsiimɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why is it important to turn or till my soil with a tractor before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ trakta atsake loo atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii dani adu ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Tilling softens hard soil, removes weeds, and allows crop roots to easily spread out and soak up water and nutrients from deep in the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ejieɔ jwɛi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: What does chemical fertilizer actually do to my crops when I put it in the soil?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer acts like concentrated food for your crops, giving them essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that help them grow taller, produce greener leaves, and yield more fruit or grain.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni mli wa kɛha onibii. Ehaa tsei niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni oha aduawai loo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Why do high-quality or certified seeds give a better harvest than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ loo ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ haa ŋmaa kpakpa fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaa ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and bred to resist local pests and diseases, sprout faster, and produce uniform, high-yielding plants compared to older, saved seeds.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akwɛɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi bibii kɛ helai, amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛwo tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni etsɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How do weed-killing chemicals work without damaging the main crops on my farm?
ga: Te tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awui?

english: Selective weed chemicals target the specific biology of unwanted weeds while leaving your main crop safe, saving you time and physical effort compared to weeding by hand.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahala lɛ tsɔɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ wala yibii pɔtɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha onibii titrii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe. Ekɛ obei kɛ omɔdɛŋbɔɔ baa shi kɛ akɛto jwɛi ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow even when there is enough rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that pests are attacking the roots and stopping the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ, loo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai etutua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkpa tso lɛ niyenii hamɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak plants that produce very small yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Will using chemical fertilizers on my land destroy my soil over time?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Using chemical fertilizers alone for many years without adding organic matter like animal manure or leaves can make soil hard and acidic, but using them in correct amounts alongside organic manure keeps the soil fertile long-term.
ga: Tsofai pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii afii babaoo ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai fataaa he Ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa ni efee acidic. Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii kɛfata ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How can I tell if insects are destroying my crops or if my plants have a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kooloi bibii miifite miŋmɔshi nibii loo hela emɔ mitsei lɛ?

english: Insects usually leave clear physical marks like chewed holes in leaves or bored holes in stems, while plant diseases often cause spotted or yellowing leaves, wilting, or strange mold growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shiɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, tamɔ bu ni amɛye yɛ baai amli loo bu ni amɛfo yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ tsei ahe helai kɛ baai ni yɔɔ srɔtoi loo ŋmɔŋ, ni shwieɔ shi loo ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to come up after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are planted too deep in the soil, if the soil is too dry, if pests or ants eat them under the dirt, or if the seed quality was poor to begin with.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Kɛji ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dumɔwui loo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ahe ehiii kɛjɛ shishijee.

english: How does burning the grass on my farm before planting affect my soil and crops?
ga: Te jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mishãa dani miduɔ lɛ saa mishikpɔŋ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While burning quickly clears the land, it kills beneficial organisms in the dirt and burns away important organic nutrients that your crops need to stay healthy throughout the season.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi amɛfiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni amɛshãa nibii ni he hiaa ni haa otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves often mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their deep green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛfee baai ni mli wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha edalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle and wither when I remove all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Keeping or planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain around them acts like a living umbrella, protecting them from heat and keeping soil moisture stable during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo amɛdumɔ Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi daa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy and will rot if submerged in standing water for too long. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa, ni amɛbaafite kɛji amɛtara nu ni ekã shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stems before any fruits start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when the ground gets too dry or when temperatures get extremely hot. Keeping the soil consistently moist by watering regularly and putting dry grass around the base as mulch keeps the roots cool.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni okɛaabɔle shishi lɛ he akɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily during windy rainstorms when they start carrying big bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support the weight of heavy fruit bunches during strong winds. Propping the stems with sturdy bamboo or wooden sticks gives them extra support so they do not snap or uproot.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tso ni mli wa tsu nii kɛfi tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha eye ebua bo babaoo. Koni akakumɔ loo akajie kɛjɛ shishi.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the funnel of growing maize. Catching them early and applying organic mixtures like neem seed extract or recommended treatments directly into the plant center protects the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu tsuɔ nii. Aloo, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to put tall bamboo stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo ŋmei kakadaŋŋ agbo koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight, which creates the energy needed to grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so the leaves get maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha tso lɛ yibii lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he, ni eha ehe atse kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juice from the leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. Controlling these pests early with neem oil spray helps keep the leaves healthy and open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni egbeleɔ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long hot spell before main rains start. Seeds planted too early may sprout and then dry up; waiting until the rains fall consistently ensures young plants get steady water to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa koni dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara.

english: Why did my crop leaves wither and dry up after I put fertilizer directly against the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer right against the stem causes fertilizer burn, drawing moisture out of the roots and damaging the plant. Fertilizer should always be placed a few inches away from the stem in a ring or line and covered with soil.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashã. Egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni efiteɔ tso lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo 2-3 inches kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ ring loo line mli ni akɛ sũ aha nɔ.

english: Does it matter which direction I turn a cassava stem cutting when pushing it into the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni atsake ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots struggle to grow upward while roots struggle to grow downward, resulting in weak plants and very small tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Ebaawa akɛ eshishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya shi. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ bulb bibii waa baa.

english: Why do some plantain shoots have narrow, sword-like leaves while others have broad, wide leaves when growing near the main stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei komɛi ahe baai bibii ni tamɔ klante lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ masɛi.

english: Shoots with narrow, sword-like leaves (called sword suckers) have a strong connection to the main mother plant's root system and produce large, heavy bunches. Shoots with broad leaves early on (called water suckers) have weak roots, trap less energy from the mother plant, and produce very small plantain bunches.
ga: Tsoi ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ klante. Tso lɛ shishifãi (ni atsɛɔ amɛ sword shoots) lɛ kɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ shishifãi lɛ kpãa gbee waa ni amɛwoɔ panicles agboi ni tsii.
