Tsei bibii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ yɛ shishijee bei amli (ni atsɛɔ amɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu) lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ato kɛjɛ tso nyɛ lɛ mli ni ewo plantain jwɛi bibii waa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow from the tip downward in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛba shi yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: This yellowing pattern is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for maize growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK around the roots helps the leaves turn green again and ensures big maize cobs.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmãa dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK fata shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni eda.

english: Why do the roots of my cowpea plants have small, round bumps attached to them when I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Ekã shi beni mifo mli lɛ?

english: Those bumps are called root nodules, and they are good for your farm. They host helpful natural bacteria that pull nitrogen from the air to feed your cowpea plant and improve the soil for the next crop you plant there.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ shishifãi. ni ehi kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ Amɛhereɔ adebɔɔ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛkɛha tsina tsei lɛ niyenii ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put strong wooden poles in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso ni wa awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need poles (stakes) so their green leaves can spread out high off the ground to capture maximum sunlight. Leaves that receive full sunlight produce more food energy, which flows down to build larger tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia stakes (pillars) koni amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Baai ni hulu la kpɛɔ amɛ fɛɛ lɛ haa niyenii hewalɛ babaoo. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ ŋmei agbo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why are the green leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and drying up in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that easily burn under strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains beside young cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu nurse tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu lɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms keep falling off the plant before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ewo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere nu kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming tight and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of the leaf, or a virus carried by whiteflies. Damaging these soft tissues prevents the leaves from expanding normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni whiteflies kɛyaa lɛ Nɔ ni fiteɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot of my maize plants and leaving tiny holes in the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛshiɔ bu bibii yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide in the soft, moist center whorl of the maize plant where they can safely eat young leaves. Treating the center shoot early prevents them from damaging the growing point of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛye baai bibii lɛ shweshweeshwe. Nibii ni afeɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe tsamɔ mra Ebaatsi tso lɛ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard and woody if I leave them in the ground past their harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: As cassava plants pass their ideal maturity age, they start converting stored soft starch inside the root into hard woody fiber to support old stem growth, making the tubers tough and difficult to cook.
ga: Beni ŋmei tso lɛ eho afii ni sa lɛ he. Ebaaje shishi etsake ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ewo tso mli ŋmeii ni wa mli koni eye ebua tso lɛ shishifã momo lɛ dalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewaa akɛ aaaho.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves dry up and turn brown during the hot sun season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is too hot, cocoa trees lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it from the soil. The leaves turn brown and dry up because the plant is struggling to keep enough water inside its main trunk and stems to survive.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni ehiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ etsitsi titri lɛ kɛ etsitsi lɛ mli koni enyɛ ehi shi lɛ.

english: How do shade trees keep my cocoa plants from dying when the sun is very scorching?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ atsĩ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ?

english: Shade trees act like giant umbrellas over your farm. They block direct, harsh sunlight, lower the air temperature around your crops, and stop the sun from quickly baking all the moisture out of the soil.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi wuji ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi ni ehaa hulu la lɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbi oya.

english: Can intense heat burn my crops even if I watered them recently?
ga: Ani dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ po?

english: Yes, extremely high temperatures can burn tender leaves and stems directly. Even if the soil has water, the hot air and bright sun can damage the surface of the plant faster than the roots can push cool water up to the leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, latsaa ni naa wa waa baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu moŋ Shi kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite tso ko hiɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ nu ni mli ejɔ kɛya baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes on hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward during the hottest hours to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This smart reaction helps the plant trap moisture inside its leaves until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Nɛkɛ ŋaa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i baa.

english: Why are small, young cocoa pods falling off my trees when the sun gets too intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Kojoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ beni hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When a tree experiences extreme heat stress, it drops its small pods to protect itself. By getting rid of the young pods, the tree saves its remaining energy and moisture to keep the main tree alive.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ kɛ hulutsoo haomɔ kpe Ebaashwie ŋmɔtɔ bibii. koni obu ohe he Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ni ooojie kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ baakwɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ koni tso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without forming fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the delicate pollen inside plant flowers, preventing them from forming seeds and fruit. When heat renders the flowers unusable, the plant naturally drops them to conserve water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataa pollen ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei fɔfɔi amli lɛ ahiɛ. Etsiɔ dumɔwui kɛ aduawai anaa Kɛ́ latsaa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii Tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: I see wavy, smoky air rising from my soil on hot days; is this heat haze burning my crop roots?
ga: Mina lasu ni miitswa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Ani nɛkɛ lasu ni mli edɔ nɛɛ miishã mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: That heat haze is warm air rising rapidly from dry ground under strong sunlight. It does not burn the roots deep underground directly, but it is a sign that the topsoil is losing its moisture very quickly to the atmosphere.
ga: Heat smog ji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni teɔ shi oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Eshãaa shishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Shi moŋ, eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ miiho oya kɛmiiya kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my crops turn yellow and drop off during a long period of bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When facing intense sun and heat, plants sacrifice their older, lower leaves to cut down on water loss. This allows the plant to send its remaining water and food to the younger leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpe Tsei lɛ kɛ baai bibii baashã afɔle koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ majeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cover the ground around my crops with dry grass during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha he ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It shields the soil from direct sunlight, keeping the dirt cooler and holding moisture in the ground much longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa muji lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it bad for me to water my vegetable crops in the middle of a hot, sunny afternoon?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ mawo aduawai anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli?

english: Yes, watering in the middle of a scorching day is wasteful because most of the water evaporates before the roots can drink it. Cold water on hot leaves can also shock the plant, so it is best to water early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni afɔɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ ji fitemɔ ejaakɛ nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Nu ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ akpokpo, no hewɔ lɛ, nu yɛ leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my cocoyam plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or it is getting too much harsh sunlight without enough water. Adding well-rotted manure or providing light shade will help the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni nu fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he loo akɛ hulutsoo ha lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Can I grow cocoyam under the shade of bigger trees on my farm, or does it require full sunlight?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi? aloo esa akɛ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ aná

english: Cocoyam grows very well in partial shade because direct, scorching sunlight can burn its broad leaves. Intercropping it under taller crops like plantains or palm trees helps retain soil moisture and keeps the leaves tender.
ga: Cocoa daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ. Dumɔ ni atsakeɔ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains loo ŋmei tsei ashishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo.

english: Why does my cocoyam plant produce very large leaves but only small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miiwo baai wuji waa lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the plant focuses all its energy on leaf growth instead of building tubers. Using balanced soil nutrients and ensuring potassium is present encourages healthy root and tuber development.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ he nii moŋ fe ni eeefee bulbs. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ nɔmimaa akɛ potassium yɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What is causing small holes in the fresh leaves of my crops, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai heei anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Holes in young leaves are typically caused by insects like beetles or caterpillars eating the soft tissue. You can control them by clearing hiding spots around your farm, hand-picking pests early in the morning, or spraying organic neem leaf solution.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ladybugs loo caterpillars ni yeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ hei ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Okɛ onine aŋɔ ŋmeii lɛ leebi. loo okɛ neem tso lɛ mli tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ afɔ nɔ

english: How do I know if my farm soil is fertile enough to grow heavy leafy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa ni tsii?

english: Healthy, fertile soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture without becoming soggy, and crumbles easily in your hand. If your soil is pale or hard, mixing in compost or dried manure will restore its nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli ni efoɔ oya yɛ enine mli Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Okɛfutuɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi mli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why is it helpful for me to spread dry leaves and grass around the roots of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ magbɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ashwã mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering bare soil around crops with dry leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool under hot weather, prevents moisture from evaporating quickly, and naturally decomposes to feed the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛbaabɔle Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe ni akɛ baai ni egbi (mulch) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya ni efite yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot after a season of heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water collects on your farm without draining, it suffocates the plant roots by cutting off air supply. Planting on raised soil beds or ridges allows excess water to run off, keeping roots healthy.
ga: Beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ saatso loo ŋshɔnaa lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl or droop during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl or droop in the heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and prevent losing water. As long as the leaves recover by early morning or evening, the plant is simply protecting itself.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle loo efo yɛ la lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni elaaje lɛ naa. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baaná hewalɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ. Tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛkɛ.

english: Can I plant cocoyam on the same plot together with plantain and cassava?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛfata plantain kɛ cassava he?

english: Yes, intercropping cocoyam with plantain and cassava works very well. The plantains provide helpful shade for the cocoyam, while the combination makes efficient use of farm space and reduces weed growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ plantain kɛ cassava fataa he lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Plantains haa cocoyam lɛ hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nɔ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ haa akɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa jwɛi ni shwereɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young crops struggle to grow when I leave weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal vital sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your main crops full access to what they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi lɛ to he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ aná nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ fɛɛ koni enyɛ eda waa.

english: How can I tell if my palm tree is dying of old age or if it is sick from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-palm tso lɛ miigbo loo hela miipiŋ lɛ?

english: Old age happens gradually over many decades with a natural slowdown in growth and yield, whereas disease usually causes sudden yellowing, leaf rot, or quick death that can affect trees of any age.
ga: Dalɛ baa fiofio yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ mli kɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ kɛ nitsumɔ mli nibii ni baa shi. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela lɛ haa tsei ahe tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgboiɔ loo amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ ená tsei ni eye afii srɔtoi fɛɛ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ.

english: How many years can a palm tree naturally live on my land?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ŋmei tso baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: A palm tree can naturally survive and stand on your farm for over a hundred years, though its best fruit-producing years usually happen during its first 25 to 30 years.
ga: Palm tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhi shi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli nɔ ni fe afii oha. Eyɛ mli akɛ afii ni woɔ yibii fe fɛɛ lɛ fɔɔ baa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Why does my old palm tree produce smaller fruit bunches now than it used to when it was young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm tso momo lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii fe bɔ ni ewo beni eji gbekɛ lɛ?

english: As a palm tree reaches old age, its trunk and roots become less efficient at carrying nutrients, which naturally reduces its yield even if the tree is completely free of sickness.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei dara lɛ Eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa he kroko. Enɛ baaha yibiiwoo aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ hela bɛ tso lɛ nɔ po.

english: Do all tree crops eventually die of old age, or is plant death always caused by pests and diseases?
ga: Ani tsei kɛ tsei fɛɛ baagboi yɛ naagbee? Aloo bei pii lɛ, kooloi kɛ helai ji nɔ ni haa tsei gboiɔ?

english: Just like humans, every tree crop has a natural natural lifespan; while diseases kill trees early, a healthy tree will eventually reach old age, stop producing, and die naturally.
ga: tamɔ adesai nɔŋŋ Tsei fɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli wala be. Kɛji hela lɛ gbe tso lɛ mra po lɛ, Shi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baagbɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, amɛbaakpa yibiiwoo, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛbaagboi.

english: Is it necessary to cut down very old palm trees if they are no longer producing good fruit?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni afolɔ tɛŋ tso momo ko kɛji ewooo yibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, once a palm tree becomes too old and unproductive, cutting it down frees up land, water, and sunlight so you can plant young, high-yielding crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ tɛŋ tso ko egbɔ tsɔ ni ewooo yibii. Kɛ́ afo lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la jeɔ kpo. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What happens if I leave very old or dead palm trees standing on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmei tso ko ni egbɔ loo egbo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Leaving old or dead standing trees wastes valuable space, blocks light from reaching smaller crops, and can attract dangerous pests like beetles that spread to your healthy plants.
ga: Tsei ni egbɔ loo ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ fiteɔ he ko ni jara wa. Etsiɔ la naa koni ekashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ladybugs, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: When is the right time for me to replace my old oil palm trees with new seedlings?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tso hee awo mi-oil palm tso momo lɛ najiaŋ?

english: You should plan to replace oil palms when they become too tall to harvest safely or when yield drops significantly, usually after 25 to 30 years of growth.
ga: Esa akɛ oto gbɛjianɔ ni okɛ o-oil palm lɛ atsake kɛji ekwɛ tsɔ ni onyɛŋ okpa shweshweeshwe. aloo be mli ni nibii ni afeɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi waa Bei pii lɛ, yɛ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 ni akɛdara lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my very tall, decades-old palm tree slowly drying out from the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-palm tso kakadaŋŋ ni eye afii nyɔŋmai abɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbi fiofio kɛmiijɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: When a very old palm tree reaches the end of its natural life cycle, its upper leaves slowly dry out and die off as part of the normal aging process rather than a contagious sickness.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei tso momo ko shɛ ebɔɔ su shihilɛ naagbee lɛ Eŋwɛi baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Egbiɔ ni egboɔ akɛ nɔ ni fata dalɛ nifeemɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ

english: Can fertilizer save a palm tree that is dying simply because it is too old?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua ŋmei tso ni miigbo akɛni egbɔ tsɔ hewɔ?

english: Fertilizer helps sick or underfed trees recover, but it cannot reverse natural old age; once a tree reaches the end of its lifespan, fertilizer will not make it young or productive again.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ loo ni ahaaa amɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Shi anyɛɛɛ aku sɛɛ atsake adebɔɔ naa dalɛ. Kɛ tsei shɛ amɛshihilɛ be ni he hiaa lɛ naagbee lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii haaa tso lɛ atsɔ gbekɛ loo ewo yibii ekoŋŋ.

english: How do tree crops like palms behave differently over time compared to seasonal crops like maize?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei, tamɔ ŋmei, feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ be mli tsei, tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Seasonal crops like maize grow, fruit, and die within a few months, whereas tree crops like palms grow slowly over decades, producing fruit for years before eventually dying of old age.
ga: Be mli tsei, tamɔ ŋmãa, baakwɛ̃, amɛbaawo yibii ni amɛbaagboi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni ji jwɛi, tamɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ daa fiofio yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli. Amɛwoɔ yibii afii babaoo dani yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants roll up their leaves like small tubes during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tamɔ jwɛi bibii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural way of saving water. By curling its leaves, the maize reduces the amount of surface exposed to the hot sun, stopping moisture from escaping so easily during dry conditions.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha ŋwɛi ŋta ni ŋmã lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ aba shi. ni etsĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje mli oya yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a vital food for plant growth. Applying the right fertilizer early gives the maize the food it needs to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsuɔ nii mra Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa.

english: Why did my maize farm yield very small ears this harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ miiwo toi bibii waa yɛ kpamɔɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Small ears happen when maize plants do not get enough water or plant food while forming cobs, or when seeds are planted too close together, forcing the crops to fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Toi bibii baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu loo tsei niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miifee lɛ. aloo kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when planting to get a big harvest?
ga: Te esa akɛ makɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: Planting maize with about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between plants allows each stalk to get enough sunlight, air, and room for roots to feed properly without competing with nearby plants.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ ni jɛkɛmɔ ni miihe ashɛ sɛntimita 75 kɛ tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimita 40 lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye nii. ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ akaŋ

english: Why do poultry feed buyers prefer yellow maize over white maize when buying in bulk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ kooloi aniyenii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ fe ŋmãa yɛŋ kɛ́ amɛheɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Yellow maize contains natural color nutrients called carotenoids. When chickens eat yellow maize, it gives their egg yolks a rich yellow color and healthy-looking skin, which market customers prefer.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni ji adebɔɔ mli su ni atsɛɔ lɛ carotenoids lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ mli. Beni kooloi yeɔ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmɔtɔ Amɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni amɛhewolo ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. ni ji nɔ ni jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ jara lɛ nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ

english: How can I know which crop variety local market women will prefer before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei srɔtoi ni maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli yei lɛ baasumɔ dani mabɔi amɛdumɔ?

english: Before planting season begins, ask local market traders what qualities buyers look for—such as taste, storage life, color, or cooking time—so you can choose seeds that meet high buyer demand.
ga: Dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ baaje shishi Bi mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ sui ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ, tamɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ, be ni akɛtoɔ, su loo be ni akɛhooɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ohala dumɔwui ni tsuɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ahiamɔ nii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ ahe nii.

english: Why should I buy certified hybrid maize seeds instead of using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa ni ji hybrid dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid harvests lose their strength over generations, leading to smaller yields and uneven growth. Certified seeds are fresh, uniform, and specially bred for high yields and disease resistance.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmaa ni akɛfee nibii sɔrɔtoi amli lɛ he waaa yɛ yinɔi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ji ehee, ni yaa nɔ daa ni akwɛɔ amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds early when my maize crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Be mli ni mi-abele lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young maize and steal water, sunlight, and soil food. Clearing them early gives your young crop total access to resources so it can build a strong foundation.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ etswa shishitoo ni wa ema shi.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of weevils so quickly while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shwieɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ oya nɛkɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weevils and mold thrive when maize is stored while it still holds moisture. Drying your maize thoroughly in the sun until the grains are hard makes the grain too dry for pests to survive and breed inside.
ga: Weevils kɛ mold lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to be mli ni edɔ lolo. Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ hulu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni ŋmeii nyɛŋ ahi shi ni amɛshwere yɛ mli.

english: Can I plant cassava on the same plot with my maize, or will one ruin the other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ? Aloo obaakpãtã tso kroko hiɛ?

english: You can plant them together safely because maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, leaving space and sunlight for the slower-growing cassava to expand afterward, giving you two crops from one field.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Shi he ko kɛ hulu la koni ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ alɛɛ mli sɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight can burn their soft leaves and dry out the soil. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide living shade umbrellas that keep the ground moist while the cocoa trees establish strong roots.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ji tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, cacao tso lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans in the same field where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can draw nitrogen out of the air and put it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize naturally fertilizes the ground and improves maize growth without needing extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the young leaves at the top, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants experience heat stress, lack of water, or irregular watering. When conditions are too dry or hot, the plant sheds its blossoms to save water and energy instead of producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei baawo yibii lɛ, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I cover the open ground around my crops with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi aha he ni etse ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, acts like a blanket that blocks heat. It slows down water evaporation from the soil, keeps the ground cool, and suppresses weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa

english: Why do I need to leave specific spaces between my crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ gbɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close forces them to fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources, light, and airflow to produce a healthy harvest.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa, la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe without air in the soil. Raising the soil into mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely so roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛfeɔ gɔji loo ŋmeii lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe. Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight, which their leaves use to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot, damp ground, exposing them to light and protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baakwɔ kɛyashɛ hulu la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Akɛ ebaai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni akɛduɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛwo la mli ni otsi helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and look dead in the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it up. They temporarily wilt to reduce leaf surface exposure and save water, but they usually perk back up once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Amɛbaagbi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛba baa lɛ nɔ ni amɛkpeɔ lɛ shi ni amɛbu nu he. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ amɛhe nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which prefer hiding inside the soft central funnel of maize plants to feed. Early detection and spraying the central leaf whorls are necessary to save the crop from severe yield loss.
ga: Nɔ ni fɔɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛtee amɛhe amɛwo ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli koni amɛye nii lɛ. Nibii ni anaa mra kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe Ehe miihia ni ahere ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ yibiiwoo ni baafite waa lɛ mli.

english: If I spray chemical pesticide on my cocoa trees today, does it mean pests will never attack my farm again?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie kookoo tsei anɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ etutuuu miŋmɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Pesticides only provide temporary defense and cannot give 100% permanent protection. Rain washes the chemical away over time, and new pests can still arrive, which is why regular monitoring of your farm is necessary.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ buɔ mɔ he yɛ be kukuoo mli pɛ. ni enyɛŋ ekɛ hebuu ni hiɔ shi daa 100% aha. Nugbɔ baajie tsofai lɛ kɛjɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai heei Obaanyɛ oba mli lolo Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ.

english: Why do black spots on a few leaves spread so quickly until my whole farm looks sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ baai fioo komɛi anɔ lɛ gbɛ eshwa oya aahu akɛ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ fee tamɔ hela mɔ lɛ?

english: Plant diseases are often caused by tiny fungal spores that travel through rain splashes, wind, or farm tools, rapidly moving from one infected plant to healthy neighbors.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal spores bibii kɛ tsei helai baa. ni tsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi, kɔɔyɔɔ, loo ŋmɔ mli nibii amli ni ejɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli oya kɛyaa amɛkutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die if I clear all the big trees off my land first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct, intense sunlight burns their leaves and dries out soil moisture before their root systems are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aba shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds right next to each other so I can fit more crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to fight one another for limited sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in tall, thin plants with very small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fioo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the roots are suffocating from too much standing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu efo shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo hewɔ.

english: Why does adding dried animal manure to my field help my crops grow better than soil alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi fata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ pɛ lɛ?

english: Manure adds essential plant food to the soil and improves its texture, allowing the ground to hold moisture longer so roots can feed easily.
ga: Manure kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Koni shishifãi lɛ aye niyenii mlɛo

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so thin and weak even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act as thieves in the farm, quickly drinking up the water and stealing the soil nutrients meant for your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ okɛbaatsu nii titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress from high heat, lack of water, or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni baahã fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the ground when the rainy season is heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked in water for too long, air cannot reach the roots, which causes natural soil fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why should I cut off good-looking extra branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji fɛfɛji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes excess foliage so sunlight and fresh air can pass through the branches, preventing damp conditions where diseases thrive and directing the tree's energy into producing pods.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekɛ helai srɔtoi aba. Tsɔɔmɔ ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni okɛfee pods.

english: How many years after planting will my new cocoa trees start producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni mi cacao tso hee lɛ baaje shishi ewo ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take about 3 to 5 years to start producing fruit. However, improved hybrid varieties can begin bearing pods in just 2 to 3 years if they are properly cared for and given enough water and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmeii feemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni aha amɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. They need temporary shade plants like plantains or bananas to shield them from excessive heat and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land has the right soil for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Cocoa trees grow best in deep, crumbly, dark soil that holds moisture well but drains easily so water does not stand around the roots. Very sandy, rocky, or waterlogged clay soils will cause the trees to grow poorly.
ga: Cocoa tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ ni hiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ shi nu hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ nu lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni ŋã yɔɔ mli, tɛi, loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant plantain or cassava on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantain loo cassava yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Yes, planting plantains with young cocoa is very good because the broad leaves provide vital shade to protect young cocoa trees. However, cassava should be planted further away, as its aggressive roots can steal water and nutrients from the cocoa roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ lɛ hi waa ejaakɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Shi kɛlɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ baanyɛ aju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do older farmers leave large forest trees standing on their cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ shiɔ koo mli tsei wuji yɛ amɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Permanent shade trees protect cocoa from strong winds, scorching sun, and heavy rains. They also drop leaves that rot into rich organic fertilizer and keep the soil cool during long dry seasons like the Harmattan.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Amɛshiɔ baai ni egboi hu akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ Harmattan mli.

english: Why are the green cocoa pods on my trees turning black and rotting during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and damp conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows air and sunlight to dry out the leaves, and clearing out infected pods stops the rot from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa baai lɛ agbiɔ. kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ koni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellowing and dropping leaves during the dry season are a survival mechanism when the tree suffers from heat stress and low soil moisture. Providing adequate shade trees helps reduce this moisture loss.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni faaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ hulutsoo ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Is it necessary for me to cut off the extra shoots growing out from the bottom of my cocoa tree trunks?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, these small shoots (called chupons or suckers) steal food and water away from the main trunk. Removing them helps the tree direct its energy into growing thick stems and bearing larger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ (ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons loo ŋmeii) juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ awo tso lɛ mli tsei ni mli wa kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: It is normal for a cocoa tree to produce thousands of flowers and shed most of them. Only flowers pollinated by tiny insects called midges turn into pods. Keeping leaf litter on the ground provides a moist home for these helpful insects.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa akɛ cacao tso ko baawo fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Nɔ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔii kɛ hulutsoo be. Fɔfɔi ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ baai amli jwɛi to shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I easily tell when a cocoa pod is mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: A cocoa pod is ready for harvest when its skin color changes completely. Green pods turn bright yellow when ripe, while red or purple pods turn to a reddish-orange color.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji amɛhewolo nɔ su etsake kwraa. Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsuru loo purple lɛ feɔ ŋmeii-tsuru.

english: Why must I ferment my cocoa beans after harvesting them instead of drying them right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli beni akpa amɛ lɛ, moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fermentation is what creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color inside cocoa beans. If you dry wet beans immediately without fermenting them, they remain purple, bitter, and chocolate companies will not buy them.
ga: Nɔ ni haa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ ni mli wa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji ogbi ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛwooo mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmeii lolo, amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni tsokolate nitsumɔhei lɛ heŋ amɛ.

english: Drying cocoa beans on the bare ground exposes them to dirt, stones, livestock waste, and moisture from the soil, which causes mold. Using raised wooden mats allows clean airflow under and around the beans for uniform drying.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ haa muji, tɛi, kooloi afɔfɔi, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa amɛnɔ. ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa Tso ni awo nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli tse tsɔɔ shishi kɛ ehe fɛɛ. Kɔfi ŋmeii kɛha ŋmɔlɔ po

english: Why do my young cocoa plants need shade from plantain trees when I first plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ biɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ adɛŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: When trees are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients. It also traps damp air inside the farm, which helps diseases like Black Pod spread quickly.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ hu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa helai tamɔ black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing at the base of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These extra shoots, called suckers or chupons, steal water and plant food from the main tree. Removing them ensures all the tree's energy goes into growing strong branches and cocoa pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo chupons. Ju nu ni odu niyenii kɛjɛ tsei wuji lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa tso lɛ niji kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree grow flowers on its main trunk instead of on thin stems like other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔii yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ moŋ fe tso lɛ shishifãi bibii tamɔ tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are heavy fruit. Growing directly on the thick trunk and strong main branches gives the pods the structural support they need so they don't break the tree as they expand.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ji aduawai ni tsii. Ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ niji wuji ni mli wa lɛ anɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akafo kɛji egbɛ eshwa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet and dark conditions. Removing infected pods quickly and trimming excess leaves lets sunlight in to dry out the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Jiemɔ tsei ni tsɛŋemɔ hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni ofolɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni eha hulu la lɛ aha ŋmei lɛ agbi.

english: Why do I see tiny white, powdery bugs on the leaves and stems of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa powda bibii lɛ? Su yɛŋ ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ

english: Those white bugs are mealybugs, which suck the sap out of your tree and can spread the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus. Spraying approved treatments early keeps their numbers low before they ruin the farm.
ga: Nakai kooloi yɛŋ lɛ ji mealybugs, ni nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ cocoa bud virus lɛ amɛshwã. Tsamɔ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ha yibɔ lɛ aba shi dani ofite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: A cocoa pod is ready to harvest when its skin changes color, usually turning from green to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting while still green means the beans inside are not fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji amɛhiɛ tsake su. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Kɛ́ akpa be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔji lolo lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ eshɛko he jogbaŋŋ lolo.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off due to dry weather stress, lack of nutrients, or lack of pollination by tiny insects called midges. Keeping soil moist with organic mulch helps the tree hold onto its flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ ahewɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Kɛ́ akɛ organic mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Can I use water from a nearby galamsey site to irrigate my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ Galamsey kpokpaa ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: No, water polluted by galamsey contains dangerous chemicals like mercury and heavy metals that poison crops, ruin the soil, and make the harvested food unsafe for people to eat.
ga: Dabi, nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ Galamsey lɛ mli tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ mercury kɛ dade ni tsii ni yeɔ awui kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii, efiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehaa niyenii ni akpa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni esaaa akɛ gbɔmɛi yeɔ.

english: How do I know if the stream water near my village is safe to put on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu ni yɔɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Safe water is usually clear, free of strong chemical smells, and supports natural life along its banks; dark, yellowish, or oily water caused by mining is a sign of contamination that will harm your plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni mli tse mli tseɔ. Tsofa ko ni mli wa bɛ ni efiɔ adebɔɔ mli wala ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ sɛɛ. Nu ni mli edɔ, ŋmɔŋ, loo fɔ ni jɛɔ ŋshɔ mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ muji ko eba ni baaye otsei lɛ awui.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I water them with muddy river water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo waa kɛ́ mikɛ faa mli nu ni mli ewo muji shwie amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Thick, muddy water coats soil particles and plant leaves with heavy silt, which blocks air and nutrients from reaching the roots and slows down the plant's growth.
ga: Nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sũ ni mli ewo muji lɛ haa sũ mli nibii bibii kɛ tsei ahe baai ahe kɛ sũ ni tsii. Enɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: If polluted mining water flows onto my land, can I plant cassava there right away?
ga: Kɛji akɛ nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ ho kɛba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, root crops like cassava absorb toxic chemicals directly from polluted soil into the edible tubers, making the crop dangerous for consumption until the land is tested and treated.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ tsofai fɔji kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni ayeɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara kɛha niyeli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni aka shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ ni atsu he nii.

english: Will heavy rainfall wash away all the bad chemicals left in my farm soil by dirty runoff?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie tsofai fɔji ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni mli ewo muji nɔ?

english: Rain washes away some surface dirt, but heavy pollutants bind tightly to soil particles and stay there for a long time, requiring organic matter or specialized soil treatments to fix.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ muji komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Shi muji nibii ni tsii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ahe ni amɛhiɔ jɛmɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi atsu nii koni akɛsaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow after bad water flooded my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni muji eyi he ni miyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves indicate that the plant's roots are damaged or suffocated by toxic substances and excess mud, preventing the crop from taking up essential nutrients.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofai fɔji kɛ muji ni fa fe nine lɛ efite tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ loo amɛmiigbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I protect my farmland if polluted water from town keeps spreading toward my fields?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he? Kɛji maŋ lɛ mli nu fɔŋ lɛ gbɛ eshwa miŋmɔji amli?

english: You can dig shallow drainage channels or raised earth mounds along your farm boundary to divert dirty runoff water away from your crops and keep your soil clean.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko. Aloo wo gɔŋ ko nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he koni okɛ nu ni hoɔ ni he tseee lɛ aya he kroko kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. ni oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ he atse

english: Can maize survive if standing water sits on my farm for a few days?
ga: Ani ŋmãa baahi shi kɛji nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Maize roots rot quickly in standing water; if flooded for more than two or three days, oxygen is cut off from the roots and the crop will die.
ga: Abele shishifãi fiteɔ oya yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli. Kɛji nu afua lɛ tee nɔ fe gbii enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ, afoɔ Oxygen kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboiɔ.

english: Which crops are best to plant on low land that gets flooded easily?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ adu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu shwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Rice and certain varieties of sugarcane grow well in wet conditions, whereas crops like cocoa, cassava, and maize will rot if planted in waterlogged soil.
ga: Omɔ kɛ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo, ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa baafite kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe to feed crop leaves to my livestock if bad runoff water touched them?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maha mikooloi lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nu ni hoɔ lɛ kɛ nakai baai lɛ kpe?

english: No, livestock can get sick or pass poisons into their milk and meat if they eat crop leaves covered in toxic sediment or polluted water residues.
ga: Dabi, kooloi baanyɛ aná hela loo amɛjie tsofai fɔji awo amɛ mliki kɛ amɛloo mli kɛji amɛye tsei ahe baai ni tsofai fɔji sũ loo nu mli nibii ni efite ehà nɔ.

english: What kind of soil is best for planting crops so they can grow healthy and strong?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe wa?

english: Sandy loam soil is usually best because it balances water drainage and moisture retention, allowing crop roots to easily breathe and absorb the food they need to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋã ni ji ŋã lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hiɔ shi lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛha tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛ mu ni amɛhe niyenii ni he hia amɛ koni amɛ dara lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm is good enough for crop roots to absorb nutrients properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good agricultural soil feels loose and crumbly when moist, rather than sticky like thick clay or loose like dry sand, which allows plant roots to spread out and drink up soil nutrients.
ga: Okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ kɛji edɔ. Mohu ɔ, e kpɛtiɔ kaa zu nɛ mi wa aloo e ngɛ kpɛe kaa zu nɛ gbi. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛnuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my sandy soil lose its nutrients so quickly when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Very sandy soil has large spaces between grains that let rainwater wash plant food straight down past the roots. Adding a little clay or loam helps hold nutrients in the topsoil longer.
ga: Shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ koni nugbɔ nu lɛ afɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ he kɛho shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ loo sũ fioo ko fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What type of soil mixture should I put inside nursery bags when nursing my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛfutuɔ nii esa akɛ mikɛwo grow bag lɛ mli beni mikwɛɔ aduawai dumɔwui anɔ lɛ?

english: A mixture of sandy loam soil with a small amount of clay works best in nursery bags because it holds enough water and nutrients without suffocating the tender young roots.
ga: Sandy loam ni akɛ shikpɔŋ fioo efutu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ grow bags amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛhiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa mli ni amɛhaaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why is it helpful to mix a little bit of clay into sandy soil when preparing seedling bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ fioo baafutu shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ mli beni asaa dumɔwui kotokui lɛ?

english: Clay acts like a sponge for nutrients and moisture. Mixing a little clay into sandy soil prevents water from draining away too fast, keeping plant food right where the seedling roots can reach it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ fioo ko futu ŋã sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Ha tso niyenii lɛ ahi he ko ni dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my seeds sprout nicely in nursery bags but stop growing after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ grow bag lɛ mli shi amɛkpaa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings often stall if the soil in the bag is packed too tightly or lacks essential nutrients, making it hard for young roots to draw up the energy needed for continued growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ yaa wɔɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ mli. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaajie hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara lɛ.

english: How do I prevent the soil in my crop polybags from getting waterlogged and ruining my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi sũ ni yɔɔ mi-crop polybags lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekafo nu mli ni efite mitsei lɛ?

english: Using loose sandy loam mixed lightly with clay allows excess water to drain out the bottom while still keeping the root area properly damp.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã ni akɛ shikpɔŋ fioo ko efutu mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my young crops looking weak and failing to grow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eda eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ lɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone isn't enough; plants also need essential nutrients from the soil. If the soil is too poor or compacted, roots cannot extract food, leaving the plant stunted.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Tsei hu taoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ajie niyenii. tsei ni egbɔjɔ

english: How do crop roots actually feed on the soil to make the plant grow tall?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei shishifãi yeɔ shikpɔŋ diɛŋtsɛ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ adara babaoo?

english: Roots collect food by sucking up soil water that has vitamins and nutrients dissolved in it. Loose, well-balanced soil makes it easy for roots to absorb this nutrient water.
ga: Shishifãi buaa niyenii anaa kɛtsɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ ni vitamini kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni egbɛ eshwa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni ja lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ nɛɛ.

english: What can I do if the land I want to plant on has soil that is too hard for crop roots to penetrate?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛji shikpɔŋ ni misumɔɔ ni madu nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa tsɔ ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ abote mli?

english: Hard soil can be loosened by tilling and mixing in lighter soils like sandy loam or organic compost, creating a soft medium where roots can spread easily and gather nutrients.
ga: Abaanyɛ ajie shikpɔŋ ni wa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tseee tamɔ ŋã loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nɔ ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛbua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa lɛ baa.

english: How can I keep my harvested cassava fresh for longer if I do not have cold storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ? Kɛji akɛ fɛ̃i tsu ko bɛ?

english: Cassava spoils quickly after harvest, but you can keep tubers fresh for up to two weeks by burying them in moist soil or damp sawdust in a shaded area, or by processing them into gari or flour.
ga: Cassava fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa. Shi obaanyɛ oha bulb lɛ ahi shi ehee kɛyashi otsii enyɔ kɛtsɔ sũ ni mli edɔ loo ŋmeii ni mli efɔ ni ooofu yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ efeemɔ ni akɛfeɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ nɔ.

english: Can I use manure from my livestock directly on my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Yes, animal manure adds rich nutrients to soil, but fresh manure can burn crop roots. You should dry and compost it for a few weeks before mixing it into your farm soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii heei baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. Esa akɛ ogbi ni okɛwo mli otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛfutu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why is my maize crop yield getting smaller every year even though I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mifeɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi lɛ? Ani eekwɛ̃ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting maize in the same soil every season drains nutrients. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and improves future yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa wɔsɛɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my maize plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-abele tsei lɛ amli?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied in split doses: once shortly after planting to build root strength, and again about three to four weeks later when the stalks grow rapidly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ: klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ koni ekɛma shishifãi lɛ anɔ hewalɛ. kɛ ekoŋŋ aaafee otsii 3-4 sɛɛ beni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ daa oya lɛ.

english: Yellowing and curling cassava leaves are typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Yucca tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Should I keep buying certified seeds from dealers or save seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ loo esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: While saving traditional seeds works, bought certified hybrid seeds produce higher yields and resist pests better. Replanting saved hybrid seeds usually results in weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni ekwɛɔ kusum dumɔwui anɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii. Shi dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni ahe ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛhe saji awo mli ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Will planting my crops closer together give me a larger harvest from my field?
ga: Ani tsei ni mikɛduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting crops too close causes them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin plants and poor yields. Proper spacing ensures each crop produces maximum fruit or grain.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso woɔ yibii loo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Is it beneficial to plant groundnuts and cassava together in the same field?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava with groundnuts works well. Groundnuts cover the soil to block weeds and add nitrogen, while cassava grows tall without competing for space in the early months.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Okɛ ŋmeii awo ŋmeii amli koni jwɛi akaje mli ni nitrogen lɛ aya hiɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ he ko akaŋ yɛ shishijee nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What causes my pepper plants to drop their flowers before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛwo yibii?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they suffer heat stress or lack water during dry spells. Mulching around roots and watering regularly keeps the soil moist and saves the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo nu ni bɛ mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops right after the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit ready in the soil and are adapted to sprout immediately with the first rain to capture light. Clearing weeds within the first three weeks gives crops the space to grow strong.
ga: Akɛ jwɛi dumɔwui woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni atsakeɔ amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛná la. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth. Applying well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea can restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni akɛ nitrogen fee tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the rainy season becomes too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains excess water easily. When soil remains waterlogged for days, air cannot reach the roots, leading to root rot and fungal decay.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my planted crops right after a good rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants already adapted to local soil conditions, so they quickly absorb sunlight and soil nutrients faster than young crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛfee nɔ ni sa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui bibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under direct hot sunlight. Plantains grow broad leaves rapidly, acting as natural shade umbrellas to protect cocoa until it matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ oya. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes exposes all the leaves to direct sunlight, helping the plant convert sunlight into energy to build much larger underground tubers while preventing soil-borne leaf diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ hulu la lɛ ewoɔ hewalɛ mli koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni dara babaoo yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe hu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ahe helai ahe.

english: Why does planting beans together in the same plot as maize help my crop yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the nearby maize and helps it grow strong without depleting soil quality.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni edaraa waa ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small bunches if I leave all the suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji mishi ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ni miida yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ

english: When too many suckers grow around one stem, they all compete for the same soil nutrients and water. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only one main stem that can produce a large plantain bunch.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tso titri kome pɛ ni baanyɛ afee plantains akui wuji.

english: Why do the yellow flowers on my tomato plants fall off without developing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants suffer heat stress or dry soil conditions. Maintaining regular watering during hot weather prevents the plant from dropping flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi shihilɛi. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why are the fresh leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by microscopic insects like thrips or aphids sucking leaf sap, or by viruses transmitted by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii waa tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to dig up my groundnuts from under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafo ŋmeii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the outer leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up, and pulling up a sample pod shows dark brown veins inside the pod shell.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ogbala sample pod lɛ kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ, etsɔɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ pod lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their green color and energy to grow, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is my cassava farm yielding smaller tubers every year even though I use the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii daa afi lɛ? Nɔ ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same piece of land continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating crops or letting the land rest helps restore soil fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer is most effective when plants have established roots to absorb it, usually about two to three weeks after germination, followed by a second application during flowering or fruit formation.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ tso lɛ etswa shishifãi ni ekɛbaaŋɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ aaafee otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni ŋmɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji nɔ ni ji enyɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔi loo yibiiwoo be mli.

english: Why does fertilizer work very well on my neighbor's field but seems to make little difference on mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli shi etamɔ nɔ ni ekɛ srɔtofeemɔ ko kwraa baaa mihe lɛ?

english: Fertilizer response depends on your soil's moisture, organic matter, and acidity levels; if your soil is too acidic or lacks organic matter, plants cannot absorb the added nutrients efficiently.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso hetoo damɔ sũ mli nu, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ acidity falɛ nɔ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ acid tsɔ loo ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni akɛfata he lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up and droop during the sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in intense heat is a natural defense mechanism. The plant closes its surface area to stop water from evaporating too quickly until the temperature cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tso lɛ ŋaa ehiɛ he lɛ koni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Flowers fall off when plants experience extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which encourages leaf growth over fruit development.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni haa baa lɛ daa fe aduawai lɛ adalɛ

english: Why are dark spots appearing on my tomato leaves and causing them to dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai anɔ ni ehaa tomato baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots are typically caused by fungal diseases that thrive in warm, humid conditions. Removing infected leaves early and avoiding watering from above helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ helai diji baa. Kɛ́ ojie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.
