english: Why did many of the crop seeds I planted fail to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ateŋ babaoo ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to germinate if they were stored in warm or damp conditions, planted too deep in the soil, or lacked sufficient soil moisture after planting.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do my crops yield smaller harvests when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the growing plants compete heavily with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in stunted growth and small fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii.

english: How do weeds growing in my farm cause my crops to produce low yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibii faaa?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, water, and sunlight that your main crop needs to grow strong, while also hosting pests and diseases that can attack your plants.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa onibii titrii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baanyɛ atutua otsei lɛ hu baa.

english: Why am I harvesting so much less food from my farm compared to what a farm is capable of producing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikpaa niyenii fioo kwraa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto nɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ he lɛ?

english: Low harvests usually happen because the soil has run out of nutrients after years of farming without replacement. Replenishing the soil with fertilizers and using good farming practices can help crops reach their full harvest potential.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ baa ejaakɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli ni awooo mli ekoŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni akɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi kpakpai tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ amɛkpamɔ he hewalɛ ni sa lɛ he.

english: What can I do to significantly increase the weight and amount of crops I harvest from my land?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ kɛ amɛfalɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: To boost your harvest, crops need proper feeding. Applying the right fertilizer at the right time provides essential nutrients that allow crops to grow larger, healthier, and yield far more produce.
ga: Niyenii ni sa he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni onine ashɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni ofɔ nii babaoo

english: Why does my land seem to produce less crop yield every single year even though I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Every time you harvest, crops take away vital nutrients from the ground. Over time, the soil becomes exhausted, leading to smaller yields unless you add nutrients back using fertilizers or manure.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni be shwieɔ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa yibiiwoo baa shi. Ja okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fata he ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli.

english: What exactly is fertilizer and how does it help my crops perform better?
ga: Mɛni tuuntu ji ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer is like food for plants. It contains key nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that nourish crops, helping them grow stronger, withstand stress, and yield maximum produce.
ga: Fertilizer tamɔ tsei aniyenii. Nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anáa hewalɛ yɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ haomɔ naa ni ehaa nitsumɔ babaoo

english: Is spending money to buy fertilizer really worth the extra harvest I will get?
ga: Ani shika ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛha ŋmaa kroko ni baafata he ni maná lɛ?

english: Yes, using fertilizer properly can increase your harvest several times over. The extra income you make from selling the increased yield usually far outweighs the cost of buying the fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ shii abɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shika kroko ni onáa kɛjɛɔ nibii krokomɛi ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ mli lɛ feɔ shika ni okɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwraa.

english: Is it true that crops grown with chemical fertilizers will make people sick or kill them if eaten?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ tsei ni akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ baaha gbɔmɛi aná hela loo amɛgboi kɛji amɛye amɛ?

english: No, fertilizers are plant nutrients, not poisons. When applied correctly according to instructions, fertilizer is absorbed by the plant to grow naturally, making the harvested food completely safe for human consumption.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ji tsei amli niyenii, shi jeee tsofai fɔji, kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi anaa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛdara yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa niyenii ni akpaa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesai ayeli.

english: Will using chemical fertilizer on my farm shorten my life expectancy?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha wala be afee kuku?

english: Fertilizers do not reduce life expectancy. As long as you handle farm inputs safely by following basic application guidelines, fertilizer is safe for both the farmer and the community.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haaa mɔ wala shihilɛ aba shi. Shii abɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii tsuɔ nii shweshweeshwe kɛtsɔ shishijee gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ bɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ahaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Fertilizer baafee shweshweeshwe aha okwaafoi kɛ akutsei lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Does eating food grown with fertilizer cause health problems for people in our country?
ga: Ani niyenii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii edu lɛ yeli baaha gbɔmɛi ni yɔɔ wɔmaŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná helai?

english: Food grown with fertilizer is chemically identical in nutrition to food grown naturally. Increased fertilizer use actually improves health by providing more food security and better nutrition for families.
ga: Niyenii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii duɔ lɛ yɛ tsofai ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo lɛ haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni anáa kɛ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa wekui lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people in my community say that fertilizer ruins human health, and is there any truth to it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ kɛɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ adesai ahewalɛ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ anɔkwalei yɔɔ mli?

english: That belief comes from misunderstandings and confusion between fertilizers (which feed plants) and pesticides (which kill pests). Fertilizers simply nourish crops and do not harm human health when used correctly.
ga: Hemɔkɛyelii ni tamɔ nɛkɛ jɛɔ shishinumɔ ni ejaaa kɛ futumɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli (ni haa tsei niyenii) kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi (ni gbeɔ kooloi) haa ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ shwereɔ, ni kɛ́ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeee adesai ahewalɛ nɔ awui.

english: Can applying fertilizer make my food crops dangerous to store and eat later?
ga: Ani mi niyenii tsei lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara akɛ mikɛbaato ni miye sɛɛ mli?

english: No, crops grown with fertilizer are fully safe to store and eat. Fertilizer only aids plant growth while in the soil and leaves no harmful toxic chemical residues in the harvested grain or fruit.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii duɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛtoɔ ni ayeɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa pɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eshiuuu tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ dumɔwui loo aduawai ni akpa lɛ amli.

english: Why do the young cocoa seedlings I planted dry up and die when the sun gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni miduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out their shallow roots before they can establish themselves in the soil.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Egbiɔ dani enyɛɔ ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack of soil nutrients, or when tiny pests like mirids damage the stems supporting the flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen lɛ fiteɔ tsei ni fiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, overly shady conditions where air cannot flow freely between trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ oya lɛ

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cover my freshly harvested cocoa beans with plantain leaves for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ plantain baai aha kookoo yibii ni akpa ehee lɛ ahe gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Covering cocoa beans allows them to ferment, a process that stops the seeds from germinating and develops the rich chocolate flavor and brown color buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛnáa tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crops turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize plants need to build strong stems and healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛma ŋmãa tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to plant a cassava stem cutting in the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be planted with the tiny raised buds pointing upward toward the sky so the shoots can sprout easily above ground.
ga: Esa akɛ adu fɔfɔii bibii ni afolɔ yɛ cassava mli lɛ. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do small insects eat holes through my dried maize grains after I store them in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli beni mikɛto ŋmɔ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These insects are maize weevils, which attack grains that still contain moisture or are stored in open spaces without airtight protection or approved protective dust.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji ŋmei ŋmeii. Etutuaa dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lolo loo akɛto he ko ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ akɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni haaa sũ loo sũ abu he lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot on my land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Why does fertilizer burn my crop stems if I put it right against the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shãa mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that draw water out of the plant stem, so it must be placed a short distance away near the roots where it can safely dissolve.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛto he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ fioo. ni abaanyɛ ajie lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my crops grow slower when my field is overgrown with weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo be mli ni jwɛi eyi miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your planted crops need to grow big and produce food.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsei ni oduɔ lɛ he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo niyenii lɛ mli.

english: Why do some imported seed varieties fail to grow well on my farm compared to our traditional local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto wɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Local seeds have naturally adapted to Ghana's specific soil types, weather patterns, and native pests over generations, whereas foreign seeds are bred for different climates and often require expensive chemicals and controlled conditions to survive here.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi anɔ. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛ Ghana kɛjɛ yinɔi babaoo mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, afɔɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi anaa. Ni bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni jara wa kɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔ lɛ he miihia koni anyɛ ahi shi yɛ biɛ.

english: How can I safely store seeds from my current harvest so they stay healthy for planting next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ ato shweshweeshwe? Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Drying your harvested seeds thoroughly in the sun and storing them in clean, airtight containers mixed with wood ash or dried neem leaves keeps moisture and insects out, ensuring high germination next season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsi ko ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso sũ loo neem baai ni egbi futu mli lɛ, ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii ahe. Enɛ baaha eda yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: What causes the soil on my farm to lose its strength, and how can I bring it back to life?
ga: Mɛni haa sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he waaa? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ?

english: Soil loses its nutrients when the same crop is grown repeatedly without rest. You can rebuild its strength by adding organic compost, animal manure, or leaving the land to fallow with leguminous cover crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. ni okpaaa Obaanyɛ oma ehewalɛ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young crops wilt and turn yellow during the intense afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crops lose water faster through their leaves than their shallow roots can absorb from dry soil under intense sun. Providing shade plants or applying mulch around the roots keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ fe amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Leaf curling and pale patches in cassava are signs of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects and infected stems. Using clean, disease-free planting cuttings prevents this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Niji ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do insects attack my maize plants more aggressively during warm, dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Warm weather speeds up the breeding cycle of pests like the fall armyworm, while dry conditions stress the maize plants, making them weaker and easier targets for pests to feed on.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ feɔ amɛhe oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa ŋmãa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ebaatutua lɛ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize, or will they fight each other for food in the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaashi akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil, which actually feeds the maize and improves your total harvest.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ ni ehaa okpamɔ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: When crops get too much water, their roots drown from a lack of air in the soil, causing the stems to turn soft and yellow while the lower leaves start to rot.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nu babaoo Amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ.

english: Why do my leafy vegetables mature in a few weeks while my yam crop takes almost a whole year to yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ shwere yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ heɔ afi lɛ mli be babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ nii lɛ?

english: Leafy vegetables focus all their energy into quick leaf growth above ground, while yam plants must build large vines first before slowly storing food underground in their tubers over many months.
ga: Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni daa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he nii. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni sweet potato tsei lɛ afee wain tsei wuji dani amɛdara fiofio. Okɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ tuber lɛ mli nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly in storage, and how can I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto lɛ? Ni te ooofee tɛŋŋ otsĩ naa?

english: Yams rot when stored in warm, damp places without good airflow or when cut during harvest. Building an elevated, shaded barn with plenty of breeze keeps the yams cool and dry so they last longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ afo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Kɛ́ ama ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni awó nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛgbiɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when I clear away all the surrounding trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight and high temperatures. They require shade from larger trees or companion plants like plantain to keep the air humid and shield their soft leaves from burning until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines. Staking lifts their leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight for photosynthesis, which provides the energy needed to form large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Staking baawó amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha fotosintɛsis. Enɛ haa anáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji.

english: How many suckers should I keep around my main plantain stem to get big bunches?
ga: Esa akɛ makɛ ŋmeii enyiɛ abɔle plantain tso wulu lɛ he koni maná ŋmeii babaoo?

english: It is best to leave only one active sucker alongside the main mother stem. Keeping too many suckers causes them to fight for nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in smaller and lighter plantain bunches.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi sucker pɛ ni tsuɔ nii lɛ yɛ tso titri lɛ masɛi. Kɛ́ akpa tsei bibii babaoo lɛ, ehaa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la he, ni no haa amɛfeɔ plantains bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning light green and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient crops need to produce deep green leaves and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts in the same farm as my corn help the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts have special nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer that improves the soil for companion crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛhaa tsei ni fata amɛhe lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crop stems help them stay healthy?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, blocks the sun from evaporating soil moisture, keeps the roots cool during hot afternoons, and prevents weeds from growing near your crop.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni aduɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu la lɛ naa ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekaho. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ naa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding in the funnels?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee mi-kone lɛ mli

english: This is typical damage from the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central growing shoot of the maize plant during the daytime and eat the leaves before they open up.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ fitemɔ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly droop and dry up during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This sudden drooping is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil organism that gets inside the root stems and clogs the tiny pipes that carry water up to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ yibii ni shwieɔ shi trukaa nɛɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni boteɔ shishifãi amli ni amɛtsiɔ paipii bibii anaa. ni kɛ nu yaa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell of many days, which will dry out the soil and kill seeds that have just started to sprout before the main rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ bei babaoo nyiɛɔ nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni egbeɔ dumɔwui ni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baa lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully grown and ready to harvest without digging everything up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the stem base begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaanyɛ ole be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and retain soil moisture, helping young cocoa plants survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for green leaf growth, and when soil lacks it, the plant moves what little it has to the newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baakɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them first naturally enriches the soil so your maize gets free nutrients later.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ mra lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaha o-corn lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛɔ he tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are too close, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other, and their roots fight for the same soil food and water, resulting in thin plants and small tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ bulb bibii baa.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot branches from my mature cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Extra non-fruitful branches suck food and energy away from the main tree. Pruning them allows airflow and sunlight through the tree, reducing black pod disease and encouraging bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni yibii babaoo bɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ he. Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa black pod hela lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa cocoa pods lɛ feɔ agbo.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young vegetables with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot days, keeps the roots cool, and prevents heavy rain from washing away topsoil.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny worms hiding inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the tight center whorl of young maize plants where they eat tender leaf tissue before the leaves open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa, he ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe fãji dani baai lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why am I advised not to place fertilizer right up against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɛɛ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishitoo lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer chemical salts can draw water out of the plant tissue, burning the stem and roots. Placing it a small distance away allows the roots to safely absorb the nutrients dissolved in damp soil.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ tsei ahe fãji amli. Ebaanyɛ eshã tsei akui kɛ shishifãi. Kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni kɛ shishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni mli ewo muji ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to build tall soil mounds or ridges for my yams instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa sweet potato gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, deep soil to expand downward without pushing against hard ground, allowing them to grow long, thick, and healthy roots easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ he miihia sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsiii amɛhe kɛyaaa sũ lɛ mli waa. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baadara kakadaŋŋ, amɛtsii, ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yam plants make food in their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines high off the ground so every leaf gets maximum sunlight while keeping leaves off wet soil where fungal rot can spread.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa aná hulu la babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akafee shikpɔŋ ni efɔ yɛ he ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green, grow tall, and yield well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛdara, ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have tiny root nodules that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting like natural fertilizer for the crops planted after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear away all the big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Taller shade trees and plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ tsei bibii ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaakwɛ̃.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the vine produce food, which is sent underground to grow large, healthy tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa wain tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not go deep into the ground. When heavy rain softens the soil, the roots lose their grip, making the top-heavy plant fall easily under wind.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Shishifãi lɛ baafee mɛi ni nyɛŋ amɔmɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei ni amɛyiteŋ tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shishi oya.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in wet, cold weather when rain splashes water and dirt containing fungal spores onto the cocoa pods.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu kɛ muji ni ŋmeii yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are there small holes and saw-dust-like waste inside the middle leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmei ni tamɔ ŋmei?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing whorl of the maize plant and eats the young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaf and transferring plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ.

english: When the weather gets too hot or the plants do not get enough water, tomato flowers fail to pollinate and drop off as the plant tries to save water.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollin ni amɛgbee shi be mli ni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ nu ato he lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when heavy rain stays on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil stays flooded with water for a long time, air cannot reach the roots. Without oxygen, the cassava tubers drown and decompose underground.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni amɛbaafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young mango trees need wooden stakes or supports when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tso tso loo sɛɛfimɔ beni aduɔ lɛ lɛ?

english: Young mango seedlings have weak stems that can easily bend or break in strong winds. Supporting them with stakes keeps the stem growing straight and protects the root system from being disturbed while establishing in the soil.
ga: Mango tsei bibii yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni baanyɛ abɔle loo akumɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ damɔɔ shi shiŋŋ, ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ haomɔ he beni etswaa ehe shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know when my mangoes are ripe enough to pick from the tree?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni mango ko ekwɛ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Mangoes are ready for harvest when their shoulders widen, the peak of the fruit flattens, and the skin color shifts from dark green to a lighter green or yellowish tint. Picking them at this stage ensures they ripen properly without rotting.
ga: Mango lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji amɛtsitsii lɛ mli lɛɛ. Yibii lɛ yiteŋgbɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni hewolo lɛ su tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛyaa eŋɔli ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛho jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee.

english: What does it mean to process my mangoes, and why should I consider doing it?
ga: Mɛni ji mi mangoi lɛ ahe nitsumɔ tsɔɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu nakai feemɔ he?

english: Processing means turning raw fruit into products like dried fruit slices or bottled juice. This prevents losses when fresh mangoes spoil quickly during peak season, allowing you to sell higher-value products later.
ga: Nitsumɔ tsɔɔ akɛ atsakeɔ aduawai ni ahoko lɛ afee nibii tamɔ aduawai ni egbi lɛ mli fãi loo aduawai amli nu ni akɛwoɔ tɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite nii beni mango heei fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni mangoi lɛ fa babaoo lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ nibii ni jara wa waa yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How does drying mangoes keep them from spoiling after harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mango ni agbiɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ekafite beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Bacteria and mold need water to grow and cause rot. Drying removes most of the moisture from the fruit slices, stopping decay and allowing the mangoes to be safely stored for many months without refrigeration.
ga: Muawai kɛ ŋmeii taoɔ nu koni amɛdara ni amɛgboi. Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ mli. Kpaa fitemɔ ni oha akɛ mango lɛ ato shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo ni akɛwooo friji mli.

english: Why do my mango trees produce so many flowers, but many of the tiny fruits drop off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo, shi aduawai bibii babaoo shwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Mango trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can feed. The tree naturally drops extra tiny fruits to save its nutrients and water for a smaller number of healthy, strong mangoes to grow fully.
ga: Mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baashwie aduawai bibii. Taakɛ eji lɛ, koni niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni mango fioo ni mli wa lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Can I use any type of mango to make commercial juice?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mango henɔ fɛɛ henɔ afee jarayeli nu?

english: While most mangoes yield juice, varieties with smooth, sweet flesh and low fiber content are best. High-fiber varieties can make the juice pulpy or stringy, which consumers generally do not prefer.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ mangoi babaoo woɔ nu moŋ, shi mangoi ni mli tse, ni ŋɔɔ ni fiber faaa yɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Fiber srɔtoi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha nu lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ. ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ fɔɔ sumɔɔɔ

english: Why do my mangoes get dark black spots and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mangoi yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egboɔ be mli ni ekã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Dark spots are usually caused by fungal diseases like anthracnose, which thrive in warm, humid conditions. Pruning branches to let air and sunlight pass through the tree helps lower moisture and protects the fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ anthracnose, ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi, ni ebaabu aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: How can processing my fruit help me access larger government or commercial markets?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi aduawai lɛ ahe nitsumɔ baaha manyɛ maya nɔyeli loo jarayeli jarayeli hei wuji?

english: Large institutional buyers and government programs prefer processed items like dried fruit or juice because they have a long shelf life and are easy to transport, unlike raw fruits that spoil quickly during transit.
ga: Nitsumɔhei wuji ni heɔ nii kɛ nɔyeli nitsumɔi sumɔɔ nibii ni afee tamɔ aduawai ni egbi loo aduawai amli nu. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe nitsumɔ waaa. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ aduawai ni ahoko ni fiteɔ oya yɛ gbɛfaa mli lɛ.

english: Does my mature mango tree need heavy watering every day during the dry season?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni awo mi mango tso ni eda lɛ nu daa gbi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: No, mature mango trees have long taproots that reach underground water. In fact, a brief dry period encourages the tree to flower, though light watering during fruit growth helps the mangoes swell nicely.
ga: Dabi, mango tso ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifã ko ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, be kuku ni akɛgbiɔ tsei lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee fɔfɔi Eyɛ mli akɛ nu fioo ni akɛwoɔ enɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ baaye abua ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ.

english: Why should I trim off dead or overcrowded branches from my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ aniji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming or pruning opens the center of the tree to sunlight and fresh air circulation. This reduces disease risk, stops wasted energy on unproductive branches, and directs food to growing bigger fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ afo loo afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. ni haa hela baa shi Kpaa hewalɛ ni ofiteɔ yɛ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ anɔ. ni okɛ niyenii lɛ atsu nii ni okɛdu aduawai wuji

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and burn easily under direct, harsh sunshine. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that create shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Ha cacao bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure back into the soil helps the maize recover its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know which direction to stick cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava ŋmɔtɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes along the stem cutting. The buds should always point upward toward the sky when planted, allowing the new shoots to easily grow up into the light.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nodes lɛ jogbaŋŋ. along the stem cutting line Kɛji oodu lɛ, esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ kɛya la lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off before any peppers form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Blossoms drop off when plants get stressed by high heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Giving plants steady water and keeping the soil covered with mulch reduces stress so flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa ha tsei lɛ miihao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha haomɔ aba shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: What makes the leaves on my garden eggs curl up and turn sticky?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Leaf curling and stickiness are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking juice from under the leaves. Spraying the leaves with organic neem oil or soap-water solution gets rid of these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwie baa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Maize seeds need continuous moisture in the soil to germinate and establish deep roots. If you plant too early during uncertain rains, dry spells can scorch the seeds in the dirt before they fully sprout.
ga: Abele dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni bɛ faŋŋ mli Be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã shikpɔŋ lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves up off the ground to catch maximum sunlight for leaf growth and underground tuber formation. Staking also keeps leaves away from wet soil pests and diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ kɛ tuber feemɔ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How does removing weeds early in the season help my crops yield more produce?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the nourishment in the soil goes directly to your plants so they grow bigger and bear more food.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ shɛɔ otsei lɛ ahe. Koni tsei lɛ afee wuji ni amɛná niyenii babaoo

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow, they naturally feed and enrich the surrounding soil, helping neighboring crops grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ amɛdara lɛ Amɛbaaye shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ niyenii ni amɛha efee nii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua tsei ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do I need to dry my harvested maize thoroughly on a drying mat before putting it in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔji ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ anɔ dani mikɛwoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Drying removes wetness from inside the seeds that leads to mold, decay, and insect infestation like weevils. Grains that are dried properly stay safe and fresh inside storage sacks for many months.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. ni kɛ fungus fitemɔ, fitemɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii baa. Ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baahi shi ehee ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe yɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ amli nyɔji babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the surrounding soil. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving some trees in the field protects the young seedlings until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why should I not plant three or four maize seeds together in the exact same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ loo ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted in one spot, the growing plants compete with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This results in weak, thin stalks that produce very small cobs instead of strong plants with large ears of corn.
ga: Beni adu dumɔwui babaoo tsɔ yɛ he kome. Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ nu he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa toi wuji lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my dried maize grains turn into fine white powder after keeping them in the room for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ batsɔ powda yɛŋ kpakpa beni akɛto mitsu lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Small insects called grain weevils eat the inside of the stored maize and lay eggs there. To stop this, grains must be dried completely until hard and stored in airtight bags or containers so the insects cannot survive or enter.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ grain moths lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ jɛmɛ. koni akpa enɛ Esa akɛ agbi Dumɔwui lɛ kwraa ni akɛto kotokui loo tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli koni kooloi akajo foi loo amɛbote mli.

english: Why do all the leaves fall off my cassava plants during the harmattan season, and does it mean the plant is dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbo?

english: The cassava plant drops its leaves on purpose during the dry season to save water and protect itself from drying out. The plant is still alive, and the cassava tubers underground continue to stay good until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo. Ni ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baaya nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open on the sides right before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli gbala kɛmiijɛ sɛɛgbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato fruits split when they receive a sudden large amount of water after a long dry period. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to crack open.
ga: Tomato aduawai lɛ tswaa kɛji akɛ amɛbote nu babaoo mli trukaa beni amɛgbi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli fã lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ fãa.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping to the ground without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil gets too dry or waterlogged. When the plant is under stress, it sheds its flowers to save energy rather than producing fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi titri kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ tsei yɔɔ haomɔ mli Ebaajie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients like nitrogen. Planting it continuously on the same spot wears out those nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ afite. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why does adding dried poultry manure make my crops grow darker green leaves and bigger stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbi woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Poultry manure contains high amounts of nitrogen and organic matter, which act like food for the plants. Nitrogen helps crops build healthy green leaves and strong stems, while organic matter helps the soil hold moisture.
ga: Nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ kooloi amli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha tsei Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. yɛ be mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce less food even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most farm crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Even with good rain, the crops suffer because the weeds consume the food in the soil first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ awui ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ sũ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How does spraying water mixed with pounded neem leaves help keep insects away from my vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa lɛ efutu mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni kooloi akabote aduawai ahe?

english: Neem leaves contain natural bitter compounds that insects hate. When sprayed on crops, it stops pests from eating the leaves and disrupts their ability to lay eggs, protecting the plant without using harsh chemicals.
ga: Nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni kooloi nyɛɔ lɛ yɛ neem baai lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ afɔse tsofa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ kpaɔ baai lɛ yeli ni egbaa amɛnyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ naa. Buu tsei ahe ni okɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsuuu nii.

english: Why should I test a small sample of seeds before planting my entire field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka dumɔwui bibii komɛi aka lɛ? Dani abaadu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ

english: Testing a small sample of seeds in a wet cloth or small tray shows you how many will actually sprout, saving you time, labor, and money before you plant your whole field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii akamɔ Yɛ mama ni mli efɔ loo tsɛnsi bibioo mli Etsɔɔ dumɔwui ayibɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni baakwɛ̃. Enɛ baaha okɛ be, mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ shika akafite dani odu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to try a new chemical or fertilizer on just a few crops first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ oooka tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko okwɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi pɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Using a small portion of your farm as a sample area allows you to see how your crops react without risking your entire crop harvest if the mixture is too strong.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ mli he bibioo ko ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ he ko, ni baaha ona bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa ni okɛ ohe wooo oshara mli akɛ obaakpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ kɛji akɛ nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ mli eyi obɔ tsɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up during the hottest part of the afternoon in the Northern Region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ Kooyigbɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas fold their leaves to shade themselves from the intense sun, which helps the plant hold onto water and keep from drying out during hot days.
ga: Bush beans lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaaa egbi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when there is heavy rainfall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ waa gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: When the soil gets soaked with too much water, the crop roots cannot breathe or take in nutrients like nitrogen, causing the leaves to lose their healthy green color.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nu babaoo ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛnáaa niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, ni no baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does cassava stay green in the dry season while my other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants have deep roots and store water inside their thick underground tubers, allowing them to survive long periods without rain.
ga: Cassava tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛtoɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli tse amli. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ahiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stalks down into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miitsi efɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei lɛ kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants flower above ground, but the fertilized pods must push under the soil to form and grow the actual nuts safely away from the heat.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi esa akɛ ashɛre ŋmeii ni awo mli lɛ awo shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛfee ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo lɛ bɛ he.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by high heat, poor watering, or a lack of food in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. nu ni ehiii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato fruits get black rotten patches on the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes usually mean the plant is not getting enough calcium or that the soil drying out and getting wet too suddenly is stopping the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ naaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni edɔ tsɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my yam tubers are ready to harvest underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines above ground naturally dry up and turn brown at the end of the rainy season.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gĩ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee.

english: Why do weeds grow back faster than my sorghum crop after the early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-sorghum tsei lɛ yɛ leebi nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds naturally live in the local soil and are adapted to sprout very quickly with minimal water, while planted crops need more consistent moisture to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shi yɛ maŋ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni atsake lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya waa kɛtsɔ nu fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ biɔ nu babaoo ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛdara waa.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sun, causing them to dry out quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to cocoa provides living shade that keeps the seedlings cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ni egbi oya Kɛ́ oodu hulutsoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Cocoa masɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize crops are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or heavy rain washing away nutrients. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the plant produce chlorophyll and turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ efo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ chlorophyll ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot and spoil so quickly when left out in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High heat speeds up the ripening process and causes harvested tomatoes to lose moisture and sweat, creating warm, damp conditions where rot-causing bacteria and fungi grow rapidly. Storing harvested fruit in a cool, shaded place extends its shelf life.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha nihoomɔ lɛ aya oya. Ni enɛ haa tomato ni akpa lɛ mli nu kɛ latsaa sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo baa. Muawai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ daa oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tso yibii ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary to dry my harvested maize thoroughly before putting it into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ kwraa dani mikɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moisture trapped inside stored maize grains creates the ideal environment for mold and weevils to spread and destroy the crop. Drying the grains until they are hard prevents decay and insect damage during storage.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa lɛ kɛyashi ewa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa efite ni kooloi akafite lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot in the ground before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water accumulates in the soil around the roots, choking them and encouraging fungal growth, especially during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges improves water drainage and keeps the tubers dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ sũ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli, ni ehaa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe ni ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why is it wrong to plant cassava stem cuttings upside down in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ aaadu ŋmei niji ni atsɔ hiɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have natural growing nodes pointing upward; planting them upside down forces the developing stems and roots to grow in the wrong direction, wasting the plant's energy and resulting in weak growth and smaller yields.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ nodes ni daa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu shishi kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ adara yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fioo baa.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without producing any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress or prolonged dry spells. Giving pepper crops consistent water and light shade during very hot afternoons helps the flowers stay on and develop into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha pepper tsei lɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛtsɔ yibii.

english: Why do my nursery vegetable seedlings grow long and thin instead of sturdy and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ miidara kakadaŋŋ ni amɛmiifee mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch upward and become thin and weak when they are searching for light in an overly shady nursery. Providing balanced, indirect sunlight encourages seedlings to grow thick stems capable of surviving transplanting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe ni amɛbaafee mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛ́ amɛmiitao la yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli fe nine lɛ mli. Hulu la ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni sa ni akɛaaha lɛ baawo dumɔwui lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ.

english: How do I tell when my yam tubers are fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-sweet potato tubers lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up. This signal shows that the plant has finished transferring nutrients into the underground tuber for full growth.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai lɛ kɛ wain tso lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ewo ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves or straw during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baai egbi loo jwɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Covering the soil with organic mulch acts like a protective blanket that traps soil moisture, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the sun, and suppresses weed growth around your crops.
ga: Organic mulching tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: How does strong wind affect my crops if I farm on top of a hill?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛji mifee okwaa yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ?

english: Strong wind can snap tender stems, break plant branches, dry out soil moisture rapidly, and blow off flowers before they can turn into fruit.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tsei akumɔ, tsei aniji akumɔ, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi oya. ni etswaa fɔfɔii dani amɛbatsɔmɔɔ aduawai

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in windy weather even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Strong wind pulls moisture out through the plant leaves faster than the roots can pull water up from the soil, causing the leaves to dry out and droop.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi, ni no haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why is the weather on elevated land different for crops compared to flat lowlands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ srɔto kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Highland areas are generally cooler and windier than lowlands, which can help prevent fungal leaf diseases but requires protection against strong wind damage.
ga: Hei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ amli jɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa fe hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ baa helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ anaa. Shi esa akɛ abu he koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akafite lɛ.

english: What can I plant around my farm boundary to protect my vegetables from heavy wind?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ makwɛ yɛ ehe? Okwaafoi lɛ anaa koni akɛbu mi-vegetables lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he?

english: You can plant tall trees or dense tall grasses around your farm edge to act as a windbreak, slowing down strong breezes before they hit your fragile crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei kakadaji loo jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔle oŋmɔ lɛ naa koni etsu nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he tsɔne. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ aba shi dani ená oŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is a greenhouse and how does it help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji greenhouse ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A greenhouse is a shelter made of plastic or mesh netting that covers your crops, protecting them from bad weather, excessive rain, harsh wind, and pests.
ga: Greenhouse ji shĩa ko ni akɛ plastic loo ŋshɔŋlooi fee ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe.

english: Is it a good idea to build a greenhouse in a windy, hilly area like Kwahu or Akuapem?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaama ŋmɔ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa yɛ gɔji anɔ tamɔ Kwahu loo Aguapem?

english: Yes, high cool areas are great for greenhouses, but you must build a strong frame firmly anchored to the ground so high winds do not rip the plastic off.
ga: Hɛɛ, hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ji hei ni hi kɛha ŋmɔji ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo be mli. Shi ehe miihia ni otswa tsɔne ko ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ akagbala plastic lɛ.

english: Can a greenhouse protect my vegetables during the heavy rain season?
ga: Ani greenhouse baanyɛ abu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Yes, the plastic cover stops heavy rainfall from beating down on plants, preventing soil-borne diseases from splashing onto leaves and saving flowers from falling off.
ga: Hɛɛ, plastic ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ tsiɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa ni nɛɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ naa. Tsi helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa koni amɛkashwie baai lɛ anɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkagbee shi

english: Why do some crops grow better on sloped land than in low, flat valleys?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔji anɔ fe jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sloped ground allows excess water to drain away easily so roots do not rot, whereas flat lowlands can flood and suffocate plant roots.
ga: Hei ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbooo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ nu ashwie shi ni eha tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How do I stop rainwater from washing my fertilizer down the hill when I farm on a slope?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa gɔji anɔ lɛ naa kɛ́ miitsu okwaayeli yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ?

english: You can plant your crop rows across the slope rather than up and down, or build soil ridges to catch water and keep your fertilizer near the plant roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ moŋ fe ni ooodu ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ. Aloo feemɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni baaha nu ahi shi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii abɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing delicate crops like sweet peppers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ ŋmeii akwɛmɔ?

english: Delicate crops need soil that drains water well, reliable sunlight, and shelter from severe winds and flooding, which you can manage naturally or with a greenhouse structure.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. hulu la ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ he ni abaanyɛ akwɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nu afua mli. ni obaanyɛ okwɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa loo kɛtsɔ greenhouse gbɛjianɔtoo nɔ.

english: What is the best time of the day to plant my young cocoa seedlings in the main field so they do not die?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu cacao tsei bibii yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli koni cacao tsei lɛ akagboi?

english: It is best to plant seedlings early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is gentle. Planting during the intense afternoon heat shocks the young root system and causes the plant to lose water quickly and dry out.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui leebi loo shwane mli. ni ji be ni hulu la ni tsoɔ fioo lɛ baa Dumɔ yɛ shwane mli latsaa mli lɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe afee shoo. ni ehaa tsei lɛ nu fiteɔ oya ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree leaves turn yellow and dry up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in harsh, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to keep them cool and retain soil moisture until their own branches grow wide enough to protect them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛha amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ ni amɛhiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi amɛniji lɛ amli baagbɛ bɔ ni sa ni baabu amɛhe.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and suckers from my cocoa tree if I want it to bear more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fata mikookoo tso lɛ he lɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Extra branches and water suckers steal food and water from the main trunk. Cutting them off directs all the tree's strength into growing big, healthy cocoa pods instead of useless leaves.
ga: Niji kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishitoo wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ebaawo kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and humid conditions. When branches are too bushy and block airflow, rainwater sits on the pods and lets the disease grow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni amɛtsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Nugbɔ nu lɛ taraa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni ehaa helai shwereɔ.

english: Why do many tiny flowers fall off my cocoa tree without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbee shi kɛjɛ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if tiny insects called midges do not pollinate them, or if the tree is stressed by lack of water or poor soil nutrients and cannot support the weight of growing new pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kooloi bibii ba amɛnɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ efɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu ni bɛ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmeii heei ni miida lɛ amli tsiimɔ nɔ

english: Can I plant cassava directly next to my young cocoa trees, or will it harm my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe? Aloo ebaaye miŋmɔ lɛ awui?

english: Cassava is a heavy feeder that spreads wide roots and dense leaves, taking away nutrients and water from young cocoa trees. It is better to use plantains or cocoyams, which share space and soil much better with cocoa.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni tsii ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ plantain loo kookoo baatsu nii, ni ekɛ kookoo yeɔ he ko kɛ shikpɔŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes the young shoots on my cocoa tree to look burned and withered like fire touched them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ tamɔ bɔ ni la lɛ tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by mirids (also called capsids), tiny sucking insects that bite the shoots and pods, injecting poison that kills the plant tissues and makes them turn dark and dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mirids (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni ŋmɔɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ tso mli fãji awo mli. ni oha efee duŋ ni egbi.

english: How does the dry Harmattan season affect my cocoa trees, and how can I protect them?
ga: Te harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ saa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe?

english: Harmattan winds suck moisture out of the air and soil, causing leaves to dry up and young pods to wither. Covering the soil around the tree base with dry leaves (mulching) keeps the soil moist longer.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm is running out of food for my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ?

english: When soil loses its richness, tree growth slows down, the leaves turn pale yellow instead of deep green, and the pods become smaller and fewer during harvest time.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ emuuyeli lɛ Tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee bibii bibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong, aggressive roots that drink up water and soil nutrients instantly, allowing them to overpower young crops if they are not cleared regularly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛboteɔ mɔ mli waa. ni baanu nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ tsei bibii anɔ kunim kɛji ajieee amɛ daa.

english: I have a piece of land in a valley that stays wet almost all year round. What kind of crops are best to grow on this type of land?
ga: Miyɛ shikpɔŋ ko yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi yɛ afi lɛ mli bei babaoo mli. Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ ni abaanyɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Lowland or swampy areas naturally collect and hold water, making them ideal for water-loving crops like rice, taro (cocoyam), or sugarcane. Crops like maize or cassava will suffer root rot if planted in such wet soil.
ga: Shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ lɛ hiɛɔ nu yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ ŋmãa, taro (kookoo) loo ŋmãa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa baafite amɛshishifãi kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tamɔ nɛkɛ nɔ.

english: What is the main difference between farming on lowland and farming on upland?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi okwaayeli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ okwaayeli teŋ?

english: Lowland areas are low-lying fields that naturally hold water and stay moist, which is perfect for crops like rice. Upland areas are higher, dry ground where water drains away quickly, making them better for crops like maize, yam, and cassava.
ga: Shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɛ nu toɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa. Gɔji lɛ ji hei ni nu hoɔ oya. Enɛ haa ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot when I plant them in muddy or flooded fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli ewo muji loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. In flooded or overly wet soil, water fills all the air spaces, suffocating the roots and causing fungi to breed, which rots the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ loo edɔ tsɔ nɔ lɛ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ he lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ babaoo. ni haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ

english: Why do people say rice needs so much water compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛɔ akɛ nu babaoo he miihia ŋmãa kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Rice plants are specially adapted to thrive in wet conditions. Water helps transport nutrients to the rice roots, keeps the plant cool, and prevents weeds from easily growing and competing with the rice.
ga: Afee omɔ tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛshwere yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni ekɛ ŋmãa yeɔ akaŋ mlɛo

english: Can I plant rice directly into a field that already has standing water?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni nu damɔ shi mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, rice can grow in standing water, but the water should only be shallow (ankle-deep). If young rice plants are fully underwater for too long, they will drown because their leaves need sunlight and air.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli. Shi esa akɛ nu lɛ afee nɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ pɛ. (ankle deep) kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ hi nu shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baagboi ejaakɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia baai lɛ.

english: How much water is too much water for a growing rice field?
ga: Nu enyiɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji?

english: If the water level completely submerges the leaves of young rice plants for more than a few days, it becomes too much. The ideal water level should only cover the base of the stems, leaving the leaves above water.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ mli lɛ shwie ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kwraa fe gbii 2-3 lɛ, ebaafee nɔ ni fa tsɔ. Esa akɛ nu ni sa lɛ aha tso lɛ shishi pɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I still grow rice in a lowland area during the dry season?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?
