english: Yes, if the lowland field stays naturally moist from underground water or a nearby stream during the dry season, you can still grow rice successfully when drier fields cannot support crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu loo faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oye omanye yɛ ŋmãa mli lolo kɛ́ ŋmɔji lɛ amli egbi ni onyɛɛɛ odu ŋmãa.

english: How can I keep water on my lowland farm for a longer time so my field doesn't dry out?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã nu ahi miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ? Bɔni afee ni miŋmɔji lɛ akagbi?

english: You can build small low walls of earth, called bunds or ridges, around your field plots. These bunds trap rainwater and river water inside your field so it stays flooded for your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ oma shikpɔŋ gbogbo bibioo ko. Atsɛɔ nakai akɛ crater loo ŋshɔkpɔ. bɔle oŋmɔji lɛ ahe Blɔkii nɛɛ baamɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ faa nu yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli. koni ekɛ nu ashwie oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ

english: What simple steps should I take to prepare a wet, swampy piece of land before planting rice?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo komɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ dani aduɔ ŋmãa?

english: First, clear out bushes and weeds. Next, level the ground so water distributes evenly across the plot, and build small soil mounds or bunds around the edges to trap and control the water level.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi, no sɛɛ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome bɔni afee ni nu lɛ aja shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni oma gɔŋ bibioo ko loo gɔŋ ko ni ebɔle ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ he koni ekɛmɔ nu lɛ mli ni ekwɛ nɔ

english: Which type of soil is best for holding water in a lowland rice field?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ̃ sa kɛha nu ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli?

english: Clay soil is best because it has tiny, tightly packed particles that trap water and stop it from soaking away quickly. Sandy soils drain water too fast to keep fields flooded.
ga: Shikpɔŋ hi fe fɛɛ yɛ emli nibii bibii lɛ ahewɔ. ni akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ koni nu lɛ ahi shi ni ekaje kpo oya Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ hoɔ oya tsɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ nu.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight because their roots are shallow and fragile. Planting quick-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates leafy canopy shade and keeps the soil moist, protecting the young trees until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaha ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen nutrients, while holes in the leaves are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK and spraying approved crop treatments early will help the plants recover and grow healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK kɛ tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra lɛ baanyɛ aye abua. Enɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ni ekwɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready to harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil right around the base of the stem begins to crack as the tubers underneath expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko egbɔ kɛji baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruits during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain and high humidity wash away or wet the pollen inside tomato blossoms, which prevents pollination from taking place. Without pollination, the flowers cannot turn into fruit and simply drop off the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo hoɔ loo ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ mli fɔ̃ɔ. Enɛ haaa pollination aba. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee aduawai ni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to make big mounds of soil before planting my yam setts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ agbo dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose soil to grow long and thick underground tubers. Mounding creates loose, deep soil that drains excess water easily, allowing the yam tubers to expand freely without hitting hard, compact dirt.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni ekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kakadaji ni mli wa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaabɔ he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛtswaaa muji ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts together in the same field with maize make my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means they absorb nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. The neighboring maize plants then feed on this extra nitrogen, helping them grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Leaf curling during peak afternoon heat is a natural way plants protect themselves. By curling their leaves, pepper plants reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which helps them hold onto their moisture. They usually uncurl once the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe he. Pepper tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa pepper tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe jɔɔ ehe beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ.

english: Chemical fertilizer is very concentrated and can chemically burn the stem and main roots if it touches them directly. Fertilizer should be applied in a circle a few inches away from the stem where the feeder roots can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsofa ni baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi titrii kɛ shishifãi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ kokroo nɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi. he ni niyenii shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Weed seeds naturally live in the soil and are adapted to sprout rapidly at the very first drop of rain. They absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than domestic crops, which is why early clearing is necessary to keep them from choking your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛ́ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ he miihia koni oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ akagbɔjɔ.

english: Why do insects attack and turn my harvested maize into powder inside the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ni amɛmiitsɔ sũ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tiny insects like weevils often lay unseen eggs in the grains while they are still on the farm. If the harvested maize is not thoroughly dried in the sun or treated with safe storage preservatives before storing, these eggs hatch into pests that eat the grain from the inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ dumɔwui amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo akɛ nɔ ko ni haa ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ tsuuu nii dani akɛtoɔ ŋmãa nɛɛ he lɛ, Nɛkɛ ŋmãa nɛɛ fɔɔ kɛfeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow after I spray them with crop medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ tsofa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaves can burn or turn yellow if crop medicine is mixed too strong or sprayed during the hot midday sun. Spraying early in the morning or late in the afternoon with the correct water mix protects the leaves from chemical heat.
ga: Baai lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ tso lɛ tsofa lɛ futu mli tsɔ loo akɛshwie nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni sa ni akɛfutu lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo shwane lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsofai lɛ amli dɔlɛ he.

english: Is it normal for my skin and eyes to burn a little after spraying my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mihewolo kɛ mihiŋmɛii baashã fioo beni mikɛ aduawai eshwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Chemical crop medicines cause skin and eye irritation if they touch you directly. Wearing a nose mask, long sleeves, and washing with soap immediately after spraying prevents this chemical irritation.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli lɛ haa hewolo kɛ hiŋmɛi mli shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkɛ bo kpe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ owo nɔ ko ni akɛhaa hiɛ, nine kakadaŋŋ agbo, ni okɛ samla shwie ohe amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni okɛ tsofa nɛɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsofa nɛɛ akafee mɔ ni mli efu bo.

english: Will pouring crop medicine directly around the stem kill my plant's roots?
ga: Tso tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ Ani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbe mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: Pouring concentrated crop medicine directly onto the base burns delicate roots, making it hard for the plant to absorb water and nutrients. Medicine should usually be sprayed lightly on leaves or properly diluted in soil.
ga: Tso tsofa ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ̃ɔ shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛha tsei akɛ amɛ baa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Taakɛ eji lɛ, esa akɛ afɔ tsofa lɛ ashwie baai lɛ anɔ fioo loo akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my spraying machine is putting too much medicine on my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sprayer lɛ kɛ tsofa babaoo ewo mi-ŋmei lɛ nɔ?

english: If medicine drips heavily off the maize leaves onto the ground, you are applying too much. A proper spray creates a fine mist that coats the leaves without washing off into the soil.
ga: Kɛji tsofa shwieɔ shi waa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ okɛ tsofai babaoo miitsu nii. Nɔ ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa afua kpakpa ko haa tsei lɛ ahe ni ekɛ ehe wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray medicine on my cassava farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaafɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Early morning or late evening is best because strong winds won't blow the spray away, and gentle sunlight allows the leaves to absorb the medicine safely without scorching.
ga: Leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ tswaŋ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ blɛoo lɛ haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ tsofa lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛshãaa.

english: Can I mix two different crop medicines together in one spray tank to save time?
ga: Ani manyɛ afutu ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: Mixing unapproved medicines can trigger chemical reactions that weaken their effectiveness, damage your crops, or clog the nozzle of your spraying machine.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ko afee nɔ ko ni haaa amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Fitemɔ oŋmɔshi nibii Aloo ebaanyɛ etsĩ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tight even when I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny hidden pests like mites or aphids sucking sap from beneath the leaves, which requires pest medicine rather than extra water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii yɛ nu kroko ni akɛbaafata he lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do caterpillars come back to my farm just a few days after spraying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni amɛshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Most medicines only kill adult insects present during spraying. Insect eggs hidden under leaves hatch a few days later, which is why a second planned treatment is often needed.
ga: Tsofai babaoo baagbe kooloi bibii ni eda ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ pɛ. Kplukai ni akɛtee baai lɛ ashishi lɛ baafɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ato helatsamɔ ni ji enyɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: How does spraying medicine help prevent black pod disease on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ black pod hela ni baa kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ naa?

english: Fungicide medicine acts like a protective raincoat on cocoa pods, stopping fungal spores from settling on the pod skin and causing rot when rain drops hit them.
ga: Tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ atade ni buɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akapɛtɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahewolo he. ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ amɛ.

english: Why does weed medicine kill the grass but leave my grown corn standing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shi ehaa mi ŋmãa lɛ yaa nɔ eduɔ lɛ?

english: Certain weed medicines are selective, meaning they are designed to target narrow-leaf grasses while leaving broad-leaf crops unharmed, or vice versa, based on plant biology.
ga: Tsofai komɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ ahala mɛi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ afee tsofai nɛɛ koni amɛkɛtutua jwɛi ni baai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ashiɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efeee amɛ, loo nɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ, yɛ bɔ ni tso lɛ wala yɔɔ ha lɛ naa.

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the soil underneath is still dry and hot. Wait until you get two or three steady rains so the ground has enough moisture to germinate the seeds without scorching them.
ga: Kaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ nɛ shi fioo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni shãaa dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn and dry out easily. Retaining tall trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool shelter that holds humidity and protects young cocoa roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa shihilɛhe ko ni mli ejɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa.

english: Why are my cassava roots staying small and thin even though the plant leaves look big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil is too hard or compacted, cassava roots cannot expand underground. Loosening the soil deeply before planting gives the tubers room to swell and store food.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ, Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ amli alɛɛ ni amɛto niyenii.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and leaves looking like they were chewed overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mibi lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baai kɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni aye amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central funnel of the plant during the day. Inspecting the leaf funnels early and applying control measures quickly prevents crop loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni akwɛɔ yɛ baai amli lɛ amli mra Ni aaaye nɔ oya lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam plants to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground, exposing them to sunlight while preventing leaf diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Shi ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ nɔ ni otsi foliar helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Will putting fertilizer right against the stem of my plant help it grow faster?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mitso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eda oya?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem will burn and damage the plant. Fertilizer should be placed in a small ring or hole a few inches away from the stem so the roots can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ ashã ni efite tso lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo bu lɛ kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow and rotting near the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by soil fungi splashing onto the lower leaves during rain or watering. Removing lower leaves that touch the ground and covering the soil with dry grass helps keep the leaves dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ loo nu be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni taa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit viruses to the plant. Controlling these insects early keeps the plant healthy and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛyaa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Too many shoots fight with the main plant for soil nutrients and water, leading to small bunches. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get eaten by insects inside the storage bags after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nitoohe kotoku lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weevils attack maize if the grains are stored while still holding moisture. Thoroughly sun-drying maize until the kernels are hard before bagging prevents insects from breeding inside storage.
ga: Weevils baatutua ŋmãa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to ni edɔ lolo. Abɛi ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani awoɔ tsɔne mli Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafee babaoo yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field without any trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because full direct sunlight scorches their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain around young cocoa creates a protective canopy that keeps the plants cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, awo kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to grow strong stems and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plant turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves is usually a sign that the soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to grow healthy green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore nutrients and keeps the plant green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni wa lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi ŋmɔji.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dried leaves or cut grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Nibii ni aduɔ ni baai egbi loo jwɛi ni afo?

english: Covering the soil, also known as mulching, prevents water from evaporating quickly during hot days, keeps the soil cool, stops weeds from growing, and adds organic nutrients back to the soil as the grass decays.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ha jwɛi lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni okɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant beans or groundnuts together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa baadu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, providing free nutrients that help neighboring crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛhaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize look like they have small holes and ragged edges with dirt inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ muji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli

english: This damage is typically caused by caterpillars known as Fall Armyworms that hide in the center funnel of the plant and eat the leaves. Scouting your farm early allows you to catch them and apply appropriate control measures before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Ehaa onyɛɔ omɔɔ amɛ ni okɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa tsuɔ nii dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean the plant is dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbo?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry periods to save water and survive the heat. The plant is not dead; it goes dormant and will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ehiɔ shi ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Why should I remove some of the young shoots growing around my main plantain stem instead of letting all of them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi tso titri lɛ jie Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛ fɛɛ amɛdara

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight the main plant for food and water, resulting in smaller bunches. Pruning back excess suckers to keep only one or two strong ones ensures the main plant yields big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛwu amɛtao niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei niji lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread across the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee tso kakadaŋŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight needed to grow big tubers underground, while also preventing wet leaves from rotting or catching soil-borne diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa baai ni efɔ lɛ akagbo loo helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akaná amɛ.

english: How do I know that my cassava crop is mature and ready for harvest without digging up all the tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ efolɔɔɔ mli?

english: Cassava maturity is usually shown by the lower leaves yellowing and falling off naturally, the main stem cracking slightly near the soil line, and reaching its expected variety age, which is usually between 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, ŋmei baakwɛ̃ ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaagbee shi. Tso wulu lɛ baagbala fioo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ. ni eshɛɔ afii ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ ebaafɔ lɛ he Enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Some crops like pawpaw have separate male and female trees. Male trees only produce pollen-bearing flowers to fertilize female flowers, so male trees will never grow fruit themselves even though they look healthy.
ga: Tsei komɛi, tamɔ paw paws, yɛ tsei hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni pollen yɔɔ mli pɛ koni amɛkɛ fɔfɔi yei abɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni ji hii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ edaŋ kɔkɔɔkɔ, kɛji akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ po.

english: How many male pawpaw trees do I actually need to keep on my farm for pollination?
ga: Pawpaw tsei enyiɛ he miihia mi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛha pollination?

english: One male tree produces enough pollen to service about 8 to 10 female trees. You only need a small number of male trees evenly spaced on your farm to get a full harvest without wasting land.
ga: Tso kome woɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsu tsei yei aaafee 8 kɛyashi 10 ahe nii. Ohe miihia ni oná tsei hii fioo komɛi ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni onine ashɛ ŋmaa ni fa nɔ ni ofiteee he ko.

english: How can I tell the difference between a male flower and a female flower on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Male flowers usually grow on long, thin stalks and only contain dust-like pollen inside, while female flowers sit directly close to the plant stem and have a small, swollen mini-fruit at their base.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi hii daa yɛ tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ ni fɔfɔi ni tamɔ sũ pɛ yɔɔ mli. yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi yei lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛyɛ aduawai bibii ni efuu yɛ amɛshishigbɛ.

english: Why does my maize crop grow tassels at the top before the ears of corn start showing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛi dani toi lɛ jeɔ shishi ejieɔ ehe kpo lɛ?

english: The tassels at the top are the male parts that produce pollen. They grow higher up so the wind can easily blow their pollen down onto the silks of the female cobs growing lower on the stalk.
ga: Tassels ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ji nɔ ni haa pollen lɛ baa. Amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ atswa ŋmɔtɔ awo yoo ŋmɔtɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ oya.

english: What will happen if I allow too many male trees to grow in my farm field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji miha tsei hii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Male trees do not produce fruit, so having too many wastes valuable space, water, and fertilizer while crowding out female trees that actually produce your food and income.
ga: Tsei ni ji hii lɛ wooo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaafee he ko ni jara wa, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afiteɔ babaoo tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, okɛ tsei yei ni feɔ oniyenii kɛ shika diɛŋtsɛ lɛ abɔ he.

english: Why do I need to take good care of male plants if they do not produce any harvest for me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ mitsei hii lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmaa amɛha mi?

english: Healthy male plants produce strong, abundant pollen. If you neglect them and they become weak or diseased, your female plants will not be pollinated properly, resulting in small or deformed fruits.
ga: Tsei hii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ pollen ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa babaoo. Kɛji oku ohiɛ oshwie amɛnɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ loo hela mɔ amɛ Otsei yei lɛ baafee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bibioo loo efite.

english: Why do my cucumber vines produce many flowers at first that just fall off without making fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kukumba wain tso lɛ wo fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ shishijee mli ni egbee shi kɛkɛ ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Cucumbers naturally produce male flowers first to attract bees to your farm. These male flowers drop off after releasing pollen, right before the fruiting female flowers begin to open.
ga: Kukumba lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi hii klɛŋklɛŋ koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii kɛba oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ fɔfɔi hii nɛɛ shwieɔ shi beni amɛjie pollen lɛ sɛɛ. Dani fɔfɔi yei lɛ baabɔi fɔmɔ

english: Can having too many unproductive or overcrowded plants in my field cause crop diseases?
ga: Ani tsei ni wooo yibii loo ni eyi obɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe hela aba?

english: Yes, having too many crowded plants blocks sunlight and stops fresh air from flowing, creating a damp environment where fungal infections and insect pests can multiply rapidly.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli. ni feɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: What will happen to my farm if I do not pay close attention to early signs of sickness on my plants?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ emaaa hela he okadii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ amli mra lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Crop diseases spread very fast from plant to plant. If you do not monitor your field regularly to catch infections early, you risk losing your entire crop yield before harvest time.
ga: Tse helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Kɛji okwɛɛɛ nibii ni odu lɛ amli daa koni ona helai mra lɛ, Okɛ ohe woɔ oshara mli akɛ obaafite onibii fɛɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why do my garden egg flowers drop off during heavy rainy seasons without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away pollen from male flowers and keeps pollinating insects away, which prevents female flowers from getting fertilized and causes them to fall off unpollinated.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ fɔfɔi ni hiɛ fɔfɔi hii ahe lɛ ahe nii, ni etsĩɔ fɔfɔi ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anaa. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi yei lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii, ni no hewɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii lɛ shɛɛɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow whenever water sits on my field after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be fɛɛ be ni nu baabote ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rain stays trapped in the soil for too long, it drowns the crop roots by blocking oxygen. Without oxygen, the roots cannot absorb nutrients from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow and growth to slow down.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ehaa tsei shishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa fioo.

english: How do raised mounds help protect my crops when heavy rains fall?
ga: Te gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Building mounds raises your crop roots above standing floodwater. The extra rain gathers in the channels between the mounds instead of soaking the roots, allowing water to drain safely away without damaging the plant.
ga: Gɔŋ ni ooofee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyaa nu afua lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni fa lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe ni efiteee tsei lɛ.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my cassava leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ feɔ diŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Damp and wet conditions during the rainy season allow microscopic fungi to grow easily on wet leaves. These spots spread fast if plants are crowded together because damp air stays trapped between the leaves.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii bibii baakwɛ̃ yɛ baai ni mli edɔ nɔ. Nɛkɛ hei nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ emɔ baai lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or too much water around the roots. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to stay alive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa miigba tso lɛ naa loo kɛ́ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Tsei baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha wala.

english: Weeds have strong, wild seeds that are adapted to drink water immediately and grow fast. They naturally compete with your crops for water and nutrients, so removing them early keeps your crops healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ koo mli dumɔwui ni wa ni nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛdaraa oya. Amɛkɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ amɛ mra. Ebaaha otsei lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing short and twisted instead of long and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eda lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft soil to expand easily downwards. If the soil is hard or packed tight by water, the tuber cannot push deeper and ends up growing small or bent.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Tubers lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shɔŋŋ ni amɛbaafee bibii loo amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to keep from drying out.
ga: Baai ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ akagbi.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ duɔ tsina loo ŋmãa?

english: Beans and cowpeas have natural helpers in their roots that pull food (nitrogen) from the air and put it back into the soil. This feeds the maize plant so it can grow stronger without depleting the land.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa niyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tso lɛ niyenii bɔni afee ni eda waa ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more aggressively right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The start of the rainy season causes crops to shoot out tender, fresh green leaves. Insects naturally hatch and travel toward these young leaves because they are soft and easy to eat.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Kplukai fɔ̃ɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛyaa nɛkɛ baai bibii nɛɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my crops grow much stronger when I plant right at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli wa waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Early rains carry natural nitrogen from the air that nourishes the soil. Planting at the beginning of the season also gives your crops enough time to build strong root systems before the rain stops or the weather becomes too hot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ lɛ baa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ hu haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛma shishifãi ni mli wa dani nugbɔ lɛ akpaa loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops stop growing well when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kpaɔ shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: The Harmattan wind brings dry air and dust that dries out the soil and strips moisture from plant leaves very quickly. Crops slow down their growth during this time to conserve water and protect themselves from dry stress.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ sũ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ oya ni egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ he.

english: How do I know if my crops are suffering from lack of water during a dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu efo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves will begin to curl, droop, or turn yellowish during the hottest part of the day. Watering early in the morning or late evening helps the soil retain moisture so plants can absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu Ebaai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛbaagbee shi, loo amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to water my crops lightly every day or give them a lot of water a few times a week?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ blɛoo daa gbi loo maha amɛ nu babaoo? Shii fioo komɛi yɛ otsi mli?

english: It is usually better to water deeply two or three times a week rather than light watering every day. Deep watering encourages roots to grow deeper into the soil, making the crop stronger and better able to survive hot weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni mli kwɔ Shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli lɛ hi fe nu fioo ni oooha daa gbi. Nu ni mli kwɔ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei hewalɛ ni amɛ nyɛɔ amɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and fall over when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving plants proper spacing ensures each stalk receives enough light and nutrients to grow thick and strong.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Why do seeds sometimes rot in the ground instead of sprouting after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when the soil is too wet and heavy, or buried too deeply, which prevents air from reaching the seed. Planting in well-drained, loose soil at the right depth helps seeds germinate safely.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni etsii. loo afu lɛ mli tsɔ Enɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni mli edɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops even when the crops are already big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe, kɛji akɛ amɛdara momo po?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops at every growth stage. Keeping your farm clean allows your crops to direct all their energy into producing larger fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji.

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil is missing essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that too much water is sitting around the roots and suffocating them. Adding compost or manure can help restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛmiigbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is buying certified seeds better than using saved seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ hi fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically selected to withstand local pests and diseases while giving higher yields. Seeds saved year after year gradually lose their strength, resulting in smaller harvests over time.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. hewalɛ ni baa shi Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, abaanyɛ akpa nɔ fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does learning about different planting methods from an extension officer help improve my harvest?
ga: Kasemɔ gbɛi srɔtoi ni akɛduɔ nii Kɛjɛ Extension Officer lɛ dɛŋ Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua ni mikpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Extension officers share tested practices on soil care, crop spacing, and pest control. Learning these correct techniques prevents wasted effort and money, helping you get the highest possible yield from your field.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jaa nifeemɔi ni aka amɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ he. ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtoɔ he kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ Gbɛi ni ja nɛɛ akasemɔ baaye abua ni atsĩ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kɛ shika ni afiteɔ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa shika babaoo kɛjɛɔ onitsumɔhe nine lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to its younger top leaves to stay alive, leaving the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi, ni ji bibii lɛ anɔ koni ehi wala mli. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that have special bacteria in their roots. These bacteria pull nitrogen out of the air and put it directly into the soil, acting like natural fertilizer for the crops you plant afterwards.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Muawai nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. When infected, the plant cannot feed itself properly through its leaves, which reduces root growth.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Beni hela lɛ emɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my stored cowpea grains develop small holes and turn to powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: This destruction is caused by cowpea weevils. These tiny pests lay eggs on the seeds, and when the larvae hatch, they eat their way out from inside the grain, leaving hollowed-out holes.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsina ŋmei lɛ. ŋmeii bibii Enɛɛmɛi woɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛbaaye amɛ gbɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. ni kɛ bu ni mli ewo muji baa

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant faces heat stress or drought. If temperatures get too high or water is scarce, the plant discards its flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu bɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Why do my maize cobs have missing kernels and empty spots when dry spells hit during flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii ni elaaje kɛ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo be mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Maize needs water to produce sticky silks that catch pollen from the tassels. If a dry spell occurs during flowering, the silks dry up quickly and cannot catch pollen, resulting in cobs with missing grains.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee siliki ni wa ni mɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa ni jɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji ŋmɔlɔ ba yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Siliki lɛ gbiɔ oya ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ pollen. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ bɛ dumɔwui.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither when I clear away all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, harsh sunlight. Big forest trees provide shade and keep the soil moist, protecting young cocoa plants from burning and drying out in their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ kooi wuji amli lɛ haa hulutsoo, ni amɛhaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkashã ni amɛkagbi yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli.

english: When planted too close, pepper plants compete for limited sunlight. Instead of producing branches and fruits, they stretch upward to reach the light, making them weak and unproductive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa. Yɛ niji kɛ aduawai najiaŋ Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, etsɔɔ ehe koni eha la lɛ abote mli. haa wɔgbɔjɔɔ ni wɔwooo yibii

english: Why do my plantain trees tip over so easily when heavy rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees naturally have shallow root systems. If underground pests like nematodes or banana root weevils chew on those roots, the tree loses its anchor in the wet soil and easily topples over.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes loo banana root weevils lɛ ye nakai shishifãi lɛ, Tsei baanyɛ afite amɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ mli oya ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and dry up long before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines usually happens when microscopic worms called nematodes attack the roots and seed tubers underground, cutting off the flow of water and food to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbimɔ mra baa kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutua shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi kɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii. Kpa nu kɛ niyenii ni hoɔ kɛyaa baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do I have to keep spraying chemical pesticides on my pepper and tomato farms all the time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyaa nɔ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pests are constantly attracted to soft vegetable crops in open fields. While many farmers resort to spraying chemicals continuously, this can be expensive and harmful. You can actually manage these pests naturally using organic methods like neem oil sprays and healthy soil management.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Eyɛ mli akɛ okwaafoi babaoo kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ miitsu nii be fɛɛ be moŋ. Shi tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa ni eyɛ oshara. Obaanyɛ okwɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa nɔ.

english: What natural options can I use on my vegetable farm if I don't want to spray chemical poisons on crops my family will eat?
ga: Mɛɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii krokomɛi manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni kɛji akɛ misumɔɔɔ ni mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miweku lɛ yeɔ lɛ anɔ hu?

english: You can make safe, natural sprays using local plants like crushed neem leaves, hot pepper extracts, or mild soapy water. These natural alternatives keep insect pests away from your vegetables without leaving harmful chemical residues on your food.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ mli tsei tamɔ neem baai ni atswa, ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. loo nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛ saamɔ ewo mli Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii krokomɛi nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akashɛɔ o-vegetables lɛ ahe. ni okɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui eshwɛɛɛ yɛ oniyenii mli

english: Is it really possible to harvest a lot of peppers without spending all my money on chemical sprays?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akpa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo diɛŋtsɛ ni afiteee nakai shika lɛ fɛɛ yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, it is possible. By practicing natural farming—such as using compost to strengthen the plants, rotating your crops, and using natural insect repellents—you can achieve high pepper yields while drastically reducing your chemical costs.
ga: hɛɛ ebaanyɛ eba mli Adebɔɔ mli okwaayeli nifeemɔi, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛwaje tsei lɛ aŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Enɛ baaha oná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo yɛ be mli ni tsofai ahe nyɔmɔwoo baa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I grow exotic vegetables like lettuce, cucumber, and cauliflower outdoors in Ghana, or do they need special green houses?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai ni yɔɔ srɔtoi tamɔ lettuce, kukumba kɛ kɔliflawa yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ Ghana? Aloo amɛmiitao shĩa krɛdɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli?

english: You can grow lettuce, cucumbers, cauliflower, and tomatoes directly in open fields. While they need regular watering, good soil, and pest protection, they do not require expensive greenhouse setups to produce well.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu lettuce, kukumba, kɔliflawa, kɛ tomato yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ehe miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu daa, shikpɔŋ kpakpa, kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Shi ehe ehiaaa ni aná ŋmɔ ni jara wa koni aná nibii kpakpai.

english: How can planting different crops like tomatoes, cucumbers, and peppers help me make more from my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi tamɔ tomato, kukumba, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná shika babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Growing a variety of vegetables prevents total crop loss if a disease attacks one specific plant. Diversification also keeps your soil healthy because different crops use nutrients in different ways and allows you to harvest and sell produce throughout the year.
ga: Aduawai srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ afite kɛji hela ba tsei lɛ eko nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni afeɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ atsu nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ ni ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa onibii ni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do crops like cucumber and cauliflower need so much more attention than traditional crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kukumba kɛ kɔliflower biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ namɔ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Vegetable crops are soft, fast-growing, and contain a lot of water, which makes them very appealing to insect pests and sensitive to intense heat. Unlike hardy cassava, vegetables need close monitoring, steady water, and protection to produce good yields.
ga: Aduawai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛdaraa oya ni nu babaoo yɛ mli, ni no haa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ sumɔɔ amɛ ni amɛnuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ ŋmei ni wa lɛ, tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu yɛ jɛmɛ daa. ni abuɔ he koni afee nibii kpakpai

english: Why do insect pests attack my vegetable crops so much more when I grow them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mi aduawai lɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Open fields expose your crops directly to wind, heat, and insect populations traveling from surrounding areas. Insects easily spot fresh green plants in the open, so field crops need consistent protection, either through natural sprays or surrounding barrier crops.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni agbele nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ, dɔlɛ, kɛ kooloi bibii ni jɛɔ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa onibii lɛ. Kooloi bibii naa tsei eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ abu ŋmɔ mli nibii ni adu lɛ ahe daa. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsei ni tsiɔ gbɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: What does growing my vegetables 'naturally' mean, and will my land still yield a lot of food?
ga: Aduawai adumɔ Mɛni ji ‘adebɔɔ naa’ shishi? Ni ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ baawo yibii babaoo lolo?

english: Growing naturally means feeding your soil with animal manure or compost and controlling pests with plant-based solutions instead of synthetic chemicals. Once your soil becomes rich with natural organic matter, your farm can produce abundant, high-quality yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ. kɛ tsofai ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ ni akɛaaye kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ yɛ tsofai ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ najiaŋ. Beni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Oŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo nibii babaoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best way for me to grow a large amount of leafy vegetables like lettuce on a small budget?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ madu aduawai babaoo ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ lettuce yɛ shika fioo ko mli?

english: Leafy crops like lettuce grow rapidly if you nourish the soil with manure and provide plenty of water. You can avoid high chemical costs by using basic netting or simple home-made plant extracts to keep bugs from eating the soft leaves.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ lettuce lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ nu babaoo ha. Obaanyɛ okpa tsofai ahe nyɔmɔwoo ni fa babaoo kɛtsɔ ŋshɔŋlooi ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo tso mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shia lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii koni kooloi akaye baai bibii lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my land is ready to start growing fresh vegetables like tomatoes and peppers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaaje aduawai heei tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shishi?

english: Tomatoes and peppers thrive in sunny, open areas with well-drained soil that does not hold excess water after rain. Clearing the land, loosening the soil, and mixing in decomposed manure will make your field ready for planting.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ. Eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ehiɛɛɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ, okɛ sũ lɛ shwie shi, ni okɛ ŋmeii ni egbo futu mli lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee klalo kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide canopy shade and keep the ground cool, protecting the cocoa plants until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Buu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or NPK fertilizer gives the crop the nitrogen required to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa babaoo koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo NPK ŋmãa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná nitrogen ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest if they grow underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji eekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is mature when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the base of the stem becomes thick and woody.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaale akɛ egbɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei

english: Why do extension officers tell me to put tall wooden stakes next to my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato wain tsei ni miduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to grow healthy leaves and make large tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves get plenty of light and stays clear of wet soil, which prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ bulbs wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. koni baai lɛ aná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite.

english: What causes my tomato leaves to curl up and stop producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo?

english: Curled leaves on tomatoes are often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses. Spraying plants with neem oil or soapy water keeps these pests away and stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akabote tso lɛ he, ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same field season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests like fall armyworms to build up. Rotating maize with beans or cowpeas restores nutrients and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet weather with poor air movement. Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and wind in to dry out the farm and prevent the fungus.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i be mli lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ Afeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ŋmeii akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before setting any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat or dry soil. Watering the plants regularly during dry, hot spells helps keep the flowers attached so they can grow into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Too many extra shoots steal water and plant food from the main stem. Removing small suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main plant grows big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Tsobii bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ Jiemɔ ni oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ plantains akuu agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Spreading dry grass, or mulching, acts like a blanket over the dirt. It blocks the sun from evaporating water out of the ground, keeps the soil moist longer, and reduces the need for frequent watering.
ga: Hay loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni ebaaha nu ni afɔɔ shwiemɔ shii abɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi

english: Why do most farmers in my area wait until April or the first heavy rains before planting crops like maize and vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ mɛɔ kɛyashiɔ April loo klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ dani amɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ aduawai lɛ?

english: April usually marks the start of the main rainy season in Ghana. Planting when the rains begin ensures that seeds have enough water to germinate and young plant roots can grow deep without drying out in the hot soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, April ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee yɛ Ghana. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃. Ni tsei bibii ashishifãi baanyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛhaaa sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ agbi.

english: Why should I clear and prepare my farm land months before the rainy season actually starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni masaa he nyɔji babaoo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Clearing early gives cleared weeds time to dry out and rot into natural fertilizer. It also ensures your soil is loose and ready to trap the very first rainwater, allowing you to plant immediately when the rains arrive.
ga: Ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ aná be ni amɛgbi ni amɛfite akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee klalo akɛ ebaamɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ nu lɛ. Ehaa oduɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba.

english: People say farming is only done during the rainy season, so how can I keep growing crops and earning money all year round?
ga: Mɛi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be mli pɛ obaanyɛ otsu okwaayeli. No hewɔ lɛ, te wɔɔfee tɛŋŋ wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni wɔná shika yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: You can farm year-round by using simple irrigation from wells or rivers, or by planting short-duration vegetables in nursery bags and gardens near your house during the dry season.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee okwaayeli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ. kɛjɛ nubu loo faa ko mli Aloo kɛtsɔ aduawai ni yeɔ be kukuoo ni ooodu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kotokui amli kɛ omaŋ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What are grow-bags and why would I use them instead of planting directly in my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni ji grow bag? Ni mɛni hewɔ mikɛtsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Grow-bags are sturdy bags filled with nutrient-rich soil. They help you grow healthy crops in small spaces or areas with poor farm soil, while making it easier to control water, weeds, and soil diseases.
ga: Grow bag ji kotoku ni wa ni sũ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ. Amɛhaa onyɛɔ oduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji bibii loo hei ni ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kwraa lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaaye nu, jwɛi, kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it better to start my pepper and tomato seeds in small nursery bags before moving them to the main field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooobɔi pepper kɛ tomato dumɔwui yɛ grow kotokui bibii amli? dani aya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ

english: Yes, starting seeds in nursery bags protects young, fragile sprouts from harsh sunlight, heavy rains, and pests until they grow strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ kotokui amli lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe. Kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting too much water or not enough water from the rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo eshɛɛɛ nugbɔ lɛ he?

english: When crops don't get enough water, their leaves wilt, curl, or turn dry. When they get too much water, their leaves turn pale yellow and their roots begin to rot because the soil is suffocating.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi, amɛbaakpã, loo amɛbaagbi kɛji amɛná nu babaoo. Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I keep the soil around my young plants moist when it stops raining for a few days?
ga: Mibaafee shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ Te mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛhiɔ nu mli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi?

english: You can cover the soil around the base of your plants with dry grass or leaves, a method called mulching. This shades the soil from the hot sun so water doesn't evaporate quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ato tso lɛ shishi. Atsɛɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. bɔni afee ni nu lɛ akatsɔ la oya

english: What is the best time to put fertilizer on my crops so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp after a light rain, and bury it slightly near the plant roots so it dissolves into the soil instead of being washed away by heavy downpours.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. ni ofu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fioo bɔni afee ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant the exact same crop on the same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases that feed on that specific plant to build up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daa waa.

english: Look for small ragged holes in the leaves and saw-dust-like droppings inside the central funnel of the maize plant. Seeing these signs means armyworms are present and actively feeding.
ga: Taomɔ bu bibii ni etse ehe yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ ona okadii nɛɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ asraafoi amli ŋmeii yɛ jɛmɛ ni amɛmiitao niyenii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, an essential food for maize growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure early can fix this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmãa dalɛ Nitrogen ŋmãa loo kooloi ŋmãa ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli mra lɛ baanyɛ atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Hot temperatures make leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it, causing the leaves to curl up to protect themselves. If they perk up again by evening, it is temporary heat stress.
ga: He ni mli edɔ lɛ haa baa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Kɛji ote shi ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eji be kukuoo mli latsaa he haomɔ.

english: Cassava root rot happens when excessive rain or poorly drained soil traps water around the tubers, allowing fungi in the soil to attack and decay the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mɔmɔ nu ni bɔleɔ tuber lɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak, thin stalks and small cobs. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Growing maize continuously on the same soil drains the same specific nutrients every season and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kpo daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants staying short and thin months after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ hiɔ shi kuku ni amɛhe waaa kɛji adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stunted growth usually occurs when the soil lacks phosphorus or when weeds are allowed to steal water and food from the young plants during their first critical weeks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa kɛji fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei bibii amli yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: Why is my maize producing tiny cobs early when the plants are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Dani, beni shishijee lɛ ji kuku kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: When crops face extreme stress like drought or poor soil early in life, they produce small cobs prematurely in a rush to reproduce before dying.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ haomɔi ni naa wa tamɔ hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kpe yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli mra lɛ, Amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii. mra koni amɛfɔmɔ oya dani amɛgboi.

english: If I keep harvesting the leaves of my cocoyam plant for nkontomire, will it stop the tubers underground from growing big?
ga: Kɛji mibua cacao tso lɛ baai lɛ anaa kɛha gontomir ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Ani ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara?

english: Yes, because the leaves act as the factory that uses sunlight to make food for the plant. If you cut off too many leaves too frequently, the plant lacks the energy needed to build and swell the root tubers underground.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ baai tsuɔ nii akɛ nitsumɔhei ni kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Kɛji ofolɔ baai lɛ shii abɔ lɛ Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do cocoyam plants thrive and look healthier under tree shade compared to my open maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ fɛo yɛ hulutsoo tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ akɛto mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoyam plants naturally prefer partial shade and high humidity because their broad, thin leaves lose water very quickly under direct, intense sunlight, which causes them to wilt easily.
ga: Cocoyam tsei lɛ sumɔɔ hulutsoo be fioo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo. Ejaakɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni mli kwɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ mlɛo

english: Why do cassava plants sometimes grow huge green leaves above ground but yield very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmei yɔɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy developing lush stems and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in its tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ starch baato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do stored yams start sprouting green shoots in my barn even though they are not planted in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes ni ato lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ aduuu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Yams are living tubers that go through a natural resting period after harvest. Once that dormancy period naturally ends, the tuber uses its stored moisture and nutrients to push out shoots, preparing itself for the next planting season.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni biɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ wɔɔhe be lɛ ba naagbee yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Tubers lɛ kɛ nu ni ato kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ kɛje kpo. Koni asaa he kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant automatically pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves and the cob at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up quickly when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Plantains drop their outer leaves during dry weather as a natural survival mechanism to save water, protecting the main stem and growing center until rains return.
ga: Dumɔwui shwieɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Buu tso lɛ yitso lɛ kɛ eshishijee lɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off during hot weather without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants experience heat stress and shed their flowers to conserve energy and water rather than spending energy developing new fruits.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei kɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ kpeɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee aduawai henɔi heei

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings burn and die if I clear all the shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie cacao tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate root systems and sensitive leaves that burn in direct sunlight; they need shade trees to act as living umbrellas that keep the air cool and moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do tomato leaves curl up tightly into a tube during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a protective behavior where the leaf reduces its exposed surface area to the sun and wind, slowing down the amount of moisture lost through its pores.
ga: Leaf curling ji subaŋ ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Baai lɛ haa he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does a cocoyam plant grow leaves rapidly after the first rains, but take almost a year before the tubers are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi ani ehe nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi dani ŋmeii lɛ fee klalo?

english: The plant prioritizes building a strong leafy canopy first so it can catch light, and only after the foliage is fully developed does it start storing excess energy underground to form the tubers.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋwɛi ŋta ni baai ni wa yɔɔ mli lɛ feemɔ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛná la. Ni kɛ́ baai lɛ edara kwraa pɛ kɛkɛ ni amɛbaabɔi hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ tomɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkɛfee bulbs.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and drop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that dry out easily under intense heat and dry Harmattan winds. Without shade trees or nurse crops like plantains to shelter them, the sun burns their leaves and causes them to dry up and drop.
