ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shishi. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛha wɔɔhe bɛ lɛ, Hulu lɛ hu shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up into tiny twisted balls instead of staying flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bɔɔlu bibii moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like mites, aphids, or thrips sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. The damaged leaf tissues shrink and curl, which stunts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Baa lɛ mli fãji ni efite lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ ehe. ni haa tsei nyɛɛɛ adara

english: Why does burning my bush before planting make my land lose its strength over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi jwɛi lɛ ni mishãa dani miduɔ nii lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the organic matter, beneficial soil organisms, and natural mulch that keep the soil moist and fertile. While the ash gives a temporary nutrient boost, repeated burning leaves the soil hard, dry, and easily washed away by rain.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ sũ lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli moŋ, shi kɛ́ ashã lɛ shii abɔ lɛ, enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa, ni egbi ni nugbɔ baatsɔ nɔ oya.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same spot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. It also gives pests like the Fall Armyworm and soil diseases a permanent home, causing yields to drop with every harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ afite afi fɛɛ afi. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ hu náa shia ni hiɔ shi daa. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually signals a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, so when there is not enough in the ground, the plant moves what little it has from older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: When cowpea plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer or are planted in overly rich soil, they spend all their energy growing thick leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and bean pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo amɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse tsɔ nɔ lɛ, tsina tsei kɛ amɛbe fɛɛ kwɛɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Yam vines need their leaves lifted off the wet ground to spread out and capture sunlight. More sunlight helps the leaves produce energy to grow large underground tubers, while keeping vines off the moist soil prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha wain tsei lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni helai ni baa wain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rain and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have a deep main root; they have a shallow root network near the surface. When the soil becomes soft and waterlogged during heavy rains, the heavy weight of a fruit bunch easily pulls the roots out of the ground.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi titrii ni mli kwɔ. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee blɛoo ni nu eyi mli obɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Yibii akui ni tsii lɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive air moisture, which prevents proper pollination. If the flower is not pollinated within a short time, the plant sheds it to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ babaoo. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ pollen yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, Tsei shwieɔ nu koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Heavy, waterlogged soil fills those air spaces with water, suffocating the roots and creating perfect conditions for fungal and bacterial rot to invade the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli eyiɔ kɛ nu. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ abatutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and burn when I clear all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, intense sunlight. Shade trees act like natural umbrellas that shield cocoa leaves from scorching heat, lower the field temperature, and keep soil moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dɔlɛ nɔ ni otsi sũ mli nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra small shoots growing around my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Surplus ni miida yɛ Mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ eje kpo.

english: When too many shoots, or suckers, grow around one plantain tree, they compete with each other for water and plant food. Removing most of them and leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main plant produces large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ fa tsɔ. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli yɛ amɛteŋ. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo ni ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii ni tsii ni dara.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow before the ears even form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ po kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which maize needs in large amounts to stay green and grow strong. Applying compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abele babaoo he miihia koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the growing center of maize. Applying approved bio-pesticides or putting clean wood ash into the plant funnel early in the morning can control them.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ he. Abaanyɛ akudɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tso sũ ni he tse ni akɛfataa ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ he leebi lɛ he.

english: Why do I have to heap up the soil into big mounds before planting my yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ agbo ko ato dani odu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, uncompacted soil to expand freely underground. Mounding creates a deep, loose soil bed that allows tubers to grow long and thick while preventing water from pooling around the roots and causing rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ajieee nɔ ko awo mli lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaabɔ he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etseɔ ehe lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa nu akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Look closely at the small raised leaf nodes or 'eyes' on the stem cutting. Plant the stem with these buds pointing upward toward the sky so the shoots can grow straight up easily and build a strong root system.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. He ni awo nɔ loo ‘buds’ yɛ tso lɛ yibii ni afo lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shishifãi ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ mlɛo. ni amɛma shishitoo gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by several hot, dry days. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the tender young roots will dry out and die before the main rains arrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ Shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans together in the same field with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has roots that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil. This extra food helps nearby corn grow healthier without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛshishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ niyenii ni akɛfataa he nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmãa ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Why should I spread dried grass or dry crop leaves over the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai ni egbi afɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, called mulching, shields the ground from harsh sunlight. This retains soil moisture, keeps root zones cool, stops weeds from taking over, and eventually decays into natural plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or irregular watering. Providing consistent soil moisture and partial shade during extremely hot periods helps the flowers stay healthy and develop into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil cool until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu lɛ naa.

english: How do I know which cassava stems are good to cut and plant for a high harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afo ni adu koni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from plants that are 8 to 12 months old and free from pests or stem diseases. Stems cut from the middle part of the main stalk sprout faster and produce stronger roots.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni edara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsei ahe helai bɛ mli lɛ amli. Tsoi ni afo kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaawo shishifãi ni wa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry out and kill young sprouts. Waiting for the rains to become steady ensures the soil stays wet enough to support early growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be kukuoo ko nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, ni ekolɛ ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agboi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni eye ebua mra be mli dalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen acts like main food for leaf growth, and adding compost or proper fertilizer helps restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why is it important to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up to catch direct sunlight, which helps the plant create energy to grow large underground tubers while keeping leaves off wet ground where diseases spread.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni hulu la lɛ aba nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Proper spacing allows sunlight and fresh air to reach all parts of the plant. When planted too close, trapped moisture creates damp conditions that bring fungal diseases and rot the fruits.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Kɛji adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Trapped moisture lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What causes small worms to eat the leaf centers of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, hatched from eggs laid by small moths. They hide in the center funnel of the maize plant where the tender leaves are easy to chew, requiring early detection to protect the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli, he ni baai bibii lɛ ŋmɔmɔ waaa lɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni ana mra. koni akɛbu ŋmãa tsei ahe

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp weather. Pruning extra shade branches helps sunlight and wind dry out the trees, reducing fungal growth.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haaa tso lɛ agbi. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: Will animal manure improve my soil health better over time than chemical fertilizer alone?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli fe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ?

english: Yes, animal manure builds up the soil by adding organic matter that holds moisture and feeds living organisms, while chemical fertilizers feed the plant quickly without improving the soil structure.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ni ekɛfataa he lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli nibii aya hiɛ.

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crops consume all the nutrients needed to produce a strong yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ atsu nii koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the giant trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct sunlight; they need shade trees or plantain plants nearby to shield their tender leaves from heat and keep moisture in the soil while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How do I choose the best suckers from my existing plantain trees to start a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ mi plantain tsei ni yɔɔ lɛ amli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for 'sword suckers' that have narrow, pointed leaves and a thick base. These grow faster and produce stronger stems and bigger bunches than suckers with broad, wide leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmɔlɔ’ ni baai lɛ mli tse, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni mli wa kɛ kui wuji fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ.

english: How many days of rain should I wait for before planting my maize seeds at the start of the season?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ nugbɔ koni okɛdu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait for two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the soil. Planting too early after just one light shower causes seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellowing leaf tips usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps the plant build chlorophyll and stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishifãi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛfee chlorophyll ni eha amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant cowpea together on the same land with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsina ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, cowpea plants collect nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When grown with maize, they share this nitrogen, making the soil richer without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cowpea tsei lɛ buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa Amɛbaajara nitrogen. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food. Staking spreads the leaves out so they catch sunlight easily, sending extra food down to expand the underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Staking lɛ gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ he mlɛo. Kɛtsɔ niyenii krokomɛi ni akɛbaa shi koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when water is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why does my crop yield drop so much if I delay removing weeds until late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi waa kɛji mikɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ shwie shi kɛyashi be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Weeds steal food, water, and sunlight during the critical early growth stages of your crop. Removing them late leaves your crops permanently stunted even if the field looks clean later.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa mra lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee shoo kɛya naanɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Tubers rot underground when heavy rains make soil too waterlogged for roots to breathe, allowing fungal rots to break down the cassava tubers before harvest.
ga: Tubers lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Ha ni fungal rot akpãtã ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ dani akpa.

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap and spreading viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees remaining very short and not growing tall like my neighbor's trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikokoo tso lɛ yɛ kuku ni ekɛɛɛ tamɔ mikutsoŋnyo kookoo tso lɛ?

english: Trees often remain stunted when the soil lacks essential nutrients or when the young plant's root system struggles to spread out. Adding organic manure around the base and loosening hard soil allows roots to take in food properly so the tree can grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei shwieɔ shi kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo beni tso bibioo ko shishifãi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ sũ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why do extension officers recommend cutting off some branches from my fruit trees when I want them to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ mi tso lɛ yibii lɛ niji komɛi lɛ? Be ni miisumɔ ni eda?

english: Trimming or pruning extra branches helps the tree save energy. Instead of wasting water and food to feed unnecessary stems and leaves, the plant sends its strength directly to the main trunk and fruit-bearing shoots.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ loo afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite nu kɛ niyenii ni akɛyeɔ tsei kɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does plant disease keep returning to my farm every year even after I spray chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Diseases often return because fungal spores and insect eggs hide in old crop waste, weeds, or fallen leaves during the dry season. To permanently break the cycle, you need to clear farm debris continuously and follow a fixed spraying calendar rather than spraying only when crops look sick.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa ejaakɛ fungal spores kɛ kooloi bibii amli ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsɛ ni eshwɛ, jwɛi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okpa sɛɛkuu lɛ daa lɛ, ehe baahia ni ojie ŋmɔ mli jwɛi lɛ be fɛɛ be ni okɛ kalanda ni ato ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ atsu nii. Mohu ɔ, ngmɛɛ tso ɔ nɔ pɛ ke e pee kaa hiɔ nɛ ngɛ ngmɔ ɔ mi.

english: Should I wait until I see insects eating my crops before I start spraying protective treatments?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi mana kooloi bibii ni miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani mabɔi tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ shwiemɔ?

english: It is much better to apply protective measures early before pests arrive. Once insects start eating your plants, the damage to your harvest has already begun, making it much harder and more expensive to recover your yield.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofee nɔ ko ni baatsi hela naa mra. Dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baashɛ Beni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ jeɔ Otsei lɛ ayeli shishi Nibii ni fiteɔ onikpamɔ lɛ eje shishi momo. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ wa ni ejara hu wa.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my trees very close together in my field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When trees are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for water and soil nutrients, while their branches block sunlight from each other. This causes weak stems and results in far less fruit overall compared to properly spaced trees.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni tsei aniji haa amɛhe feɔ hulu la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibii ni baa lɛ faaa kwraa kɛ akɛto tso ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my young crops regularly throughout the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ehe miihia ni madu mi dumɔwui lɛ daa yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal both rain water and fertilizer meant for your crops. Keeping the area around young plants clean ensures all available soil food goes straight into growing your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Dumɔwui lɛ ahe saamɔ haa anyɛɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ amli.

english: Bare soil loses moisture quickly to sun heat through evaporation. Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or straw—known as mulching—keeps the soil cool and retains water around the roots for many days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji hulu la lɛ ha edɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Mulching ni bɔleɔ he lɛ Akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni nu ahi ehe. Shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi gbii babaoo

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and droop during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in intense afternoon heat is the plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss. As long as the leaves bounce back in the cooler morning, the plant is simply saving moisture to survive the hot sun.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ shi. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba yɛ leebi ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ Tso lɛ miikwɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ kɛkɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How long will it take for my farm to produce more harvest after I start following proper management practices?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe miŋmɔ lɛ dani ekɛ nibii babaoo aba beni mibɔi gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa lɛ he nitsumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Improving farm health happens step-by-step over time. While short-season crops like vegetables show results in a few weeks, tree crops like cocoa or citrus usually need one to two years of consistent care before you see a big increase in fruit yield.
ga: Okwaafoi agbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baa mli fiofio yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ aduawai baatsɔɔ yibiiwoo yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, jwɛi tsei tamɔ kookoo loo citrus baabi ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be afii kome kɛyashi afii enyɔ dani obaana yibii ni anáa lɛ mliyaa ni sa kadimɔ waa.

english: What clear signs show that my young trees are responding well to the new farm care routine?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii komɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ miitsu okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoo hee lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look for fresh green shoots at the ends of branches, dark green healthy leaves, and stronger trunks. If new leaves appear regularly and old leaves stop yellowing, it means your care routine is working properly.
ga: Taomɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anaagbee. Baai lɛ ahe wa, eŋɔli diŋŋ. kɛ tso ni mli wa Kɛji baai heei jeɔ kpo daa ni momo lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No tsɔɔ akɛ bɔ ni okwɛɔ ohe daa lɛ miitsu nii bɔ ni okpaa gbɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the surrounding soil. Leaving tall canopy trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby provides essential shade and keeps the root area cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaa bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ ni aaashi loo tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba ni ebaaha shishifã lɛ he afee fɛ̃i.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an important plant food. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant pulls whatever energy it has left from its bottom leaves to feed the upper growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ gbalaa hewalɛ ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard and woody if I do not harvest them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfee tsei kɛji mikpaaa amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store food as soft starch, but as the plant gets older, it uses that energy to build tough plant fibers. Harvesting at the right time—usually between 9 to 12 months—keeps the tubers soft and easy to cook.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ niyenii toɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo mli. Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ eda lɛ Ekɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tso lɛ mli tsɔji ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ be ni sa mli (bei pii lɛ, yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ) lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehoɔmɔ waaa.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the air and direct sunlight. When the leaves catch more sunlight, the plant can make more food, which results in bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi ni hulu la lɛ aba nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ Tsei baanyɛ afee niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize make my farm soil richer?
ga: Te cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have tiny nodules on their roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. This provides free, natural food that helps neighboring crops like maize grow better.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa anáa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to cover the soil around our plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ sũ awo he ni ebɔle wɔhe lɛ he lɛ? Dumɔ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi?

english: Covering the dirt with dry leaves or grass—known as mulching—acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the ground, keeps moisture in the soil longer, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants curl up and fall off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni pepper ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed, usually by extreme heat, lack of water, or attacks from tiny sap-sucking insects. Giving the plants consistent water and shade during peak heat saves the flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli, loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuamɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo be ha tsei yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why should I cut away the small extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main tree. By leaving only one or two strong suckers and cutting the rest, the main plant gets enough food to produce big, healthy bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Shi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ofo nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli. Tso titri lɛ baaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo dumɔwui wuji ni he wa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, rotten spots on the bottom while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Dark spots on the bottom of tomatoes mean the plant is struggling to absorb calcium, which usually happens when watering is uneven. Keeping the soil consistently moist allows the roots to draw up nutrients smoothly.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitao ni ejie calcium. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the stems of my vegetable crops rot at the ground level after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water cuts off oxygen to the root system and encourages harmful fungi in the dirt to attack the stems. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, hot sunlight. Keeping taller trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains beside them creates shade and holds moisture in the soil, protecting young cocoa during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei akwɛmɔ koni amɛdara loo amɛdu tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant build leaves and strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo baai kɛ toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific food from the soil and lets pests accumulate in the land. Alternating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I put fresh chicken manure directly around my young crops to make them grow faster?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee awo he fɛɛ he. Ani manyɛ matsɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ gbɛ koni amɛdara oya?

english: Fresh poultry manure produces strong heat as it breaks down, which burns delicate crop roots. It should be stacked and allowed to rot completely into compost before being added to the soil.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi heei jieɔ dɔlɛ kpo beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Esa akɛ ato amɛhe ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii dani akɛwo sũ lɛ mli.

english: What is causing holes in the inner leaves of my young maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ amli nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: This damage is often caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the growing center of the plant during the day and feed at night. Inspecting plants early and applying safe control measures stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ shwane mli ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early and removing severely affected plants prevents the disease from spreading across your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Mra Ni tsei ni ena hela waa lɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so much more when the plants are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifite miŋmɔshinii lɛ babaoo lɛ? He ni tso lɛ yɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have weak root systems and compete poorly. Weeds grow faster and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your small plants need to survive, so clearing weeds early gives crops a head start.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyeee akaŋ jogbaŋŋ. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why do I need to erect wooden stakes for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso ko he gbɛjianɔ koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the ground away from diseases and helps the plant produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. Staking haa tso lɛ baa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ helai, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the field during the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Roots rot when water sits around them for too long because soil air is blocked. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ etsĩ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the soil has enough water to plant my seeds after the first rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaadu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The initial rain often leaves deeper soil dry even if the surface looks wet. Dig down about a hand's depth; if the soil at that level can be squeezed into a loose ball without water dripping, it is ready for sowing.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shishijee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ, kɛji akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Tsɔɔmɔ shi aaafee nine kome. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nakai ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. ni nu shwieee shi Efee klalo kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up to protect the plant from losing too much water in intense heat. It acts like the plant closing its windows to keep moisture inside, though severe curling can also be a sign of tiny insects sucking the plant's sap.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu tso lɛ he koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tso ko ni haa samflɛ nɔ, ni emɔɔ nu ni mli edɔ yɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ. Ni aaamu tsei amli nu lɛ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning light yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure or compost helps bring back their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly from very dry to very wet. This stress stops pollination, so the plant sheds flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛyaa nɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ haa pollination kpaɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my sweet pepper fruits turn black and rot from the bottom while still hanging on the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi bell pepper yibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite kɛmiijɛ shishi be mli ni amɛkã jwɛi lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, which usually happens when watering is inconsistent. When the soil goes from very dry to very wet, the plant cannot transport calcium properly to the bottom of the fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ lɛ Tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ calcium aya aduawai lɛ ashishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with plenty of leaves but give me small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛkɛ lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or receives excessive water, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of sending nutrients down into the roots to build large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ shweremɔ mli yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye níhi kɛ yaa sisi ɔ mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why do I get smaller corn cobs when I plant many seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Ani oooha dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Crops planted too close together must fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. When they have to share limited food, none of the individual stalks can grow big enough to make large cobs.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. be mli ni esa akɛ amɛja niyenii fioo pɛ Tso lɛ tsei lɛ eko kwraa edaaa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without big trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, strong sunlight because their delicate leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains creates a protective canopy that keeps the cocoa cool and moist until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni baaha kookoo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants look droopy and dead in the afternoon sun but look fresh again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi kwɛmɔ akɛ ohe ejɔ bo ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: This is a temporary defense mechanism. During hot afternoon hours, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can drink it up, so the plant wilts to save water. Once the sun sets, the roots catch up and replenish the leaves.
ga: Enɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he yɛ be kukuoo mli. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Bɔni afee ni nu akafite lɛ, tsei gboɔ. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Shishifãi baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaayi baa lɛ mli obɔ.

english: How does a stored yam seed know it is time to sprout even before the rains start coming?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni sweet potato dumɔwui ni ato lɛ leɔ be ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ dani nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi?

english: Yams have an internal biological clock that senses changes in temperature and humidity in the air. Even stored indoors, the yam knows when the dry season is ending and uses its own stored moisture to start sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ko ni yɔɔ mli ni nuɔ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli latsaa kɛ latsaa mli lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ akɛto shĩa mli po lɛ, Sweet potatoes hu le be ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baagbe naa. Ni ekɛ nu ni ekɛtoɔ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ emli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛjeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shishi.

english: Why does my land produce a good harvest in the first year but gives much less when I plant the same crop the second year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ kpaa nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli shi ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Every crop pulls specific nutrients out of the earth. Planting the exact same crop on the same plot year after year drains those specific nutrients completely, leaving the soil tired until you rotate crops or restore it with organic matter.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baatsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start planting my maize when the rains begin in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa dumɔ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Planting maize right after the first 2 or 3 steady rains ensures the seeds get enough moisture to germinate without rotting in soil that dries out too quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi 2 loo 3 ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants take longer to harvest in some seasons compared to others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekpaa nii yɛ bei komɛi amli fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava growth relies heavily on rain and sunshine; during dry months or harmattan, the plant slows its growth to conserve water instead of building up its tuber roots.
ga: Kasava dalɛ damɔ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la nɔ waa. Yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ loo harmattan lɛ amli lɛ Tsei lɛ baa amɛdalɛ mli fioo koni amɛbu nu he yɛ shishifãi ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean tiny insects like aphids are sucking the plant's juice, or the plant lacks essential soil nutrients needed to stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids miinu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Aloo tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can my crops recover and produce good yield after being damaged by pests or dry weather?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ efite lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, if you catch the damage early, apply proper organic or inorganic fertilizer, and ensure adequate water, plants can rebuild their strength and yield well.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ fitemɔ tsu nii mra. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Ni kwɛmɔ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi jɛmɛ. Tsei baanyɛ ama hewalɛ amɛma shi ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning excess cocoa branches lets in sunlight and air flow to keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ black pod hela baa. Kpɔ̃ɔ kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Koni kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does putting dried animal manure in my farm soil help my crops grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛfataa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Animal manure acts like rich food for the soil, feeding tiny beneficial organisms and slowly releasing nutrients that give crops the strength to grow thick stems and healthy leaves.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ Nɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ baai ni wa lɛ nɔ fiofio.

english: What makes cowpea or bean plants good for the soil before I plant my next crop?
ga: Mɛni haa tsina loo ŋmei tso hi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ dani miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛduɔ wɔsɛɛ be mli nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food. Climbing up tall stakes keeps the leaves exposed to the sun, which helps the plant grow large, healthy tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni akwɔɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants fall over when they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛbɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are naturally flexible and become top-heavy once heavy fruits grow. Tying the stems to strong wooden stakes keeps the fruit off the wet ground and prevents rot.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ ahe tsɔi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fĩ tso ni wa ko he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my plantain suckers dry up and die when I transplant them during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo he kroko yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers need constant soil moisture to grow new roots. Transplanting them during hot, dry weather makes them lose water faster than they can draw it from the dry ground.
ga: Plantain dumɔwui lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni shishifãi heei akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu tsei yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ afite oya fe bɔ ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive and cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted beside them to shade their tender leaves until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ he waa ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la naa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. koni akɛha baai bibii lɛ anɔ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to build strong, green leaves, so adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help restore the plant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale waa ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava crop growing very tall with big bushy leaves, but the tubers underground remain very thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai lɛ ji jwɛi agbo. Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or the plants are crowded, cassava puts all its energy into growing stem and leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to build fat root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei kɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni yɔɔ fɔ

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers just dry up and fall off without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are extremely high or when water is inconsistent. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to shed flowers to save energy rather than grow fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or by viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees get easily uprooted and fall over during heavy rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that hold a very heavy stem and fruit bundle. Without windbreaks or wooden poles to prop them up, strong winds easily pull their shallow roots out of the wet soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni fiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni fiɔ aduawai ni tsii waa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔne loo tso ko bɛ ni baaye abua lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Ejeɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ mlɛo

english: Why do I need to stack wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tsei ato he koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking allows yam leaves to capture maximum sunlight for growth while keeping the vines off damp soil, which reduces fungal diseases and leads to bigger tubers.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa hulu la babaoo koni amɛdara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, bu wain tso lɛ he kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai baa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops look limp and wilted during the mid-day heat, but stand back up in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ? Shi ani obaanyɛ ote shi leebi?

english: In intense afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the ground. They wilt temporarily to preserve water, then recover overnight when soil cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛhiɛ nu mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ehiɛɔ shi nyɔɔŋ kome mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow healthy green leaves for months without showing any flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ ewo baai eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ nyɔji babaoo ni fɔfɔi ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Certain cowpea varieties only flower when daylight hours shorten during specific times of the year. Planting them at the right seasonal window ensures timely flowering and pod development.
ga: Cowpea henɔi komɛi fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni hulutsoo be lɛ faaa yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi pɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep root systems and quick seed germination that allow them to absorb rainwater and soil nutrients faster than cultivated domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛheɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya fe shia tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves and grow tall. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up and get tightly curled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites hiding under the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kudɔmɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining away, creating ideal conditions for fungal diseases to attack and decay the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baatutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds while my crops are still small instead of waiting until they grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ aakwɛ̃?

english: Young crops have weak root systems that easily lose the fight against weeds for water, light, and soil food. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to establish strong stems.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaawuu ashi jwɛi koni ana nu, la, kɛ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa tso lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: When planted too close together, maize plants compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stems and tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the soil lacks enough calcium or when the soil dries out irregularly while the plant is forming fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from prolonged dry heat, water stress, or insect attacks, dropping the blossoms to save energy and protect the tree from dying.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli. nu mli haomɔ loo kooloi ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ Ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why is covering the ground around my vegetable plants with dry grass or leaves helpful?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi baaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground, known as mulching, protects the soil from direct heat, keeps moisture in the ground longer, and prevents weeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ naa.

english: Yam tubers grow deformed when planted in hard, compact soil or shallow mounds, as the growing tuber cannot easily push through dense soil blocks.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ loo yɛ gɔji ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii ni miida lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ sũ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my okra plants keep growing very tall but produce almost no pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa shɔŋŋ shi ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive shade or giving plants too much rich nitrogen fertilizer causes okra to use all its energy making leaves and high stalks instead of producing flowers and fruit pods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ha tso lɛ loo akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli lɛ, no haa okra lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji kɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ahe ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees get burned easily by direct sunlight. Planting plantains alongside them provides natural shade and keeps the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa trees can survive their first few years.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Enɛ ji koni cacao tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows their leaves to capture more sunlight to feed the growing yam underground, while also preventing leaves from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa etso lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni eye ebua sweet potato ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai hu shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help green up the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni tso lɛ ada lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot wears out the specific nutrients in that soil and encourages pests to stay. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. ni eye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote ŋshɔ lɛ naa Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough before I plant my vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa dani madu aduawai?

english: Healthy farm soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, retains moisture without becoming soggy, and contains earthworms or decaying plant material.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kpakpai amli lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ŋmɔtɔ ehiɛɛɛ mli. kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ahe nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties is the best way to protect your harvest.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa Ekɛbaa Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ obu onibii ahe.

english: How can I stop tiny insects from eating the leaves of my cowpea crop?
ga: Matsi kooloo bibioo lɛ naa. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mi-cowpea baai lɛ?

english: Insects like aphids feed on plant juice and weaken cowpeas. Spraying your crops with a natural water and neem leaf extract solution early in the morning can drive them away without harming the plant.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ aphids yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛhaa cowpea gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nu kɛ neem baa mli nu shwie tsei anɔ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshwie tsei lɛ ni eyeee amɛ awui.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular. Planting after just one isolated rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if a hot dry period follows before the main rains settle.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji akɛ be ko ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very wet to very dry. Keeping the soil consistently moist by putting dry leaves around the base of the plant helps fix this.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ baai ni egbi ni okɛbaabɔle he lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why are my sweet pepper fruits turning black and rotten at the bottom end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi bell pepper yibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Black rotted bottoms on peppers are caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often triggered by irregular watering. Watering your farm evenly and consistently helps the roots absorb calcium properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa kɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily dry out. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide wide leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, protecting them from heat while retaining soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave wide space between my cassava stems when planting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ miidu shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need room underground to expand into large tubers. Planting them too close together forces them to compete for water and nutrients, resulting in thin, small roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant does not get enough water. Extremely dry air or irregular watering stresses the plant, causing it to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from young leaves, or by a viral infection spread by insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ kooloi amli ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli waa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which flows down into the ground to build big, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or beans in the same farm with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Corn needs a lot of nitrogen, so growing them together feeds the corn naturally and improves your soil over time.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo ekomefeemɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmãa lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Too many extra shoots share the food and water coming from the soil. Keeping only one or two strong shoots allows the main plant to produce a bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsobii babaoo ni fa fe nine lɛ jaa niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to be moist before putting fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture in the soil to dissolve so that plant roots can soak it up. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the crop roots or waste the fertilizer as wind blows it away.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ.

english: How can planting trees on my farm help my crops survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Trees hold water deep in the soil with their roots and provide shade that stops the intense sun from drying out your soil and crops too fast.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛshishifãi toɔ nu kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛhaa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi oya tsɔ.

english: Will planting big forest trees near my food crops steal all the nutrients and water from my crops?
ga: Ani koo mli tsei wuji ni miduɔ yɛ mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baaju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: If you plant the right trees, their deep roots pull nutrients up from far underground that your crops cannot reach, enriching the topsoil when tree leaves fall and rot.
ga: Kɛji odu tsei jogbaŋŋ Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyaa he ni oŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ ashɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii be mli ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ.

english: Which food crops are best for me to plant on my farm when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni ji niyenii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Drought-tolerant crops like cassava, cowpeas, millet, and sorghum are best because they require very little water to survive and still yield a good harvest.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ nu fioo pɛ he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lolo.

english: What can I cover my farm soil with to stop it from drying out quickly in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Covering your soil with dried grass, crop stalks, or leaves (called mulching) acts like a blanket, keeping moisture trapped in the ground and protecting plant roots from heat.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, tsei ashishifãi, loo baai (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to mix tree planting with my regular crop farming instead of planting crops alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui baafata daa dumɔwui ahe moŋ fe ni madu tsei pɛ lɛ?

english: Mixing trees with crops improves long-term soil fertility, protects your farm from wind damage, and gives you extra income from fruits or wood alongside your regular harvest.
ga: Tsei ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Buu oŋmɔ lɛ he koni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite. ni ekɛ shika kroko ni jɛɔ aduawai loo tsei amli baa lɛ aha yɛ ŋmaa ni akpaa daa lɛ masɛi.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow and drop off when the weather gets very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plants drop their leaves during dry hot spells to prevent water from evaporating out of them, which is a survival mechanism to keep the root and stem alive.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni nu lɛ akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahiɔ shi koni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi.

english: How can I prevent the strong dry Harmattan winds from breaking my tall crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ akafite miŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Planting a border of fast-growing trees or shrubs along the edge of your farm creates a windbreak that slows down harsh winds before they reach your crops.
ga: Tsei loo tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ baa shi dani eshɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Can I plant beans and maize together on the same piece of farm land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer that helps the maize grow taller and stronger.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening prevents the water from evaporating immediately in the hot afternoon heat, allowing plant roots to drink fully.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ trukaa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ koni amɛnu nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do tree leaves and old crop leaves improve the richness of my farmland?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe baai kɛ tsei momo ahe baai aha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ?

english: When leaves fall and rot into the ground, they break down into organic compost, adding natural fertilizer that feeds the soil microbes and keeps the earth rich and soft.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baai lɛ fãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni efeɔ bɔdɔɔ

english: Can I use animal manure instead of store-bought chemical fertilizer to grow my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi atsu nii yɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ shwapo mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ najiaŋ kɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, well-rotted animal manure adds rich organic matter to the soil, improving its ability to hold water and nutrients naturally, which keeps crops healthy without depending on expensive imported fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo fataa sũ lɛ he. Ehaa nyɛmɔ ni oyɔɔ ni okɛbaahiɛ nu kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ he afɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and looking weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth, or that the roots are suffering from poor drainage or lack of nutrients in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo shishifãi lɛ bɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How does adding compost to my soil help my crops survive long dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Compost acts like a sponge in the soil, holding onto rainwater for a long time so your crop roots can continue drinking even when it stops raining.
ga: Kompost tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ nugbɔ nu toɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aya nɔ anu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ekpa po.

english: How do I tell if my crops are getting too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛnáaa nu bɔ ni sa?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves roll up, droop, or turn brown; when they get too much water, the leaves turn yellow, roots rot, and the plant stops growing because the soil lacks air.
