ga: Kɛji nu bɛ tsei lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgbeeɔ shi, loo amɛfeɔ asarasu. Kɛ́ onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni tsei lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before producing any fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of moisture stress the plant, causing it to drop its flowers to conserve energy and survive rather than spending resources on developing fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ haoɔ tsei. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite ni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baatsu nii koni akɛfee aduawai lɛ

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my cereal crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, which naturally feeds neighboring crops like maize and improves soil fertility.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows pests and soil diseases that target that specific plant to build up in the soil, making your crops weaker and less productive each season.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aaaya nɔ adu lɛ baaha sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tsɔɔ nakai tso lɛ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than my planted crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to compete aggressively for light, water, and soil nutrients, allowing them to sprout and grow faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛye niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli, ni no haa jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my seeds take so long to germinate when the ground is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ?

english: Seeds need moisture to soften their outer shell and trigger growth; without enough soil water, the seed remains dormant to protect itself from dying in dry ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ nu koni eha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo ni eha amɛdara. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛhiɛ aka shi. Koni obu ohe kɛjɛ gbele he yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil or get eaten by insects so quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ loo kooloi yeɔ amɛ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains spoil if they are not dried properly before storage because extra moisture attracts mold and leaves them vulnerable to insects that feed on soft, damp grains.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ agbiko amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when I plant on the same piece of land every single year without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni miduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Soil loses its natural nutrients and food supply when cropped continuously without a break. Resting the land or rotating crops gives the soil time to rebuild its nutrients so future plants do not starve.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii enaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni hɔmɔ akaye tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does burning cleared weeds on my farm harm the land over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ashãa lɛ náa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fire kills beneficial soil bugs and earthworms that break down leaves and keep the ground fertile. Burning leaves the soil bare, dry, and easily washed away by heavy rains, leading to poor crop growth.
ga: La gbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ tsei ahe tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbiɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ adalɛ ni ehiii.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts or beans together with cassava on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally pull food from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them alongside heavy-eating crops like cassava feeds the soil naturally and helps both crops yield better.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up and turn yellow when the rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Curling leaves is a plant's way of rolling up to save water and reduce sweating in hot weather. Yellowing happens when dry roots cannot absorb nutrients from the dry earth.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛfoɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛha latsaa aba shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Yellow baa kɛji shishifãi ni egbi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: When a cocoa tree lacks enough water, shade, or soil nutrients during hot or dry periods, it sheds some young pods to save enough strength for the remaining ones to survive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei bɛ nu, hulutsoo, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Eshwieɔ ŋmeii bibii koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa aha kookoo tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do insect pests multiply so quickly on my farm during very dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ?

english: Hot weather speeds up how fast insects lay eggs and hatch. At the same time, dry weather weakens plants, making it easier for pests to attack them.
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha kooloi bibii awo amɛwui oya amɛha tɛŋŋ? yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ baatutua amɛ.

english: Seeds carry only a small amount of stored energy to push their first leaf above ground. If buried too deep, the shoot runs out of energy before reaching the surface and dies underground.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato ni amɛkɛtsiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ baa lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tu lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the stems of my young crops help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass acts like a blanket that shades the ground from the burning sun. It traps moisture in the soil longer so roots stay cool and hydrated between rains.
ga: Mulch ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my crops stay pale yellow even after I apply fertilizer during a drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can drink it in. If the soil is completely dry, fertilizer sits uselessly in the dirt and can even burn the roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lɛ, Fertilizer baata shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ po.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and bigger than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛdaraa fe tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are better adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil food. Clearing them early prevents them from crowding out your main crops and causing hunger.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni nyɛɔ amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkawo onibii titrii lɛ amli ni amɛkɛ hɔmɔ aba.

english: Why would I spend money to grow my crops inside a greenhouse instead of just planting them directly in my open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shika he hiaa mi koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu nii yɛ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Greenhouses protect young plants from harsh sunlight, heavy rainfall, and pests, giving them a controlled environment to grow stronger and faster before they are exposed to harsh field conditions.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛdara oya dani amɛyashɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wa lɛ amli.

english: Is it good to start my young cocoa seedlings in a greenhouse before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Yes, nursing cocoa seedlings in a greenhouse protects them from heat stress and pests early on, which leads to stronger stems and much higher seedling survival rates.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ hewalɛ waa, ni dumɔwui lɛ hu hiɔ shi babaoo.

english: Will a greenhouse structure be strong enough to withstand the heavy rains and strong winds we get here in Ghana?
ga: Ani ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni wɔnaa yɛ Ghana lɛ naa?

english: Durable greenhouses built with strong frames and UV-resistant covers are specifically designed to handle heavy tropical rains and winds without collapsing or wearing out quickly.
ga: Akɛ tsɔne ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ nɔ ni nyɛɔ ekɛ UV shwieɔ nɔ lɛ ema, ni afee tsũi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ naa ni amɛkumɔ shi loo amɛfiteee oya.

english: How much does it usually cost to set up a small, reliable greenhouse unit on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shika enyiɛ eheɔ koni akɛto ŋmɔ bibioo ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana?

english: A standard, durable single-unit greenhouse in Ghana generally starts around one thousand Ghana Cedis, making it a manageable long-term investment for raising healthy crops.
ga: Ghana shĩa kome ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ Ghana cedis akpe kome mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli shika ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii koni akɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important for my young seedlings to develop deep and strong roots before I plant them out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni midumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa dani madu amɛ lɛ?

english: Strong roots allow plants to anchor firmly in the soil and absorb water and nutrients efficiently, helping the crop survive dry weather spells and grow faster.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli wa haa tsei fiɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ he ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Can I prepare my own cocoa seeds for planting on my farm, or do I need special shade structures to nurse them?
ga: Ani manyɛ masaa mi diɛŋtsɛ mi-cocoa ŋmeii ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Aloo ehe miihia ni mafee hulutsoo gbɛjianɔtoo krɛdɛɛ ko koni mawo kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ?

english: While you can nurse seeds outdoors, using a shaded structure or greenhouse protects delicate young seeds from extreme heat and heavy downpours that can wash away seedling soil.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ okwɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ kpo nɔ moŋ. Shi kɛ akɛ tsɔne ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, ni baanyɛ ahoo dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither easily when the hot dry season starts in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛ̃i ba yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that lose water very quickly in direct heat, which causes them to dry out unless they are protected by shade or structures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ wo mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Enɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ja akɛ hulutsoo loo tsɔne ko ebu amɛhe.

english: How many years can I expect a durable greenhouse structure to last under our intense sun in Ghana?
ga: Afii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ ŋwɛitsu ko ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baahi shi yɛ wɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ shishi?

english: A well-built greenhouse using strong, weather-resistant materials can last for several years, allowing you to nurse multiple seasons of crops without needing frequent repairs.
ga: Tsũ ni akɛ nibii ni mli wa ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ama lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baahi shi afii babaoo. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ bei babaoo mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni osaa amɛ shii abɔ.

english: How does growing my seedlings inside a structure protect them from insects and diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsũ ko mli lɛ buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii kɛ helai ahe?

english: The fine mesh or plastic covering of a structure creates a physical barrier that keeps insects from eating young leaves and carrying diseases to delicate seedlings.
ga: Net loo plastic ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛhaa tsũ lɛ he lɛ feɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye baai bibii lɛ ni amɛkɛ hela akahã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: How do I know when my nursery cocoa plants are strong enough to be moved onto the open land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni agbele nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa plants are ready for transplanting when they have formed a firm, woody stem, strong root system, and multiple mature green leaves, usually after a few months in the nursery.
ga: Cocoa tsei efee klalo akɛ abaadu amɛ kɛji amɛyɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ tsei. shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo ni eda kwraa Bei pii lɛ, amɛhiɔ shi nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What makes a crop a 'cash crop', and how do I know if my land is right for growing one like cocoa or cashew?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ‘Shika ŋmɔshi nibii’ ni te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo cashew nuts adumɔ?

english: A cash crop is grown primarily to sell for profit rather than for your family to eat. To know if your land is suitable, you need to check if your soil holds enough water, if your district gets the right rainy season, and if buyers are active in your area.
ga: Aduɔ shika helɛtemɔ he ŋmɔshi nibii titri koni akɛhɔ̃ɔ bɔni afee ni ana sɛɛnamɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu niyenii ni oweku lɛ aye lɛ. Ani oosumɔ ni ole kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ sa? Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lo. Ani he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be ni sa? Ni ani mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava together with young cash crops on the same field without harming them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmei, kɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni miyeee amɛ awui?

english: Yes, growing short-term food crops alongside young cash crops can work well if spaced properly, because the food crops give you early food and income while providing shade for the young cash crop seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni akɛyeɔ be kukuoo mli ni aduɔ yɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ejaakɛ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onáa niyenii kɛ shika oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shika ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ hu náa hulutsoo.

english: Why do old cash crop trees stop giving high yields after many years on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii momoi lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ afii babaoo ni amɛye yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Over decades, trees exhaust specific nutrients in the soil and their root systems age, making them less efficient at taking up water and fertilizer and more vulnerable to diseases.
ga: Yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli lɛ, tsei lɛ laajeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ amɛshishifãi ni egbɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli. ni amɛyɛ oshara babaoo kɛha helai srɔtoi.

english: Why is the district encouraging us to plant new crop varieties instead of keeping our traditional local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Kpokpaa lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii heei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔkɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii tsutsu lɛ baato lɛ?

english: New improved varieties are bred to mature faster, resist local pests and diseases better, and withstand dry spells, leading to higher and more reliable harvests for your farm.
ga: Afɔ ŋmeii heei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛshwere oya. Ehe wa jogbaŋŋ kɛha maŋ lɛ mli helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli ni nɔ kwɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ baa kɛhaa oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do crops grow very well on my neighbor's farm but fail on my farm just across the road?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli shi amɛshwereɔ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops react strongly to small differences in topsoil thickness, shade, and underground water drainage, which can vary significantly even between neighboring plots.
ga: Tsei hereɔ srɔtofeemɔi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ waa. Enɛ baanyɛ asoro lɛ kwraa yɛ shikpɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ po.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves turning yellow means the plant needs water or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yellow leaves that droop and dry out usually mean a lack of water, while yellowing that starts at the bottom leaves while the plant stays upright often means the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni gbeeɔ shi ni egbiɔ lɛ tsɔɔ nu ni bɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ beni tso lɛ ema shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, niyenii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop plants grow tall and green but fail to produce fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ shi ewooo yibii loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Plants grow very leafy without fruit when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, causing the plant to put all its energy into stem and leaf growth instead of flowering.
ga: Tsei baakwɛ̃ baai babaoo ni yibii bɛ mli kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi.

english: Is it better to plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the season or wait longer?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ loo aaamɛ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady, because a single early rain is often followed by a long dry stretch that can scorch and kill newly germinated seeds.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ tso kome nɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ.

english: Will planting my crops closer together give me a bigger harvest from my small farm?
ga: Kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ, ebaaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space, resulting in weak, thin plants that produce smaller total yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ atswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fɛɛ lɛ faaa.

english: How do sudden heatwaves affect the way my crops produce seeds and pods?
ga: Te hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ saa bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extreme heat stresses plants, causing them to drop their flowers early to save water, which prevents pods and fruits from forming.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya koni nu akafite. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii kɛ aduawai afee.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants use to make food. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni tsei lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛyeɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts or cowpeas helps improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the ground, naturally fertilizing the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Will planting my seeds very close together give me a bigger total harvest?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants with smaller yields compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni sa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into high mounds before planting my yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa sũ naa yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ dani miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to expand. High mounds give the tubers soft soil to grow long and thick without struggling against hard ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa abɔ mɔdɛŋ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and small worms inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which feed on leafy tissues. Catching them early with recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts prevents crop failure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai amli fãji lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nu lɛ ni akɛbaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, atsĩɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds before I plant my seeds instead of waiting until after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ dani adu nii moŋ fe ni aaamɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and quickly steal water, light, and nutrients from the soil. Clearing them before planting gives young seeds a clean environment to establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa he ko ni he tse koni amɛná shishifãi.

english: It is better to buy fresh certified hybrid seeds each season. Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their special strength in the second generation, leading to smaller yields and uneven growth.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni fa fe tsutsu lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable garden during the hot afternoon or in the early morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi?

english: Early morning is best because afternoon heat evaporates water quickly before the roots can absorb it, and hot wet leaves can encourage fungal diseases.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ. Ni baai ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft and spoil quickly if I harvest them right after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ akpa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ blɛoo ni amɛgboi oya kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause cassava plants to absorb excess water into their roots, diluting starch content and causing rapid rotting after harvest. It is best to harvest when the soil is damp but not waterlogged.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Okɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ falɛ awo mli. ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ akpa be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and stop growing when there is heavy rainfall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain floods the soil, it fills up all the small air spaces underground and suffocates the plant roots. Without air, the roots cannot absorb nutrients from the land, causing the leaves to turn yellow and the plant to stop growing until the soil dries out.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaawo kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii lɛ amli. Eyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛ mumɔ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi anɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ kpaa daamɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni sũ lɛ gbiɔ.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture for me to start planting after the first rain of the season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ oje dumɔ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant after the very first rain, as the ground underneath is often still dry. Dig a small hole hand-deep into the soil; if you can squeeze the soil at the bottom into a firm ball that stays together without dripping water, the soil is ready for planting.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Akɛni bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo hewɔ lɛ, okɛ oniji atsa bu bibioo ko ni mli kwɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shwie shi ni ofee bɔɔlu ni mli wa ni nu shwieee shi lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why is my farmland producing much smaller harvests now than it did five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ miiwo yibii fioo kwraa fe bɔ ni eji afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crops on the same land every season slowly drains all the food out of the soil. Just like a person needs food to stay strong, soil needs a break, crop rotation, or organic manure to rebuild its fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be. Bei lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fiofio. Taakɛ niyenii he hiaa wɔ koni wɔhe awa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he miihia ni akumɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ koni akɛfee babaoo hee

english: How does adding dried animal manure onto my soil make my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure acts like a slow-releasing food for the soil. It improves the soil structure so it can hold water longer during hot days and releases natural nutrients that plant roots can easily drink up.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni jieɔ sũ lɛ fiofio. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ anu mlɛo lɛ kpo

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that easily burn and dry up under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and cool air for the young cocoa to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ebaanyɛ eha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly during the dry Harmattan season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli, kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ po lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind blows away moisture from crop leaves much faster than the roots can suck up water from the ground. Covering the soil around the base of your crops with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and slows down water loss.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo.

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by small moths on the leaves. They hide inside the moist inner leaves of the maize plant where it is safe from heat and birds, eating the soft leaves before the plant can grow tall.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei amli baai ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Eji he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulutsoo kɛ okpoi ahe. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani tso lɛ daa.

english: What is making the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and shrink?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny, almost invisible insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant juice, which damages the leaf tissue as it tries to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ nɔ ni anaaa, tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu. ni fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji beni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much strong fertilizer. When stressed, the plant saves its energy to stay alive rather than spending energy to make fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ koni amɛhi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee aduawai

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and small instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bibii yɛ agbo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose soil to push through as they grow bigger. Hard, packed soil, hidden rocks, or small worms in the ground block the root from expanding smoothly, making the tuber bend or stay small.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛtsɔ mli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ tɛ ni akɛtee Aloo ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. ni haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi loo efeɔ bibioo

english: Why are the leaves of my corn plants developing small brown spots and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: This is often a sign of a fungal disease like leaf blight or rust, which spreads during warm, humid weather. Removing severely affected leaves early and using recommended treatments can prevent it from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ enɛ ji ŋmei hela ko he okadi, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Baai ni ena hela waa lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common crop pest in Ghana. They hide inside the central leaves (whorl) to feed, but applying approved control measures early in the morning or late evening when they are active can protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli (rings) koni amɛye nii. Shi kɛ okɛ gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni amɛtsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe.

english: How does leaving weeds in my corn field cause my crops to get sick?
ga: Bɔ ni jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ hela

english: Weeds act as living homes for crop diseases and harmful insects while stealing water and soil nutrients from your corn plants, making your crops weaker and more vulnerable to diseases.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ shihilɛhe kɛha tsei ahelai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejuɔ nu kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-corn tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall but produce tiny cobs when I plant on the same land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? When planted on the same area every year?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil exhausts specific nutrients like nitrogen. Rotating your crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore soil fertility naturally, giving you bigger cobs.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ fiteɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa onáa cob ni da fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at leaf tips in a V-pattern usually means your soil lacks nitrogen, which is needed for healthy green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer at the right stage will help the plant recover.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa yɛ V gbɛ nɔ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Leaf rolling is the corn plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss and protect itself from intense heat, showing that the soil is getting dry and needs water.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miibɔi gbimɔ ni nu he miihia.

english: Why should I avoid planting my corn seeds very close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ ahe?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin stalks and lower yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my corn plants look weak if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain often moistens only the top layer of soil without deep moisture, causing seeds to germinate quickly and then suffer or die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli fũuɔ ni fɛ̃i ni mli kwɔ bɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. No sɛɛ lɛ, ebaana amanehulu loo ebaagbo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do high-yield hybrid maize seeds produce poor results when I replant seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds lose their special vigor, uniform growth, and disease resistance after the first harvest, so buying fresh certified seeds each season is necessary for a high yield.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ. shweremɔ ni tamɔ ekome kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase yɛ be fɛɛ mli koni anyɛ ana yibii babaoo.

english: Mold forms when moisture remains inside the cob core or when stored grain absorbs dampness from the ground or air, so storing dried maize in raised, ventilated areas or airtight bags is essential.
ga: Mold baa kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ehi cob core lɛ mli. aloo beni dumɔwui ni ato lɛ shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni egbi ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli loo vacuum bag lɛ he miihia waa.

english: This usually means your soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the food plants use to grow green leaves. When nitrogen is low, the plant takes it from its older leaves at the bottom to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ. Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain only wets the top surface, but the soil underneath remains dry and hot. If you plant right away, the intense heat trapped in the dry ground can cook and kill the cassava cuttings before the heavy rains fully arrive.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋwɛigbɛ pɛ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lolo. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni amɔmɔ yɛ hei ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aho ni egbe ŋmei tsei dani nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: How do I choose the right plantain suckers from my old farm to start a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni sa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for maidenhead or sword suckers, which have narrow, spear-like leaves and strong bases. Avoid suckers with broad, wide leaves because they are weak, take longer to yield fruit, and produce smaller bunches.
ga: Taomɔ gbekɛ yoo lɛ yitso loo klante tu lɛ. Eyɛ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi kɛ shishitoo ni mli wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe ejaakɛ amɛhe waaa. Eheɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii. ni amɛfee tsei bibii bibii

english: Why is it wrong for me to place my granular fertilizer right against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ mikɛ granular fertilizer baawo he ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is full of strong salts that draw water out of the plant tissue. Placing it directly against the stem can burn the bark and roots, so you should always place it in a ring a few inches away where the root tips can safely absorb it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ amɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi mli be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I see tiny holes and dirt inside the center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Kɛ muji ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the growing cone of the plant during the hot day to eat the soft leaves. You must spray early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii lɛ.

english: Why do many of the small green cocoa pods on my trees turn shriveled and black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Mɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gboi ni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdara lɛ.

english: This is often caused by a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the tree deliberately drops pods it cannot feed, or by fungal diseases like black pod. Pruning heavy shade branches helps air circulate and reduces fungal growth so more pods survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherelle Wilt, ni tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ ŋmeii ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji amli. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi babaoo.

english: Why is my harvest getting smaller when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize pulls the exact same nutrients out of the soil every season, leaving the ground completely exhausted. Rotating your crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the dirt and breaks the life cycle of soil pests.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ kwraa. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ashihilɛ

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and greener than the crops I planted and cared for?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ fe tsei ni miduɔ ni mikwɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally built to survive poor conditions, deep droughts, and harsh weather. Because they grow faster roots than cultivated crops, they quickly steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your farm.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni adebɔɔ fee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. hɔmɔ ni mli kwɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyɛ shishifãi ni daa oya fe tsei ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ oya.

english: How do insects get inside my tightly tied bags of dried harvested beans in the storehouse?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii boteɔ mi ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Insects or their invisible eggs are often already on the beans when you harvest them from the field. If the grain is not fully dried under the sun or sealed in airtight bags, those eggs hatch inside the sack and eat your stored crop.
ga: Ekolɛ kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ yɛ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ momo beni okpaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ mli loo akɛwooo vacuum kotoku mli lɛ, Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotokui lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly into a ball during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bɔɔlu yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is the plant's natural shield against losing moisture in extreme heat. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to conserve water until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Tsei baa shikpɔŋ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛfoɔ koni amɛbu nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the nutrient that gives plants strong, healthy green leaves, and without it, growth slows down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Ni kɛji nitrogen bɛ lɛ Dalɛ baafee mlɛo.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller harvests each year when I plant maize in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the ground. Rotating your maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate hot, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and retaining moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing thin and tall with tiny ears when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ toi bibii beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and food from the soil. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow thick stems and big ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ toi wuji baakwɛ̃.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or a shortage of phosphorus, which is the nutrient needed to hold onto flowers and form fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ hao tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe ni ewoɔ yibii

english: How do I know if my tomato plants are getting too much water or not enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛmiiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Under-watered tomatoes wilts and gets dry leaves, while over-watered plants get yellow leaves and rotted roots because too much water starves the roots of air.
ga: Tomato ni nine shɛɔ nu nɔ lɛ baagbi ni ebaaná baai ni egbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni nu babaoo baa amɛnɔ lɛ baaná baai ŋmɔŋ kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ ejaakɛ nu babaoo baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and shrinking during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Curled leaves during dry spells are often caused by sap-sucking insects like mealybugs or spider mites, which attack plants when water is scarce. Planting clean, resistant cuttings prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs loo spider mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa. ni tutuaa tsei kɛji nu faaa Tsei ni he tse ni wa ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly and choke my crops right after clearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ajie jwɛi lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil and quickly sprout as soon as clearing exposes them to rain and sunlight. Clearing weeds early while they are small prevents them from taking food from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ kɛ hulu la shɛ he ni ajie lɛ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: What causes cocoa beans to lose flavor or get rejected by buyers after harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo yibii lɛ amli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ loo mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Poor flavor and lower quality happen if cocoa beans are harvested when underripe or if they are not fermented in plantain leaves and dried properly in clean sunshine.
ga: Nɔ ni ehiii kɛ nɔ ni ehiii baaba kɛji akɛ akpa kookoo yibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛshɛko kwraa. Aloo kɛji akɛ plantain baai lɛ efɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni mli tse mli.

english: How can I tell when a bunch of plantains is ready for harvest so it doesn't spoil before sale?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-plantains lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni egboŋ dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Plantains are ready to harvest when the individual fingers become plump and lose their sharp, angled edges, but before any green skin begins turning yellow on the stalk.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji inchi fɛɛ inchi mli eyi ni eshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ efo mli. Shi dani no baashɛ lɛ, hewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their roots are delicate and leaves dry out quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains around them protects the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ waaa, ni baai lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to breathe. When heavy rain sits in the soil for too long without draining, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛgboɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves grow green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Flowers often fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and adding organic compost encourages the flowers to turn into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ he amanehulu. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaawo fɔfɔii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight to make food for their tubers underground. Staking the vines helps leaves catch maximum sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni ehaaa helai aba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my ripe tomatoes split open right before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shwereɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Tomato skins crack when the plant gets a sudden large amount of water after a dry period. The inside grows too quickly for the skin to stretch, so keeping soil watering steady prevents cracking.
ga: Tomato hewolo lɛ mli fãa kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbala.

english: Why are small holes suddenly appearing inside the central leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii eba trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by fall armyworms that hide and eat inside the soft center leaves of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying organic remedies like ash or neem extract helps save the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fallworms ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra kɛ tsofai ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli tamɔ sũ loo neem mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know when my plantain suckers are ready to flower and produce a bunch?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-plantain tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaawo fɔfɔi ni amɛbaawo ŋmeii?

english: Plantains usually produce a flowering stalk about nine to twelve months after planting, once the plant has grown around 20 to 30 healthy leaves to support the heavy fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains woɔ fɔfɔii aaafee nyɔji nɛɛhu kɛyashi nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni tso lɛ yɛ baai ni mli wa 20 kɛyashi 30 ni baaye abua aduawai ni tsii lɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark weather. Pruning overgrown tree branches lets sunlight and air flow through, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni atatu ewo mli lɛ kɛbaa. Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules, naturally fertilizing the soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small roots that cannot handle direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava beside them creates shade and keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantain loo cassava lɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves is a sign that the soil is running out of nitrogen, which the plant needs to stay green and grow. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea around the base of the plants will give them the food they need to recover.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei baai lɛ shishi tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miiho. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni hiɛ nitrogen, tamɔ urea fata tso lɛ shishigbɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize on the same spot every season drains the specific nutrients maize needs from the soil and allows maize pests and diseases to build up. Rotating your field with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients naturally back into the soil.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa. Oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei baatsake lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: What is eating small holes in the middle leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ teŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms hiding inside the central leaf funnel. Applying recommended organic sprays like neem leaf extract or appropriate insecticides early in the morning or late evening will help control the worms before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that feed on plant sap and spread diseases. Controlling these pests early with soapy water sprays or recommended insect sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni egbɛɔ helai srɔtoi eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛ samla loo kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Which part of a cassava stem should I cut and plant to get a heavy yield?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ afo ni adu koni ená yibii babaoo?

english: You should choose the middle section of a mature, healthy cassava stem cut to about 20 to 30 centimeters with 4 to 6 raised buds. Avoid using the soft green top or the dry bottom part, as they do not sprout strongly.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni eda ni ehe wa lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ amɛ aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30 kɛ ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni awó nɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shishi ni egbi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛkwɛɛɛ waa.

english: How can I select the right plantain suckers from my old farm to plant on a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni sa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers' that have a thick, heavy base and narrow, blade-like leaves. Avoid 'water suckers' with broad leaves and thin bases because they grow slowly and produce small, weak bunches of plantain.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’ ni shishitoo lɛ mli tse ni tsii kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ ŋmeii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘suckers’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛdaraa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding excessive fertilizers during flowering helps the blossoms stay on and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high toward sunlight using stakes. When leaves get plenty of sunlight, the plant creates more food, which travels down to make larger, healthier yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli kɛtsɔ tso nɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ baafee niyenii babaoo. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛná hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry out and kill newly germinated seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become frequent and consistent so the soil stays wet enough for seeds to establish roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ shii abɔ kɛ daa bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ atswa shishifãi.

english: Planting maize on the same field year after year removes the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific crop pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts vital nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry hot spell that bakes the topsoil. If seeds germinate during this break in the rain, the young sprouts will dry up and die before regular rains start.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni mli edɔ ni shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ be mli ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aje shishi.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is plenty of sunshine for all plants in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and root space from your crops under the soil. Even if there is enough sunlight, crops choked by weeds grow slowly because they are starved of water and nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ moŋ Dumɔwui ni jwɛi ehà nɔ lɛ daa fiofio ejaakɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize yield much less than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii fioo kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high yield in their first generation only. If you save seeds from that harvest, the second-generation plants lose those special qualities, resulting in smaller cobs and uneven growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji ohere dumɔwui kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei ayinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baafite nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or that the roots are waterlogged from heavy rain. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shishifãi lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating small, ragged holes into the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-bibii ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the growing center leaf (the whorl). Checking your plants early and applying targeted treatments into the whorl stops them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni miida lɛ ateŋ (whorls) lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ amli mra. ni okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ awo ring lɛ mli koni tso lɛ akafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants keep falling off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant faces stress, such as extreme hot dry weather, insufficient soil water, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Mulching the soil to keep it moist and cool helps the flowers stay on the plant.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ kpe. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in open sunny fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain beside them creates a shaded canopy that keeps the seedlings cool and moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ lateral plantains ni aduɔ Ehaa hulutsoo ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to harvest underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, the stems turn brown and woody, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ shishi feɔ blɔfo ni efeɔ tso. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why should I pinch off the extra small shoots growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Extra ni miida yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Removing extra side shoots (suckers) directs the plant's energy toward making large fruits rather than growing excess stem and leaves. It also improves airflow around the leaves to prevent rot.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine (suckers) lɛ, etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ewo yibii wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ hu yaa hiɛ koni ekɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from intense heat and bright sunlight. By curling, the leaf reduces its exposed surface area, which helps the plant conserve water and prevent drying out during hot days.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ abɔle baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa amɛhe ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛtsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and wither when planted without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have thin, sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade trees or companion crops like plantains to shelter them and keep the surrounding air and soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and die after heavy rain sits on my field for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the field for too long, it pushes air out of the soil, effectively suffocating the roots and preventing them from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha he ko nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When a plant lacks sufficient nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, it moves available nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛjieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce smaller peppers when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ pepper bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots compete with neighboring plants for soil nutrients, fertilizer, and water, leaving less food and energy for the plant to grow large fruits.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu, ni no haa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii kɛ hewalɛ fioo ni amɛkɛwoɔ aduawai wuji.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I keep growing maize on the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously consumes the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year without giving the land time to recover, which weakens plant growth over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii afi fɛɛ afi ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do crops growing near heavy weeds look smaller and paler than clean crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe tse fe tsei ni he tse lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, groundwater, and soil food from your crops. Because weeds grow quickly, they starve your crops of the resources needed to grow healthy green leaves.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. Amɛjieɔ nibii ni he hiaa bo koni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of pollination from insects, causing the plant to abort flower development to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii ni haaa tso lɛ aná fɔfɔi lɛ. Ehaa tsei kpaɔ fɔfɔi akwɛ̃mɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my plantain crop yield smaller bunches when I allow many shoots to grow around the main plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni miha ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso titri lɛ he hewɔ lɛ.

english: Young side shoots, called suckers, feed off the main mother plant. Leaving too many suckers splits the plant's energy among many shoots instead of focusing it into growing one big bunch.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ nyɛ titri lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaja tso lɛ hewalɛ mli ewo ŋmeii babaoo mli. Mohu ɔ, moo hyɛ kaa tso ɔmɛ nɛ a wa nɛ a peeɔ kui nguahi.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to produce big tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ko ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji aba lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce food through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight, producing the energy required to swell the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ koni ená hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants die when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight, which scorches their leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving mature shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa from heat stress and keeps the soil moist while the plants establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Enɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he haomɔ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize plants usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. Adding organic manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the green color and improves the overall crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating ragged holes through the leaves of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni ekpɔtɔ kɛmiitsɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which target young corn leaves and feed inside the leaf whorls. Inspecting plants early and applying recommended biological treatments or safe crop protection sprays early in the morning helps stop them from destroying your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii yɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofa ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ baaye abua ni amɛtsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: If I plant my cassava cuttings very close to each other, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani nibii babaoo baaba?

english: Planting cassava too close together causes the plants to compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients, leading to small and thin roots. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly after I burn all the dry bush on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ beni mishã tsei ni egbi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning off dry bush destroys essential organic matter and nutrients in the topsoil while killing beneficial soil organisms that help feed plants. Clearing weeds without burning helps preserve soil moisture, prevents soil erosion, and improves long-term crop growth.
ga: Tsoi ni egbi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei niyenii lɛ. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ ni ashãaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Tsi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni oha tsei adalɛ aya hiɛ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without producing any fruit when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive heat causes tomato flowers to dry up because high temperatures prevent proper pollination inside the blossom. Keeping the root zone moist with regular watering and using straw mulch around the base of the plant helps lower soil heat and reduces flower drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ejaakɛ dɔlɛ ni fa babaoo tsiɔ pollination ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Kɛ́ shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli fũu kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ daa kɛ jwɛi ni akɛha shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni sũ lɛ mli dɔlɛ aba shi, ni fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hu aba shi.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid maize harvests lose their strength, disease resistance, and high-yielding traits in subsequent generations. Planting certified seeds ensures high germination rates, stronger resistance to local pests, and a much higher grain yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ he waaa. Helai ahe shiwoo kɛ sui ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.
