Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ adumɔ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo. Kuu lɛ mli hewalɛ ni teɔ shi woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. kɛ ŋmaa ni anáa babaoo fe tsutsu lɛ

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal infection that thrives in cold, overly damp, and humid conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let in air and sunlight, weeding the undergrowth, and removing infected pods quickly prevents the fungal spores from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ. Eyɛ fɛ̃i tsɔ ni eyɛ fɛ̃i, ni efoɔ tsei niji krokomɛi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ kɛjɛ mli Ni kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize on the same field, or will they harm each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpeas loo beans kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ? Aloo amɛbaaye amɛhe awui?

english: Planting beans or cowpeas alongside maize is actually beneficial because leguminous plants pull nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil, which helps feed the maize. This practice improves soil fertility and maximizes your land space.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni baaye abua ni aha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii Nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwereɔ babaoo.

english: Why do insects attack and turn my harvested maize grains into dust while stored in the granary?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ni amɛfeɔ sũ be mli ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils thrive when grain is stored with too much moisture or in open containers where bugs can enter. Thoroughly drying your grain under the sun until it is hard and storing it in airtight, sealed bags prevents insects from surviving and destroying your harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli. aloo yɛ tsɛnsii ni agbele mli ni kooloi baanyɛ abote mli Dumɔwui lɛ agbimɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi amɛhe wa ni okɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum efo mli lɛ amli lɛ baatsi kooloi anaa koni amɛkajo foi ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and soil moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do improved hybrid maize seeds yield more than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid maize seeds are specially bred in labs to resist local pests and handle dry weather efficiently. Saved seeds lose these strong protective traits over generations, leading to smaller yields and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ nɔ yɛ laboratori ko mli koni ekɛte shi ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ akpee naa jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ hebuu sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi.

english: What does it mean when a bag of crop seeds comes with an official certification tag or seed passport?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ dumɔwui kotoku ko kɛ maŋ lɛ hegbɛ loo dumɔwui ahe passport ba?

english: An official tag or seed passport means agricultural officers inspected and tested the seeds to ensure they germinate well, produce strong plants, and are completely free from dangerous seed-borne diseases.
ga: Official tag loo seed passport tsɔɔ akɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ekwɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli ni amɛka amɛkwɛ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ewoɔ tsei ni he wa ni helai ni yɔɔ oshara ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ bɛ mli kwraa.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during prolonged dry spells to conserve water and survive drought. Once the rains return, the plant quickly sprouts fresh leaves and continues growing its roots.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei oya ni shishifãi lɛ baaya nɔ amɛdara.

english: How can I tell if fall armyworms are attacking my maize field early on?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji fall armyworm miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mra?

english: Look for small ragged holes in the central leaves of young maize plants and green, sawdust-like droppings inside the leaf funnel. Early detection allows you to treat the crop before caterpillars eat the plant's growing point.
ga: Taomɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ mli. mra mli ni anaa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ he ni tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Excessively high daytime temperatures destroy pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. Without fertilization, the flowers dry up and fall off instead of turning into fruits.
ga: Gbi mli latsaa ni yaa hiɛ tsɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji fɔmɔ bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted or cracked instead of smooth and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbɛ eshwa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers warp or split when they meet hard, stony soil or when heavy rains suddenly follow a long dry period. Building high, loose soil mounds allows tubers to expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ baafite loo amɛbaagbala kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛ sɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Crowded pepper plants compete for sunlight and grow tall to reach light instead of branching out. Giving them enough space allows each plant to branch, flower, and produce abundant fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛmɔmɔ la lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee niji. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso niji, ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why does Striga weed keep appearing and ruining my sorghum and maize fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ ehe kpo lɛ? ni efite mi ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Striga seeds lie hidden in the soil until they detect chemicals released by cereal roots. The weed attaches directly to your crop's roots to steal water and food, causing the crop to stay stunted.
ga: Striga dumɔwui lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni anaa tsofai ni ŋmaa shishifãi lɛ jieɔ lɛ. Jwɛi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii. tsei ni egbɔjɔ

english: Weevil insects lay microscopic eggs on pods before harvest. Once in storage, the eggs hatch into larvae that eat the inside of the grains. Storing thoroughly dried seeds in airtight hermetic bags suffocates pests naturally.
ga: Moth lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani ekpaa. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli niyenii. Dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the green color and keeps the plant growing.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha amɛdara.

english: Why should I put fertilizer a few inches away from my plant stems instead of touching them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi moŋ fe ni mata he?

english: Placing chemical fertilizer directly against plant stems can burn the soft skin of the plant and kill it. Placing it a short distance away allows the roots to spread out and absorb the nutrients safely without burning the stem.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni egbe tso lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Akɛwoɔ he ko ni kɛ he ko jɛkɛɛɛ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ jaa ni amɛheɔ niyenii kpakpai shweshweeshwe ni amɛshãaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ.

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot, dry hours to protect themselves from losing too much water into the air. It is the plant's natural way of conserving moisture until the cooler evening comes.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ, ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Koni obu ohe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ he. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or too much water. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy so that the rest of the plant can survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu babaoo ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantains on the same plot with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko miikɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa plants shade and cool air until they are strong enough to face the sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tso ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Ha ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni edɔ kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hulu lɛ baakpe.

english: Cassava feeds heavily on soil nutrients. Planting it on the same spot repeatedly drains the soil of food and lets pests build up in the ground, causing your harvest to get smaller each year. Rotating with crops like beans helps restore the soil.
ga: Cassava yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni ooodu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ Enɛ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee bibioo daa afi. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Pods turn black due to a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in wet, humid air. Pruning extra shade branches lets sunlight and wind dry the trees, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Pods lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods lɛ hewɔ. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ mli. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo titri lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ agbi amɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɛɔ ŋmei lɛ eshwaa.

english: What is making small, round holes in the leaves of my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cabbage baai lɛ feɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually made by small caterpillars, like the Diamondback Moth larva, eating the leaves. Spraying an organic neem leaf solution early protects the leaves before the insects destroy the whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ daimondback moth larvae, ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni baa kabaaji baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Organic neem tso mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Ebaabu baai lɛ ahe dani ŋmeii lɛ akpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why does my cassava have huge leaves above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or manure, the plant spends all its energy growing big top leaves instead of storing food underground. Adding wood ash or potassium helps the plant focus on growing fat, healthy roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi Tso mli sũ loo potassium ni akɛbaafata he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni yɔɔ fɔ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into mounds or ridges before planting my sweet potatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabua sũ lɛ naa kɛfee gɔji loo ŋmeii dani madu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes need soft, loose soil so their roots can expand easily into large tubers. Planting on mounds prevents heavy rain from drowning the roots and gives the tubers room to grow big without getting squeezed by hard ground.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse. koni eshishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ bulb agboi oya. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa bulb lɛ ni edaraa ni shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ emɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do certified maize seeds produce big cobs while seeds I save from my own harvest produce smaller ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa wuji lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Certified seed varieties are specifically bred for high yield and vigor. Seeds saved from a previous harvest lose these strong genetic traits over generations, leading to smaller cobs and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛ hewalɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ fɔmɔ nii ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: What is the benefit of planting an early-maturing cowpea variety instead of the traditional long-season type?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tsina ŋmeii ni shwereɔ mra lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ blema ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ he?

english: Early-maturing varieties complete their growth cycle quickly, which helps escape late-season droughts when rains stop early and allows you to harvest ahead of market shortages for better prices.
ga: Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ gbeɔ amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hɔmɔ baa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ oya lɛ. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa nii dani jara nɔ nibii faaa yɛ jara ni hi fe tsutsu lɛ nɔ.

english: Rice thrives in low-lying, wet valley areas (inland valleys) that hold water, whereas maize needs well-drained, fertile soil where water does not sit around the roots.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. (mligbɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli) ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia ŋmãa. ni nu bɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: What will happen to my yams if I plant the mounds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potato lɛ nɔ kɛji midu gɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting mounds too close forces the yam plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in many small, thin tubers rather than large, heavy yams.
ga: Kɛ́ adu gɔŋ ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha sweet potato tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa moŋ fe ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing lots of bushy green leaves but very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of reproduction; adding fertilizers rich in phosphorus encourages the plant to set flowers and fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni phosphorus yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do groundnut plants make the soil better for the next crop I plant on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: During the Harmattan, dry air and strong winds strip moisture from leaves fast. The cocoa tree drops leaves as a self-defense mechanism to conserve water and keep its trunk alive.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe he koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha amɛtso lɛ ahi wala mli.

english: Why does cassava manage to stay green during long dry spells when my other crops wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi feɔ nakai lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ gboɔ?

english: Cassava has deep root systems that tap into water stored deep underground, and it can slow down its leaf growth to conserve water during dry periods.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni boteɔ nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize crop so quickly while leaving my cassava nearby untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kpata mi ŋmãa lɛ hiɛ oya yɛ be mli ni amɛshi ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer grass-family plants like maize and sorghum because of their soft, sweet leaves, while cassava leaves contain chemical compounds that these pests cannot easily digest.
ga: Autumn cutworms sumɔɔ jwɛi tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ŋɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmei baa mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ amɛ mlɛo.

english: Why does Striga weed keep attacking my maize field every year despite my clearing it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ tutuaa mi-ŋma ŋmɔji lɛ daa afi lɛ? ni mikɛjie lɛ?

english: Striga seeds can survive hidden in the soil for over 10 years and only sprout when they detect roots from crops like maize, living off the host plant's nutrients in low-fertility soils.
ga: Striga dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nɔ ni fe afii 10 ni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ kɛji ana shishifãi kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwereɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa shoots wither when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Keeping larger shade trees or temporary shade crops like plantains creates a cooler environment that protects the tender leaves from burning and drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil runs low on nitrogen. Nitrogen gives leaves their green color and helps the plant grow, so yellowing is a sign that the plant needs nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, su ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Does it matter which direction I point my cassava stem cuttings when I bury them in the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni atsɔɔ ŋmei nine lɛ gbɛ nɔ beni aduɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stems have growth buds that point upward. If you plant the stem upside down, the shoots have to bend around to reach the surface, which wastes the plant's energy and reduces root yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ Esa akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ abɔle ehe koni eshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni shishifãi ni baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off mainly due to heat stress or irregular watering. When the weather gets too hot or the soil dries out completely, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: What is causing the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and stop expanding?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbɛɛɛ amɛhe?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck sap from the leaves. This feeding damages the young tissues, causing the leaves to twist and stunt crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Niyenii nɛɛ fiteɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend that I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally enrich the soil with nutrients that help the maize grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni baaye abua ŋmãa lɛ ni etsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for growing large underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stay safe from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant corn on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. It also allows specific pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Ehaa kooloi kɛ helai komɛi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and hang down during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves and require large amounts of water to stay healthy. During the dry harmattan, the plant naturally sheds its outer leaves to reduce water loss and protect its main trunk.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu babaoo he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ harmatta ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he.

english: Why can my swamp rice grow well in flooded land while my maize rots and dies in waterlogged soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-swamp rice lɛ shwereɔ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni mi-corn lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their stems that carry oxygen down to roots underwater. Maize roots lack these air tubes, so standing water smothers the roots by blocking oxygen.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ŋtayaai krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Is starting a plantain farm a good investment for a new farmer in Ghana?
ga: Ani plantain ŋmɔ shishijee ji shika kpakpa kɛha okwaafoi heei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Yes, plantains are a high-demand staple food in Ghana that offer strong returns because they produce fruit year-round once established, provided you plant them in fertile, well-drained soil with adequate moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains ji niyenii titri ni ataoɔ waa yɛ Ghana he ni sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɔɔ he lɛ. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ, ebaawo yibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ,.

english: How long does it take for a new plantain shoot to produce fruits I can sell?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani dumɔwui heei woɔ yibii ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: A plantain plant usually takes about 9 to 12 months to flower, and another 3 to 4 months for the heavy fruit bunch to fully mature for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ dumɔwui lɛ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, ni eheɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi dani aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ shwereɔ kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches. If the soil is loose or if pests like root nematodes damage the roots, strong winds can easily blow the tree over unless you support it with wooden props.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ewoɔ aduawai babaoo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tsei akumɔ oya. Ja okɛ tso ni akɛfee nibii fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Can I plant beans together with my main crops on the same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside main crops like plantains or corn is very beneficial because beans capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, improving overall field fertility.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo ŋmãa he lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa jɛmɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Why do bean plants make the soil better for other crops grown after them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei krokomɛi ni aduɔ yɛ esɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bean plants have tiny nodules on their roots filled with helpful bacteria that turn air into soil fertilizer, leaving nitrogen behind for the next crop you plant in that spot.
ga: Bean tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyi mli obɔ Eshiɔ nitrogen kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: Can I feed my farm crops or plantain peels to my chickens?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha mikooloi lɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo plantain ŋmɔji?

english: Yes, plantain peels, crop residues, and farm grains can be processed and added to feed for chickens, helping reduce your feed costs while keeping the birds healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ afee plantain ŋmeii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ kɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmaa ni akɛfata he koni akɛye kooloi niyenii. Enɛ haa niyenii ni okɛyeɔ lɛ baa shi, yɛ be mli ni okwɛɔ okpo lɛ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: How does adding chicken manure help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Chicken manure is extremely rich in nitrogen and organic matter, which breaks down in the soil to feed your crops quickly and improve the soil's ability to hold water.
ga: Nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ mli waa. Enɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ

english: What crops can I grow on my farm to improve my family's daily diet?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni miweku lɛ daa gbi niyenii aya hiɛ?

english: Growing a mix of carbohydrate-rich crops like plantains along with protein-rich legumes like beans gives your family a balanced diet of essential energy and protein directly from your farm.
ga: Nibii ni carbohydrate eyi mli obɔ tamɔ plantains ni ooodu kɛfata legumes ni protein eyi mli obɔ tamɔ beans lɛ he lɛ haa oweku lɛ niyenii ni ja ni hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛ protein jɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow during heavy rain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots drown when water sits around them for too long. Poorly drained soil starves the roots of oxygen, preventing them from taking up plant food, which causes leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli kɛ́ nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye tsei aniyenii. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops, which is why early clearing is vital to prevent them from choking your young plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni otsi otsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo amɛhe lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sun, the delicate leaves dry out and burn. Shade trees also keep moisture in the soil to help young cocoa survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ Koni atsĩ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa Baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi ni amɛshã. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to build wooden stakes to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa tsei koni mikɛwo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking holds the leaves up to catch the sun and keeps them off damp soil where rotting and plant diseases spread quickly.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ŋmɛɔ hulu la lɛ he, ni ehaaa sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, he ni helai ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow fast. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsina loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei fata he lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their root systems. When planted alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil and boost the growth of neighboring crops without high fertilizer costs.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ daraa ni ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo babaoo bɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground when there is too much heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain floods the land and water sits around the roots for too long, it smothers them, allowing rot fungi to easily attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu lɛ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ni ekɛ tuber ŋmeii baa mlɛo.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the top layer of rich soil on my sloping farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bare soil on a slope has no plant roots to hold it together when heavy rain falls. Planting across the slope or keeping grass cover helps root networks act like anchors, stopping the rain from sweeping away your fertile topsoil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ tso shishifãi ni baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa. Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo jwɛi ni akɛha nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋshɔkei. Etsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the leaves of my maize plant during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide inside the cool central leaves of the maize plant to shield themselves from the hot afternoon sun and hungry birds. They come out to eat late in the evening or early in the morning when temperatures drop.
ga: Asraafoi amli ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli. Koni obu ohe kɛjɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ okpoi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into small wrinkled shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Wrinkled leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant's juices and spreading viruses. Controlling these small insects early prevents the leaf damage from stopping fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Emuɔ tsei amli nu ni egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baa ni fiteɔ lɛ naa koni ekakpa aduawai adalɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during very hot weather helps the flowers set into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eyɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie dormant in dry soil, waiting for the first drops of rain. Because they are wild, they are adapted to absorb water and nutrients faster than crop seeds, so early weeding gives your crops a fair start.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛkã shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ amɛmiimɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ. Ejaakɛ amɛyɛ koo lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaaha onibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling up in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantain alongside young cocoa creates natural shade that keeps the soil cool and protects the young plants until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the bottom of the plant going up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow big cobs. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore leaf color and crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ ŋmãa wuji. Kompost loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ su kɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough nourishment to produce strong stems and large ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii toi wuji.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yams when I plant yam on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating yams with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts gives the soil time to rebuild its strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛtswaa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely high heat, irregular watering, or lack of soil food. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and watering regularly helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛmiihao, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Groundnuts are natural soil builders. Their roots capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil, leaving free natural food behind that the next crop of maize can feed on.
ga: Peanuts ji adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ tswalɔi. Amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Shi adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaye lɛ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are there small ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ yɛ bu bibioo ko yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in the center leaves of maize are typically caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworm feeding on the tender growth inside the leaf funnel. Early spraying with appropriate biological or chemical treatments protects the growing point of the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni daraa yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Ebaabu he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready for harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava plants signal readiness when their lower leaves naturally yellow and fall off, and the main stem becomes woody and thick. You can gently scrape around one side of the plant base to check if the roots have swollen to a good size.
ga: Cassava tso tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso lɛ tso titri lɛ baatsɔ tso ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔlɔ atsu nii blɛoo. Abɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ fã kome he koni akwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ efu kɛyashɛ dalɛ kpakpa he.

english: Weeds grow much faster than most crops and steal soil food, water, and sunlight before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life ensures your plants get all the benefits of the rain and soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ náa nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ he sɛɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I wait for steady rains before planting my maize seeds instead of planting after the first single rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: Planting after just one early rain is risky because if a dry spell follows, the germinated seeds will dry up and die under the hot ground. Waiting for consistent rainfall ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to grow into healthy seedlings.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ ji oshara. Ejaakɛ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko ba ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants get sick even when I start with good seed from the shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ lɛ? No je shishi kɛ dumɔwui kpakpai ni jɛ shwapo lɛ mli?

english: Diseases often travel on your hands, clothing, dirty cutlasses, or footwear after you visit an infected field. Wiping your hands and washing your tools with clean water before touching healthy plants prevents carrying hidden sickness into your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ tsɔɔ oniji, otadei, glasei loo tokotai ni mli ewo muji lɛ amli beni oya he ko ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli tse tsumɔ oniji ahe ni okɛ nu ni mli tse tsumɔ odɛŋdadei ahe dani ota tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ akabote oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do farm animals or visitors walking through my pepper field cause my plants to rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi loo shisharalɔi ni nyiɛɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa mitsei lɛ fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Animals and visitors can carry harmful bacteria and fungi on their feet from infected soil elsewhere. Restricting access or fencing your field helps protect crops from foreign germs that cause plant rot.
ga: Koolooi kɛ saralɔi baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela lɛ emɔ nɔ yɛ he kroko lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛnaji anɔ. Gbɛtsii nii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo gbogbo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ helai ni baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afite lɛ ahe.

english: Can spraying my crops with river water bring diseases to my field?
ga: Ani faa mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba miŋmɔji amli?

english: Yes, water flowing from other farms upstream can carry fungal spores, bacteria, or chemical runoff. Using clean, protected water sources for irrigation and spraying reduces the risk of infecting your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji krokomɛi amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, loo tsofai ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Nu ni he tse ni abuɔ he ni okɛshwieɔ nu nɔ kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha helai ni baa onibii amli lɛ aba shi.

english: If I spray agricultural chemicals on my vegetables, can it affect the fish in my farm pond?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ okwaayeli tsofai shwie aduawai anɔ lɛ, ani ebaana loo ni yɔɔ nubu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, chemical sprays wash into nearby ponds during heavy rains. These substances can enter the water and harm fish, making it important to leave a unsprayed barrier zone around water sources.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ŋshɔi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ baanyɛ abote nu lɛ mli ni amɛye loo lɛ awui. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni ashi gbɛtsii nii ko ni afɔɔɔ nu lɛ he yɛ nu jɛɛhei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight when they are small. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides shelter and keeps the soil cool and moist while the young trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Cassava plants shed leaves to save moisture when dry winds blow. This natural defense helps the plant conserve water in its roots so it can survive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tswa. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ amɛshishifãi amli koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does black pod disease spread so quickly across my cocoa trees when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Rain splash lifts fungal spores from dirty soil and diseased pods onto healthy ones. High humidity helps the fungus grow quickly, so removing infected pods with clean tools slows down the spread.
ga: Nugbɔ nu gbalaa ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ amli. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ daa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni he tse jie ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Why do weeds make my crops suffer even if I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the added fertilizer, sunlight, and water. They also create a damp environment that hides insect pests and plant diseases.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, hulu la, kɛ nu. Amɛhaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ hu haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahelai teɔ shi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak without producing big cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ ni efeee ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants compete against each other for food, light, and water. Giving each plant enough space allows roots to spread and produce larger cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii, la, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and turn moldy inside my storage shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ miifite ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Storing maize while it still holds moisture creates a damp environment where molds and insects thrive. Drying your grains completely and keeping the storage area clean and covered prevents crop loss.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to be mli ni edɔ lolo lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ Ŋmãa ni agbiɔ kwraa kɛ hei ni akɛtoɔ lɛ ni akwɛɔ koni ehe atse ni aha nɔ ko nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water when the sun is very hot. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture during dry spells, and they will unfold again when the weather cools down or after rain.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Ni ebaaku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ loo nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and survive high heat. Once the rains return, the plant will use the energy stored in its roots to sprout fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. They need shade from larger trees like plantain or forest trees to shield them from intense heat and keep the surrounding soil moist while their roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantain loo koo mli tsei amli. koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do so many small cocoa flowers fall off my trees without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mitso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support. The tree naturally drops excess flowers so it can save energy to grow the pods that successfully get pollinated into full size.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ kpo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛye omanye yɛ fɔfɔi ni awo mli lɛ amli kɛyashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Why are my tomato fruits splitting open on the sides right before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ sɛɛgbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they get a sudden abundance of water after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit grows very quickly with the new water, causing the outer skin to crack before it can stretch.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛ́ amɛná nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya waa kɛ nu hee. Enɛ haa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli fãa dani enyɛɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my young yam vines stop growing well if I do not give them tall sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso bibioo lɛ ekpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Akɛni miŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ akwɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi hewɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need to spread their leaves high up toward the sun. Staking keeps the leaves away from damp ground weeds and catches sunlight needed to feed the growing yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛtso lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa koni eye ebua sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize plants turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize are a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants use to build healthy stems and bright green leaves.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma tsei ashishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my farm help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil. When the roots decompose, they leave this natural fertilizer behind for future crops to use.
ga: Peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ Amɛbaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Curled and wrinkled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of young leaves, damaging them as they expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni baaha efite nii beni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when my farm becomes too bushy and wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy shade and excess moisture create a cool, damp environment where the fungus that causes black pod disease spreads rapidly from pod to pod.
ga: Shade ni tsii kɛ fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i feɔ. Fuji ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli.

english: Why do people plant plantains around young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi duɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies that burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants are forced to compete for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. This competition leads to thin, weak stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, anyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the sap out of young leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early stops the leaves from curling and dying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akabɔle amɛhe ni amɛgboi.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on young maize leaves and stems. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts helps protect your yield.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo neem mli nu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but have small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If cassava plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer or grow in heavy shade, they put all their energy into growing top leaves and stems instead of storing food in their underground roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo akwɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Amɛbaatsu amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he nii kɛkwɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any small fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai bibii jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop without setting fruit when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences drought stress followed by sudden heavy watering. Consistent moisture keeps the flowers healthy enough to turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ naa hɔmɔ he haomɔ ni nu ni mli wa trukaa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crops so much in the first month after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small roots and grow slowly. Fast-growing weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from young crops, choking them before they can establish strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛdaraa blɛoo. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. ni ehaa amɛmuɔ dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tip downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the tips of lower leaves is a clear sign that your maize lacks nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps the leaves turn deep green and feed the plant properly.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni sa.

english: Why should I wait until the soil is moist after rain to apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: Applying dry fertilizer on dry soil can burn crop roots and waste the fertilizer as gas in the heat. Moisture helps dissolve the fertilizer so roots can absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ gas yɛ latsaa be mli. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly after I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest or stored in hot, unventilated rooms. Storing clean, undamaged tubers on raised wooden racks in cool, well-aired barns extends their shelf life.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni efiteee lɛ to tsei ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make green leaves and food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help them turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni niyenii ni he hiaa ni akɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli kɛ niyenii yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaf undersides, or by a plant virus. Spraying with neem oil or an appropriate organic spray can help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai bibii shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess water, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to swell the tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo tsɔ lɛ Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ kɛ yaa si konɛ e ha nɛ bulb nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ nɛ tsɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets extremely hot, when there is not enough water, or when bees fail to pollinate them. Keeping soil evenly moist and providing light shade helps tomatoes set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Be mli ni nu faaa loo be mli ni ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ la ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food. Climbing stakes lifts the leaves into the light, allowing the plant to generate enough energy to grow big, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Tso lɛ nɔ kwɔɔ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kane lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: This is Black Pod disease caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, cool shade. Pruning crowded tree branches lets sunlight and dry air in, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela ni ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi boteɔ mli. Koni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã

english: Why do my mature plantain trees blow over so easily when strong winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can easily be weakened by tiny soil pests called nematodes. Staking heavy fruit bunches with strong wooden poles prevents the wind from pulling up the roots.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ oya. ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes Yibii ni tsii ni aduɔ Kɛ tso ni mli wa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbala shishifãi lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that get scorched by full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or temporary shade plants keeps them cool and moist until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu lɛ shãa amɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo be kukuoo mli shade tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings grow very tall, thin, and weak instead of bushy and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ miida waa, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch upward and become weak when they are not getting enough direct sunlight. Placing them in a sunnier location makes them grow thicker and stronger stems.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why does the soil around my young crops dry out so fast after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil exposes moisture directly to the hot sun, causing it to evaporate. Covering the dirt with dry grass or leaves (mulch) shades the ground and keeps the soil moist longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. evaporate Mulch kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi. (Mulch) koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or large forest trees protects young cocoa from excessive heat and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei wuji lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed leaves during severe dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from dying. Providing shade and leaving mulch around the root area helps retain soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why is it recommended to use a spraying machine on my back to care for my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ sɛɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ atsu nii kɛkwɛ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: A knapsack sprayer helps spread liquid fertilizers and pest control treatments evenly across all leaves and pods, protecting the whole tree far better than manual splashing.
ga: Backpack sprayers lɛ jaa nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ. Ebuɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he jogbaŋŋ fe ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ.

english: What happens if I spray liquid treatments on my cocoa farm during the hot mid-day sun?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ tsofa shwie kookoo ŋmɔ ko nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Spraying in intense heat causes the chemical liquid to evaporate too quickly or scorch the crop's leaves. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when it is cooler.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ni ji nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ loo ebaashã tso lɛ baai lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in humid, overly dark conditions. Pruning extra branches and clearing infected pods helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ amli. Nibii krokomɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my cocoa trees more when flowers and young shoots appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ kɛ́ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii je kpo lɛ?

english: Pests like mirids (capsids) target young shoots and flowers because they are soft, juicy, and full of sweet nutrients needed for the insect's survival.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ fɔfɔi anɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli nu, ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni ŋɔɔ ni he hiaa koni kooloi ahi shi.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow directly on the main tree trunk instead of on the small branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow flowers and pods directly on thick trunks and heavy stems—a process called cauliflory—allowing the plant to carry the heavy weight of mature pods safely.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ tsei ni mli tse ni tsii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ kɔlifloa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni enyɛɔ ekwɛɔ ŋmeii ni edara kwraa lɛ amli shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves typically indicate a lack of key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged and preventing the roots from absorbing food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does cutting off extra branches help my cocoa tree yield more pods?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso ni afolɔ afata he lɛ aye abua mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes non-producing branches so the tree can direct its energy and nutrients into pod production, while also improving airflow and sunlight exposure to reduce disease.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afolɔ mli lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ koni helai aba shi.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting burned by too much sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ eshã mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Sun-stressed cocoa trees show dry, brown leaf edges, stunted yellow growth, and dropping leaves, signaling that the crop requires more canopy shade.
ga: Cacao tsei ni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baaná baai ni egbi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dalɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia hulutsoo babaoo.

english: Why is it important for me to clear away diseased plants completely from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei fɛɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Removing infected or sick plants completely prevents diseases and pests from spreading to your healthy crops, keeping the rest of your farm safe.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akagbɛ ashwã onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Ha oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: What are farm inputs, and why should I apply fertilizer early in the crop's life?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii ni haa ŋmɔ mli nibii feɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli yɛ gbekɛbiiashi?

english: Inputs are basic supplies like seeds, tools, and fertilizers used at the start of planting. Applying fertilizer early gives young roots the nutrients they need to build strong stems and leaves.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ nitsumɔ mli lɛ ji nibii titrii tamɔ dumɔwui, nitsumɔ dadei, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ dumɔ shishijee mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛma ŋmeii kɛ baai ni wa.

english: How does joining a local farmers' group benefit my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafoi akuu ko ni mikɛ mihe woɔ mli lɛ baaná miŋmɔ lɛ he sɛɛ?

english: Joining a group helps you share labor with other farmers, buy inputs like seeds and fertilizer cheaper in bulk, and receive training from extension officers more easily.
ga: Kuu ko ni okɛ ohe woɔ mli lɛ haa okɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi jaa nitsumɔ. Hemɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ jara ni waaa nɔ. ni amɛná tsɔsemɔ kɛjɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ adɛŋ mlɛo

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize needs nitrogen fertilizer or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni eŋɔli lɛ su lɛ mli waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even though the leafy tops look very big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa waa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ ayiteŋ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara waa ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Cassava puts too much energy into growing leaves if the soil has high nitrogen but lacks potassium. Potassium helps the plant store energy underground to grow larger tubers.
ga: Cassava kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ baai lɛ adalɛ mli kɛji akɛ nitrogen fa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi potassium bɛ mli. Potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my crops wither quickly during hot days even after a brief rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture fast under intense heat. Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves (mulch) traps water in the ground and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ŋmɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. (Mulch) baaye abua ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: How do I know if my young cocoa trees are getting too much sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tsɔ?

english: Young cocoa leaves will burn, turn brown, and dry up under direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains around them shields the young trees until they grow stronger.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baashã. etsɔɔ blɔfo ni egbiɔ kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe. kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ

english: How can I tell when my yams are mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready for harvesting when the leaves and vines dry up and turn yellow naturally, showing that the plant has finished storing energy in the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why are small insects eating holes in my vegetable leaves, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Insects feed on tender leaves for nutrients. You can protect your vegetables by spraying them early in the morning with a natural neem leaf solution or recommended insect spray.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ baai bibii koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Obaanyɛ obu o-vegetables lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ neem tso ni ji adebɔɔ mli tsofa loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ kooloi amli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ leebi lɛ nɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to put seeds in the ground at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Plant after two or three steady rains have thoroughly soaked the soil, so your seeds have enough moisture to germinate without drying up during short dry spells.
ga: Dumɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ yɛ be kukuoo ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my rice crop is fully ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains turn from green to a golden-yellow color, and the lower part of the plant stalk begins to dry out.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee shika tsuru mli. ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ jeɔ shishi egbiɔ

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Rice leaves usually turn yellow early when the plant is missing essential nutrients like nitrogen, or when water has been standing in the field for too long without proper drainage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I leave my ripe rice in the field too long before harvesting it?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa?

english: If rice stays in the field too long after ripening, the grains dry out excessively, crack, and drop onto the ground naturally, leading to heavy loss of crop volume.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baagbi tsɔ. Egbɛɔ ni egbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa tsei ayibɔ ni he hiaa waa lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I prevent insects from eating my harvested rice while it is inside storage sacks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmãa ni akpa be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Before putting rice into sacks, dry the grain completely under the sun until it is hard, and store the filled sacks off the bare floor on wooden planks inside a dry room.
ga: dani okɛ ŋmãa awo kotokui amli Ha ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni okɛ kotokui ni eyi obɔ lɛ ato shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ tsu ko ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why does my harvested grain spoil or smell bad when I keep it in tightly closed bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛfuɔ waa kɛ́ mikɛto kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Grain spoils in closed bags if it was not dried well before bagging; trapped moisture creates heat and allows mold and bacteria to grow quickly inside the bag.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa fiteɔ yɛ kotokui ni aŋã mli kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani awo kotoku mli. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ daa oya yɛ kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Why is it recommended that I try a new seed variety on a small patch of land first before planting my whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ maka dumɔwui heei aka yɛ he bibioo ko lɛ? dani abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ

english: Testing on a small area allows you to observe how the crop behaves in your local soil and climate without risking all your money and effort if the yield is poor.
ga: Kaa yɛ he bibioo ko Ehaa okwɛɔ bɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ omaŋ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli ni okɛ oshika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ fɛɛ wooo oshara mli kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts in my field help my crop grow better in the next season?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops like rice or maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.
