english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly during the hottest parts of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense to protect the plant from excessive heat and reduce the amount of water escaping from the leaves.
ga: Abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni efee adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he. ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa shi

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than domesticated food crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe tsei ni akɛyeɔ nii yɛ shia lɛ.

english: How does heavy rainfall right before harvest affect the quality of my cereal grains?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani akpaa nii lɛ saa miŋmaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain close to harvest causes ripe grains to absorb water, which can cause them to sprout early on the stalk or rot before you can cut them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ be lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ aŋɔ nu. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya yɛ tso lɛ nɔ loo amɛgboi dani ofolɔ amɛ.

english: Can I use sprays made from natural plants to protect my crops instead of buying expensive chemicals?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni jɛ tsei amli ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii kɛbu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe moŋ fe ni mahe tsofai ni jara wa?

english: Yes, sprays made from natural plant extracts are a cost-effective alternative to expensive chemical pesticides. They are effective at repelling pests while being safer to apply across your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ji tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni jara wa lɛ najiaŋ. Amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashwiemɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe hu kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do plant-extract sprays work to protect my crops from insect damage?
ga: Te tso mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ koni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe?

english: Plant extracts contain natural protective compounds that plants use to defend themselves. When sprayed onto crops, these extracts act as natural repellents or poisons to crop pests without damaging the crop.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛbuɔ amɛhe he lɛ yɛ tsei amli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni gbeɔ tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsofai fɔji ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What makes plant-based pesticides different from synthetic chemical pesticides?
ga: Mɛni haa tsofai ni akɛ tsei tsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ tsofai ni akɛfee nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe?

english: Plant-based pesticides are derived directly from natural plant matter, making them a unique option that is often safer, more affordable, and flexible enough to spray both in open fields and around homes.
ga: Anaa tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni bei pii lɛ ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe. Jara lɛ ji nɔ ni jara waaa fe tsutsu lɛ. Ni eyɛ mlɛo bɔ ni sa ni ekɛshwieɔ ŋmɔji ni mli tse kɛ shia lɛ he fɛɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to use pest sprays inside my home or storage shed to protect harvested crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baatsu nii yɛ mishia loo shĩa lɛ mli koni mikɛbu mikpamɔ lɛ he?

english: Certain plant-based extract sprays are safe and versatile enough to be used both outdoors on farm areas and indoors in storage spaces to keep pests away from harvested goods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsei amli lɛ ekomɛi yɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛhe yɛ srɔtoi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli kɛ shĩa mli yɛ hei ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akakpa nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ

english: Why do insects keep attacking my stored maize inside my house even after I sprayed my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛtutuaa ŋmãa ni ato yɛ mishia lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛshwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: Pests often migrate from farm fields into cool storage areas inside homes. Treating both your field area and indoor storage areas with suitable plant-based sprays stops insects from destroying your harvested crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛyaa hei ni akɛ nibii ni mli ejɔ toɔ yɛ shĩai amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ahe tsofa ni sa tsu ŋmɔji kɛ hei ni akɛ nibii toɔ yɛ shia lɛ fɛɛ he nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ.

english: What can I do if the recommended chemical pesticide for my farm is too expensive for me to buy?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛji tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jara wa tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ mahe?

english: You can switch to plant-extract remedies, which offer an affordable and effective alternative for spraying large farm areas without spending heavily on costly commercial chemicals.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsake kɛya tsofai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ anɔ, ni ji gbɛ kroko ni jara waaa ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔji wuji amli ni jarayeli tsofai ni jara wa waa he ehiaaa.

english: Why do some pest treatments only last for two days before pests come back?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbii enyɔ pɛ dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi ni agbeɔ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Certain chemical treatments break down quickly in heat or rain, lasting only a couple of days. Utilizing stable or easily reapplied plant-extract sprays provides a cost-effective way to manage pests continuously.
ga: Tsofai komɛi fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa loo nugbɔshiimɔ he. ni hi shi gbii fioo pɛ Tso mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ loo ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii ekoŋŋ oya lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa anáa gbɛ ni he ehiaaa ni akɛkwɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Will using natural plant extracts harm my soil or family when applied near my living compound?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli tsei amli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ loo miweku lɛ awui kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ?

english: Because plant extracts are made from natural botanical materials, they are generally less toxic than synthetic chemicals, making them safer for application around dwellings and less harmful to your soil.
ga: Ejaakɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe nibii feɔ tsei amli nu. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhe bɛ awui fe tsofai ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi. Enɛ haa efeɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha shihilɛhei, ni eyeee shikpɔŋ lɛ awui hu.

english: Can I spray the same pest remedy on my outdoor crops and inside my farm store?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ nɔŋŋ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ kpo nɔ kɛ miŋmɔ mli shwapo lɛ mli?

english: Yes, multi-purpose plant-extract remedies are formulated so you can spray an entire crop area outdoors or use them indoors to control pests around your storage areas.
ga: Hɛɛ, afee tso mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nibii babaoo he nii lɛ bɔni afee ni onyɛ okɛ tsofa afɔ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ kpo nɔ. Aloo okɛtsu nii yɛ oshia lɛ mli koni okɛkudɔ kooloi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. he ni okɛ nibii toɔ

english: How do I know if a non-chemical pest spray will actually work on my farm fields?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni tsofa bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Unique remedies prepared directly from active plant extracts have proven natural defenses that effectively control targeted field pests when sprayed properly across affected crop areas.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he ni asaa kɛjɛɔ tsei amli nu mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni yeɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ afɔse ashwie ŋmɔ mli hei ni ena naagbai lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If strong winds blow my maize down to the ground, will the plants die or can they still grow?
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa mi ŋmãa lɛ Ani tso lɛ baagbo loo ebaaya nɔ eda?

english: Maize plants are quite resilient. If the stem is bent but not completely broken, the plant can often bend itself back up toward the sun and continue growing normally, though it may take extra time before it is ready for harvest.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe kwraa. Kɛji tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ebɔle ehe shi efolɔko kwraa Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɔ efoɔ ehe ekoŋŋ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa. Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ebaahe be kroko dani eshɛ he ni abaakpa moŋ.

english: Why do some of my plantain trees fall over during heavy storms while others stay standing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ekomɛi gbee shi yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu gbee shi lɛ? Edamɔ shi shiŋŋ lolo

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and carry heavy fruit bunches. If the soil is too wet or the roots are damaged by pests, strong winds can easily push the tree down. Staking your plantains with strong wooden poles gives them extra support against wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ loo ŋmeii efite shishifãi lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbo oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni wa fĩ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha amɛhewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fold up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves fold up in intense heat to protect themselves and prevent water loss. Once the sun goes down or after rain falls, the leaves will return to their normal position.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ fɔ̃ɔ amɛhe yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛtsi nu ni elaaje lɛ naa. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi loo nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛshihilɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cocoa crop take so many years before I can start harvesting the pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi eshishifãi lɛ akpamɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to develop a strong trunk and deep root system to support fruit production. Depending on the variety you plant, it takes between 2 to 5 years of careful weeding and shade management before the tree matures enough to produce pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia be koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baaye abua ni amɛwo yibii. Edamɔ tsei srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baahe aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 5 dani tso lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii aba.

english: What happens to my profit if I harvest my peppers early instead of waiting for them to mature fully?
ga: Mɛni baaba misɛɛnamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpa mi-peppers lɛ mra? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: Harvesting peppers too early means the fruits will be smaller, weigh less on the scale, and lack full color and spiciness. Waiting for full maturity gives you heavier yields and better prices at the market.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwie mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ afee bibioo. Etsiimɔ waaa yɛ sɛkɛl lɛ nɔ ni ebɛ su kɛ ŋmɔlɔ fɛɛ Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi ebaada lɛ, ebaaha oná nyɔmɔwoo ni tsii kɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the stems of my bean plants try to wrap around other plants and sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-nut tso lɛ shishifã lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ ehe abɔle tsei kɛ tsei aniji krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Climbing bean varieties do not have thick wooden stems to stand on their own. They naturally search for poles or neighboring crops to climb so their leaves can reach maximum sunlight for healthy growth.
ga: Climbing bean henɔi lɛ bɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛdamɔ shi. Amɛtaoɔ tsei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛkwɔ koni amɛtso lɛ aná hulu la babaoo koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough strength to grow heavy tubers like yam?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmeii?

english: Good yam soil needs to be deep, loose, and rich in decomposed organic matter. If the soil is too hard or full of tight clay, the yam tubers cannot push down easily into the ground and will grow small or misshapen.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi ni ji sweet potato lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni nyɛɔ efiteɔ lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ ashɛ Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo. ni ebaafee bibioo loo ehiɛ su ni ejaaa

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your soil is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged and suffocating the roots. Adding compost or manure can restore the soil's strength and bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni etsɔ eŋɔli.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops even when the crops are already big and tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe, kɛji akɛ amɛdara ni amɛkwɔ momo po?

english: Even big crops have to share soil water and food with weeds. Clearing weeds removes competition, allowing your crops to put all their energy into forming healthy fruits and seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji po kɛ jwɛi lɛ aja nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛyaa. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Does heavy rain help my tomato plants grow faster or can it hurt them?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaye abua mi tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛdara oya loo ebaafite amɛ?

english: While tomatoes need water, heavy continuous rain can splash soil-borne diseases onto the leaves and rot the roots. Creating raised beds and clearing pathways helps excess water drain away quickly so the plants stay healthy.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, nu he miihia tomatoi. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ agbɛ ashwã baai lɛ anɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Saji ni awo nɔ kɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni agbele naa lɛ ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are small worms eating the middle parts of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, which target the growing tip of young maize plants. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed helps protect the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni amɛkwɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miitao niyenii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plants dry up and die suddenly even when I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting of healthy green tomatoes is usually caused by bacterial wilt living in the soil. Planting tomatoes in the exact same spot every season builds up this disease, so rotating your plot with crops like maize or sorghum stops the sickness.
ga: Tomato eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ trukaa, bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ kɛ hela nɛɛ baaba. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔji ni atsakeɔ koni akɛdu nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa hela lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that spread a plant virus. Controlling these insects early with neem oil spray prevents the virus from spreading and damaging your harvest.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaatsi helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni efite onibii.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when the dry Harmattan wind starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during severe dry spells to conserve water and protect their trunks. Planting permanent shade trees like Terminalia or fruit trees helps break the dry wind and retain soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu tso lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa, tamɔ Terminalia loo tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ni aaadu lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ko, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning excess branches to allow sunlight into the farm and removing infected pods keeps the rest of the crop healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Afoɔ tsei lɛ amli fe nine koni hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy soil during wet periods. Planting on raised mounds or soil ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the tubers safe underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to manufacture food for the tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun, resulting in much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow tall with big green leaves but give me very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛ baa agbo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of roots. Using balanced soil nutrients with higher potassium encourages the plant to expand its underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ ebaa lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe eshishifãi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛshwã amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Is it better to clear weeds by burning them or by leaving them on top of the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaajie jwɛi kɛtsɔ la ni ashãa loo ni aaashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving cut weeds on top of the ground acts as mulch, which keeps the soil cool, holds moisture during dry days, and rots into free plant food, whereas burning destroys nutrients in the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ be mli ni shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rains are unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ baanɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground receives two or three heavy, deep rains that thoroughly soak the soil before planting, rather than sowing immediately after the very first light rainfall.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ dani odu nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to build green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer feeds the soil and helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce empty pods with no seeds inside when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut pods need calcium in the soil while developing underground. If the soil lacks calcium or is too dry during pod formation, the shells will grow empty without forming the nuts inside.
ga: Calcium he miihia ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium loo egbi tsɔ yɛ be mli ni afeɔ pod lɛ, Shell lɛ baafee efolo ni efeee ŋmeii komɛi yɛ mli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in wet and shady conditions. Pruning extra branches lets sunlight in to dry the farm and stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la babaoo aba ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni eha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the crop from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekadara lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking plant juice and spreading a virus. Protecting the plants from these tiny bugs early keeps the leaves open and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ahe mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ agbeleɔ amɛhe ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam leaves get brown spots and drop off before the yams are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani sweet potato lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Browning leaves are often a sign of a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads easily when leaves touch wet soil. Staking the yam vines high off the ground keeps leaves dry and disease-free.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ he okadi. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ ajie sweet potato wain tsei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni helai bɛ amɛhe.

english: These are fall armyworms that hide inside the center whorl of the corn plant during the hot day and eat leaves at night. Spraying neem liquid or recommended insecticides directly into the center funnel kills them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni afolɔ amɛhe ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ shwie ŋmei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ dani amɛbaafite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I bother clearing weeds around my crops when the crop plants are already tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyaa haomɔ ni ji jwɛi ni shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ mli be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ momo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and light from your crop no matter how tall the crop gets. Weeds also hide insects and diseases that can move onto your crops and reduce your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni amɛkwɔ ha. Jwɛi hu kɛ kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni baanyɛ aya oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni eha oŋmɔshi nibii aba shi lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil moist and giving plants light shade protects flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni oha tsei lɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil, the roots drown and fungi quickly cause them to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baaha amɛgboi oya.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the surface. When the heavy bunch of plantains grows at the top, the tree becomes top-heavy, so propping the stem with strong bamboo poles prevents storm damage.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Beni plantains babaoo yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ahum akafite tso lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunshine and strong heat. Plantain trees or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist so the young cocoa roots can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Dumɔwui loo shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shade. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy winds blow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots near the surface and carry heavy bunches at the top. When heavy rain softens the soil, the shallow roots lose their grip, so strong winds can easily blow the heavy top over unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛ fɔfɔi ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa ŋwɛi fã ni tsii lɛ oya. ja tso fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why are the leaf tips of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient for green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my garden produce plenty of dark green leaves but no fruits after I give it a lot of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo shi yibii ko bɛ mli beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ewo mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much leaf-building fertilizer like high-nitrogen chemical fertilizer tricks the plant into using all its energy on leaves instead of flowers and fruits.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa baai babaoo baa lɛ baatsu nii, tamɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen fa yɛ mli lɛ Ebaaha tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ atsu nii yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the dirt when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, it suffocates the roots and creates the right conditions for rot fungi to eat the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Nu lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni afee shihilɛ ni sa koni rot fungus lɛ aye ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow leafy bushes in heavy rain but fail to form seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jwɛi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli shi enyɛɛɛ efee dumɔwui akutsei lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are naturally adapted to drier conditions. Heavy continuous rain encourages the plant to put energy into growing long branches and leaves rather than making flowers and seed pods.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ niji kɛ baai kakadaji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites hidden under the leaves. As they suck out the plant juices, their saliva poisons the leaf, causing it to wrinkle and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Beni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ Amɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ woɔ baa lɛ mli poison. Ha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe.

english: Why am I finding small holes in my maize stems filled with sawdust-like dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa tso ni muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by maize stem borer caterpillars. They hatch from eggs on the leaves, chew their way inside the stalk to live, and push out waste that looks like powdery sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii. Amɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishi koni ehi wala mli. ni ojie jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwo ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off to the ground without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, so no fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ yibii ko wooo.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my yam vines on tall poles instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need to reach up to lift themselves toward direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp wet ground, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ sweet potato baai lɛ awo ŋwɛi koni hulu la lɛ akpee tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni akɛtsi baa helai anaa

english: Why do these new foreign hybrid crop seeds need so much special care and fertilizer compared to our local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome nɛɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ akɛto wɔmaŋ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Foreign hybrid seeds are bred to give very high yields, but to do that, they require a steady supply of nutrients and protection like high-yielding farm animals. Local seeds yield less, but they have adapted over many years to survive on poor soil and natural rain with minimal care.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ ewo mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo waa. Shi bɔni afee ni afee nakai lɛ, niyenii kɛ hebuu he miihia Nakai dumɔwui lɛ daa. Nakai eji yɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ hu ahe. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. Shi etsake ehe yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli koni ehi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it better for me to spray chemical pest medicine on my crops early in the morning or late evening rather than during midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ tsofa awo mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: During midday heat, the strong sun quickly evaporates liquid spray before the plant can absorb it, and the hot chemical can scorch the leaves. Spraying in the cool morning or evening allows the plant leaves to safely absorb the medicine.
ga: Yɛ gbi lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, edɔ waa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ afee la oya dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Ni tsofai ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ baai lɛ ni amɛŋɔ tsofa lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and thin with no corn cobs when I plant them under shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ, kɛ́ midu yɛ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce food for making cobs. When planted under dense shade, the maize plant wastes all its energy stretching upward to search for sunlight instead of building thick stems and grain.
ga: Hulu la he miihia tsei tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha cob. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkpã amɛhe koni amɛna hulu la. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi kɛ dumɔwuhi nɛ a mi wa.

english: Does sunlight really affect how crops grow, or is soil water all that matters?
ga: Ani hulu la lɛ náa tsei adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ, aloo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu he miihia?

english: Sunlight acts as the plant's cooking fuel. Plants use sunlight on their green leaves to turn water and soil nutrients into food, so without enough sunlight, crops cannot grow or produce fruit even if the soil is wet.
ga: Hulu la tsuɔ nii akɛ tsofa kɛha tsei lɛ anihoomɔ. Tsei kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛ baai eŋɔli nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ tsakeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ loo amɛwo yibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why shouldn't I dump all my crop fertilizer onto the field at once right when I plant the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ midu midumɔwui lɛ?

english: Young plants have tiny roots that cannot absorb a large amount of food at once. Excessive early fertilizer burns young roots or gets washed away by heavy rain; feeding plants in small stages as they grow ensures they actually use the nutrients.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii babaoo yɛ be kome mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli oya lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi bibii lɛ ashã loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho amɛ. Niyenii ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ bei bibii amli Beni amɛdaraa lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkwɛɔ koni amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning pale yellow even when there is plenty of rain on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign of crop hunger, usually indicating a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Rain gives plants water to drink, but plants also need soil nutrients to maintain green leaves and stay healthy.
ga: Kaadi ŋmɔŋ ji hɔmɔ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnuɔ nu. Shi tsofai hu he miihia tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛha baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop and curl up during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Extreme midday heat causes water to leave the leaves faster than the roots can draw it up from the soil. Leaf curling is the plant's natural defence to reduce leaf area exposed to the sun and preserve moisture until it cools down.
ga: Gbi teŋ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu jeɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ.

english: Why do cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ harmatta be ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves release water into the dry air. During the dry harmattan, cassava intentionally drops its leaves to conserve precious moisture inside its stem and roots so it can survive until the rains return.
ga: Baai lɛ jieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ egbi lɛ, ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ eyiŋ ni ekɛ ebaa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni jara wa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruit during extremely hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Very high heat damages tomato pollen and prevents flower fertilization. When a flower is not pollinated, the plant drops it to conserve its energy until weather conditions become favorable again.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee fɔmɔ nii. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ pollen lɛ Tsei baashi fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do crops planted close together produce smaller yields than crops given space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe tsei ni haa gbɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients when planted too close. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures its roots and leaves get enough food and light to produce large fruit.
ga: Tsei baawuu kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso fɛɛ tso to he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ náa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji.

english: What is this green plant growing directly on my cocoa branches, and why is it harming my tree?
ga: Nɛkɛ tso eŋɔli nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo nine lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ni mɛni hewɔ eeye mi tsei lɛ awui lɛ?

english: That is a parasitic plant like mistletoe. It attaches itself to your cocoa branches and steals water and vital nutrients directly from the tree, weakening it over time.
ga: No ji, tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ tamɔ mistletoe. Ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ kookoo niji ahe ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do the branches on my cocoa trees dry up and die even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Parasitic plants attached to your cocoa branches suck away the water before it can reach the leaves and pods, causing the branches to dry out despite good rain.
ga: Tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ kookoo niji ahe lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani eshɛɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Ha niji lɛ agbi kɛji nugbɔ miinɛ po.

english: Can a parasite actually kill a whole mature cocoa tree if I leave it there?
ga: Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbe cacao tso ni eda lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji mishi lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Yes, as a parasitic plant spreads and grows larger on the tree, it drains more and more water until the host cocoa tree becomes too weak to survive and dies.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ejaakɛ tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛdaraa yɛ tsei anɔ. Ebaaha nu babaoo ajɛ mli. Kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ baagbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ehi shi ni egbo.

english: Do parasitic plants on cocoa trees steal water, food, or both?
ga: Ani tsei ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, loo fɛɛ?

english: Parasites attach directly to the inner system of the cocoa tree, continuously sucking away both water and essential plant food that the tree needs to produce cocoa pods.
ga: Parasite lɛ kpɛtɛɔ cacao tso lɛ mli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Ekɛ nu kɛ tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛfee kookoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do I need to check and clean parasitic plants off my cocoa trees every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli ni matsumɔ amɛhe daa afi lɛ?

english: Parasites can spread quickly across your farm. Removing them every year ensures your cocoa trees keep all their water and nutrients, keeping the trees healthy for future seasons.
ga: Parasites baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ daa afi lɛ, ehaa cacao tso lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ. ni oha tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi bei ni baa lɛ amli.

english: How do parasitic plants spread from one cocoa tree to the rest of my farm?
ga: Te tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛyaa miŋmɔ lɛ fã kroko lɛ nɔ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Birds often eat the seeds of parasitic plants and drop them onto other healthy cocoa branches, where they take root and start sucking water from new host trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okpoi yeɔ parasait dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ kookoo niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. he ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi yɛ ni amɛjeɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei heei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ numɔ shishi lɛ

english: What is the best way for me to remove parasitic plants from my cocoa branches without killing the tree?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ majie tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛjɛ kookoo niji amli ni mifiteee tso lɛ?

english: You should carefully cut off the affected branch just below where the parasite has attached itself so that it cannot continue sucking nutrients or grow back.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ afo tsei niji ni ena hela lɛ yɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yɔɔ lɛ shishi. Koni ekɛtsi enaa koni ekaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why am I harvesting fewer cocoa pods this year even though my cocoa trees look green and full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpa kookoo ŋmeii fioo pɛ afi nɛɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli ni dumɔwui eyi mli obɔ moŋ.

english: The green growth might actually be parasitic plants. Because these parasites steal the cocoa tree's water and energy, the tree cannot produce as many pods as it used to.
ga: Ekolɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ juɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo tamɔ tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why should I spend part of my cocoa profit every year to maintain and clean my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ shika ni mináa yɛ kookoo mli lɛ fã ko atsu nii daa afi kɛkwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛsaa mihe lɛ?

english: Reinvesting a portion of your profit into annual farm maintenance, like removing water-sucking parasites, protects your trees from dying and secures your income for future years.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔi ni anáa lɛ fã ko ni akɛaawo daa afi ŋmɔ mli saamɔ mli ekoŋŋ, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ nu lɛ ajiemɔ. Ebaabu otsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ gbele he, ni ebaaha shika ni onáa lɛ ahi shi yɛ wɔsɛɛ afii amli.

english: What are the early warning signs that a parasite is starting to drain water from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni ji mra be mli kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai miibɔi mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ shwiemɔ?

english: Look for unusual extra leaves or small bushes growing directly out of main cocoa branches, yellowing cocoa leaves around that area, and small or drying pods.
ga: Taomɔ baai krokomɛi loo jwɛi bibii. Nɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo nine wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kookoo baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni bɔle he lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni egbi

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or plantains to retain moisture and survive their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains adɛŋ koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ shishijee dalɛ mli.

english: Which way up should I stick cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, nɛgbɛ esa akɛ adu ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: The small growth buds on the stem cutting must point upwards toward the sky so that leaves and branches can sprout correctly above the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close makes crops compete for light, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stalks and smaller corn ears rather than a larger harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii baa yɛ ŋmãa babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Covering the soil keeps it cool, stops rainwater from evaporating quickly, prevents weed growth, and adds nutrients back to the ground as the leaves rot.
ga: Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛji baai lɛ egbo.

english: Should I put fertilizer on my seeds at the exact same time I plant them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ be kome too mli ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until seeds sprout and form roots—usually one to two weeks after planting—so the young plant can actually absorb and use the fertilizer.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi. (bei pii lɛ, otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ sɛɛ) koni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why shouldn't I grow cassava on the same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing cassava repeatedly in the same spot empties the soil of nutrients and allows pests and plant diseases to build up in the dirt.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baafite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahelai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do caterpillars keep eating the inside leaves of my young corn during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These pests, often Fall Armyworms, hide inside the central funnel of corn plants during warm weather to eat the soft, developing leaves where moisture gathers.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ amɛgbeeɔ asraafoi a-armyworms lɛ anɔ lɛ, teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛye baai bibii ni miiya hiɛ ni ebua ŋmɔtɔ naa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the air becomes too hot, when watering is uneven, or when the soil lacks essential plant nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tsei, tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper seeds rot in the soil during the rainy season instead of sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Too much water in soggy soil starves the seeds of oxygen and encourages fungal growth, causing the seeds to decay before they can sprout.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ewo ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow before the crop is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tsei lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that the soil is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost gives the leaves their healthy green color back so they can produce big maize ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataa he. Ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa. Koni enyɛ ekɛ ŋmãa toi wuji aba

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or beans on the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that naturally take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil, helping your maize crop grow better and reducing how much commercial fertilizer you need to buy.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ baa shi.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and dry up while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni mikɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads easily in wet, damp weather. Pruning extra shade branches and clearing weeds allows air and sunlight to flow through, keeping your cocoa pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fungi hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ enɛ baa. Ni gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei aniji koni ona hulutsoo babaoo ni ojie jwɛi lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to hide and eat inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli?

english: These caterpillars are known as Fall Armyworms, a pest that attacks young cereal crops. Catching them early and applying appropriate control methods—like recommended insecticides or neem extract late in the evening—helps protect your crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni ale amɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ ji ŋmeii ni tutuaa ŋmaa tsei bibii. Ni aaamɔ amɛ mra ni akɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ amɛ tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ atsu nii gbɛkɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: How do I know which direction to stick my cassava stem into the soil when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds or 'eyes' on the stem. Make sure these buds point upwards towards the sky when you put the stick into the ground, otherwise the plant will grow upside down and struggle to yield good roots.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi beni okɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi ni ebaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ená shishifãi kpakpai.

english: Is it really necessary to cut sticks and stake my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafolɔ niji ni madu mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Yes, staking lifts the leaves high into the sunlight so the plant can make more food. Yam plants that trail on the hot ground catch more leaf diseases and produce much smaller tubers than staked plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔ ni fata staking he ji baai lɛ ni awó nɔ kɛyashɛ hulu la he koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Sweet potato tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aná foliary helai oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa fe staking tsei.

english: Why do my pepper plants look strong in the morning but droop and wilt during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ leebi lɛ? Shi egbo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes leaves to lose water faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. Placing dry grass around the base of the plant (mulching) keeps the soil cool and moist so the plant stays upright.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi (mulching) lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. koni tso lɛ ahi shi jaŋŋ

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, severe dry spells, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly watered and avoiding excess chemical fertilizer helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni ajie tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily whenever a small storm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni ahum bibioo ko baa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots stay close to the soil surface, and heavy fruit bunches make the plant top-heavy. Planting suckers in deeper holes and building up soil around the base gives the roots a firm grip against wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ni aduawai akui ni tsii tsiiɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii lɛ awo bu ko ni mli kwɔ mli ni ama sũ abɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant plantain trees on a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under bright sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that shade the delicate cocoa trees like an umbrella until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and start to wither when the rains suddenly stop early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ trukaa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Crops need a continuous supply of water to transport nutrients from the soil up to their leaves. When the rains stop, the roots can no longer draw water, causing the plant to close its pores to save moisture, which stops its growth and leads to wilting.
ga: Nu he miihia tsei daa koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛbaai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbala nu dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ŋaa amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni nu lɛ ahi mli. Enɛ haa ekpaa dalɛ ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Are there specific crops I can plant that will still give me a good harvest even when rainfall is scarce in my area?
ga: Ani tsei komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ makwɛ ni baawo yibii kpakpai lolo kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ po?

english: Yes, drought-tolerant crops like cassava, sorghum, millet, and cowpeas have deep root systems or water-saving leaf structures that allow them to extract deep groundwater and survive long dry spells better than crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni haa nu hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ egbalaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Why do my crop flowers drop off without turning into fruits or grains during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences heat and water stress, it enters survival mode. It drops its flowers and young fruits to conserve energy and water for its stem and roots, sacrificing reproduction to keep the main plant alive.
ga: Kɛ tsei na dɔlɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ Tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli. Ekɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai bibii shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ato kɛha tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛtsɔ fɔmɔ ni akɛshaa afɔle koni tso titri lɛ ahi shi lɛ nɔ.

english: How does choosing the right crop variety help me make a better income from my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni sa ni mihalaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná shika kpakpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Improved crop varieties are bred to yield more per acre, resist local pests, and tolerate unpredictable weather. Higher yields and better quality produce mean you have more surplus to sell in the market, bringing in better profits.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ acre kome mli. Eteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni bɛ faŋŋ lɛ hu teɔ shi ewoɔ Yibiiwoo ni fa kɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oyɛ nibii babaoo ni fa fe nine ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ. ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ aba

english: How does planting two different crops together on the same plot of land help increase my gains?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha sɛɛnamɔ ni miná lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Intercropping—like growing maize with beans—maximizes your land space and reduces risk. If dry weather damages one crop, the other may survive. Additionally, leguminous crops like beans fix nitrogen in the soil, which helps feed the neighbouring crop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ awoɔ mli—tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ—haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ko feɔ babaoo ni ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ fite ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu baanyɛ ahi shi. Kɛfata he lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa ni esaa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass or leaves help them survive when it does not rain?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It shields the soil from direct sunlight, reducing water evaporation and keeping the root zone cooler and moist for much longer.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry period before the main rainy season fully sets in. If seeds sprout during that early rain, the young seedlings will dry up and die when the soil dries out in the days that follow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ yɛ gbii fioo ni baa lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops suffer from extreme heat even if the soil was wet a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: High temperatures cause water to evaporate rapidly from both the soil and the plant leaves. If the air is too hot and dry, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil, causing temporary heat stress.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai fɛɛ amli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ be kukuoo mli dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa

english: How deep into the soil should I put my seeds so they get enough water to sprout safely?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni maná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe?

english: Seeds should generally be planted at a depth equal to two or three times their size. Planting too shallow leaves them exposed to surface heat and drying air, while planting too deep prevents the young shoot from reaching sunlight before running out of stored energy.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ amɛdalɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ naa la ni tsoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gĩɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ baatsi ŋmeii bibii lɛ anaa koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ dani amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ baaho.

english: Why do my crops look yellow and weak even when there has been plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash away essential soil nutrients like nitrogen below the root level, a process called leaching. Without nitrogen, leaves lose their green chlorophyll and cannot make food, leading to pale, stunted plants.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishi lɛ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaching. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ amɛ chlorophyll eŋɔli lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe tseee lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their delicate leaves and dries out soil moisture. Keeping shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain creates a protective canopy that reduces heat stress until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hulutsoo he haomɔ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa.

english: How can I tell if my soil is missing nutrients without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛyaaa laboratori?

english: Your crops show visible signs when they lack nutrients: pale yellow leaves usually mean a lack of nitrogen, purplish leaves indicate low phosphorus, and dry, burnt leaf edges point to a lack of potassium.
ga: Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baajie okadii ni anaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ kpo. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Ni baai lɛ ahe ni egbi ni eshã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium bɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and turn yellowish during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is typically caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects that thrive in warm weather. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by local agricultural officers is the most effective way to prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Whiteflies bibii ni yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela naa.

english: If I plant my maize seeds closer together, will I harvest more corn from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together actually reduces your total yield because the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified hybrid seeds from an agro-store instead of replanting seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe hybrid dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli shwapo ko mli? Mohu ɔ, mo du wuhi nɛ a je kpami be nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ ekohu.

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specifically bred to produce higher yields, withstand local pests, and tolerate dry spells better than saved seeds. Seeds saved from a previous harvest lose these strong traits in the next generation, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi fe dumɔwui ni ato. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baafite sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: The first rain often wet only the top layer of soil, and dry spells frequently follow immediately after. Waiting for consistent, steady rains ensures deep soil moisture so newly sprouted seeds do not dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Ni bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, ni baa daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ egbiŋ ni amɛgboii.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow lots of dark green leaves but produce very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa shi ewoɔ tomato fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer causes tomato plants to focus all their energy on growing leaves rather than flowers and fruit. Using a balanced fertilizer richer in phosphorus and potassium encourages stronger flowering and better fruit development.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ aya hiɛ waa ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when the ground around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli egbi moŋ? Ani ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can pull it up from the ground, causing temporary wilting. As long as the soil remains moist, the plant will recover in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ he okadii baa Be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why is it better to leave old crop stalks on my land to rot instead of burning them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mashi tsei momoi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛgboi moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving old crop stalks to rot adds organic matter back into the soil, which improves soil structure, helps hold moisture longer, and releases steady nutrients for your next planting season.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi ni egbɔ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ yaa hiɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ejieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛha odalɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and naturally feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for maize while also ground-covering to suppress weeds.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shwiemɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni egbe jwɛi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava plants shed their lower leaves during dry spells as a natural defense mechanism to conserve water. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ ŋmeii heei ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into thin tubes during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from intense heat. By rolling, the leaf reduces its exposed surface area to lower water evaporation and keep the plant hydrated until temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni hulutsoo ni fe nine akafee. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni oootsi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ha amɛhiɛ he lɛ aba shi koni nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni eha tso lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is usually a sign that tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies are feeding on the underside of the leaves, or that a plant virus is disrupting normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ ŋmɔtɔ, tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies, miiye ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ. Aloo tso mli hela ko miitsi baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Why are my pineapple plants producing flowers at different times even though I planted them on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple tsei lɛ fɔɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli beni midu amɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Pineapples naturally react to unpredictable stress like sudden drops in night temperature or cloudy weather, causing individual plants to flower at different times unless a uniform flowering treatment is applied.
ga: Pineapple tsuɔ haomɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba, tamɔ hulutsoo ni baa shi trukaa gbɛkɛ loo atatu ni ewoɔ lɛ ahe nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha tso fɛɛ tso afɔlɔ yɛ be srɔtoi amli. ja fɔfɔii yɛ daa

english: Tomato flowers drop off when high afternoon temperatures stress the plant, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, causing the plant to focus on growing leaves rather than setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. aloo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tomato tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do pineapples harvested during heavy rains taste less sweet than those harvested in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ŋɔɔɔɔ fe nɔ ni akpaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall causes the pineapple plant to take up excessive water, which dilutes the natural sugars inside the fruit. Additionally, cloudy skies mean less sunlight for the plant to manufacture sugar.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa anana tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli sugars ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Ŋwɛi ni atatu yɔɔ mli lɛ hu tsɔɔ akɛ hulu la fioo pɛ baa nitsumɔhei ni feɔ sugar lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra sucker shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: Extra sucker shoots steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the main mother plant. Removing them allows the main plant to direct all its energy into producing large, heavy bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ plantains babaoo ni tsii.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have friendly bacteria living in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ naanyobɔɔ helai ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi amli. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crop roots rot when rainwater collects and stays on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water sits on the field without draining, it pushes out all the oxygen in the soil, causing the roots to drown, decay, and turn rotten.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ mli lɛ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ fɛɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboɔ, ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help them turn green and grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water very quickly in hot, dry weather. The plant naturally drops its outer leaves to save water for its main stem and central shoot so it can survive until the rains return.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ nu ato kɛha tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ eshishifã lɛ teŋgbɛ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cowpea plant leaves fold inward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas fold their leaves to reduce the amount of surface area facing the direct sun, which stops water from evaporating too quickly. It is a natural protection mechanism to survive intense daytime heat.
ga: Cowpea shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ kwɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ayeɔ wala yɛ hulutsoo be mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the daytime temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping the soil evenly moist and giving plants light shade during extreme heat helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eha tso lɛ ná hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my pepper plant stop growing new leaves once it starts making peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ baai heei kɛji ebɔi pepper feemɔ pɛ?

english: The pepper plant shifts its energy from growing leaves to developing its fruits. Harvesting mature peppers promptly encourages the plant to produce new leaves, new flowers, and another round of fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei tsakeɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni miida kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni egbɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ woɔ baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ aduawai heei ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my okra plants growing very tall with large leaves but producing very few okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa kɛ baa wuji shi okra ŋmeii fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them spend all their energy growing tall stems and leaves instead of flowers. Switching to balanced nutrients and ensuring full sunlight will help them produce more pods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai kakadaji amli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ amɛtsake kɛtee niyenii ni ja kɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee pods babaoo.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so the roots do not get spoiled in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akagbo yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off naturally. Leaving cassava roots in the ground too long past maturity makes them woody, hard, and lose their starchy quality.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha etsɔ tsei, ewa ni ehiɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei.

english: What causes my yam tubers to grow crooked and small instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni haa mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfee kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yam tubers become crooked when they hit hard, compacted soil or stones underground as they try to expand. Preparing deep, loose, stone-free soil mounds or ridges gives the tubers space to grow long and smooth.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛmi shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ. Shikpɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni tɛi bɛ mli lɛ ni asaa lɛ baaha hei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aba kɛha ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting right while attached to the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ mikɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, overly humid, and shady conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to let air and sunlight in, along with removing spoiled pods, helps stop the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ, hei ni edɔ tsɔ, kɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofo tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ hu. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa hela lɛ.
