english: Why do my cabbage heads stay loose and open like leaves instead of forming a hard, tight ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ etse amɛhe ni amɛgbele tamɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee nɔ ko ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads fail to form tight balls when plants are spaced too close together, lack steady water, or experience high heat. Giving each plant enough space and consistent moisture encourages them to form firm, heavy heads.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei nyɛŋ afee kui ni mli wa kɛji akɛ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ, nu bɛ amɛhe daa, loo akɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: What farm work should I start doing during the dry season before the main rains begin?
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, mɛɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔ esa akɛ aje shishi dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ waa?

english: Clearing weeds, tilling, and preparing your land early in the dry season ensures that your soil is ready to trap the very first rains, allowing your crops to get planted on time and start strong.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ hesaamɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ klalo ni ekɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baamɔ. Ye obua onibii ni odu yɛ be naa ni obɔi hewalɛ.

english: Is it better to plant as many seeds as possible close together to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni aaanyɛ koni aná yibii babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to weak plants and small yields. Giving crops proper space allows each plant to grow big and produce more.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. He ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I pull out some healthy young crop plants from my farm after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Removing extra seedlings from crowded spots—a process called thinning—reduces competition so the remaining crop plants get enough food and light to grow big and produce strong yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni eyi obɔ lɛ Nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ thinning. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ akaŋshii baa shi No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Will cutting back some leaves and branches on my growing crops hurt my harvest?
ga: Ani baai kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ ekomɛi ni mafolɔ mli lɛ baaná mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: Pruning or cutting back excess leaves directs the plant's energy into producing bigger fruits and seeds rather than just growing leaves, and it helps airflow prevent crop diseases.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ, loo baai ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii kɛ dumɔwui wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaakwɛ̃ kɛkɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ koni ekɛtsi tsei ahe helai anaa lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why are extension officers advising us not to plant our whole land all at once at the start of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkadu shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ shikome yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Planting in stages protects you against unexpected dry spells and gives you time to care properly for each plot, ensuring better crop survival and higher overall yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ baabu ohe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ bei ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ ahe. ni ehaa bo be ni okɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ jogbaŋŋ Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni baa lɛ he nɔmimaa.

english: How do I know the right time to start sowing my crop seeds at the beginning of the year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli?

english: The best time to sow seeds is right after the first steady rains soak the soil deeply enough to support germination without drying out young seedlings.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ji yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo mli bɔ ni sa koni eye ebua tso bibioo lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni egbiŋ.

english: Why is it necessary to remove old plant stems and roots from last season before planting new crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie tsei ashishifãi momo kɛ amɛshishifãi kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli dani adu tsei heei lɛ?

english: Old crop residue can hide pests and fungal diseases from the past year. Clearing them out reduces pest attacks on your new seedlings.
ga: Tso momo ni eshwɛ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ato. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa odumɔwui heei lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing thin and weak instead of thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Thin stalks usually mean your crops are planted too close together and are fighting for sunlight. Spacing plants properly makes stalks sturdy enough to support heavy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ adu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛmiitswa hulu la he akaŋ. He ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ shishitso lɛ mli awa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I change my traditional planting methods to these new recommended practices?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake mi blema gbɛi ni mitsɔɔ nɔ mikwɛɔ nii lɛ kɛya nifeemɔi heei ni ajieɔ yi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: New farming practices rely on tested scientific methods that protect soil fertility, conserve moisture, and optimize plant growth, giving you higher yields with less wasted seed.
ga: Okwaayeli nifeemɔi heei damɔ jeŋ nilee gbɛi ni aka amɛ akwɛ lɛ anɔ. Bɔni afee ni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ ni oha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ Enɛ haa onáa yibii babaoo ni dumɔwui fioo pɛ afiteɔ.

english: How does clearing dead vegetation early help my land keep moisture for new crops?
ga: Tsoi ni egboi lɛ ajiemɔ mra Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei?

english: Clearing excess dry vegetation and mulching properly allows rainwater to penetrate deep into the ground without getting blocked or wasted, keeping the soil moist for your young plants.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni egbi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni etsĩii enaa loo efiteee. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha otsei bibii lɛ.

english: Can using too much manure or fertilizer ruin my farm land?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite nibii ni midu lɛ?

english: Yes, putting too much strong fertilizer or raw manure on your land can spoil the soil. It makes the ground too acidic or salty, which burns crop roots, kills beneficial insects in the soil, and makes it hard for crops to yield well in the future.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. Efiteɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa ewaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo yibii kpakpai wɔsɛɛ

english: How do I know if my crop land is getting spoiled or losing its strength?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo hewalɛ efo mli?

english: Unhealthy soil often turns very hard, cracks easily when dry, loses its dark color, and fails to hold water. You will also notice that your crops stay small and have pale or yellow leaves even when there is enough rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ waa lɛ mli wa waa. Egbɛɔ oya kɛji egbi, eyɛ ediŋŋ ni enyɛɛɛ emɔ nu. Obaayɔse akɛ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ faaa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ.

english: How can I bring back the strength of my land if it has been damaged?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛji efite?

english: You can heal tired land by letting it rest, planting cover crops like velvet beans, and adding well-rotted compost. These practices put good organic material back into the soil and restore its natural strength.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ hejɔɔmɔ ni ooohã lɛ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ velvet beans ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ afata he. Nifeemɔi nɛɛ baaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha ebɔi hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is fresh chicken droppings good to put directly onto my young crops?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei hee sa akɛ akɛbaawo mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, fresh poultry manure is too hot and strong for young crops. If you put it directly on plants, it will burn the stems and roots. You must let it dry and rot completely before applying it to your field.
ga: Dabi, kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni amɛhe wa tsɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ baashã. Esa akɛ oha egbi ni egbo dani okɛtsu nii yɛ oyale mli.

english: Why do I need to wait for chicken manure to rot before putting it on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ ni tsina ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbo dani okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Fresh chicken manure contains harsh chemicals and heat that can destroy crop roots and harm the soil. Letting it rot breaks down those harsh chemicals into soft food that your crops can safely eat.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni baanyɛ afite tsei shishifãi ni eye shikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee mli. Kɛ́ oha egbo lɛ, efiteɔ nakai tsofai ni mli wa lɛ ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni oŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye shweshweeshwe.

english: Can I mix different animal droppings together to feed my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi afutu? ekome kɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, you can mix poultry manure with cow or goat dung, but you should heap them together and let them rot well first. Mixing them fresh and putting them straight on the farm can create too much heat and destroy your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsina loo too ŋmɔtɔ afutu tsina loo tsina ŋmɔtɔ. Shi esa akɛ ato amɛhe ni aŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ futu ehee ni okɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha edɔ fe nine ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When is the right time to apply poultry manure to my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifãi atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: The best time is during land preparation, about two to three weeks before you plant your seeds. This gives the manure time to blend safely into the soil so it feeds the seed roots without burning them.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Aaafee otsii enyɔ loo etɛ dani obaadu dumɔwui lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe. koni anyɛ aye dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni ashãaa

english: Why did my young vegetable plants wither and die after I applied manure near their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The manure was likely too fresh or placed too close to the plants. Fresh manure sucks moisture out of delicate plant roots instead of feeding them, causing the crop to dry up and die.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ ehee tsɔ loo akɛwo tsei lɛ ahe tsɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a main food crops need to grow strong. Adding properly aged manure or the right fertilizer will help the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the main difference between chemical fertilizer and animal manure for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizer acts like fast food that feeds the crop immediately but does not build the soil. Animal manure feeds the crop more slowly while improving the soil so it can hold water and stay rich for many years.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni ayeɔ oya, ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ shi etswaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Koolooi ashishifã haa ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii blɛoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ nu mli ni ehi shi afii babaoo.

english: How many times in a year am I supposed to clear the weeds on my cocoa farm that is under rehabilitation?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafo jwɛi yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ni asaa he lɛ mli yɛ afi mli?

english: Under standard rehabilitation guidelines, a farm should be weeded every year, with the official Cocobod scheme recommending up to four weedings per year to keep the crop fully healthy.
ga: Yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ shishitoo mlai ni aku sɛɛ akɛba lɛ shishi lɛ shishi lɛ, esa akɛ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli daa afi, ni Cocobod gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ajie jwɛi shii ejwɛ yɛ afi mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does the Cocobod rehabilitation scheme ask us to weed four times a year instead of just once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Cocobod Hesaamɔ Nitsumɔ lɛ biɔ ni wɔjie jwɛi shii ejwɛ yɛ afi mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaajie shikome pɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ

english: Weeding four times a year prevents weeds from choking young or recovering trees, ensuring the crops get enough sunlight, nutrients, and water to recover and produce well.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi shii ejwɛ yɛ afi mli lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekatsi tsei bibii lɛ anaa loo amɛkafee amɛhe ekoŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ ni tsei lɛ aná hulu la, niyenii, kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Am I allowed to clear my cocoa farm more times than what the official scheme requires?
ga: Ani aŋmɛ mi gbɛ ni majie kookoo ŋmɔji babaoo fe bɔ ni maŋ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ biɔ?

english: Yes, if you have the capacity, you can weed more than the required scheme amount. Extra weeding keeps the farm clean and helps crops grow even faster without weed competition.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ oyɛ nyɛmɔ ni okɛbaafee nii lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi atsu nii fe nitsumɔi ayibɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: What does it mean when extension officers say my rehabilitated farm has reached handover time?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ miŋmɔ ni asaa lɛ ji be ni esa akɛ akɛha?

english: Handover time means your rehabilitated farm has matured sufficiently under official care and is ready to be returned to you for full daily management.
ga: Be ni akɛbaahã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔ ni asaa lɛ edara bɔ ni sa yɛ maŋ onukpai lɛ akwɛmɔ shishi. ni efee klalo akɛ abaaku sɛɛ akɛba bo koni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa gbi.

english: Will my farm be cleared of weeds right before it is officially handed back to me?
ga: Ani abaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani aku sɛɛ akɛha yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ?

english: Yes, when a farm reaches handover time, it is given at least one full session of weeding before being placed back into your hands.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni ŋmɔ lɛ be shɛɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, abaajie jwɛi lɛ shikome dani aku sɛɛ akɛba onine mli ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens if the rehabilitation service cannot provide full maintenance work on my farm at the time of handover?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ Restoration Services lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nibii fɛɛ ni kɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ he nii yɛ be mli ni akɛbaahã lɛ?

english: Even if full services cannot be provided at handover time, the program ensures your farm receives at least one complete weeding session so you receive a clean farm.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ anyɛɛɛ atsu sɔɔmɔ fɛɛ he nii yɛ be mli ni akɛhaa lɛ moŋ. Shi kɛ hoo lɛ, gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baaha oŋmɔ lɛ aná jwɛi tsamɔ kome ni yeɔ emuu. No hewɔ lɛ onine shɛɔ ŋmɔ ni mli tse nɔ.

english: Why is regular weed control so important for young cocoa trees on a restored farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni asaa amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young and restored crops are vulnerable. Clearing weeds regularly ensures they do not have to fight aggressive bush plants for soil nutrients and moisture.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni darako kɛ nɔ ni asaa lɛ yɛ oshara mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkwɛɔ koni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I only clear the weeds once a year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mijie jwɛi shikome pɛ yɛ afi mli?

english: Weeding only once a year allows overgrown weeds to steal vital nutrients and harbor pests, which slows down tree growth and reduces crop yields compared to weeding multiple times.
ga: Shikome pɛ yɛ afi mli ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ haa jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli babaoo lɛ he.

english: How does keeping my field clean throughout the year help my crops produce better yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tse afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: A clean field allows crop roots to absorb all available fertilizers and water, leading to stronger trees that flower better and produce healthy pods.
ga: He ko ni mli tse lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni he wa lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni he wa.

english: What is the minimum care required to keep a rehabilitated farm alive if resources are limited?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔkwɛmɔ bibioo ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔ ni awo mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ aya nɔ ahi shi kɛji akɛ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ faaa?

english: At the bare minimum, a farm must be weeded at least once a year, particularly around handover, though four times a year is ideal for proper crop performance.
ga: kɛ hoo lɛ Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ hoo lɛ shikome yɛ afi mli. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ eba tsɔsemɔ he. Eyɛ mli akɛ shii ejwɛ yɛ afi mli ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ.

english: How long can a rubber tree keep producing latex before the tree becomes too old?
ga: Be enyiɛ rɔbɔt tso baanyɛ afee latɛs dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: A rubber tree can remain productive for 25 to 30 years or more if tapped properly. With good care, mature trees over 10 years old can yield consistent latex for decades before needing replacement.
ga: Rɔba tsei baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ jogbaŋŋ. kɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa Tsei ni eda ni eye fe afii 10 lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be afii nyɔŋmai abɔ dani ehe baahia ni atsake amɛ.

english: How many years does it take after planting a rubber tree before I can start tapping it for latex?
ga: Kɛ́ adu rɔbɔt tso sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani ajeɔ rɔbɔt tswamɔ shishi?

english: Rubber trees usually take about 5 to 7 years after planting to reach maturity. You can start tapping when the trunk reaches about 50 centimeters in circumference at waist height.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 5 kɛyashi 7 yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ sɛɛ dani amɛdaraa. Obaanyɛ oje ŋmɔlɔ shishi kɛ́ ogbɔmɔtso lɛ shɛ aaafee sɛntimita 50 yɛ ebɔlemɔ he yɛ etsitsi nɔ.

english: How much dried cocoa bean weight should I expect to get from a healthy acre of cocoa trees?
ga: Kookoo tsei ni egbi ni enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ maná kɛjɛ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ji acre kome mli?

english: On average, a traditional cocoa farm in Ghana yields between 200 to 400 kilograms of dried beans per acre each year, though well-maintained farms with improved hybrid varieties can produce significantly more.
ga: Kɛ aja mli lɛ, Kusum kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni egbi kilogram 200 kɛyashi 400 yɛ acre kome mli daa afi. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔji ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo moŋ, shi.

english: How many fresh cocoa pods do I need to harvest to get one kilogram of dried cocoa beans?
ga: Esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii heei enyiɛ koni aná kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi kilogram kome?

english: It typically takes about 20 to 30 healthy, mature cocoa pods to yield one kilogram of fully dried cocoa beans, depending on the variety and size of the pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 20 kɛyashi 30 dani anyɛ afee kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi kwraa lɛ kilogram kome. Edamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahenɔi kɛ amɛdalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose some of their tiny young pods before they grow into full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifite amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ dani amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. It happens naturally when the tree cannot support all the pods, but it can also be caused by drought, lack of nutrients, or pests like capsids.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Ebaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ lɛ. Shi ekolɛ hɔmɔ hu kɛbaa. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids

english: How often should I run my water tank irrigation system to keep my farm nursery moist without overwatering?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ mi nu ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ atsu nii koni mikɛha miŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ mli nu lɛ mli ahi shi ni mikɛ nu akawo mli fe nine?

english: Setting up phased watering schedules—such as running water for fixed periods every few hours—ensures seedlings get steady moisture without drowning the roots or overflowing your water tanks.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni ato, tamɔ nu ni aaaha eho yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli daa ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be ni shishifãi lɛ shwieee nu mli loo ehaa nu ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ.

english: Is water stored in an overhead tank safe to use directly on my young crops and seedlings?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛto ŋwɛi ŋtayaai amli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, tank-stored water is safe as long as the tank is kept clean, covered, and free of algae or chemicals. Letting water sit in a tank can also warm it up slightly, which is gentle on young roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛtoɔ tanki mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe, kɛji tanki lɛ mli tse, eyɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ, ni ŋmeii loo tsofai bɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi nu lɛ yɛ tanki lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha edɔ fioo. ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ shishifãi bibii anɔ lɛ

english: Why is it important to carefully measure fertilizer in kilograms instead of just guessing the amount?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ kilogram lɛ asusu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni aaasusu bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fa ha lɛ he kɛkɛ?

english: Measuring fertilizer accurately ensures your crops get the exact nutrients they need. Adding too little won't boost growth, while adding too much can burn plant roots and waste expensive inputs.
ga: Kɛ́ osusu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ otsei lɛ miiná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko fioo fata he lɛ, ehaaa dalɛ aya hiɛ. yɛ be mli ni kɛ akɛ babaoo fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni efite nibii ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Can I plant rubber trees and cocoa trees together on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ rɔba tso kɛ kookoo tso yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: While both grow well in Ghana, rubber trees grow very tall and cast dense shade that can reduce cocoa yields. It is generally better to plant them in separate plots or use specific wide-spacing agroforestry methods.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛ fɛɛ amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana moŋ, Shi rɔbɔt tsei hu daa waa ni amɛnáa hulutsoo ni mli wa, ni baanyɛ aha kookoo ni afeɔ lɛ aba shi. Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amɛ yɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ srɔtoi anɔ loo okɛ agroforestry gbɛi ni gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ko yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Should I continue tapping my rubber trees during the dry season or give them a rest?
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ani esa akɛ maya nɔ matswa rɔbɔt loo maha lɛ hejɔɔmɔ?

english: It is best to give rubber trees a rest during the main dry season when they shed leaves. Continuing to tap during this period lowers latex yield and can permanently damage the tree's bark.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha rɔbɔt tso lɛ hejɔɔmɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be titri lɛ mli beni rɔbɔt tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ. Kɛ́ oya nɔ otswa tso lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha latex ni ajieɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ebaanyɛ efite tso lɛ yibii lɛ kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I put dried animal manure into the soil before planting my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Dried manure acts as natural food for the soil. It improves the soil's ability to hold water during dry periods and slowly releases nutrients that young plant roots need to establish themselves.
ga: Nibii ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiofio.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the leaves of my young maize, and where do they come from?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? koni maye mibi lɛ ŋmãa baai Ni nɛgbɛ amɛjɛɔ?

english: These caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, hatch from eggs laid on the leaves by adult moths that fly across farms. They feed on leaves to grow, which weakens the plant's ability to make food.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ, fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii ni eda ni foɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai koni amɛdara. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tsei yɔɔ ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark brown spots and dry up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dark spots are usually caused by fungal diseases that thrive in damp weather and spread when rain splashes mud onto the lower leaves. Clearing lower leaves near the soil helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black spot baa. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and droop during the hot afternoon sun but recover in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi obaaná hewalɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli?

english: When the sun is very hot, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can pull it from the soil. Drooping is the plant's way of reducing leaf exposure to the hot sun to save moisture.
ga: Beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji tso gbɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebaa baai lɛ shi yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. The plant drops flowers to conserve energy for its survival.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: If I plant my cassava stalks very close to each other, will I get more cassava roots at harvest?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani ŋmei shishifãi babaoo baaba kɛji akpa?

english: Planting too close makes crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in many small, thin roots instead of large, healthy cassava tubers.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni mli wa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do some seeds I plant in the soil grow into healthy plants while others rot in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of soil moisture, air, and warm temperature to sprout. Soil that is too waterlogged, too hard, or infested with soil fungi can suffocate or rot the seeds before they hatch into seedlings.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ, ni wa tsɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ loo efite dani amɛbatsɔ dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why do experienced farmers spread dry grass on the bare ground around their pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ gbɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni amɛbɔleɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) protects it from the hot sun, keeps the soil moist for longer, and stops weeds from getting sunlight to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la koni amɛkwɛ̃

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and causes specific pests to build up in the field. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts puts nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi baa ŋmɔji amli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant is taking whatever nitrogen it has left from its older bottom leaves and sending it to the new top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei miihe nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli ni amɛkɛmiiya ŋwɛi baai heei amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Cassava tubers need soil that drains water easily. When heavy rains flood flat ground, water sits around the roots and starves them of air, causing rot-causing germs to break down the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ lɛ Nu bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Enɛ haa helai ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young maize and leaving small green droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the inner funnel of the maize leaf to feed on soft new growth. Finding them early and applying recommended treatments inside the leaf funnel stops them before they ruin the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛ́ ona amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛnaa dani amɛbaakpãtã tso lɛ hiɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from high afternoon heat or dry soil. When the plant feels stressed by weather or lack of water, it drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji amɛna shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba amɛnaa lɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: How does planting beans together with my maize make my soil better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes collect nitrogen from the air and trap it in small nodules on their roots. When left in the field, these roots release natural food into the ground that helps nearby maize grow strong.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi bibii amli kɛji ashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps direct sunlight from baking the earth. It traps water in the ground longer, stops weeds from growing, and cools down plant roots.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ nu ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the hot ground on tall stakes helps the plant catch more light and keeps leaves safe from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ lɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa la babaoo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up tight during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves roll inward to protect themselves from intense heat. By shrinking the leaf area exposed to the sun, the plant reduces the amount of water it loses through evaporation.
ga: Akɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ mli koni ekɛtsi hulutsoo naa fe nine. Kɛ́ ajie he ni baai lɛ shɛɔ yɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhaa nu ni amɛlaajeɔ kɛyaa lasu mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my stored dried maize turn into white powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda yɛŋ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects called weevils lay eggs inside dry maize kernels, and the hatching larvae eat the inside of the grain, leaving behind fine powder. Storing thoroughly dried maize in airtight Hermetic bags starves these insects of air so they cannot multiply.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi mli. Ni ŋmeii ni baa lɛ baaye ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ashiɔ lɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ wo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nɛɛ. no hewɔ lɛ enyɛɛɛ eha yibɔ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: How can I tell that my cassava under the soil is mature and ready for harvest without digging everything up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open as the tubers expand beneath.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei ko miida kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and capture maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the plant to produce food through its leaves, which is then sent down to grow a larger, healthier yam tuber underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii. Atsuɔ amɛ kɛyaa shi koni amɛkwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. It can happen when the soil is worn out or when heavy rains wash the nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: When maize is planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, weak plants that produce small or empty cobs instead of strong, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tso kakadaŋŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo efolo Moŋ lɛ, amɛyɛ toi ni mli wa, ni mli wa.

english: Why does rice thrive when flooded with water, while my maize rots and dies in the same condition?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shwereɔ kɛ́ nu afua ba lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-abele lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shihilɛ kome mli?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels that carry oxygen from their leaves down to their roots underwater, whereas maize roots do not have this system and will drown and rot if trapped in stagnant water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa shishifãi bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo nɛɛ. ni ebaagbo ni ebaagbo kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So mine lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast during cool, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight in to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do officers advise me to cut away some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpa lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mifolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: The small shoots (suckers) steal water and food from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the plant puts all its energy into growing a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii (tso) juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ ŋmeii agboi ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and shrinking into tiny shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, or viruses they spread. These pests suck the sap out of leaves, making them distort and slowing down the growth of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ srɔtoi ni ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot, when the plant receives uneven water, or if insects aren't around to pollinate them. Without proper conditions, the plant drops the flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nu nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii bɛŋkɛɛɛ koni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ, kɛji shihilɛ ni sa bɛ. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛhi shi.

english: The first rain often tricks farmers because the deep soil remains dry beneath the surface. If a long dry spell follows that first rain, your newly germinated seeds will dry out and die before the main rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ lakaa okwaafoi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli egbi lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ.

english: My land is very dry and sandy, can I still grow good maize on it?
ga: Mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ. Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kpakpa ko yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Yes, you can improve dry, sandy soil by adding animal manure or compost, which acts like a sponge to help the soil hold onto water and nutrients so your maize roots can feed properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmei loo kooloi ŋmei ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Bɔni afee ni o-corn shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What can I do to turn a hard, dry patch of land into a place where crops can grow?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi lɛ afee he ko ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ?

english: You can break up the hard soil with a hoe and mix in decayed leaves and manure to soften it, allowing water to sink deep into the ground so crop roots can easily spread and grow.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei akumɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli ni okɛ baai kɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ afutu mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo. Enɛ ji koni nu lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and dry up so quickly even when I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbiɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ nɔ nu daa leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Watering in the full sun of the morning causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before roots can drink it; watering late in the afternoon allows the soil to stay wet all night so the plants absorb maximum moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli leebi lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to cover the soil around our crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle wɔŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket that keeps the hot sun from drying out the earth and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better to pour water directly onto the crop leaves or around the bottom of the stem?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔse nu yɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ?

english: It is best to pour water around the bottom of the stem because roots are the only part of the plant that drink water from the soil, and wet leaves can easily attract plant diseases.
ga: Ehi akɛ ooofɔse nu yɛ tso lɛ shishi ejaakɛ shishifãi pɛ ji tso lɛ fã ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni baai ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala tsei ahe helai oya.

english: Can extreme sun and heat stop my tomato plants from producing fruits?
ga: Ani hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ baanyɛ atsĩ mi tomato tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii?

english: Yes, intense heat causes tomato flowers to dry up and fall off before turning into fruit, but planting tall shade crops nearby or providing temporary shade can keep them cool enough to fruit.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai. Shi kɛ́ adu tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ loo ahã amɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Which crops are best to plant if the rainy season is very short and unreliable?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ?

english: Crops like cowpeas, millet, sorghum, and early-maturing cassava need less water and survive hot, dry conditions much better than crops that rely on heavy rain.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni shwereɔ mra lɛ biɔ nu fioo ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the young plants fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, causing them to grow weak and tall instead of strong and full of fruit.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli, ni no haa dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛdaraa yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives leaves their green color and energy, which you can fix by adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa hewalɛ. Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I stop heavy rains from washing away the good topsoil on my sloping farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting your crop rows across the slope rather than up and down creates natural barriers that slow down running water and keep your rich topsoil on the farm.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ fioo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni baa nii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks important nutrients, especially nitrogen, or when the ground is waterlogged. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the food it needs to keep its leaves green and healthy.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa. titri lɛ nitrogen loo be mli ni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni eha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Twisted or curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant's juice, or by a virus spread by these insects. Spraying neem oil solution or an approved pesticide early helps control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Neem fɔ mli tsofa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperatures get too high, when the soil gets too dry, or if bees aren't visiting to pollinate them. Regular watering at the roots and mulching the soil helps keep the roots cool and preserves the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji ŋmeii baaa koni amɛbafee pollination. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa ni okɛ sũ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your young crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong root systems and produce good yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii bibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb on wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɔ tso tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make food for their underground tubers using sunlight on their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground into the air and light, preventing diseases and helping the plant produce much larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ehaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni ekɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la mli. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs ni dara kwraa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the middle leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely fall armyworms, which hide in the central whorl of the maize plant where the leaves are soft. Checking your farm early and spraying insecticides or organic controls directly into the center of the plant stops them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni afolɔ amɛhe ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ afɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits around them for too long in heavy rain, or when soil fungi attack them. Planting on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutua ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I remove all the trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, hot sunlight because their roots are shallow and leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shelter and moisture until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni baai lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛ cocoa tsei bibii lɛ, ebaaha aná he ko ni ahiɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cocoa tsei lɛ baadara.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit, making them top-heavy. Supporting the stems with sturdy bamboo poles and piling soil high around the base gives the roots extra grip against strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ, ni akɛ sũ ni nɔ kwɔ toɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ buɔ amɛhe waa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why does mixing dry animal manure into my soil make my vegetables grow better during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa mi-aduawai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge in the soil, holding onto moisture for a longer time after rain and slowly releasing rich nutrients to the roots so crops survive better during short dry spells.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ ni ejieɔ niyenii ni fa babaoo kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli fiofio. Enɛ ji koni tsei ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves are tender and dry out easily in direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees or planting plantains alongside them acts like a sun canopy, keeping the moisture in the air and soil so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ ji bibii ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Amɛbaafee ekome tamɔ parasol. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many small flowers, but most of them fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo nɛkɛ, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers if they lack sufficient water, soil nutrients, or tiny insects like midge flies to pollinate them. Proper fertilization and keeping farm soil moist helps more flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu bɛ amɛmli. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ midges koni ekɛ amɛ afee pollination. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to prune and cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mikookoo tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing branches so the cocoa tree can send all its food and energy into growing big pods. It also opens up the tree so sunlight and air can dry out leaves, preventing pod diseases.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ koni cacao tso lɛ anyɛ akudɔ eniyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛya tsei agboi ni miida lɛ anɔ. Agbɛnɛ hu, gbelemɔ tso lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ aha baai lɛ agbi. Tsi hela ni yɔɔ pod lɛ mli lɛ naa

english: Pods are ready for harvest when their color turns completely yellow or bright orange. If you harvest them while they are still green, the beans inside will not be fully developed, and if you wait too long, the seeds will start sprouting inside the pod.
ga: Pods lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji su lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kwraa. Kɛji okpa be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ, Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kwraa. Ni kɛji omɛ be kakadaŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer feeds the crop so the green color comes back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava and beans on the same piece of land, or will they spoil each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo amɛbaafee ekome kɛgboi?

english: You can plant them together safely. Beans pull food from the air and put it into the ground, which enriches the soil and actually helps cassava grow bigger roots without taking away its space.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome shweshweeshwe. Beans gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii babaoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛheee he ko.

english: Leaves curl up to shade themselves and stop water from evaporating too quickly in the heat. As long as they stand back up in the cooler evening, the plant is just protecting itself from the sun.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛha hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ latsaa be mli. Shii abɔ ni amɛteɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛmiijɛ hulu lɛ he kɛkɛ.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the branch during rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This rot is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and shaded environments. Clearing heavy weeds under your trees and harvesting mature pods quickly helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishi babaoo kɛ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ni akpaa oya lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani mana yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to crowd each other out and fight over food, sunlight, and water. Correct spacing allows every single plant to grow strong and yield far more food than a crowded field.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ekome ni amɛye niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edaraa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even when there is plenty of rain for everything to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo koni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ akwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the fertilizer and nutrients out of the soil before your main crops can drink them. Cleaning weeds ensures your crops get all the soil food for themselves.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani otso titri lɛ baanyɛ anu amɛ. Jwɛi ni oootsumɔ lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily scorch and dry out under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and broad, providing natural shade and maintaining moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Ha adebɔɔ mli shade ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crops turning yellow before the plant even flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to grow green leaves. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newer leaves at the top, leaving the older lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai eŋɔli Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha ni shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread leaf-curl viruses. Controlling these sucking insects early stops the leaves from crumpling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. No shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ eshwaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Plantain roots are naturally shallow, but microscopic worms called nematodes or stem borer insects often chew through those roots underground. Without healthy root anchors, the heavy weight of the growing plantain bunch causes the whole tree to fall during strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ shwieɔ nakai shishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji shishifãi ni mli wa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ baaha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ akumɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains stay on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field without draining away, it starves the roots of oxygen, allowing waterborne fungi to attack and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ŋmɛ ŋmɔ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ Hɔmɔ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetable garden early in the morning instead of at noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to absorb moisture before the hot sun arrives. If you water at midday, much of the water evaporates into the air before the roots can take it up, and hot water drops on leaves can stress the plant.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa. Kɛji okɛ nu wo mli shwane mli Nu lɛ babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná haomɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without forming fruit when temperatures are too high or when the plant experiences sudden water stress. Heat dries out the pollen inside the flower, preventing it from fertilizing into a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ aduawai amli fɔmɔ naa.

english: Why do I need to clear heavy tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers using sunlight caught by their leaves. Staking gets the leaves high off the ground, opening them up to receive maximum sunlight while protecting them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la ni tswaa baai lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ ŋmeii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Agbeɔ amɛ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which can pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the legumes are harvested, that leftover nitrogen fertilizes the soil naturally for crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa Nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa kɛha ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do weeds left around my crops make the harvest turn out small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi hiɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe, ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for light, water, fertilizer, and root space. Because weeds grow aggressively, they steal nutrients away from your crops, leaving the crops weak and undernourished.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná la, nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ. Ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hu bɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full sunlight because their leaves are tender. Planting shade crops like plantain beside them provides a cover that protects the cocoa from heat and helps the soil stay moist while the trees grow.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ baai bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, yɛ masɛi Ebaafee he ko ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ latsaa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin, then fall over when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo waa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crops stretch upward to reach sunlight instead of growing thick, strong stalks. Giving them proper space helps them build strong stems that resist wind.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baagbala ehe koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeená ŋmãa ni mli wa ni mli wa. Kɛ́ aha amɛ he ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmaa tsei ni wa ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant lacks sufficient water. Extreme heat stresses the crop, causing it to drop its flowers to save energy instead of producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Cassava leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that carry diseases between plants. These pests suck the plant juices, weakening the crop and slowing down tuber growth underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni kɛ helai baa tsei ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ tsei amli nu. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers coming out small and cracked instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams crack and stay small when the soil is too hard, stony, or dry. Yam roots need loose, deep soil so the tubers can expand easily without running into hard barriers.
ga: Sweet potatoes baagbala ni efee bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. tɛi loo egbi tsɔ Sweet potato shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo ni etswaaa gbɛtsii nii ni wa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves drop off after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants do not like staying in soaked ground. Too much water around the roots stops them from breathing, which causes the roots to rot and the leaves to drop off.
ga: Pepper tsei sumɔɔɔ ni amɛhiɔ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. nu ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ baafo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ hu shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my cowpeas after clearing the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-cowpeas lɛ beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are tough and lie asleep in the soil until clearing exposes them to light and water. Because weeds adapt faster to poor soil than cultivated crops, they quickly steal nutrients if not controlled early.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛkãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa la kɛ nu baa amɛnɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛbaaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Will putting three or four maize seeds in one hole give me more corn cobs at harvest?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ etɛ loo ejwɛ wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha maná ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ babaoo kɛ́ akpa?

english: No, putting too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to fight each other for water, light, and nutrients. This results in weak plants with smaller, poorly filled cobs rather than a bigger harvest.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu, la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛpaakiee jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona yibii babaoo lɛ

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are fully grown and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ edara ni esa akɛ mafo?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and drying up. You can check by pulling up a test plant and opening a pod—if the inside of the shell has dark markings, they are ready.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ kaa tso ko ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi ni ogbele ŋmɔtɔi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ duŋ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfee klalo

english: Why does planting beans in the same field as my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and leguminous crops capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil through their roots. This acts like a natural fertilizer that feeds the neighboring maize plants.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient away, but adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii nɛɛ kɛya. Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha eda waa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain sits in flat soil, it drowns the roots and causes rot; planting on raised soil mounds allows excess water to drain away easily.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Nu ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on my farm land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of food from the soil, while groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground through their roots, naturally refreshing your soil for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmeii lɛ, amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are crowded together, plants fight with each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space ensures it gets the food it needs to grow larger fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ abua dumɔwui lɛ anaa lɛ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni enáa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ aduawai wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, hot sunlight and dry winds. Keeping larger trees or planting fast-growing plants like plantains gives young cocoa the shade and cool air it needs to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ kookoo plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the sunshine to manufacture food for the tuber underground. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground where they would rot, allowing maximum sunlight reach.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni ená niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa ajieɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaagboi yɛ lɛ koni hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ anyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants drop off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plants experience severe heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulched keeps the flowers attached so fruit can grow.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over on their own when the bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbeeɔ shi beni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches during wind. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden Y-props prevents the weight from pulling the plant out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai akui ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ be mli. Tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y lɛ fiɔ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa muji lɛ agbala tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from under the leaves. Clearing surrounding weeds and spraying recommended controls halts the infestation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn weak even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and steal water, fertilizer, and light directly from your crops. Removing weeds early ensures all the goodness in your soil goes straight to feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nibii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa niyenii ni okɛhaa onibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving larger shade trees or planting nurse crops like plantains provides shelter and keeps the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa can establish strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni akɛha hulutsoo loo adu tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Bɔni afee ni kookoo bibioo lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to quickly swallow up available water and soil nutrients. Because they grow so aggressively, you must clear them early so they do not starve your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya. Esa akɛ ojie amɛ mra. Bɔni afee ni hɔmɔ akaye oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ.

english: Why should I leave space between my maize plants instead of planting them very close together to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When maize is planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows it to grow a thick stem and produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: How do I pick the best cassava stems to cut and plant for a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ ni madu koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Choose clean, mature stems from the middle section of healthy cassava plants that show no signs of rot or insect damage. Avoid using the very top green tips or the tough, woody bases near the ground.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni he tse ni eda kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ejieee ŋmei loo kooloi ni efite lɛ he okadi ko kpo. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ loo tsei ni wa ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ he.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm help my crops grow better than just planting straight into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with essential plant nutrients and helps the ground hold water longer, making it easier for crop roots to soak up food and stay hydrated.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ niyenii ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential food crop plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps neighboring crops like maize grow bigger.
