ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are small holes appearing in the young leaves of my corn right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like fall armyworms that hatch when the rain begins. Inspecting your plants regularly lets you spot them early and control them before they destroy the center of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ cutworms, ni fɔɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ otsei lɛ amli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona amɛ mra. ni amɛye amɛnɔ dani amɛkpãtã tso lɛ mli fã lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper or tomato on the exact same spot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating with different crops starves the pests and lets the soil recover.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ atsakemɔ Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii lɛ ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my garden eggs and tomatoes crack open on the bush before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ tomatoi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitswa yɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ dani amɛshwere kwraa lɛ?

english: Fruits crack when water supply is irregular, such as a heavy downpour following a dry stretch. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the skin can stretch, causing it to split.
ga: Yibii fɔ̃ɔ kɛji nu ni bɛ be fɛɛ be bɛ, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa beni nu lɛ egbi sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice so it sells well at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni ejara jogbaŋŋ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Harvesting rice when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains turn straw-colored ensures maximum yield and good grain quality, preventing loss from grains falling off in the field or getting rejected by market buyers.
ga: Omɔ ni akpaa ni omɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 feɔ jwɛi su. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa yibii babaoo kɛ ŋmaa kpakpa. Etsiɔ dumɔwui ni baagbee shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli loo ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ akpooɔ amɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do buyers at the market offer me lower prices for my harvested rice grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ haa mi jara ni baa shi yɛ amɛŋmaa ni amɛkpa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Buyers reduce prices if grains are mixed with small stones, weed seeds, broken pieces, or are not dried properly down to the right moisture level.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ akɛ tɛi bibii, jwɛi dumɔwui, fãji ni ekumɔ lɛ efutu ŋmaa lɛ mli, loo egbiko jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛɛɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to dry my freshly harvested rice directly on bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa ehee lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying rice on bare dirt mixes soil, stones, and animal droppings into your crop, which lowers grain quality, spoils the appearance, and drastically reduces market value.
ga: Omɔ ni ooogbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ futuɔ muji, tɛi, kɛ ŋmeii kɛyaa onibii amli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. efiteɔ ehefɛo ni eha jara ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ ba shi waa.

english: Why are my rice plants producing empty grain heads with nothing inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty rice heads, or chaffiness, usually happen when the crop lacks key nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, suffers severe dry spells during flowering, or gets attacked by insect pests like stem borers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa yitsei loo ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa he gbɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem borers lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Will planting my rice seeds closer together give me more bags of harvest from my field?
ga: Ani ŋmaa ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa kotokui babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight over light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stems and small yields; proper spacing actually produces healthier plants and more bags of rice overall.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa kotokui babaoo.

english: How do weeds in my field lower the total number of rice bags I am able to harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmãa kotokui fɛɛ ni manyɛ makpa lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Weeds grow faster than young rice and steal essential nutrients, water, and sunlight, which starves the rice plants and prevents them from forming heavy, full grain heads.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa bibii ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu kɛ hulu la, ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni ehaaa amɛwo dumɔwui ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Does my rice field need to stay flooded with water all the way until harvest day?
ga: Ani nu baaho yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛyashi nikpamɔ gbi lɛ nɔ?

english: Rice needs water during growth and flowering, but draining the field about 10 to 14 days before harvest encourages uniform grain ripening and makes the soil firm enough for easy harvesting.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni edaa kɛ fɔfɔi. Shi kɛ́ ajie nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 dani akpa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni akpamɔ mlɛo.

english: How can I stop my rice crop from falling over in the field before I harvest it?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ ŋmãa tsei ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani akpa ŋmãa lɛ naa?

english: Rice falls over, or lodges, when too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the stalks weak, or when water isn't drained from the field in time before the heavy grain heads mature.
ga: Omɔ shwieɔ shi loo efeɔ ais kɛ́ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ ha tsei bibii ba. aloo kɛ́ ajieee nu kɛjɛɛɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli dani dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ adara.

english: Why do flocks of birds attack my rice field just when the grains start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi akui tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ be mli pɛ ni ŋmaa lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: During the early grain-forming stage, rice grains contain a sweet, soft liquid called 'milk' that birds easily feed on, requiring farmers to use scaring techniques until the grains harden.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be mli ni ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ Nu ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘milk’ ni okpoi yeɔ oya lɛ yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ okwaafoi kɛ gbɛi ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he gbeyei atsu nii kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What causes my stored bags of rice to get full of small insects after just a few months?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-rice kotoku lɛ mli eyi kɛ kooloi bibii? Yɛ nyɔji fioo pɛ mli?

english: Insects like rice weevils multiply quickly if the rice is stored with high moisture content or in dirty, unsealed bags that let humid air and pests inside.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii fɔɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to he ko ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. Aloo okɛwo kotoku ko ni mli ewo muji ni atsĩko naa mli, he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ kɛ kooloi baanyɛ abote mli.

english: If I use dirty wastewater from nearby houses to irrigate my vegetables, will the plants get sick or die?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ nu fɔŋ ni jɛ shia ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii kɛwo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, Ani hela baamɔ tso lɛ loo ebaagbo?

english: Household wastewater contains soaps, fats, and harsh chemicals that can burn delicate crop roots, block soil pores, and introduce bad bacteria, causing root rot and stunting your crop's growth.
ga: Samla, fɔ, kɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ shĩa nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli. Etsiɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa ni ekɛ helai fɔji tsuɔ nii Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster after fresh rain compared to when I water them with local river water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔ hee sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto nu ni jɛɔ faa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he.

english: Rainwater is pure, free of harmful wastes, and full of dissolved nitrogen that plants love. Local river water that has waste and chemicals in it forces the plant to spend energy surviving instead of growing.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ mli tse Ebɛ muji ni yɔɔ oshara Ni eyi obɔ kɛ nitrogen ni tsei sumɔɔ. Kuu lɛ mli faa mli nu ni jwɛi kɛ tsofai yɔɔ mli Enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃.

english: Can polluted or muddy canal water cause my crops to rot faster than clean well water?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ewo muji loo ni mli ewo muji lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii oya fe nu ni mli tse ni jɛɔ nu bu mli lɛ?

english: Yes, water contaminated with household waste carries fungi and disease-causing germs. When sprayed onto leaves or stems, these germs quickly cause leaf spots, blights, and soft rot on your crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni shĩa mli jwɛi ewo mli lɛ baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni kɛ helai baa lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ afɔse baai loo tsei ahe lɛ, nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ haa baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ oya.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when I irrigate them with water that has a lot of chemical treatments in it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni tsofai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ wo amɛmli lɛ?

english: High levels of chemicals in water can burn the fine feeder roots of crops. When roots are damaged, they cannot absorb nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Tsofai ni fa babaoo yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ni haa lɛ niyenii lɛ ashishifãi. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my plant leaves curl up after I water them with stream water near residential areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mikɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural stress reaction. When plants sense heavy chemicals or soaps in their water, they curl their leaves to reduce water loss and protect themselves from absorbing more toxic substances.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli. Kɛji tsofai ni tsii loo samla ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ kpe tsei lɛ Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkaŋɔ tsofai fɔji babaoo.

english: If my irrigation water has dirty chemicals in it, will my crops still produce healthy fruits?
ga: Kɛji tsofai ni he tseee yɛ mi nu ni mikɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaya nɔ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Crops stressed by polluted water usually focus on basic survival rather than fruiting, which leads to dropped flowers, small or deformed fruits, and much lower total yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu fɔŋ haa amɛhaoɔ lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishijee wala nɔ moŋ fe aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ. ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi Yibii lɛ ji bibioo loo efite. ni nɔ ni afee lɛ fɛɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Is water heavily treated with chemicals like chlorine safe to pour directly onto my young seedlings?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛ tsofai tamɔ chlorine etsu nii waa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔse midumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Young seedlings are very sensitive. Strong chemical treatments in water can shock their tender roots and kill helpful microbes in the soil, so it is best to let treated water sit in an open tank for a day before using it.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsu nu lɛ he nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha eshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni egbe nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu ni atsa lɛ lɛ ahi nu ni agbele naa lɛ mli gbi kome dani okɛtsu nii.

english: How does plastic and rubbish dumped near my farm affect the way my crops grow?
ga: Te plastic kɛ jwɛi ni ashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Trash blocks rainwater from soaking into the ground properly, and dumping waste can leak toxins into the soil that prevent crop roots from spreading deep enough to find nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi tsinsii baatsi nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ni jwɛi ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai fɔji atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa tso shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛna niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are my crops growing so slowly in areas where soap water from washing clothes drains into my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ hei ni nu ni akɛ samla nu ni jɛɔ atadei ni afɔɔ he lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ kɛbaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Laundry water contains high amounts of salts and sodium that damage the soil structure, making it hard for roots to drink water and causing the soil to become hard and compact.
ga: Nu ni akɛfɔɔ atadei ahe lɛ mli ŋmei kɛ sodium babaoo yɛ mli. ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaanu nu. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Will adding extra chemical fertilizer help my crops if the water I use is already polluted with waste?
ga: Ani tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ni mikɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji akɛ nu ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli ewo muji momo ni jwɛi yɛ mli?

english: No, adding more fertilizer to soil receiving polluted water can worsen root burn by creating too much salt buildup in the soil, making it even harder for the crop to recover.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni akɛ muji ewo mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã waa kɛtsɔ ŋmei babaoo ni ebaabua shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaatsake amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and provide wide leaves that shelter the young cocoa plants from harsh sunlight while keeping the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stay small even after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ nugbɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow, stunted leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow tall. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost gives them the nutrients they need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni egbɔjɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni oná niyenii ni he hiaa bo lɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up and look distorted?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by extension officers helps stop this disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ duɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa hela nɛɛ.

english: Covering the mounds with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the soil moist, shields roots from intense heat, and stops weeds from stealing food and water from your yams.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ Buɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni ehaaa jwɛi akaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ ŋmeii amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when watering is uneven, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients. Mulching the soil and watering regularly early in the morning helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Mulching kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow strong stems and produce bigger yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni etsɔ tso lɛ shishi ni wa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are there small holes raggedly chewed into my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii ni ashɛreɔ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Catching them early and applying safe bio-pesticides or neem extract prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Why should I place fertilizer in a circle around the crop stem instead of touching it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ kɛbɔle he lɛ? tso lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooota he

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's delicate skin and roots. Spacing it a few inches away allows the spreading root system to safely drink up the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko lɛ, ehaa shishifãi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll inward during extreme heat to reduce their surface area and save water from evaporating too quickly. It is a natural protection mechanism against drought.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn into powder after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ tsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize turns to powder when insects called grain weevils feed inside the dry kernels. Thoroughly drying your grain before storage and using airtight storage bags (PICS bags) starves the insects of oxygen and keeps your harvest safe.
ga: Abɛi tsɔɔ powda kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ grain weevils lɛ ye ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni ooogbi dani okɛto ni okɛ vacuum-sealed storage bags (PICS) tsu nii lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi lɛ ni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, ni ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does it take several years for my young cocoa trees to start bearing fruits after planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi yibii womɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees require time to build a deep root system and strong trunk to support heavy pods. Traditional varieties take about 3 to 5 years to mature, though modern hybrid varieties can begin producing pods in about 2 to 3 years with proper care.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia be koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. Kusum mli tsofai srɔtoi lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛdaraa. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsofai ni akɛfee tsofai sɔrɔtoi lɛ baanyɛ aje tsofai fɔji afeemɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ, shi.

english: What fast-growing crops can I plant on my farm so I have money and food while waiting for my main cash crops to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Bɔni afee ni maná shika kɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mishika ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Intercropping with short-season crops like plantain, cassava, maize, or vegetables provides quick food and monthly income within 3 to 12 months without damaging slow-growing cash crops like cocoa or oil palm.
ga: Be kukuoo mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains, cassava, ŋmãa loo aduawai amli lɛ haa niyenii kɛ nyɔji amli shika yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 12 mli ni eyeee shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmãa fɔ lɛ awui.

english: Why are the small, tiny cocoa pods on my trees turning black and shriveling up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Small pods turning black can be caused by cherelle wilt, where the tree naturally sheds extra pods it cannot support, or by black pod disease caused by excess moisture. Pruning extra branches helps air flow through the farm and reduces fungal infections.
ga: Ekolɛ cherelle lɛ ni egbo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni feɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. aloo kɛjɛ black pod hela ni hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛbaa lɛ mli Nibii krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it important to harvest my cocoa pods as soon as they turn completely yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛji amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa pɛ?

english: Leaving ripe yellow pods on the tree too long causes the cocoa beans inside to start germinating or rotting. Harvesting promptly protects the cocoa quality and prevents pests from attacking the pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Kɛ́ akpa kookoo lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai atutua kookoo lɛ ŋmɔji lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leafy growth. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leafy branches above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eniji lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil and builds up soil-borne pests. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills the soil with natural nitrogen.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantains or shade trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu tso bibioo loo tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under intense full sunshine. Shade crops like plantains act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa seedlings can survive.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into small wrinkled balls during the dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee bɔɔlu bibii lɛ? Wrinkles yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that hide under leaves, or viruses spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early stops new leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai heei ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ anaa.

english: Why do tomato flowers fall off my plants without turning into fruits during hot months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress that prevents tomato flowers from properly pollinating. When temperatures get too high, the plant naturally drops its flowers to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ baa. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: If I give my crops water during the dry season, will they grow as well as they do during the rainy season?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ nu wo tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Ani ebaakwɛ̃ tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ?

english: Yes, crops need consistent water to grow. With artificial watering during the dry season, crops actually get plenty of strong sunlight alongside the water, which can often lead to even better growth and yields than in the heavy rainy season.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni yaa nɔ daa he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛfee nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baaná hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛfata nu he. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa shweremɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ yibiiwoo baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa be amli.

english: How can I tell if my maize is getting too much water from my irrigation setup?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ mi-irrigation lɛ mli?

english: When maize gets too much water, its leaves turn pale yellow instead of dark green, its growth slows down, and the roots can rot because excessive water drowns the soil and stops air from reaching the roots.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa ná nu babaoo lɛ Ebaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. slow growth Ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo ejaakɛ nu babaoo shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɛɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die as soon as the regular rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ kpa pɛ?

english: Crops use water to carry nutrients from the soil up into their stems and leaves. When the rains stop and the soil dries out, the crop can no longer feed itself or keep cool, causing it to wither and die.
ga: Tsei kɛ nu tsuɔ nii kɛ tereɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ lɛ, Dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛye amɛhe niyenii loo amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i dɔŋŋ. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ ni egboɔ

english: Is it possible for me to plant and harvest crops on the same piece of land twice in one year?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ madu ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli?

english: Yes, if you have a reliable water source to water your crops when there is no rain, you can harvest one crop and immediately plant another, allowing you to farm continuously throughout the entire year.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji oyɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni okɛbaafɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii kome ni odu ekroko amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ehaa otsuɔ okwaayeli he nii daa afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Will my soil get weak if I plant crops on my land continuously all year round?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Continuous planting can exhaust the soil nutrients, but if you rotate different types of crops—like switching between maize and beans—and add manure or fertilizer, your soil can stay healthy and productive all year.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ otsake ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni okɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa hu? ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he Oshikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi ni ebaawo yibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant the exact same crop on the same land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the ground every time and allows pests and diseases that attack that specific plant to multiply in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi kɛ helai ni tutuaa nakai tso lɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does clearing and plowing my land with a tractor help my crops grow better than using a hand hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ trakta shwieɔ shi ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ nine ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii?

english: A tractor plows deeper into the ground than a hand hoe can, loosening the hard soil so crop roots can easily push down deep to find water and food.
ga: Trakta baanyɛ atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii kɛya shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛre kɛya shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛyana nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Can heavy farm machinery spoil my soil and hurt my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli tsɔnei ni tsii baanyɛ afite mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni eye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: If heavy machines drive over your farmland when the ground is very wet, they squash the soil tight like brick. This prevents crop roots from growing through and stops water from sinking in properly.
ga: Kɛji tsɔnei ni tsii tsɔɔ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa lɛ. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ brikii. Enɛ baatsi tsei lɛ ashishifãi anaa ni amɛkatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekabote shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce smaller roots when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are spaced too closely, their leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil, leaving less energy to build large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo pɛ aná ni akɛfee yitsei wuji.

english: Why do some of my crops start producing flowers very early when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi mra beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When crops experience extreme heat and dry conditions, they feel threatened and quickly produce flowers and seeds to try to reproduce before they die from lack of water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ he lɛ, Amɛnuɔ he akɛ awo amɛhe gbeyei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui oya yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛfɔ dani amɛgboi yɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are some of the cocoa pods on my trees turning black and rotting before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods turn black mainly due to a fungal infection commonly called Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet and humid conditions. The fungus attacks the pod skin, spreads inside, and rots the beans.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmɔji ni feɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ lɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ black pod hela. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Fungs lɛ tutuaa pod hewolo lɛ. shweremɔ mli ni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my cocoa pods seem to rot much faster during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ fiteɔ oya kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The fungus that causes pod rot needs water to travel. Raindrops splash fungal spores from the soil and infected branches onto healthy pods, and the high humidity helps the disease grow quickly.
ga: Fung ni kɛ pod rot baa lɛ biɔ nu koni enyɛ efã gbɛ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ lɛ kɛ tsei niji anɔ kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai daa oya.

english: How can I tell if a small dark mark on my cocoa pod is just a dry spot or actual rot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ okadi diŋ bibioo ko yɛ mihiɛ? Yɛ mi-cocoa pods lɛ anɔ lɛ, hei ni egbi loo egbo kɛkɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: A normal blemish stays small and dry, but pod rot spreads quickly across the pod, turning it soft, dark brown or deep black, and sometimes producing a white powdery mold on top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛgbi. Shi pod rot lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa pod lɛ mli fɛɛ oya, ni ehaa efeɔ blɛoo, efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ kwraa. Ni bei komɛi lɛ, ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa nɔ.

english: What will happen to my farm if I leave rotten black cocoa pods hanging on my trees?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi kookoo diji ni egbo yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Leaving rotten pods on the tree creates a home for disease. The fungal spores from those dead pods will blow in the wind or splash in the rain onto nearby healthy pods, infecting your entire farm.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni egboi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ekɛ hela baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa fungal spores ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ amli lɛ loo egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nugbɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baatswa oŋmɔ lɛ he hela.

english: Why is an extension officer telling me to cut off all infected pods even if they have no good beans left?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii kpakpai bɛ jɛmɛ moŋ? Mɛni eshwɛ?

english: Removing infected pods breaks the disease cycle. Even if the pod is completely ruined, removing it prevents it from spreading spores to new flowers and healthy young pods growing on the tree.
ga: Pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fite kwraa po Shi kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa fɔfɔi heei kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ amli.

english: Can black cocoa pods that have fallen onto the ground still hurt the healthy pods on my trees?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmeii diji ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ awui lolo?

english: Yes, rotten pods lying on the ground still carry live fungal spores. When heavy rains fall, drops splash off the ground and carry the disease up onto the lower pods hanging on your trees.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni egboi ni kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka lolo. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa Nu ŋmɔtɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛwoɔ helatsɛmɛi kɛyaa shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔi ni fĩɔ otso lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: What is the best thing to do with black rotten pods after I cut them off the tree?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee beni mifo ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni egbo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After cutting down rotten pods, collect them and take them far away from your active cocoa trees, or bury them deep in the ground so rain and wind cannot spread their spores back onto your crop.
ga: Beni ofolɔ ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Buamɔ amɛ naa ni okɛ amɛ aya cacao tsei ni miitso lɛ ahe. Aloo fuu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ akagbɛ amɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amɛshwã onibii amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it bad to leave mature cocoa pods on the tree for extra weeks if I am not ready to harvest?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni edara lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ otsii babaoo kɛji mifeee klalo akɛ makpa?

english: Yes, leaving ripe pods on the tree for too long causes them to overripe and decay. Overripe pods lose bean quality, attract pests like mirids and rodents, and easily catch pod rot.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshwere fe nine ni amɛgboi. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ laajeɔ amɛ bean su lɛ. Egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. ni emɔɔ ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ oya

english: Why should I make sure to clear every single mature pod off the tree during my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tso lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eda yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Completely harvesting mature pods leaves the tree clean and ready for the next flowering stage. It stops leftover pods from decaying on the branch and attracting pests into your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni edara lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ he atse ni efee klalo kɛha fɔfɔii ni baa lɛ fã ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Ehaa ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ ni egbalaa ŋmeii kɛbaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Does having too much shade from big trees cause cocoa pods to turn black more easily?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be babaoo mli lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ baatsɔ ediŋŋ?

english: Yes, thick shade traps cold, damp air around your cocoa trees and blocks sunlight. Fungi love dark, humid spaces, so removing excess shade helps air flow through and keeps pods dry and healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulutsoo ni mli edɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Cocoa tsei kɛ hulutsoo be Fungi sumɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does growing crops inside a greenhouse help them grow better than growing them out in the open field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: A greenhouse protects your crops from extreme sun, heavy rains, and pests, creating a controlled environment where plants spend less energy surviving bad weather and more energy producing high-quality yields.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ tsei kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli lɛ baa. kɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni akɛbaafee nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: Will it get too hot for my crops if I put them inside a greenhouse structure here in Ghana?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baadɔ fe nine kɛji mikɛwo ŋwɛitsu ko mli yɛ Ghana?

english: While greenhouses capture heat, proper design with mesh side-vents allows air to flow through freely, keeping crops protected from pests while maintaining a cool enough temperature for healthy growth.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ greenhouse lɛ hiɛɔ dɔlɛ mli moŋ, shi bɔ ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ sɛɛ ŋtayaai egbele lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ oya. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I harvest vegetables year-round if I build a greenhouse on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa aduawai afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji mima ŋmɔ mli ŋtayaai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, because a greenhouse protects your crops from severe dry seasons and heavy downpours, allowing you to control water supply and grow vegetables constantly regardless of the outside weather.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmɔji ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ nu lɛ jɛɛhe lɛ ni oduɔ aduawai be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ kɔɔɔ he eko.

english: Why do my tomato flowers sometimes fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience extreme heat stress or sudden dry conditions, which prevents the flowers from pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Removing those extra side branches, called suckers, directs the plant's food and energy into making larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on unnecessary stems and leaves.
ga: Nakai niji krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ lɛ shoo lɛ ni ajieɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ feɔ tso yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ tsei kɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow much slower during the dry harmattan season compared to the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kwraa yɛ harmatta be ni egbi lɛ mli kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he lɛ?

english: The low air humidity and dusty atmosphere during harmattan cause plants to lose water quickly and receive less clear sunlight, forcing them to slow down their growth to conserve energy.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ fioo kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni amɛnáaa hulu la ni mli tse fioo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ aba amɛ dalɛ nɔ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why is it better to water my crops directly at their roots instead of spraying water over their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ nu ashwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Watering at the root level sends water straight to where the plant drinks, while leaving foliage wet creates a warm, moist environment that encourages fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nu yaa he ni tso lɛ nuɔ nu yɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ be mli ni eshiɔ baai lɛ ni efɔ lɛ ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from getting too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ?

english: Overwatered plants often develop soft, yellow leaves and wilting stems because soggy soil chokes the roots, preventing them from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu babaoo baa amɛnɔ lɛ feɔ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa. Ehaa mɔ nyɛɛɛ amu ni enine ashɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ

english: Why do vegetable leaves turn yellow when exposed to strong midday sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can be a sign of sun scorch or intense heat stress, where sunlight causes the plant to lose water faster than its roots can absorb it from the soil.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee hulutsoo loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa he haomɔ he okadi. Hulu la haa tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do pests spread so much faster across my vegetable farm during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects reproduce much faster in warm, dry weather, and without heavy rains to wash them or their eggs off the leaves, their populations explode rapidly.
ga: Kplukai fɔɔ oya yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baaha amɛ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ bɛ. Amɛyibɔ ​​baaya hiɛ oya.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow at the bottom while the plant is still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for healthy growth. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps restore green color and healthy leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha baai lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds keep growing faster than my crops even after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Weed seeds rest underground and sprout very quickly when exposed to sunlight and rain. Clearing weeds early before they produce new seeds helps your crops get sunshine and nutrients first without competition.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya waa kɛ́ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Dani dumɔwui heei baaje kpo lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai klɛŋklɛŋ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Keeping or planting shade plants like plantains shields them from heat stress and keeps soil moisture in place while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni akwɛɔ loo akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: How do I know which cassava stem is good enough to cut and plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mafolɔ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Choose strong, mature stems from healthy plants that are about 8 to 12 months old. Avoid soft, thin, or diseased stems to ensure high sprouting rates and strong root growth.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ ashishifãi ni wa, ni eda. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe koni ona akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu daraa waa.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my seeds when the rains start coming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Wait until the soil stays consistently moist for a few days after regular rains begin. Planting during small temporary showers can cause seeds to sprout and dry up if hot weather returns.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ bibii ni nɛɔ be kukuoo mli Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: What causes holes in my young corn leaves and ragged damage inside the main leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nɔ ni efite ni elaaje yɛ baa wulu lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the plant leaves and eat young growing tissues, which slows down plant development if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ tsei ahe baai amli ni amɛyeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ mra.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce flowers but fail to grow any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off due to high heat stress, erratic watering, or lack of insects to move pollen. Keeping soil moisture steady and ensuring good plant spacing helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: How do groundnuts form pods underground after flowering above the soil?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii beni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, they grow long stems called pegs that bend downward and push themselves into the soil, where the actual pods swell and mature.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg. ni baakoto shi ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Pods diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baafu ni ebaada kwraa.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make energy for growing heavy underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and giving leaves maximum access to sunshine.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fɔfɔi ahe helai anaa ni oha fɔfɔi lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the mother plant for food and water. Pruning to leave only one main stem and one small successor ensures big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛjie ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, no haa amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli koni ashi tso titri kome pɛ kɛ nɔ bibioo kome ni baaye esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and intense heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava planted alongside them during their first few years to protect them from heat stress and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli Koni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and boosts crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava stems so the tubers grow big?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-cassava tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ koni maná bulbs wuji?

english: Cassava stems should generally be planted about one meter apart in all directions. Giving them enough space prevents the roots from fighting each other for nutrients, sunlight, and water, allowing the tubers to expand fully.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ he fɛɛ he. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii, hulu la kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no baaha bulb lɛ mli alɛɛ kwraa.

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by a soil disease called bacterial wilt, which blocks the tubes inside the stem that carry water. Using disease-resistant tomato seeds and practicing crop rotation helps prevent the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ bacterial wilt lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. ni tsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli ni hiɛɔ nu lɛ naa Tomato dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ he nifeemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why does removing weeds early give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ehaa miwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the nourishment in the soil goes straight into growing your crops instead of feeding unwanted grass.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa nibii ni odu lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ ni oooha lɛ najiaŋ

english: What are these tiny caterpillars eating the leaves and funnel of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Those are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that destroys corn crops rapidly. Catching them early by inspecting your field and applying recommended bio-pesticides or chemicals directly into the central plant leaf funnel stops them from ruining your yield.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmãa tsei oya. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans in my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them after maize restores nutrients back into your farmland naturally without spending extra money on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abele ni ooodu yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ofite tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right plantain shoots to start a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain ni sa kɛha ŋmɔ hee shishijee?

english: Always pick sword suckers, which have strong bases and narrow, spear-shaped leaves. Avoid water suckers with wide leaves because sword suckers grow faster, form stronger roots, and produce much heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Halamɔ klante tsei ni shishi wa kɛ baai bibii ni tamɔ lance be fɛɛ be. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ahe ejaakɛ klante tsei lɛ daa oya. Bɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ plantains akuu ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the plants absorb moisture before the midday heat evaporates it. Evening watering leaves leaves wet overnight, which creates a damp environment where fungal diseases thrive.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ mli dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni oooha amɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Certified seeds are specially tested to guarantee high germination, uniform crop growth, and resistance to common pests and diseases. Saved seeds often lose their strength over generations and result in smaller, weaker yields.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. tsei lɛ adalɛ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ kɛ amɛhe ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct sun and burn easily. Plantain trees grow quickly with large leaves, acting as a natural umbrella to provide shade and cool moisture that young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Dumɔwui daa oya kɛ baai wuji. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni tsiɔ hulutsoo naa koni ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ aha.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings need to be planted in a slanted position instead of straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni adu lɛ jaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at an angle helps them root deeper and spread horizontally, which allows the plant to produce larger, healthier tuber roots that are easier to harvest.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa eshishifãi yaa shɔŋŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋwɛigbɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekpamɔ waaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn pale yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient green leaves need to grow strong, or that the plant is not getting enough water to feed on the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa baai eŋɔli koni amɛdara waa. Aloo tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly into tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or by viral diseases spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers fall off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot, when there is irregular watering, or when wind and insects are not available to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cowpeas put all their energy into growing green leaves rather than producing the flowers that turn into pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaha cowpea afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛkwɛ baai eŋɔlii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔi ni tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in warm, wet conditions when trees are overcrowded or lack proper sunlight and airflow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ loo hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my yams start rotting underground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when soil stays waterlogged for too long, suffocating the roots and creating a damp home for soil diseases to attack the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ feɔ shia ni mli ewo fɔ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How does planting legumes like groundnuts help make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legumes pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop season ends, that stored nutrient remains in the soil as natural food for your next crop.
ga: Legumes gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every year and allows maize-loving pests and diseases to build up heavily in your field.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa babaoo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: I heard people use salt water to test seeds before planting, but won't the salt kill my maize seeds?
ga: Minu akɛ mɛi kɛ nu ni mli edɔ tsuɔ nii kɛkaa dumɔwui amɛkwɛɔ dani amɛduɔ. Shi ani ŋmei lɛ egbeŋ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Salt water float testing is a safe way to select good seeds if done quickly. Healthy seeds are dense and sink to the bottom, while damaged or dead seeds float. As long as you rinse the good seeds with clean water right after testing, the salt will not harm them.
ga: Brine buoyancy kaa lɛ ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahalaa dumɔwui kpakpai kɛji akɛ afee oya. Dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ shishi. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni efite loo egboi lɛ baaho. Shii abɔ ni okɛ nu ni mli tse baafɔ dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ kaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nu lɛ yeŋ nakai dumɔwui lɛ awui.

english: How can I check if the seeds I stored from last season are still alive and good to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni esa akɛ adu?

english: You can perform a simple germination test by placing ten seeds in a wet cloth for a few days. If eight or more sprout strong roots, your seed batch is very good to plant in the field.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Abaanyɛ afee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni akɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii 2-3 kɛji shishifãi kpaanyɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui akuu lɛ sa kɛha dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if insects have ruined my stored bean seeds before I waste time planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miitutua mi ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ dani mafite be kɛdu amɛ?

english: Drop a sample of your seeds into a bowl of clean water. Seeds that have been eaten inside by weevils become light and hollow, so they will float to the top, while healthy, whole seeds will sink.
ga: Okɛ odumɔwui lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ awo nu ni mli tse mli. Dumɔwui ni ŋmeii yeɔ lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛhe ewo muji. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbaafo kɛya ŋwɛi. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwu ni yeɔ emuu lɛ baagbee shi kwraa lɛ.

english: How can I be sure that the seeds I buy from the market will actually sprout and give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Look for certified seed packages sealed with official government tags from registered agro-dealers. Certified seeds undergo strict laboratory testing to guarantee high germination rates and disease resistance.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛ okadii ekadi kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yaa laboratori mli kaa ni mli wa mli koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ.

english: Will putting chemical fertilizer too close to my seeds kill them when I plant?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛfataa dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ baagbe dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yes, chemical fertilizers contain strong salts that can draw water away from a germinating seed and burn it. You should always place fertilizer a few centimeters to the side of the seed, not directly touching it.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ amli ni eshã amɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo dumɔwu lɛ he 2-3 centimeters ni okɛ ohe akataa dumɔwu lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout even when I give the soil plenty of water after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nu babaoo yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: Too much water fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the seed because it needs oxygen to sprout. Drowned seeds will rot in wet soil instead of growing into strong seedlings.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa he miihia amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni miiho lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and dry up when the farm soil becomes hard and salty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Salty or hard soil makes it very difficult for plant roots to drink water and pull nutrients from the earth. Even if moisture is present, high salt levels choke the roots, causing the crop to dry out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaanu nu ni amɛjie niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ moŋ, shi ŋmei ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi

english: How deep should I plant my seeds so they don't die underground or get eaten by birds?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo okpoi akaye amɛ?

english: A general rule is to bury a seed at a depth equal to two or three times its thickness. Planting too deep uses up all the seed's stored energy before it reaches the sun, while planting too shallow causes it to dry out.
ga: Mla ni afɔɔ namɔ ji ni afu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ amɛmli ŋtayaa lɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaafite hewalɛ fɛɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ eto lɛ dani eshɛ hulu lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi.

english: My neighbors say planting during certain moon phases makes crops grow better, is this true?
ga: Mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ adu tsei yɛ nyɔŋtsere ni miiho lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Ani nakai eji anɔkwale?

english: While traditional beliefs are common, crop growth depends mainly on soil moisture, temperature, and seed quality. Planting right after the first steady rains gives your crops a much higher chance of success than following moon phases.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ blema hemɔkɛyelii ji nɔ ni afɔɔ namɔ moŋ Shi tsei adalɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, latsaa, kɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ titri. Kɛ́ odu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛye omanye fe ni ooodu yɛ nyɔŋtsere ni miiho lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Does soaking my crop seeds in plain water overnight help them grow faster in the soil?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ wo nu mli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, soaking hard seeds in clean water overnight softens the outer coat and signals to the seed that it is time to wake up, leading to faster and more uniform sprouting across your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni wa lɛ wo nu ni mli tse mli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ, ebaaha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo. ni etsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛte shi Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni amɛfee ekome yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build strong green leaves. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the crop regain its rich green color and grow bigger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ waa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rain falls for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air inside the soil to stay alive. When water logs the ground for too long without draining away, the roots suffocate and rot-causing organisms in the wet soil easily attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatutua amɛ oya.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from extreme heat, lack of water, or insect attacks like capsids. Giving young trees partial shade and controlling pests helps the flowers turn into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi tamɔ capsids tutua amɛ. Tsei bibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe shade kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by small sucking insects like whiteflies that spread viruses, or by severe water stress. Protecting the plants from insects and keeping the soil evenly moist prevents leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa mli Tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that carry a very heavy stem. Microscopic soil worms called nematodes or stem-boring insects damage these roots, making the plant lose its balance and fall easily.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ tsii waa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ fiteɔ nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛgbee shi oya.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the earth. When the plant harvested, that trapped food stays in the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpa tsei lɛ Niyenii ni ekã shi lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make the energy required to swell the tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground away from diseases and exposes them fully to the sun.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ aba. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, helai kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally built to survive tough conditions, so they drink water and suck soil nutrients faster than farmed crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing the food meant for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni adebɔɔ fee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛjieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off before any small peppers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the days are too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers stay on the plant and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ waa loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why can swamp rice grow directly inside standing water while my other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ marsh rice lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni mi tsei krokomɛi lɛ gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow tubes inside their stems that carry air from above the surface down to their under-water roots, allowing them to breathe while submerged, unlike maize or cassava.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu lɛ shishi lɛ amli. Ehaa omuɔ beni oyɔɔ nu shishi lɛ. Ejeee tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Is it harmful if I double the amount of pest medicine I spray on my vegetables to kill insects faster?
ga: Ani ebaafee oshara kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ falɛ toi enyɔ shwie aduawai lɛ anɔ koni egbe amɛ oya?

english: Using excessive pesticide can burn your crop leaves, contaminate the soil, leave dangerous chemical residues on food, and make insects resistant to the medicine over time.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã otso lɛ baai lɛ. shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji Tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ni eshiɔ yɛ niyenii mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I safely test a new pest spray on a small part of my farm before spraying the whole field?
ga: Mibaaka tsofa hee ko ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ makwɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko bibioo. ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ekɛ tsofa afɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Spray a small amount of the mixed spray on just two or three affected plants and wait two days. If the pests die without the leaves turning brown or burning, the spray is safe to use across your farm.
ga: Okɛ tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ fioo ko afɔ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ ni omɛ gbii enyɔ. Kɛji tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbo ni baai lɛ etsɔko blɔfo loo shãaa Abaanyɛ akɛ spray lɛ hu atsu nii shweshweeshwe yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and showing big holes overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛná buji wuji nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm feed on maize leaves during the cool night hours and hide inside the central leaf funnel during the hot day, leaving yellowed foliage and large ragged holes.
ga: Kooloi tamɔ Fall Armyworm yeɔ ŋmãa baai yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be mli. ni ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Baai lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ buji agboi ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do grasscutters and rodents attack my cassava roots right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ŋmɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Rodents target mature cassava roots because they contain high amounts of starch and energy. Clearing weeds along your farm boundaries removes their hiding spots and discourages them from invading.
ga: Rodents lɛ kwɛɔ cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ anɔ yɛ starch kɛ hewalɛ ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie hei ni mɛi yɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe lɛ, ni ebaaha amɛnijiaŋ aje wui koni amɛkatutua bo.

english: Can I trap pests in my farm using physical traps instead of buying expensive chemical sprays?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ tsɔnei ni akɛtswaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni mahe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ ni jara wa?

english: Yes, physical methods such as sticky traps, pitfall traps, or insect barriers can capture farm pests effectively without chemical costs, helping you monitor and control pest numbers naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛi tamɔ tsɔnei ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ nii ahe, booby tsɔnei. loo tsofa ni tsiɔ kooloi anaa Ebaanyɛ emɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ tsofai tsuuu nii. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ ni okwɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: If pests return to my farm every season, how does rotating my crops help stop them?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa be hu? Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsakeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa amɛ?

english: Rotating different crops breaks the pest life cycle. Pests that live in the soil and feed on a specific crop like maize will starve and die when you plant a different crop family, like groundnuts, in the following season.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ wala shihilɛ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛbaagboi kɛ́ odu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How should I safely collect a sick plant sample to bring to the agricultural office for testing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maŋɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii shweshweeshwe koni aka amɛ akwɛ yɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: Cut a fresh sample showing both the healthy and diseased parts of the plant, place it in a clean plastic bag, keep it shaded, and bring it to the agricultural office quickly before it dries out.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ nɔ ko ni hiɛ ka ni tsɔɔ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ helai fɛɛ. Okɛwo plastic kotoku ni mli tse mli. Ha ehi hulutsoo be mli. ni okɛya okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ oya dani egbi.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Overwatering or soil-borne diseases can rot plant roots. Damaged roots cannot transport water to the leaves, causing the plant to wilt and die even if the surrounding soil is wet.
ga: Helai ni nu loo sũ babaoo kɛbaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ashishifãi lɛ agbo. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ nu aya baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ewo nu po.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and curl down during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves droop and curl in peak afternoon heat to conserve water and reduce evaporation. As temperatures cool down in the late afternoon, the leaves will naturally expand again.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛba la ni hoɔ lɛ shi. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ, baai lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know if a chemical spray will harm my farm animals if it washes into the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baaye miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ awui? Kɛji akɛ awo mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Every agricultural chemical has specific safety guidelines printed on the label. Always keep livestock away from recently sprayed fields and consult an extension officer to confirm the safe waiting period before grazing animals nearby.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi pɔtɛɛ ni akala awo nɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ha kooloi ahi ŋmɔji ni ashwie nɔ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ ahe ni okɛ sɛɛkpee nitsulɔ ko agba sane koni ema be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni esa akɛ amɛmɛ lɛ nɔ mi dani okɛ kooloi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow while the rest of the plant stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ kã he eji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil beyond the reach of the maize roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni ŋmãa shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and turning twisted instead of opening wide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbele babaoo lɛ?
