english: Curled or twisted leaves are often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips, or by viruses transmitted by these insects. They feed on the tender sap of young leaves, causing them to deform.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ, ni no haa amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants produce lots of big green leaves but fail to form hard heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitsei ni wa lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer or hot weather encourages the cabbage to grow quick, loose outer leaves rather than wrapping tightly to form a firm head.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha kaabe lɛ ada oya. loose outer leaves Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni eyitso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground if I leave them past the normal harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe be ni sa ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ?

english: Mature cassava roots stop growing and start absorbing excess water from wet soil, which invites soil bacteria and fungi to break down and rot the stored starch in the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ni eda lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛjeɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ŋmɔmɔ shishi. Enɛ fɔ̃ɔ helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nine koni amɛfite ni amɛfite ŋmeii ni ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy windstorms even when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain plants have very shallow root systems that stay close to the topsoil. When heavy bunches of fruit grow at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and easily pulled up by high winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni aduawai babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi Tsei lɛ tsii yɛ ŋwɛi ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa amɛ oya.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out twisted and bent instead of straight and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams bend when their growing tips hit hard, unplowed soil, rocks, or tree roots underground. Loose, deep, well-tilled soil allows yam tubers to expand downwards smoothly.
ga: Sweet potatoes baabɔle kɛji akɛ naagbee ni miida lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni wa, tɛi, loo tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo kɛyaa shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without growing any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes dry and inactive, preventing pollination. The plant drops its unpollinated flowers to conserve water and energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tomato pollen lɛ baagbi ni ebaafee nɔ ni tsuuu nii. Tsi pollination naa Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni pollination bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees dry out and turn brown during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot drink enough water to keep up with the dry, hot Harmattan winds. Planting shade crops like plantains protects them from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ anu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ naa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ akagbi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my maize grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil. This natural nitrogen feeds the nearby maize.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ ji niyenii ni ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly right after I clear and burn my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mishã lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds remain hidden under the soil for a long time. Clearing the ground lets sunlight and heat reach the soil surface, triggering buried weed seeds to germinate all at once after rain.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: If I divert water from a nearby stream to my farm, will it help my maize grow better during the dry season?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ mli lɛ tee miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani ebaaye ebua mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Diverting stream water brings steady moisture to crop roots, allowing maize to grow green and produce heavy cobs even when rain stops, as long as the water flows gently and does not wash away the soil.
ga: Nu ni atsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ faai amli lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ baa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛɔ eŋɔli ni ewoɔ ŋmãa ni tsii kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ekpa po. Shii abɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ blɛoo ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieee lɛ,.

english: Will diverting water through long dirt channels reduce the amount of water that actually reaches my crops?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ gbɛi kakadaji anɔ lɛ baaha nu ni shɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, unlined dirt channels soak up a lot of water into the ground and allow evaporation, so less water reaches distant crops unless the channels are kept short, clear, and well-maintained.
ga: Hɛɛ, muji gbɛi ni bɛ tsɔne mli lɛ baaŋɔ nu babaoo kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaaha etsɔ la. No hewɔ lɛ, nu fioo pɛ baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ ahe. Ja gbɛ lɛ yɛ kuku, ehe tse, ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can redirecting a stream away from my farm cause my crops to dry up and die?
ga: Ani faai ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ ni mikɛbaatsake lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi?

english: Yes, crops rely on groundwater from nearby streams, so redirecting the water flow elsewhere reduces soil moisture and can cause leaves to wilt and crops to dry up if rain is scarce.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe fɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni jɛ faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie nu ni hoɔ lɛ kɛtee he kroko lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ aba shi. Ni ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ agbi ni ŋmɔshi nibii hu agbi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: What happens to my soil if I temporarily block water from entering my field to prepare the land?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mitsi nu naa be kukuoo ko koni ekabote miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Temporarily blocking water dries out wet soil so you can clear weeds and prepare ridges easily, but you must restore controlled water flow after planting so crops do not suffer from thirst.
ga: Nu ni atsĩɔ naa be kukuoo ko lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ agbi. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ oya ni osaa ŋmeii lɛ. Shi ehe miihia ni okudɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ koni kumai akaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Can I plant crops like cocoa or vegetables in a swampy area if I drain the excess water out first?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo aduawai yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ? Kɛji mikɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwie shi klɛŋklɛŋ

english: Yes, draining excess water creates workable soil rich in nutrients, but you must keep drainage channels open so heavy rains do not trap water and rot the roots later.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Shi esa akɛ oshi nu ni hoɔ lɛ gbɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akamɔ nu mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ akagbo sɛɛ mli.

english: How does creating multiple channels for water to enter my farm affect my crop growth?
ga: Te gbɛi srɔtoi ni mifeɔ koni nu abote miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Using multiple smaller water routes spreads moisture evenly across the farm, preventing a single strong flood from washing away young crops and fertilizer.
ga: Nu gbɛi bibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii Gbɛi babaoo jaa ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Tsi nu afua wuji ni baafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop when water overflows onto my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ho ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Excess standing water drowns plant roots by cutting off air, which causes cassava roots to rot underground and the leaves to turn yellow and fall from stress.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ haomɔ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt even after I divert water directly into my crop rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mikɛ nu lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If diverted water pools around the base of the plant without draining, the roots rot and stop taking up nutrients, causing the plant to wilt just as if it were in a drought.
ga: Kɛji otsake nu gbɛ ni bɔleɔ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni okɛ nu shwieee lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaakpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gboɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: How long can vegetable crops like tomatoes survive if water fills up the field after I block a water route?
ga: Be enyiɛ aduawai tsei tamɔ tomato baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji nu eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ beni mitsi nu gbɛ lɛ naa sɛɛ?

english: Most vegetables can only survive one to two days under standing water before their roots die from lack of air, so pooled water must be removed quickly to save the harvest.
ga: Aduawai babaoo baanyɛ ahi shi gbii 1-2 pɛ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ shishi. Dani shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie nu ni ebua naa lɛ oya koni nibii ni anáa lɛ aya nɔ.

english: How does changing the route of water across my field affect the topsoil where my crop roots feed?
ga: Te nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ saa shikpɔŋ ni mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Fast-moving water on a new path can strip away the dark, fertile topsoil and expose crop roots, so water routes must be sloped gently to nourish plants without washing the soil away.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ oya yɛ gbɛi heei anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋ lɛ. ni ejieɔ tsei ashishifãi kpo No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsɔ nu gbɛ lɛ nɔ blɛoo koni ekɛha tsei lɛ niyenii ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akafɔ.

english: This usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, which is essential food for the plant. The maize plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new leaves at the top, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without growing into fruit during the very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkwɛɛɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely high, tomato plants get stressed and lose moisture quickly. To save water and survive the heat, the plant naturally drops its blossoms instead of spending energy turning them into fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛhe feɔ shoo oya. Bɔni afee ni ekɛ nu akafite ni ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli Tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ adebɔɔ naa moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Plants compete with each other for sunlight. When cassava plants are placed too close, they stretch upwards to fight for light, spending all their energy growing tall stems and leaves instead of storing food in underground tubers.
ga: Tsei kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaakpã mli koni ekɛ la akaŋ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kɛ baai kakadaji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why does my maize grow slowly and look weak when planted under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Maize needs direct sunlight for most of the day to make its own food. Large trees block the sunlight and their big roots also steal water and nutrients from the soil that the maize needs to grow strong.
ga: Hulu la he miihia ŋmãa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei babaoo mli koni enyɛ efee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii. Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni shishifãi wuji juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cold, wet weather. When there is too much shade and humidity around the cocoa trees, the fungus multiplies and rots the pods from the outside in.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i babaoo yɛ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ, ŋmei lɛ fɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ kɛboteɔ mli.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars hide inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms. They hide in the center funnel of the plant because the leaf tissue there is soft, fresh, and protected from the hot sun and predators, allowing them to eat the young leaves safely.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Asraafoi. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ejaakɛ baai lɛ amli fãji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa efeɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ amɛyeɔ baai bibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground when water sits on my farm after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need air in the soil to stay healthy. When rainwater floods the soil and cannot drain away, it blocks oxygen and creates a wet environment where harmful bacteria and molds multiply and rot the roots.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nu lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ ni nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie kɛya. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ naa ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa yɛ ni amɛfiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts make my farm soil better for growing maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii adumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that have special bacteria on their roots which pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that added nitrogen remains in the earth to nourish the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa ŋmei Nitrogen ni akɛfata he lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eya nɔ eha ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does a small weed with pink flowers cause my maize crop to remain short and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa bibii lɛ? Ani eji pinki ni haa mi-abɛi lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: That weed is Striga, also known as witchweed. Its roots attach directly to the roots of your maize underground and suck out water and nutrients, starving the maize plant before it can grow tall.
ga: Nakai jwɛi lɛ ji striga. Ale lɛ hu akɛ Witchweed. Eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi shwieɔ shi Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into tight balls when little insects cluster underneath them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa beni kooloi bibii bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: Insects like aphids and whiteflies suck the sap out of pepper leaves and often spread viruses. The leaf curling is the plant's reaction to losing sap and being infected, which stops the leaf from opening and growing normally.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ aphids kɛ whiteflies nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ pepper baai amli lɛ ni bei pii lɛ amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji bɔ ni tso lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa kɛji nu ni elaaje kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ agbele ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential food crop plants need to build strong leaves and produce big ears.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa kɛ toi wuji.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help improve my soil for future crops?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, acting like a natural fertilizer for the next crop planted there.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaves of young maize plants and feeds on new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa heei ni eda lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Excess water fills up air spaces in the soil, suffocating the cassava roots and creating a damp environment where fungal rot diseases spread quickly.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni fungal rot hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small harvests when I sow seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni mikpamɔ lɛ hu faaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving every plant weak and low-yielding.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crop plants with dried grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the sun, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and short roots that cannot handle intense direct sunlight, requiring temporary shade from plants like plantain to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni tsei aná hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily when strong winds blow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems, making them top-heavy and easy for strong winds to uproot unless they are supported with wooden stakes.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni tsii. Enɛ haa efeɔ tso ni tsii, ni ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatse lɛ. ja akɛ tso ko efi sɛɛ

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures become too hot or when they do not get steady water, as a natural response to save energy and stay alive.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu be fɛɛ be. Eji adebɔɔ mli hetoo ni akɛbuɔ hewalɛ he ni ahiɔ wala mli.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by drought, lack of shade, or pest attacks. Ensuring proper shade trees and protecting the farm from mirid bugs helps the tree hold onto flowers so they can form pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Tso ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔii lɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why are my plantain bunches small even though the main tree grows very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso titri lɛ kwɔ waa moŋ?

english: Plantains need a lot of food and water to make big bunches. If you allow too many suckers to grow around the mother plant, they compete for nutrients, leaving less energy for the main plant to build a large fruit bunch.
ga: Niyenii kɛ nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ jwɛi wuji. Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he lɛ, amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ he hiaa koni tso titri lɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground away from diseases and exposes them to maximum sunlight for bigger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ni ajie kɛjɛ helai ahe. ni oha ená hulu la babaoo kɛha ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore the rich green color and improves grain yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmaa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa?

english: Beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally and gives you an extra harvest from the same piece of land.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abele ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa bo ni onáa yibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: When is the safest time to put fertilizer around my young crops so it does not spoil them?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi tsei bibii lɛ amli koni amɛkafite?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain, but make sure the plant leaves are dry. Always place the fertilizer in a small ring or hole a few centimeters away from the plant stem so it does not burn the roots or stalk.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shi kwɛmɔ ni tso lɛ baai lɛ agbi. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo bu lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai 2-3 be fɛɛ be. Bɔni afee ni akashã shishifãi loo ŋmeii lɛ

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water settles around them or when soil fungi attack wet roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu ni ekã shi ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots continuously absorb calcium from the ground.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli kɛ́ afɔɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids under the leaves. Spraying an organic neem leaf extract or appropriate insecticide stops the pests and allows new leaves to grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ akpa ni eye ebua baa heei lɛ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my young crops hurt their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani mi dumɔwui lɛ miigba amɛdalɛ naa?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from them. Clearing weeds around your crops gives your plants full access to the resources they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛdɛŋ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ naa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dry even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight. Without shade plants like plantains or shade trees above them, the harsh sun scorches their tender leaves and slows down their growth.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden stakes to climb instead of just spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants produce larger tubers when their leaves are lifted off the hot ground toward the sun. Staking helps the leaves catch maximum sunlight while keeping them away from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji kɛji ajie amɛbaai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ lɛ kɛtee hulu la lɛ mli. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with plenty of leafy branches but only gives me very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ niji babaoo, shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa pɛ lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or water early on, it spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Pruning excess stems helps redirect energy back to the tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ mra lɛ, Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa bulb lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the exact same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Soil gets tired when you plant the same crop repeatedly without giving it a break or adding organic manure. Crops strip the soil of specific nutrients, so rotating crops or adding compost is needed to restore fertility.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui kɛ́ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ efooo loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he Tsei jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni atsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tight and stop growing new peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi pepper tsei heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites feeding on the sap and transmitting viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf curl disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni yeɔ latex lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi leaf curl hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why are my maize leaves full of holes with stuff that looks like sawdust inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni nɔ ko ni tamɔ ŋmãa yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This is a clear sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide inside the plant's funnels to eat the tender growing leaves, leaving behind chewed leaves and frass (waste) that looks like sawdust.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ebatutua. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai ni miida blɛoo lɛ. Eshiɔ baai ni ashɛre kɛ ŋmeii (sũi) ni tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off the plant before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when temperatures get too high, during dry spells, or when there is too much fertilizer. The plant drops flowers to save its own life when it feels stressed.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli loo be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛhere amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala yiwala beni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during small rains even before the bunches are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli dani panicles lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be destroyed by microscopic worms called nematodes or weevil borers. Weakened roots cannot support the heavy fruit bunch, causing the entire plant to stem-topple in slight winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo borers lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɔne lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa.

english: Why do my vegetables wilt and dry out after just two days without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbi yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Uncovered soil loses moisture quickly to the hot sun. Placing dry grass or leaves around the bases of your plants (mulching) keeps the soil cool and traps moisture around the roots for longer periods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ ŋwɛitsu nɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ enɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi wo tsei lɛ ashishi (mulching) lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ abɔle he. shishifãi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ

english: How do I know if I planted my maize crops too close to each other in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If maize plants are overcrowded, they will grow thin and tall while competing for light, their lower leaves will turn yellow early from lack of nutrients, and they will produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔi tsɔ Amɛfeɔ shwiili ni amɛkwɔ be mli ni amɛyeɔ la he akaŋ lɛ. Eshishi baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ mra. yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ Ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Leaf yellowing and curling in tomatoes is often caused by heat stress, irregular watering, or sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses. Providing consistent moisture and controlling insect pests helps keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ejaaa loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa. Ehaa hulutsoo be fɛɛ be ni eyeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui anɔ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers mainly due to extreme heat, prolonged dry spells, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruit. Consistent watering and balanced nutrients help hold the flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ babaoo yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my garden egg plants look wilted during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot, sunny days, plant leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can pull water up from the soil. This causes temporary afternoon wilting, but the plant usually recovers by evening as temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ be kukuoo ko yɛ shwane mli. Shi tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or receives excessive rainfall, cassava plants put most of their energy into growing stems and foliage above ground rather than swelling their nutrient-storing roots below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ tsɔ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ etsitsi kɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e haa nɛ shishifãhi nɛ a kɛ niye níhi toɔ zugba a sisi ɔ mi bliɔ.

english: How do I know when my maize is ready to harvest for fresh eating versus drying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa kɛha niyenii hee kɛ gbimɔ?

english: For fresh eating, the silks on the cob turn dark brown and squeezing a kernel releases a milky liquid. For dry grain maize, wait until the whole stalk turns brown and dry, and the kernels become hard.
ga: Kɛha niyenii hee Siliki kpãai ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Ni kɛ́ amɔ mli lɛ, ŋmei lɛ jieɔ nu ni tamɔ mliki. Kɛha ŋmãa ni egbi Mɛɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ baatsɔ ŋmãa ni egbi. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee shiŋŋ

english: Why do my vegetable seeds rot in the ground instead of sprouting during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil pushes out oxygen, suffocating seeds and creating ideal conditions for soil fungi to attack and rot the seeds before they can germinate. Good field drainage prevents seed rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atutua ni amɛfite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ akafite.

english: Why are my cabbage heads splitting open right before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa dani mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages split open when heavy rainfall or sudden watering follows a dry period. The inside leaves absorb water quickly and grow faster than the outer leaves can stretch, causing the head to burst.
ga: Cabbage mli gbalaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu ho trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni amɛdaraa oya fe bɔ ni baa ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe, ni no haa bulb lɛ mli gbalaa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my sweet peppers turn black and dry out before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egbiɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular, which prevents the roots from taking up calcium continuously from the soil.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni shɛɛɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: How does planting legumes like cowpeas help improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have special bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and convert it into a natural fertilizer in the soil, which feeds the next crop you plant in that same spot.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Akɛ enɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my vegetables grow weak and thin when I plant them under large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Vegetables need full sunlight to produce the food required for strong stems and good yields. Tree canopy shade starves them of light, causing them to stretch tall and thin toward the sun.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia aduawai koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha tsei ni wa kɛ yibiiwoo kpakpai. Tsei lɛ ahe hulutsoo lɛ haaa amɛná la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa hulu lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy. This often happens when the soil is depleted or when heavy rains wash fertilizer away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii je shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller crop yields every year even though I plant at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the soil every season to grow. If you keep planting on the same land without adding manure, fertilizer, or letting the soil rest, the earth becomes tired and runs out of nutrients for new crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji odu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni niyenii ni haa tsei heei baaná nii lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my corn cobs have missing kernels and empty spaces when I husk them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ mli kɛ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli beni mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Corn needs good wind and moderate weather to spread pollen from the top tassels to the silk on the cobs. If the weather is too dry or extremely hot during flowering, the pollen dies before fertilizing the grains, leaving empty gaps on the cob.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ shihilɛ ni sa he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛgbɛ ŋmãa ni jɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ anɔ kɛya siliki ni yɔɔ ŋtayaa lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Pollen baagbo dani ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Enɛ haa he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ baa ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, usually caused by sudden high heat or irregular watering. When the plant feels stressed, it drops flowers to save water and energy just to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiifee basaa. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Eshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere nu kɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛha ehe ahi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers under the ground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen from excess manure, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves above ground instead of sending food down into the roots to swell the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo jɛɔ ŋmeii babaoo mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai eŋɔlii lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ aya nɔ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are a common sign that tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies are hiding underneath and sucking sap from the leaf. As they drain the sap, the leaf loses shape and curls.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛji kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi ni amɛmiinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Beni amɛjie mliki lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, dark shade. If the canopy trees are too thick or weeds are overgrown, moisture stays trapped on the cocoa pods and helps the fungus spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni efɔ, ni eyɛ duŋ. Kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli eyi tsɔ loo jwɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Fɛ̃i lɛ shɛɔ kookoo lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Plantains have shallow roots near the soil surface. Microscopic worms called nematodes often attack these roots under the ground, weakening the tree's hold on the earth so it easily falls when heavy fruit grows.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutuaa nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, egbeeɔ shi oya beni aduawai lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of insects and rot so quickly in my store room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ eyi kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ oya yɛ mi-nitoohe lɛ?

english: If corn is put into storage before it is completely dried in the sun, moisture gets trapped inside the grain. Trapped moisture creates a warm, damp space that attracts weevils and causes mold to grow.
ga: Kɛji okɛ ŋmãa lɛ to dani ogbi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Moisture boteɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa he ko ni mli edɔɔ, ni mli ejɔ ni gbalaa ŋmeii ni ehaa ŋmeii daa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my farm help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen directly from the air and fix it into the soil. When the cowpea plant dies, that natural fertilizer stays in the ground for the next crop to feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ cowpea tso lɛ gbo Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni sɛɛ mli tsei lɛ aye.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have flooded the roots, preventing the plant from taking up essential nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise planting groundnuts or beans on my field before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans capture natural nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, acting as a free, natural fertilizer for high-demand crops like maize that follow them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ataoɔ waa tamɔ ŋmãa ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer to my crops immediately on the day I sow the seeds or wait a few weeks?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ dumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ loo ooomɛ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: It is usually best to wait until the seed sprouts and forms early roots, because a seed carries its own initial food supply, and young roots need to be active to absorb applied fertilizer without getting burned.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛtswa shishifãi oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ shishijee niyenii. Ni esa akɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ atsu nii koni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfata he lɛ ni ashãaa amɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees alongside my newly transplanted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that create necessary shade and keep the soil moist during the cocoa plant's vulnerable early stages.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kookoo tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb high off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso koni enyɛ ekwɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb to lift their leaves into direct sunlight, which allows the plant to produce maximum energy to feed and grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning dark black and shriveling up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This blackening is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in cool, excessively damp, and densely shaded conditions created by heavy rains.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ duŋ nɛɛ baa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ. ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upward and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on leaf sap, or by viruses transmitted to the plant by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do small insects bore holes into my harvested maize grains after I store them in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli beni mikɛto ŋmɔ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These insects are grain weevils that thrive inside stored crops that still contain moisture; thoroughly sun-drying your harvested maize until it is completely hard stops them from multiplying.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmaa ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lolo lɛ amli. Akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ gbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa aahu akɛ enyɛŋ eshwere.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become excessively hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when too much chemical fertilizer causes the plant to grow leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo haa tsei lɛ woɔ baai yɛ yibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efolɔɔɔ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open from expanding tubers below.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen or the plants are competing for nutrients. Adding well-timed nitrogen fertilizer or manure helps keep the leaves green so the maize ears can grow full.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tso lɛ miitswa akaŋ koni ena niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava tubers need well-drained soil to stay healthy. Excess water causes waterlogging, which suffocates the roots and encourages fungal diseases that make the tubers rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ nu shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: What makes my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa baaa?

english: Flower drop in peppers is usually caused by extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Consistent watering and balanced fertilizing help the plant turn flowers into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, chili ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ fɔfɔi amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why does my tomato crop get dark patches on the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ okadii diji yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Dark patches on the bottom of tomatoes are known as blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium intake. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps prevent this.
ga: Atsɛɔ hei ni yɔɔ diŋŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves get covered in tiny insects during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ yɛ kooloi bibii bibii lɛ? Ani aha nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be mli?

english: Dry weather creates ideal conditions for pests like aphids to multiply rapidly without rain to wash them off. Regular monitoring and using neem oil sprays help keep these insects under control.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aphids lɛ aya hiɛ oya ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ amɛ. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ kɛ nitsumɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that act as natural umbrellas, offering shade and keeping the soil moist for the cocoa seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha hulutsoo ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kookoo dumɔwui.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui?

english: Planting in rows gives every plant enough space, air, and sunlight to grow properly. It also makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly help my crops yield more food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛná niyenii babaoo?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Removing weeds ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Healthy soil is usually dark, crumbles easily, holds moisture without getting waterlogged, and contains earthworms. Adding compost or animal manure can improve poor or weak soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli ewo duŋ, efoɔ oya, ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu shwieee nɔ. ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up early before the tubers are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry early when attacked by fungal diseases or soil nematodes that damage the roots. Staking vines high off the ground and rotating crops helps prevent this problem.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ tutua amɛ. Wein tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and need partial shade to grow properly. Yellowing and burning edges usually mean they are getting too much direct sunlight, so planting shade trees or plantains alongside them helps shelter the leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo fioo koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni eshã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ eshɛ amɛhe tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi. No hewɔ lɛ amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa kɛbuɔ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the leaves inside my young maize plant's funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu kɛmiitsɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ a-funnel lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the tender leaves in the center of young maize plants. Catching them early by inspecting the leaves and applying appropriate control measures prevents them from destroying the central growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ gbɛi ni sa ni oootsɔ nɔ okudɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ obaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every single season when I plant it on the same farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa be mli beni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up large amounts of nitrogen from the soil every season. When you plant maize on the same plot repeatedly without resting the land or planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts, the soil becomes exhausted and produces smaller crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ, ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ loo oduŋ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmãa bibii baa.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so I do not waste it?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Bɔni afee ni mikafite lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing, typically around two weeks after germination and again during rapid growth. Applying fertilizer on dry soil or right before heavy rainfall can burn root systems or wash the nutrients away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ be mli ni edara oya lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know the exact time cassava is ready for harvesting so the roots don't turn woody?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-cassava lɛ esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ tsakeee tso?

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off. Leaving roots in the ground too long after maturity makes them fibrous, woody, and prone to rotting in wet soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi Shishifãi ni ashiɔ yɛ sũ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdara lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa amɛfeɔ tsɔi, tsei ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ mli.

english: Staking exposes the yam leaves to maximum sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture energy to grow big subterranean tubers. Keeping vines off the damp ground also prevents leaf diseases caused by humidity and soil contact.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsei ahe helai ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: You should limit the group to three stems of different ages: the main producing mother plant, one medium sucker, and one small shoot. Leaving too many suckers creates competition for water and soil nutrients, leading to small bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ kuu lɛ atsu nii kɛya tsei etɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi lɛ anɔ: tso ni ji nyɛ ni woɔ yibii titri lɛ; 1 ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kɛ 1 ni dalɛ ji bibioo. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo ni agbele mli lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba kɛha niyenii ni jɛɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii bibii

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems before making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by intense midday heat, dry soil, or a lack of key nutrients like phosphorus and calcium. Providing consistent soil moisture and organic mulch around the base helps retain the blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ phosphorus kɛ calcium ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Ni aaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ organic mulch aha nɔ. Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt suddenly during the hot afternoon even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is often caused by root damage or soil-borne bacterial diseases that block the plant's water transportation system inside the stem. Rotating pepper crops with non-related plants like maize helps clear the soil of these bacteria.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni efite loo helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. ni gbalaa tso lɛ nu gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Pepper ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe bɛ tsakpaa tamɔ ŋmãa baatsake lɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop curl tightly inward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to shrink their leaf surface area and reduce water evaporation during high heat. Covering the soil with dried leaves or straw retains moisture around the roots so the crop suffers less heat stress.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba baa lɛ nɔ ni amɛha nu ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni hulutsoo akagbala tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people always tell me to plant plantain on the same farm with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi yaa nɔ amɛkɛɛɔ mi akɛ midu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mikɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like small babies that burn easily under full sun. Plantain grows very fast and has big leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa plants shade and moisture so they can survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii tamɔ abifabii bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my harvested cocoa beans are properly dried and ready to be sold?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cocoa yibii ni mikpa lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Properly dried cocoa beans will crackle crisply when you squeeze a handful in your palm, and the inside of the bean will turn dark brown rather than purple, showing that all moisture has evaporated.
ga: Kokoo ŋmeii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatswa kɛji okɛ nine kome mimɔ onine mli, ni ŋmeii lɛ amli baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ efo.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and spoil so quickly before I can carry them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni egboɔ oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight, heat, and bruising during transport cause plantains to release gases that speed up ripening. Keeping them in a cool, shady spot and handling them gently helps them stay green longer.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, dɔlɛ, kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni baa yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ oya lɛ kpo. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ tee he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni okɛ amɛ tsu nii blɛoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the roots under the ground are small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing tall stem and leaves above the ground instead of growing big tuber roots under the ground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a duɔ tso nguanguahi ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Which direction should I point the buds when planting my cassava stem cuttings in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ akwɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: The small buds on the stem cutting should always point upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the plant to waste energy trying to bend its growth upward, which delays sprouting.
ga: Esa akɛ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ tsei niji ni afo lɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ tso lɛ da ni ehiɛ tsɔɔ shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Enɛ baaha kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: What happens to my soil if I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Cassava feeds heavily on soil nutrients. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot without adding fertilizer or giving the land a rest will exhaust the soil, leading to smaller yields over time.
ga: Cassava yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome ni awooo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ahaaa lɛ he ko ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee shoo. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I use manure from my chickens directly on my cassava and vegetable crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmei kɛ aduawai aŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Chicken manure is very strong and rich in nutrients, but using it raw can burn plant roots. It is best to dry it or mix it with rotted leaves for a few weeks before applying it to your crops.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã lɛ mli wa waa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli. Shi kɛ akɛ tsina ŋmei ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooogbi loo okɛ baai ni miifutu afutu mli otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛwo onibii amli.

english: Why do my crops grow faster in dark, loose soil than in hard, reddish soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tsuru nɔ lɛ?

english: Dark, loose soil usually contains decayed plants and organic matter that hold water and plant food well, while also letting roots spread easily and breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni etse ehe lɛ nɔ tsei amli nibii ni fiteɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii lɛ hiɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo ni amɛmuɔ.

english: Why is it dangerous to let weeds grow freely around my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, midumɔwui lɛ yɛ oshara.

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbours—they steal the soil water, sunlight, and plant food that your young crops need to grow strong, leaving your crop weak and small.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni duɔ ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Shi onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ni egbɔjɔ ni efee bibii.

english: Why is it better for me to grow different kinds of crops instead of just one single crop on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ makwɛ tsei babaoo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makwɛ tso henɔ kome pɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Growing multiple crops protects your family income if one crop fails due to bad weather or pests, and different plants use and restore soil nutrients in balanced ways.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oweku lɛ shika he kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahewɔ. Ni tsei srɔtoi kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛbaa ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry weather to save water. It is a natural survival trick to keep the root alive until the rains return, so your crop is usually not dead.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ ahi wala mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbooo.

english: Why are my young maize leaves looking light green or yellowish instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ji eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale green leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or organic manure will turn them dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni tomato diɛŋtsɛ ko kwraa bɛ ni miida lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. When it is too hot or dry, the plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in wet weather and heavy shade. Trimming tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei aniji koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the plant's sap, or by a plant virus. Spraying with neem oil or a suitable insecticide helps protect new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baai heei ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why am I finding small holes and sawdust-like material inside my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Ni nibii ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by stem borer caterpillars eating their way through the inside of the stalk. Applying a recommended control method into the leaf funnel early in the plant's growth prevents the caterpillars from weakening the stalk.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛboteɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ tsei lɛ tsu nii yɛ baai lɛ ashishijee be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɔjɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches of fruit during high winds. Supporting the stems with strong wooden props or planting them in sheltered groups helps keep them upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tsei lɛ asɛɛ loo adu amɛ yɛ kui ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight so their leaves can produce energy. Lifting the vines off the wet ground with stakes also prevents leaves from rotting and helps the tubers underground grow much bigger.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ aná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ, no hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing plenty of leafy vines but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cowpeas produce heavy leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas fix their own nitrogen from the air, so they need far less fertilizer than crops like maize.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea woɔ baai ni tsii yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ saa nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe tsei tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why is my rice crop falling down flat on the field just before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Rice stalks fall over, or 'lodge,' when the heads become heavy with grain and the stems are weakened by too much nitrogen or soft soil. Using balanced fertilizer and choosing strong-stemmed varieties prevents this.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ‘efoɔ’ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ eyi kɛ dumɔwui ni nitrogen babaoo loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ egbɔjɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii ni ahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni shishifãi lɛ wa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and small root systems that cannot handle intense heat. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains to keep the soil moist and protect them from burning until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Can I grow cassava on the same plot of land together with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: It is better to avoid planting cassava close to young cocoa because cassava roots spread aggressively and steal nutrients and water from the soil, which can stunt the cocoa tree's growth.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo bibii lɛ he. Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ kookoo tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my mature cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary foliage so the tree can direct its nutrients into growing bigger cocoa pods instead of extra leaves. It also opens up the branches so air and sunlight can flow through, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ahe tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi baafata he. Egbeleɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ hu koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Why should I cover the soil around my plantain stems with dry grass and leaf litter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, also known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, retains moisture during dry spells, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly rots to feed nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: This rot is called Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and shady conditions. You can reduce it by clearing weeds, pruning excess branches to let sunlight in, and removing the infected pods from the tree immediately.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ akɛ black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ okɛba shi kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni oootsi lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What causes the young shoots and small pods on my cocoa trees to develop dark spots and wither?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa? Yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo ni amɛgboɔ?

english: This damage is usually caused by small insects called mirids or capsids that suck the juice from tender parts of the tree. Spraying with recommended organic or approved chemical treatments during their peak breeding season protects the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids loo capsids, ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofai ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ yi yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ fɔɔ bii babaoo lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Weeds compete with your crops for essential soil nutrients and sunlight. Even with enough rainfall, the weeds will steal the food your crops need to stay healthy and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ hulu la. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ, Jwɛi hu baaju niyenii ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can support as pods. However, excessive flower drop can happen if the tree lacks water, if key soil nutrients are missing, or if there aren't enough tiny insects in the farm to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe ŋmeii. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ fe nine baanyɛ aba kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa pod is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Look at the color of the pod skin. Unripe pods are green or dark red, but when fully ripe, green pods turn a rich yellow and red pods turn orange-yellow, indicating the beans inside have fully developed.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni pod lɛ hiɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ. Pods ni eshɛko lɛ ji eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ. Shi kɛ́ ahoo kwraa lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Ni ŋmeii tsuru lɛ baatsake ni etsɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ edara kwraa.

english: How do I know if my soil is losing its richness before I plant my next crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiɛ edɔ dani madu tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If your previous crop leaves looked pale yellow instead of dark green, if plants grew very slowly, or if your harvest yield dropped compared to previous years, your soil is likely low on essential nutrients.
ga: Kɛji otsutsu tso lɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ Kɛji tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa Aloo kɛji okpamɔ lɛ eba shi kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa.
