english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and short roots that cannot survive direct hot sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping the air cool and moist around the seedlings until they grow strong enough to endure sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ afee fɛo Ha dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the bottom up while the stalk is still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to stay green and grow leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps the plant recover its bright green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ amɛ eŋɔli kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli tse ekoŋŋ.

english: Yes, direction matters a lot. Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the tiny buds on the stem pointing upward toward the sky so the shoots can sprout easily above ground and roots can push down into the dirt.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛtsɔɔmɔ he miihia waa. Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. ni shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers drop off without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or tiny insects sucking sap from the stems. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots and protecting plants from pests helps flowers set fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebɔleɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi kɛ tso lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tuber through their leaves using sunlight. When the vine climbs high on a stake, leaves catch more sunlight, leading to larger and healthier yam tubers at harvest time.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Beni wain tsei lɛ kwɔ kɛtee akulashiŋi kakadaji lɛ anɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking crinkled like old paper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ wolo momo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves. Spraying plants with diluted neem oil or soapy water helps clear these insects so new leaves grow out normal.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛwo mli loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. Koni ebaaha baai heei akwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa

english: Maize takes away heavy amounts of food from the soil, leaving it tired. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas draw nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground through their roots, naturally feeding the soil for the next season.
ga: Abele gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. let it be tiring Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why should I cut off some of the small plantain shoots growing around the main mother stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajieɔ nyɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ.

english: When too many small shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal water, soil food, and sunlight from the mother plant. Removing excess shoots leaves energy for the main plant to produce big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ plantains ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: It is best to water early in the morning while the weather is cool. Watering in the afternoon heat causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can soak it in.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu lɛ leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why do small black insects attack my harvested maize grains when I store them inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ beni mikɛtoɔ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These insects are grain weevils that lay eggs in grains that were not completely dried before storage. Drying your maize thoroughly in the bright sun until the kernels are very hard and storing them in airtight sacks stops weevils from multiplying.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui ni egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ he lɛ amli. Akɛ ŋmãa ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa ni akɛtoɔ vacuum kotokui amli koni ŋmãa akafee babaoo.

english: How do I calculate whether planting pepper this season will make me a profit or a loss?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ abu he akɔntaa kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni aduɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha sɛɛnamɔ loo sɛɛnamɔ aba?

english: To run your farm as a business, you need to add up all expected costs—like seeds, land clearing, fertilizer, labor, and transport—and compare that total against the expected yield and average selling price before planting.
ga: Bɔni afee ni otsu oŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ he nii Ehe miihia ni okɛ shika fɛɛ ni okpaa gbɛ, tamɔ dumɔwui, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, nitsumɔ, kɛ gbɛfaa afata he, ni okɛ nakai yibɔ fɛɛ lɛ ato yibiiwoo ni okpaa gbɛ kɛ jara ni akɛbaahɔɔ lɛ mlijaa mli dani odu.

english: Why do crop prices drop so low right when everyone in my community harvests their maize at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara baa shi nɛkɛ be mli ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When every farmer harvests together, the market gets flooded with maize. High supply with constant demand causes buyers to pay less; holding back dried grain until supply drops gets you a better price.
ga: Beni okwaafoi fɛɛ feɔ ekome kɛkpaa nii lɛ Jara lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ ŋmãa. Nibii ni akɛhaa babaoo kɛ nibii ni ataoɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo. Dumɔwui ni egbi ni oootsi ohe kɛyashi nɔ ni yɔɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ haa onáa jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly before I can get them to the city market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ fite oya dani mikɛtee maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Fresh tomatoes continue to breathe and ripen after harvest. Exposure to heat, sunlight, and rough handling causes bruising, which allows decay fungi to quickly destroy the fruit.
ga: Tomato hee yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekwɛɔ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Dɔlɛ, hulu la, kɛ nitsumɔ ni mli wa haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ aduawai lɛ oya.

english: How can I process my harvested cassava so it doesn't rot within three days of digging it up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ he nii koni ekafite yɛ gbii etɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni mifo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots naturally spoil fast once removed from the ground. Processing the roots into gari or high-quality flour removes moisture and stabilizes the starch, allowing it to stay fresh and sellable for months.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ shishifãi lɛ tsu nii ni afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa ashikishaŋ lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ehee ni anyɛɔ ahɔ̃ɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: How does proper drying of my cocoa beans affect the price buyers are willing to pay me?
ga: Te mi-kookoo yibii lɛ ni mikɛgbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaná jara ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo mi lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Drying cocoa beans correctly reduces moisture to safe levels, preventing mold and developing the desired chocolate flavor. Clean, well-dried beans meet high quality standards and prevent price deductions.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa amɛmli nu lɛ baa shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa ni ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ baa. Beans ni he tse ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ shishitoo mlai ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ ni etsiɔ jara ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stay small even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. While rain provides water, crops still need soil nutrients to build healthy green leaves and produce large cobs.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ lɛ haa nu moŋ, shi niyenii he miihia lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cocoa trees shed leaves during dry weather to protect themselves from losing too much water through evaporation, conserving energy to survive until the rains return.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ he. Too hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni onyɛ ohi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans in my field make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans work with helpful bacteria in the ground to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural food source for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: What standards make crops like yam or ginger good enough to be exported to international markets?
ga: Mɛɛ shishitoo mlai yɔɔ ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ sweet potatoes loo ginger afee nɔ ni hi bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaaya maŋsɛɛ jarayeli hei?

english: International buyers look for consistent size, zero chemical residues, no insect damage or skin cuts, and clean packaging that protects the produce from damage during long shipping journeys.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ jarayelɔi taoɔ dalɛi ni yaa nɔ daa. Tsofa ni eshwɛ bɛ mli Kooloi loo hewolo nɔ fitemɔ ko bɛ. kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni he tse ni buɔ nibii ni afee lɛ ahe koni akafite yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he ko shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do insects like fall armyworms attack my young maize crops so aggressively?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi-babi ŋmãa tsei lɛ waa lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms target tender, young maize leaves because they are soft and easy to digest, giving the pest quick energy to reproduce rapidly if not managed early.
ga: Fall armyworms lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ oya. Enɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfɔɔ bii oya kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: What is this hand pollination people are talking about, and how does it help my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛi miiwie nɔ ni nɛkɛ nine nɔ pollination nɛɛ ji lɛ he. Ni te eyeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Hand pollination means manually transferring pollen from one cocoa flower to another using a small brush or tool. This helps flowers turn into pods much faster and increases the number of cocoa pods your tree produces compared to relying on natural insects alone.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ niji jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ brɔsh loo dɛŋdade bibioo ko nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii oya kwraa. ni ehaa kookoo ŋmeii ni otso lɛ woɔ lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ. Kɛ akɛto adebɔɔ mli kooloi pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but natural pollinators like tiny midges only reach a small fraction of them. Unpollinated flowers naturally drop off after a day, which is why assisted pollination helps more flowers develop into harvestable pods.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa, tamɔ midges lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ fã bibioo ko pɛ he. Fɔfɔi ni awoko amɛmli lɛ baagbee shi yɛ gbi kome sɛɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni pollination yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛfeɔ pods ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ.

english: I see many ants crawling on my cocoa tree trunk; are they damaging my crop or helping it?
ga: Mina ŋmeii babaoo ni miiho yɛ mikoo tso lɛ nɔ. Ani amɛmiifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo amɛmiiye amɛmiibua lɛ?

english: Some ants protect cocoa trees by eating harmful bugs like capsids, while other ants spread mealybugs that cause diseases like Swollen Shoot. Identifying the specific type of ant helps you know whether to clear them or let them stay.
ga: Akpɔlɔi komɛi buɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids ni amɛyeɔ lɛ nɔ, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu buɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids ni amɛyeɔ lɛ nɔ. Mealybugs lɛ gbɛɔ helai ni kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ baa. Kɛ́ oyɔse ŋmei pɔtɛɛ ni ji ŋmei lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ole kɛji esa akɛ ojie lɛ loo oha eya nɔ.

english: What causes small insects to attack my young cocoa pods, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Pests like capsids attack cocoa pods to feed on the plant sap, leaving dark spots that spoil the pod. You can protect your trees by pruning thick branches to let in sunlight and applying approved pest protection at the right time of year.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ tutuaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛye tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu otso lɛ he kɛtsɔ niji ni mli tse ni ooofolɔ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ. koni eha hulu la lɛ akpɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa lɛ atsu nii yɛ afi lɛ mli bei ni sa amli.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting enough care to produce a strong yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ akwɛɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Healthy cocoa trees have deep green leaves without yellowing, smooth trunks, and regular flowering cycles. Good care involves regular pruning of dead wood, clearing weeds around the base, and keeping a balanced canopy of shade trees.
ga: Cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ, ni amɛfeee ŋmɔŋ, amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi daa. Nɔ ni fata kwɛmɔ kpakpa he ji niji ni egboi lɛ ni afolɔ daa. Ajieɔ jwɛi ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ahe ŋwɛitsu ni ja lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ

english: Why do my neighbor's cocoa trees yield so many more pods than mine even though our farms are side by side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔŋmɔji lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe moŋ?

english: Higher cocoa yields often come from adopting updated practices like artificial pollination, regular pruning, timely weeding, and using proper soil nutrients rather than just leaving the trees to grow naturally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni anáa babaoo lɛ jɛɔ nifeemɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. Tso lɛ mlifomɔ daa Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Yɛ tso lɛ ni oooha ekwɛ̃ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to prune my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or extra branches so air and sunlight can reach all parts of the tree. This prevents fungal diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to put energy into growing new flowers and pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwieɔ shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Koni akɛtsi fungal helai tamɔ black pods naa ni awo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ fɔfɔi kɛ pods heei.

english: How does having too much shade affect the way my cocoa trees produce pods?
ga: Te hulutsoo babaoo ni anáa lɛ saa bɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive shade keeps the farm too damp and dark, which encourages black pod disease and slows down pod growth. Balanced shade protects young cocoa from harsh sun while still letting in light for healthy flowering.
ga: Shade babaoo baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i tsɔ ni efee duŋ. Enɛ haa black pod hela baa ni ehaa black pods lɛ adalɛ baa shi. Susumɔ ni ja lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa amɛnáa fɔfɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lolo.

english: What practical benefits will I get if I join a cocoa farmers' cooperative in my community?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii maná kɛji mikɛ mihe wo kookoo okwaafoi akuu ko ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Joining a cooperative gives you access to training on new techniques like hand pollination, shared tools, subsidized farm inputs, and a stronger collective voice when selling your harvested cocoa beans.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo co-op mli lɛ, ehaa onáa tsɔsemɔ yɛ ŋaai heei amli, tamɔ nine-pollination. Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛyeɔ abuaa ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ gbee ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ kɛji oohɔ̃ɔ o-cocoa yibii ni okpa lɛ.

english: Why are extension officers encouraging us to move away from traditional cocoa farming methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔkpa blema kookoo lɛ dumɔ lɛ?

english: Modern practices like assisted pollination, proper shade control, and organized pest management allow farmers to harvest significantly more cocoa pods from the same plot of land compared to older, low-intervention methods.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nifeemɔi tamɔ pollination yeɔ ebuaa Shade nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛtsuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nii Enɛ haa okwaafoi nyɛɔ amɛkpaa kookoo ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ akɛto blema gbɛi ni akɛ he wooo mli fioo lɛ he

english: Why are modern hybrid cocoa seedlings able to bear fruit much faster than the old trees my parents planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrid dumɔwui baanyɛ awo yibii oya fe tsei momo ni mifɔlɔi du lɛ?

english: Modern hybrid seedlings are specially bred by agricultural scientists for early maturity, high yield, and disease resistance. While traditional cocoa trees took up to eight years to produce pods, modern varieties can start producing fruit in just two years with proper care.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi ekwɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ anɔ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara oya, amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛŋ helai ana amɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ blema cacao lɛ heɔ afii kpaanyɔ dani ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa moŋ, shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cacao henɔi lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii enyɔ pɛ mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better for me to buy improved cocoa seedlings instead of just planting seeds from my old cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe kookoo dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makwɛ dumɔwui kɛkɛ kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji momo lɛ amli

english: Seeds taken directly from old pods often lose their parent tree's best qualities and can inherit low yields or weak resistance. Certified nursery seedlings are carefully selected and bred to guarantee fast growth, early fruiting, and high pod production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii momo amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ laajeɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ ena amanehulu kɛjɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi loo shitee-kɛ-woo ni baa shi lɛ mli. Ahalaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛdara oya, amɛwo yibii mra ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: What causes some cocoa varieties to mature in two years while older types take many years?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo henɔi komɛi shwereɔ yɛ afii enyɔ mli yɛ be mli ni kookoo ni eda lɛ heɔ afii babaoo?

english: Early-maturing cocoa varieties have been genetically developed to establish root systems faster and trigger flowering early. Older varieties spend many years developing heavy foliage before they start flowering.
ga: Afee kookoo henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni yaa oya ni ewo fɔfɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ he hewalɛ. Henɔi ni edara lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ baai ni tsii dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why should I cut down my old cocoa trees to replant when they are still giving me a few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei momo koni madu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ? Akɛni kookoo tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii lolo hewɔ lɛ?

english: Old cocoa trees gradually lose their strength, yield fewer pods over time, and require more effort to maintain. Replanting your farm with new, fast-yielding varieties replaces unproductive trees with young, vigorous ones that will yield significantly higher harvests in a short time.
ga: Kookoo tso momo lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli fiofio Ebaafee nɔ ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ beni be hoɔ lɛ. Ni ebiɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo dani anyɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei heei ni woɔ yibii mra lɛ du ekoŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni darako ni he wa ni baawo yibii babaoo yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ atsake tsei ni wooo yibii lɛ.

english: Will replanting my farm with new seedlings give me more cocoa in the long run?
ga: Ani dumɔwui heei ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha maná kookoo babaoo yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, new cocoa seedlings produce far more pods per acre than aging trees. Although replanting takes effort, the high yield from modern seedlings within just a few years far outweighs the low production of old trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo dumɔwui heei woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ acre kome mli fe tsei momoi. Shi kɛlɛ, dumɔ ekoŋŋ biɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ. Shi yibii babaoo ni jɛɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui amli baa yɛ afii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ feɔ tsei momo ni woɔ yibii fioo kwraa lɛ anɔ.

english: How many years does a new cocoa tree normally take before I can start harvesting pods?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko jeɔ eshishifãi lɛ akpamɔ shishi?

english: With old cocoa types, harvesting used to take five to eight years. However, with modern fast-growing seedlings and good farm management, you can begin harvesting pods in about two years.
ga: Kɛha kookoo momo lɛ Nikpamɔ heɔ afii enumɔ kɛyashi kpaanyɔ, shi kɛlɛ, kɛ dumɔwui ni daa oya kɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ kpakpa. Obaanyɛ oje pods lɛ akpamɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii enyɔ mli.

english: Why do some cocoa farms start producing pods very early while others take a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi jeɔ ŋmɔji amli ŋmɔji lɛ afeemɔ shishi oya waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ be babaoo lɛ?

english: Early production depends on the type of seedling planted and how well the farmer cares for the land. Using improved seedlings alongside proper weeding, pruning, and soil care allows plants to produce fruit much earlier than neglected old-style farms.
ga: nibii ni afeɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee Edamɔ dumɔwui ni adu lɛ ahenɔi kɛ bɔ ni okwaafonyo lɛ kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehaa lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ fataa he. ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa tsei woɔ yibii oya fe blema ŋmɔji ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: What basic care do my young cocoa seedlings need so that they bear fruit quickly?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee kwɛmɔ he hiaa mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ koni ewo yibii oya?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade from companion crops like plantains, regular weeding to remove nutrient competition, protection from harsh sunlight, and proper water and soil nutrition during their first two years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa koni ajie niyenii mli nibii ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ. Hebuu kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni sa he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How does learning modern farming techniques help me get a better cocoa harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he ŋaai ni mikaseɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni mináa kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Applying modern techniques like proper spacing, timely pruning, weed control, and fertilizer use ensures your seedlings grow without stress, enabling them to start fruiting early and produce healthy pods.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai tamɔ gbɛ ni sa nɔ atsu nii Jwɛi ni afoɔ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni odumɔwui lɛ daraa ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I plant plantains alongside my new cocoa seedlings during the first few years?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli?

english: Yes, planting plantains with young cocoa provides vital shade to protect the young seedlings from hot sunlight. It also gives you food and income while you wait for your cocoa trees to begin harvesting in two years.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bibii duɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika hu yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ aje shishi akpa yɛ afii enyɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my okra plants falling off before any okra pods grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi okra tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani okra ŋmɔji lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Okra plants drop flowers when they experience stress from irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding well-rotted manure helps the plant retain flowers and form pods.
ga: Rosella tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni efee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn yellow during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often a natural reaction to conserve water during high heat, but yellowing can mean a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies. Providing light shade and controlling pests with neem oil spray helps keep the plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni baa kɛjɛɔ nu ni ahiɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ mli. Shi ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ atsɔɔ helai ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Ni akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ ni akudɔɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do holes appear in the leaves of my garden egg plants after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates ideal conditions for leaf-eating beetles and caterpillars to multiply and feed on tender leaves. Dusting wood ash on wet leaves or spraying diluted neem tree seed extract helps stop insect pests from damaging the leaves.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ koni amɛfɔ ni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Tso mli sũ ni akɛshwieɔ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ loo ni akɛ neem dumɔwui ni ajie mli nu lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating the dark green inner leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai ni ji eŋɔli lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks the growing tip of maize plants. Applying a handful of clean sand mixed with wood ash directly into the plant funnel early in the morning can suffocate and kill the caterpillars.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmeii tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã ni he tse fioo ni akɛ tso sũ efutu mli lɛ wo dumɔwu lɛ ŋã lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because they cannot breathe when water stays too long around the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away quickly and keeps the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya. ni ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow lots of green leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam plants grow too many leaves at the expense of tubers when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when vines are not staked properly. Proper staking allows light to reach all leaves, signaling the plant to send energy down to grow bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ, ni amɛyitsei lɛ laajeɔ kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ wain tso lɛ shishifãi efɔɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ leɔ akɛ ebaatsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and burn easily under strong sun and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to cocoa seedlings creates temporary shade and holds moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily get weakened by soil pests like banana weevils or soft wet soil. Heap extra soil around the base of the plant stem and support heavy fruiting stems with wooden props to keep them standing.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ banana ŋmeii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ oya. Okɛ sũ kroko abɔle tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Maize drains specific nutrients from the soil every season, leaving the land tired. Rotating your crop by planting legumes like beans, groundnuts, or cowpeas after maize puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and restores its strength.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, etɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo tsina ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni oha ehewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing very bushy foliage, but making very few pod flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii ashishifãi fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ?

english: Cowpeas produce too many leaves and few flowers when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen, so they only require small amounts of phosphorus fertilizer to produce plenty of flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpea woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ ni fɔfɔi fioo pɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsɔ. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔsfɔs ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ he hiaa koni fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba.

english: What is the difference between growing yellow corn and white corn on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: White corn is mostly used for local staple foods like kenkey and banku, making it popular with food traders, while yellow corn is widely sought after by poultry and livestock feed producers. Selecting the right color depends on who your target buyers are in the local market.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa yɛŋ tsuɔ nii titri kɛhaa maŋ lɛ mli niyenii tamɔ kenky kɛ banku. ni haa niyenii jarayelɔi lɛ sumɔɔ waa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛi ni feɔ kooloi kɛ kooloi aniyenii lɛ biɔ ŋmãa ni ji yellow ŋmãa babaoo. Su ni sa ni ooohala lɛ damɔ mɛi ni otaoɔ amɛhe yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ anɔ.

english: Does yellow corn mature faster or yield more than white corn?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ lɛ daa oya loo ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmãa yɛŋ?

english: Growth speed and yield depend on whether you plant an improved hybrid seed rather than the color of the grain. Both white and yellow corn can produce high yields and mature quickly if you buy certified improved seeds suited to your region.
ga: Bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ daa oya kɛ yibiiwoo lɛ damɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ fe dumɔwui lɛ ahe su. Abɛi yɛŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ fɛɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ oya kɛji ohe dumɔwui ni asaa he ni awo he odaseyeli ni sa kɛha okpokpaa lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right crop variety so that market traders buy my harvest quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tso henɔ ni sa koni jarayelɔi lɛ anyɛ ahe minibii lɛ oya?

english: Before planting, talk to local traders or extension officers about what consumers are asking for in terms of taste, grain size, and color. Planting high-demand varieties ensures your crop sells fast without sitting in storage.
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, okɛ mɔ ni hɔ̃ɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ loo mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ agba nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ yɛ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ, dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ, kɛ amɛhe su he. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni ataoɔ waa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ haa onibii lɛ hɔ̃ɔ oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛto he ko ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe.

english: Why do buyers offer me a low price even when I fill a very large bag with corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa mi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa kotoku agbo ko wo mli moŋ?

english: Buyers price crops based on quality, moisture levels, and grain type, not just volume. If the corn is damp, damaged by insects, or a variety consumers dislike, buyers lower their price to cover their own risk of spoilage.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ damɔ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ nɔ amɛtsɔɔ amɛjara. Humidity level kɛ dumɔwui ahenɔi Jeee bɔ ni amɛfa ha lɛ pɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ ni kooloi bibii efite Aloo mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ateŋ mɛi babaoo sumɔɔɔ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baajie jara lɛ shi koni amɛkɛwo oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ nɔ ko baafite lɛ he nyɔmɔ.

english: Why do some small-sized corn varieties sell for higher prices than large cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa bibii komɛi kɛ jara ni wa fe ŋmãa wuji lɛ?

english: Market value is driven by end-use quality, like grain sweetness or milling texture, rather than cob size. Specialized or sweet varieties often fetch higher prices per bag even if the cobs appear smaller.
ga: Sui ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ naagbee, tamɔ bɔ ni ŋmaa lɛ ŋɔɔ loo bɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ ji nɔ ni tsirɛɔ jarayeli jara. fe cob size Specialty loo sweet henɔi lɛ fɔɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ ni akɛwoɔ kotoku kome mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ cob lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eji bibioo moŋ.

english: How does drying my harvested corn thoroughly help me get better market prices?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ni mikɛaagbi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Properly dried corn does not rot, mold, or attract damp-loving pests during storage. This allows you to hold your grain safely until market prices rise, rather than rushing to sell wet grain cheaply.
ga: Abɛi ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fiteŋ, ehiɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ loo egbalaŋ kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛba be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ odumɔwui lɛ toɔ shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ jara nɔ jara lɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee oya ni okɛ dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni waaa nɔ lɛ

english: Why do insects damage my corn after I store it in woven bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-abele lɛ beni mikɛwo mama kotoku mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects or their eggs often enter the cobs while still in the field, or they crawl into standard woven bags through tiny gaps. Storing well-dried corn in airtight hermetic bags suffocates pests and keeps your grain safe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi loo ŋmeii boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Aloo amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ kotokui ni akpɛ́ ni afɔɔ feemɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ wo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eye ebua ni oŋmãa lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Will leaving my corn cobs to dry on the plant in the field harm the crop?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni ashiɔ koni egbi yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Leaving corn in the field too long exposes it to rain, birds, rodents, and field pests that lay eggs in the grain. It is safer to harvest once mature and dry the cobs on a clean tarp or raised platform.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaagbala nugbɔ, okpoi, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaakpa ŋmeii lɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ ni agbi yɛ tarp ni he tse loo kpoku ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I save seeds from my white corn harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛŋ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Saving seed from hybrid corn varieties causes yield to drop significantly in the second generation. Buying fresh, certified seeds each season guarantees strong plant growth and heavy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why does my corn crop turn yellow and produce small cobs during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii miiwo lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the corn lacks nitrogen fertilizer or the soil is waterlogged. Corn needs enough nutrients and well-drained soil during its early growing stage to form large, full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia ŋmãa yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmãa wuji ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the plants do not get enough water, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which makes the plant focus on leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai lɛ.

english: Why is my cowpea crop producing plenty of green leaves but no pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen in the soil. If you give them extra nitrogen fertilizer, the plant will spend all its energy growing leaves instead of flowering and producing pods.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ha Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pods baa lɛ

english: Why do my cabbage heads crack open right before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaabe yitsei lɛ fãa dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split open when heavy rains or sudden watering happen after a dry period. The inside of the cabbage absorbs water quickly and grows faster than the outer leaves can stretch.
ga: Kaabeji yitsei lɛ baatswa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu ho trukaa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Kaabeji lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni edaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up into tight little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap underneath the leaves, or by a leaf-curl virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ hela ko ni haa ŋmeii yɛji shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The young worms hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant and chew through the tender leaves before they open up.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ. Kplukai bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋshɔi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and wet on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy seasons when moisture is high and there is too much shade around the cocoa trees.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ.

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up at the end of the rainy season, showing that the plant has stopped growing.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting just two days after I dig them out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ beni mikɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ tsu nii lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a natural thick skin like yams, so once they are cut from the stem and exposed to air, chemical reactions inside the root cause it to spoil rapidly within 48 to 72 hours.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ hewolo ni mli tse tamɔ sweet potato. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi ni akɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ Chemical reactions ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ haa amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow from the middle outward when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Applying well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ kɛ́ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up tight during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up during extreme afternoon heat to protect themselves from losing too much moisture into the air. If the leaves unwind when the evening cools down, it is just the plant protecting itself, but keeping the soil moist helps reduce this stress.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ he. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni amɛhe jɔɔ lɛ Eji tso ko kɛkɛ ni buɔ ehe he. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha nɔnyɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava right next to my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ mi-baby ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cassava develops very thick roots and dense leafy branches that aggressive steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from neighboring crops. Planting them too close causes the shorter maize to starve and produce tiny ears.
ga: Yucca shishifãi ni mli tse waa kɛ niji ni mli tse ni kɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmãa ni yɔɔ kuku lɛ ni ená toi bibii.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop season ends, that trapped nitrogen stays behind to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience sudden shock, such as very hot and dry soil, irregular watering, or excessive chemical fertilizer. Consistent light watering and shade help the plant hold onto its flowers so fruits can form.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe trukaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa, ni egbi. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Nu kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: What causes black spots to spread across my cocoa pods during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods during wet weather are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and shaded environments. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds lets sunlight dry out the farm and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulutsoo. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ajie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulu la akashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my crops wither so fast when the rain stops for only a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Plants wither quickly if their roots stay shallow near the surface, which happens when hard soil prevents deep root growth or when organic compost is missing. Adding compost acts like a sponge that holds rainwater underground for roots to drink during dry spells.
ga: Tsei baagbi oya kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni wa tsi shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ adalɛ naa. aloo kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ laaje Kompost ni akɛfataa he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ spunji, ni ebuaa nugbɔ nu naa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni shishifãi lɛ anu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell when my cassava roots are fully grown under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem with just a cluster of green leaves at the top. You can gently scrape away topsoil near one plant to confirm the tubers are thick before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yuccas lɛ daa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Tso lɛ tso lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni eshwɛ. Baai eŋɔlii akuu ko pɛ eshwɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ blɛoo ajie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ eko lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛma nɔ mi akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ dani akpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally adapted over hundreds of years to survive in harsh conditions and grab water and nutrients faster than cultivated domestic seeds. Clearing weeds while your crops are young prevents the weeds from robbing your farm's food supply.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ shia lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaju niyenii ni jɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why did many of the maize seeds I buried in the ground fail to come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mifu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to shoot up if they were planted too deep for the weak shoot to push through, if the ground was too dry to awaken the seed, or if soil insects ate them before they sprouted. Planting seeds at finger-depth in moist soil gives them the best start.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni enyɛŋ etswa dumɔwui lɛ Aloo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ amɛ dani dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nine mli lɛ haa amɛjeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are too old and need to be replaced?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni atsake amɛ?

english: When cocoa trees reach around 30 to 40 years old, their trunks and roots become weak, causing them to produce far fewer pods and become susceptible to diseases. Replacing old trees with fresh seedlings restores strong farm yields over time.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ko eye aaafee afii 30 kɛyashi 40 lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa, ni helai nyɛɔ emɔɔ lɛ oya. Tsei momo ni akɛ dumɔwui heei tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ mli waa ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their early years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when rain does not fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks moisture, preventing the roots from absorbing essential nutrients like nitrogen. The plant steals nutrients from its lower leaves to keep the top alive, turning them yellow.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Tsei juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving them proper spacing allows each crop to grow strong and bear bigger fruits.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the field.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa ŋmɔji amli.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects. Stress forces the plant to drop its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ faaa lɛ Haomɔ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing light patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny whitefly insects transmitting the Cassava Mosaic Virus. The virus prevents the leaves from making food properly from sunlight, which stunts root growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii yɛŋ bibii ni gbɛɔ cassava mosaic hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Virus lɛ haaa baai lɛ ahoo jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: How does putting animal manure in the soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure releases nutrients like nitrogen into the soil over time and improves the soil's power to hold onto water, providing stable food and moisture for crop roots.
ga: Muji jieɔ niyenii mli nibii, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ aya hiɛ Ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa tsei shishifãi.

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and aggressively steal the nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crops need to produce healthy yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. ni ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant in the farm fail to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if the soil is too dry, if they are planted too deep, or if the seeds were old or damaged. Healthy seeds need moisture, warm soil, and the correct depth to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji adu mli tsɔ loo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ loo efite Dumɔwui kpakpai he miihia ŋmɔtɔ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ mlibotemɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need to grow strong. When the soil lacks nitrogen or gets washed out by heavy rains, the plant takes whatever food it has left from its lower leaves to feed new growth, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ lɛ. Tsei kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ baa beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Every crop pulls specific nutrients out of the soil to grow. Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains those specific nutrients faster than the soil can recover, while also allowing maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Enɛ baaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ atsɔ oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsake. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under the harsh direct sun. Plantains grow very quickly and produce large leaves that create a cool, shaded environment, protecting the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do rubber trees need so much space between them when I am planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ rɔbɔt tsei lɛ aná gbɛ babaoo yɛ amɛteŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ lɛ?

english: Rubber trees grow wide branches and deep root systems to produce high amounts of latex liquid. If they are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another, reducing the total latex yield.
ga: Rɔba tsei lɛ feɔ amɛniji ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛkɛfeɔ latɛs babaoo. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni baai lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, latɛs ni afeɔ lɛ fɛɛ ba shi.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow so tall with big green leaves, but the tubers under the ground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen from soil or fertilizer without enough potassium, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in their root tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before growing into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ anɔkwa tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or dry stress. The plant treats flowering as a secondary task and drops the flowers to save water and keep its main stem alive during tough conditions.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ he. Tsei buɔ fɔfɔii ahe nitsumɔ akɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ ni baa ni amɛjieɔ fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is a plant's natural self-defense mechanism. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to conserve moisture, and the leaves usually relax once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Ni baai lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe be mli ni gbɛkɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the plant's roots are developed enough to take up nutrients, usually a few weeks after sprouting, and again when the plant starts flowering or building fruit. Applying fertilizer too early wastes it because young roots cannot absorb it yet.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu beni tso lɛ jeɔ fɔmɔ loo ewoɔ yibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaafite ejaakɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my crop roots with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, acts like a blanket over the soil. It blocks the sun from drying out the earth quickly, keeps the soil cool, and slows down the growth of weeds around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsĩɔ hulu la naa, ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa jwɛi ni bɔleɔ onibii lɛ ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow weak and thin even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors; their fast-growing roots steal food nutrients and fertilizers from the soil before your crops can reach them, leaving your main crops undernourished regardless of rainfall.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Eshishifãi ni daa oya lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii ni faaa yɛ onibii titrii lɛ amli lɛ baa ekɔɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that create living shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moist during its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow strong. Rain often washes nitrogen out of the soil, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa Nugbɔ lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is making holes in the leaves of my maize plants and leaving tiny waste inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ miifee bu ni amɛshiɔ gunk fioo ko yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the central leaf funnel of maize to feed on soft leaves. Catching them early with appropriate bio-pesticides or neem extract helps protect the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei mli ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ koni eye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ bio-insecticide loo neem mli nu ni sa lɛ nɔ lɛ ebuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so I can get more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Giving them proper space lets each plant grow strong and produce larger, healthier yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edaa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the rainy season becomes very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates high humidity, which helps a fungal disease called Black Pod spread fast across cocoa trees. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm and reduce pod rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa cacao tsei lɛ amli oya. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaa pod ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground if the heavy rains stay for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When rain leaves the soil waterlogged for days, the roots choke from lack of oxygen and decay due to rotting fungi.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce fewer yields even if I water and fertilize my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal food, water, and sunlight away from your main crops. If weeds stay on the farm, your crops remain starved and cannot produce full yields.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli. Kɛji jwɛi tee nɔ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaya nɔ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo amɛyibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass around the base of my crops during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi mashwã mitsei lɛ ashishi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that shades the soil. It stops sunlight from drying out the ground rapidly, keeping moisture around plant roots much longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ahiɔ nu mli yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines produce tubers by catching sunlight through their leaves. Staking the vines off the ground lifts the leaves into the light and airflow, allowing the plant to generate big, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Wein tso lɛ ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa enaa baai lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains specific nutrients out of the soil and builds up maize-specific pests and diseases in that area. Rotating with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ he yɛ nakai kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa Kɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: What kind of crops can I plant along my farm borders to mark my land boundaries permanently?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he koni makadi mishikpɔŋ lɛ husui lɛ daa?

english: You can plant long-lasting boundary trees or shrubs like Jatropha, cashew, or teak along your borders. They stay in place for decades, clearly marking your land limits so neighbors do not encroachment on your field.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei loo tsei bibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ jatropha kɛ cashew ŋmeii. loo teak yɛ ohusu lɛ he. Amɛhi shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ nɛ. Kɛtsɔ husui ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni oootsɔɔ mli faŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni akutsoŋbii akabote he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Is it better to burn dry weeds after clearing my land or leave them on the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaashã jwɛi ni egbi lɛ beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ loo abaashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving cleared weeds on the soil as mulch is better than burning. As they decay, they feed nutrients back into the soil, keep the ground cool, and prevent rain from washing away your topsoil.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ehi fe ni oooshã amɛ. Kɛ amɛgboi lɛ Ebaaye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni otsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafɔ osũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in bright sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, sheltering young cocoa from intense heat and conserving soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same land, or will they fight each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo béi baaba?

english: You can plant them together safely. Maize grows quickly and is ready for harvest in a few months, while cassava grows slower and takes over the space after the maize has already been cleared.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome shweshweeshwe. Abɛi daa oya ni eshɛɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eŋɔ he ko beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do leguminous plants like beans help other crops grow better in my field?
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa tsei krokomɛi ni amɛdaraa. Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Beans and peanuts work like natural fertilizer factories. They capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the surrounding soil for nearby crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔhei. Amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay tiny when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete underground for light, water, and nutrients. Giving cassava enough space allows each root stem room to swell and form big tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ oha o-cassava lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli alɛɛ ni efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow maize leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Even with enough water, crops need proper soil nutrients to maintain dark green, healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po lɛ, Dumɔwui hu he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa koni amɛha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get too hot or experience sudden water stress. Giving plants light shade and regular water during peak hot weather stops the flowers from dropping.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo ena nu he haomɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo ha tso lɛ ni oha lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every time I plant maize on the same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize draws heavy nutrients from the exact same depth of soil each season. Switching to cover crops or legumes like cowpeas every couple of seasons allows the soil to rebuild its natural fertility.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ atsake koni akɛha ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii daa bei fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam mounds wash away whenever heavy rains hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ ni naa wa baa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain easily breaks down bare soil mounds on sloping land. Planting cover crops like Mucuna or building mounds across the slope prevents rainwater from carrying your soil away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa gɔji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ Mucuna ni aduɔ loo gɔji ni amaa yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ baatsi nugbɔ nu naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves are tender and lose moisture quickly. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that keep the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa establishes strong roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ ji bibii ni amɛmli shwieɔ oya. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi hulutsoo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. yɛ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa seedlings very close together so I can fit more trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting trees too close together causes them to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough food and air circulation, which reduces disease spread and leads to higher overall pod yields.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ baa shi ni ehaa pod yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Dropping leaves is a cocoa tree's natural defense mechanism against drought. The tree loses most of its water through its leaves, so shedding them helps conserve precious moisture inside the trunk and roots until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he. Tsei fiteɔ amɛnu lɛ babaoo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but most of them fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi akpe lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support. Only a small fraction get pollinated by tiny insects like midges; if the tree is stressed by drought or poor soil, it intentionally sheds extra flowers to save energy for the pods it can feed.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii pɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ lɛ pollin; Kɛji hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii miigba tso lɛ naa lɛ Tsei lɛ baajɛ amɛtsui mli amɛfo fɔfɔii lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my mature cocoa trees turning pale yellow even when we are getting enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni eda lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the tree is hungry and lacks essential nutrients, especially nitrogen, in the soil. Rain provides water, but the tree also needs nutrients from fertile soil or fertilizer to stay green and produce pods.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ ni niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli bɛ. Nitrogen titri: Nugbɔ haa nu, shi tsei hu he miihia niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii amli loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and rot when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which thrives in cool, wet, and dark conditions. Raindrops bounce the fungus from the soil onto low pods, so keeping the farm weeded and pruned helps air and sunlight dry out the pods and prevent infection.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ekpa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ agbi ni ekɛ helai akabote mli.

english: Why is a bushy green plant growing on my cocoa tree branches causing that branch to dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi kookoo nine lɛ nɔ lɛ miiha nine lɛ miigbi lɛ?

english: That plant is likely mistletoe, a parasite that attaches its roots directly into the cocoa branch to steal water and food. Because it starves the host branch, that part of the cocoa tree becomes weak and stops fruiting until you physically cut the parasite away.
ga: Ekolɛ tso nɛɛ ji mistletoe. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ shishifãi kpãa kookoo niji ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. ejaakɛ ehaa tso nine ni hiɛ ka lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ No hewɔ lɛ cacao tso lɛ fã ko bɛ hewalɛ ni ebaakpa yibiiwoo kɛyashi obaafolɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: Why does cutting off healthy-looking branches actually help my cocoa tree produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary or overcrowding branches that block sunlight and waste the tree's food. Opening up the tree allows sunlight to reach the inner trunk, improves airflow to stop diseases, and directs energy straight into growing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni egbɔ fe nine ni tsiɔ hulu la naa ni efiteɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ agbele tso lɛ naa lɛ, hulu la lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ mligbɛ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni ekpa helai ni etsɔɔ hewalɛ mli kɛyaa pod agbo ko mli

english: How can I tell exactly when a cocoa pod is mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color clearly—green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. If you tap a ripe pod, it makes a hollow sound because the seeds inside have loosened from the outer husk.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su yɛ faŋŋ mli. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuji loo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei. Kɛ́ ota ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ he lɛ, ebaafee tamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli ejɛ mli.
