english: Why must I heap my freshly harvested cocoa beans under plantain leaves for several days before drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa ehee lɛ toɔ plantain baai ashishi gbii babaoo dani mikɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering wet beans triggers natural fermentation, a process that kills the seed so it won't sprout and creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color inside the bean. Drying beans immediately without fermentation leaves them bitter and low in quality.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ha ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni gbeɔ dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ hu akafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow from the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants need to make leaves green and grow strong. Applying the right nitrogen-rich fertilizer early helps the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra ni sa lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on the same nutrients in the soil every season, eventually starving the ground. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like beans or groundnuts puts essential nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ babaoo daa be. and eventually starves the land. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow much faster than my crops right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer feeds any plant it touches, including weeds. If you do not clear the weeds before applying fertilizer, the weeds will steal the nutrients meant for your crops and choke them.
ga: Fertilizer haa tso fɛɛ tso ni ekɛkpeɔ lɛ niyenii. Jwɛi fata he. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni efoɔ amɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving tall trees like shade trees or planting plantains provides necessary shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei kakadaji tamɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni adu lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning extra branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds under the trees helps keep the pods dry.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ duŋ kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni afoɔ koni hulu la babaoo abote mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling tightly and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni ehaa tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Spraying neem oil or recommended organic treatments early controls these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ haa mra. Abaanyɛ akudɔ kooloi bibii nɛɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when the weather is extremely hot or when water supply drops suddenly. Watering plants consistently at the base helps them hold onto flowers and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ba shi trukaa. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ daa yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains fall for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up around them because they cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu ni ekã shi ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches, especially during strong winds. Supporting the heavy stem with a strong wooden prop or bamboo pole prevents them from toppling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ asɛɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fi tsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with wooden stakes instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsei lɛ afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the sunlight to manufacture food for the root. Staking the vines keeps them off the hot ground and catches maximum sunlight, leading to much larger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii amɛha shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tsei lɛ wo tso mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛkashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ, ni ebaaha hulu la ni tsoɔ waa aba amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara babaoo baa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam plants instead of letting the vines creep on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ tso mli moŋ fe ni mahã wain tsei lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and stay dry. Sunlight gives the leaves power to grow large underground tubers, while keeping them off the damp soil prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbi. Hulu la haa baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha tsei lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ koni helai ni baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape pattern?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen runs low, the plant takes whatever food is left in its older, bottom leaves and sends it to the growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ heɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ ni ekɛmajeɔ baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and twisting tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking juice from the underside of leaves and passing along a virus, which distorts leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛkɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baa. ni gbalaa baai lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to protect itself. By getting rid of its leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation and stays alive by conserving moisture in its roots until the rains return.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni ekɛbu ehe he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei baaha nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni amɛha wala ahi shi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ

english: What is causing ragged holes in the middle whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The moth lays eggs on the leaves, and when the caterpillars hatch, they crawl into the center growing point of the plant to feed on the tender young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fall armyworm caterpillar, ni ji ŋmei ko ni woɔ ewui yɛ baai anɔ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛshwereɔ kɛyaa hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods develop dark brown spots that spread and turn the whole pod black?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ediŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. When moisture sits on the pods without drying out, the fungus spreads quickly through water droplets.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ duŋ mli, beni fɛ̃i ta ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni egbiɛɛ amɛ lɛ. Muji gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu mli ŋmeii amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when plants experience stress from irregular watering. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination inside the blossom, causing the unpollinated flower to die and drop off.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts together with my grain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adu ŋmei?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when the rain is too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need to breathe air that sits between soil particles. When heavy rains flood the soil for too long, oxygen gets cut off, suffocating the roots and causing soil fungi to rot the tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni cassava shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hoɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ baafo ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agboi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key food plant roots take from the soil. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green so the plant can produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei shishifãi jieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my cowpea farm produce plenty of green leaves but very few beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Cowpeas make their own nitrogen in the soil. If you add too much extra fertilizer rich in nitrogen, the plant uses all its energy to grow big leaves instead of making flowers and bean pods.
ga: Cowpeas feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ wo mli tsɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the ground, but groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and fix it back into the soil, leaving the land fertile for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Extremely high heat dries out tomato pollen, preventing the flowers from being fertilized. When flowers cannot form seeds, the plant drops them to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha tomato pollen lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo fɔmɔ Beni fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui Tsei shwieɔ dumɔwui amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my okra plants grow tall and thin with very few fruits when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Okra needs full sunlight all day to make food. When shaded by trees, the plant stretches upward trying to reach the sun, wasting energy on tall stems instead of growing okra pods.
ga: Okra needs full sun throughout the day to cook. Beni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ hulu lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni afiteɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ yɛ okra tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my yam field is getting too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ fa tsɔ?

english: When soil stays soaked in water, yam leaves turn yellow and wilt because roots cannot breathe. Underground, the yam tubers will stop growing and begin to rot and smell foul.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ Sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the undersides of leaves. Spraying with neem water or insecticidal soap stops these pests before they ruin the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ehaa kooloi nɛɛ kpaa tso lɛ dani amɛkpãtãa tso lɛ hiɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads in cool, wet shade. Pruning tall shade trees and clearing overgrown weeds lets sunlight in to dry out the pods and prevent the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shĩa mli hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Tsei kakadaji ni afoɔ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa kɛ jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ baaha hulu la lɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni etsi ŋmeii anaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small when I plant the stems very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii waa beni adu tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need room to expand under the ground. When stems are planted too close, their roots compete with each other for water and soil nutrients, resulting in small, woody tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia he ko ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ adu tso lɛ tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso bibioo ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo baa.

english: Why do armyworms attack my young maize field instead of the cassava next to it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ emasɛi lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer grass-family plants like maize because the leaves are soft and easy for caterpillars to chew, whereas cassava leaves contain bitter fluids that deter caterpillars.
ga: Autumn cutworms sumɔɔ jwɛi tamɔ ŋmãa ejaakɛ baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaaye. yɛ be mli ni nu ko ni mli edɔ ni tsiɔ ŋmeii anaa lɛ yɛ ŋmei baa lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant my plantains in straight lines instead of just planting wherever there is space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ he ni gbɛ yɔɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines leaves open walking paths through your farm, making daily work like weeding, spraying, and harvesting much easier without damaging your crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa gbɛ ni agbele naa kɛtsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa daa gbi nitsumɔi tamɔ jwɛi shwiemɔ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni efiteee oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does leaving proper spacing between my plantain trees help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Proper spacing prevents plants from competing with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, allowing each plantain tree to grow strong and produce larger bunches.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsei akaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko adara waa ni amɛdara ni amɛfee kui wuji.

english: Why do plantains grow poorly when they are planted too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When overcrowded, plantains shade each other out and fight for soil nutrients, which stunts their growth and delays fruit production.
ga: Kɛji gbɔmɛi fa tsɔ lɛ, Plantains lɛ feɔ amɛhe shade ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haaa dalɛ aya hiɛ ni ehaa aduawai ni anáa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: What will happen to my plantain suckers if I rush or take shortcuts while transplanting them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ oyaiyeli tsu nii loo mikɛ gbɛ kukuji tsu nii beni mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Rushing can damage the delicate roots and result in an unorganized farm layout, making it much harder to care for the plants and reducing your total harvest.
ga: Oyaiyeli baanyɛ akpata shishifãi ni waaa lɛ ahiɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo ni atooo he gbɛjianɔ aba. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa waa, ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni obaawo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it important to take my time and transplant suckers carefully into neat rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okɛ obei kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Careful transplanting in neat rows protects root systems, ensures every plant gets equal access to soil resources, and creates an organized farm that is easy to manage.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ wo tso lɛ mli yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsei fɛɛ náa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii lɛ ahe gbɛ kome. ni afee ŋmɔ ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni nɔkwɛmɔ waaa

english: Why is it important to keep clear walking paths along my plantain lines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ nɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Clear paths make it easy to navigate your farm safely without tripping or stepping on young plants, which saves you time and physical stress during field work.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli tse lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ oootsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe ni okɛ ohe wooo tsei bibii amli loo okɛ ohe akawo mli. Enɛ haa be kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ baa shi yɛ shiɛmɔ nitsumɔ be mli.

english: How does clearing weeds along my plantain lines protect my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ plantains lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Clearing overgrown weeds along plantain lines removes hiding spots for pests like rodents and insects while keeping soil nutrients available solely for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi kɛhaa onibii pɛ.

english: Why does an unorganized farm make weeding much harder later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji ni atooo he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa waa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Without organized rows and clear paths, you cannot easily move tools like cutlasses or sprayers through the field without accidentally damaging your plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ linei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni mli ka shi faŋŋ bɛ lɛ, Onyɛŋ otsi nibii tamɔ dade loo tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya ni efiteee dumɔwui yɛ oshara mli.

english: If I take a shortcut during land clearing, will it really affect my farm work in the future?
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ gbɛi kukuji miitsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shwiemɔ be mli Ani ebaana ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ nɔ hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ wɔsɛɛ loo daabi?

english: Yes, taking shortcuts during land clearing leaves blocked paths and hidden obstacles, which makes future tasks like transplanting, weeding, and harvesting much more exhausting.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛ kukuji ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ gbɛi ni atsĩ naa kɛ gbɛtsii nii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ baa. Enɛ haa wɔsɛɛ be nitsumɔi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ. Ni kpamɔ lɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: How does setting up clear crop lines from the start save me money on farm labor?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mikɛ shika ato ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ he?

english: Well-defined crop lines allow farm laborers to work faster and more efficiently, reducing the total days you need to pay them for weeding and harvesting.
ga: Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi ni amɛtsuɔ nii oya ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ gbii fɛɛ ni esa akɛ owo kɛha jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa seedlings the shade and soil moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for plant growth and green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to chew holes inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. The moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the hatched caterpillars crawl into the central leaves (funnel) to feed on young tissue before the leaf opens.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ (cone) koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani baa lɛ agbeleɔ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in cool, wet weather. Excessive moisture and dense shade help the fungus multiply and spread via rain drops onto the pods.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ feɔ babaoo ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear ground weeds and put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need maximum sunlight to build big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil toward the sun, which improves growth and reduces leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. ni haa shweremɔ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa baa helai baa shi

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetable roots with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetable shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, allowing your crops to stay hydrated longer with less watering.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ye obua otsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ kɛ nu fioo.

english: Why should I remove some of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow together, they fight with the main plant for food and water in the soil. Keeping only 2 to 3 strong shoots ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ Amɛkɛ tsei ni ji gbɔi lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei bibii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden hot weather, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save its energy for survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting or becoming woody if I leave them in the ground too long after maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ loo amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, high soil moisture promotes fungal rots. Overripe tubers also convert their starch into tough fiber, making the root woody and unsuitable for eating.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ. Tubers ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ hu tsɔɔ starch mli efeɔ fibers ni wa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei, ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap and spreading plant viruses. The virus disrupts how the leaves grow, causing them to wrinkle and shrink.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ mli helai lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. The virus blocks leaf growth. Causes wrinkles and shrinkage

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen food. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa du cowpea lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull natural food (nitrogen) out of the air and put it into the soil through their roots, which helps feed the maize growing next to them.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. which helps feed the corn growing next to it

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rain leaves water sitting on the field, the roots choke and rot, which is why planting on soil mounds or ridges helps drain excess water away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni nu yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to heap up soil around the stems of my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa muji naa yɛ mi sweet potato tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to expand and grow big underground. Making mounds keeps the soil loose and protects the developing tubers from scorching sun heat.
ga: Sweet potato tubers he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi hei wuji. Gɔŋ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ebuɔ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli dɔlɛ he.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stems with small or missing corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmãa bibii loo ŋmãa ni bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to make food. When the leaves get enough sunlight, that food travels down to build big underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Nakai niyenii lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the leaf sap. Spraying early helps clear the insects so new leaves grow straight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi bibii. Baai heei lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating holes in the middle of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the tender center of young corn plants. Catching them early and applying proper pest control saves the central growing tip of your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni abu onibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stems down into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miitsi efɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei lɛ kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts develop their pods underground instead of on top of branches. After the flower is pollinated, the stem naturally bends down and burrows into the soil so the nuts can grow safely under the earth.
ga: Peanuts lɛ feɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ fe niji anɔ. Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baakoto shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die when I plant them in an open field without any bigger trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong, direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them protects them from the harsh sun until they are strong enough.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak when I allow grass to grow closely around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mihaa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your maize for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. When grass grows too close, it steals the plant food first, leaving your maize starved and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha hɔmɔ aye o-corn lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tip along the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to make green leaves and grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or compost helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ naagbee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant too many seeds very close together in the same space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When crops are packed too tightly, their roots fight over the same underground food and water, and their leaves block light from each other. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough personal space to produce big, healthy yields.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kome lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly soaked. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to shed flowers to survive instead of spending energy making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or beans in my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are special crops that trap natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them restores good food to your soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Tsei nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii kpakpai aku sɛɛ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch full sunlight. Sunlight gives the plant energy to feed and swell the underground yam tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la lɛ fɛɛ. Hulu la haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants showing big holes and filled with saw-dust-like dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ buji wuji ni muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep center funnel of the maize plant to eat tender leaves. Applying approved treatments directly into the central funnel early in the morning destroys these pests.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo tsɔne ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ mra lɛ, ebaakpata nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and collapse during the day even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden daytime wilting in moist soil is often caused by bacterial wilt, a disease in the soil that blocks the water pipes inside the plant stem. Removing infected plants immediately stops the bacteria from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ hulutsoo be mli la ni shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ anaa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa helatsɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow strong stalks and big cobs. Adding NPK fertilizer or compost early in the plant's life helps keep the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni tsei ashishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei bibii wuji lɛ adara. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha yibii babaoo aba.

english: Why does leaving dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow better in dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, traps moisture in the soil so it doesn't evaporate under the hot sun. It keeps the soil cool and eventually breaks down into natural plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii.

english: Why does planting beans in the same farm with my maize help the maize produce more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa babaoo baa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas directly from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow next to maize, they naturally feed the soil with this essential nutrient, helping the maize grow larger without extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa Amɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ni tsofai krokomɛi fataaa he.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the branches before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ dani akpaa?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads very fast in warm, damp, and shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds around the trunk helps air flow through and stops the fungus from growing.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba mli kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ ni ekpaa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the dirt before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits around them for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ebɔle amɛhe. sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often spread by tiny whiteflies carrying a virus, or caused by extreme heat and uneven watering. Clearing weeds that harbor whiteflies and keeping soil moisture steady protects the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛ hela ko loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ baa ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Jwɛi ni haa ŋmeii yɛji yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe.

english: A cocoa tree naturally produces thousands of flowers but drops most of them because it can only support a limited number of pods. It also relies on tiny beneficial insects called midges to pollinate flowers, so preserving natural shade helps those insects work.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua pods fioo ko pɛ. Ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ hu anɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni haa fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ahiɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa nakai kooloi lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be easily weakened by tiny pests like nematodes or banana weevils in the soil. Propping up heavy fruiting trees with sturdy wooden poles prevents wind from blowing them down.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii tamɔ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ oya. Yibii tsei ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni wa damɔ shi lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa amɛ shi.

english: How do groundnut plants make nuts under the ground when their flowers grow above the soil?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tso ko awo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni efɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Once groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, the plant grows long stalks called pegs that bend down and push themselves deep into the soil, where the actual nuts mature underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from very high daytime temperatures or sudden dry spells. Giving the plants steady water and light shade during the hottest dry months stops flower fall.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli baa. Ha tso lɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ waa lɛ amli koni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why is it bad to leave my mature rice standing in the farm for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaashi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Leaving mature rice standing in the field for too long exposes it to excessive heat and sudden rains. This causes the grains to crack, drop onto the soil, or rot before you can harvest them.
ga: Ni aaashi ŋmãa ni ahoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa aba. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ gbálaa, egbeeɔ shikpɔŋ, loo egboɔ dani onyɛɔ okpaa.

english: Your rice is ready for harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains turn golden yellow. Harvesting at this stage prevents the crop from drying out too much or getting damaged by unexpected weather.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo akɛ obaakpa beni o-rice lɛ mli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ akafite amɛ.

english: Why does my rice spoil quickly after I cut it and leave it on the farm ground for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mifolɔ ni mishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: When harvested rice sits on the open ground, moisture from the soil and rain gets trapped inside the pile. This creates heat and dampness, causing mold to grow and ruining the crop before you can process it.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ nugbɔ baatsɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ daa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani obaanyɛ otsu he nii.

english: Can rain ruin my rice crop after I have already cut it down?
ga: Ani nugbɔ baanyɛ akpata ŋmãa tsei ahiɛ beni mifo amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, rain beating down on harvested rice soaks the grains and starts the decay process. The moisture causes grains to sprout, turn dark, and spoil quickly.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔi ŋmãa lɛ fitemɔ. Fɛ̃i haa omɔ ŋmaa kwɛ̃ɔ, efeɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ oya.

english: Why do extension officers advise us not to leave cut crops in the open sun and rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akashi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulu kɛ nugbɔ mli lɛ?

english: Alternating between hot sun and heavy rain forces grains to wet and dry repeatedly. This stress weakens the grain structure, causing it to break easily into tiny pieces when milled.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsakeɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni egbiɔ shii abɔ. Nɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ shishitoo lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa kɛ́ atswa lɛ, ebaafee mlɛo akɛ ebaakumɔ mli bibii bibii.

english: What is the best way to keep my harvested rice safe while it is still on the farm?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maha mikpamɔ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Always bundle harvested rice immediately and keep it off the bare ground using mats or tarpaulins. Cover it with a waterproof sheet to protect it from rain while waiting to transport it.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ato he amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni okɛto shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli loo tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ wolo ni nu nyɛɛɛ abote mli lɛ aha he koni nugbɔ akashɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni akɛ bo aya lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested grain turn dark and start smelling bad before I take it to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ahe su lɛ mli edɔ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ dani mikɛ amɛ yaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Dark color and bad smell happen when wet grains are piled together without proper drying. Damp conditions breed fungi and bacteria that digest the grain starch, causing it to rot.
ga: Su ni tsuɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ fɔŋ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ abua dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ anaa ni egbiko jogbaŋŋ. Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmãa lɛ baa. ha egbo

english: Why do my rice grains shatter into tiny pieces whenever I take them for milling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice ŋmeii lɛ fãa bibii bibii be fɛɛ be ni mafolɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Grain shattering usually happens when rice stays in the field too long under harsh weather or gets rained on after harvest. This causes microscopic cracks inside each grain that break open during milling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mligbalamɔ baa kɛji ŋmãa hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii waa baa ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli ni gbálaa yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How does rain beating on cut crops lower the price buyers will pay for my harvest?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afo lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha jara ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ kɛha mikpamɔ lɛ aba shi eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Rainwater causes grains to become discolored, spotty, and soft. Buyers offer lower prices for this damaged grain because it yields poor quality food and spoils quickly in storage.
ga: Rainwater causes the grain to become discolored, ragged, and soft. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa kɛha ŋmaa ni efite lɛ. This is because it produces low quality food and spoils quickly in storage.

english: Why does rice that was rained on during harvest spoil faster in storage than dry harvested rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni nɛɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ fiteɔ oya fe ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ?

english: Rainwater trapped inside the outer husk keeps the grain moisture level high. Storage pests and rot-causing molds thrive in wet grains, leading to rapid destruction of the whole sack.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni emɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmaa ni efɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ ha akpata kotoku muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ oya.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds from around the base of my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds around the base removes competition for nutrients, water, and sunlight. It also prevents pests and destructive bush animals from hiding near the main stem where they can easily chew or damage your tender cocoa.
ga: Eliminating surrounding weeds The base reduces competition for nutrients, water and sunlight, and it also keeps pests and bushwhackers from hiding near the main trunk. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛye loo amɛfite o-cocoa ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why should I clear the undergrowth around my cocoa trees when they are only knee-high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie he ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi kookoo tso He ni kookoo tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji pɛ?

english: At knee height, young cocoa plants are rapidly developing their root systems and branches. Clearing around them early prevents weeds from choking the tender crop and ensures all available soil nutrients support cocoa growth.
ga: Beni eshɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ, kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miifee amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛniji ahe oya. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ajiemɔ Kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. ni ehaa sũ mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my cocoa plants, and how does this affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi cacao tsei lɛ? Ni te enɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that naturally absorb moisture and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. If you do not clear them early, they starve your cocoa trees, resulting in weak plants and very low pod yields.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji ojieee mli oya. Hɔmɔ baaye o-cacao tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ pod yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa baa.

english: What is the safest way for me to clear weeds around a young cocoa stem without damaging the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Te eji tɛŋŋ akɛ afee cacao tsei blɛoo ni efiteee amɛ?

english: Use a sharp cutlass or hand tools carefully around the stem, cutting weeds right at ground level without digging deeply into the soil, which can cut the shallow feeder roots of the young cocoa tree.
ga: Kɛ tsɔne ni mli wa loo nine mli nibii krokomɛi atsu nii. stem carefully Kpɔ̃ɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ akafo mli. ni baanyɛ afo kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ

english: Can leaving tall grass near the stem of my cocoa trees cause plant diseases?
ga: Ani jwɛi kakadaŋŋ ni ashiɔ yɛ kookoo tso shishi lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba tsei anɔ?

english: Yes, tall grass traps moisture and blocks airflow around the base of the tree. This damp environment allows harmful fungi and black pod disease to develop and spread easily.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi kakadaŋŋ amɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ naa. Shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ tamɔ nɛkɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ black pod hela lɛ baaná ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: How can I prevent wild bush animals from destroying my cocoa plants when they are still small?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite mi-cacao tsei lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Regularly clearing the bush surrounding your crop eliminates the dark hiding spots wild animals use for shelter. Keeping clean field borders makes animals hesitant to enter open, visible areas to eat your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni ooojie Onibii ni ooodu daa lɛ baajie hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni koo mli kooloi kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli akɛ amɛhiɔhe lɛ kɛya. Kɛ́ oha ŋmɔ lɛ naa he tse lɛ, ehaa kooloi sumɔɔɔ ni amɛboteɔ hei ni agbele, ni anaa lɛ amli koni amɛye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do wild animals attack young cocoa farms that have thick bushes surrounding them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ tutuaa kookoo ŋmɔji ni jwɛi wuji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Overgrown bushes provide shade and protection for animals like rodents and bushbucks. When crops are hidden in overgrown areas, animals can feed on tender stems and leaves without being spotted by the farm owner.
ga: Tsoi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ jwɛi ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tee hei ni tsei ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ, kooloi baanyɛ aye tsei lɛ ahe tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni ŋmɔtsɛ lɛ enaaa.

english: How often should I visit my cocoa farm to make sure my crops are doing well?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maya mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya nɔ jogbaŋŋ lo?

english: It is best to inspect your farm two to three times a week. Frequent visits allow you to spot early weed growth, pest attacks, or animal damage before significant harm is done to your cocoa.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli. Saramɔi ni yaa nɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa onaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ yɛ eshishijee fãi amli. tsɛŋemɔ helai loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ atuatsemɔ Dani abaaye o-cocoa lɛ awui waa

english: Why do some farmers lose most of their cocoa to pests while neighboring farms remain healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi fiteɔ amɛ kokoo lɛ mli babaoo yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahewɔ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo.

english: Farms with good harvests usually have alert caretakers who clear undergrowth regularly and inspect plants often. Neglected farms allow weeds and pests to multiply unchecked, leading to crop loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ nɔkwɛlɔi ni shwieɔ jwɛi ni amɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ amli daa lɛ. Okwaafoi ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa babaoo ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ.

english: What early signs show that my young cocoa trees are struggling because the farm is overgrown?
ga: Mɛni ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ ejaakɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi tsɔ?

english: Look for thin stems, yellowing leaves, slow height growth, and chewed leaves near the base. These signs mean weeds are stealing light and soil nutrients, or pests are hiding in the surrounding bush.
ga: Taomɔ tsei bibii, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. kɛ baai ni ashɛreɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishi Okadii nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ jwɛi miiju la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli.

english: Sir, why do my older fields yield far less corn and cassava now compared to when I first cleared the land?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ momo lɛ woɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fioo kwraa fe be mli ni mijie ŋmãa klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Soil gets tired and loses its food when you farm it continuously without giving it fertilizer or organic matter. Letting the land rest or fallow allows native vegetation to return nutrients and organic matter to the soil naturally.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baaje mli kɛji oya nɔ otsu okwaayeli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli haaa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ashiɔ ni ehiɛ edɔ loo ehiɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Sir, when I clear bush to start a new farm, is it better to burn the cleared leaves or leave them on the ground?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, beni mijie jwɛi lɛ koni mije ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ. Ani ehi akɛ abaashã baai ni ajie lɛ loo abaashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Burning clears the land quickly, but leaving the cut bush to decompose into mulch protects the ground from strong sun, keeps soil moisture in, and turns into free natural food for your crops.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei bibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ fite tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebatsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha onibii.

english: Sir, how can I easily tell if my soil is healthy enough to plant corn?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well, and crumbles easily in your hand when moist. If soil is pale, hard like stone, or full of dry sand, crops will struggle to feed and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Ni efoɔ oya kɛ́ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ewa tamɔ tɛ. aloo ŋã ni egbi yɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaná naagba yɛ niyenii namɔ kɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ mli.

english: Sir, is it safe to plant cassava and corn together on the same plot of land?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because corn grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly over a whole year, so they do not compete heavily for light and food.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa fiofio yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛshiuuu la kɛ niyenii babaoo he akaŋ.

english: Sir, if I let my farm animals walk and feed on my field during the dry season, will it spoil the land for crops?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, kɛji miha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ nyiɛ ni amɛye kooloi yɛ miŋmɔji amli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Ani ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: As long as you remove animals before planting, their droppings serve as valuable manure that feeds the soil, making it richer and ready for your next crop.
ga: Shii abɔ ni ooojie kooloi lɛ dani odu lɛ. Amɛshwiei lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Ha kooloi lɛ afee niiatsɛmɛi ni amɛfee klalo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Sir, why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the corn is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. This happens when soil is worn out, choked by weeds, or flooded with water.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ fite. jwɛi ehà nɔ loo nu afua eba

english: Sir, why do my cassava plants grow tall and skinny with tiny tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ yitso bibioo lɛ? Akɛni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe hewɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight and stretch upward toward the sky instead of sending energy downward into building thick root tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Ebaatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni ekɛ ehe aaawo ŋwɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni efee ŋmei ni shishifãi ni mli tse.

english: Sir, why can cassava tubers stay inside the ground for months without rotting before I harvest them?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo ni amɛfiteee dani akpa?

english: Cassava roots are living storage organs where the plant saves energy, allowing the tubers to remain fresh underground until you need to harvest them, as long as the ground isn't waterlogged.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa bulb lɛ feɔ ehee yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehe baahia ni okpa amɛ, kɛji akɛ nu ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Sir, why does my corn wither so fast when rain stops for just a short period while the plants are flowering?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko lɛ? Be mli ni tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Corn needs the most water when forming cobs and tassels. Without water during flowering, the plant rolls up its leaves to conserve moisture, which reduces grain formation.
ga: Nu he hiaa abele fe fɛɛ kɛ́ efee ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, kɛji nu bɛ Tso lɛ baafolɔ ebaa lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Enɛ haa ŋmaa ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Sir, I have land right next to a stream, can I plant cassava right by the water's edge?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, miyɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ faa ko masɛi. Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ nu masɛi?

english: Cassava roots will rot if they stay submerged in wet, waterlogged ground for days. It is better to plant water-loving crops like vegetables or rice right by the water, and place cassava on dry, elevated ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagboi kɛji amɛhi shi yɛ hei ni nu efɔ yɛ, ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ gbii babaoo. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu tsei ni sumɔɔ nu, tamɔ aduawai loo ŋmãa, yɛ nu masɛi, ni okɛ ŋmãa awo he ko ni egbi ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide natural shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer feeding on the tender inner leaves of young maize. Identifying them early allows you to use neem leaf extracts or recommended sprays before they destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmei baai bibii lɛ amli. mra be mli nibii ni ayɔseɔ lɛ Ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ yi loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii dani ofite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stems when I put them in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani ebaatsɔɔ he ko?

english: Yes, the small growth buds on the cassava stem must point upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down forces the new shoots to grow downward first before bending up, which weakens the plant and lowers tuber yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii heei daa kɛyaa shishi klɛŋklɛŋ dani amɛkotoɔ shi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi aha he ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves creates mulch, which stops the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps the roots cool, and gradually breaks down into rich plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei niyenii ni jara wa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread diseases. Controlling these pests early with insecticidal soap or neem oil stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. No shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ helai srɔtoi eshwaa. Ni oooye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or beans on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally enriches the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it uses that stored food to grow bigger leaves and larger cobs.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do extension officers tell me not to burn the dry bush on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛkashã jwɛi ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔji amli dani amɛdu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic material, kills helpful organisms like earthworms, and strips nitrogen from the soil. Clearing without burning allows the plant matter to decay and nourish the soil.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashãaa lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ agbo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to place long wooden stakes next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the plant make food, which is sent down to grow big underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni atsu kɛba shi koni amɛyadu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji

english: Why does my stored maize turn into white powder after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ etsɔ powda yɛŋ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Insects called grain weevils burrow into the stored maize to feed and lay eggs, leaving behind powder. Ensuring the maize is thoroughly dried and stored in airtight bags prevents weevils from surviving.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli koni amɛtao niyenii ni amɛwo wɔji, ni amɛshiɔ powda yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi.

english: Why does placing fertilizer directly touching the stem of my crop kill the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that draw moisture out of the plant roots if placed too close, causing the plant to burn and dry up. Fertilizer should always be applied in a small circle a few inches away from the stem.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tsei ashishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo amɛhe tsɔ. Ebaaha tsei lɛ ashã ni amɛgbi. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii amli. Inchi fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: If I spray medicine on my crops to protect them, will the chemical stay inside the harvested beans when I sell them?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofa ko shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni mikɛbu amɛhe. Ani tsofai lɛ baakã mi-kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ amli beni mikɛbaahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, if you harvest too soon after spraying or use wrong dosages, high levels of chemical residue remain inside the crop. This makes the produce unsafe to eat and can cause international buyers to reject your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okpa mra tsɔ yɛ be mli ni okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ loo okɛ nɔ ni esaaa tsu nii. Tsofai ni eshwɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ, ni ebaanyɛ eha majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ akpoo okpamɔ lɛ.

english: What is the safest way to keep wild animals from destroying my crops without damaging my yield?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ atsĩ koolooi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite miŋmɔshi nii ni amɛfiteee miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Using approved animal deterrents around the perimeter of your field or constructing physical barriers is best. Pouring harsh chemicals directly around crop roots or pods can harm the crop and pollute the soil.
ga: Kɛ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ hela lɛ tsu nii yɛ Space oyale lɛ he loo ofee gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ Direct tso shishifãi loo ŋmeii ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii awui ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Is it okay for me to crush pesticide tablets and pour them directly on the soil near my plants?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mafo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ amli ni mafɔse shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, crushing and pouring raw chemical concentrations directly into the soil can burn the plant's roots and cause the crop to absorb dangerously high chemical levels that poison the produce.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni afee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. ni ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ tsofai ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ oshara ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ.

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying chemical medicine on my farm before it is safe to pick the pods?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani onyɛ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe?

english: Every agrochemical has a required waiting period called a Pre-Harvest Interval, usually between 14 to 30 days. Waiting gives the chemical enough time to break down naturally so your crop becomes safe for human consumption.
ga: Agrochemical fɛɛ agrochemical yɛ be ni ekɛmɛɔ ni ale lɛ akɛ be ni tsɔɔ ŋmaakpamɔ hiɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yeɔ gbii 14 kɛyashi 30 teŋ. Mɛɛmɔ haa tsofai lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesa niyenii.

english: How can I receive spraying schedules and crop care advice directly on my mobile phone?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná be ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa nɔ kɛ ŋaawoo ni kɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ he tɛ̃ɛ yɛ mi-mobile phone lɛ nɔ?

english: You can register your phone number with agricultural extension programs to receive SMS text updates with timely advice on weather, pest alerts, and correct chemical application steps.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ otɛlifoŋ nɔmba awo Agricultural Extension Program lɛ mli koni onine ashɛ SMS niŋmaa heei ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he ŋaawoi yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Pest alert kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my harvested cocoa beans turn bad or get rejected even after I have dried them well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo yibii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo akpooɔ amɛ eyɛ mli akɛ migbi amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Beans can be rejected if they contain high chemical residues from improper chemical use before harvest, or if pest eggs were trapped inside the pods during storage in damp conditions.
ga: Abaanyɛ akpoo ŋmeii kɛji akɛ amɛyɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni eshwɛ babaoo ni jɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ dani akpaa. aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my crop turning yellow after I poured pest medicine around the roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Heavy chemicals applied directly to the root area damage the fine roots that suck up water and plant food. When roots are damaged, the plant starves and its leaves turn yellow.
ga: Tsofai ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ shishifã lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baafite shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli Kɛji shishifãi lɛ fite Tso lɛ hɔmɔ baaye lɛ ni baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the weather becomes very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Wet conditions encourage fungal diseases like Black Pod to grow and spread through water drops. Clearing heavy shade and weeds lets sunlight and air dry out the trees, keeping the pods healthy.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛtsɔ nu mli ŋmeii anɔ. Shade ni tsii ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha tsei lɛ agbi. ni ehaa pod lɛ mli waa

english: Can I mix my own herbal mixtures with factory crop medicines to make them stronger against pests?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsofai amli lɛ afutu tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli lɛ mli koni eha amɛhe awa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe?

english: It is not safe to mix unknown materials with farm chemicals. Uncontrolled mixtures can cause bad chemical reactions that destroy your crops or leave dangerous chemical residues in your food.
ga: Nibii ni aleee ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai lɛ bɛ shweshweeshwe. Nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni akudɔɔɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai fɔji ni fiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba loo eshi tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ oniyenii lɛ mli.

english: Why do flowers fall off my crops before turning into actual fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when plants suffer from stress like extreme heat, lack of water, or insect attacks. Keeping the soil moist and protecting young flowers from pests ensures they develop into good yields.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ naa nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi tutuamɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ baaha amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many days does it usually take for my maize seeds to sprout after I put them in the ground?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii enyiɛ eheɔ dani mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize seeds usually take between 4 to 7 days to sprout, provided the soil has enough moisture and warmth. If the soil is too dry, germination will be delayed or fail entirely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui heɔ gbii ejwɛ kɛyashi kpawo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni edɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ, Ekwɛ̃mɔ baahe sɛɛ loo ebaafite kwraa.

english: How do I know the exact month or number of days my cassava crops will be ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa yɛ nyɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko loo gbii ayibɔ ko mli?

english: Most improved cassava varieties in Ghana mature within 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell they are ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and shed, and the soil around the base starts cracking from the expanding tubers.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. You can tell they're ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base begins to crack from the expanding bulbs.

english: Why do I need to keep my pepper seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ pepper dumɔwui awo dumɔwui atsu lɛ mli dani mikɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are very delicate when sprouting. A nursery bed acts like a protective baby home where you can manage heat, moisture, and pests easily until the seedlings develop strong stems to survive in the open field.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ he waaa waa kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ̃. Nursery beds act like baby houses where you can easily deal with heat, humidity, and pests until the seedlings develop strong stems to survive in the open field.

english: What is the proper formula or method for applying fertilizer so it doesn't destroy my maize crops?
ga: Ani fɔmula loo gbɛ ni ja yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli koni ekafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer about two weeks after planting by placing it in a small hole 5 centimeters away from the plant stem, then cover it with soil. Never let the fertilizer touch the plant stem or leaves directly, as it will burn them.
ga: Aaafee otsii enyɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he kɛtsɔ bu bibioo ko ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. 5 centimeters kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ. Kaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo baai lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ enɛ baashã amɛ.

english: Is it good for me to soak my hard okro seeds in water overnight before planting them?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makɛ okra dumɔwui ni edɔ lɛ awo nu mli gbɛkɛ kome dani madu?

english: Yes, soaking hard okro seeds in clean water overnight softens their tough outer coat, which helps water penetrate faster and allows the seeds to sprout evenly in a shorter number of days.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ okɛ okra dumɔwui ni wa wo nu ni mli tse mli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ fã ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo. Enɛ haa nu boteɔ mli oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ gbii kukuji amli.

english: How often am I supposed to water my tomato plants during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ nu yɛ harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Vegetables like tomatoes need steady moisture during the dry season. Water them twice a day—early morning before the sun gets too hot and late afternoon—so the soil stays moist without becoming waterlogged.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ tomato hia nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Nu shii enyɔ daa gbi. Leebi maŋkpa dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ tsɔ kɛ shwane mli. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ni nu akabote mli.

english: Why is it important to measure exact distances between my crops instead of planting them closely together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ni kã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Proper plant spacing gives each crop enough room to spread its roots, soak up sunlight, and draw nutrients from the soil without competing with neighboring plants, resulting in bigger fruits and higher yields.
