ga: Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ eshishifãi lɛ, ekɛ hulu la, ni ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ wuji ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open space without bigger trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ he ko ni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide necessary shade and maintain soil moisture, protecting young cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off without turning into fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to tomato plants, drying out the flower pollen before fertilization can happen. Giving the plants enough water and shade during high temperatures helps save the flowers so they can form fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ dani fɔmɔ nii lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo ha tsei yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do fall armyworms suddenly attack my maize crop right after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi-corn ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay eggs on young, tender maize leaves as soon as new shoots emerge after the rains. The warm weather causes these eggs to hatch rapidly within a few days into hungry caterpillars.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baa bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii heei je kpo yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ pɛ kɛkɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Why did my young cocoa plants die suddenly even though the leaves were still intact?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ yɛ lolo lɛ?

english: When weedkiller accidentally lands on young cocoa leaves, the chemical gets absorbed inside the plant. It travels through the system and kills the crop from within, leaving the plant standing even though it is dead.
ga: Kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbee kookoo baai bibii anɔ yɛ oshara mli Tsofai lɛ boteɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli. Etsɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli ni egbeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli. Ha tso lɛ adamɔ shi kɛji egbo po.

english: Can weedkiller sprayed on a nearby farm damage my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Yes. Fine chemical mist can easily drift in the wind from a neighboring plot onto your young cocoa leaves, causing delicate seedlings to wither and die.
ga: Hɛɛ. Tsofa mli ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa baanyɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nɔ oya kɛba okɔkoo baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: What happens if strong chemical mixtures or 'marriage medicines' touch my cocoa leaves?
ga: Mɛni baaba kɛji tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ loo ‘Gbalashihilɛ Tsamɔ’ Ta Mikokoo Baai lɛ Ahe.

english: Mixing strong herbicides creates powerful chemical combinations that burn soft leaves instantly and destroy the internal living tissues of young cocoa plants.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni fa babaoo ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ haa tsofa ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ feɔ ekome. Enɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni efite cacao tso bibioo lɛ mli fãji ni hiɛ ka lɛ.

english: How far away should weedkillers be sprayed to protect my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ he ni mikɛbuɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: You should leave a wide safety boundary around young seedlings and avoid spraying on windy days so that drifting chemical mist does not land on the crop's leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi shweshweeshwefeemɔ he ko ni da obɔle tsei bibii ahe ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbii ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ anɔ. Bɔni afee ni tsofai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ akaho yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai lɛ anɔ

english: Are young cocoa plants more easily killed by chemical sprays than mature cocoa trees?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ cacao tsei bibii anɔ lɛ gbeɔ amɛ mlɛo fe cacao tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Yes. Young cocoa plants have thin bark and tender green leaves that absorb chemicals very quickly, whereas mature cocoa trees have thick bark and strong root systems that make them much more resilient.
ga: Hɛɛ. Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ amɛhewolo ni mli tseee kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shwieɔ tsofai oya waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, cacao tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ tsitsii ni mli tse kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni haa amɛhe wa waa.

english: Why are the leaves of young cocoa trees so sensitive to chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ cacao tsei bibii amli lɛ baai lɛ nuɔ he waa lɛ?

english: Young leaves are the breathing organs of the seedling and have thin surfaces, making it very easy for herbicides to seep inside and poison the entire plant.
ga: Baai bibii ji dumɔwu lɛ mumɔ he nibii ni amɛhiɛ yɔɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo waa akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baabote tso lɛ mli ni ekɛ tsofa fɔŋ awo tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do young cocoa trees require more careful management than old cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ kookoo tsei bibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ fe kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are fragile and easily harmed by weed competitors, direct sun, and accidental chemical sprays, whereas established trees can endure more harsh conditions.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii waaa ni jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ oshara mli lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai anaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I safely clear weeds around my young cocoa trees without harming them?
ga: Majie jwɛi kɛjɛ he ni ebɔle he lɛ. cocoa tso bibioo Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mifoŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni eyeee mi awui?

english: It is safest to clear weeds around young cocoa using a hand cutlass or by using a protective spray shield over the chemical nozzle so no weedkiller touches the crop leaves.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ jwɛi ni bɔle Cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ kɛtsɔ dagger nɔ Loo akɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ shwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ akashɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it important for me to keep tending to my old cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maya nɔ makwɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Old cocoa farms already have established root networks, and with proper clearing, pruning, and protection from chemicals, they can continue to give reliable yields.
ga: No mli lɛ, kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ eto shishifãi akuu ko shishi momo. Ni kɛtsɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ tsofai ni sa ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eya nɔ ekɛ nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ aba.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa crop died from disease or chemical drift?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ egboi yɛ hela loo tsofai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ahewɔ?

english: Disease usually causes gradual spotty damage or rotting over time, whereas chemical drift acts quickly, causing young leaves to dry up and die shortly after spraying occurs nearby.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ fiteɔ loo efiteɔ fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofa ni haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii oya. Enɛ haa baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ etsɛɛɛ beni ashwie amɛ nɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the new store-bought crop seeds perform differently than the traditional local seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe akutsoŋ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields and resist specific diseases, but their seeds cannot be saved for the next season because they lose their strength. Local seeds yield less but can be saved and replanted year after year.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai komɛi. Shi anyɛɛɛ akɛ amɛdumɔwui lɛ ato koni akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli ejaakɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ shi abaanyɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ ni adu ekoŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do my traditional local maize seeds take longer to mature than the new improved varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shishijee maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani eshɛɔ fe ŋmãa ni atsake lɛ lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are bred by scientists to grow fast so they can mature before the dry season starts, whereas traditional varieties follow a natural, longer growing cycle adapted to older climate patterns.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi baafɔ tsei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya bɔni afee ni amɛshwere dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kusum mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni kɛ ehe kpãa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni etsɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big green leaves, but the tubers underground are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excessive fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to grow leaves above ground instead of storing food and expanding tubers in the soil.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baato shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when water sits on my field for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii 2-3 lɛ?

english: Too much standing water drowns the roots by cutting off oxygen in the soil. Without oxygen, roots cannot take up nutrients like nitrogen, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ oxygen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ebaafo mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, ni no baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without ever forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when the soil lacks water, or when there are no beneficial insects around to help pollen move inside the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Koni eye ebua pollen lɛ ni efã kɛya fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings need shade even though mature crops need full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ he hiaa hulutsoo lɛ? Tsei ni eda lɛ po he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Young seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that lose water very quickly under hot sun. Shade protects them from drying out until their root systems are deep enough to find water.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya waa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade lɛ buɔ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna nu.

english: Why is burning the dried grass on my land before planting bad for my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani aduɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Burning grass kills helpful living organisms in the soil and burns away natural food for crops, leaving the soil dry and weak, whereas letting cleared grass rot naturally builds rich soil.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ gbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni eshãa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii baa lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make my soil better for the maize crop I plant next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen food from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that food stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni gbalaa niyenii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai niyenii lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the young leaves, or spreading a plant virus that deforms growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. or the spread of plant viruses that cause deformed growth

english: Why are my yam vines turning brown and drying up long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by microscopic worms called nematodes or soil fungi attacking the root system, preventing water from traveling up to the leaves.
ga: Early drying of sweet potato vines is often caused by tiny worms called nematodes or fungi in the soil that attack the root system. Ehaa nu shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen fertilizer, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the center of my maize crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs on leaves and crawl into the central heart of the plant to feed on tender green leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ ni amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, especially during warm and dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long or when underground pests create wounds that let fungi enter the tuber.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ pilamɔi ni haa ŋmeii boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa flowers falling off without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop without setting pods if the farm experiences extreme heat, prolonged dry weather, or if there are not enough tiny midges to pollinate them.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli dɔ waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Aloo kɛji bibii komɛi yɛ Eshɛɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee pollination

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems; when soil becomes soft from heavy rain or stem borers damage the base, strong winds easily blow them over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo tso lɛ mlibotemɔ hewɔ lɛ ekɛ shishitoo lɛ fitemɔ baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatsɔ mli oya.

english: If I plant my crops closer together, will I harvest more food from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to small, weak plants and lower overall harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy downpours, and cover it lightly with soil near the plant root zone so it stays in place.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni okɛ sũ fioo ko aha he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ koni sũ lɛ ahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the fertilizer, soil water, and light meant for your crops, starving your plants despite the extra food you added.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ kɛji akɛ okɛ niyenii kroko fata he po.

english: Can I use wood ash from my kitchen fire to help my vegetables grow better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tso sũ ni jɛ mi-kitchen la lɛ mli lɛ aye abua mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, wood ash contains potassium and helps reduce soil acidity, making nutrients more available to vegetables when sprinkled lightly on the field.
ga: Hɛɛ, potassium yɛ tso mli sũ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa shi. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛji akɛ afɔse amɛ fioo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when there is full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight without shade. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates a living umbrella that protects the young cocoa seedlings until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ amɛhe lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava stems so I get big tubers?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu amɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni anyɛ ana bulbs wuji?

english: Planting cassava stems about one meter apart gives the roots enough space in the soil to grow big and heavy without fighting neighboring plants for food and water.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara ni amɛfee tsiimɔ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after a light rain. Avoid putting fertilizer right before heavy downpours, as rain can wash the food away before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ baaha niyenii lɛ afite dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air into their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free natural plant food for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and brown dust inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage comes from the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the plant shoot, so spraying approved treatments early in the morning or late evening reaches them best.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ashishifãi amli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ.

english: Black rot on the bottom of tomatoes is blossom end rot. It happens when the soil moisture changes too suddenly or when the soil lacks calcium as the fruit is growing.
ga: Diŋ ni fiteɔ yɛ tomato shishi lɛ ji fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ calcium bɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will quickly steal the water, sunlight, and soil food your small crops need to establish strong roots early on.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ oya koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa mra.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks in the ground to lift up my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni mikɛwo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on wooden stakes allows the leaves to spread out and capture more sunlight. Sunlight gives the plant energy to build much larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo. Hulu la haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my plantain stems with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around plantains with dry organic matter keeps the ground cool and moist, prevents weed growth, and turns into rich natural food as it rots.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ Plantains lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo kɛji egbo

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow strong. It can also happen when the soil is too full of water, which prevents the roots from taking up food from the dirt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha shweremɔ kpakpa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves from the soil. It also lets pests and diseases that feed on maize build up in the soil, making your yield smaller each harvest.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei taoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mli.

english: Should I apply my fertilizer during the hot dry season or wait until the rains start?
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ enyɔ shi lɛ, ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he loo mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaje shishi?

english: You should wait until the rains start or when the soil is moist. Crop roots can only drink up fertilizer when there is water in the ground, and applying it to dry soil during heat can burn and damage your plants.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baabɔi nɛmɔ loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shãa aba ni efite tsei.

english: What is making tiny holes in my young corn leaves and leaving saw-dust looking dirt inside them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mibi lɛ mli ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: This is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana. They hide inside the central leaves of the plant and eat the tender leaves before they fully open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe kwraa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap, which can pass a virus to the plant. It stops the leaves from catching sunlight properly to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ashwã tsei amli Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la ni sa kɛha amɛdalɛ.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot inside the wet soil before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ amɛ po shwie shi?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long, causing fungal infections. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. kɛ fungal infection baa Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough steady water. Without proper moisture and mild temperatures, the flowers cannot set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily as soon as the plantain bunch starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji amɛbɔi shweremɔ pɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and the heavy fruit bunch makes them top-heavy. Strong winds can easily push them down unless you support the stem with a wooden prop or bamboo pole.
ga: The seedlings have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches, making them heavy. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashɛ amɛ shi mlɛo. Unless you use a wooden or bamboo pole to support the trunk.

english: Why do I need to place tall sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce energy. Staking the vines helps the leaves catch maximum light, which feeds the growing yam tuber under the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa la babaoo. ni haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii

english: Why do cocoa farmers leave big trees in the farm instead of cutting all of them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi lɛ shiɔ tsei wuji yɛ amɛŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafolɔ amɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily in direct harsh sunlight. Keeping select tall shade trees protects young cocoa from heat, retains soil moisture, and protects the farm from strong winds.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni oooha amɛfee hulutsoo lɛ baaye abua ni ebu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni obu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: How can I tell if my vegetable seeds are growing well right after I plant them in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Healthy seeds typically sprout above the soil within three days if the ground is kept moist, popping up as tiny green shoots that show the crop is alive and growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii etɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Ebaaje kpo akɛ tso bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. No tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛmiida.

english: What does an officer mean when they say my newly planted seeds are 'flashing'?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni onukpai lɛ tsɔɔ beni amɛkɛɛ midumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ ‘miikpɛ’ lɛ?

english: Flashing' is a term used when tiny green crop shoots suddenly break through the soil surface all at once, usually within three days after planting.
ga: Blinking’ ji wiemɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ́ tso bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ je kpo. Eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikome Bei pii lɛ, yɛ gbii etɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: What basic care do my seeds need in the first few days so they pop up above the ground quickly?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee kwɛmɔ he hiaa midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli koni amɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya?

english: You need to keep the top layer of soil lightly watered every day, which softens the hard seed coat so the baby shoot can easily sprout within three days.
ga: Ebaabi ni okɛ nu afɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo daa gbi, ni no baaha dumɔwui ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo yɛ gbii etɛ mli.

english: Why do some small crop seeds need to be buried near the top of the dirt rather than deep down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afu dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ moŋ fe ni aaafu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ lɛ?

english: Small seeds planted close to the surface receive the light and warmth they need to sprout quickly, popping up above the soil in just three days.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ naa la kɛ dɔlɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Ebaatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii etɛ pɛ mli.

english: Are there quick crops I can plant in Ghana that will yield food in just a couple of weeks?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ko yɛ ni manyɛ madu oya yɛ Ghana ni baawo yibii yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ mli?

english: Yes, fast-growing leafy greens like amaranth or gboma sprout in three days and can give you your very first harvest in as little as two weeks.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai eŋɔli ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ spinach loo burdock. baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbii etɛ mli Ni ebaanyɛ eha bo oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ otsii enyɔ pɛ mli.

english: Why do fast-growing leafy greens allow me to start harvesting so much sooner than maize or tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni mijeɔ mikpamɔ shishi mra fe ŋmãa loo tomato lɛ?

english: Leafy crops put most of their early energy into growing thick, green leaves instead of stems or fruits, allowing you to pick your first harvest in about two weeks.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ amɛshishijee be mli. Yaa kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni miida yɛ tsei loo aduawai najiaŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ yɛ aaafee otsii enyɔ mli.

english: If I cut leaves from my fast-maturing crops after two weeks, will the plant stop producing?
ga: Kɛji mifo tso ko ni daa oya lɛ baai lɛ yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ Ani tso lɛ baakpa yibiiwoo?

english: If you gently pick only the mature outer leaves during your first harvest at two weeks, the plant will keep growing fresh new leaves for you to pick again later.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ shwie kponɔgbɛ baai ni eda lɛ pɛ yɛ otsii enyɔ ni akɛkpaa klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Tso lɛ baaná baai heei heei ni okɛbaakpa ekoŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: What fast crop can I grow to make quick income while waiting for my main crops like cassava to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu oya ni maná shika oya yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni miŋmɔ titri tamɔ ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Fast leafy vegetables sprout within three days and give you a harvest in two weeks, providing quick food and immediate market sales while long-term crops grow.
ga: Aduawai ni baa mra lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbii etɛ mli. Ni obaanyɛ okpa yɛ otsii enyɔ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii ni anáa oya ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ shwereɔ lɛ baa.

english: How do I know if the tiny green plants popping up early are my crops and not weeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha mi? Nakai shweremɔ oya lɛ ji miŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee jwɛi?

english: Your planted crops will 'flash' or pop up at the same time in straight rows where you planted them within three days, whereas weeds grow randomly all over the bed.
ga: Tsei ni odu lɛ ‘baatswa’ loo amɛbaaje kpo yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli yɛ he ni odu lɛ yɛ lɛ mli yɛ gbii etɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi baakwɛ̃ trukaa yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: How long should I expect to care for seeds in a nursery bed before seeing the green shoots?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mana ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli?

english: With proper daily watering and good soil, seeds in a nursery bed will sprout and show green shoots—often called flashing—in about three days.
ga: Kɛ nu ni sa daa gbi kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmeii eŋɔli. Flash jeɔ kpo (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ flash) yɛ aaafee gbii etɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to raise my crop seeds in plastic nursery bags before planting them on the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu aduawai dumɔwui yɛ plastic culture kotokui amli dani madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Nursery bags give delicate seeds a protected environment to build strong root systems away from harsh weather, heavy rain, and weeds before they are mature enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Grow bags haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ naa he ko ni abuɔ he koni amɛto shishifãi ni mli wa ni kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ jwɛi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ dani dumɔwui lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why should I mix sand with my farm soil when filling containers for seedling growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋã afutu ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ beni mikɛ tsɛnsii ni akɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ mli lɛ?

english: Pure soil can become tight and hard when watered, which suffocates young roots. Mixing sand creates tiny pockets that allow water to drain properly and give tender root tips room to spread.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ awo nɔ nu. Enɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã lɛ futu mli lɛ, ehaa kotokui bibii baa. No haa nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa

english: Why is it necessary to press and pack the soil firmly inside the bag before dropping my seed inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atswa shikpɔŋ lɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli dani adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Packing soil gently removes large empty air pockets. This ensures the seed stays in firm contact with moist dirt, which is required for the seed to absorb water and sprout evenly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atswa lɛ baajie kɔɔyɔɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ fiofio. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ muji ni mli efɔ kpeɔ. Enɛ he hia koni dumɔwui lɛ aŋɔ nu ni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and turn brown when left in direct sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop leaves lose moisture quickly under hot sun, and their small roots cannot drink ground water fast enough to keep up, causing the plant to dry out and burn.
ga: Baai bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ anu shikpɔŋ shishi nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛhiɛ nu mli. Ebaanyɛ eha tsei agbi ni amɛshã.

english: Why does covering the base of my young crops with dry grass help them grow better during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a blanket over the dirt, blocking the hot sun from evaporating soil moisture and keeping the crop's root area cool and damp.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight each other for limited sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients, leaving every plant malnourished.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my cassava crop reduce the size of the harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni oha jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? Mi cassava tsei lɛ miiha nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ayibɔ miiba shi?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal food, water, and sunlight directly from your crop, leaving the cassava with insufficient energy to expand its underground tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my crops turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate the crop is lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, forcing the plant to pull energy from its older leaves to feed new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa tso lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tso lɛ shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crop seedlings droop and look lifeless immediately after I move them into the field soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Transplanting disturbs delicate root hairs, causing short-term shock because the plant temporarily loses its full ability to take up water until roots settle into the new ground.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ kroko mli lɛ gbaa shishifãi ahe yitsɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ naa. Ekɛ be kukuoo mli shoofeemɔ baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛɔ lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I tell if a seedling bag is too small for my growing crop plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui kotoku lɛ ji bibioo tsɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: If a bag is too small, the roots will hit the bottom and begin to curl in circles around the inside walls, which prevents the plant from anchoring deeply when moved into the farm.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kotoku lɛ ji bibioo tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baatswa shishigbɛ ni amɛje shishi amɛbɔle gbogboi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe yɛ kooyigbɛ, ni no baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekatswa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ajie lɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there is too much sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade that protects them and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ehaa amɛnaa hulutsoo ni buɔ amɛhe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet conditions. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight into the farm, which helps dry out moisture and reduce fungus growth.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for maize. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant regain its green color and grow stronger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmãa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo nitrogen ŋmãa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Maize seeds may fail to germinate if the soil is too dry, if they were planted too deep for rain to reach them, or if underground pests like ants and birds ate the seeds before they could sprout.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni nugbɔ nyɛŋ an Aloo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ okpoi yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You will know it is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaale akɛ edara beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why is it important to stake my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahã mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on wooden stakes allows the leaves to catch more sunlight, which makes the plant produce larger tubers underground while keeping the leaves away from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Too many young shoots compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients, resulting in small bunches. Keeping only 2 to 3 healthy suckers ensures bigger and healthier plantain bunches.
ga: Tsobii bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni jeɔ kpo. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ to lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants curl up and fall off without producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbee shi ni amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Blossom drop happens when plants suffer from water stress, extreme heat, or damage from tiny pests like thrips. Regular watering during dry spells and controlling pests helps flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Blossom drop baa kɛji tsei lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu mli haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nibii bibii tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants start curling and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by small sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses, or by severe heat stress. Controlling whiteflies early helps prevent the spread of the virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Early Whitefly Control Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɛ-kɛ-shwamɔ naa.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans help my soil produce better crops next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient, or the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe and absorb food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: If I plant three maize seeds together in one hole, will I get more corn than planting just one?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui 3 ekome yɛ bu kome mli Ani maná ŋmãa babaoo fe ŋmãa dumɔwui kome pɛ ni adu?

english: Planting too many seeds in one spot forces the stalks to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants with small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense against heat. By curling up, the leaf reduces its exposure to the direct sun and conserves water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ baa shi.

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so the roots can absorb it. Applying it to dry soil can burn the plant's roots and damage the crop.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni efite tsei lɛ.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars gather inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miibua amɛhe naa yɛ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are pests like the fall armyworm that seek the cool, moist center of the plant to feed safely on tender green leaves away from direct heat and predators.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms ni taoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ hei ni mli ejɔ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ yɔɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Curling leaves with pale patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects sucking sap from plant to plant.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmeii ni etsake lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Agbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my maize produce long silky threads at the cob, and what do they do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ yɛ siliki kpãai kakadaji yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni etsuɔ?

english: The silks catch pollen floating in the wind from the top tassel. Each individual silk thread must receive pollen for a single corn grain to form on the cob.
ga: Siliki lɛ mɔ̃ɔ pollen ni hoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Esa akɛ siliki kpãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná pollen koni ŋmãa ŋmãa kome afee ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Maize is mature when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and a tiny dark black spot forms at the base of each kernel where it connects to the cob.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ batsɔ ŋmãa ni egbi kwraa. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Su ko ni tsuɔ diŋ baa yɛ ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni kɛ ŋmei lɛ kpaa gbee lɛ shishi.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn to powder and get full of holes when I store it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ feɔ powder kɛ ŋmeii kɛ́ mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Insects called weevils feed inside dry grains and lay eggs. If the maize isn't dried properly to low moisture levels before storage, weevils multiply quickly and ruin the grain.
ga: Kooloo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui ni egbi ni ewoɔ wɔji. Kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ baa shi dani akɛtoɔ ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ oya ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why does my maize grow better when I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, acting as natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa

english: How do I know if a pesticide I buy in the market is safe and approved for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Always look for an official approval label from the Plant Protection and Regulatory Services Directorate (PPRS). Safe pesticides have clear English instructions, active ingredients listed, and an official registration number on the bottle.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, taomɔ wolo ni tsɔɔ akɛ akpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛ Tsei Ahe Bulɛ kɛ Nitsumɔhe ni Kwɛɔ Tsei Anɔ lɛ (PPRS) lɛ dɛŋ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ Blɔfo mli. Nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ nɔmba ni aŋmala awo tɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why do agricultural officers recommend spraying my farm a second time a few weeks after the first treatment?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ shii enyɔ nɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ tsofafeemɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first spray usually kills the adult pests, but eggs already laid on the crops often survive. The second spray is necessary to kill the newly hatched insects before they grow old enough to lay more eggs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni eda lɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ hiɔ shi. Ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofa ni ji enyɔ awo mli koni akɛgbe kooloi bibii ni efɔ ehee lɛ dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast during rainy weather when there is too much shade and humidity around the cocoa trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ,.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This curling and yellowing is caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii mosaic hela lɛ mli. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ.

english: What causes the roots of my pepper plants to turn soft and rot under the ground?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Root rot happens when soil stays too wet for long periods, creating a environment where harmful soil fungi can attack and destroy the roots.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ atutua ni amɛfite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves fold up and look weak during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during the hottest part of the day to reduce water loss through their leaves, and they will naturally open up again once the weather cools in the evening.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ baai lɛ shi. ni ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning purplish instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ purple yɛ green ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Purplish leaves on young maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking phosphorus in the soil or that cold, wet ground is preventing the roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why does my yam crop grow thick green leaves but produce very small tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ hiɛ baai ni mli tse shi kɛ́ akpa lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the roots to build large tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ tsei ahe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ sisi a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: If I want to grow medicinal herbs alongside my main crops, will they affect how my crops grow?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miisumɔ ni madu tsofai yɛ mitsei titrii lɛ ahe hu? Ani tsofai baaná tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Wild medicinal herbs can compete with your main crops for water, sunlight, and soil food, so it is best to plant them in separate beds or along the farm boundaries.
ga: Koo mli tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛ otsei titrii lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu amɛ yɛ saatsoi ni yɔɔ srɔtoi amli loo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ husui ahe.

english: Can I bring crop seeds from another region or country and plant them straight into my field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpokpaa kroko nɔ loo maŋ kroko nɔ aba ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: It is risky to plant uncertified seeds because they can introduce new crop diseases or foreign pests to your land; seeds should be inspected by plant quarantine officers first.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ he odaseyeli ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei ahe helai heei loo maŋsɛɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ akwɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate intense heat. They need shade from larger trees or fast-growing food crops like plantains to protect them from sun damage and to keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo niyenii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantain lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little it has from the older lower leaves up to the newer top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ amli koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize relies on, while allowing pests and soil diseases that target maize to build up in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ srɔto ni abɛi damɔ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does growing groundnuts or cowpeas help make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the soil without proper drainage, the standing water suffocates the roots and promotes fungal diseases that cause rotting.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ baa.

english: The first rain of the season is often a 'false rain' followed by hot, dry days. If you plant right away, the hot soil and lack of follow-up rain will dry out and kill the germinating seeds before they can establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji ‘apasa nugbɔ’ ni gbi ni mli edɔ ni edɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ, egbiɔ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers when I give them wooden poles to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji beni mihaa amɛ tso ni akɛkwɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves act like power collectors that use sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Lifting the vines on stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and protects them from heat and diseases on the soil surface.
ga: Sweet potato baai tsuɔ nii akɛ hewalɛ nibii ni akɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi dɔlɛ kɛ helai ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the plant experiences sudden water stress. Severe heat prevents pollen from fertilizing the flower, causing the plant to discard it.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baatsi pollen lɛ naa koni ekawo fɔfɔi lɛ mli fɔ. ni haa tso lɛ shiɔ lɛ

english: Leaving too many suckers around one main plantain stem creates competition for water and soil nutrients. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest sucker, allowing the main plant to produce a much larger bunch.
ga: Ni aaashi ŋmeii lɛ abɔle tso titri kome he lɛ fa tsɔ. Enɛ baaha akaŋshii aba kɛha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ashiɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ niji wuji.

english: Upward twisting leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites, aphids, or thrips sucking the sap from young leaves, or transmitting viruses that distort leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii, aphids, loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni etsi ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo ekɛ helai ni haa baa lɛ adalɛ fiteɔ lɛ haa

english: Why do my crops start wilting and drying up so quickly around February in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii jeɔ shishi egboɔ ni egbiɔ oya waa yɛ February mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: February is usually the peak of the dry season in Ghana, with high temperatures and low air moisture. Crops lose water through their leaves much faster during this time, so without extra watering or soil protection, they quickly show signs of heat stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, February ji be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana. Dɔlɛ lɛ mli wa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ hu faaa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya kwraa yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ nu krɛdɛɛ ko bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo abuuu he lɛ, No hewɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ hulutsoo he haomɔ he okadii akpo oya.

english: Which crops can handle the dry February weather better if I have limited water on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baanyɛ atsu kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi yɛ February mli lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crops like cassava, cowpea, and millet have deep root systems or drought-tolerant features that allow them to survive dry periods much better than delicate crops like tomatoes or cabbage.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo amɛhe nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato loo cabbage.

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening is best. Watering during the hot midday heat causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ.

english: Should I water my young crops on a fixed daily schedule or wait until I see the leaves drooping?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo tsei bibii lɛ nu yɛ daa gbi gbɛjianɔtoo naa loo mamɛ kɛyashi baai lɛ baagbee shi?

english: It is better to keep a regular watering schedule before signs of wilting appear. Waiting until leaves droop causes stress that weakens the plant, reduces your eventual harvest, and makes the crop vulnerable to pests.
ga: Esa akɛ ato nu ni akɛhaa lɛ he gbɛjianɔ daa dani okadi ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ egbo lɛ aba. Kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ kɛyashi baai lɛ baagbi lɛ, ekɛ haomɔ ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ baa. Nikpamɔ fioo ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui

english: How early before the dry season starts should I prepare my watering schedule and sources?
ga: Te esa akɛ masaa mi nu ni mikɛhaa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ nu ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ he mra tɛŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: You should set up your water supply and irrigation plan at least two to three weeks before the dry season sets in. Preparing early prevents your crops from suffering sudden drought shock when the rains stop.
ga: Esa akɛ ofee nu kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ hoo lɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba. Hesaamɔ mra Ebaatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hɔmɔ trukaa kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: If water becomes scarce in my community, how can I keep the soil wet for longer?
ga: Kɛji akutso lɛ mli nu bɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground around your crop roots with dry grass, straw, or leaves (known as mulching) shades the soil from direct sunlight. This slows down water evaporation and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi, loo baai (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ koni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: How do I know if I am giving my crops too much water or too little water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikɛ nu miiwo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli babaoo loo fioo tsɔ?

english: If crops get too little water, the soil turns hard and leaves curl or dry up. If you give too much water, the soil stays muddy, leaves turn pale yellow, and roots can rot because they cannot get air.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nu fioo nɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha baai lɛ abɔle loo amɛbaagbi. Kɛji okɛ nu babaoo ha lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baakã he ahi shi akɛ muji. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agboi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Do my crops need the same amount of water when they are seedlings compared to when they start flowering?
ga: Ani nu ni he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni he hiaa dumɔwu lɛ nɔŋŋ? Kɛ akɛto be ni ebɔi fɔfɔii lɛ he?

english: No, crops need more water as they grow bigger, especially when they start flowering and forming fruits. Seedlings need light, frequent watering, while mature flowering crops need deeper watering to produce good yields.
ga: Dabi, nu babaoo he miihia tsei beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ ebɔi fɔfɔii ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ. Ehe miihia ni awo dumɔwui lɛ nu shii abɔ kɛ daa. Yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ nu ni mli kwɔ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying during the dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, the plant naturally sacrifices its older, bottom leaves to save moisture. It channels the limited water it has left to keep its upper young leaves and growing tip alive.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, tsei kɛ baai ni egbɔ kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shaa afɔle koni eye ebua ni ekwɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Ekɛ nu fioo pɛ yaa koni ekɛkwɛ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ kɛ nɔ ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I use water drawn directly from a dam or stream for my vegetable crops during dry periods?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ faa loo faa mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsu nii kɛha aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, stream or dam water is fine for crops, but it is best to apply it directly to the soil around the base of the plant rather than splashing the leaves, which can spread fungal diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni yɔɔ faai loo faai amli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshwie baai lɛ anɔ, ni baanyɛ agbala tsɛŋemɔ helai ashwã lɛ

english: What is the main difference between hybrid maize seed and OPV seed that I buy for planting?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ hybrid corn dumɔwui kɛ OPV dumɔwui ni miheɔ koni mikɛdu lɛ ateŋ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two distinct parent plants to give high yields and uniform growth, while OPV (Open-Pollinated Variety) seeds can be saved and replanted for the next season, though they usually produce slightly less grain than hybrids.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛha yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ OPV (open pollinated variety) dumɔwui lɛ ato ni adu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ amɛwoɔ dumɔwui fioo fe hybrids moŋ.

english: Why do different maize varieties behave differently on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Every maize variety has its own genetic traits, such as how tall it grows or how fast it matures. These unique characteristics determine how efficiently the plant uses sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to produce grain.
ga: Abɛi henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ efɔmɔ sui, tamɔ bɔ ni ekɛlɛ loo bɔ ni edaa oya. Sui nɛɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni tsei kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ koni amɛ wo dumɔwui.

english: If I buy high-quality maize seeds, why is that alone not enough to give me a big harvest?
ga: Kɛ mihe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwu kome pɛ faaa ni baaha mikpamɔ babaoo?

english: Good seeds only provide high yield potential, but that potential can only be reached if you set up the land properly, plant at the right spacing, and manage the crop according to its specific variety requirements.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai woɔ yibii babaoo pɛ. Shi nakai nyɛmɔ lɛ baanyɛ aba mli pɛ kɛji oto he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Adu yɛ he ni sa. ni ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ naa.

english: Why is the way I arrange and space my corn seeds in the field so important for my yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bɔ ni mitoɔ mi-ŋmã dumɔwui lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ he hiaa yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Proper field arrangement ensures that every single corn plant receives enough sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients without fighting with neighboring plants, allowing each cob to grow full and heavy.
ga: Dumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awui Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ehe feɔ tsiimɔ.

english: Does every type of maize need to be planted at the exact same distance apart in the field?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni adu ŋmãa henɔi fɛɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, different maize varieties have unique growth characteristics like plant height and leaf spread, meaning taller or wider varieties need more room between rows compared to shorter varieties.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa henɔi Eyɛ dalɛ sui srɔtoi tamɔ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛ baai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ loo amɛlɛɛmɔ lɛ baabi gbɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kuku lɛ ahe.

english: Why does planting my corn seeds at precise, measured distances help prevent crop health issues?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni asusu he pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ ŋmãa hela he naagbai anaa lɛ?

english: Precise spacing allows enough airflow and sunlight to pass between the corn stalks, which keeps leaves dry and reduces the chances of fungal diseases taking hold in your field.
ga: Gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tsɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: How does crowding my corn seeds together affect the growth of the plants?
ga: Te ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfataa he lɛ saa tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When corn plants are crowded together, they compete heavily for underground nutrients and surface light, leading to tall, thin stalks with small or poorly filled cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii kɛ la ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni dumɔwui bibii loo amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why do I get lower yields when I plant my maize seeds by hand without measuring?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mináa yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ́ mikɛ minine du ŋmãa dumɔwui ni misusuuu he lɛ?

english: Hand planting without measuring usually results in uneven seed depth and irregular spacing, causing seeds to sprout at different times and grow unequally across the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛ niji duɔ ni asusuuu he lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ amli boteɔ shi, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ hu kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli ni amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can moving from random hand-sowing to a structured field setup improve my harvest?
ga: Te tsakemɔ ni jɛɔ nine ni akɛduɔ nii trukaa lɛ nɔ kɛyaa dumɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baaha mikpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: A structured field setup gives every seed the exact same planting depth and room to grow, leading to uniform crop growth and maximum yields across the entire farm.
ga: He ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu mlibotemɔ kɛ he ni aduɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if a specific maize variety will perform well under my current planting methods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ ko baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛi ni mitsɔɔ nɔ miduɔ nii amrɔ nɛɛ shishi?

english: You can check with your local extension officer about the seed's specific characteristics, as some high-yielding varieties require precise planting distances and modern field setups to give full results.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ o-extension agent lɛ agba dumɔwui lɛ ahe saji. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei srɔtoi komɛi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ ni ato he pɔtɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ koni anyɛ ana yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my crops get damaged when I spray chemical medicine on them during a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai shwie nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spraying chemicals under intense midday sun causes the liquid to evaporate too fast or burn the leaves like hot water. It is best to spray early in the morning or late evening when the air is cool so the crop absorbs the medicine safely without getting damaged.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ loo ebaashã baai lɛ tamɔ nu ni mli edɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ koni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ tsofa lɛ shweshweeshwe ni ekɛ nɔ ko akafite.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and thin with tiny cobs when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu yɛ tso agbo ko shishi?

english: Maize needs full sunshine to make food and grow strong stalks. When planted in deep shade, the plant stretches upwards searching for light, leaving it with very little energy to produce large, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Hulu ni fa babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ efee niyenii ni ehiɛ tsei ni wa. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo pɛ ahi shi koni akɛwo ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look weak during the middle of the day even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. The leaves curl to protect themselves from losing more moisture, and they usually bounce back once the sun goes down and the air cools.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ he. Ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛyaa sɛɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks nutrients, especially nitrogen, which helps plants make food and stay healthy. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer gives the crop the strength it needs to turn green and yield bigger tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ otso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmeii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch and allowing good airflow helps the flowers stay on the stem and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Will I harvest more cassava if I plant my cuttings very close together on the farm?
ga: Ani makpa ŋmei babaoo kɛji midu tsei lɛ aniji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting too close creates competition among the plants for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each cassava plant proper space allows its roots to spread and form large, healthy tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa tsei ateŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ aha cassava tso fɛɛ tso he gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni efeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my vegetable leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-vegetables baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: That white powder is a fungal disease that spreads easily in warm, wet weather when plants are crowded together. Pruning lower leaves and giving crops proper breathing room allows air to dry the leaves and stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: White powder ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛ́ tsei eyi amɛhe obɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni oha amɛ he ni sa ni amɛmu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aha baai lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my maize crops grow greener and stronger when I plant cowpeas between the rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ewaa kɛji midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally feeds the neighboring maize crops with rich food, helping them grow greener without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aná niyenii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out crooked and small when planted in hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downwards by pushing into the earth. If the soil is hard, compacted, or full of rocks, the tuber cannot expand smoothly, leading to bent or undersized yams that are difficult to dig up.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa shi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Yitso lɛ hu nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baakɔ loo amɛbaafee bibii aahu akɛ ewa akɛ abaafo.

english: Why is burning dry weeds on my field bad for the soil before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mishãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ dani miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Burning weed cover destroys beneficial living organisms in the soil that break down organic matter into natural food for crops. It also dries out the topsoil, making it harder for new crop roots to find moisture and nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni gbálaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi heei lɛ akɛ amɛaana ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to make leaves green and healthy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛ baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grew maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?
