english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, especially nitrogen. Groundnuts and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen from the air and fix it back into the soil, naturally restoring nutrients for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop yields drop when I plant my seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to produce large grains or fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo dumɔwui loo aduawai wuji.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds around my young cassava plants every few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Cassava tso bibioo fɛɛ bibioo Otsii fioo komɛi?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and light from the soil. Clearing weeds gives your young cassava plants full access to those resources so they can form big tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa o-cassava tsei bibii lɛ náa nakai nibii lɛ fɛɛ. koni amɛfee yitsei wuji

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain sits in the soil without draining away, it drowns the roots, allowing rot fungi and bacteria to quickly decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu shwieee lɛ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long hot dry period before the main rains start. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout but then dry up and die in the hot soil due to lack of steady water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ daa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars eat my maize leaves mostly during the night and early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ kɛ leebi lɛ?

english: Pests like armyworms hide inside the plant leaves or in the soil during the hot afternoon to stay cool and avoid birds. They come out during the cooler hours at night to feed on soft leaves.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tsei ahe baai loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ okpoi ahe Amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ amli koni amɛbaye baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do my stored dried maize grains end up full of small holes and insects after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni kooloi bibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Insects called weevils lay tiny hidden eggs inside the grains while they dry. Over time in warm storage, these eggs hatch into beetles that eat the inside of the grain, leaving powdery dust and holes behind.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Akɛwoɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ nibii ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli niyenii. Eshiɔ sũ kɛ bu yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant lacks steady water. Mulching the soil with dried grass and watering regularly keeps the roots cool so flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu daa. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Fɔfɔi lɛ batsɔ aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last maize harvest yield less crop than new certified seeds bought from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and can carry diseases from the previous season. Certified hybrid seeds are specially produced to resist pests, endure hot conditions, and yield much more grain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ashwã. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Enyɛɔ shiɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ ni ehaa dumɔwui ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out their roots. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees protects them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ oodu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and overly shaded conditions. You can prevent it by regularly harvesting ripe pods, pruning extra branches to let in sunlight and air, and clearing weeds around the base.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, fɔ́, kɛ shade babaoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni ooobua naa daa lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. ni ojie jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Side shoots (chupons) and extra branches steal food and water from the main tree without producing much fruit. Removing them allows the tree to focus its energy on producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Side shoots (chupons) kɛ niji krokomɛi juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo. Kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eeefee lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip and moves down the middle of lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the season helps keep the leaves green and boosts yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaagbɛ ni eyaa shishi kɛyaa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-ŋmã lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that eats young maize leaves and stems. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides into the leaf funnel will protect your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each stalk enough room to grow thick and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baaha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Standing water suppresses weeds that compete with young rice plants for light and nutrients. Keeping a light layer of water in lowland fields also keeps the soil moist and supports healthy root growth.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi ni kɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ anaa. Kwɛmɔ ni aná nu ni mli tseee Yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are many of my rice grains empty and light at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa lɛ babaoo egboi ni ekpɛɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Empty rice grains often happen if birds feed on the soft, milky grains before they harden, or if the soil lacks key nutrients during flower formation. Using scarecrows or bird nets and applying proper fertilizer during flowering ensures heavy grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko baa kɛji okpoi ye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo dani amɛwa. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo okpo ŋtayaa tsu nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ afee shwiili.

english: Why shouldn't I burn my land before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani miduɔ nii?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and beneficial soil insects that feed your crops. Clearing the land without burning allows the plant material to rot and turn into natural compost that keeps soil moist and fertile.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ sũ mli kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ amli nibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests to build up. Rotating crops, especially with beans or groundnuts, restores soil fertility and stops pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi shwereɔ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sun and can dry out quickly. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛ baanyɛ agbi oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tso lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, humid conditions. Pruning dense branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm, which helps dry out moisture and prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gĩɔ, ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a key nutrient maize needs for leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer near the plant roots will help restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni ŋmãa he hiaa koni baa lɛ akwɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my maize farm within the first three weeks of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ ni mikɛdu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young maize plants have weak roots at first. If weeds grow around them early on, they steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients the young maize needs, which permanently slows down crop growth and reduces yield.
ga: Abele tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shishijee mli. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi tɔ̃ɔ. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa abifao lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi daa ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do I need to make high soil mounds or ridges before planting my cassava and yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ama gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ dani adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei?

english: High mounds loosen the soil so tubers can expand freely underneath without resistance. Mounds also improve drainage so heavy rains do not cause water to stand around the roots and rot them.
ga: Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã amɛshishi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akatsi amɛnaa. Gɔji hu haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akaha nu abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why are my cassava leaves shrinking and showing yellow wrinkled patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus transmitted by tiny whiteflies. To stop it from spreading, plant stem cuttings taken only from healthy, disease-free plants or resistant cassava varieties.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Bɔni afee ni ekagbɛ eshwa Afolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni helai bɛ mli loo ŋmei henɔi ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ hela lɛ pɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep dropping off before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture consistent and avoiding excess nitrogen helps the plant hold its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yibii amli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward during hot sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural response to protect the plant from losing too much water in intense heat. Ensuring regular watering in the cool morning helps the plant manage heat stress.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hetoo ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni awo tso lɛ nu daa yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsu dɔlɛ he haomɔ he nii.

english: Why shouldn't I burn crop remains on my field after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Burning crop remains destroys valuable organic matter and kills helpful organisms living in the soil. Leaving crop remains to rot back into the soil adds natural nutrients and helps hold moisture for the next planting season.
ga: Nibii ni eshwɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ gbɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ afata he yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when light wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Plantains fall easily when pests like stem weevils or microscopic root worms (nematodes) damage the underground roots and stem base. Using clean planting material and mulching protects the root structure.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem weevils loo shishifãi bibii ni anaa lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. (Nematodes) lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi kɛ shishifãi. Kɛ akɛ dumɔ nibii ni he tse kɛ mulching tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their dark green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe su kɛ dalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my tomato plants with dried grass during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dried leaves or grass—called mulching—acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and prevents moisture from evaporating into the air too quickly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya tsɔ.

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to produce big, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ he tse kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Why is it helpful to cut off the extra tiny branches growing on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ no hewɔ lɛ ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Removing these extra shoots, called suckers, stops the plant from wasting energy on growing extra leaves. This forces the plant to send its food directly into making larger fruits.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine nɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ kɛtsɔ baai ni fa fe nine ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tso yibii wuji amli.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that create living shade, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu lɛ.

english: Maize pulls nutrients out of the ground, but leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts put nitrogen back into the soil, naturally refreshing the land for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha jɛmɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to eat holes through the fresh leaves inside the center of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ni oooye bu ko kɛtsɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: These pests are usually Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant where it is soft and moist, feeding on the developing leaves before they open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli, he ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the land without draining, it smothers the roots and creates the wet conditions that cause root rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ko ni mli edɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if they are growing next to them without covering them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi moŋ? Ni akɛhaaa nɔ?

english: Weed roots spread quickly underground and steal water and soil fertilizer away from your crop's roots long before you notice the plants suffering above ground.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe dani oyɔseɔ tsei lɛ ni miipiŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make food and build larger corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni tso lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii ni ekwɛ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant groundnuts on the same land as cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are special plants that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, which feeds the cassava and keeps your farmland rich without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji tso krɛdɛɛ ko ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ekwɛɔ ŋmei ni eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofai ni jara wa atsu nii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt and drop during the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛshwieee shi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense heat, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up, so they droop to shield themselves from the sun. Covering the soil around the plant stem with dry leaves or straw helps trap moisture in the soil.
ga: yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. No hewɔ lɛ, tomato shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwie tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and spoil before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungus called black pod disease, which spreads quickly in wet, dark places. Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and fresh air into your tree canopy, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fuŋɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ lɛ Niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote tso lɛ shishi. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows with measured spaces instead of scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni gbɛ kã amɛteŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets its own fair share of sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing against neighboring plants, making it much easier for you to weed and harvest.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa nɔ. ni okɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ akaŋ Akaŋ Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ oookpa jwɛi ni oookpa.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant garden eggs on the exact same patch of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the dirt and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating to legumes like cowpeas restores nutrients and starves remaining pests.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ atsake kɛtee ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences sudden temperature changes, irregular watering, or a lack of key minerals like calcium, which causes the plant to abort its fruits to conserve energy.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo tsakemɔi trukaa. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa loo nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ, ni haa tsei lɛ shiɔ aduawai koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Weeds act like intruder plants that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops' roots, effectively starving your plants so they do not have enough energy to develop properly.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei ni boteɔ shi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsɔ hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do many of the seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout when planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Farm-saved seeds often fail to sprout if they were stored in damp conditions, attacked by small insects, or harvested from weak parent plants. Using fresh, certified seeds ensures strong, uniform germination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni ŋmeii bibii tutuaa lɛ loo ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ mli Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa ekwɛ̃ɔ waa ni ehiɔ shi daa.

english: Why do my harvested yams begin to rot rapidly after I place them in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni mikɛwo nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they were scratched during harvesting or kept in hot, poorly ventilated storage rooms where fungal spores can enter cuts on the skin and spread from tuber to tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto nitoohe ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ mli. Fungal spores lɛ baanyɛ abote pilamɔi ni yɔɔ hewolo nɔ lɛ amli ni egbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ tuber kome mli kɛya ekroko mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right stage helps the leaves turn green and photosynthesize properly to produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfee fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know which direction is up when I am planting cassava stem cuttings in my farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni obaadu o-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ?

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes along the stem cutting. These buds should always point upwards toward the sky; planting them upside down will delay sprouting and lower your harvest yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nodes lɛ jogbaŋŋ. along the stem cutting line Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ adu nii awo ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ fioo, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without growing into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, water supply is irregular, or small insects like thrips attack the blossoms. Keeping soil moisture steady and using shade or insect management helps the plant set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ shade loo kooloi akwɛmɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do extension officers encourage me to plant beans or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi hewalɛ koni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally feeds the surrounding maize crop, improving soil fertility and reducing the amount of chemical fertilizer you need to buy.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ aye niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i babaoo. ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ aba shi

english: Black Pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, damp shade. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds around the base of the tree helps the air stay dry and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Blaki pod hela jɛɔ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni efɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la aba mli, ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: How can I prevent my seed yams from rotting in the ground after I cut and plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni mifolɔ amɛ ni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Freshly cut seed yams have open wounds that easily attract rot in moist soil. Rubbing wood ash on the cut surfaces and letting them dry in the shade for a few days before planting seals the cut and protects it from soil germs.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni afolɔ ehee lɛ yɛ pilamɔi ni agbele naa ni ehaa egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ oya. Okɛ tso sũ awo he ni afo lɛ nɔ ni oha egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii fioo komɛi dani odu koni ekɛtsi he ni afo lɛ naa ni ebu he kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and wilt during the middle of the day even when the soil is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko kwraa moŋ?

english: In intense sun, pepper leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it up, causing temporary wilting. Covering the soil around the plant base with dry grass or leaves keeps the roots cool and holds moisture in the ground.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it so important to clear weeds from my farm within the first month of planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni mikɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young maize seedlings are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing weeds in the first 3 to 4 weeks gives your crop a strong start before the weeds can choke it.
ga: Abele dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ ashi akaŋ yɛ hulu la mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ dani jwɛi lɛ anyɛ agbe amɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain suckers turning brown and dying off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: This is often caused by leaf spot diseases or pests like plantain root borers attacking the corm. Cutting off infected leaves and planting only clean, treated suckers stops the problem from spreading across the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa mli hela loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ plantain root borers ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Afoɔ baa ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni aduɔ ŋmeii ni he tse ni atsa amɛ pɛ. Enɛ baaha naagba lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to settle before planting seeds instead of planting right after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ waa dani madu dumɔwui? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell. Seeds planted too early will sprout and then dry up and die in the hot soil before the next rain falls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Planting maize too close together makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper space ensures they grow strong stems and produce large, full ears of corn.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha eshishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni ewo ŋmãa toi agboi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under direct heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava to shelter them and keep the surrounding soil moist while their roots mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Koni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahi shi ni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread from plant to plant by small whitefly insects. Infected plants produce tiny tubers because damaged leaves cannot make food for the root.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Agbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmei bibii yɛŋ nɔ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ejaakɛ baai ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii aha shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why should I pluck off and destroy leaves with dark spots from my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ pepper tsei amli lɛ ni makpãtã amɛhiɛ?

english: Dark spots are usually caused by fungal or bacterial diseases. Plucking and burning infected leaves prevents rain drops or farm tools from splashing the disease spores onto healthy leaves nearby.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal loo bacteria helai kɛ helai ni tsuɔ diŋ baa. Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ ni ashãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nugbɔshiimɔi loo okwaayeli nibii akashwieɔ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato crops get sick if I plant them in the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ saatso kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes repeatedly in the same soil allows tomato-specific pests and fungal spores to build up in the ground. Rotating with different crops like maize or beans starves those soil diseases.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ tomato he lɛ baanyɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ naa

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop in the middle of the afternoon even when the ground was wet in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Nɛgbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ leebi?

english: In intense midday heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can absorb it. Plants temporarily droop to protect themselves from water loss and usually perk back up as temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli latsaa be lɛ mli lɛ, latsaa ni naa wa waa ba. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni nu akafite. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: Why do my bean flowers drop off without forming pods when the weather gets very dry and hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and drought stress cause bean plants to drop their blossoms as a survival mechanism, saving energy for the plant rather than spending it on forming seeds.
ga: Haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli baa lɛ haa ŋmeii tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo moŋ fe ni eeefite kɛfee dumɔwui.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my young maize turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tips of lower leaves means the maize is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen feeds leaf growth, and when soil lacks it, the plant moves nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. Nitrogen haa baa lɛ daa. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn a dark purple color during long rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ purple ni tsuɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Purple leaves occur when cold, waterlogged soil prevents roots from absorbing phosphorus. Once the weather clears and the soil warms up and dries, roots resume taking up phosphorus and leaves green up.
ga: Foji ni ji purple lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ fɔsfɔs. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ. Shishifãi lɛ hu kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛba koni amɛbahe fɔsfɔs ni amɛha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli.

english: Why do crops growing close to weeds turn pale green and grow slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ jwɛi ahe lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa blɛoo lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal nitrogen and water directly from your crops. Without enough nitrogen, crop leaves lose their rich green color and cannot make the food needed for fast growth.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nitrogen kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ baaje amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya lɛ atsu nii.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them provides the canopy and moisture young cocoa needs to grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi. Tsei ni ashiɔ amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Enɛ baaha ŋwɛi ŋta kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛdara waa lɛ aba.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots near the surface of the soil and carry heavy bunches at the top. To keep them standing during strong winds, you need to support the fruiting stems with bamboo poles or strong wooden forks.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni fɔfɔii ni tsii yɛ nɔ. Kɛji oosumɔ ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ, Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmei tsei loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni wa afi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil is running low on nitrogen, an essential food for green growth. Adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer near the base of the plants will help restore their dark green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmɔŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ su ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ kpakpa aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize in the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and lets specific pests accumulate in the ground. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni oha tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: What is making holes in the fresh leaves inside the center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: Holes and saw-dust-like waste in the center of young corn plants are caused by caterpillars, commonly Fall Armyworms. Checking your farm early in the morning and using recommended organic or chemical sprays in the leaf whorl will save your crop.
ga: Buji kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii kɛbaa. Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground after a heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates them by cutting off air in the soil. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily and keeps the roots safe from rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni ekɛ mumɔ baa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to soaked. Mulching the base of the plant to keep the soil at a steady moisture level and temperature helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ha tso lɛ shishi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛ latsaa be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to use sticks to lift my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso nine awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the leaves into the sunlight and off the wet ground where diseases spread. When leaves catch more sunlight, they produce more energy to grow bigger yam tubers underneath.
ga: Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ. Ebaaha hewalɛ babaoo aba ni eha sweet potato tuber lɛ adara babaoo yɛ shishi.

english: Why does covering the dirt around my crops with dry grass make them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the ground, prevents weeds from growing, and slowly turns into nutrient-rich compost as it decomposes.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ, ni fiofio lɛ, etsɔɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden in the cool morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso loo shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso?

english: Watering early in the morning gives plants the moisture they need before the sun gets hot. Afternoon watering wastes water through evaporation and can burn delicate leaves heated by the intense sun.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni enáa nu ni he hiaa lɛ dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa shwane mli lɛ baafite nu kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eha baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he dɔlɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them out in the open sun without any plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse ni plantains ko bɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that dry out and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains alongside cocoa provides immediate shade and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ kookoo he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal food, light, and water from the main mother plant. Removing excess suckers leaves only the strong main plant to produce bigger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ebɔle plantain kome he lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii, la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso titri ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baaha ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ pɛ ahi shi.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my corn seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain after a long dry spell is often followed by several weeks of heat without rain. If you plant immediately, seeds germinate but then dry up and die; waiting for consistent rain ensures enough soil moisture to sustain young shoots.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ Bei pii lɛ, otsii babaoo ni mli edɔɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of maize stems usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food corn needs to grow green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores color and helps the plant produce full ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does my land yield fewer crops every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?

english: Maize continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without putting anything back. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ekɛ nɔ ko fataaa he ekoŋŋ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: How does spreading dry grass over my vegetable beds help my crops survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the ground shaded and prevents water from evaporating quickly. It also stops weeds from taking over and keeps the soil cool during hot afternoons.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni jwɛi akayeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, when soil moisture changes suddenly from dry to wet, or when insects fail to pollinate the flowers. Keeping irrigation consistent helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines climb to catch sunlight, which leaf surfaces use to create food for the growing tuber under the soil. Staking keeps leaves off the hot ground, protects them from soil diseases, and allows tubers to grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Akɛ baai lɛ ahiɛ feɔ niyenii ahaa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ahe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo babaoo

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving tiny black spots behind?
ga: Mɛni ji mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ ŋmeii diji bibii yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing cone of young maize plants. Checking crops early and applying neem extract or recommended sprays directly into the leaf center prevents leaf destruction.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli. Nibii ni akwɛɔ mli mra Ni akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ akafite.

english: Why does my harvested cassava start turning dark and rotting just two days after digging it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ bɔi duŋ ni efite yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni mikɛfo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots react quickly with air and lose moisture rapidly, causing internal rot within 48 to 72 hours. It is best to leave cassava roots buried in the soil until the exact day you are ready to sell or process them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ amɛnii oya kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ oya. Enɛ haa emli lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi gbi ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ loo obaatsu he nii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing well after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water in the soil washes away vital nutrients like nitrogen and starves the roots of air. Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant cannot get enough nitrogen from the soil to stay healthy and green.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I tell if I am putting too much fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo miiwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: When crops receive too much fertilizer, the edges of their leaves look scorched or brown, a condition called fertilizer burn. The plant might also grow very tall and bushy with leaves but fail to produce good fruit or seeds.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashãa. Tsei baanyɛ adara waa ni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwooo yibii loo dumɔwui kpakpai.

english: If your soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium faaa lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why is there usually a shortage of fresh tomatoes in Ghana during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, tomato ŋmɔŋ faaa yɛ Ghana yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Most tomato farming relies on rain. During the dry season, water becomes scarce, causing national production to drop significantly until farmers with irrigation systems harvest their crops.
ga: Tomato ŋmɔshi nibii damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ babaoo. Yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ, nu baa shi, ni no haa maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa kɛyashi okwaafoi ni yɔɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baakpa amɛdumɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up inward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense against extreme heat. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to conserve moisture and avoid drying out.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ baa amɛhe nɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛtsi amɛbaai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or nutrient stress. It is the plant's way of conserving energy to stay alive until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ he haomɔ he. Eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atoɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni tsei ahi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to yield more tons per acre, resist common local diseases, and tolerate weather changes better than saved seeds, which lose their strength over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo nɔ ni fe tɔn kome yɛ acre kome mli. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi hu fe dumɔwui ni ato ni hewalɛ baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli

english: What causes plantain bunches on some farms to be very large while mine stay small?
ga: Mɛni haa plantains ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji komɛi amli lɛ daraa waa yɛ be mli ni minɔ lɛ ji bibioo waa lɛ?

english: Bunch size depends on soil nutrients and regular water supply during the flowering stage. Farms with organic manure and good soil moisture retention produce much heavier bunches.
ga: Bunch dalɛ damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni yɔɔ daa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ nɔ. Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ sũ mli nu ni ŋmɛɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ aba.

english: Why do crops seem to mature faster in hot weather than in cooler weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ fe hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures speed up a crop's internal chemical processes, causing it to flow through its life stages—from sprouting to flowering—much faster.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei tsɔɔ amɛshihilɛ mli kɛjɛɔ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ mli kɛyaa fɔfɔii amli oya.

english: How does planting my crops in straight, spaced rows increase my total harvest?
ga: Te tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spacing crops evenly ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants, allowing every individual plant to yield to its full potential.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ Ye obua tso fɛɛ tso ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without bearing much fruit when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ shi amɛwooo yibii babaoo beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, they compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients. They stretch upward to reach the light instead of using energy to grow strong stems and produce healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it better to put three or four maize seeds in one hole to get more food at harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ baawo bu kome mli koni aná niyenii babaoo yɛ kpamɔ be mli?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole causes the young plants to fight each other for root space and food. Planting fewer seeds per hole gives each plant enough space to produce larger, fuller cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ awuu koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ niyenii. Dumɔwui fioo ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmei agbo ni eyi obɔ.

english: How far apart should I space my plants when making my farm rows?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tsei amli kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ miito ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Proper row spacing depends on the crop, but giving plants enough room ensures their roots can spread out for water and their leaves can trap sunlight without shading neighboring plants.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ line lɛ teŋ lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Shi kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛmɔ nu. Ni amɛbaai lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la ni amɛtsĩii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my crops turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves often mean the top leaves are overcrowded and blocking sunlight from reaching the bottom, or the plant is losing the fight for soil nutrients against nearby crops or weeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ ebɔle tsɔ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shishigbɛ. Aloo tso lɛ miiye kunim yɛ ta ni ekɛ tsei loo jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ miiwu koni ená niyenii kpakpai yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds reduce my crop yield even if I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water and fertilizer meant for your crops. They act like extra hungry mouths at a table, leaving your crops weak and underfed.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ mɛi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ babaoo yɛ okpɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves but small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded or get too much leafy growth fertilizer, they put all their energy into leafy top growth rather than storing food down in the tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe loo akɛ baai babaoo ewo amɛmli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai bibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha niyenii ahi oyitsoŋ lɛ

english: Why do my tomato plants develop black spots and rot when they grow into a thick bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni amɛgboɔ beni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Overcrowded, bushy plants trap damp air around their leaves. Without proper space for wind to dry the leaves, fungal diseases spread quickly in the damp, closed space.
ga: Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔji lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ amɛbɔleɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛji he ko bɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ agbi baa lɛ. Fungal helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni aŋã, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why is black pod disease worse in parts of my cocoa farm where the canopy is very thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ ehiii kwraa yɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: A canopy that is too dense blocks air and sunshine from reaching the pods underneath. The trapped moisture allows the black pod fungus to multiply and spread fast.
ga: Tsu lɛ yiteŋ ni etse tsɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa black pod fungus lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do some young cocoa pods shrivel and fall off the tree before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii komɛi gboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Trees drop extra pods when they carry more fruit than their roots can feed. This happens often if the trees are stressed by drought, poor soil, or severe shade.
ga: Tsei woɔ ŋmeii babaoo kɛ́ amɛwo yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛji hɔmɔ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, loo hulutsoo be ni mli wa miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: Why should I keep clear pathways between my farm plots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ he hiaa mi yɛ mishikpɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Clear pathways allow air to flow freely across the farm to dry wet leaves, make it easy for you to inspect crops for pests, and create barriers that slow down the spread of diseases.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli tse lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya koni eha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaakwɛ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ onibii amli. ni amɛfee gbɛtsii nii ni haaa helai agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and conserving soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hɔɔŋ ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the young shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishɛreɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ashwieɔ? mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo

english: When too many shoots grow around a single plantain stalk, they compete for nutrients and water, resulting in smaller bunches. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one or two main stems, ensuring bigger and healthier fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ, Plantains baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso bibioo ni afoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ yibii titri kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi, ni ebaaha yibii lɛ afee wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the plants are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize plants use nitrogen to build green leaves, so when soil nutrients run low, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older leaves to support new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei kɛ nitrogen tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee.

english: Why does rice thrive in standing water while my maize rots in flooded ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shwereɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes that transport oxygen from the leaves down to the roots under water. Maize roots lack this feature, so standing water starves their roots of oxygen and causes them to rot.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Abele shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ, ni ebaaha amɛgboi.

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of surviving drought. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation, resting quietly until the rains return to produce new leaves and grow its roots.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji cassava adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejoɔ hɔmɔ naa foi. Kɛtsɔ baai ni eshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. jɔɔ ohe dioo Kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ eba ni ekɛ baai heei aba ni ekwɛ shishifãi.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes more leaf area to light and prevents damp leaves on the ground from catching fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baa lɛ he lɛ aná la babaoo, ni ebaatsi baai ni mli ewo fɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná tsɛŋemɔ hela.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, drought, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the plant hold its blossoms and produce peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei na nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused by calcium deficiency or irregular watering. When soil moisture fluctuates dramatically, the tomato plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil to form the bottom wall of the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsake waa lɛ Tomato tsei nyɛŋ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛma aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ gbogbo lɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts help improve my farm's soil for next season?
ga: Te ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop is harvested, these nutrients stay in the soil to nourish future crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ Niyenii nibii nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaba wɔsɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the midday sun even if the ground was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ gboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi po.

english: During peak afternoon heat, leaves lose water faster than the roots can pull it from the soil. The plant wilts to shrink its leaf area and slow down water loss, usually recovering once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛha baai lɛ afee bibioo ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fiofio. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa tree keep falling off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack moisture, shade, or pollination from tiny insects called midges. Keeping shade trees on your farm and avoiding harsh chemical sprays during flowering helps more flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛbɛ ŋmɔtɔ, hulutsoo loo pollination ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii amli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii babaoo baa ni amɛfeɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and feel sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and stickiness are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids sucking the sap from the plant. Spraying the leaves with neem leaf extract or mild soapy water helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Ni akɛ neem tso mli nu loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie baai lɛ anɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off when the heat becomes very intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Extreme sun heat causes pepper plants to drop flowers to save water and protect themselves. Giving the plants light shade or watering early in the morning helps them retain their flowers so peppers can form.
ga: Hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo ha tso lɛ loo okɛ nu wo enɔ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains key nutrients like nitrogen from the soil and allows maize pests to build up. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa abɛi mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why don't cowpea or groundnut crops need as much fertilizer as maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea loo peanut tsei ahe ehiaaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts work with good bacteria in the soil to trap nitrogen gas from the air and feed themselves. Because they make their own plant food, they require very little extra fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ bacteria kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛhe niyenii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfeɔ amɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ ni akɛfataa he.

english: What benefit does spreading dry grass around the base of my plants provide?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ tso shishi lɛ he?

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under hot sunshine and traps water so you don't need to water as often. Over time, the grass breaks down and adds richness back into the soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni aduɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the young shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one main stem and one or two strong suckers ensures the tree grows big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ shishifã titri kome pɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ adara ni etsɔ aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why must I put wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso he hiaa mi koni mikɛha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the sunlight to produce the energy required to grow big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp soil, protecting them from rot and disease.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. yɛ hulu la mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai anaa

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛtsuuu nii fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is generally ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off. You can test-dig just one root from a plant at the edge of the farm to check if the tubers are big enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka tso ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ shishifã kome ni ooofo lɛ okwɛ kɛji shishifã lɛ da bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the big trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct, harsh sunlight dries out the soil and burns their leaves. Leaving mature trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains creates a living umbrella that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni eshã baai lɛ. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight. Elevating the vines on stakes helps the leaves catch more sunlight to produce food, which is then sent down into the ground to grow larger, healthier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni ekɛwo niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ enɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older leaves to feed the young upper growth, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei bibii lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many leaves but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks nutrients like potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into leaf growth above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium bɛ mli. Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why should I plant legumes like cowpea on my land after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa, tamɔ tsina ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikpa ŋmãa? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ

english: Maize takes nutrients out of the soil, while legumes like cowpeas have special root nodules that draw nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally renewing the soil for future crops.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ hee kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do my crop seeds rot in the ground when I sow them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too soon, seeds absorb moisture to start growing but then dry out and rot in the hot soil before continuous rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu koni amɛje dalɛ shishi. Shi no sɛɛ lɛ, egbiɔ ni egboɔ yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baa.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my crop field so the heavy rains do not carry it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo midumɔhei lɛ amli? Koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akaho?

english: Applying fertilizer when the soil is moist and crops are actively growing—rather than right before expected heavy rainfall—ensures the crop roots absorb the nutrients before rain washes them deep into the soil or off the field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha yɛ be ni sa mli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii kpakpai dani nugbɔ lɛ kɛ amɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo ejɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.
