english: What causes tiny caterpillars to hide inside the central leaves of my young maize plants and eat holes through them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Mikɛ mihe woɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni miyeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ amɛmli.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which target the inner funnels of young maize plants where it is moist. Identifying them early helps you protect the central growing point of the plant before it gets destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amligbɛ gbɛi ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ anɔ. mra be mli ni ayɔseɔ Enɛ baaha onyɛ obu tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa lɛ he dani efite.

english: Can I plant cassava and plantain close together on the same piece of land, or will they affect each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ plantain ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome? Aloo ani ebaaná amɛhe nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cassava and plantain can grow together, but if planted too close, their roots will fight for the same water and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller plantains and poor cassava roots.
ga: Kasava kɛ plantain baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ he kome. Shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yeɔ egbɔ yɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli. Enɛ haa plantains bibii kɛ cassava shishifãi ni ehiii baa.

english: If people build houses and clear trees on the land right next to my farm, will that change how my crops grow?
ga: Kɛji gbɔmɛi ma tsũi ni amɛjie tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ani ebaatsake bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Clearing nearby land removes windbreaks and shade, making the air around your farm warmer and dryer. Stronger winds can break your crops, and hotter ground dries out soil moisture faster.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, ebaajie kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei kɛ hulutsoo. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ Oŋmɔ lɛ mli adɔ ni egbi. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ afite onibii. Ni hei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps the leaves turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni eha baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize stalks with brownish dust coming out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ nɔ kɛ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo?

english: This damage is caused by stem borers, which are caterpillars that hatch from moth eggs and eat into the stem. Spraying an approved pesticide early inside the center leaf whorl kills the worms before they destroy the plant from the inside.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji stem borers. Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii akui amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛboteɔ tso lɛ mli. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, amɛgbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛkpãtãa tso lɛ hiɛ kɛjɛɔ emli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Leaving tall trees or planting plantains provides shade and keeps the air moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough for full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to hold the heavy weight of a maturing fruit bunch during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a double wooden prop (bamboo or branches) keeps the plant upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Akɛ sɛɛfimɔ tsei enyɔ fiɔ tsɔne wulu lɛ sɛɛ. (Bamboo tsei loo tsei niji) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Water sitting in the soil starves the roots of air and encourages fungal rot. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots remain healthy.
ga: Nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground, maximizing sun exposure and preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni otsi baa helai anaa

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist and using balanced fertilizer helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo fɔsfɔs ni faaa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and turning crinkly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites sucking the sap and spreading a plant virus. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or insecticidal soap prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them stay healthy during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eha amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground, keeps root temperature cool, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why is my field rice falling flat on the ground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa nii lɛ?

english: Rice stalks fall over (lodge) when they grow too tall and weak, usually from using too much nitrogen fertilizer or planting seeds too close together. Proper spacing and balanced nutrients keep the stalks sturdy.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi (overhang) kɛji tsei lɛ kwɔ tsɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sun, the delicate leaves burn, lose moisture quickly, and turn yellow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ Koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa Baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baashã. Efoɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Plantains have shallow roots that stay near the surface of the soil. When the heavy fruit bunch grows, the top becomes too heavy for the shallow roots to support, so you need to prop up the stem with strong wooden poles.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji akɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baafee tsiimɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua, no hewɔ lɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ tsei ni wa afi tso lɛ shishi.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves with sawdust-like powder inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the growing center of the maize plant and chew through the leaves, leaving behind waste that looks like fine sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Eshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei kpakpa yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during the hot afternoon even when the soil has enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Ani nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt. Bacteria enter the plant through the roots from warm, wet soil and block the narrow tubes that carry water up the stem, causing the plant to collapse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muawai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Muawai boteɔ tso lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi amli kɛjɛɔ sũ ni mli edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ mli. kɛ paipii bibii ni tsiɔ nu kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei shwieɔ shi

english: Why does my maize harvest get smaller every year if I plant it on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes high amounts of nitrogen and nutrients out of the ground. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains those specific nutrients from the soil unless you rotate with beans or add fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ja okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii wo mli.

english: Why shouldn't I place dry fertilizer directly against the main stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts. Putting them directly against the stem draws water out of the plant tissue and burns the stems and roots, which can stunt or kill the crop.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ fãji lɛ amli. ni ashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbo.

english: Why are my cassava tubers small and woody even though the stems grew very tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛji tsei eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ waa ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing leaves and branches instead of storing starch in the underground roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ eniji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: How do I know if the first rainfall after the dry season is safe for planting seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Early rains can be 'false rains' that leave the soil dry a few days later. You should dig into the ground and ensure the soil is thoroughly moist down to about a hand's depth before planting.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ afee ‘nugbɔ ni nɛɔ amale’ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Esa akɛ otsa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ aaafee inchi kome dani okɛdu.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food for growing underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to light and prevents soil-borne diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ naa la, ni ehaaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akatutua baai lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and spoil so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and generate internal heat after being picked. If they are left under hot sun or packed tightly into warm containers, heat builds up rapidly and breaks down the fruit tissues, causing fast rot.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekɛ mligbɛ dɔlɛ baa beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo akɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni mli edɔ ni mli wa mli. Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa oya ni efiteɔ aduawai lɛ amli fãji lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fitemɔ oya

english: Does the time of day I pick my tomatoes affect how long they stay fresh?
ga: Ani gbi lɛ mli be ni mikɛbaakpa mi-tomato lɛ baaná be ni amɛhiɔ shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, harvesting during midday heat stresses the crop, causing rapid water loss and early spoilage. Picking crops early in the morning when temperatures are cool keeps the fruit firm and extends its shelf life.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmaakpamɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya ni efiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha aduawai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni eha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do tomatoes harvested late in the afternoon make watery or bad-tasting soup?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni akpaa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa shwiili feɔ nu loo ehiii lɛ?

english: When tomatoes sit under intense heat late into the day, their natural sugars break down and water balance changes. This loss of essential sugars and acids reduces their natural flavor and firmness when cooked.
ga: Kɛ́ tomato ta la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Tomato adebɔɔ mli sugars lɛ fiteɔ ni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ. Nɛkɛ sugar kɛ acid ni he hiaa ni laajeɔ nɛɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ kɛ shifimɔ baa shi kɛ́ ahoo.

english: If my transport car is delayed, how should I keep my picked tomatoes from spoiling on the farm?
ga: Kɛji mitsɔne lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ Mɛni esa akɛ afee koni tomato ni ajie lɛ akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Keep harvested tomatoes under a shaded canopy or tree, spread them out slightly to allow cool air to pass through, and never leave them stacked in sealed bags exposed to the sun.
ga: Okɛ tomato ni akpa lɛ ato hulutsoo shishi loo tso ko shishi. Gbalamɔ mli fioo koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ atsɔ mli. Ni kaato amɛ yɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers advise using wooden crates instead of deep sacks to carry tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tso adekai atsu nii moŋ fe kotokui ni mli kwɔlɔ ni akɛtoɔ tomatoi lɛ?

english: Deep sacks trap heat and press heavy weight on the bottom tomatoes, crushing them and causing rapid decay. Crates protect the fruit from weight pressure and allow ventilation to keep them cool.
ga: Saak ni mli kwɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ la lɛ ni ekɛ muji baa tomatoi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ amɛ bibii bibii ni oha tomatoi lɛ agbo oya. Krɛti lɛ buɔ aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shwiili ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ he, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli koni aduawai lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Can I harvest my tomatoes while they are still pale green so they don't spoil on the farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa tomato be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo koni ekafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, picking tomatoes at the mature green or light pink stage allows them to ripen safely during transport without losing quality, preventing them from over-ripening or rotting on the farm while waiting for transport.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tomato to eŋɔli loo eŋɔli ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa amɛshwereɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ mli ni amɛfiteee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Etsiɔ tomato naa koni ekakwɛ fe nine loo ekafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni emɛɔ gbɛfaa.

english: Tomato leaves curl during peak hot hours as a natural defense mechanism to conserve water and prevent moisture from escaping under intense sunlight.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he ni akɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje kpo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my tomatoes burst or crack open after a heavy rain following a dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When dry tomato plants suddenly receive a lot of water, the inside of the fruit grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to split open.
ga: Kɛ́ tomato tsei ni egbi lɛ ná nu babaoo trukaa lɛ, tso yibii lɛ loo lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium and irregular watering while the fruit is growing, not a disease or bad luck. Consistent watering helps the plant take up the calcium it needs.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Jeee hela loo shweremɔ ni ehiii. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants develop mold and rot faster when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting too closely blocks sunlight and traps humid air between leaves. Without fresh air flowing through the field, moisture stays on the plants and encourages fungal diseases to spread quickly.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baatsi hulu la naa ni ebaamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ko bɛ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ Fɛ̃i baakã tso lɛ nɔ ni ebaawo ŋmãa helai ahe hewalɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya.

english: How do I know if my land needs fertilizer even if my crops are still growing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida lolo po?

english: Crops can still grow in weak soil, but they will show signs like yellow leaves, poor flowering, and light harvests because the soil lacks the necessary nutrients to feed them properly.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ lolo. Shi ebaajie okadii tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ fɔfɔi ni ehiii. kɛ ŋmaa fioo Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekɛ niyenii ni sa aha.

english: Does my soil lose its richness over time if I keep harvesting cocoa from it every year?
ga: Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli kɛji mikpa kookoo kɛjɛ mli daa afi?

english: Yes, every crop you harvest takes natural food away from the earth. Over time, the soil becomes exhausted unless you add nutrients like compost, manure, or fertilizer back into it.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni okpaa lɛ heɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ja okɛ niyenii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it still necessary to add plant food to my farm if the land used to be a rich virgin forest?
ga: Ani ehe miihia lolo akɛ mikɛ tsei niyenii afata miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛji akɛ tsutsu lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji koo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Forest land starts with rich soil, but after several seasons of farming and harvesting, those original nutrients run out, and the land will eventually need extra food to stay productive.
ga: Kooi amli hei jeɔ shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii. Shi yɛ okwaayeli kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ bei babaoo sɛɛ lɛ Nakai shishijee niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ faaa. Ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, niyenii krokomɛi he baahia shikpɔŋ lɛ koni eya nɔ ewo yibii.

english: Why are my harvested cocoa beans weighing much lighter than usual when I take them to be weighed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii ni mikpa lɛ mli waaa kwraa fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ kɛ́ misusu he lɛ?

english: Light cocoa beans usually mean the trees did not get enough soil nutrients or water while the pods were developing, causing the seeds inside to remain small and thin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu mli beni ŋmeii lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe tseee.

english: Why do my crops produce a small harvest even though the rain was plenty this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ewo yibii fioo pɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Good rain helps plants grow, but water alone is not enough. If the soil lacks essential plant nutrients, the crops cannot produce full, heavy fruits or seeds.
ga: Nugbɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa. Shi nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ Dumɔwui nyɛŋ awo yibii loo dumɔwui ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your trees are starving for key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the roots are struggling to draw food from the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgbala niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani eda lɛ?

english: Young pods shrivel when the tree lacks enough soil nutrients or water to feed all of them, forcing the plant to shed some pods so the remaining ones can survive.
ga: Pods bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛ fɛɛ amɛye amɛbua lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ ajie ŋmeii komɛi koni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Trees shed flowers if the soil is too weak to support pod development, or if there are not enough beneficial insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tso lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua pod lɛ shweremɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ faaa.

english: If I cannot find chemical fertilizer to buy in the market, what else can I use to feed my farm?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ jara nɔ hu? Mɛni kroko mikɛbaatsu nii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ niyenii?

english: You can feed your farm naturally by spreading rotted cocoa pod husks, animal manure, or decomposed plant waste around the trees to return nutrients to the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii aha oŋmɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni egboi, kooloi ashishifãi, loo tsei amli ŋmeii ni oookɛshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Will putting fertilizer on dry ground during a dry spell help my crops grow faster?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: No, crops need soil moisture to drink in fertilizer. Applying fertilizer to very dry soil can burn the tree roots and waste your money until the rains arrive.
ga: Dabi, tsei he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛnu nu akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika kɛyashi nugbɔ baashɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore healthy leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii ni he hiaa waa he miihia tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experts advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nilelɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ, kɛ́ mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, esa akɛ madu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next season without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, keeps moisture in the ground during hot dry spells, protects root systems from extreme heat, and stops weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni otsĩ jwɛi ni yeɔ oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ naa.

english: What is the best way to apply fertilizer so the rain does not wash it all away?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mikɛwo mli koni nugbɔ lɛ akashwie nɔ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist rather than right before a heavy downpour, placing it a few centimeters away from the plant stem and covering it lightly with soil.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo moŋ fe be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Okɛto sɛntimitai fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to bore holes through the leaves and leaves funnels of my maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ tsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛjeɔ mi-corn cones lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young maize leaves and requires early detection and targeted treatment to save the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ehe miihia ni ana mra. kɛ tsofafeemɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the soil when rain falls continuously for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents air from reaching the roots, causing the soil to drown the plant tissues and creating a moist environment where fungal rot thrives on the cassava tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ tsei amli fãji amli ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off before they form any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop due to heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of insect pollination, which prevents the flower from developing into a fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ faaa Enɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ eyaaa nɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows with measured distances instead of scattering seeds freely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni asusu gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã heyeli mli lɛ

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors, making weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni akɛ akutsoŋbii ewuuuu Enɛ haa jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade the delicate cocoa trees while keeping the surrounding soil damp.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Lifting yam vines on wooden stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight for tuber growth and keeps the foliage off wet ground where leaf diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni tuber lɛ akwɛ̃. ni etsĩ baai lɛ anaa koni ekashwɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni baa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin when I plant them in hard, unplowed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need loose, well-tilled soil to expand easily underground. In hard, tightly packed soil, the roots struggle to penetrate deep enough to absorb water and cannot easily stretch out to store starch, resulting in woody, thin roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni edɔ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbote mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛŋɔ nu. ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei ni amɛhe tseee.

english: Why is my yam harvest poor even after using heavy machinery that packed down the soil flat on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpaaa mi-sweet potato lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ tsɔnei ni tsii etsu nii ni mikɛfee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ po lɛ?

english: Heavy machinery can compress the soil too tightly, which suffocates the soil and blocks root development. Yams require loose, soft soil—usually built up into raised mounds or ridges—so the tubers can easily push through the earth and grow long and thick.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato. Bei pii lɛ, amaa amɛ akɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya ni amɛdara ni amɛfee shwiili.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to bear fruit when planted on steep, stony hillsides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains need deep, moist, and nutrient-rich soil to feed their large leaves and heavy fruit bunches. Stony hillsides allow rainwater to wash away topsoil quickly, leaving the plant roots with limited water and nutrients to grow efficiently.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli edɔ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia plantains koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ baai wuji kɛ aduawai ni tsii. Gɔji ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei shishifãi lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and slender with small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When maize is planted too close, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The crop spends all its energy growing tall to reach light instead of using that energy to produce full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ́ amɛmiida yɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ koni amɛná la. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ jamɛ a he wami ɔ tsuɔ ní kɛ woɔ tso nɛ ngɛ he wami nɛ a he wa.

english: Why do young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up if I clear all the tall trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight. Shade trees act as living shields, protecting young cocoa leaves from scorching heat and keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gãimlibi ni hiɛ ka. Ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa

english: Why do weeds choke my young rice plants so quickly during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi shwieɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds in the soil germinate fast and swallow up water and nutrients quicker than young rice seedlings can. In the early stages, rice plants grow slowly and need clean ground so they aren't starved of light and nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe bɔ ni ŋmãa dumɔwui baanyɛ afee. Yɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná he ko ni he tse koni la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my pepper plants rot at the base whenever heavy rains leave standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni ekɛ nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants have delicate roots that need oxygen in the soil to breathe. Standing water cuts off air to the roots, causing root suffocation and allowing waterborne fungi to attack and rot the base of the stem.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni hoɔ yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa tso lɛ shishi ni efiteɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller groundnut harvests if I keep planting groundnuts on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji midu ŋmeii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets soil-borne pests and diseases build up over time. Rotating groundnuts with crops like maize or cassava restores soil balance and reduces disease pressure.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ be ni sa mli. Peanuts kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ekoŋŋ ni ehaa helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up and burn after I apply chemical fertilizer directly next to their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are strong salts. Placed too close to the main stem, they draw water out of the root zone, causing fertilizer burn which makes the leaves curl, turn brown, and dry up.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he tsɔ Ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashãa lɛ. ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi Etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ

english: Why are the leaves of my cowpea plants curling up and covered in a sticky liquid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni nu ni mli tse ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on cowpeas are usually caused by tiny sucking insects called aphids. They feed on the leaf juices and secrete a sweet, sticky fluid, which stunts the plant's growth and distorts the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ tsina ŋmei nɔ lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ aphids Amɛyeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu ni mli tse ni tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ kpo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither when I remove all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct sunlight because intense heat burns their leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool canopy that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ la ni naa wa lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Enɛ haa hulutsoo be ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce very small bunches when I plant them close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ woɔ panicles bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow thick trunks and yield large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse ni ewo aduawai agboi ni tsii.

english: Why should I wait for the rains to settle properly before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Planting maize during early erratic rains risks seed failure because a sudden dry spell after germination can scorch the delicate seedlings. Waiting for consistent rains ensures the soil stays moist enough for seeds to sprout and establish deep roots.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa mra lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ afee oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa yɛ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ashã. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛwo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Yellow and curled cassava leaves are typically caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant stem cuttings for planting prevents this disease from spreading and destroying your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii beni oduɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã ni efite onibii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and covering the soil with dry grass or mulch keeps the roots cool, helping the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ awo mli koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔii ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Extra shoots, known as chupons, draw energy and nutrients away from the main stem of the cocoa tree. Removing them regularly directs all the plant's food toward growing strong main branches and developing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ gbalaa hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Kɛji ajieɔ lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ ahi niji titrii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even though there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for leaf growth. Heavy rain can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will turn the leaves dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after clearing the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to the local soil and sprout rapidly to steal sunlight, water, and nutrients before your crop seedlings can get established. Clearing weeds early in the season gives your main crop the advantage to grow tall and strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ ehe kɛyaa he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya koni eju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai dani dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Jwɛi ni ogbeɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haa otsei titrii lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ akɛ amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder and get tiny holes after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powder ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Holes and powdery dust in stored grain are caused by weevils, small insects that eat the inside of the kernel. Thoroughly drying your maize to low moisture levels and storing it in airtight bags keeps weevils from destroying your harvest.
ga: Bu kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii, ni ji kooloi bibii ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa gĩ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly and smell bad in the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya ni eŋɔɔɔ yɛ shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam rot occurs when bacteria and fungi enter cuts or bruises created during harvesting and transport. Handling tubers carefully to avoid wounds and storing them in a well-ventilated, shaded barn keeps the yams dry and rot-free.
ga: Sweet potato rot baa kɛji bacteria kɛ fungi bote ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni baa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ kɛ tsɔne mli lɛ mli. Okɛ yitso lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ koni pilamɔi akafee bo. ni okɛ amɛ ato ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛkafiteɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and build leaves. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the plant green and produces larger corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehaa ŋmãa toi lɛ daraa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce a lot of green leaves but very few beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants get excess water, cowpeas put all their energy into growing leaves instead of flowers. Also, tiny insects like thrips can eat the flower buds before they open, stopping the pods from forming.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ náa nu babaoo tsɔ. Cowpeas kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ he nii moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Kɛfata he lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips baanyɛ aye ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛwo fɔfɔi. Enɛ baatsi pods lɛ anaa koni ekafee.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot in the ground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the farm, the roots drown from lack of air, which allows rot-causing soil fungi to attack and spoil the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni miifite lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up during hot afternoons to protect themselves from losing too much water in the sun. It is the plant's natural shield against heat, but adding grass mulch around the stem helps keep the roots cool and wet.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ hulu lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ he tsɔne kɛha tsei. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɔleɔ Tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops immediately after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and can sleep in dry soil for months, waiting to sprout instantly at the first drop of rain. Young crops grow slower initially because they are busy establishing new roots, so clearing weeds early gives your crops a fighting chance.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkã shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji babaoo, ni amɛmɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ. Tsei bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ejaakɛ amɛhe ejɔ amɛ ni amɛfee shishifãi heei. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛwuu.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller with every new harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ kpamɔ hee fɛɛ kpamɔ hee lɛ?

english: When too many young shoots, or suckers, grow around the main plantain trunk, they steal food and water from the mother plant. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main plant produces big bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii ni miida yɛ plantain tso wulu lɛ he lɛ fa tsɔ. Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes all leaves to light and air, preventing leaf diseases and giving the plant the energy needed to form large tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaa lɛ fɛɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with big leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the cool shade and moist air young cocoa trees need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ. Ehe miihia ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed by sudden heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the soil helps the flowers stay attached and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni baa trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ ŋmeii ahe ni amɛfee amɛhe.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up during the cool rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet, dark, and humid conditions. Pruning shade leaves to let wind and sunlight reach the pods helps keep them dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, duŋ, kɛ hei ni edɔ. Kɛ́ afo baai lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛgbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. It can also happen when the farm gets waterlogged and the roots cannot breathe properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi ŋmɔ ko mli ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful. Beans take nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which feeds the maize plants and improves the fertility of your field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak plants that produce very small yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves burn easily. Shade trees act as a cover, keeping the temperature cool and the soil moist until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ebaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ abobaahe. Ha hulutsoo be lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the land, water fills up all the air spaces, suffocating the roots and allowing rot-causing organisms to destroy them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ mli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa bɔɔ nii ni miifite lɛ kpataa amɛhiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Without steady moisture and moderate temperatures, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni tamɔ ekome kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the sunshine to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the vines off the damp ground, exposing leaves to light and preventing soil diseases from infecting them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu la lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha wain tsei lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli ni ehaaa helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba.

english: What is eating holes inside the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji niyeli bu ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Holes inside the center of maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the plant funnel to feed on young leaves, but applying proper control early prevents heavy crop loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa teŋ lɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei akui amli koni amɛye baai bibii. Shi nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa mra Ebaatsi ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni baafite lɛ naa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking sap from the leaves, or by viral diseases they carry. Controlling these pests stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital food, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Because weeds grow very fast, they can choke your crops if you do not clear them early in the season.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa. Ebaanyɛ efite onibii kɛji okɛ jwɛi shwieee nɔ mra yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same field as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu banana yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade from direct sunlight to survive. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide natural canopy shade while giving you food and income before the cocoa starts producing pods.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhi wala mli. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani kookoo lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi.

english: How does placing cut plantain leaves around my cocoa trees help my crop?
ga: Plantain tsei ni afo lɛ ni akɛaawo he fɛɛ he Te cacao tsei yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cut plantain leaves act as natural mulch. They hold moisture in the soil during dry periods, stop weeds from growing, and decay over time to enrich the soil with nutrients.
ga: Plantain baai ni afo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efite yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛ niyenii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do some farmers plant scent leaf around their cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ baai ni jeɔ ŋma amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ? Amɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Scent leaf produces a very strong natural smell that repels insect pests like capsids and mirids, helping to keep insects away from your cocoa leaves without using harsh chemicals.
ga: Baai ni ŋɔɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa waa. Amɛshwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids kɛ mirids. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii akashɛɔ kookoo baai ahe ni akɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsuuu nii.

english: Can I use crushed scent leaf extractions as a spray to protect my cocoa foliage?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kookoo baa lɛ mli nu lɛ atsu nii akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mikookoo baa lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, extracts from aromatic plants like scent leaf act as natural insect repellents. They can protect young shoots from pests, though they may require more frequent application than chemical sprays.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni ŋɔɔ tamɔ baai ni ŋɔɔ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi. Ebaanyɛ ebu ŋmeii bibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ehe baahia ni akɛtsu nii shii abɔ fe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ moŋ.

english: Why is it important to spray insecticides directly onto the leaves and foliage of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔse tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ashwie kookoo tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Pests like capsids hide and feed directly under cocoa leaves and soft shoots. Spraying the foliage directly ensures the chemical contacts the pests where they live and feed.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ kookoo baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ashishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsofai lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tsofai lɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ hela lɛ kpeɔ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if I have sprayed enough chemical on my cocoa leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni fa bɔ ni sa eshwie kookoo baai anɔ?

english: The leaf canopy should be lightly and evenly misted. If the liquid is dripping heavily off the leaves, you are over-spraying, which wastes chemical and can damage the crop.
ga: Esa akɛ baa lɛ yiteŋ lɛ aná afua bibioo, po. Kɛji nu lɛ hoɔ waa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ooshwie nɔ babaoo. Enɛ fiteɔ tsofai ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I apply chemical sprays on my cocoa trees at any time of the day?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ kookoo tsei anɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cooler. This prevents the chemical from evaporating quickly or burning the leaves in hot sunlight.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsofai lɛ akafo oya loo eha baai lɛ ashã kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do I need to cut back thick foliage and extra branches on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ baai ni mli tse kɛ niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ cacao tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning thick foliage allows sunlight and air to move freely through the canopy. This reduces humidity inside the tree, which prevents fungal problems like black pod disease.
ga: Baai ni afolɔ mli waa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli oya. Enɛ baaha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ naa.

english: What happens if the shade from my plantains becomes too thick over my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni jɛɔ mi plantains lɛ mli lɛ mli ewo mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ tsɔ?

english: If there is too much shade, cocoa trees cannot get enough sunlight to make food. This results in weak growth, lower flowering, and reduced pod production.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ hu nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji fɔfɔi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni dalɛ baa shi ni ehaa pod feemɔ baa shi

english: Why does the agricultural extension officer need to inspect my farm before reporting that my chemical treatment is complete?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko akwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ebɔ amaniɛ akɛ mi tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ egbe naa lɛ?

english: Extension officers inspect farms to ensure treatments are applied correctly, safely, and on time. This confirms that pest control measures across the area are effective and protects neighbouring farms from outbreaks.
ga: Extension officers lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ atsu helatsamɔi lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ, shweshweeshwe kɛ be naa. Enɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ fɛɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ebuɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why are extension officers telling me to stop burning my land before planting, even though my family has done it for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛkpa shikpɔŋ lɛ shãa dani amɛdu nii, eyɛ mli akɛ weku lɛ efee nakai afii babaoo nɛ?

english: Burning clears land quickly, but it destroys the beneficial organic matter, kills helpful organisms in the soil, and reduces the ground's ability to hold water, leading to lower crop yields over time.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Shi ebaakpãtã nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ. Egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Why does my soil produce fewer crops now compared to twenty or thirty years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo fe bɔ ni eji afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ loo nyɔŋmai etɛ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Farming the same piece of land continuously without resting it or adding organic nutrients drains the soil of essential food that crops need to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni aya nɔ atsuɔ okwaayeli he nii ni akɛ hejɔɔmɔ haaa loo akɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I consider buying certified improved seeds instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odase lɛ ahe? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahere dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Improved seed varieties are bred to handle modern challenges like longer dry spells and new pests, while older saved seeds gradually lose their strength and yield less over time.
ga: Amɛmiikwɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkɛtsu ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ naagbai tamɔ hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai heei ahe nii. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui momo ni ato lɛ baafite fiofio Hewalɛ ni ebaawo yibii fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and dry up before the ears are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani toi lɛ dara kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen or is suffering from water stress, preventing the plant from making food for its grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu he haomɔ miipiŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛwo niyenii amɛha amɛdumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I rely only on chemical fertilizers to feed my crops every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ koni mikɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii daa be mli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers feed the plant quickly, but they do not improve the structure of the soil. Over time, using only chemicals without animal manure or compost makes the soil hard and dry.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya. Shi ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ aya hiɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tsofai pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes the plant spend all its energy growing leafy branches instead of storing energy in the roots to form thick tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei aniji kɛ baai. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee tso ɔmɛ a mi mi wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I cut down all the large shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct sunlight and intense heat; larger shade trees protect them from burning and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my crops failing even though I plant them in the exact same month every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ nyɔŋ kome mli daa afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Weather patterns have changed over the years, meaning rain starts at different times now; crops fail if planted by calendar dates rather than waiting for sustained rainfall.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi etsake yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ jeɔ shishi enɛɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ adu yɛ kalanda gbi ko nɔ moŋ fe ni aaamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my tomato plants get sick with the same diseases every time I plant them in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ náa hela kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni madu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously in one field allows disease organisms and pests that target that specific crop to build up in the soil year after year.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, ebaaha helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ anɔ lɛ abɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ he afi fɛɛ afi.

english: How should I test a new farming practice recommended to us before using it on my entire farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka okwaayeli nifeemɔi heei ni ajie yi aha wɔ lɛ makwɛ dani mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Try the new method on a small section of your field first so you can observe how your crops respond to your local soil conditions before taking a risk with your whole harvest.
ga: Kaa gbɛ hee lɛ okwɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli he bibioo ko klɛŋklɛŋ koni onyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Dani okɛ okpamɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ awo oshara mli

english: How do I clear and prepare my forest land before I start planting plantains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo mi koo lɛ mli ni masaa he dani mabɔi plantains dumɔ?

english: You need to clear weeds, cut low bushes, and dig pits about 30cm to 60cm deep. Leaving some tall forest trees helps shade the soil, while digging deep pits allows the plantain roots to go deep for water and food.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ ohe. ŋmɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ Ni ofo bu ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee 30 cm kɛyashi 60 cm, ni oshi tsei kakadaji yɛ koo lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni bu ni mli kwɔ ni akuɔ lɛ haa plantain shishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛyana nu kɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: You should space plantain plants about 3 meters (10 feet) apart from each other. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and gather sunlight without competing with its neighbors.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni ebuaa hulu la naa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains together with young cocoa trees in the forest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantains ni kookoo tsei bibii yɔɔ mli yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants die easily under direct hot sun. Fast-growing plantains provide thick leaf shade and shade moisture that protects the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii gboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi oya. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Enɛ buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin when I plant them under big forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi yɛ koo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants stretch upward searching for light when big tree branches block the sun. When plants waste energy stretching for light, they grow skinny stems and produce smaller fruits.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ koni amɛtao la beni tsei wuji aniji tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa lɛ. Kɛ tsei fite hewalɛ ni amɛkpãa la Tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii.

english: How can I select the best plantain shoots from an old farm to plant on my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which have broad stems at the bottom and narrow, spear-shaped leaves at the top. These grow much faster and produce heavier, healthier bunches than shoots with wide leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword bud,’ ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ mli kwɔ, ni baai bibii ni tamɔ lance yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya kwraa ni amɛwoɔ niji ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ.

english: How long will my plantain plant take from the day I plant it until I can harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe kɛjɛ gbi ni midu amɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: It typically takes between 11 to 15 months for a plantain sucker to grow, produce a flower, and ripen into a harvestable bunch of plantains depending on rain and soil fertility.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 dani dumɔwui lɛ daa, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛshwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa. Edamɔ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Should I cut off the small extra shoots that grow around the main plantain trunk?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani plantains titrii lɛ je kpo?

english: Yes, you should cut off extra shoots and leave only 2 or 3 strong shoots per stand. If you leave too many shoots, they steal food and water from the main plant, leading to smaller bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2 loo 3 pɛ yɛ shidaamɔhe fɛɛ shidaamɔhe. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain plants start turning yellow during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water quickly. During the dry season, soil water drops, causing the plant to turn its outer leaves yellow and dry to save moisture for its center stem.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai wuji ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ, ni no haa baai ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily even when there is no heavy storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ahum ni naa wa po bɛ lɛ?

english: Small insect pests called root weevils or worms in the soil often eat the plantain roots and weaken the underground base, causing the heavy plant to fall over under its own weight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ root weevils loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ plantain shishifãi ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishitoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ni eha tso ni tsii lɛ gbee shi yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsiimɔ shishi

english: What can I add to the soil so that my plantains produce bigger bunches?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni mi plantain tsei lɛ afee wuji?

english: Adding well-rotted poultry manure, compost, or potassium-rich fertilizer around the plant base feeds the roots and gives the plant energy to form thick, long fruits.
ga: Ni akɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baafata he Tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ niyenii ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo yibii ni mli tse ni kɛlɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to spray or water my crops early in the morning or late in the evening instead of at noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nu afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ loo mawo amɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ? Mohu ɔ, jinɛ e maa hi wawɛɛ ngɛ nyɔ mi.

english: During noon, intense sun causes water and spray chemicals to evaporate too fast, which can burn plant leaves or waste supplies. Cooler morning and evening hours allow plants to absorb moisture and treatments safely without stress.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai loo efite nibii ni efite lɛ Leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ nuɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsaa amɛhe shweshweeshwe ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: What basic inspection should I carry out on my farm every morning before starting major field tasks?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee kwɛmɔi esa akɛ mafee yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa leebi dani mabɔi ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ titri lɛ?

english: Every morning, walk through your crop rows to inspect leaf undersides for early signs of pests, wilting, or yellow spots. Detecting problems early prevents diseases and insects from spreading to the rest of the farm.
ga: Daa leebi lɛ, nyiɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ni okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi eba mra. ŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Naagbai ni ayɔseɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai kɛ kooloi bibii akagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: How does harvesting my leafy vegetables in the cool morning affect how long they stay fresh?
ga: Aduawai ni baai yɔɔ mli ni akpaa yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ saa be ni amɛhiɔ shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ he.

english: Crops retain maximum moisture and cool temperatures overnight, so harvesting in the early morning keeps produce crisp and extends shelf life. Harvesting in hot afternoon sun causes quick wilting and faster spoiling.
ga: Tsei lɛ baaha hulutsoo be ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ aba mli nyɔɔŋ kome. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi ni eha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi oya ni amɛgboi oya.

english: Why should I avoid transplanting my young pepper seedlings during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Hot midday sun severely shocks young seedlings, causing leaves to drop and roots to dry out before establishing. Transplanting early in the morning or late afternoon gives seedlings cool soil to recover and take root.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane teŋ lɛ ha tso bibioo lɛ he fee lɛ yaa waa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni shishifãi lɛ hu gbiɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko leebi loo shwane mli Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛwo shishifãi.

english: Why do my cassava and vegetable leaves droop during hot afternoons even when there is moisture in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava kɛ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: When sunlight is very strong, crops lose water from leaf pores faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant intentionally droops its leaves to reduce surface area exposed to the sun, recovering once temperatures cool in the evening.
ga: Beni hulu la lɛ mli wa waa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. ni ebaahe ewa lɛ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my maize plant leaves start curling inwards during a hot dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛyaa mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism crops use to trap air and cut down water loss through evaporation. It signals that the crop is suffering heat stress and needs soil moisture to stay healthy.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛha nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni ehe miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do insects and pests seem to attack my crops more during the early morning and late evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ leebi maŋkpa kɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Most agricultural pests hide under leaves or in soil to avoid the intense afternoon heat, coming out to feed when air temperatures drop. Checking your crops during these cooler hours helps you spot and capture them actively.
ga: Okwaayeli mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ateŋ babaoo teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ashishi loo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbatao niyenii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔlɛ ba shi. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ ekãa ana amɛ ni omɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to weed around young crops regularly instead of waiting for weeds to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? tsei bibii daa Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni jwɛi lɛ adara

english: Young crop seedlings have small roots and struggle to compete with aggressive weeds for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Regular weeding ensures young plants get all available food to build strong stems.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛma tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa.

english: Why is it dangerous to cut or prune branches on my cocoa or tomato plants when leaves are wet with morning dew?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaafo loo aaakpa kookoo loo tomato tso ko beni leebi ŋmɔtɔ ewo baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Water droplets carry fungal spores and bacteria across plant surfaces. Cutting plants while wet allows these disease germs to easily enter open plant wounds, whereas dry conditions allow wounds to heal cleanly.
ga: Nu mli nu bibii hiɛɔ fungal kɛ bacteria spores kɛtsɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ. Tsei ni afoɔ be mli ni amɛhe efɔ lɛ haa nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ boteɔ tsei lɛ apilamɔi ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ amli mlɛo. Yɛ be mli ni shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa pilamɔ lɛ ni etsaa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a shortage of key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. The crop naturally channels its limited food supply to feed top new leaves, causing older lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ haa niyenii fioo ko pɛ ni akɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How do I know if I have left too many big shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishiɔ tsei wuji babaoo yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If your farm stays dark, chilly, and dripping with water late into the morning, you have too many shade trees. Excess shade traps moisture and prevents sunlight from drying out your crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ, fɛ̃i kɛ nu miiho leebi? Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oyɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ babaoo tsɔ. Shade babaoo baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi.

english: Do shade trees help keep moisture on my cocoa farm during dry weather?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, shade trees protect crops from hot sun and retain humidity, but if there are too many trees, they gather excessive dew that can drip onto cocoa pods and cause disease.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Shi kɛji tsei babaoo yɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baabua ŋmɔtɔ babaoo naa, ni baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hela aba.

english: Why does my farm feel cold and dark when I leave many trees standing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nuɔ he akɛ fɛ̃i kɛ duŋ miiwo mli kɛ́ mishi tsei babaoo ni damɔ shi lɛ?

english: A dense canopy blocks direct sunlight and air movement, creating a cool microclimate that traps damp air and heavy dew around your crops.
ga: Kpoji ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni nyiɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ onibii lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does the cool Harmattan wind from the savannah affect my crops?
ga: Te Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni jɛɔ Savannah lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?
