english: The cool Harmattan wind pulls moisture out of plant leaves and the surrounding air, which causes heavy dew to condense and fall on your farm at night.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why does my farm get so much heavy dew on cool mornings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ leebi ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cool air arrives, it draws moisture from tree leaves and the surrounding air, causing water drops to condense into heavy dew on your crop leaves and fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ fɛ̃i ba lɛ Ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu mli nui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ obaai kɛ oyibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves look stressed during cool, windy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiifee basaa yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry, cool winds can pull water out of plant leaves faster than the roots can take up water from the soil, causing leaves to temporarily wilt or drop.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni egbi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ loo amɛshwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko.

english: Is heavy morning dew on my cocoa pods bad for my crop?
ga: Ani leebi ŋmɔtɔ ni naa wa ni yɔɔ mikookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: While some moisture is normal, excessive dew that stays on pods for too long creates a damp environment where fungal diseases like black pod thrive.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo be ko ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ moŋ. Shi ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni hiɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji baanyɛ ada yɛ lɛ

english: What happens to my crops if air cannot blow through my farm properly?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ?

english: Without proper airflow, trapped moisture and dew cannot evaporate, creating a wet environment that encourages mold and rot on pods.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: How much sunlight should reach my cocoa pods to keep them healthy?
ga: Hulu la enyiɛ esa akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ aná koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa?

english: Your farm needs filtered sunlight so that morning dew evaporates quickly off pods while still shielding young trees from severe sun damage.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ he miihia hulu la ni atsɔ mli koni eha leebi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ajɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni fiteɔ amɛ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do the newer cocoa varieties react differently to weather changes compared to older varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo henɔi heei lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe kookoo henɔi momo lɛ?

english: Newer crop varieties are bred to yield faster, making them more sensitive to changes in shade, humidity, and moisture levels than traditional trees.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi heei koni amɛwo yibii oya. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ hulutsoo, hulutsoo, kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he jogbaŋŋ fe blema tsei lɛ.

english: Why do yam prices change so much depending on the month I bring them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato jara tsakeɔ waa yɛ nyɔŋ ni mikɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Yam prices depend heavily on supply and demand. Early in the harvest season around August, few farmers have fresh yams, so buyers pay more; by September, many farmers harvest at once, overflowing the market and driving prices down.
ga: Sweet potato jara damɔ nibii ni akɛhaa kɛ nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ anɔ waa. Yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ shishijee mli aaafee August. Okwaafoi fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ ŋmeii heei. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ babaoo. Beni shɛɔ September lɛ Okwaafoi babaoo kpaɔ nii yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fa fe nine yɛ jara nɔ, ni ehaa nibii ajara hu baa shi.

english: Is making a good profit on my farm just a matter of luck?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa ni maná yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji shweremɔ he sane kɛkɛ?

english: Profit is not just luck; it relies heavily on market timing and planning. By understanding crop growth cycles and planting early to beat the main market rush, you can consistently secure higher prices for your harvest.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ jeee shweremɔ kɛkɛ. Edamɔ jarayeli be kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo nɔ waa. Kɛtsɔ bɔ ni tsei lɛ daraa amɛhaa lɛ shishinumɔ kɛ amɛdumɔ mra nɔ. Bɔni afee ni oye jarayelihe wulu lɛ oyaiyeli lɛ nɔ kunim lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ nɔmimaa aha akɛ jara ni yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be kɛha onibii lɛ.

english: What advantage do I get if I plant my yams early in the season?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ maná kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ be lɛ mli mra?

english: Planting early allows your yams to mature ahead of the main harvest. Selling during early months like August lets you catch traders when crop supply is still low, allowing you to command top prices.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ye obua o-sweet potatoes lɛ ni amɛdara dani kpamɔ titri lɛ aba. Nihɔɔmɔ mra yɛ nyɔji tamɔ August mli lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni omɔɔ jarayelɔi be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa lolo lɛ. Ehaa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ jara ni fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do crop prices usually drop so much around September in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara baa shi waa yɛ September beaŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: September is the peak harvest period for many staple crops, meaning almost every farmer is trying to sell at the same time. When market supply is very high, buyers lower their offer prices.
ga: September ji ŋmaakpamɔ be ni fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii wuji babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ okwaafonyo fɛɛ okwaafonyo miitao ni ehɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli. Beni jara nɔ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fa babaoo lɛ Mɔ ni heɔ lɛ baaha jara ni akɛhaa lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I avoid selling my produce at a low price when every other farmer is harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mihe kɛjɛ minibii ni miduɔ lɛ ahe jara ni baa shi nɔ yɛ be mli ni okwaafoi krokomɛi miikpa lɛ?

english: You can avoid low market prices by planting early-maturing crop varieties, staggering your planting dates, or storing non-perishable produce to sell after the main harvest season ends.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa jarayeli jara ni baa shi lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Too dumɔ gbii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ. aloo akɛ nibii ni fiteee lɛ ato koni ahɔ̃ɔ beni kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ eba naagbee lɛ.

english: Does harvesting my crops a bit early affect their market value?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa mra fioo lɛ baaná jara nɔ jara lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Harvesting crops as soon as they reach maturity lets you sell when prices are highest. However, harvesting them before they are fully mature can lead to smaller yields and quick spoilage, which reduces their value.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛdara lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ amɛjara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ akpa amɛ dani amɛdara kwraa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi ni efite oya. Enɛ baaha ejara aba shi.

english: Why are yams often sold at higher prices compared to other food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ sweet potato kɛ jara ni wa fe niyenii krokomɛi ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are high-value crops because they require significant labor, carefully selected seed tubers, and specific soil conditions to grow, making them in high demand for domestic consumption and export.
ga: Atomɔ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa ejaakɛ ebiɔ nitsumɔ babaoo. Dumɔwui ayitsei ni ahala jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ kɛha dalɛ Enɛ haa ehe hiaa waa kɛha maŋ lɛ mli niyeli kɛ maŋsɛɛ ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ fɛɛ.

english: How do I calculate the best month to plant so I can sell when prices are high?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu nyɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu nii lɛ he akɔntaa koni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ be mli ni jara wa lɛ?

english: Find out which month prices peak in your local market, then count backward by the number of months your crop variety takes to grow from planting to maturity.
ga: Taomɔ nyɔji ni jara wa fe fɛɛ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, kanemɔ nyɔji abɔ ni heɔ ni otso lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edara lɛ.

english: Why do market traders pay different amounts for the exact same crop in different months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi woɔ shika srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome he yɛ nyɔji srɔtoi amli lɛ?

english: Traders adjust prices based on availability. When a crop is scarce in the market, traders compete with each other for supply by offering higher prices, but when produce is everywhere, they buy at lower prices.
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi tsakeɔ jara lɛ yɛ bɔ ni nibii yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii faaa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ Jarayelɔi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nibii ni amɛbaahe lɛ amli kɛtsɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ ni amɛkɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ nibii ni adu lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Amɛbaahe yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ.

english: Can unexpected rainfall changes ruin my plan to harvest early for better market prices?
ga: Tsakemɔi ni akpaaa gbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite mikpamɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo mra lɛ. Ani jarayeli jara lɛ baanyɛ ahi fe enɛ?

english: Yes, late or early rains can affect planting dates and crop growth rates. To lower this risk, farmers use early-maturing crop varieties and good soil management so their crops stay on track for target market dates.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ loo mra baanyɛ aná dumɔ gbii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Bɔni afee ni ajie oshara nɛɛ shi Okwaafoi kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa tsuɔ nii. koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ jarayeli gbii ni amɛto amɛhiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die when the rainy season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ gbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Most crops rely on water to draw nutrients from the soil into their stems and leaves. When the rains stop, the dry soil starves the roots of moisture, causing plants to wilt, stop growing, and eventually dry up.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ pii kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu nɔ koni amɛgbala niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛya amɛshishifãi kɛ baai amli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa nu. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛkpaa dalɛ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why is it best to plant my seeds right at the beginning of the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Seeds need constant soil moisture to sprout and grow strong early roots. Planting at the start of the rainy season ensures young plants receive steady water naturally, giving them a strong start before the heat sets in.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shishifãi ni wa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ aná nu ni ji adebɔɔ mli nu ni yaa nɔ daa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ dani latsaa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow much faster during the rainy months compared to the dry months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kwraa yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli kɛ akɛto nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Rainwater dissolves plant food in the soil so the roots can drink it easily. With plenty of water, plants can process sunlight faster and grow rapidly, whereas dry periods force them to slow down growth to save water.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni efee mlɛo aha shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛnu nu. Kɛ nu babaoo yɛ lɛ Tsei baanyɛ aná hulu la oya ni amɛdara oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ bei haa tsei lɛ daraa fioo koni amɛbu nu he.

english: How can storing rainwater in a small farm dam help me grow crops throughout the year?
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli nu ŋshɔ bibioo ko mli Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mi ni madu tsei afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: A farm dam collects and holds heavy rainwater during wet months. When the dry season arrives, you can draw water from this stored supply to irrigate your crops, allowing you to harvest food even when there is no rain.
ga: Okwaafoi akuu lɛ buaa nugbɔ nu babaoo naa ni ekɛtoɔ yɛ nugbɔ nyɔji lɛ amli. Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba Obaanyɛ ojie nu kɛjɛ nɛkɛ nu ni ato nɛɛ mli ni okɛfɔ onibii anɔ nu. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: Why is it better for me to clear my vegetable farm close to a water source like a dam or stream?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ebaafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafo aduawai aŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe ko tamɔ faa loo faa ko mli lɛ?

english: Farming near a water source saves you time and energy when watering your crops by hand or pump. Soil close to water sources also stays naturally moist for longer periods, helping your crops survive short dry spells.
ga: Okwaayeli ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu jɛɛhe lɛ haaa okɛ be kɛ hewalɛ akafite kɛji okɛ onine loo pɔmp miiwo onibii amli nu. Shikpɔji ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli.

english: Can I grow crops during the dry season if I do not have a river near my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛji faa ko bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, you can build small water catchment dams or dig shallow wells on your farm to trap rainwater. Using this collected water lets you farm year-round without relying on a nearby river.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oma nutoohe bibioo ko loo otsa nubu ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni okɛmɔ nugbɔ nu. Nu ni abua naa nɛɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ okwaayeli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ ni okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔɔ faai ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ anɔ.

english: Can giving my crops too much water from my dam hurt them?
ga: Ani nu babaoo ni jɛɔ faai amli lɛ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii awui?

english: Yes, overwatering floods the soil and drowns plant roots by cutting off their air supply. This causes the roots to rot and leaves to turn yellow, which damages the plant just as much as a drought.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ awo nu mli ni ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni boteɔ mli lɛ ni ebaafo mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni fiteɔ tsei babaoo tamɔ bɔ ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting enough water or if they are thirsty?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kumai miiye amɛ?

english: Thirsty crops will have weak, curling, or drooping leaves that turn pale or yellow. If your crops are getting enough water, their leaves will look firm, upright, and bright green.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ baaná baai ni bɛ hewalɛ. Efoɔ ehe loo egbeeɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji otsei lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Ebaai lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa, amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ, ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my plants with dry grass keep the ground wet longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shades the soil from the hot sun. This stops soil moisture from evaporating into the air, keeping the water in the ground where your crop roots can use it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii lɛ mli.

english: Which crops should I plant if I live in an area with very little rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji mihi he ko ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo pɛ?

english: Crops like cassava, cowpeas, and millet are naturally drought-tolerant. They have deep root systems or thick leaves that store water, allowing them to produce a good harvest even with minimal rainfall.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni mli tse ni kɛ nu toɔ. Enɛ haa amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ po.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plant turning yellow from the tip down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves forming a V-shape starting from the tip down the center usually mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves and grow strong, so adding urea or NPK fertilizer can help fix this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ V su mli ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, o-corn tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ urea loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that have a special ability to take nitrogen out of the air and put it into the soil through their roots. When the crop is harvested, that natural nitrogen stays in the earth to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I need to leave tall shade trees on my land when planting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei kakadaji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni miduɔ kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under the hot afternoon sun. Tall shade trees act as natural umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist so your young cocoa plants can survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ o-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with sticks instead of letting them grow along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ niji aha mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they can catch maximum sunlight and avoids leaf rot diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ yɛ fe fɛɛ yɛ lɛ, ni ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ ni sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the afternoon even when the soil was wet in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi lɛ?

english: When the afternoon sun gets very hot, leaves sweat out water faster than the roots can pull it up from the dirt. The plant wilts on purpose to protect itself from drying out, and it will usually stand back up once the sun goes down.
ga: Beni shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Ha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ shi yɛ yiŋtoo ko hewɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. ni be fɛɛ be lɛ, eteɔ shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain floods the soil for too long, water fills all the tiny air pockets, suffocating the roots and letting soil fungi attack and rot them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni amɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ni amɛgboi.

english: Why am I seeing ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dirt-like powder inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse yɛ ŋmãa bibii ahe baai ni mli nibii bibii ni tamɔ muji yɔɔ mli lɛ? yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides inside the deep center of the maize plant during the day, eating the tender leaves before they unfurl and leaving behind its waste.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ yɛ gbi mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants twisting up into tight curls and growing very tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bibioo lɛ?

english: Curled, twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices out of the tender leaves, or passing a plant virus to them that distorts their growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni etse ehe lɛ baa. loo ekɛ tsei ahe helai ni fiteɔ amɛdalɛ lɛ haa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant feels stressed, it abandons its flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashi fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi shi.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots around my plantain stand and leave only two or three stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni bɔle mi plantains lɛ ahe lɛ ni mashi tsei 2-3 pɛ?

english: If too many plantain shoots grow from one base, they all fight for the same water, fertilizer, and light. Cutting back extra shoots ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantain tsei babaoo ni miida kɛjɛ shishitoo kome mli lɛ fa babaoo. Tsoi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ haa tso lɛ yitso lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ kuu agbo ni tsii.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed leaves during dry spells like the Harmattan to conserve water. Providing shade trees and placing dry grass around the base of the trees helps retain soil moisture and prevents excessive leaf loss.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli, tamɔ Harmattan, koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi fɔ̃ɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi fe nine.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Mature cocoa pods change color from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange-yellow. You can also tap the pod; if it makes a hollow sound, the seeds inside have separated from the outer shell and are ready.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. loo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ-ɔranji nɔ. Obaanyɛ otswa pod lɛ hu. Kɛji gbee ko ni mli ewo muji ko yɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ egbala kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ he ni amɛfee klalo.

english: Why do my orange trees shed so many small fruits before they fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo dani amɛdara kwraa?

english: Young orange trees drop excess fruit when they lack enough water or nutrients to support them all. Regular watering during fruit setup and feeding the soil with manure or compost helps the tree hold onto its fruit.
ga: Citrus tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ aduawai ni fa fe nine kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni emɔ aduawai lɛ amli.

english: My orange leaves are curling up and covered in a sticky black film, what is wrong with them?
ga: Mi-orange baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni akɛ sini diŋ ko ni shwieɔ shi ehà nɔ. Mɛni miiya nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by tiny insects like aphids feeding on the sap and releasing a sweet substance that turns into black mold. Spraying the leaves with soapy water or neem oil destroys the insects and cleans the leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nɔ ko ni ŋɔɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe atse.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted coconut tree to start producing nuts?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ ŋmeii feemɔ shishi?

english: Dwarf coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, whereas traditional tall coconut trees take about 6 to 8 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my coconut palms turning yellow and drooping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Lower leaves turn yellow and die as part of the coconut tree's natural aging process. However, if yellowing spreads quickly to younger leaves, it signals a lack of soil nutrients like nitrogen or potassium.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ nifeemɔ lɛ fã. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛ eshwa oya kɛtee baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium.

english: Why should I keep tall shade trees on my farm alongside my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tsei kakadaji ahi miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Tall trees protect crops like cocoa from intense direct sunlight and strong winds. Their deep roots bring up minerals from deep underground, and their fallen leaves break down into free fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Tsei kakadaji buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa shika tsuru kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Ni ebaai ni egbee shi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Will shade trees steal water and food away from my food crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ miniyenii tsei lɛ amli?

english: If shade trees are pruned properly, their deep roots take water from lower soil levels that your main crops cannot reach. Pruning the lower branches lets enough sunlight through while keeping the soil cool.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛha hulutsoo lɛ, Otsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ hu baajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni otso titri lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ koni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ atsɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ohaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How does keeping beehives near my crop field help my crop yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii atsu ni mikɛtoɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔji lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Bees visit the flowers of crop trees like oranges and cocoa to collect nectar. In doing so, they carry pollen from flower to flower, which fertilizes them and leads to more and bigger fruits.
ga: Wuobii yasaraa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ citrus kɛ cocoa fɔfɔii koni amɛyabua ŋmeii amli nu. Yɛ nakai feemɔ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Enɛ baaha amɛfɔ ni ebaaha amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Can I use water from my fishpond to irrigate my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ loo ŋshɔ mli lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Yes, fishpond water is rich in fish waste, which acts as a powerful natural liquid fertilizer. Using it to water your crops feeds them organic nutrients and helps them grow faster.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni yɔɔ loo ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ loo ŋmɔtɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nu ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Kɛ́ okɛtsu nii ni okɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nu lɛ, ebaaha amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why should I spread my harvested cocoa beans out in the sun to dry instead of leaving them piled up in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ mashwã ni mikɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ ato kotokui amli lɛ

english: Sun-drying cocoa beans removes trapped moisture and allows fresh air to pass through them, which stops mold from growing and preserves the quality of your crop.
ga: Kookoo yibii ni hulu ŋmɛɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does drying my cocoa properly help me get a better price when selling?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cocoa ni agbiɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná jara kpakpa kɛ́ mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers pay top money for well-dried, clean cocoa beans, whereas damp or moldy beans lose value quickly or get rejected at the market.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ shika babaoo kɛhaa kookoo yibii ni hi, ni egbi, ni he tse. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni mli efɔ loo ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jara baa shi oya loo akpooɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: Why is it important to start drying my cocoa beans immediately after harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aje kookoo yibii lɛ agbimɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested cocoa beans rot and gather mold very quickly if left wet, so immediate drying protects your crop from being ruined before you can sell it.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni akpa ehee Ebaafite oya ni ebaabua ŋmeii anaa kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ ni efɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ogbi amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaabu onibii ahe kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ dani obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear fallen branches and dried waste away from the bottom of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei niji ni egbee shi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Clearing debris away removes hiding places for pests and prevents diseases like black pod rot from surviving near your living cocoa trees.
ga: Nibii ni efite lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teɔ shi yɛ lɛ, ni ehaaa helai tamɔ black pod rot ahi o-cacao tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe.

english: Can leaving cut weeds and damp bush on my farmland ruin my cocoa crop?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni afolɔ kɛ tsei bibii ni mli efɔ ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, leftover wet plant waste traps extra moisture and breeds fungi that can jump onto your healthy cocoa pods and rot them.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei amli jwɛi ni efɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni efɔɔ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ atsɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ ni amɛgboi.

english: What should I do with diseased leaves and bad pods to protect my clean cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni ehiii koni mikɛbu mi-cacao tsei ni he tse lɛ ahe?

english: You should clear all infected plant waste away from the farm area so the disease doesn't spread to healthy pods.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why is good airflow around my cocoa trees so important?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo tso lɛ he hiaa waa.

english: Moving air dries off excessive dampness from rainwater or dew on the leaves and pods, preventing fungal diseases from taking hold.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ehe lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ nugbɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ haa baai kɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ agbiɔ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: How does trimming extra branches off my cocoa trees help the pods grow better?
ga: Te niji krokomɛi ni afoɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree so sunlight and fresh air can reach the inner branches, keeping the pods dry and encouraging healthier growth.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli tseɔ bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa anyɛ ashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn bad and rot before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ fiteɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Excess humidity, lack of air movement, and dirty ground conditions allow fungal rots to attack growing pods and turn them black.
ga: hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ ni bɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛ ni mli ewo muji lɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ni ehaa amɛfeɔ diji.

english: How do I ensure my harvested cocoa beans do not spoil before I get them to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mi-cocoa yibii ni mikpa lɛ efiteee dani mikɛwo jara nɔ?

english: Remove all trash and dirt from the beans, keep them in an area with good air circulation, and dry them thoroughly in direct sunlight.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi kɛ muji fɛɛ kɛjɛ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Okɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli. ni egbi yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside young cocoa creates a canopy that shields the seedlings from heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmei dumɔ. Enɛ, kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ, feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits in the soil for long periods, it suffocates the roots and promotes fungus, so planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their flowers before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Providing consistent moisture to the soil and light shade during the hottest peak hours keeps the blossoms healthy enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa be fɛɛ be yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a maize stalk usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which gives leaves their healthy green color. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores soil fertility and green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I get a smaller harvest every time I plant maize on the exact same patch of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that plant needs and allows specialized pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen naturally and disrupts crop disease cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai krɛdɛɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tso helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ

english: Why do my bean plants grow big green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, bean plants focus all their energy on growing leafy foliage instead of flowers and seed pods. Using balanced soil amendments without extra nitrogen encourages the plant to set plenty of pods.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ, Bean tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ he nii moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui akutsei. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsakemɔ ni ja ni nitrogen fataaa he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo awo mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the tops of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms that feed on the soft center leaves where the stalk grows. Inspecting fields early and applying targeted neem treatments or recommended sprays directly into the leaf funnel stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ he ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ daa lɛ. Kwɛmɔ he lɛ mra ni akɛ neem tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsu nii. Kpa nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insect pests early with insecticidal soaps or neem oil prevents leaf damage and keeps plants productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ numɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite baai lɛ, ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches during windstorms. Supporting the fruit-bearing stems with sturdy wooden poles or bamboo props prevents trees from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fi aduawai ahe tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akakumɔ loo eshishifãi.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb tall sticks instead of trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves in full sunlight, which allows the plant to produce the energy needed to swell tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he.

english: How can I get an agricultural extension officer to come to my farm and line my field for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni ba miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ebato mi gbɛ koni edu kookoo?

english: You can visit your district Department of Agriculture or local COCOBOD office to request 'lining and pegging' services. Officers visit farms to help space trees correctly, ensuring crops get enough light, air, and nutrients for better yields.
ga: Obaanyɛ oya okpokpaa lɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ loo COCOBOD nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ni oyabi nitsumɔ. ‘Blotting and fixing’ nitsulɔi lɛ yaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛye amɛbua kɛto tsei lɛ ahe hei lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ naa la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Does my farm need to be near the main road before an extension officer can come help me?
ga: Ani esa akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ abɛŋkɛ gbɛjegbɛ wulu ko dani sɛɛgbɛ nitsulɔ ko aye abua?

english: No, extension officers are assigned to serve all farming communities within their designated zones, regardless of how far the farm is. You can arrange a visit through your local farmers' association or district office.
ga: Dabi, aha Extension officers lɛ koni amɛsɔmɔ okwaayeli akutsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kpokpaa ko nɔ lɛ. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ kɛ shɔŋŋ ha. Obaanyɛ oto saramɔ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ okwaafoi akuu loo kpokpaa nɔ nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: My farm soil feels very hard; can cocoa trees still grow well on it?
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ewa waa. Ani cacao tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa trees need soft, deep, and well-drained soil so their roots can spread easily. If the ground is very hard, you can loosen it with compost or organic manure and prepare planting holes properly before putting in seedlings.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia kokoo tsei. Bɔni afee ni kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ajie lɛ ni esa akɛ asaa dumɔ bu lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo mli.

english: Why is cocoa producing well on my neighbor's land while my cocoa on the same land type is failing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ afeɔ kookoo jogbaŋŋ yɛ akutsoŋbii ashikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-kookoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii.

english: Crop yield depends on more than just land quality. Differences in tree age, shade levels, seedling variety, pest management, and initial field spacing all affect how well cocoa trees perform.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ nɔ ni fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kpakpa kɛkɛ nɔ. Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ afii amli, bɔ ni ehiɛ yɔɔ ha, dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ He nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ he ni ejɛɔ ni ejeɔ shishi lɛ fɛɛ saa kookoo tso lɛ nitsumɔ he.

english: If insects are attacking my cocoa trees, should I uproot the whole farm?
ga: Kɛji kooloi bibii tutua mi-kokoo tsei lɛ Ani esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Uprooting is usually a last resort for untreatable diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus. For most common insect pests, spraying approved insecticides, pruning infected branches, and keeping the farm clean can save your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni anyɛɛɛ atsa, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fɔɔ baa lɛ ji naagbee gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ helai. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ashwiemɔ Ni oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oooha ehe atse lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni oŋmɔshi nibii akafite.

english: How do I know if my crop is struggling because of pests or because the land is poor?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahewɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehiii?

english: Pest damage usually shows visible signs like chewed leaves, holes in stems, or damaged pods. Poor soil condition typically causes uniform yellowing, stunted growth, or poor leaf formation across large areas without insect marks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ jieɔ okadii ni anaa, tamɔ baai ni ashɛre, bu yɛ tsei lɛ amli, loo tsei lɛ amli tsei ni efite. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be fɛɛ be. shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo baai ni ehiii yɛ hei wuji ni kooloi akadi bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is it safe to clear my old oil palm trees to plant cocoa in their place?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ majie mi-oil palm tsei momo lɛ koni mikɛdu kookoo moŋ?

english: Yes, cocoa can grow on former oil palm land, but you must completely remove old palm stumps and roots. Decaying palm stumps can host fungal diseases that might attack young cocoa roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu kookoo yɛ tsutsu tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ŋmɔji amli. Shi ehe miihia ni ojie tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi momo lɛ fɛɛ. Palm tsei ni egbo lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ atutua kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ aba.

english: What steps should I take to prepare my land after uprooting old trees before planting new crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mijie tsei momoi lɛ sɛɛ dani madu tsei heei?

english: After clearing old trees, clear the crop debris, loosen the soil, establish temporary shade crops like plantains, and ask an extension officer to line and peg the land for correct plant spacing.
ga: Kɛji ajie tsei momo lɛ agbe naa lɛ Jiemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ, ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, feemɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains, ni obi extension nitsulɔi lɛ ni amɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ ni amɛtswa shi koni amɛkwɛ akɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ja.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily if they get too much direct sunlight without shade crops, or if they are affected by drought or sap-sucking pests like mirids (capsids).
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji amɛná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ ni tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo bɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ emɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How far apart should I plant cocoa seedlings so they don't destroy each other as they grow?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe kɛjɛ he ko tɛŋŋ koni amɛkafite amɛhe kɛ́ adu?

english: The standard recommended spacing for cocoa in Ghana is 3 meters by 3 meters (10 feet by 10 feet). Proper distance prevents trees from overcrowded competing for light, water, and soil food.
ga: Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akɛ kookoo awo mli yɛ Ghana lɛ ji mitai 3 x mitai 3 (naji 10 x naji 10). Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ eyiɔ shi fe nine ni amɛmiitao la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: What happens to the chemicals I spray on my crops if it rains right after spraying?
ga: Mɛni baa tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni mikɛshwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rain can easily wash away chemical sprays from crop leaves before they have time to settle or absorb into the plant, which makes the treatment ineffective and wastes your investment.
ga: Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ baai anɔ lɛ ahe dani amɛná be ni amɛkɛba shi loo amɛbote tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsofafeemɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ni oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ hu fiteɔ.

english: Why does the sun need to shine for a short time after I spray my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni hulu lɛ akpɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛkɛ? Beni mikɛ spray shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ?

english: Sunlight and mild heat help the sprayed chemical dry and adhere properly to the crop leaves, ensuring the treatment stays in place to fight off pests and diseases.
ga: Hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ fioo yeɔ ebuaa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsofa lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ koni ekɛwu eshi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai.

english: If a few drops of rain fall shortly after I finish spraying, do I need to re-apply the chemical?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fioo beni agbe tsofa lɛ nɔ ashwie shi lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ, Ani ehe baahia ni akɛ tsofa lɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, even light rain can disrupt chemicals that have not fully dried or settled on the leaves, so you should check your farm and consider re-spraying to keep the crops protected.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo po. Ebaanyɛ eha tsofai ni egbiko kwraa loo ni kpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ahe ni efite lɛ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni osusu he akɛ oookɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ ekoŋŋ koni obu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: How does hot, sunny weather affect the way chemical sprays work on my crops?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ saa bɔ ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Sunny weather helps chemicals dry and settle quickly on the plant, but extreme heat without proper preparation can stress the plant, so spraying is best done when conditions are warm but calm.
ga: Hulu lɛ haa tsofai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛwaa oya yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni asaaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaashwie tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ shi eyɛ kpoo lɛ.

english: What does it mean to prepare or induce my crop trees before the flowering season?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei ni asaa amɛhe loo awoɔ amɛ hewalɛ dani fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ tsɔɔ?

english: Preparing or inducing a tree involves pruning, clearing bad growth, and applying specific treatments to trigger the tree to produce strong flower buds ahead of fruit production.
ga: Nɔ ni fata tso he saamɔ loo ekanyamɔ ​​he ji tso ni afolɔ. Jiemɔ dalɛ gbonyo kɛjɛ shi Ni okɛ gbɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi atsu nii ni okɛwo tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni mli wa dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why must I prepare my tree first before introducing flower-stimulating treatments?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masaa tso lɛ dani mikɛ tsofa ko ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ aná hewalɛ lɛ awo mli lɛ?

english: A tree needs to be healthy, well-nourished, and properly pruned first so that when flower-inducing treatments are added, the tree has enough strength to support the heavy fruit growth.
ga: Esa akɛ tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Na niyenii kpakpa ni okɛfolɔ tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ Bɔni afee ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ tsirɛɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, tso lɛ mli awa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eye ebua aduawai ni tsii lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my fruit trees sometimes fail to produce flowers even when the weather seems good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ fɔfɔi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hi moŋ?

english: Good weather alone is not always enough; trees often require specific preparation, such as branch pruning and chemical flower induction, to trigger abundant blooming.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa pɛ kɛkɛ fa. Bei pii lɛ, tsei biɔ hesaamɔ krɛdɛɛ ko, tamɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli. Koni ekɛ fɔfɔii babaoo aba

english: What are the basic stages involved in getting a tree ready for a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii titrii ni esa akɛ afee koni akɛsaa tsei kɛha nikpamɔ kpakpa?

english: Getting a tree ready involves three main preparation stages: clearing and pruning the tree, nourishing the roots and soil, and inducing flower buds at the right climatic moment.
ga: Otso lɛ ni ooofee klalo lɛ biɔ nibii titrii etɛ ni ooofee osaa ohe: tso lɛ mli ni oootsi kɛ eshishitoo; Shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ niyenii kɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi ni kanyaa mɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ lɛ hi

english: Why is it important for me to physically visit my farm regularly instead of sending someone else?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mayasara miŋmɔ lɛ daa moŋ fe ni matsu mɔ kroko kɛba jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Visiting your farm directly allows you to personally observe subtle weather changes, spot early pest or disease outbreaks, and judge the exact timing needed for spraying or harvesting.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ mli saramɔi tɛ̃ɛ baaha bo diɛŋtsɛ ona kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni bɛ faŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo helai ni jeɔ kpo yɛ shishijee mli ni okojo be pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ.

english: How should I handle farm activities during the minor farming season in Ghana?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ matsu ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ahe nii yɛ okwaayeli be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana?

english: The minor season often brings bright sunshine and milder weather, which is ideal for tree induction and spraying, but you must carefully time your work around unpredictable light rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be ni ji enyɔ lɛ haa hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli dɔɔ. ni sa kɛha tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ amɛshwiemɔ Shi ehe miihia ni okɛ be atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ootsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli. anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have wide leaves that provide necessary shade and keep the soil moist, helping the cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food it needs to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ená bɔni afee ni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the exact same field three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients. Planting it continuously on the same spot drains those nutrients out and attracts maize-specific pests and diseases that build up in the soil year after year.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ ajɛ mli. ni egbalaa ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ mli kooloi kɛ helai ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant receives too much water. Stress causes the plant to drop flowers to protect itself.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo tso lɛ ná nu babaoo Haomɔ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my tomatoes get black rotting spots at the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔi diji yɔɔ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil lacks calcium or when water supply is irregular, making it hard for the tomato plant to move calcium to the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tomato tso lɛ akɛ ebaajie calcium kɛya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my harvested onions start rotting so quickly after I pull them from the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Onions rot fast if they are harvested while the ground is too wet or if they are not left to dry (cure) properly in the sun for a few days before storage.
ga: Sabolai fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni egbi (etsa) yɛ hulu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ gbii fioo komɛi dani akɛto.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks too close to one another in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛɔ he tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava sticks are planted too close, their roots compete heavily underground for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in many small roots instead of big, thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛha la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi bibii Babaoo yɛ yitsei wuji ni mli tse najiaŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my cassava field early instead of waiting until harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal nutrients, sunlight, and water from young cassava. Clearing them early ensures the cassava roots grow strong before the crop canopy closes.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmei bibii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ mra lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ adara waa dani ŋmei lɛ aŋmɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops produce mostly big green leaves but very few pods during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai agboi babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much water and excess nitrogen in the soil make cowpea plants put all their energy into growing leaves instead of flowering and setting pods.
ga: Nu babaoo kɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pods awo mli lɛ

english: How do I know whether to use poultry manure or chemical fertilizer for my yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji esa akɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishi loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛha mi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Poultry manure improves soil structure and holds moisture for a long time, making it great for poor, sandy soil. Chemical fertilizer works faster to give quick nutrient boosts when the soil is already in good condition.
ga: Kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ehiɔ kɛha shikpɔji ni ŋã bɛ nɔ lɛ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ afata he oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shihilɛ kpakpa mli momo.

english: How do I know if my land has enough clay to hold water for rice farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Clay soil feels sticky when wet and rolls easily into a smooth ball that doesn't break apart. If soil is too sandy, water runs through it like a sieve, whereas clay holds moisture in place, which is ideal for crops that prefer wet conditions like swamp rice.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ efɔ ni etsɔ bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shwieee shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋã babaoo Nu lɛ baatsɔ mli tamɔ ŋã. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ hi kɛha tsei ni sumɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants dry up so quickly when I grow them in sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large spaces between dirt particles, causing water to drain away very quickly beyond the shallow roots of tomatoes. Adding organic matter like compost or animal manure helps sandy soil retain moisture longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛ agbo yɛ sũ bibii ateŋ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛhoɔ tomato lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ ahe. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋã shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant groundnuts on land that turns into heavy, sticky mud when it rains?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsɔɔ muji ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts grow best in loose, sandy-loam soil because their pods develop underground. Heavy, sticky mud hardens when dry, which prevents the flowering stems from penetrating the soil and makes harvesting difficult without damaging the nuts.
ga: Peanuts daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Muji ni mli tse ni tsii lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni enɛ haa ewaa akɛ abaakpa ni afiteee ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rain floods my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits on the field without draining, it starves the roots of air, causing them to drown, turn soft, and decay underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi ŋmɔji amli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaha ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛshwieɔ nu mli, amɛfeɔ blɛoo, ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up after I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow root systems that easily burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving large shade trees or intercropping with plantains creates a cool environment that protects young cocoa from drying out.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo akɛ plantains du amɛ lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Yellow maize leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. This often happens in continuously farmed land or when heavy rains wash nutrients deep out of reach of the roots.
ga: Abɛi baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli yɛ ŋmɔji ni yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ amli loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii lɛ ahe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ fe shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and squeezing together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiimii amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the underside of leaves, or by a viral infection spread by these insects. They suck out essential plant juices, stunting growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu ni he hiaa waa lɛ. ha dalɛ akpa

english: Legumes like cowpea and beans have special root nodes that pull nitrogen from the air and release it into the dirt. Planting them with maize acts like natural fertilizer, helping the maize grow better while improving soil health.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii pɛpɛɛpɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ hu yaa hiɛ.

english: How deep should I plant my yam setts inside the mounds so they don't rot?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-sweet potato lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkafite?

english: Yam setts should be planted about 10 to 15 centimeters deep inside well-aerated mounds. Planting them too deep traps excess moisture and starves them of air, causing rot, while planting too shallow causes them to dry out in the heat.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15 yɛ gɔŋ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu nii ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba. kɛ fitemɔ baa be mli ni dumɔ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baagbi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la mli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a long time to start growing if I plant them during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ dalɛ shishi kɛji midu amɛ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains require continuous soil moisture and high humidity to establish new roots. Dry Harmattan winds and dry soil shock the young sucker, putting it into a resting state until steady rains return.
ga: Plantains he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo koni ekɛ shishifãi heei aba. Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa mɛi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe feɔ amɛ yaa. ni oha ehi shi yɛ hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ daa.

english: How does water move from the ground all the way up to the leaves of my crops?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni nu jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli?

english: Roots take up water from the soil like small straws. This water travels through tiny channels inside the stem up to the leaves, keeping the crop firm, cool, and healthy.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tamɔ jwɛi bibii. Nu nɛɛ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ gbɛ bibioo ko nɔ. Yɛ tso lɛ mli kɛyashi baai lɛ anɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi, amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops start drooping and wilting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves wilt when a plant loses water faster than its roots can pull it from the ground, or when disease blocks the internal tubes that carry water up to the top.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ nu fite oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo beni hela tsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ mli ni kɛ nu yaa ŋwɛi lɛ anaa lɛ.

english: Can giving my farm too much water cause the leaves to wilt?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ agbi?

english: Yes, too much water drowns the roots by filling all the air space in the soil. Damaged or rotten roots can no longer draw water, causing the leaves above ground to wilt from thirst.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ekɛbaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ni efite loo egbo lɛ nyɛŋ agbala nu dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kumai hewɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves look withered even when the soil around them is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: If the soil is wet but leaves are withering, it usually means soil diseases have damaged the roots or blocked the stem base, stopping water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi baai lɛ egbo lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ loo etsĩ tso lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu nyɛɛɛ abote baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop leaves give off a bad smell when they start withering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ sũɔ waa kɛ́ amɛbɔi shwiemɔ lɛ?

english: A foul smell usually means bacteria or fungi have infected the plant tissue, causing it to rot and break down wetly instead of drying out naturally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii tsɔɔ akɛ helatsɛmɛi loo ŋmeii ebote tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ amli. Enɛ haa egboɔ ni efiteɔ ni efɔ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my leaves are wilting from hot weather or from a plant disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ baai lɛ miiho yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hewɔ loo eji tso hela?

english: Sun-wilted leaves usually recover in the cool evening or after watering. Disease-related wilting stays bad overnight, does not recover, and often comes with foul smells or discolored stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hulu lɛ etswa amɛ lɛ ahe baa shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi loo beni awo amɛ nu sɛɛ. Wilt ni kɛ hela lɛ baa lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shi jogbaŋŋ nyɔɔŋ kome, etsaaa, ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ fɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni tsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ fataa he.

english: Why do the stems of my crops turn mushy and bad-smelling when leaves die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ baai lɛ gboi lɛ?

english: Rotting bacteria break down the hard walls of the plant stem into soft liquid, creating a foul odor and completely cutting off water travel to the leaves.
ga: Muawai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ gbálaa tsei ahe gbogboi ni wa lɛ amli ni amɛfeɔ nu ni mli jɔ. ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo baa ni ehaa nu hoɔ kɛyaa baai lɛ amli kwraa.

english: Why does wilting sometimes start on just one leaf before taking over the whole plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ shishi yɛ baa kome nɔ dani ehaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Diseases often enter through a single leaf or branch first. As the germ multiplies, it blocks water flow in that specific area before spreading into the main stem to affect the rest of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela boteɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ kɛtsɔɔ baai loo niji aŋkroaŋkroi anɔ. Kɛji helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ mli lɛɛ Etsĩɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ nakai he lɛ naa dani egbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ koni ená tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does crop withering spread so fast that it seems impossible to control?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya aahu akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ lɛ?

english: Certain aggressive soil bacteria multiply rapidly inside the plant's water channels. By the time you see the leaves droop on the outside, internal damage is already severe.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ helai komɛi ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ faa oya yɛ tsei amli nu gbɛi lɛ amli. Kɛ ona baai ni miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ Mligbɛ fitemɔ lɛ mli wa momo.

english: What should I do immediately when I notice a single smelly, wilted leaf on my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mina baai ni egbee shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Carefully cut off and destroy the infected leaf away from your field, and clean your hands and tools so the rot-causing germs do not spread to healthy crops nearby.
ga: Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ afolɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ. ni otsumɔ oniji kɛ onitsumɔ dadei ahe Enɛ ji koni helai ni fiteɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if a plantain sucker is healthy enough to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sucker dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for sword suckers that have narrow leaves and a strong, heavy bulb at the bottom. Avoid suckers with wide, broad leaves early on or those showing black spots and holes at the roots, as those often carry pests like nematodes or banana weevils.
ga: Taomɔ klante tsei ni baai lɛ mli tseee kɛ bulb ni mli wa ni tsii yɛ shishigbɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ mra loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ bu yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, amɛhiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted under direct sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow root systems that cannot handle intense sunlight and heat. They require temporary shade crops, like plantain or cocoyam, to shield them and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cocoa. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival trick cassava uses to conserve water when the rain stops. The plant slows down its top growth while keeping the underground tubers alive until the rains return to sprout fresh leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni ŋmei kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Tso lɛ haa ŋwɛi dalɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ ni baai heei shwereɔ.

english: What causes my plantain trees to fall over easily right when the fruit bunch becomes big?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and as the bunch grows heavier, the plant becomes top-heavy. Strong winds easily push them over unless you support the main stem using a sturdy, double-bamboo stake or a wooden Y-prop.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ tso lɛ da Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa mlɛo. Ja okɛ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ shii enyɔ loo tso ni tamɔ Y ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ fiɔ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent morning watering and avoiding excessive synthetic fertilizers help flowers stick and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa leebi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ babaoo ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize help my crop?
ga: Te ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through small root nodules. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the surrounding maize plants and improves soil fertility.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to burn my bush clearings or let the cleared weeds rot on the soil before planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaashã ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ loo aaaha jwɛi ni egboi lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu?

english: Leaving cleared vegetation to decay as mulch is better because burning destroys vital soil nutrients and kills helpful soil organisms. Mulch protects the ground from heavy sun, prevents erosion, and keeps moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Ehi akɛ oooshi tsei ni ajie lɛ koni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: How many years can a plantain field continue to produce good yields before I need to replant?
ga: Afii enyiɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔ ko baanyɛ aya nɔ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dani esa akɛ adu ekoŋŋ?

english: A well-managed plantain farm usually gives strong yields for about 3 to 5 years. After this, soil nutrients become exhausted and pest populations build up in the soil, requiring you to clear and fallow or replant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain ŋmɔji ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afii 3 kɛyashi 5, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ onɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛdu loo okɛdu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting inside the ground if I do not harvest them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpaaa amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Leaving mature cassava roots in waterlogged soil exposes them to soil fungi and lack of oxygen, causing root rot. Harvesting tubers as soon as they reach full maturity prevents rot losses.
ga: Shishifãi ni eda ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Ebaaha ŋmeii aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ hu bɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛdara kwraa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛfite ni amɛfite.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my maize so it does not get spoiled by mold after picking?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ akafite beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize is ready when the outer leaves surrounding the cob dry up completely and turn papery brown, and the kernels become hard when pressed with a thumbnail. Harvesting while kernels are still soft leads to mold problems in storage.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ efee klalo. Kooloi lɛ agbiɔ kwraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ wolo. ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmei bibioo ko miimɔ nɔ. Nikpamɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ edarako lolo lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai baa yɛ nitoohe lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my maize is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves and husks turn brown and dry, and the grain becomes hard enough that you cannot easily dent it with your fingernail, usually around 3 to 4 months after planting.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa akɛ onyɛŋ okɛ oniji atsɔ mli mlɛo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: How many years does a grafted mango tree take to start bearing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: A grafted mango tree usually starts producing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas a tree grown directly from a seed can take 5 to 7 years to bear fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu amɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahe afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and small root systems that easily dry out in direct sun. They require temporary shade crops like plantains to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ, egbiɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on cassava often indicate a lack of nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, extreme drought stress, or attack by pests such as cassava green mites and mealybugs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cassava green mite lɛ tutuamɔi. kɛ ŋmeii

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa awo mi-pepper tso lɛ mli?

english: Apply the first dose of fertilizer about two weeks after transplanting when the roots have settled, and apply a second dose when the plants start flowering to support strong fruit growth.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni atsake lɛ beni shishifãi lɛ ewa lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he shii enyɔ nɔ beni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi lɛ koni eye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is typically caused by a viral infection spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, especially during dry and hot weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ latsaa be mli.

english: Yam tubers rot underground mostly due to poor water drainage in the soil during heavy rains, which causes excessive moisture and fungal infections that decay the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi titri lɛ yɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why should I wait for the main rains before planting my grain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Grain seeds need consistent moisture in the soil to germinate and develop strong early roots; planting too early in dry soil causes seeds to dry up and fail.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgbee shi.

english: When plantain suckers are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller stems and smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ aduawai akui bibii baa.

english: How long can a well-maintained cocoa tree continue to yield pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ cacao tso ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo ŋmeii?
