english: A healthy cocoa tree that receives proper weeding, pruning, and disease control can continue to produce good yields of cocoa pods for 25 to 30 years or more.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli lɛ Ni akwɛɔ helai anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo kookoo tsei kpakpai afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and burn when there is full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally grow under taller forest trees, so their young leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Young cacao trees grow naturally under trees in tall forests. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli oya. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow with yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmɔŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from making leaves properly, which reduces the growth of the cassava roots underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei afee baai jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the soft inner leaves of young maize. If left untreated, they eat the growing tip of the plant and prevent the maize cob from forming.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii amli baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Amɛyeɔ tso lɛ yitsei lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekafee.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open right when they are getting ready to turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ tswaa trukaa beni efee klalo akɛ ebaatsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they receive a sudden heavy watering or rainfall after a dry period. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst open.
ga: Tomatoi baatswa kɛji amɛná nu ni naa wa trukaa loo nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough room to produce large, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yams need loose, deep soil so the tubers can grow long and thick without pushing against hard ground. Mounds also keep water from pooling around the seeds and causing them to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa mli. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle ehe. dumɔwui ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ

english: Maize heavily uses up specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil every season. Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the soil, whereas rotating maize with beans or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the dirt.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii waa daa be. Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I wait until my seeds sprout leaves before putting fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds use their own stored energy to sprout roots and shoots first. Fertilizer applied before plants have roots to absorb it can burn the delicate young roots or be washed away by the rain.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei lɛ amli dani amɛná shishifãi ni amɛbaaŋɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ loo efɔ amɛ kɛjɛ nugbɔ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so small even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the nutrients and fertilizer from the soil. Removing weeds early allows your crops to take in all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops stay small and weak when I plant too many seeds close together in one field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete for the same limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures every crop gets enough plant food and light to grow strong and produce good yields.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fa babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la ni faaa nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ba tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná tso niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do the bottom leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and fall off when the farm becomes very crowded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi lɛ?

english: When plants grow too close together, the upper branches block sunlight from reaching the bottom leaves. Because leaves need light to make food for the crop, the plant sheds the lower leaves that are shaded out.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la he miihia baai koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛkɛ ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ shade lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is hungry for fertilizer just by looking at the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-ŋmã lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Crops show hunger through leaf colors. For example, when maize lacks nitrogen food, its lower leaves turn yellow starting from the tip and moving down the center in a V-shape, signaling that it needs fertilizer.
ga: Tsei jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ ahe su nɔ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ, Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛyaa shi yɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli. Ekɛ okadi ko tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia bo.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer to my crops early in the morning or in the hot afternoon heat?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning when the soil is cool and moist. In the hot afternoon, heat causes plants to conserve water and close up, making it harder for roots to absorb nutrients safely.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni amɛkpaa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How do my plant roots search for food and water deep under the soil?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ?

english: Roots naturally grow toward damp areas and nutrient pockets in the earth. Soft, loose soil makes it easy for roots to spread outward and downward to pull up food and anchor the crop.
ga: Shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã kponɔgbɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛjie niyenii ni amɛfi ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Does heavy rainfall help my crops absorb soil nutrients better, or does it wash the food away?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo ebaaha amɛlaaje?

english: Moderate rain dissolves soil nutrients so roots can drink them up. However, heavy continuous flooding carries dissolved nutrients deep down past the reach of the roots or washes them off the topsoil entirely.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni eha amɛnu kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, nu afua ni naa wa ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ asɛɛ shɔŋŋ loo ejieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and rot when water stays standing around their roots for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air from the soil to stay healthy. Standing water fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots so they can no longer take up food and water, causing the plant to rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛye niyenii kɛ nu dɔŋŋ. haa tsei fiteɔ

english: Can I use the water drained from my fish pond to irrigate my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ loo ŋshɔ mli lɛ awo mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu?

english: Yes, water from fish ponds contains natural fish waste, which acts as a rich liquid fertilizer. Using it on crops supplies both the moisture and organic nutrients the plants need to grow fast.
ga: Hɛɛ, loo nubu mli nu lɛ yɛ loo adebɔɔ mli jwɛi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ akɛwo tsei amli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young tomato stems bend and lean toward one side of the farm instead of growing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei bibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Crops naturally lean toward the direction where sunlight is strongest. Leaves need sunlight to turn water and soil nutrients into food, so the stem bends to capture as much light as possible.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baatsɔ adebɔɔ naa kɛya he ni hulu la ni naa wa fe fɛɛ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Hulu la he hia baai koni amɛ tsake nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, abɔleɔ tso lɛ he koni emɔmɔ la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow faster and greener after the very first rains following a long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During the dry season, organic matter accumulates in the dry soil. The first rains wake up beneficial soil microbes that quickly break down this matter, releasing a rich burst of nitrogen food for the crops.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ teɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fiteɔ sane nɛɛ oya lɛ shi. ni ejieɔ nitrogen niyenii babaoo kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I plant beans in the same field where I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Beans naturally take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil through their roots. When planted alongside maize, they feed the soil, helping your maize grow taller and greener without needing as much expensive commercial fertilizer.
ga: Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Ye obua oŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa he ehiaaa.

english: How does adding dried animal droppings to my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Dried manure acts as natural food for crops, releasing nutrients slowly into the ground. It also improves the soil structure so that it holds water like a sponge, helping your crops stay green longer during dry weeks.
ga: Nibii ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejieɔ lɛ fiofio kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ fɛo koni ekɛ nu ahi shi tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up into tight tubes when the sun gets very hot during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ wo amɛmli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the maize plant's natural way of saving water. By curling its leaves, the plant hides its surface from the harsh sun, stopping moisture from evaporating too quickly so it can survive the heat.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji ŋmãa tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ baaha hulu la ni naa wa lɛ ahi ŋwɛigbɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ kɛyashi ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa.

english: Why does the flower at the top of my corn plant appear before the corn cob grows lower down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: The flower at the top produces pollen dust, which needs to fall down onto the soft silks of the developing cob below. This pollination process is necessary for every single grain of corn to form on the cob.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ jieɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. ni esa akɛ egbee ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ mli siliki ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ pollination gbɛ nɛɛ he miihia koni ŋmãa ŋmãa fɛɛ ŋmãa aba yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young corn turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the corn plant steals nutrients from its older, lower leaves and sends them up to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, Abɛi tsei juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli. ni atsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni baai bibii lɛ aya nɔ ada

english: Why do my cowpea bean plants spread wide across the ground instead of growing tall like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants are naturally designed to spread out to shade the ground. This leafy cover keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from escaping, and prevents weeds from getting sunlight to grow.
ga: Afee cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɛkɛ baa ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ

english: If I put three or four seeds in one hole, will I get more harvest from my crops?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ wo bu kome mli lɛ Ani mahã minitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole causes the plants to fight each other for soil food, water, and light. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks and tiny cobs, whereas giving each plant its own space produces bigger, healthier yields.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ la mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ be mli ni tso fɛɛ tso ni ahaa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops stop growing and look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi dumɔwui lɛ miikpa dalɛ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that grow faster than young crops, allowing them to steal the water, light, and nutrients meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni daa oya fe tsei bibii. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii kɛhaa otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars hiding deep inside the center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworm hide deep inside the tender center leaves because those new leaves are soft and easy to eat. The surrounding wrapped leaves also protect the caterpillars from the hot sun and heavy rain.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ejaakɛ nakai baai heei lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛyeɔ mlɛo. Baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ hu buɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: How will I know that my corn is completely ready to harvest from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Corn is mature when the green outer leaves wrapping the cob turn dry and brown, and the soft silks at the top turn dark brown. You can also press a grain with your thumbnail; if it is firm or releases a milky juice, it is ready.
ga: Abɛi eda kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai eŋɔli ni ha ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. ni siliki ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ oshishifã lɛ hu anyɛ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ewa loo mliki je kpo lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct harsh sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries up the soil moisture quickly, causing the leaves to turn yellow and fall off.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Dropping leaves during Harmattan is a natural defense mechanism for cocoa trees to save water and keep the main trunk alive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni kookoo tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce hundreds of flowers, but only a few of them grow into real pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ohai abɔ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many extra flowers to attract tiny pollinating insects, but the tree only keeps as many pods as its energy, nutrients, and water can support.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi krɛdɛɛi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛgbala fɔfɔi bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Shi tso ko baahiɛ ŋmeii babaoo bɔ ni ehewalɛ, niyenii, kɛ nu baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my tiny, young cocoa pods turn dark and shrivel up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often called cherelle wilt, which is the cocoa tree's natural way of reducing extra pods it cannot feed, though it can also be worsened by a lack of rainfall or nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ Cherelle Wilt, ni ji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ efoɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ eye lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ebaanyɛ efee nɔ ni ehiii kwraa kɛji nugbɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ moŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut off healthy-looking branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ aniji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the branches so sunlight and fresh air can flow through the farm, which stops fungal diseases like Black Pod from spreading and encourages the tree to grow bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ mli tseɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ akagbɛ ashwã. ni ewo tsei hewalɛ koni amɛná ŋmeii wuji

english: What will happen to my crop if I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close together, their roots fight over soil food and their branches block out all sunlight, creating dark, damp conditions where diseases thrive easily.
ga: Kɛ́ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ni kookoo tso lɛ niji tsiɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli edɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ oookwɛ

english: Can I grow cassava inside my young cocoa farm without hurting the cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni miyeee kokoo tsei lɛ awui?

english: Cassava roots spread heavily underground and its broad leaves block light, which steals water and sunshine away from tender young cocoa seedlings and slows down their growth.
ga: Cassava shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi waa. ni ebaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ tsiɔ la ni juɔ nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli lɛ naa ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do plantain trees make good companion crops for newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui feɔ nanemɛi tsei kpakpai kɛha kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like natural sunshades for young cocoa, while keeping the ground cool and damp during the hotter months.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛha kookoo bibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why is a green plant growing directly out of my cocoa tree branch, and why is that branch dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei eŋɔlii miikwɛ̃ kɛmiijɛ mi-kookoo niji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ nakai tso nine lɛ gbo lɛ?

english: That plant is mistletoe, a harmful plant parasite that attaches itself to the cocoa branch to steal water and food, which eventually starves and kills that specific branch.
ga: Nakai tso lɛ ji mistletoe. Enɛ ji tso mli tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ oshara ni kɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ kookoo niji ahe koni eju nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha yɛ naagbee lɛ hɔmɔ aye tso nine lɛ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbo.

english: Why do I have to cover my freshly harvested cocoa beans with plantain leaves for a few days before drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baa haa kookoo yibii ni akpa ehee lɛ ahe gbii fioo komɛi dani mikɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Heaping beans under plantain leaves allows them to ferment properly, which stops the seed from sprouting and develops the rich chocolate flavor and dark brown color buyers look for.
ga: Okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ato plantain baai lɛ ashishi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛshwie jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛnáa tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen nutrients or the soil is too waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing food from the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can safely absorb it. Applying chemical fertilizer to completely dry soil can burn and destroy the plant roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi.

english: Fall Armyworms chew ragged holes in maize leaves and leave sticky brown waste inside the central shoot of the plant. They also have an inverted 'Y' shape mark on their heads.
ga: Fall Armyworms lɛ ŋmɔɔ bu yɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni amɛshiɔ ŋmãa ni mli tse ni mli tse yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Amɛyɛ okadi ko ni tamɔ ‘Y’ ni atsake lɛ hu yɛ amɛyitso nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and turning stiff?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up mainly due to heat stress, irregular watering, or tiny insects like whiteflies that suck sap from the plant and pass diseases to it.
ga: Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi fe fɛɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ni amɛkɛ helai baa.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if tiny beneficial insects like midges are not available to pollinate them, or if the tree is severely stressed by dry weather and lack of water.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo amɛmli. aloo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa waa.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their blossoms before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔlɔ dani pepper lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when daytime temperatures get too high or when soil moisture drops too low, causing the plant to shed load to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi tsɔ. Ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ ejatsu lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow during fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be damaged by tiny root worms or stem borers. Weakened roots cannot support the heavy weight of mature plantain bunches against strong wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shishifãi bibii ni shwieɔ shi loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ afite. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ plantain tso ni eda lɛ muji ni tsii lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants die when I cut down all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mifolɔ tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Nakai kookoo tso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. They need partial shade from taller trees to keep them cool and hold moisture around them while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil if I do not harvest them during the heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akpaaa mi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain fills all the spaces in the soil with water, suffocating cassava roots and allowing fungi to multiply rapidly, which rots the tubers underground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ha jɛmɛ fɛɛ eyi kɛ nu. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ mli shwereɔ oya Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my seed yams start sprouting in the barn before the planting season even begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Seed yams break their natural resting period when air in the storage barn becomes warm and moist, which signals to the yam that it is time to start growing.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli dɔɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ obɔi dalɛ.

english: Is it better to give fertilizer to my crops early, or should I wait until they start looking weak?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli mra? Aloo esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi tsei lɛ abɔi gbɔjɔmɔ?

english: It is better to feed crops early so they build strength from the start. Feeding soil early prevents weakness and disease, just like eating good food keeps a human body healthy before getting sick.
ga: Esa akɛ aha tsei niyenii mra. Koni ama hewalɛ kɛjɛ shishijee Shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛjɛ egbekɛbiiashi Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ bɔjɔmɔ kɛ helai anaa. Tamɔ niyenii kpakpa ni ayeɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. No yeɔ ebuaa adesa gbɔmɔtso lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ dani hela mɔɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen. Plants need good soil nutrients for strength, not just water, to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ, shi jeee nu kɛkɛ, koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can adding manure and compost to my soil help reduce the need for expensive chemical spray later?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, manure and compost feed the soil naturally, making plants strong and resilient so they can resist pests and sickness on their own without heavy chemical treatment.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo No hewɔ lɛ enyɛɔ eteɔ shi ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ekɛ tsofai ni tsii tsuuu nii.

english: How does planting cowpeas in the same farm with my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas trap natural food from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, which acts as free nutrient strength for the nearby maize.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ jɛɛhe ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers instead of turning them into peppers during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When heat is too intense, pepper plants drop flowers to save their remaining energy and keep the main plant alive until conditions improve.
ga: Kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he. ni amɛkwɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ kɛyashi eshihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves split into strips during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ harmath be lɛ mli kɛji amɛgbi pɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split naturally during heavy dry winds so the breeze can pass through easily without uprooting or snapping the main stem.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ baajara yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa ba. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo ni efoŋ tso titri lɛ loo efoŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop in the afternoon heat even when the ground feels wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink during hot afternoons. Drooping reduces leaf exposure to sunlight, and the plant usually recovers by evening.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Foji ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi. Ni bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ he jɔɔ lɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do insects attack weak cassava plants more than the strong, well-fed ones in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa ŋmei tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ fe ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects target weak plants because their stems and leaves are soft and easy to break down. Healthy, well-nourished plants produce tough natural defenses that deter pests.
ga: Kplukai shwieɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛkuɔ oya. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni niyenii kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa.

english: How does spraying water mixed with pounded neem leaves help keep pests away from my vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa lɛ efutu mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mi-aduawai lɛ amli?

english: Neem leaves contain bitter natural compounds that act like a protective barrier, stopping insects from feeding on vegetable leaves without damaging the plant.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni mli wa ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ Neem baai lɛ amli. Etsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye aduawai ahe baai ni amɛfiteee tsei.

english: Why do some cocoa trees produce big healthy pods while neighboring trees in the same farm produce small ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Trees produce differently based on how much light, soil nutrients, and root space they get. Trees in richer soil with less competition naturally grow stronger pods.
ga: Tsei lɛ ayibii sɔrɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni la fa ha lɛ naa. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ shishifãi ni tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ Tsei ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo ni akaŋshii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baawo ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Does rice always need to grow in standing water, or can I grow it on dry land?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni adu omɔ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo abaanyɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: Not all rice needs flooded fields. While lowland rice thrives in standing water which also helps control weeds, upland rice varieties are bred to grow on dry land using normal rain water just like maize or cassava.
ga: Omɔ henɔi komɛi biɔ nu afua. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli moŋ, shi eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni eyeɔ jwɛi anɔ. Shi akwɛɔ omɔ kakadaŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Nakai nɔŋŋ eji yɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa hu he.

english: Why do my rice plants turn yellow a few weeks after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rice plants usually turn yellow when they lack essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or when there is too much or too little water. Applying the right amount of fertilizer at the right growth stage turns the leaves green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, omɔ tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni nu babaoo loo fioo pɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are some of my rice heads filled with empty husks instead of full grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-rice ŋmɔji lɛ ekomɛi eyi kɛ ŋmɔji ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Empty rice husks happen when extreme heat, dry weather, or sucking insect pests attack the plant while it is flowering. This prevents the flower from developing into a solid grain of rice.
ga: Omɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa waa. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi Loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuaa tso lɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmaa ni wa.

english: Why does my farmland give me less rice harvest every year even though I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baa shi daa afi lɛ? Dumɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting the exact same crop on the same piece of land every season drains the soil of specific nutrients. Rotating crops or adding organic manure restores soil fertility so your harvest stays high year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii pɔtɛɛi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni aaatsake loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni nibii ni ofeɔ lɛ aya nɔ aya hiɛ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do birds attack my rice farm more heavily than my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ waa fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Birds target rice fields that mature earlier or later than the surrounding farms. If you plant at the exact same time as nearby farmers, the bird population gets spread across all fields instead of destroying just yours.
ga: Okpoi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni daa oya loo blɛoo fe ŋmɔji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu yɛ be kome mli kɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ Okpoi ayibɔ lɛ baagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔji fɛɛ amli moŋ fe ni oookpãtã okpoi lɛ ahiɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my young crop seedlings after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to quickly absorb water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early gives your young seedlings the light and food they need to grow ahead of the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara dani jwɛi aba.

english: Why do my tall rice plants fall over flat on the ground right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over—a problem called lodging—when their stems are weak due to excessive nitrogen fertilizer, planting seeds too close together, or heavy wind and rain pushing down on heavy matured grain heads.
ga: Omɔ tsei shwieɔ shi, ni eji naagba ko ni ale lɛ akɛ shĩa. Beni tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hewɔ lɛ Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ Aloo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni miitswa kɛba shi yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei ni edara kwraa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do rice grains drop off the plant onto the soil if I delay harvesting by a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa lɛ shwie shi otsi kome lɛ?

english: Once rice grains fully mature and dry on the stalk, the tiny stem holding each grain becomes brittle. Delaying harvest causes wind or simple touching to shatter the grains, causing them to fall off and go to waste.
ga: Kɛ́ omɔ ŋmaa lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni egbi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmaa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nikpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nibii ni akɛtswaa mɔ he mlɛo baa. ni haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: No, planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunshine, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing allows each plant to grow thick stems and yield larger, fuller crop heads.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ tsei wuji ni ewoɔ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do some rice seed varieties take three months to harvest while others take five months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi heɔ nyɔji etɛ dani akpaa ŋmãa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi heɔ nyɔji enumɔ dani amɛkpaa lɛ?

english: Different rice varieties are developed for different weather patterns. Short-duration varieties mature quickly to avoid dry spells, while long-duration varieties spend more time feeding from the soil to produce higher yields in areas with reliable water.
ga: Omɔ henɔi srɔtoi Afee lɛ yɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Henɔi ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ daa oya koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ yeɔ be babaoo kɛtaoɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ hei ni nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. This often happens in nutrient-poor soil or after heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii bɛ mli lɛ nɔ loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rain storm comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani ahum aba?

english: No, applying fertilizer right before heavy rain will wash the nutrients off your field before the crop roots can drink them in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a light rain.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my farm if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that attack maize to multiply in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt during the hot afternoon even if the soil was wet in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to close its pores and save water, and it usually recovers once the sun sets and temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛŋa eshishifãi lɛ ni ekɛ nu akafite. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same farm alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa seedlings need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Will cutting off some of the side branches on my tomato plants help them produce bigger fruit?
ga: Ani mi-tomato tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ewo tomatoi wuji?

english: Yes, pruning unnecessary branches and lower leaves helps the plant focus its energy and nutrients directly on growing larger, healthier fruit rather than spending energy on feeding excess leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei niji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛha baai ni fa fe nine lɛ niyenii

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomatoes turning black and rotting before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit as it grows. It often happens when soil moisture fluctuates wildly between being too dry and too wet, preventing the roots from absorbing calcium steadily.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ nɔ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are small insects attacking the flowers on my pepper plants and causing them to fall off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ni amɛmiiha amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Insects like thrips and aphids feed on flower sap, which stresses the plant and causes it to drop flowers before fruit can form. Controlling these pests early helps protect the blooms so they can develop into healthy pepper pods.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ thrips kɛ aphids yeɔ fɔfɔi amli nu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baabu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔ pepper pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster right after I clear and till my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mitsu he nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant underground for months or years. When you till the soil and clear the bush, you bring those hidden seeds to the surface where warmth, air, and sunlight trigger them to germinate quickly.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. Ebaanyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ shishi nyɔji loo afii babaoo. Kɛji otsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii ni ojie jwɛi lɛ Okɛ nakai dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baaba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulutsoo, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ hulu la woɔ shweremɔ oya he hewalɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are fully ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will see the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem will start to crack open as the swelling tubers push upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni tso lɛ ni efuu lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and dry up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their leaf tissues are thin and fragile. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the direct heat, the sun dries out the moisture in the leaves faster than the roots can drink it, causing the leaves to burn.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, ebaa lɛ mli fãji lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa lɛ, Hulu la baaha nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baa shãa

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the rest of the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a key food crop plants need to stay green and strong. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the maize plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, Abɛi gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe kɛmiiya mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites living under the leaves. As these insects suck out the sap from the leaves, the damaged leaf tissue twists and curls up as it tries to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Beni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Baa lɛ mli fãji ni efite lɛ tsɔɔ ni ebɔleɔ ehe be mli ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot underground when it rains heavily for many weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa otsii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves water standing in the soil without proper drainage, the ground becomes waterlogged and suffocates the tubers, allowing fungi and bacteria to rot them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaha nu afua ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans in my field help the next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the roots decay after harvest, that stored nitrogen stays behind in the soil as natural plant food for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to grow if I plant them right after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season usually wets only the top layer of dirt, which dries out fast under the hot sun. If seeds sprout in that shallow moisture and no more rain falls for a few days, the delicate baby roots dry out and die before reaching deeper moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ pɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ he eko Ni kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛná hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why do I need to place tall sticks for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need to grow upwards so their leaves can catch enough sunlight to make food for growing large tubers. When vines lie flat on hot soil, the leaves block sunlight from each other and can catch rot or fungal diseases from wet soil.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ adara babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ niyenii aha bulbs wuji ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why do flowers drop off my tomato plants without ever turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or a sudden lack of water. When the weather gets too hot or the dry soil stresses the plant, it sheds its flowers to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni faaa trukaa. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, tso lɛ he feɔ shoo. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: When too many shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they compete for the same food, water, and sunlight in the soil. Removing extra shoots leaves just one or two strong stems, allowing the main plant to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe single main trunk Nakai ŋmeii lɛ hu baatswa niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ awo niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and get moldy inside the storehouse if I put it there right after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ kɛji mikɛwo mli beni mikpaa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize grains still contain high moisture inside them. Storing grain before drying it properly under the sun creates a damp environment inside the storage bags where mold, fungi, and insects multiply quickly.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ mli lolo. Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ dani agbiɔ yɛ hulu la shishi lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa nitoohe kotoku lɛ mli he ni ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo baa oya.

english: Why does it take so much more physical strength and extra help to dig up my land when the soil is soaked with water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aná gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ babaoo kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ kroko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋmɔ mli beni nu ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When soil gets full of water, it turns into thick, heavy mud that sticks to your tools. This extra weight makes digging exhausting, so you often need more hands to finish the work than on dry ground.
ga: Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaatsɔ muji ni mli edɔ ni tsii ni kpɛtɛɔ odɛŋdadei lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ muji ni fa nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli taomɔ feɔ mɔ ni nijiaŋ jeɔ wui. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, niji babaoo he baahia bo koni ogbe nitsumɔ lɛ naa fe shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to dig my land right after a heavy rain or wait for the ground to dry out a bit?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oootsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ loo ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi fioo?

english: It is best to wait until the soil is moist but not soaking wet. Digging very wet ground destroys the soil structure, packs it into tight mud balls, and leaves hard crusts when it dries, making it tough for roots to spread.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ shi ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafee ŋmɔtɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa ni akuɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ. Akɛmimɔ mli ni efee sũ ni mli wa. ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa kɛji egbi. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has too much water underneath before I start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɛ nu babaoo yɛ shishi dani mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: You can dig a small hole about knee-deep in your field. If water quickly pools at the bottom or if the soil stays squishy like paste days after it rains, your land has too much water sitting close to the surface.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa bu bibioo ko. Yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli aaafee tsitsi nɔ Kɛji nu hoɔ oya yɛ nubu lɛ shishi Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lolo tamɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ gbii babaoo sɛɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ.

english: What will happen to my crop roots if there is too much water sitting in the ground for a long time?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji nu babaoo hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water fills all the tiny spaces in the soil, the roots choke, stop growing, and eventually rot, which can kill the whole plant.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu yi he bibioo ko yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. ekpaa dalɛ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ ni baanyɛ agbe tso muu lɛ fɛɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even though the ground around them is full of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ moŋ? Ani nu baayi mli obɔ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is suffocating from waterlogged roots. When roots sit in excess water, they lose their ability to drink up nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to lose their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miigbɔjɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli lɛ Enyɛŋ ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Which crops can I safely plant if my farmland naturally holds a lot of water throughout the year?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ shweshweeshwe kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Crops like rice, cocoyam (taro), and sugarcane love wet soil and thrive in heavy moisture. Crops like cassava, maize, and groundnuts will easily rot in watery ground and should be planted elsewhere.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ omɔ, kookoo (taro), kɛ sugar cane sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni esa akɛ adu yɛ he kroko

english: How can I build mounds or ridges to help my crops survive in soil that gathers too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo hiɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Heaping soil into high mounds or raised ridges lifts the plant's main roots above the muddy ground level. This keeps the root zone well-aerated while excess water settles lower in the furrows.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooofee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ baaye abua ni awo tso lɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ anɔ kɛteke shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli. yɛ be mli ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: What simple methods can I use to direct excess water away from my crop field?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can dig shallow drainage ditches along the edges or lower points of your field. These trenches capture surface runoff and allow surplus water to flow safely away into a nearby bush, stream, or pond.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nubu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa loo shishigbɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ hiɛɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. ni oha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ shweshweeshwe kɛya jwɛi, faai, loo ŋshɔi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Can walking and working on very wet, muddy land ruin the quality of my soil for future farming?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni nɔ efɔ kɛ muji nɔ nyiɛmɔ kɛ nitsumɔ baanyɛ afite mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha okwaayeli wɔsɛɛ?

english: Yes, walking or working on soaking wet land squashes the natural air spaces in the earth. When the mud dries, it bakes into hard, brick-like clods that make it difficult for future crop roots to penetrate.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nyiɛmɔ loo nitsumɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ sũ lɛ gĩ lɛ Ebaafee nɔ ni wa ni efee nɔ ko ni wa tamɔ brikii. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso shishifãi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ akɛ amɛaabote mli.

english: How do I plan the number of farm workers I need to hire when clearing land with high water levels?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi ayibɔ ni ehe baahia ni maŋɔ amɛ nitsumɔ mli beni mijieɔ he ko ni nu fa babaoo yɛ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ?

english: You should account for soil conditions before hiring help. Wet, heavy ground doubles the time and effort needed per acre, so you will need to recruit extra workers to complete field preparation before the main planting season begins.
ga: Esa akɛ osusu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ he dani okɛ yelikɛbuamɔ aha. He ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni tsii lɛ baaha be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ acre kome mli lɛ afee enyɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe baahia ni okɛ nitsulɔi krokomɛi afata he koni amɛgbe he lɛ he saamɔ naa dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear away all the big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They act like human babies and burn easily, needing fast-growing shade crops like plantain to create a living umbrella that provides shade and traps moisture while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ abifabii ni amɛshãa oya. Enɛ biɔ ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ afee hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni haa hulutsoo be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava on the same plot with my maize without one choking the other?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe akatswaaa mɔ he?

english: Yes, because they grow at different speeds. Maize feeds aggressively early on and matures in a few months, while cassava grows slowly at first and expands after the maize is harvested, allowing both crops to share light and soil nutrients without fighting.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ amɛdaraa yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Abɛi yeɔ nii oya ni ekwɛɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ yeɔ la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni amɛwuuuu amɛhe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil stress. The plant drops its flowers to save water and stay alive, so consistent moisture during flowering helps flowers stay on and become fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛha amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing short, bent, and thick instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kukuji, amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe, ni amɛhe tseɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam roots push straight downward as they grow. If they encounter hard, unplowed soil or underground stones, the tubers are forced to stop expanding downward and become bent or stunted, which is why loose mounds of topsoil help them grow straight.
ga: Sweet potato shishifãi lɛ baatsi kɛya shi tɛ̃ɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ kɛji amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kpe. Anyɛɔ yitso lɛ nɔ koni ekpa shweremɔ kɛmiiya shi ni ebatsɔ ŋwɛi loo ŋwɛi ŋwɛi. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni etse ehe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which works with natural soil bacteria to pull nitrogen out of the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpeas finish growing, that stored nitrogen stays in the earth, serving as natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ekɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji tsina ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural defense against heat. By rolling its leaves tight, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to sunlight, preventing precious water from evaporating out of its leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ́ abɔle baai lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ nu ni jara wa lɛ naa koni ekajɛ baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce smaller fruit bunches after several years of heavy harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ miiwo aduawai bibii bibii yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛkpa nii waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Over years of heavy production, palm trees drain vital minerals like potassium out of the soil. Without adding organic compost or fertilizer back into the soil, the tree conserves energy by reducing the size and number of fruit bunches it forms.
ga: Yɛ afii ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo lɛ amli fɛɛ lɛ, Palm tsei lɛ jieɔ nibii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ potassium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei baanyɛ abu hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ aduawai akui lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibɔ ​​ni amɛbaa shi lɛ nɔ ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does spear grass make my young maize plants turn pale yellow and stay short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ spear jwɛi lɛ miiha mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni efee kuku lɛ?

english: Spear grass has underground root stems that spread quickly and consume nutrients and water faster than young maize can. It literally steals the food from the maize plants' roots, causing the yellowing from nitrogen starvation.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni eyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu oya fe ŋmãa bibii. Ejuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishifãi amli diɛŋtsɛ. Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ nitrogen ni bɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why does cutting off the lower branches of my tomato plants give me bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ afo tomato tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa yibii lɛ feɔ agbo lɛ?

english: A plant has a limited amount of food energy. When you remove extra branches and suckers, the plant stops wasting energy on unnecessary leaves and directs all its water and nutrients into making the remaining fruits larger and healthier.
ga: Tsei yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ko. Kɛji ojie niji kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ Tso lɛ baakpa hewalɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. ni ekwɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ nɔ koni eha aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ adara ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do armyworms eat through young maize leaves so much faster than mature maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii oya fe ŋmãa baai ni eda lɛ?

english: Young maize leaves are soft, tender, and rich in moisture, making them easy for young caterpillars to chew and digest. As maize plants mature, their leaves become tough and fibrous, which naturally slows down insect feeding.
ga: Baby corn baa lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmeii bibii akɛ amɛaaye ni amɛye nii. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ dara lɛ Ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nii fioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How long does it usually take from the day I plant cassava until it is fully mature for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ ŋmei kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edara kɛha nikpamɔ?

english: Cassava generally takes between 8 to 12 months to reach full maturity. Some early varieties can be harvested around 6 to 8 months, but giving the plant enough time allows underground tubers to grow full and heavy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei heɔ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 dani eshɛɔ ŋmei he. Abaanyɛ akpa mra be mli ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi yɛ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 mli, shi kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛhe afee shwiili.

english: Why do some of my cocoa seedlings wither and die within the first month of moving them to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni akɛwo amɛmli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings suffer from transplant shock when moved to the open field. In their first few weeks, direct sunlight and lack of steady moisture quickly dry out their delicate roots before they can establish deep into the soil.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ naa shoofeemɔ he amanehulu kɛji akɛ adu amɛ awo ŋmɔji ni mli tse mli. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nu ni bɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gĩɔ oya dani amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my young maize crop is hungry for fertilizer while it is growing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-baby corn lɛ hɔmɔ miiye lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii beni edaa lɛ?

english: Maize shows clear signs on its leaves when it needs nutrients. If the lower leaves start turning yellow in a V-pattern starting from the tips, the crop is short on nitrogen and needs feeding to build healthy stalks and ears.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia lɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni niyenii he miihia lɛ koni ekɛma ŋmeii kɛ toi ni wa.

english: Why do young plantain plants need shade from bigger trees when they are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei wuji ahe hiaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ? Tso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa?

english: Young plantain suckers have tender, broad leaves that lose water very quickly under direct, intense heat. Shading them keeps the surrounding soil cool and moist so the plant can focus energy on building strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. ni baaha nu afite oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ shishi Shading yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ shishifãi ni wa amamɔ he nii.

english: Why do my tomato plants start falling to the ground after a few weeks of growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miibɔi shikpɔŋ nɔ gbee yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛdara lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are naturally flexible vines that cannot stand upright on their own once heavy branches and fruits develop. Staking them with wooden sticks gives the plant the strong support it needs to stay upright and avoid rot.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ ji wain tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛtsei lɛ aniji kɛ amɛyibii lɛ eda. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni ekɛtsi enaa koni ekafite.

english: Why do cassava plants shed their leaves during prolonged dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival behavior for cassava during drought. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation and protects its underground tubers until fresh rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala su ni ŋmei yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Tsei haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbuɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ hee baa ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and thin with very small ears when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ toi bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, individual plants compete fiercely for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Instead of storing energy in thick stems and large cobs, the plants stretch thin trying to reach light.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baato amɛ tsei ashishifãi ni mli tse kɛ amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ amli lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Mohu ɔ, tso ɔ ngmɛɛ e he tsɔ, nɛ e ngɛ mɔde bɔe kaa e maa su la a he.

english: Why is it dangerous to let weeds grow around my pepper plants during their early month of growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-pepper tsei ni mikwɛɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli lɛ yɛ oshara.

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and steal water and nutrients from the soil. In the first few weeks, pepper plants are too weak to compete, leading to stunted growth and very few peppers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dalɛ baa shi ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to grow cabbage seeds in a protected seedbed before transplanting them into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu kaabii dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he dani akɛyaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tiny vegetable seeds are extremely vulnerable to heavy rainfall, hot sun, and soil insects. A nursery provides a safe environment to nurture young roots until the plants are strong enough to survive open field conditions.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nyɛɔ efiteɔ aduawai dumɔwui bibii titri. He ni akwɛɔ tsei lɛ yɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha shishifãi bibii lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ he baawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli tse mli.

english: Why do crops planted right at the start of the major rainy season grow better than those planted later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ shishijee mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting at the very start of the rains allows crops to take advantage of consistent soil moisture and cool ground temperatures, helping them establish deep root systems before heavy downpours or dry spells set in.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa nibii ni aduɔ lɛ náa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ lɛ he sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo hɔmɔ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which acts like food to keep plants green and strong. When the plant does not find enough food in the soil, it steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ tsei enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejuɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water in intense heat. By rolling their leaves, they reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and wind, helping them hold onto moisture until temperatures cool down.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ mli. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are like young human babies—their leaves burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and cool air it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ abifabii. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo lɛ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: If cassava plants are packed too closely, their underground roots fight each other for nutrients and water. This competition causes the plant to produce many thin, woody roots instead of big, starch-filled cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ shishifãi bibii babaoo yɛ ŋmeii agboi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop so fast even when it rained just two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbee shi oya nɛkɛ? Ni nugbɔ nɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ?

english: If your soil is very sandy or lacks organic matter like dry leaves and manure, it cannot hold water for long. The rainwater drains away quickly deep into the ground where short plant roots cannot reach it, leaving the soil dry.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋã waa loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmeii bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛŋ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tso lɛ shishifãi kukuji lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Why are the roots of my pepper plants turning soft and rotting under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like human beings do. When heavy water stays trapped around the roots for too long without draining, the roots drown and soil organisms attack the weak roots, making them rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛji akɛ muji ŋmɛ Shishifãi ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ baatutua shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ. ha egbo

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive chemical fertilizers. When the plant feels it does not have enough resources to raise fruits, it sheds its flowers to save energy and stay alive.
