ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ hao amɛ. Beni tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii lɛ bɛ. Ebaafolɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite ni ehi wala mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers take so long to grow big and swell underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need specific plant food, especially potassium, to swell up. If the soil is exhausted or if weeds are stealing nutrients, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy green tops instead of thick tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ tso niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi koni amɛfuu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ loo jwɛi lɛ miiju niyenii mli hewalɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ najiaŋ.

english: During the dry season, wild bushes and weeds dry up, forcing hungry insects to migrate to irrigated crop fields where plants are still green and juicy. Warm weather also causes pest eggs to hatch much faster.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, koo mli jwɛi kɛ jwɛi baagbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ afã kɛya ŋmɔji ni afɔɔ amɛ nu yɛ mli lɛ amli. Tsei lɛ yɛ eŋɔli lolo ni amɛhe yɛ nu. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ hu haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔ̃ɔ oya kwraa.

english: When a yam plant reaches full maturity, it naturally stops feeding its leaves and sends all remaining food energy down into the underground tuber. The drying of the vine is a natural signal that the yam is fully grown and ready to harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ebaakpa foliar niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi kɛya ŋmeii lɛ amli. Wein tsei lɛ ni agbiɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potatoes lɛ eda ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why should I space my maize plants out instead of planting many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli yɛ he ko moŋ fe ni madu babaoo? Dumɔwui ni abua naa yɛ bu kome mli.

english: When you put too many seeds in one hole, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to build strong stems and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso ni mli wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why does my farmland produce less yield every year if I keep planting cassava on the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same piece of land continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops with beans or leaving the land to rest helps restore soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii loo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers spread dry grass and leaves around the base of pepper plants during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo lɛ shwã jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ebɔle he lɛ? Pepper tso shishi yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: This practice is called mulching. The dry grass acts like a blanket that shades the soil from hot sunshine, keeps moisture in the ground longer, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is essential plant food. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newer top leaves, leaving the older bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, or by severe heat and water stress. Controlling pests and watering consistently helps protect the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa loo dɔlɛ kɛ nu mli haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni abu tso lɛ he.

english: Why do I find small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: This is damage caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm or stem borers. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the hatched caterpillars eat the tender inner tissues of the plant.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm loo stem borers lɛ kɛbaa. Kplukai fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni baa lɛ baaye fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear all the large trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and heavy heat. Shading trees or plantains act as natural umbrellas, keeping the air moist and protecting young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Shade tsei loo tsei bibii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn watery and rot underground during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ hoɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive. When water collects on the field for too long without draining, it drowns the roots and invites fungal diseases that cause rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔɔɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ aba.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers fall off before producing any bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant suffers stress, such as heavy rain knocking off blossoms, extreme hot weather, or tiny insects like thrips eating the flower buds before pod formation.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ kpe, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ dani ashishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and light away from your crop roots, leaving your plants starved.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ la ni jɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli oya Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which acts as food for green leafy growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps restore the green color and keeps the plant strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha baai eŋɔlii lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ aná su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop have huge bushy leaves but very tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen late in the season, the plant puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of roots. Avoiding heavy manure late in the growth cycle forces the cassava to store its energy underground in the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ he nii moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ. Nibii ni tsii ni tsii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ naagbee lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep falling off without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if the farm gets too hot and dry, or if there are no tiny midges (insects) to pollinate them. Keeping shade trees and moist leaf litter on the ground preserves the right climate for those insects to do their work.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii bɛ ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ, tsei ni akɛbaawo hulutsoo mli ni baa ni mli efɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shihilɛ ni sa ni nakai kooloi lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii yɛ mli lɛ ahi shi.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking sap from the underside of the leaf. Spraying the leaves with organic neem leaf extract or insecticidal soap helps stop the insects and lets the leaves open back up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem leaf extract loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi lɛ anaa ni eha baai lɛ agbele ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my sorghum survive long dry spells much better than my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Sorghum has deeper roots and leaves that roll up tightly in heat to hold onto moisture, whereas maize leaves stay open and lose water quickly. This makes sorghum naturally built for drier climates.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ latsaa koni ekɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa baa lɛ hiɔ shi ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Enɛ haa ŋmãa feɔ nɔ ni ama yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans together in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil through their roots. This feeds the neighboring maize plants naturally, reducing your need for expensive store-bought fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ lɛ aná niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ahe ehiaaa.

english: You should wait until rain has soaked the soil at least wrist-deep for a few days in a row, rather than planting right after the first shower. Planting in dry or barely damp soil causes seeds to rot or dry out before roots can form.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hoo lɛ kɛyashi onineshi gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ, moŋ fe ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nɔ ni mli edɔ fioo nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛgbi dani shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to clear tall trees and put stakes up for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni mikɛ amɛ awo tso nɔ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food that grows large underground tubers. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also protects them from rot and fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baa ni fiteɔ kɛ fungal baa helai anaa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani etsɔɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This black spot is caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when roots cannot get enough calcium due to irregular soil moisture. Mulching around the roots keeps the soil wet evenly so the plant can draw up calcium to build strong fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ nɛɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ anaagbee ŋmɔtɔ, ni baa beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Mulching around Shishifãi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ mli koni amɛfee aduawai ni mli wa.

english: Why do weeds damage my young crops much more during the first month than when the crops get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli fe be mli ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have short roots and small leaves, making them too weak to fight weeds for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Once crops grow tall and cast shade on the ground, they naturally stop weeds from growing fast.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji kɛ baai bibii. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo lɛ Jwɛi lɛ baakpa shweremɔ oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting if I leave them in the ground too long past harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe kpamɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are storage organs that keep absorbing water from the soil. Once they mature, leaving them buried too long during wet periods exposes them to excess moisture and soil fungi, causing them to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji gbɔmɔtso mli nibii ni toɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji edara kwraa Ashi lɛ ni afu lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Enɛ baaha amɛná hulutsoo kɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ha egbo

english: Why do some of my cassava stems taste bitter when cooked while others are sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ekomɛi ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ ahoo amɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: The bitterness is caused by naturally occurring chemical compounds called cyanogenic glucosides. 'Bitter' cassava has high levels and needs soaking or fermenting before cooking, while 'sweet' cassava has very low levels and is safe to boil directly.
ga: Tsofai ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ cyanogen glucosides lɛ ji nɔ ni haa ŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa. ‘Bitter’ cassava lɛ yɛ nɔ ni fa babaoo ni ehe miihia ni awo mli loo afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ dani ahoo. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ‘Sweet’ cassava lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa kwraa, ni abaanyɛ ahoo lɛ shweshweeshwe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and show yellow patches during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Curling and yellowing leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by planting stem cuttings taken from already infected plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. aloo kɛtsɔ niji ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ momo lɛ amli lɛ ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoyam plants grow better in shaded areas than under direct hot sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoyam leaves are large and tender, making them lose water quickly under strong sun. They naturally thrive in cool, moist, and partially shaded environments like tree canopies.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ dara ni amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛ daa yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo fioo yɔɔ, tamɔ tsei ashishi.

english: What causes my cocoyam stems and leaves to yellow and rot close to the ground?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo tsei kɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: This rot is usually caused by excessive waterlogging in the soil or a fungal disease called cocoyam root rot, which thrives in poorly drained soils during heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cocoyam shishifãi ni fiteɔ. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How long does a pineapple sucker usually take from the day I plant it to produce a mature fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ shwereɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni adu lɛ?

english: A pineapple plant takes between 12 to 18 months to produce a harvestable fruit, depending on the plant variety, soil fertility, and rainfall pattern.
ga: Pineapple tsei heɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 dani amɛwoɔ yibii ni abaanyɛ akpa. Edamɔ tsei henɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔmɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why are the pineapples on my farm developing small and uneven sizes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Uneven pineapple sizes usually happen when you plant suckers of different initial sizes together, or when the plants are spaced too closely and compete for soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni dalɛi kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji okɛ ŋmeii ni dalɛi srɔtoi jeɔ shishi lɛ ekome du. Aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ ni amɛmiitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell that a pineapple fruit on my field is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A pineapple is ripe for harvest when the color at the base changes from dark green to yellow or orange, and the fruit gives off a sweet aroma when smelled.
ga: Pineapple lɛ eshɛ shi kɛha nikpamɔ kɛ́ eshishigbɛ su lɛ tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Ni kɛ́ onu he lɛ, ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I safely grow cassava together with cocoyam on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei kɛ kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, cassava and cocoyam can be grown together because cassava grows tall and takes light from above, while cocoyam stays lower and tolerates the shade created by the cassava branches.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ he kome beni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa la kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo hiɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ ni ekpɛlɛɔ hulutsoo ni ŋmei niji kɛbaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield better when I plant different types together instead of just one crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ tsei babaoo fee ekome lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ tso kome pɛ

english: Mixing crops helps maximize land space, provides soil cover to retain moisture, and reduces the risk of pests and diseases destroying your entire farm output.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yaa hiɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi. ni oha oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baafite oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ lɛ aba shi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct sunlight and dry winds. Without shade trees or plantains around them to block the harsh sun, the leaves lose moisture faster than the roots can drink water, causing them to burn and shrivel.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛshãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and dry out easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist for the cocoa seedlings during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kookoo dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: What causes my maize leaves to turn yellow at the tips and along the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbee kɛ amɛteŋgbɛ?

english: Yellowing along the center of older maize leaves is a common sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is the main food plants use to make healthy green leaves, so adding organic compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps them regain their deep green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa momo lɛ teŋ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my main crops help improve my soil?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that work with beneficial soil bacteria to capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. As their roots and leaves decay, they naturally feed and enrich the surrounding soil for other crops.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwo sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fite lɛ Amɛbaana niyenii ni amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ fɛfɛo koni amɛkwɛ tsei krokomɛi.

english: Why is my cassava producing very tall stems and green leaves, but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ waa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has excessive nitrogen or when plants are crowded too closely together, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves and stems rather than storing food underground. Giving cassava plants proper spacing encourages them to build thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ebaai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ha gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaawo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and put up stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ amli jwɛi ni mawo tso nɔ koni makwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need full sunshine on their leaves to manufacture food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leafy vines off the ground away from shade and damp soil where weeds and rot can harm them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu ni fa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa he ni hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ he ni jwɛi kɛ fitemɔ baanyɛ aye amɛ awui yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain mat produce smaller bunches if I leave all the young suckers growing around the mother stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii ni bɔle nyɛ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: All the suckers growing around a single plantain stem compete for the same soil nutrients and water. Cutting back extra suckers so that only one or two strong shoots remain ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Single stems lɛ he lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce its flowers directly on the main trunk instead of at the tips of leafy branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni ewoɔ tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower on older, thick wood (a behavior called cauliflory) so that the trunk and main limbs can support the weight of heavy cocoa pods as they develop and mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei ni egbɔ ni mli wa lɛ anɔ. (su ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cauliflower) koni tsitsi lɛ kɛ eniji titrii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni tsii lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience sudden weather stress, such as extreme heat or dry soil. Keeping the root zone cool and evenly damp using mulch helps the plant hold onto its blossoms until fruits set.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe trukaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Kɛ́ akɛ muji tsu nii ni akɛha shishifã lɛ mli fɛ̃i ni edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture for me to start planting maize after the early rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ?

english: The first light rain only wets the surface, which dries out fast under the sun and can kill sprouting seeds. It is best to wait until rain soaks deep enough into the soil so that when you dig a small hole, the earth feels damp down to the depth of your palm.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baaha ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ. Egbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni ebaanyɛ egbe dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni kɛ́ otsa bu bibioo ko Shikpɔŋ lɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi onine mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient required for foliage growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying urea or NPK fertilizer helps the plants remain green and produce strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ urea loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast even after I water my vegetable crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo mitsei lɛ anɔ po lɛ?

english: Soil with low organic matter cannot hold moisture effectively. Adding dry animal manure or compost improves the soil structure, acting like a sponge that holds water near the roots for a much longer time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli faaa yɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be babaoo.

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing—typically 2 to 3 weeks after germination for the first application, and at 5 to 6 weeks for the second application. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the root system.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida waa, bei pii lɛ, otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ beni eje kpo kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, kɛ otsii 5 kɛyashi 6 kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: What causes the small green pods on my cocoa tree to turn black and dry up?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ? Yɛ mi koko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in cool, damp, and overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and harvesting mature pods regularly prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa koni hulu lɛ ashɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ni oookpa daa lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies sucking the leaf juices or transmitting leaf-curl viruses. Controlling these insects early using neem oil solution or recommended pesticides keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa nu loo helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the ground when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excess standing water suffocates the roots and promotes fungal rot, which is why planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Yams need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce food through photosynthesis, which feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground where they are exposed to sunlight and protected from ground rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe tsei lɛ akashɛɔ hei ni hulu la shɛɔ yɛ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How deep should I plant my maize seeds during planting season?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep (roughly up to your first knuckle). Planting too shallow causes seeds to dry out or get eaten by birds, while planting too deep wastes the seed's energy before it reaches sunlight.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 (aaafee klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmãa lɛ shishi). Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo okpoi baaye amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ afite dani amɛyashɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden lack of water. Providing consistent moisture and light shade during extremely hot periods keeps the blossoms healthy so they turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli dɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu bɛ trukaa. Kɛ́ akɛ fɛ̃i kɛ la haa be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa bɔni afee ni amɛtsɔmɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when heavy winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko tswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a bamboo fork (propping) and planting windbreak trees along farm borders stops them from blowing down.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Akɛ ŋmei fɔk ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ kɛ tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa amɛ shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings scorch and die when I plant them in a field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate roots that cannot handle full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa from direct sun heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋta. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to build green leaves and grow strong, so adding organic compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: When crop seeds are planted too close to each other, the plants fight for the same limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each seed proper distance ensures every plant gets enough food to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa nakai nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ dumɔwui wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: How can I tell if my pepper crops are getting too much water during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: When pepper plants get excess water, their roots drown because they cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. You will notice the leaves yellowing, drooping, and soft rot developing at the base of the stems.
ga: Kɛji pepper tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Obaana ŋmɔtɔ, baai ni miigbee shi, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant groundnuts in the same farm where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them after a heavy-feeding crop like maize naturally restores soil fertility for future plantings.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ yɛ kooloi aniyenii nibii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli nibii ni aduɔ.

english: Curled leaves with yellow spots on cassava are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems helps protect your farm from this illness.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hela nɛɛ he.

english: Why do officers advise us in the Northern Region to sow sorghum right at the very start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooyigbɛ onukpai lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Sorghum needs moisture early on to germinate and send down deep roots. Sowing right as the early rains begin ensures the crop establishes itself quickly before the dry spell returns, allowing it to complete its growth cycle.
ga: Sorghum he miihia ŋmɔtɔ mra. Koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ amaje Dumɔ ni sa beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa. Enɛ baagbe dalɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ naa.

english: How do I know that my yam tubers under the ground are mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams indicate maturity above ground when their green leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up naturally. This means the vine has stopped growing and has transferred all its energy down into expanding the yam tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yaa shi koni ekɛwo sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my tomato plants even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa mi-tomato tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal nutrients, root space, and sunlight away from your tomato plants. Even with plenty of rain, the weeds absorb the plant food before the tomatoes can get to it.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tomato tsei amli lɛ oya. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Jwɛi hu shwieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli dani tomatoi lɛ shɛɔ he.

english: Why should I spread dry grass around the base of my garden vegetables during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi mashwã mi-aduawai lɛ ashishi yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, acts as a protective blanket over the earth. It shields the soil from hot direct sunlight, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ je lɛ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes go soft and rot so quickly when I transport them from my farm to the market in Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya kɛji mikɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee jara nɔ yɛ Accra lɛ?

english: Tomatoes bruise easily when stacked in deep wooden crates, and heat during long travel speeds up rotting. Using shallow, ventilated crates and transporting during cooler hours helps them stay firm and fresh until you reach the market.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ oya kɛ akɛto adekai ni mli kwɔ amli. Ni dɔlɛ ni baa yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ baaha efite oya. Kɛ́ okɛ adekai ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli tsu nii, ni okɛ amɛ tee yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ehee kɛyashiɔ be mli ni obaashɛ jara nɔ.

english: How can I prevent my harvested yams from rotting while waiting for buyers to come to my village?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ aba mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if left on damp ground or in direct sunlight. Storing them off the ground in a cool, shaded, well-ventilated yam barn allows air to flow around them, preventing moisture buildup and fungal decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ loo yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ sweet potato ato shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ sweet potato shĩa ko ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ abɔle ohe. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buaa ehe naa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do market women in the city tell me my harvested cassava is bad inside even though the outside skin looks fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jara nɔ yoo lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ yɛ fɔ yɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ hiɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ

english: Cassava begins to spoil internally within 24 to 48 hours after harvest due to exposure to air, causing dark streaks inside the tuber. Processing it quickly into gari or flour, or keeping the tubers intact without skin cuts, helps preserve quality.
ga: Cassava jeɔ shishi efiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Ehaa okadii diji baa yitso lɛ mli Afeɔ lɛ oya ni efeɔ kri loo ashikishaŋ. aloo ni aha yitso lɛ ahi shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli ni afooo hewolo lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes my stored dried maize get full of tiny insects and turn to powdery dust after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ nɔ? ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Weevils attack maize when the grain is not dried completely before storage. Ensuring your maize is thoroughly sun-dried until hard and storing it in clean, airtight bags prevents insects from multiplying and destroying your crop.
ga: Weevils tutuaa ŋmãa kɛji ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ koni o-abele lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛto vacuum kotokui ni mli tse mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi bibii akafee babaoo ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantains turn soft and yellow prematurely before I can get them to the city market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ mra dani amɛshɛɔ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally produce a gas as they ripen, which speeds up ripening in surrounding bunches when packed tightly in warm trucks. Harvesting them at the proper green maturity stage and keeping them shaded and ventilated delays this process.
ga: Plantains lɛ jieɔ gas kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ akwɛ̃ oya kɛ́ akɛwo lɔle ni mli edɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akpa lɛ beni eshɛ he ni sa ni eda lɛ, ni akɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: If some of my harvested vegetables show small black spots, does that mean the whole harvest is completely ruined?
ga: Kɛji akɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii diji Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ fɛɛ fite?

english: Not necessarily. Sorting damaged crops immediately stops rot from spreading to healthy ones. Slightly spotted produce can often be sold locally right away or processed for cooking rather than being thrown out entirely.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ nibii ni anaa yɛ fioo lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ he ni atsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ loo atsuɔ he nii koni akɛhoo nii moŋ fe ni aaashɛrɛ ashwie kwraa.

english: Is it better for me to sell my crops to local buyers in my village or pay to transport them to big city markets?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ maha maŋbii ni heɔ nii yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ loo mawo nyɔmɔ koni mikɛya jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ maji wuji amli lɛ?

english: City markets offer higher prices, but long transport increases the risk of crop spoilage and heavy transport costs. Selling locally reduces handling damage and guarantees a quick sale, which is safer for perishable crops.
ga: Maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ haa. Shi be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ haa oshara ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ kɛ shika babaoo ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kuu lɛ mli nihɔɔmɔ haa nibii ni elaaje yɛ nitsumɔ mli lɛ baa shi ni ehaa ahɔ̃ɔ oya. Enɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ oya.

english: Why are my pepper fruits rotting right on the bush before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ miifite yɛ jwɛi lɛ nɔ dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: High humidity and fungal diseases attack peppers when plants are overcrowded or watered directly on their leaves. Proper spacing between plants and harvesting ripe peppers promptly prevents fruit rot on the farm.
ga: Fɛ̃i lɛ fa babaoo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa ŋmeii kɛji akɛ awo tso lɛ nɔ fe nine loo awo lɛ nu yɛ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa lɛ baatsi aduawai ni fiteɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my harvested grains are dry enough to store without moulding overnight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto ni mikɛfeee nɔ ko nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: You can test grain dryness by biting a kernel; if it makes a sharp cracking sound instead of denting, it is dry enough. Properly dried grains prevent mold spores from growing during storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ egbi ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ amɛ ni oooye lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efee gbee ni naa wa waa yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ lɛ, no lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa. Ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsiɔ ŋmei tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni ekakwɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How can I stop my leafy green vegetables from wilting and losing value on the way to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-green lɛ naa koni ekagbo ni ekafite yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Leafy greens lose moisture rapidly in heat, causing them to limp and look spoiled. Harvesting early in the morning, keeping them wrapped in damp sacks, and protecting them from direct sun keeps them crisp for buyers.
ga: Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ amli fɛ̃i lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛwo la mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo. Kpamɔ leebi ni akɛ kotokui ni mli efɔ ewo mli. Ni hebuu kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Sir, why do my tomato leaves keep curling and turning yellow even after I spray them with expensive pest chemicals?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ moŋ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by viruses spread by tiny insects like whiteflies. Chemicals can kill the insects, but once the virus is inside the plant, spraying will not cure it; choosing disease-resistant seeds is a better solution.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsofai baanyɛ agbe kooloi lɛ. Shi kɛ́ hela lɛ bote nitsumɔhe lɛ, Spraying lɛ tsaŋ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooohala lɛ ji tsabaa ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to need more and more chemical spray every year just to protect them from insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ he hiaa daa afi koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ?

english: Over time, insects can build up resistance to the same chemical if it is used repeatedly. Switching between different types of spray and allowing beneficial insects to live on your farm helps keep pest populations down naturally.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, kooloi baanyɛ atswa tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he hewalɛ amɛma shi kɛ akɛtsu nii shii abɔ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ahe tsakemɔ ni oooha kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ahi oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are wilting because of a disease or simply because they need water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miigbo loo nu kɛkɛ ni ehe hiaa lɛ hewɔ?

english: Plants that need water will usually droop during the hot afternoon sun and recover by early morning. If a plant has a disease, it will stay wilted even after watering and may show yellow spots or rotting stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu he hiaa lɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ leebi maŋkpa. Kɛ́ tso ko yɛ hela lɛ, ebaaya nɔ egbɔjɔ kɛ́ awo lɛ nu po. ni ebaanyɛ ejie ŋmɔtɔ loo tsei ni egboi kpo.

english: Why are the first harvests from my newly planted crop usually very small and low in yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa ni jɛɔ mitsei heei ni midu lɛ amli lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Young crops spend most of their early energy building strong roots and thick stems rather than fruit. As the plant matures and its root system expands, it produces larger and more abundant harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni mli tse yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Beni tso lɛ daa ni eshishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ. Ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni fa babaoo aba.

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow after heavy rains fall on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away essential nutrients like nitrogen from the topsoil and fill air pockets in the ground with water, making it hard for the plant roots to breathe and absorb food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ nu awo kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Is there a reason why weeds grow much faster than my planted crops right after land preparation?
ga: Ani yiŋtoo ko yɛ ni haa jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni misaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are native plants that have adapted over centuries to quickly grab soil nutrients and water, giving them an advantage over farm crops that require specific soil conditions to grow.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛjie niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni biɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Sir, why do crops grown inside a greenhouse grow much faster than the ones I plant in the open field?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Greenhouses create a controlled environment that keeps temperature and humidity steady while protecting crops from harsh weather, allowing the plants to grow without stress.
ga: Greenhouses haa shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why do insects still attack my vegetables inside a greenhouse when the house is completely covered?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-vegetables lɛ lolo yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ? Ani shĩa lɛ eha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Tiny insects like thrips can enter on workers' clothes, through small tears in the netting, or on young seedlings brought from outside, and the warm greenhouse environment helps them multiply quickly.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ thrips baanyɛ abote nitsulɔi atadei amli. Kɛtsɔ yaafo bibii ni yɔɔ ŋshɔŋ loo yɛ dumɔwui bibii ni akɛba kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni shihilɛ ni mli edɔ yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfɔɔ oya.

english: Why do vegetables inside a greenhouse require extra feeding compared to plants in the open soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii kroko he hiaa tsei ni yɔɔ greenhouse lɛ kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Greenhouse crops are often grown in limited soil or bags where roots cannot search far for food, so they depend entirely on the farmer to supply all their daily nutrients through water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ greenhouse tsei yɛ sũ loo kotokui fioo komɛi amli. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aya shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao niyenii, no hewɔ lɛ tsei nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ okwaafoi pɛ anɔ koni amɛtsɔ nu nɔ amɛha amɛ daa gbi niyenii.

english: Why does mixing different crops in the same field help reduce the amount of chemical spray I need to use?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Pests usually target one specific type of crop. When you mix different crops, pests get confused by the different smells and shapes, making it harder for them to spread and destroy the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi futu mli lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe mfonirii srɔtoi futuɔ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkpãtã amɛhiɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods growing so small instead of getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miidara bibii moŋ fe agboi lɛ?

english: Small pods often happen when older cocoa varieties, such as Nkrumah cocoa, are planted. Upgrading to newer cocoa varieties and feeding the trees nutrients like potassium helps produce larger, heavier pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji akɛ adu kookoo henɔi momo, tamɔ Eunkruma kookoo. Kɛji akɛ atsake kɛya kookoo henɔ hee nɔ ni aha tso lɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii lɛ aba.

english: What is Nkrumah cocoa, and why are farmers replacing it?
ga: Mɛni ji Nkrumah kookoo ni mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi miitsɔ amɛhe amɛmiiwo enɔ lɛ?

english: Nkrumah cocoa is an older cocoa variety that frequently produced small pods. Farmers are moving away from it in favor of modern varieties that yield much larger and heavier pods.
ga: Eunkruma cocoa ji kookoo henɔ ko ni etsɛ ni bei pii lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii. Okwaafoi miitsɔ amɛjwɛŋmɔ kɛmiijɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii kwraa lɛ anɔ.

english: How do newer cocoa varieties compare to the older ones used in Ghana?
ga: Te kookoo henɔi heei lɛ kɛ kookoo henɔi momo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ Ghana lɛ toɔ he amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Newer cocoa varieties produce much larger and heavier pods compared to older types like Nkrumah cocoa, which suffered from producing small, light pods.
ga: Kookoo henɔi heei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii kwraa kɛ akɛto kookoo henɔi momo tamɔ Nkrumah kookoo, ni na amanehulu yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsiimɔ waaa lɛ ahe.

english: How can I get my cocoa trees to produce larger and heavier pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cacao tsei lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii?

english: You can achieve bigger and heavier pods by planting improved cocoa varieties and giving the trees sufficient potassium, which supports pod expansion and weight.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná ŋmeii wuji ni tsii kɛtsɔ kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni ooodu kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni oooha tso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni pod lɛ dalɛ kɛ emli tsiimɔ aya hiɛ.

english: What specific role does potassium play in cocoa farming?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ pɔtɛɛ potassium tsuɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Potassium is an essential nutrient that helps cocoa trees build large, heavy pods, overcoming the problem of small pod development.
ga: Potassium ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii. Aye naagba ni ji pods bibii ni afeɔ lɛ nɔ kunim.

english: What should I do if my current cocoa farm is giving small, low-yielding pods?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ ni miyɔɔ mli amrɔ nɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yibiiwoo faaa?

english: You should gradually phase out low-yielding varieties like Nkrumah cocoa, plant improved high-yielding varieties, and apply potassium to boost pod size.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni wooo yibii babaoo tamɔ Cocoa Nkrumah lɛ fiofio. Dumɔ tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo. and use potassium to increase pod size

english: My mango trees are having growth and fruiting issues. Can fertilizer help them?
ga: Mi mango tso lɛ miina naagbai yɛ dalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo mli. Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua amɛ?

english: Yes, applying potassium can greatly assist mango trees when they face growth or fruiting problems, helping them recover and perform better.
ga: Hɛɛ, potassium ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mango tsei waa kɛ́ amɛkɛ dalɛ loo yibiiwoo he naagbai kpe. Helps the mango recover and function better.

english: Can I use potassium to treat problems on crops other than cocoa, like mangoes?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ potassium atsa naagbai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi amli fe kookoo, tamɔ mango?

english: Yes, while potassium is great for making cocoa pods large and heavy, it is also very effective at helping resolve yield and health issues in mango trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ potassium hi kɛha kookoo ŋmeii agboi ni tsii moŋ. Shi etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ hu yɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛtsuɔ mango tsei afeemɔ kɛ hewalɛnamɔ he naagbai ahe nii lɛ mli.

english: Can the same nutrient treatment be used for both my cocoa and mango trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ mi cacao kɛ mango tsei lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, potassium is beneficial for both crops; it helps cocoa produce heavy, large pods and assists mango trees in overcoming production problems.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, potassium he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji ni tsii baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa mango tsei yɛ ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ ahe naagbai anɔ kunimyeli mli.

english: How did other cocoa farmers solve the problem of small cocoa pods?
ga: Te kookoo okwaafoi krokomɛi miitsu kookoo ŋmeii bibii ahe naagba lɛ he nii amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Farmers solved the small pod issue by phasing out older varieties like Nkrumah cocoa and introducing improved cocoa types supported by proper potassium fertilization.
ga: Okwaafoi tsuɔ ŋmeii bibii ahe naagba lɛ he nii Ejieɔ kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ tamɔ Nkrumah kookoo lɛ fiofio ni ekɛ kookoo henɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni potassium ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and heat. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist while they are establishing roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for leaf growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Extreme heat damages tomato pollen, preventing the flowers from being fertilized. When pollination fails, the plant drops its flowers to save energy until cooler conditions return.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Ehaa fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do fall armyworms hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of my maize plants during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms avoid direct heat and sunlight. They crawl into the central leaves because it stays cool and moist, allowing them to safely feed on soft inner leaves without drying out.
ga: Autumn shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Amɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa baa lɛ teŋ ejaakɛ ehiɔ shi ni eyɛ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even though the leaves above ground look very big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava spends all its energy growing heavy leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ starch baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai ni tsii kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and roll inward during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from heat. By reducing leaf surface area exposed to the sun, the plant slows down water loss through evaporation.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛtsɔ baai ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ ni abaajie lɛ shi lɛ nɔ. Tsei haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my farm before planting maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani miduɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas work with beneficial soil microbes to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, providing natural plant food that the next maize crop uses to grow strong.
ga: Cowpea kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cassava using stem cuttings instead of using the seeds from the plant flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ atsu nii yɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds from cassava produce unpredictable offspring that may yield small roots. Planting stem cuttings produces an exact copy of a strong, heavy-yielding parent plant.
ga: Cassava dumɔwui woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba ni baanyɛ aha shishifãi bibii aba. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ eko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo baa.

english: Why does Striga weed cause my maize plants to turn yellow and stop growing when it grows next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ miiha mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni ekpa shweremɔ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches its roots directly to the roots of the maize plant, stealing water, nutrients, and plant food before the maize can use them.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa ŋmãa tsei ashishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ, ni ejuɔ tso lɛ nu, niyenii mli nibii, kɛ niyenii dani ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. The energy gathered by leaves in direct sunlight goes down into the soil to build larger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hewalɛ ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ amli lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an important food they need to grow. This happens when the soil lacks nutrients or when heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdu. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii jeɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is mostly caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that suck the sap out of leaves, or by leaf-curl viruses spread by whiteflies.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ hela ko ni haa ŋmeii yɛji shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays around them for too long in poorly drained soil. The excess standing water chokes the roots and allows fungal rots to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why are my yam vines drying up prematurely before the tubers grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miigbi oya dani bulbs lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up early when they are attacked by fungal diseases like leaf spot or anthracnose, or when severe dry weather causes the plant to run out of water before completing its growth cycle.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa mli tsɛŋemɔ hela loo anthracnose tutua amɛ. aloo be mli ni shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ náaa nu dani amɛdalɛ be lɛ baa naagbee.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought or when pest insects like mirids bite the flower stems. The tree drops its flowers to save energy when conditions are difficult.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ loo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids lɛ ŋmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli wa.

english: What causes the bottom of my tomato fruits to turn black and rot while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit. It frequently happens when watering is inconsistent or when weather is extremely dry.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ shi be fɛɛ be loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ miwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the earth. When the heavy bunch forms, the plant becomes top-heavy, and weak roots or soil pests can easily cause the whole tree to tip over in light wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji kuu agbo ko fee Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Ni shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ loo kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ mli oya.

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that hides inside the tender inner leaves of young maize plants to feed on new leaves before the plant matures.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii amli baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei dani tsei lɛ adara.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant maize after harvesting cowpeas or groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa beni mikpa tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting maize afterwards allows the maize to feed on that leftover natural plant food.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Sɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid applying dry fertilizer on dry soil under strong heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Chemical fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve and work. When applied to dry soil in heat, the fertilizer concentrated around the roots can scorch and burn the plant roots, causing damage instead of helping.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli ni etsu nii. Kɛji akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni mli edɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã ni amɛshã. Ekɛ fitemɔ baa moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or are standing in too much water. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps them turn green again so they can produce large, healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ miiye nitrogen loo amɛyɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛha toi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look wilted in the hot afternoon sun but recover in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi obaaná hewalɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the ground, so they curl to conserve moisture. As the weather cools in the evening, water balance returns and the leaves stand back up.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛfoɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Nu lɛ sɛɛ fo ekoŋŋ ni baai lɛ te shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences water stress. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ tamɔ tomato.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but have tiny, thin roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo, shi amɛshishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is planted in very hard soil, it spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of roots. Loose soil and balanced nutrients encourage the plant to swell its underground tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa waa nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ baatsu nii. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during cold, damp rainy seasons. Clearing heavy shade and removing affected pods quickly prevents the fungus from destroying the rest of your harvest.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ́ ojie hulutsoo be ni tsii ni ojie ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akafite onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants look crumpled and covered in light green and yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and using clean stem cuttings keeps your farm free from this virus.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ kɛ tsei ni he tse ni ooofo lɛ baaye abua ni oŋmɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni hela nɛɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and thin when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too close together fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to spread its roots and catch light to grow thick and strong.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni enáa la ni haa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ shi.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can be damaged by soil pests like nematodes or weighed down by heavy bunches. Supporting the stems with strong wooden props and mounding soil around the base keeps them standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni sũ mli kooloi tamɔ nematodes baanyɛ afite loo amɛtsɔ jwɛi babaoo. Kɛ nɔ ko ni akɛ tso ni wa fee ni akɛ muji ebɔle he lɛ fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ. Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni edamɔ shi.

english: Why do my cowpea crops stop growing and look sickly after heavy rains flood my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ekpa shweremɔ ni amɛfeee nɔ ni ehiii yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots so they cannot take up nutrients. Digging simple drainage channels allows excess water to run off so the roots can breathe.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaatsɔ mli Enɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting shoots in the barn before planting season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally break dormancy and sprout after a period of rest, especially if stored in warm or humid conditions. Storing tubers in a cool, well-ventilated yam barn slows down sprouting until you are ready to plant.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ wɔɔhe ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe be fioo sɛɛ. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulu tsoɔ loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo ŋmeii atoohe ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛyashi be mli ni obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when I clear all the big trees away from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Shading trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the air cool and preserving soil moisture so the young plants can establish strong roots.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ambrela ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Bɔni afee ni tso bibioo lɛ anyɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to make green leaves and food. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli kɛ niyenii. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: When water collects and sits in the soil for too long, it pushes out all the air roots need to breathe. Without air, the roots suffocate and harmful fungal diseases quickly move in to cause rotting.
ga: Beni nu buaa ehe naa ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ ni he hiaa shishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu lɛ kɛyaa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ boteɔ mli oya ni amɛkɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small stems growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain tree, they steal water and nutrients. Removing extra suckers ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ kɛbɔle Dumɔwui titrii babaoo tsɔ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients that your main crops need to grow. Removing weeds gives your crops full access to the resources in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei titrii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes small holes appear on my maize leaves with little green caterpillars hiding in the funnels?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-abɛi lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii lɛ miifee? Ejeɔ kpo kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Ekɛ ehe ewo koni lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that eats the tender leaves inside the plant. Controlling them early prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ tso lɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛ nɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does placing dry grass around the roots of my crops help them grow better in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi awo he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la mli.

english: Dry grass acts like a blanket over the soil, called mulch. It shades the soil from the hot sun, slows down water evaporation, and keeps the roots cool during hot days.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce lots of flowers, but the flowers fall off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat is too extreme, when watering is inconsistent, or when the plant lacks nutrients needed to form fruit. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ shi.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans together with my maize make my soil richer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ kɛfataa ŋmãa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can draw nitrogen out of the air and put it directly into the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing neighboring crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ mawo tso ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for developing big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni baa lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni eha sũ lɛ he tse kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that create natural shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until it matures.
