ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines to tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ fĩɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to capture as much sunlight as possible to grow large tubers. Staking also prevents the leaves from rotting due to damp soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away surface nutrients or flood the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ loo ekɛ nu ewo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Maize pulls a lot of nutrients out of the ground, while leguminous crops like groundnuts and beans have roots that capture nitrogen from the air and return fertility back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi ni shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same limited water, soil food, and sunlight, causing all the plants to remain small and weak.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la ni faaa nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even when I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water and fertilizer nutrients faster than your main crops can reach them, leaving your crops hungry and dry.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otso titri lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii ni oduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with brown powders inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛmli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the stem and leaf whorls during the day, eating the soft plant tissue and leaving behind droppings.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei kɛ baai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛyeɔ tsei amli fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot and dry or when the plant suffers from water stress, which prevents proper pollination and fruit development.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ aduawai ni sa lɛ anaa.

english: The very first rain is often a 'false rain' followed by intense heat. If you plant too early, the hot soil will dry up and kill the young seeds before the true rainy season settles.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ ji ‘amale nugbɔ’, ni hulutsoo ni naa wa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbeɔ dumɔwui bibii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baashɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally dry up and fall off, the main stem grows thick, and the ground around the base of the plant starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ mli tsɔne titri lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ.

english: Why should I use liquid fertilizer on my crops instead of the solid granular ones I usually buy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni mifɔɔ hemɔ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Liquid fertilizer works faster because plant leaves and roots can absorb nutrients immediately without waiting for rain or soil moisture to dissolve solid granules.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya ejaakɛ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛmɛ nugbɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛjie ŋmeii ni wa lɛ.

english: Are fertilizers made here in Ghana just as good for my crops as imported ones from places like Russia?
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni afeɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ bɔ ni ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaajɛ hei tamɔ Russia?

english: Yes, locally produced fertilizers are specially made for Ghana's specific soil types and tropical weather conditions, making them very effective and often easier to get fresh.
ga: Hɛɛ, afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni afeɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ krɛdɛɛ aha Ghana shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ. Enɛ haa nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa, ni bei pii lɛ, ewaaa akɛ aaahi shi ehee.

english: How can I tell if my crops need liquid fertilizer to help them flourish?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia nu ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves turn pale or yellow, growth slows down, and stems stay thin. Spraying liquid fertilizer gives them a quick boost to turn deep green and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. shweremɔ blɛoo ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli etse lolo Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara oya.

english: How do crops actually take in liquid fertilizer when I spray it on my farm?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hiaa nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahaa tɛŋŋ beni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops absorb liquid fertilizer directly through tiny openings on their leaves called stomata, as well as through their roots when the excess liquid drips into the soil.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. yɛ baai ni atsɛɔ amɛ stomata lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ho kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Do I need to mix liquid fertilizer with water before applying it to my crops?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ nu afutu nu dani mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Yes, liquid fertilizer comes in a strong concentrated form and must be diluted with clean water according to instructions so it does not scorch the plant leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baa yɛ gbɛ ni mli eyi obɔ nɔ, ni esa akɛ akɛ nu ni mli tse awo mli taakɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ koni akashã tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I put too much liquid fertilizer on them?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu ni mli tse babaoo fata he?

english: Applying too much fertilizer can burn the crop's leaves and damage root systems, causing the plants to wither or die instead of growing well.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ baai lɛ ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ loo egboɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What time of day is best to spray liquid fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because the hot afternoon sun can dry out the liquid too fast on the leaves, which reduces nutrient uptake and can cause leaf burn.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli Enɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ shwane mli hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa shi, ni ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã.

english: Will liquid fertilizer make my farm soil poor after harvest?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii kwraa yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, when used in correct amounts, liquid fertilizer nourishes the growing crop directly without harming soil microbes, though adding organic manure alongside it helps maintain long-term soil health.
ga: Dabi, kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ bɔ ni sa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni eyeee sũ mli nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ awui. Eyɛ mli akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli moŋ.

english: Is it safe to spray liquid fertilizer on food crops that my family will eat?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ niyenii tsei ni miweku lɛ yeɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, liquid fertilizers are safe for food crops as long as you follow recommended dosage rates and wait for the recommended period after spraying before harvesting.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛji akɛ onyiɛ bɔ ni esa akɛ okɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ ni omɛ be ni atsɔɔ akɛ okɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani okpa.

english: How can I get reliable advice or contact suppliers for genuine farm fertilizers in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná ŋaawoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ loo matswa mɔ ko ni kɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ baa yɛ Ghana lɛ abɔ?

english: You can reach out to local agricultural extension officers or registered farm input dealers through official helpline numbers to buy certified fertilizers and get proper guidance.
ga: Obaanyɛ oya okwaabuamɔ he nitsulɔ loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ jarayelɔ ni aŋmala egbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ nɔmba ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aŋmala he odaseyeli lɛ ni onine ashɛ ŋaawoo ni sa nɔ.

english: Yellow and curling leaves on young cocoa trees usually mean they are getting too much direct sunlight or not enough water. Cocoa seedlings need shade trees or plantains nearby to protect them from harsh sun while their root system develops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ he miihia tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛbu cocoa tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Healthy, fertile soil is usually dark in color, feels moist, crumbles easily in your hand, and contains earthworms or organic matter. If your soil is pale, hard, or dusty, adding compost or letting cut weeds decay on top will help feed it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Feeling moisturized Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ oookumɔ yɛ nine mli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli hu yɛ Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, ewa, loo sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo jwɛi ni afo lɛ ni oooshi koni amɛgbo yɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha lɛ niyenii.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a tiny fungus that grows quickly when the air around the tree is very damp, cold, and dark. Trimming excess branches lets in sunlight and air, which keeps the pods dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛ ŋmei bibioo ko mli. ni daa oya beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ duŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Is it fine for me to plant cassava right next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ masɛi?

english: It is better not to plant cassava too close to young cocoa because cassava roots spread aggressively and steal water and soil nutrients that the cocoa tree needs. Plantain or food legumes make much safer neighbor crops for cocoa.
ga: Esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛɔ kookoo bibii lɛ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa cacao tsei lɛ. Plantains loo legumes ji niyenii lɛ, ni no haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe kwraa kɛha kookoo.

english: Why should I cut off branches from a cocoa tree that looks green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting away unnecessary or low branches allows the tree to direct its energy into producing strong cocoa pods instead of feeding leaves. It also prevents branches from blocking sunlight and hiding pests.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ baai. Ehaa tsei niji hu tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ekɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teeɔ.

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is right at the start of the rainy season when the ground is moist. Moist soil helps the plant roots absorb nutrients safely without the fertilizer burning the roots in dry soil.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa tsei ashishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni shãa shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than can turn into pods, and they require tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen between flowers. Leaving fallen leaves on the farm floor creates a moist place for these helpful insects to live and pollinate your trees.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni abaanyɛ atsake amɛ afee ŋmeii. Ni kooloi bibii he miihia amɛ. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi ateŋ. Kɛ́ oshi baai ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa jɛmɛ feɔ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kɛha nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo otsei lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is burning weeds on my farm before planting harmful to my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani aduɔ lɛ yeɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the vital organic nutrients stored in topsoil and kills beneficial insects that keep the earth soft. Leaving cleared weeds to rot into the soil naturally fertilizes the ground and holds moisture.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. ni egbeɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni he tse lɛ fite yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ahi shi.

english: How can I keep my cocoa seedlings alive during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can protect young plants by placing a thick layer of dry leaves or straw around the base of each stem as mulch. This covers the dirt, stopping the hot sun and dry winds from evaporating moisture from the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu tsei bibii ahe kɛtsɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni mli tse ni oookɛwo shi lɛ nɔ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he. koni akɛ muji ato Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ naa koni amɛkajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: A cocoa pod is ready to harvest when its skin color changes completely from green or deep red to a bright yellow or orange-yellow. Harvesting only fully ripe pods ensures the beans inside have developed the right sugars needed for proper fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhewolo lɛ su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ-ŋɔli ni mli tse waa. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ enáa sugar ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni sa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu tso ko ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn and dry out under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects them from heat stress and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa becomes established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ jeɔ shishi ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa trees when they get too thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji komɛi beni edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning thick branches opens up the canopy so sunlight and air can circulate through the tree. This reduces dampness that causes black pod disease and encourages the tree to spend its energy producing pods instead of excess leaves.
ga: Niji ni mli tse ni afoɔ Enɛ baagbele ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee pod moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni fa fe nine baatsu nii.

english: What makes the pods on my cocoa tree turn black and dry up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads fast during heavy rainy seasons when humidity is high. Removing infected pods quickly and clearing weeds from around the base of the trees helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves and green color. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni esa akɛ tsei awo baai ni mli wa, ni eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I keep planting cassava on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting cassava repeatedly on the same land drains all the specific nutrients from the soil and allows cassava-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or peanuts restores nitrogen and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does putting dried grass around the roots of my crop plants help them handle hot weather?
ga: Hay ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkpeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that stops soil moisture from evaporating in the sun. It keeps the roots cool, prevents weeds from growing, and decomposes into rich plant food over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekafo kɛji hulu la lɛ shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsei niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough space and food to grow strong stalks and big harvests.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tso ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant in the ground fail to come up at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ekomɛi waaa lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to sprout if they are buried too deep for the shoot to reach sunlight, if the soil is too dry, or if insects eat them before they germinate. Planting seeds at the correct shallow depth in moist soil improves sprouting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔ ni hulu la nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Aloo kooloi bibii yeɔ amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ baaha shweremɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can suck it up from the ground. Plants wilt temporarily to conserve moisture, and watering early in the morning or late evening gives roots time to drink deeply.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Ni nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do flowers fall off my tomato plants without turning into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants face extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Consistent watering during hot dry spells and protecting plants from strong afternoon heat helps the blossoms set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ shwane mli latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ he lɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai yaa hiɛ.

english: What happens to the agrochemicals I spray when they fall onto my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni baa okwaayeli tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ kɛ́ amɛshɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: When you spray chemicals, part of the mixture falls to the ground and stays there as leftover traces called residues. These tiny amounts stay in the dirt long after the main spraying is done.
ga: Kɛji okɛ tsofai wo mli lɛ Nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ fã ko baagbee shikpɔŋ ni ehi jɛmɛ akɛ nɔ ko ni eshwɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ residue. Nɛkɛ nibii bibii nɛɛ baahi muji lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ beni agbe muji ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ titri lɛ naa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says a spray leaves 'residues' in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɛ akɛ spray ko shiɔ ‘nibii ni eshwɛ’ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: Residues are the small leftover traces of chemical concoctions that remain in your soil after you finish spraying your crops.
ga: Nɔ ni eshwɛ ji tsofai bibii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eshwɛɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ogbe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tsofa lɛ naa lɛ.

english: How fast do chemical sprays break down and leave my farm soil after application?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baafite oya ni amɛbaashi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya aha tɛŋŋ beni akɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Chemical sprays move and break down very slowly in the ground. They do not disappear immediately, meaning small traces stay in your soil for a long time.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe ni amɛfiteɔ blɛoo waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛlaajeŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, nibii bibii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it dangerous if I use more chemical spray on my crops than recommended?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ tsu nii fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛfee lɛ?

english: Using excessive amounts puts too much chemical into the soil. Over time, these high levels build up and can turn your soil toxic, damaging your crops and land.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tsofai awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ nibii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ nɛɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofa awo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Fitemɔ onibii kɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: If I keep using strong crop sprays every season, can my farmland become poisonous to crops?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ ni mli ewo muji tsu nii daa afi Ani miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee tsofa fɔŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, if you continuously apply heavy chemical mixtures, the residues build up until the soil becomes toxic, which can harm or destroy future crops you try to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni tsii tsu nii be fɛɛ be. Nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ baabua ehe naa kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee tsofa fɔŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aye wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni odu lɛ awui loo efite.

english: Can chemical spray used on one crop spread through the soil and harm other plants nearby?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso ko nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eye tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ awui?

english: Yes, excessive chemicals seep into the soil and slowly spread out. If the soil becomes toxic from chemical buildup, it affects all other crops growing in that same ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa fiofio. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ji tsofai fɔji kɛjɛ tsofai ni abua naa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaana tsei krokomɛi ni adu yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ hewalɛ

english: Why does my land seem to lose its productivity after many years of heavy chemical spraying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yibiiwoo miiho yɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwie nɔ afii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Continuous use of heavy chemicals causes traces to accumulate in the dirt over time. This excessive accumulation creates soil toxicity, making it hard for plants to grow healthily.
ga: Tsofai ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ haa muji buaa ehe naa yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɛkɛ nibii ni abua naa fe nine nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ muji. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛha tsei akɛ amɛaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can spraying my crops with strong chemical mixtures cause me to get sick later in the evening?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mli wa ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hela amɔ mi gbɛkɛ?

english: Yes, handling or inhaling strong chemical concoctions during application can cause health ailments that make you feel sick later in the day if you are exposed to excessive amounts.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni oootsu he nii loo okɛmu yɛ be mli ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha oná hela yɛ sɛɛ mli kɛji akɛ okɛtsu nii fe nine.

english: Why should I test a new chemical spray on a small portion of my farm before spraying everything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka tsofa hee ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ makwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko? Yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ nɔ

english: Doing a small trial lets you observe how the chemical behaves and how slowly it moves in your soil, helping you avoid over-dosing your entire farm with toxic amounts.
ga: small experiment Ehaa okwɛɔ bɔ ni tsofai feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa kɛ bɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli blɛoo. Ehaa otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ tsofai fɔji amli fe nine lɛ he.

english: Are imported farm chemicals safer for my soil than the ones mixed locally?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ fe tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Both local and imported chemical products leave residues in the soil, so both must be measured carefully to prevent excessive toxicity in your land.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ fɛɛ shiɔ nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ asusu enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ he jogbaŋŋ koni akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei fe nine yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy leaves. This often happens when heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where short roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai ni wa Enɛ fɔɔ baa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi kukuji nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs extra fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi awo mli dani adu?

english: If your previous crops were small, grew very slowly, or had pale leaves, your soil nutrients are depleted. You can also tell if weeds grow thin and weak, which shows the soil lacks the natural strength to feed your crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ faaa, edaa blɛoo waa, loo eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, no lɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baafite. Obaanyɛ ole hu kɛji jwɛi lɛ miidara ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of putting energy into making big fruits, they stretch upward quickly to try to outgrow neighboring plants for light.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ peeɔ yiblii nguahi. Amɛheɔ oya yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛtsɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛná la.

english: The mother plantain stem shares its food with every sucker attached to it. Leaving too many suckers starves the main plant, resulting in small, light plantain bunches.
ga: Plantain nyɛ lɛ tso lɛ kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni fata he lɛ jaa niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii babaoo shwie shi lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye tso titri lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantain tsei lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why is it bad for my soil to plant maize on the exact same land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ baadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Maize sucks out the exact same nutrients every season, leaving the soil tired. Changing crops, especially planting beans or groundnuts, puts nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi. bore shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Titri lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves dry up and turn brown during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that lose water very quickly under dry winds and intense sun. Plantains or shade trees act like natural umbrellas to shield cocoa leaves until they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya waa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting inside the ground during heavy rain periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water collects in the soil without draining away, root tubers cannot get oxygen. The trapped water smothers the cassava roots, causing underground rot.
ga: Beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Nu ni emɔ mli lɛ baakpã ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ, ni ebaaha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off before producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get extremely high or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. The heat damages the flower's pollen, making the plant reject the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Dɔlɛ fiteɔ pollen. haa tsei kpooɔ fɔfɔi

english: What is causing tiny caterpillars to eat holes inside the central leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. Moths lay eggs inside the young leaves, and when caterpillars hatch, they eat the tender growing center of the plant where it is softest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai bibii amli lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛyeɔ hei ni tsei ni miida lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than my main crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitso titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants natively built to survive tough conditions. Their seeds lie dormant in the soil and absorb water and fertilizer much faster than farm seeds, taking over the field if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni adebɔɔ bɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. ni ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ kɛji ajieee mra.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from directly under my mango trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mango tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds from under mango trees stops the weeds from stealing soil nutrients and water meant for the tree. It also removes hiding spots for insects and fungi that can spread diseases to the tree leaves and fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ o-mango tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ejieɔ hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛha kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ agbala hela kɛya baai kɛ aduawai anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my fruit trees fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Fruit flowers often drop early if the tree is stressed by lack of water, sudden pest attacks, or a shortage of essential plant nutrients during the flowering period.
ga: Yibii fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee oya kɛji nu ni bɛ lɛ ha tso lɛ miihao. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa amɛ trukaa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ bɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ

english: Will spraying chemical weedkillers near my crops hurt their growth?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ baafite amɛdalɛ?

english: Chemical weedkillers can stunt crop growth or burn leaves if the spray drifts onto your crop's green leaves or stems. Using a spray shield and applying chemicals on calm days keeps your crops safe.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa loo amɛshã baai kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shwie tso lɛ baai loo eshishifãi eŋɔli lɛ anɔ. Shield sprays ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbii ni yɔɔ toiŋjɔlɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: What is the best time of day to spray chemicals on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because temperatures are cooler and wind is light. This prevents the chemical from evaporating too quickly or blowing onto plants you didn't mean to spray.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsofa lɛ akafo oya tsɔ loo etswa kɛya tsei ni osusuuu akɛ obaashwie nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves get burned after I spray them with farm chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shãa beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf burn happens if the chemical mixture is mixed too strong, or if it is sprayed under direct, scorching afternoon sun, which heats up the liquid on the leaves and burns plant tissue.
ga: Baai lɛ ashãa baa kɛji tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ futu amɛhe waa tsɔ. Aloo shwie nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni eshãa tso lɛ fãji.

english: How does using a tractor to plow help my crops grow better than doing it by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ trakta ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ niji baatsu nii?

english: A tractor plows deeper into hard ground, loosening dense soil so plant roots can easily push down, breath air, and reach underground water during dry periods.
ga: Trakta shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa mli shɔŋŋ Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anyɛ shi oya, amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ, ni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Can driving heavy tractors too close to my crops damage their growth?
ga: Ani trakta ni tsii ni mikɛkudɔɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛdalɛ?

english: Yes, heavy tires pack the soil tightly around crops, which stops air and water from reaching roots and can snap shallow roots under the surface.
ga: Hɛɛ, rɔba ni tsii lɛ haa sũ ni ebɔle ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni ebaanyɛ efo shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: How far apart should I space my crop rows if I plan to use machines for weeding?
ga: Gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ maŋmɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ ateŋ kɛji mito gbɛjianɔ akɛ mikɛ tsɔne baatsu jwɛi ahe nii?

english: You should leave enough row space—usually at least 1 to 1.5 meters—so machine wheels and blades can pass easily without cutting crop stems or crushing roots.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ—bei pii lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, mitai 1 kɛyashi 1.5—koni tsɔne lɛ shwiili kɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo ni okɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo shishifãi lɛ akakumɔ.

english: Why do weeds always grow back faster than my planted crops after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally wild and hardy, lying dormant in the soil ready to burst open with the first rain, whereas farm crops take longer to germinate and establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wa, ni amɛkã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaatswa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Is it better to clear weeds using a hand cutlass or a motorized weeding machine?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ nine ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baakpa jwɛi?

english: Hand weeding with a cutlass is safer very close to crop stems to avoid accidental cuts, while motorized machines clear wide open field spaces much faster before weeds choke crop roots.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ okɛ nine baajie jwɛi lɛ kɛ tsɔne ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ koni akafo lɛ yɛ oshara mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsɔnei ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii lɛ jieɔ hei ni mli tse lɛ oya kwraa dani jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ tsei shishifãi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow before the corn is even ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani abele lɛ po feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient needed for green growth. It can also happen when heavy rains make the soil too wet, causing the roots to drown and fail to pick up nutrients from the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot during heavy rains because water stays trapped around them when soil drainage is poor. Standing water cuts off oxygen to the roots, creating conditions for fungus to grow and decay the crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli ejaakɛ nu ebɔle amɛhe. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shihilɛi baa ni ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ.

english: You should wait until the soil has received two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the ground. Planting too early after the very first light shower can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they face extreme heat or dry soil. High temperatures stop effective pollination, so the plant naturally sheds the unpollinated flowers to save its energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa pollination baa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, sunken spots on the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit as it grows. It usually happens when watering is irregular—switching quickly between dry soil and very wet soil—which stops the plant from moving calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa lɛ ni etsakeɔ oya lɛ nɔ Enɛ haaa tso lɛ ajie calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my yam tubers grow into twisted shapes instead of growing straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ etsake yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers bend and twist when they hit hard, stony, or tightly packed soil underground. Clearing rocks and building loose, tall soil mounds allows the tubers to expand smoothly downward.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa. tɛi loo shikpɔŋ shishi ni akɛwo mli Tɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ haa tuber lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo kɛyaa shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees take so long to fruit compared to my neighbor's trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantain trees take longer to fruit if too many suckers are allowed to grow around the main mother plant, as they all compete for nutrients. Pruning away excess suckers and keeping only two or three allows the main tree to put energy into fruiting quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baahe be babaoo dani amɛwo yibii kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ he, ejaakɛ amɛmiitao niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ahiɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ woɔ yibiiwoo mli oya.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around my young cocoa trees early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Cocoa tsei ni darako lolo ni amɛdarako No hewɔ lɛ ehe hia mi.

english: Weeds grow much faster than young cocoa trees and steal the water, sunlight, and nutrients your cocoa needs to get established. Clearing weeds regularly prevents young trees from being choked and reduces places where pests can hide.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe kookoo tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa okookoo lɛ koni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi daa lɛ, ebaatsi tsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe, ni ebaaha hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ahi amɛhe lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do caterpillars appear on my farm right after my young maize sprouts come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ je kpo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Moths lay their eggs on tender young maize leaves because soft green shoots provide easy food for newly hatched caterpillars, such as the fall armyworm. Checking leaves early helps you catch and manage them before they destroy the plant's growing center.
ga: Kplukai lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ ejaakɛ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee, tamɔ fall cutworms lɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni omɔ baai lɛ ni otsu he nii dani amɛfite tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to focus energy on leafy growth rather than flowers and pods. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen, so adding extra rich fertilizer often reduces your pod yield.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsina ŋmei kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa babaoo wo mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes my rice grains to break into small pieces when I take them to be milled?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ fãa bibii bibii kɛ́ atsɔ mli?

english: Rice grains break during milling mainly if they were harvested when too dry or dried too quickly in high heat, which creates tiny internal stress cracks before milling.
ga: Afoɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmãa lɛ. Enɛ baa mli titri kɛji akɛ akpa be mli ni edɔ tsɔ loo egbi oya tsɔ kɛ la ni mli edɔ waa. ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa Interior dani afee mfoniri

english: How can I check if the rice seed I bought is healthy and will germinate well before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ dani madu?

english: You can perform a simple water test by dropping seeds in a bucket of water; heavy, healthy seeds sink to the bottom, while hollow or diseased seeds float and can be scooped out.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka nu lɛ okwɛ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni oooshwie nu baagi mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni tsii ni mli wa lɛ baagbee shi kɛya shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni mli ewo muji loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baaho ni abaanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why does my rice crop grow tall and leafy but produce very few grain heads at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ daa ni ewoɔ baai shi ewoɔ dumɔwui ayitsei fioo ko pɛ kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: This usually happens when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which forces the rice plant to spend all its energy growing leaves rather than forming healthy grain heads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ nyɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ dumɔwu yihi nɛ a he wa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a survival trick where the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight to conserve internal water during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa yiwalaheremɔ ni tsei kɛbaa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛmli nu lɛ he yɛ gbi lɛ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cassava tubers rot under the ground when heavy rain falls for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive; saturated, waterlogged soil cuts off air to the roots and allows rotting fungi to spread rapidly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves during drought indicate that the plant is dropping older leaves to reduce water demand and save its remaining moisture for the core stem and roots.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miifɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni ekɛba nu he hiamɔ nii shi ni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛha tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization, which causes the plant to shed the useless flowers instead of forming fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa yɛ yibii ni ewoɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farmland help my next crop grow better without buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni midu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, leaving behind natural food for future crops.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni eshwɛ ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop right after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds are tough and lie dormant in dry soil, ready to sprout immediately with the first moisture, whereas crop seeds take longer to absorb water and wake up.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui wa ni amɛwɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ, amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛmɔɔ nu ni amɛteɔ shi.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt by noon even when I watered the surface soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: Light surface watering keeps roots near the top where heat dries them fast; deep watering forces roots to grow deep into the soil where moisture stays cooler for longer.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛi he ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ baaha amɛgbi oya lɛ. Nu ni awoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhe jɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a major plant nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. Adding manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps restore green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK fataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ daalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing lots of lush leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Cowpeas produce excessive leaves and few pods when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when they do not receive enough direct sunlight. Cowpeas naturally fix their own nitrogen, so extra nitrogen forces them to make leaves instead of flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpeas woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ faaa. Cowpeas kɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen lɛ toɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ nyɛɔ enɔ koni ekɛ baai awo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed small pods (a process called cherelle wilt) when they do not have enough water, nutrients, or sunlight to support all the pods. It is the tree's way of saving energy for the remaining fruit.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii (nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cacao cherry hela) yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ amɛbɛ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii muu lɛ fɛɛ. Eji tso lɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my oil palm leaves develop yellowing and brown spots during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palms react to water stress and potassium deficiency during dry spells by yellowing and developing brown spots on older fronds. Mulching around the base retains soil moisture, and applying potassium fertilizer helps prevent this stress.
ga: Mu tso lɛ tsuɔ nu he haomɔ kɛ potassium ni faaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ he nii. Ehaa baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa baai ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ. Mulching ni akɛwo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni potassium ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: How does heavy rainfall during the flowering stage affect my maize crop?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ saa ŋmãa he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain during flowering can wash pollen off the male tassels before it reaches the female silks on the cob. Without pollen reaching the silks, the cobs will have many missing kernels.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ ahe dani eyashɛ siliki ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe. Kɛji pollen ko bɛ ni shɛɔ siliki lɛ he lɛ Cob lɛ baaná dumɔwui babaoo ni elaaje.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but no tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi tomato ko bɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers without forming fruit if temperatures get too high, if pollinating insects are missing, or if excessive nitrogen fertilizer was applied. Keeping the soil cool with mulch and reducing nitrogen helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato baafɔ̃ ni ewooo yibii kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Pollinators lɛ laajeɔ loo kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen fertilizer babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nitrogen ni abaaba shi lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Plantain suckers require heavy soil moisture, full sunlight, and rich organic soil to grow quickly. If planted during dry periods or in deep shade without regular weeding, their growth slows down significantly.
ga: Seedlings need high soil moisture. hulu la ni eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ oya. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni jwɛi shwieee shi daa lɛ, Dalɛ baa shi waa.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You will see the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant will begin to crack open as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmei lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ baabɔi gbee be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting while in the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ be mli ni miyɔɔ shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from dormancy and sprout when warmth and humidity rise, signaling that a new growing season is approaching. Storing yams in a cool, well-ventilated barn on raised racks delays early sprouting.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baate shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i yaa hiɛ lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be hee miiba. Atomo ni akɛtoɔ tsũ ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli yɛ adekai ni awó nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha ekwɛ̃ mra.

english: Why are my pepper plants suddenly wilting and drying up even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by root rot or soil-borne bacterial wilt that blocks water from moving up the stem. Uprooting and destroying infected plants and rotating crops helps prevent it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo helai ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekaya tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni akpãtãa amɛhiɛ kɛ tsei ni atsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: If my household is running out of food, which crop can I plant that will give us something to harvest in the shortest time?
ga: Kɛji niyenii bɛ mishia lɛ Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu ni baaha wɔkpa nii yɛ be kukuoo mli?

english: Sweet potatoes and short-duration maize varieties are fast options. Orange-fleshed sweet potatoes can be harvested in just 3 to 4 months, providing quick energy and essential nutrients for your family when food supply is low.
ga: Atomɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ ji gbɛi krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii oya. Abaanyɛ akpa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli, ni enɛ haa oweku lɛ hewalɛ oya kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛ́ niyenii bɛ.

english: Why do my neighbors leave their cassava roots in the ground for months without harvesting them all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ shiɔ ŋmei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ mli nyɔji babaoo ni ekpaaa amɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Cassava roots act like natural underground storage. Unlike maize or tomatoes, cassava roots stay alive and fresh in the soil for up to two years until you dig them up, making it a reliable crop to protect your family against sudden food shortages.
ga: Cassava shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ ŋmãa loo tomato lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaafee ehee kɛyashi afii enyɔ kɛyashi obaatsa amɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ tso ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni baabu oweku lɛ he kɛjɛ niyenii ni faaa trukaa lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up into tight tubes when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the maize plant's way of protecting itself from drying out. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, which stops water from evaporating too quickly from its body.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni ŋmãa tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa nu akajɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: My tomato plants have plenty of leaves and flowers, but the yellow flowers keep falling off without turning into tomatoes. Why is this happening?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ gbee shi ni etsɔko tomato. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high or when the plant lacks water. Heat stress causes the plant to shed its flowers to save water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu. Dɔlɛ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas together in the same field with my maize crop?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting cowpea with maize is very beneficial. Legumes like cowpea take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the maize plants and keeps the soil healthy without buying expensive extra fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ náa niyenii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe ŋmãa kroko ni jara wa.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil food. Because weeds grow faster and stronger, they steal the nutrients meant for your crops, leaving your crops starved and small.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛbaafee bibii.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make food for the large tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight and prevents the leaves from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ

english: Why does my harvested dried maize turn into powder and dust after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikpa lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by small insects called maize weevils that burrow inside the dried corn kernels to feed and lay eggs. The growing larvae eat the inside of the corn, leaving behind hollow husks and white dust.
ga: Kooloi bibii kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei ŋmei. ni shwieɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli koni amɛtao niyenii ni amɛwo ŋmeii Larvae ni miida lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kpoji ni mli ewo muji kɛ sũ yɛŋ pɛ eshwɛ.

english: What does it actually mean when people call cocoa a 'cash crop' in Ghana?
ga: Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, kɛ́ mɛi tsɛ kookoo akɛ Mɛni ji ‘shika ŋmɔshi nibii’ tsɔɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: A cash crop is a crop you grow mainly to sell on the market for income rather than for direct consumption by your family at home.
ga: Shika ŋmɔshi nibii ji tsei ni oduɔ titri koni okɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ koni onine ashɛ shika nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a duɔ konɛ weku ɔ nɛ ye ní tɛ̃ɛ ngɛ we mi.

english: Can I grow a cash crop like cocoa together with food crops like plantain or cassava on the same plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo kɛfata niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantain loo cassava he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop them while the cocoa is young because food crops provide shade for the young cocoa trees while giving you food and early income before the cocoa matures.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu tsei yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ be mli ni kookoo lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii tsei lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa niyenii kɛ shika mra dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How do I know if my land has good soil for starting a crop farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni manyɛ maje ŋmɔ shishi?

english: Good soil is usually dark in color, crumbly to the touch, drains water well without turning into a swamp, and contains lots of decayed plant leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ kɛji akɛ ata he lɛ Efoɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋshɔ. ni tsei ahe baai ni egboi babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ

english: What happens to my plants if I pack them too close together when planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants that yield very little crop.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to intense direct heat; they need shade trees to protect their leaves from burning and keep the soil moist while their roots grow.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ koni baai lɛ akashã, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so much better during the major rainy season compared to the Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛ akɛto harmattan he lɛ?

english: Rainwater dissolves nutrients in the soil so roots can absorb them easily, whereas the dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of leaves and forces plants to slow down growth to survive.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ oya, yɛ be mli ni harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting cocoa before I can start harvesting pods?
ga: Kɛ́ odu kookoo lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani obɔi ŋmeii lɛ ŋmɔmɔ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing pods in about two to three years, whereas older traditional varieties take four to five years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover, and it builds up pests that prefer that crop.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. ni ebaafee tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is waterlogged and choking the plant's roots.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my crops when they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will quickly steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your crops need to survive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food found in soil. Rain often washes nitrogen out of the earth, so adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps restore the green color and boost crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ sũ mli Nugbɔ sumɔɔ ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ afɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry leaves and grass around the base of my crops help them during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ ashishi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that blocks the direct heat of the sun, keeping water in the soil much longer and preventing the dirt from baking hard.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ muji naa koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my maize yield better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cowpea ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-ŋmãa lɛ yibiiwoo?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. When grown alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil, providing free nutrients that help the maize grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaaye nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛhaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full, direct sunlight. They need living shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to shelter their soft leaves until their roots grow strong enough to withstand the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni akɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ aaawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to grow up tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam plants make large tubers by capturing sunlight through their leaves. Staking lifts the vines high into the air so all leaves catch maximum sunlight and stay off the damp ground where weeds and soil diseases can damage them.
ga: Sweet potato tsei feɔ bulbs agboi kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛnaa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa aná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni jwɛi kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil gets too dry. When a tomato plant feels heat stress, it drops its blossoms to conserve energy rather than trying to feed growing tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Beni Tomato Tsei lɛ Nuɔ Dɔlɛ He Haomɔ He Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha tomato ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays soaked in excess water for long periods, especially during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu ni fa fe nine mli be kakadaŋŋ. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking sap from under the leaves. Spraying the underside of the leaves early with neem oil or insecticidal soap gets rid of these pests so normal leaf growth can resume.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. Koni ebaaha baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my cabbage leaves suddenly filled with small holes like someone shot them with pellets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii trukaa lɛ? It's like someone shot it with a pellet?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are caused by small caterpillars, such as the larvae of the diamondback moth, eating the leaves at night. Checking leaves early and spraying natural remedies like neem water stops caterpillars before they ruin the cabbage head.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ diamondback moth larvae, ni yeɔ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ. Baai lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko tamɔ neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa dani amɛbaafite kaabe yitsei lɛ.

english: The first rain of the season can be deceiving because the soil deep below is often still hot and dry. If hot, dry weather returns right after, newly sprouted seeds will wither and die; waiting until rains become frequent ensures steady moisture for young roots.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni egbi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ shii abɔ koni eye ebua shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ daa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or is getting too much water. Nitrogen helps plants make green leaves and food, so adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer can help bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai kɛ niyenii eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant juices, or by a virus spread by those pests. Clearing weeds around your plot and controlling pests early keeps the leaves healthy and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ mra Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli waa ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it important to leave space between my crops instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, ground water, and soil food without fighting its neighbors. It also lets air flow through the farm, which stops diseases from spreading quickly between crowded leaves.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa oya yɛ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to start planting my crops after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the main rainy season has truly set in and the soil has received two or three deep, heavy rains. Planting after just one light rainfall can cause your seeds to germinate and then die when the sun returns.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni naa wa aaafee shii 2-3. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛ́ hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat gets too high, when the soil dries out completely, or if the soil lacks key nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil evenly moist and covered with dry grass mulch helps the plant keep its blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ daa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: What makes my cocoa trees produce fewer pods as they get older?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older, their branches often become dense and overgrown, blocking sunlight from reaching the inner branches where flowers form. Pruning dead or overcrowded branches lets sunlight in to trigger fresh flower and pod growth.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ Bei pii lɛ, amɛniji lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdara fe nine, ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ niji lɛ amli he ni fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ lɛ. Niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni aaafolɔ mli lɛ baaha hulu la abote mli koni ewo fɔfɔi heei kɛ ŋmeii ahe hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots need loose soil to swell up big. If the ground is packed too hard, or if the cuttings were planted too close together, the roots cannot push through the dirt or get enough nutrients to expand.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfuu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo amɛnáaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why are some of my yam tubers rotting inside the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot under the soil mainly due to standing water from poor drainage or attacks by soil pests like beetles and worms. Planting on high earthen mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, titri lɛ yɛ nu ni ekã shi yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ hewɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my farm soil turn very hard and crack during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens and cracks when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves, straw, or manure. Adding compost or dry leaf mulch holds moisture in the ground and keeps the soil soft even under strong sun.
