ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi, jwɛi, loo ŋmeii bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ, ni ehaa efeɔ blɛoo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa po mli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a long time to start growing after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers take long to sprout if the planting material was damaged by pests like stem borers or if there is not enough moisture in the soil. Cleaning the base of the sucker before planting and watering well gives it a fast start.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem borers lɛ efite nibii ni aduɔ lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Susu lɛ shishi ni aaatsumɔ dani adu ni awo mli nu jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ajeɔ shishi oya.

english: Why does my heap of plant waste and manure get so hot inside after a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei kɛ ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ mli woɔ la waa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli lɛ?

english: When you stack crop waste together, tiny invisible organisms start eating and breaking down the materials. This activity generates natural heat inside the pile, which is a healthy sign that your compost is decomposing properly.
ga: Kɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ to nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ahe lɛ Nibii ni anaaa lɛ baabɔi nakai nibii lɛ yeli ni amɛfite. Nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ baa ŋtayaa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji okadi kpakpa ni tsɔɔ akɛ o-compost lɛ efite jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why must I leave my compost heap untouched for three days before turning or adding water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha mi-compost pile lɛ ahi shi gbii etɛ dani matsɔ mli loo mikɛ nu awo mli lɛ?

english: Leaving the pile untouched for about three days allows heat and moisture to build up to a high level. This high heat kills weed seeds and disease-causing germs in the waste so you get clean, safe manure for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋtayaa lɛ aaafee gbii etɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ he lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo aba. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa nɛɛ gbeɔ jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ helai ni kɛ helai baa ni yɔɔ jwɛi lɛ mli lɛ. Koni eha bo ŋmɔshi nibii ni he tse ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What should I do if my organic manure pile becomes too hot and dry inside?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi yɛ emli?

english: You should open up the pile and mix in fresh water. Adding water brings down the excess heat and restores the moisture balance that beneficial organisms need to continue breaking down the plant material.
ga: Esa akɛ agbele ŋtayaa lɛ mli ni akɛ nu kpakpa afutu mli. Nu ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ koni amɛgbala tsei amli nibii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farm waste mixture has enough air inside it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ mli?

english: If the mixture smells sour or feels overly soggy without producing heat, it lacks air. Turning the pile and adjusting the water level lets fresh air in, bringing it to the right consistency for healthy decay.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ loo enuɔ he akɛ edɔ tsɔ ni dɔlɛ bɛ mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ otsake ŋtayaa lɛ ni otsake nu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba. Ehaa nɔ ni sa kɛha fitemɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why does my compost pile need both air and water at the same time to rot well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu fɛɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: The tiny organisms breaking down your plant waste need water to stay alive and air to breathe. If there is too much water, air gets blocked, but having the right balance of both turns waste into rich plant food faster.
ga: nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli Otso lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ he miihia nu koni ehi shi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ekɛmu. Kɛji nu fa babaoo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatsi. Shi kɛ́ mɔ ko ná nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi feɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa oya.

english: Why do I need to keep fresh cocoa beans covered in a heap for three days before opening them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii heei toɔ ŋtayaa mli gbii etɛ dani migbeleɔ lɛ?

english: Keeping the beans covered for the first three days traps the necessary heat and moisture inside. This initial hot phase is essential to start fermenting the beans so they develop good flavor and high quality.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ ha klɛŋklɛŋ gbii etɛ lɛ, ebaaha dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa waa lɛ ahi mli. Nɛkɛ shishijee hulutsoo gbɛ nɛɛ he hiaa koni aje ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi koni amɛná ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa kɛ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I cool down fermented crop materials if they stay hot for too long?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee tsei ni afee amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛ̃i kɛji amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: You can lower the temperature by spreading out the material and stirring in clean water. Opening up the mass lets hot air escape while fresh water brings the heat down to a safe level.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha hulutsoo lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ nibii ni okɛbaagbɛ ashwã ni okɛfutu nu ni mli tse mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ agbele mass lɛ naa lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu kpakpa haa dɔlɛ baa shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Can high heat inside my soil bed damage young plant roots?
ga: Ani dɔlɛ ni fe nine ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi?

english: Yes, extreme underground heat can burn sensitive young crop roots and dry them out. You can protect your seedlings by adding water and mulching to keep the soil moist and cool.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni eha tsei bibii ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi. Obaanyɛ obu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ nu kɛ mulching ni okɛbaafata he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my nursery soil mix has reached the right texture for planting seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni akɛfutuɔ nii yɛ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui akwɛmɔ?

english: Your soil mix has the right consistency when it feels damp like a wrung-out sponge—not dripping wet and not powdery dry—showing it has the right balance of air space, moisture, and temperature.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛfutu lɛ yɛ bɔ ni sa kɛji enu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ sponji ni ajie kɛjɛ mli. Ejeee ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɛɛ ni etsɔ powda. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ latsaa ni sa.

english: Why is it important to mix fresh water into hot decaying soil matter before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ nu kpakpa futuɔ sũ ni mli edɔ ni egbo dani aduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Adding fresh water cools down the intense heat created during plant decay and mixes moisture evenly, ensuring the ground is safe and gentle enough for new seeds to sprout without burning.
ga: Nu kpakpa ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ mli baa yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afutu mli pɛpɛɛpɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee shweshweeshwe ni efee blɛoo bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui heei akwɛ̃ ni shãaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees burn and turn yellow after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: When fertilizer inputs are too strong or applied too close to the stem, they draw moisture out of the roots instead of feeding the tree. Young or sensitive trees need milder doses spread around the dripline of the tree.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli waa tsɔ loo ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi tsɔ Egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha tso lɛ niyenii. Tsei bibii loo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he miihia ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã he fɛɛ he. tso mli nu ni shwieɔ shi

english: What will happen if I give my young cocoa trees the same amount of input chemical as my mature trees?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ miha cacao tsei bibii lɛ tsofai ni tamɔ cacao tsei ni eda lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate roots and leaves that cannot handle high chemical doses. Strong inputs meant for mature trees will stunt the growth of young plants or kill them completely.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ tsofai babaoo. Saji ni mli wa ni kɔɔ tsei ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ baatsi tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ naa loo ebaakpãtã amɛhiɛ kwraa.

english: Why do pests keep destroying my cocoa pods even after I spray my farm with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yaa nɔ efiteɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: If chemicals are too strong or used continuously without variation, pests can build up resistance. Applying sprays at the wrong time of the day or during heavy rain also washes the input away before it can work.
ga: Kɛji tsofai lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo akɛtsu nii be fɛɛ be ni tsakemɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ama shi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsu nii yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni esaaa mli loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ hu baanyɛ aha nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ afite dani enyɛ etsu nii.

english: Why am I harvesting fewer cocoa pods this year even though I used the same amount of inputs as last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpa kookoo ŋmeii fioo pɛ afi nɛɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nibii ni afee yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii moŋ.

english: Soil loses its natural nutrients over consecutive seasons, and rainfall patterns change. As trees grow older, their nutrient needs increase, meaning the input amount that worked two years ago may no longer be enough for current soil conditions.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ bei lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ hu etsake. Kɛ tso lɛ da lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ niyenii mli nibii ni tsu nii afii enyɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ faaa dɔŋŋ kɛha ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shihilɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the branches instead of turning into pods during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ niji anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience heat stress or lack of water to protect themselves. The tree conserves its energy and moisture to keep the main plant alive rather than producing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Tsei buɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he koni tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahi shi moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do some cocoa trees on my farm produce large pods while others right next to them stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ekomɛi ji bibii lɛ?

english: Trees experience uneven competition for soil nutrients, shade, and root space. Some spots in the farm retain water better or receive better shade, allowing those specific trees to respond better to added inputs.
ga: Tsei kɛ akaŋshii ni ejaaa kpeɔ kɛha sũ mli niyenii, shade kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ. He komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ loo amɛbaaná hulutsoo kpakpa. Enɛ haa tsei pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ tsuɔ nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Excessive sunlight causes young cocoa leaves to curl, dry up, and turn brown around the edges. Cocoa seedlings need plantains or shade trees above them to shield their soft leaves from direct heat.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo lɛ haa kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛnaagbɛ. Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ he miihia tso bibioo loo tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to trim off the extra branches and shoots growing at the base of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei niji kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients that the main trunk needs. Removing them allows the fertilizer and inputs you apply to go directly into producing big, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ tsũi lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso titri lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ feɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa tree turning pale green instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale green leaves usually mean the tree lacks key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. It shows the tree is struggling to make food and needs balanced soil nourishment to regain its health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni efee niyenii, ni ehe miihia ni shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa aha lɛ koni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can rainy weather affect how strong chemical sprays work on my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ baaná tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, heavy rain shortly after spraying washes the inputs off the leaves and into the soil before the tree or pest can absorb them, making the treatment ineffective and wasting your efforts.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa beni afɔseɔ tsofa lɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ hoɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa tsofafeemɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ.

english: How do I know if the soil on a new piece of land is fertile enough for my crops to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni miŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fertile soil is usually dark brown or black, soft to dig, and retains moisture well without waterlogging. If wild plants and trees are growing densely and green on the uncultivated land, it is a strong natural signal that crops will grow abundantly there.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛji atsa, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli. Kɛji koo mli tsei kɛ tsei kwɛ̃ babaoo ni amɛfee eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu nɔ nii nɔ lɛ nɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baakwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do crops yield much better in plains areas like the Afram Plains compared to rocky or hilly lands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ Afram shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto hei ni tɛi loo gɔji yɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plains and valley lands tend to collect topsoil, organic matter, and moisture washed down from surrounding areas over time. This creates deep, rich soil that lets crop roots spread easily and access constant nutrients.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi kɛ jɔɔ lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii ni haa tsei shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai daa.

english: What causes crops on some farms to grow huge and green while the same crops on a nearby farm look small and weak?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji komɛi amli lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ nɔŋŋ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa?

english: Crops grow abundantly when the soil has a rich supply of organic nutrients and can hold water during hot days. Even on neighboring farms, differences in past soil use, organic matter, and water drainage can cause huge differences in crop growth.
ga: Tsei daa babaoo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli, ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ po amli Yinɔsane mli srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ hu baanyɛ aha srɔtofeemɔi wuji aba tsei adalɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and produce very small ears even when I clear the weeds regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyɛ toi bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ mishwieɔ jwɛi daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeding removes competition, but crops also need nutrients like nitrogen from the soil to grow strong and green. If the soil lacks natural organic matter or nutrients, the crops will stay stunted despite weed clearance.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛyaa. Shi tsei hu he hia niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee eŋɔli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ sɛɛ po.

english: Why are many crop farmers moving to the Volta Region to set up their farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsulɔi babaoo miifã kɛmiiya Volta kpokpaa lɛ nɔ koni amɛyato amɛŋmɔji lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ lɛ?

english: The Volta Region has reliable rainfall patterns, abundant water sources, and deep, fertile soil. These natural conditions allow farmers to harvest heavy yields of staples like yam, cassava, and maize with less spent on inputs.
ga: Volta kpokpaa lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Nu jɛɛhei babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛi nɛɛ haa okwaafoi nyɛɔ amɛkpaa ŋmɔshi nibii wuji tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛyeɔ be fioo yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Is it true that certain regions in Ghana allow you to farm continuously without the land getting exhausted quickly?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ kpokpai komɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ŋmɛɔ bo gbɛ ni oya nɔ otsuɔ okwaayeli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ efooo oya?

english: Some river basins and plains have deep topsoil that holds higher reserves of natural nutrients. However, every soil eventually loses its strength if farmed continuously without adding manure, compost, or letting the land fallow.
ga: Faai kɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo hiɔ shi. Shi kɛlɛ, yɛ naagbee lɛ, shikpɔji fɛɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli kɛji akɛ aya nɔ atsu he nii ni ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ashi amɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli.

english: How can I make enough yield from my farm to both feed my family and pay my children's school fees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni manyɛ makwɛ miweku lɛ ni mawo mibii lɛ askulyaa he nyɔmɔ?

english: To get a high yield for home use and market sales, combine good land selection with high-yielding seed varieties, correct crop spacing, and soil fertility management using animal manure or compost.
ga: Koni aná nyɔmɔwoo babaoo kɛha shia nitsumɔ kɛ jarayeli yɛ jara nɔ. Okɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni ahala lɛ afata dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ahe. jajemɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ kɛtsɔ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my soil produce fewer food crops now than when I first cleared the virgin land five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miiwo niyenii fioo fe beni mijie shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tseee lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: When virgin land is cleared, it has years of built-up leaf litter and nutrients. Every harvest takes nutrients away from the soil, so without replacing them through fallowing or fertilizers, the land gradually loses its power to produce heavy crops.
ga: Kɛji ajie shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai amli jwɛi kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baabua naa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ bɛ najiaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite fiofio Hewalɛ ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster right after the first heavy rains of the season start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rainwater carries dissolved atmospheric nitrogen and thoroughly cools the warm soil, activating beneficial microbes that release locked nutrients directly to the crop roots for rapid growth.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ekanyaa nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni jieɔ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara oya lɛ.

english: What happens to my root crops like cassava and yam if rainwater sits on the farm field for too many days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-tubers tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔ? Kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ hi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents air from reaching the roots, causing the underground tubers to rot and the leaves to turn yellow and drop due to suffocation.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ. ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔlɔ hewɔ.

english: Why do I need to cover my harvested yams with grass or dry weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni egbi haa mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are very sensitive to heat and sun after harvest. Covering them with dry weeds or straw acts as a sunshade that keeps the tubers cool, stops them from getting scorched, and prevents quick spoilage.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la he waa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi ha oyitso he lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni oyitso mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ yitso lɛ naa koni ekashã. ni atsĩ nɔ ni fiteɔ oya lɛ naa

english: What happens to my yams if I leave them lying under the open sun after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potato lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni mifo amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Direct sunshine cooks the surface of the yam tuber, causing it to lose water quickly, soften, and rot within a few days before you can sell or eat it.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ shwereɔ. Nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amɛ oya, amɛfeɔ blɛoo, ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ dani obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ loo oye amɛ.

english: Why should I put weeds or straw inside the transport truck when moving my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi awo tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ mli kɛ́ mikɛ sweet potatoes miifã gbɛ?

english: Weeds and straw act as a soft cushion to prevent the heavy yams from bruising each other on rough roads, while also shielding the top layer from hot sunlight during transport.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kushɛnii ni yɔɔ blɛoo koni ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ akatswa yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ edɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he beni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Can I use dry crop straw like rice or corn stalks if I don't have dry weeds to cover my yams?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsei atsu nii kɛji mibɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni haa ŋmãa lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, dry rice straw or corn stalks work just as well as dried weeds. The main goal is to use clean, dry plant materials to shade the yams from direct sunlight and heat.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmãa ŋmeii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ nakai nɔŋŋ. kɛ jwɛi ni egbi Otii titri ni ma ehiɛ ji ni ekɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he tse ni egbi atsu nii ni ekɛbu ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How does covering my harvested yams with grass keep them heavier for market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛhaa mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpaa lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛha jarayeli?

english: The layer of grass keeps wind and sun from drying out the tuber. By locking in moisture, your yams retain their weight and stay fresh and firm for buyers.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la akagbi bulb lɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ooohiɛ mli lɛ nɔ O-sweet potatoes lɛ baaye abua ni ehiɛ amɛhe ni ehi shi ehee ni ehi shi shiŋŋ kɛha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ.

english: Is it better to burn all cleared weeds or keep them on my yam farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaashã jwɛi ni ajie lɛ fɛɛ loo akɛ amɛ ahi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is better to keep cleared weeds to use as protective mulch. Throwing away or burning all weeds leaves your farm soil and harvested crops exposed to intense sun damage.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni he tse ato koni akɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni buɔ mɔ he. Jwɛi fɛɛ ni oooshɛrɛ loo oshã lɛ baaha hulu lɛ afite oŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ waa.

english: Why should I put a layer of dry weeds over my planted yam mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ jwɛi ni egbi lɛ awo nɔ? Yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni adu lɛ nɔ

english: Covering yam mounds with dried weeds keeps the soil moist, reduces heat on hot days, and protects delicate young yam shoots from burning when they first emerge.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha sweet potatoes ni ato lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ la yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ ni obu sweet potato tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã beni amɛkwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ.

english: Will covering my harvested yams with dry weeds attract pests or diseases?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaagbala tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai?

english: As long as you use dry, clean weeds free from rot or active pest infestations, the weeds will simply act as a safe shade layer without harming your tubers.
ga: Shii abɔ ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni ehe tse, ni ŋmɔtɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii. Jwɛi lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni eyeee oyitso awui.

english: How do I know if the weeds I cleared are dry enough to cover my yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ jwɛi ni migbeɔ lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ anɔ?

english: The weeds should be wilted or fully dried in the sun so they do not trap excessive moisture or heat against the yam, which could encourage fungal rot.
ga: Esa akɛ jwɛi lɛ agbo loo amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli bɔni afee ni sweet potato lɛ akahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo dɔlɛ babaoo. Enɛ baanyɛ awo fungal rot he hewalɛ.

english: Why do experienced yam farmers refuse to harvest yams without having straw nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Experienced farmers know that a yam uncovered even for a few hours in intense heat begins to spoil, so they always prepare straw or weeds ahead of time to cover yams immediately upon digging.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ le akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi pɛ ewo la ni naa wa mli po lɛ, ejeɔ shishi efiteɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛsaa jwɛi loo jwɛi kɛtsɔ hiɛ koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛji atsa amɛ pɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in a clear, open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight because their leaves burn easily and lose too much water. They need shade crops like plantain or forest trees above them during their first few years to protect them from the harsh sun while they build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni nu babaoo hu sɛɛ foɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ amɛyiteŋ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why does cocoa grow better in forest areas like the Western and Ahafo regions than in dry northern regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kooi yɔɔ tamɔ Anaigbɛ kɛ Ahafo kpokpai lɛ anɔ fe hei ni hulu enyɔ shi yɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need consistent rainfall, high humidity, and deep, fertile forest soil to grow properly. Drier regions lack the steady rainfall and soil moisture that cocoa trees require to keep their leaves green and produce heavy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei taoɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, hulutsoo babaoo, kɛ koo mli shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni cacao tsei he hiaa koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: How many years must I wait after planting hybrid cocoa before I can start harvesting pods?
ga: Kɛ́ odu cocoa hybrids lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani obɔi ŋmeii lɛ akpamɔ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start flowering and producing pods within 2 to 3 years if properly cared for, compared to older traditional varieties that take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ enɛ toɔ blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ ahe.

english: What are those quick-growing shoots coming out of the lower trunk of my cocoa tree, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii ni daa oya ni jɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli kɛbaa lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ mihe?

english: Those shoots are called suckers or 'chupons.' You should cut them off because they steal food, water, and energy from the main tree without giving you good pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo ‘chupons’ ni esa akɛ ofolɔ amɛ akɛni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni amɛhaaa bo ŋmeii kpakpa ko lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to allow my cocoa tree canopy to become too thick and dark?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mahã mi-kokoo tso lɛ shishi tsɔne lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee duŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: A canopy that is too thick traps moisture and blocks sunlight and air, creating a wet environment where fungal diseases thrive. Trimming excess branches lets air flow and sunlight reach the trunk, which keeps the tree healthy.
ga: Kpoji ni mli tse tsɔ lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaatsi hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli waa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa tree turn yellow even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the tree is lacking nutrients like nitrogen or potassium in the soil, or that the soil is waterlogged and drowning the roots. Adding compost or the right fertilizer usually helps restore the dark green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ miiho. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do many tiny green cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they reach full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ Mɛi babaoo feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshɛɔ amɛdalɛ he.

english: This is a natural process called 'cherelle wilt.' The cocoa tree voluntarily sacrifices some of its young pods when it realizes it does not have enough water or nutrients to grow every single pod to maturity.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ni ale lɛ akɛ 'cherelle wilt'. Cacao tso lɛ jɛɔ etsui mli ekɛ eshishifãi bibii lɛ ekomɛi haa. Beni ana akɛ kookoo tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛyashi amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn completely black and rot on the tree during rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads rapidly when water drops splash soil particles onto pods during heavy rains.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nu mli ŋmeii shwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do flowers fall off my cocoa tree trunk without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei amli ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction get pollinated by tiny insects called midges. Unpollinated flowers naturally drop off the trunk within a day or two.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kplukai bibii pɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ lɛ pollin. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pick a cocoa pod from the trunk?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their outer skin changes color completely—usually from green to bright yellow, or from red to orange-yellow—and makes a hollow sound when gently tapped.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ lɛ tsakeɔ su kwraa—bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. loo kɛjɛ tsuru mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei—ni efeɔ gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛji akɛ ata he fioo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves in maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. The maize plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves, which is a sign that the crop needs nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines naturally search for sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers. Raising the leaves on stakes catches maximum sunlight and keeps the foliage off damp soil, preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei taoɔ hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha bulb agbo ni daa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ, ni ebaaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Koni akɛtsi baa helai ni ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do small shoots keep growing around the root of my main plantain tree, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ɔ ebɔleɔ Mi-plantain titri lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe Ni ani esa akɛ mafo lɛ?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers, and they steal food and water from the main plantain tree. You should cut down all extra suckers except one strong shoot that will take over after you harvest the main tree.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ akɛ suckers. Ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli. Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ fɛɛ. Ja tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baaye egbɛhe beni okpa tso titri lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly upward and turning light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe kɛtee ŋwɛi ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny whitefly insects transmitting the Tomato Leaf Curl Virus. It can also happen when the plant tries to protect itself from losing water during extreme heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ Tomato Leaf Curl Hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ tsei bɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ he.

english: Why are the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off before turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off easily when the tree experiences stress from extended dry weather, lack of protective shade trees, or damage from insects like mirids (capsids) that attack young flower stalks.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ mli baa lɛ kpe. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo nɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni tutuaa fɔfɔii bibii lɛ ahe lɛ fiteɔ lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers drop off during dry spells even if I water the soil occasionally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli moŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when the air temperature is extremely hot and dry. Even if the roots have water, high heat prevents pollen from fertilizing the flowers, causing the plant to drop them to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu moŋ Shi la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ pollen lɛ naa koni ekawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔ. Ha tsei agbo koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does my lowland rice crop grow better when standing in shallow water than in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-flat rice lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli fe shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland rice plants have special roots designed to thrive in water-covered ground. The shallow water smothers weeds that compete for sunlight and helps the soil release nutrients that rice needs to grow fast.
ga: Omɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni afee koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ jwɛi ni kɛ hulu la miitswa akaŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda oya lɛ kpo.

english: Cassava plants show they are mature when lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stalk, and the ground around the base of the plant starts to swell and crack open.
ga: Cassava tso tsɔɔ akɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ shishi tsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni eshwɛ kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni ejaraa.

english: Why is my young oil palm tree producing small black fruit bunches that rot before turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso bibioo lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii lɛ? Ani ediŋŋ ni fiteɔ dani etsɔɔ etsuru?

english: Very young oil palm trees often produce unpollinated female fruit bunches during their first flowering season. As the tree grows older and pollinating insects establish in your field, the bunches will stay healthy and ripen to a reddish-orange color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei ni darako waa lɛ woɔ yei aduawai ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli. Beni tsei lɛ daraa ni ŋmeii babaoo ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, Tsei lɛ aniji lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ-tsuru.

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and rich pollen that attract destructive insects like thrips and pod borers. These pests feed on the flower parts, which stops young pods from forming unless protected early.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ nu mli nu kɛ pollen babaoo. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fãi komɛi, ni no haaa fɔfɔi bibii lɛ afee nɔ ko. ja atsĩ naa mra

english: Why do my coconut trees grow much faster right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tso lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi lɛ?

english: Rainwater carries natural nitrogen and hydrates the soil deeply, which allows coconut trees to absorb nutrients quickly and fuel rapid trunk and leaves growth.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ kɛ nitrogen baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ waa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei tso lɛ ni eŋɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daraa oya

english: Why does heavy rain make my tree fruits swell up so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa aduawai lɛ daa oya lɛ?

english: When trees receive abundant rain, their roots draw up water rapidly and send it directly to developing fruits, expanding their cells and making them grow large in a short time.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei ná nugbɔ babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Gbalamɔ wala yibii lɛ amli ni oha amɛdara yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: How can I tell if my crop is getting enough rainwater to produce big fruits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nugbɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii wuji?

english: A crop getting enough rainwater will have deep green leaves, steady new branch growth, and fruits that expand noticeably week after week rather than dropping off early.
ga: Tsei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa. Niji heei miida be fɛɛ be. Ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baaya hiɛ waa otsi fɛɛ otsi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbee shi oya

english: How does using shade coverings help my young crops survive harsh heat?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ mli?

english: Coverings act as a shield against direct sunlight, keeping the soil cool and reducing moisture loss so young plants do not wither before their roots settle.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baaha tso bibioo lɛ akagbi dani shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my existing farm crops with palm fronds or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei tsei loo baai aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi okwaayeli nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii momo lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground traps moisture in the soil when it rains, prevents weeds from taking over, and protects vital surface roots from sun damage.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni ebuɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe koni hulu akafite amɛ.

english: Why do trees planted in an orchard layout grow bigger than trees crowded close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ tso yibii abɔɔi amli lɛ daraa fe tsei ni yɔɔ kui ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Orchard spacing ensures each tree gets its own direct sunlight and rain collection area, so roots do not fight each other for water and nutrients.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã abɔɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ, ni enáa he ko ni ekɛbuaa nugbɔ nu lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe etswaaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why are coconut trees able to survive on my farm for many years while other crops die easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli afii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi gboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Coconut trees have deep, tough root systems designed to store water and withstand heavy weather, making them long-lasting established crops.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni afee koni enyɛ ehiɛ nu mli ni enyɛ edamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa naa. Ehaa efeɔ tso ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I manage a tree crop that is carrying too much fruit heavy burden on its branches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ amɛniji anɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: Supporting heavy branches with wooden props or gently thinning out sickly fruits ensures the main branches do not snap under the weight before harvest.
ga: Niji ni tsii ni akɛ tsei fiɔ sɛɛ loo afolɔ aduawai ni hela mɔ amɛ blɛoo. Enɛ baatsi niji titrii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo yɛ muji lɛ shishi dani akpa.

english: What causes my crops to look weak and stunted even when they have been on the farm for a long time?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Plants become stunted when soil nutrients are depleted or when prolonged dry weather stresses their roots, preventing them from taking up plant food.
ga: Tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye tsei aniyenii.

english: What should I do on my farm to prepare my crops for unpredictable bad weather?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛsaa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbohii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ?

english: Building proper drainage channels, keeping ground soil covered, and planting windbreak trees around your plot helps protect crops from weather extremes.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ ni afee, sũ ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa waa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when there is no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be ko bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct, harsh sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the soil around their small roots, preventing them from taking up the water and nutrients they need to grow.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ ahe lɛ agbi, ni no haaa amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly during the wet season when high humidity and dark shade keep the pods constantly damp.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient that maize plants need in large amounts to make strong stalks and healthy leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni ŋmãa tsei taoɔ babaoo koni amɛma ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes small ragged holes to appear in the leaves and center whorl of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai kɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar pest that feeds on the soft leaves inside the plant heart, which can severely reduce your harvest if not controlled early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ tso lɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ tsui mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha okpamɔ lɛ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ mra.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot in the ground if I harvest them during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji mikpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When rain saturates the soil for long periods, it starves the roots of air and allows water-loving fungi to attack, causing the tuberous roots to spoil underground.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, sũ lɛ nɔ fɔ̃ɔ be kplaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ aye shishifãi lɛ ahe hɔmɔ ni eha hydrophilic fungi lɛ atutua. Enɛ haa tuber shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it better for my field if I do not burn the bush before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mishãaa jwɛi lɛ dani miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys beneficial organisms and natural plant mulch that nourish the soil; leaving organic material to decay naturally improves soil fertility and holds moisture longer during dry periods.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ ahe helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my crops yield better when I plant them in straight rows instead of broadcasting seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures each crop gets equal access to sunlight, water, and nutrients without competing with its neighbors, while also making weeding and fertilizer application much easier.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ akaŋ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden heavy rains, because the plant conserves energy rather than setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso nɛɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi fe yibii ni ewoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my ripening tomatoes get a dark, sunken rot spot at the bottom end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ fãi ni egboi ni tsuɔ waa lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot and is caused by a shortage of calcium in the fruit, usually triggered by irregular watering patterns during fruit development.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and wither whenever rainwater stands on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When rainwater covers the land and cannot drain away, it suffocates the plant roots by cutting off air. Without oxygen in the soil, the roots rot and cannot send nutrients to the leaves, causing the plants to turn yellow and fail.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya baai lɛ amli. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why should I dig small gutters or channels through my farm before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo nubu loo nubu bibioo ko? Yaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani obɔi dumɔ?

english: Drainage channels give heavy rainwater a clear path to flow off your farm. Without these channels, water will overflow onto your fields, sit on the land, and destroy whatever crops you try to grow.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji gbɛi nɛɛ bɛ lɛ Nu baaho oŋmɔji lɛ amli. ni eta shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni odu

english: Why is it bad if leaves and trash block the pathways where water leaves my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji baai kɛ jwɛi tsi nu ni jɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Blocked water paths stop rainwater from escaping. When the water gets stuck, it backs up and overflows into your planting area, creating standing water that destroys your crops.
ga: Nu gbɛi ni atsĩ naa lɛ tsiɔ nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ kpo lɛ naa. Kɛ́ nu lɛ ŋmɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eku esɛɛ ni eho kɛya he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ baa.

english: Can I clear and plant crops on low valley land without building any water channels?
ga: Ani manyɛ majie jɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ni madu ni mifeee ŋshɔkpɔ ko?

english: Planting on low land without building proper drainage channels is risky because water naturally flows downhill and collects there. When heavy rain comes, the uncontrolled water will submerge your farm and ruin your work.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ nɔ ni aduɔ ni afeee gbɛ ni sa ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara ejaakɛ nu lɛ baatsɔ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaabua ehe naa yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa Nu ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ lɛ baagbe oŋmɔ lɛ shishi ni ekpata onitsumɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english: What happens if water from my neighbor's farm overflows onto my farmland?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji nu ni jɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli lɛ ho kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: If water overflows across land without connected channels to guide it away, it washes away topsoil and leaves crops drowning in excess water, preventing them from producing a good yield.
ga: Kɛji nu ho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni gbɛ ko bɛ ni kɛ lɛ kpaa gbee ni baatsɔɔ lɛ gbɛ lɛ, Nu lɛ baaho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii boteɔ nu ni fa fe nine mli. Nibii kpakpai afeemɔ ni atsĩɔ naa

english: What should I do if rain always creates a large pond in the middle of my crop field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nugbɔ lɛ haa nu agbo ko baa ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: You need to construct connected drainage ditches leading from the flooded area to a safe outlet off your field so the trapped water can flow out instead of sitting there and rotting your crop roots.
ga: Esa akɛ oma nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni nu afua lɛ eyi lɛ kɛyaa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ kponɔ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni nu ni emɔ lɛ anyɛ ajɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeetara jɛmɛ ni efite tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does building mounds or raised beds help my crops during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gɔŋ loo saatso ni awo nɔ lɛ maa yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Raised mounds keep the crop roots elevated above ground water levels, allowing air to reach the roots even when excess rainwater is flowing around the base of the mounds.
ga: Gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔ nu babaoo ho kɛbɔle amɛhe po. gɔŋ lɛ shishi

english: Does heavy rain sitting on my field help feed my crops or hurt them?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii loo eyeɔ amɛ awui?

english: While crops need rain to grow, heavy rain that sits on the soil without draining causes serious damage by drowning root systems and carrying away the good nutrients in your soil.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ moŋ, Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ nii waa kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ nu mli ni ejieɔ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground during the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil remains completely soaked for long periods. Standing water creates soggy soil where rot-causing organisms thrive and air cannot reach the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tee nɔ ehi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ baa yɛ he ni nibii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ daa yɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why did my maize crop fail even though I applied fertilizer and cleared all the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ miifee nɔ ni ehiii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli ni mikɛ jwɛi ewo mli moŋ?

english: Fertilizer and weed control cannot save crops if the land floods and lacks proper drainage. Excess water sitting on the field overpowers the plants and prevents them from using the nutrients you applied.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nyɛŋ ahere ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nu eyi jɛmɛ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni fa fe nine ni bua ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aye amɛhe nɔ, ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii ni okɛwo mli lɛ akatsu nii.

english: Why do crops planted by a tractor machine usually sprout at the exact same time across my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛ trakta duɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shikome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Tractor planters drop seeds at an exact, uniform depth and press the soil evenly around each seed. Because every seed receives the same amount of moisture and warmth, they all germinate and emerge at the same time.
ga: Trakta lɛ duɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miibɔle ehe pɛpɛɛpɛ. dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu nine shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ latsaa ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli.

english: What will happen to my crops if they are planted too close to each other in the ground?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When crops grow too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes the plants weak and results in smaller crop yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does planting my crops in straight, measured rows make them grow better than scattering seeds by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ nine baagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã lɛ?

english: Straight rows give every plant equal access to sunlight and air circulation. It also creates clear pathways, making it much easier for you to clear weeds and apply fertilizer without stepping on your crops.
ga: Nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ehaa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ hu baa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni okɛ onaji efɔɔɔ onibii anɔ.

english: Why is it important for machinery to plow and loosen my land deeply before I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsɔnei atsu nii ni amɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli akwɔ dani amɛdu nii lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil makes it difficult for delicate young roots to push downwards. Loosening the soil allows crop roots to spread quickly, drink water easily, and build a strong foundation for the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akɛ amɛaatsi kɛya shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Nu ni anuɔ lɛ waaa ni ehaa tsei feɔ shishitoo ni wa

english: What happens to my seed if the planting machine buries it too deep underground?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji tsɔne lɛ du amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If a seed is buried too deep, the young sprout burns up all its stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil, often dying before it ever reaches the sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ Tso bibioo lɛ baashã ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛbaatsu nii waa lɛ nɔ. ni bei pii lɛ egboɔ dani eshɛɔ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither so quickly during short dry spells compared to adult plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ be kukuoo ni nu bɛ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto tsei ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have very short, shallow roots that can only reach water in the very top layer of soil. Older plants have deep root systems that can pull water from deep underground during dry periods.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ nu he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing when rainwater sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ beni nugbɔ nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess water covers the field, it drowns the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and stunt growth.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu babaoo ha he lɛ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Tsi niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛdaraaa.

english: How do weeds actually slow down the growth and yield of my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha midalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo aba shi?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that grow faster than your crops. They steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops, leaving your plants starving and weak.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni daa oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my crops need so much extra food and fertilizer right when they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji amɛje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi pɛ?

english: Producing flowers, pods, or grain heads requires a huge burst of energy. During this stage, the crop works extra hard and pulls large amounts of nutrients from the soil to form healthy fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi, ŋmeii, loo dumɔwui ayitsei ni afeɔ lɛ biɔ hewalɛ babaoo waa. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui tsuɔ nii waa fe tsutsu lɛ ni amɛgbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of my seeds rot in the soil without ever sprouting into a seedling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ ni amɛfeee dumɔwui kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when the soil is too wet, cold, or packed too tightly. Without the right balance of warmth and air, harmful fungi in the soil attack the seed before it has a chance to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ, edɔ tsɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ bɛ Fungi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa dumɔwui dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Do my crops have their own natural ways of fighting off sickness, or do they always need chemical sprays?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai? Aloo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ he miihia amɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Crops actually have their own natural defense systems to fight off diseases, much like humans do. However, when diseases are severe, plants need proper care or specialized boosters to help activate and support these natural defenses.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoi ni amɛkɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai. Shi kɛlɛ, taakɛ adesai feɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hela lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Tsei biɔ kwɛmɔ ni sa loo nibii krɛdɛɛi ni kanyaa mɔ koni eye ebua ni ekanya adebɔɔ mli hebuu nibii nɛɛ ni eye ebua amɛ.

english: How can I help my crops build a strong internal defense before diseases attack my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛma mligbɛ hebuu ni mli wa dani helai atutua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You can strengthen your crops by using plant boosters. Unlike standard chemicals that only work on the outside, boosters trigger the plant's internal system, helping it naturally resist bacteria and infections.
ga: Obaanyɛ owaje oŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ tsofai ni haa tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kponɔgbɛ pɛ lɛ ahe. Booster lɛ tsirɛɔ tsei lɛ amli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ wuɔ.

english: What is the difference between a normal chemical spray and a plant booster?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ kɛ tsofai ni haa tsei ahe feɔ fɛo lɛ ateŋ?

english: Regular chemical sprays usually sit on the outside of the crop to kill pests or sickness on contact. A plant booster works differently by helping the plant strengthen its own internal system to control and fight off bacteria from within.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ asɛɛ koni ekɛgbe ŋmɔshi nibii loo helai kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he. Nibii ni haa tsei tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni amɛhaa tsei lɛ woɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkudɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ni amɛwu amɛshi amɛ kɛjɛ amɛmli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my mango trees still get sick even when I spray them regularly with standard chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei lɛ yeɔ hela lolo eyɛ mli akɛ amɛshwieɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ anɔ daa moŋ?

english: Standard chemical sprays only protect the surface of the fruit and leaves. If bacterial diseases get inside the plant, regular sprays cannot always reach them, which is why internal treatments like plant boosters are needed.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ buɔ aduawai kɛ tsei ahe tsei ahe pɛ. Kɛji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli lɛ bote tso lɛ mli lɛ Jeee be fɛɛ be tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ hela lɛ he. Enɛ hewɔ ni mligbɛ tsofai tamɔ tsofai ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ he hiaa lɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I consider using a plant booster on my mango farm alongside my regular sprays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu tso mli tsofai ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi mango ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he kɛfata tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ daa lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Using a plant booster helps control bacterial infections from inside the plant's system, giving your mangoes an extra layer of protection that regular external chemical sprays cannot provide alone.
ga: Tso mli nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ helai ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa mango lɛ hebuu kroko ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ aha.

english: If I spray medicine on my crop leaves, does it stay inside the plant forever to protect it?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ fɔ Ani ebaahi tso lɛ mli kɛya naanɔ koni ebu ehe?

english: No, many treatments do not stay inside the leaf for long. Over time, sunlight, rain, and natural growth reduce the medicine, which is why proper and timed reapplication is necessary.
ga: Dabi, tsofafeemɔi babaoo ehiɛɛɛ baa lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, hulu la, nugbɔshiimɔ, kɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ haa tsofa lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akɛtsu nii ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ kɛ be ni sa mli lɛ.

english: Why is it important to apply crop medicine carefully instead of just splashing it on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni akɛaashwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Medicines like plant boosters need to be applied properly so the leaves can absorb them correctly. If applied poorly, the medicine will not stay in the leaf long enough to help the plant fight off bacteria.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai tamɔ tsofai ni haa tsei tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tsofai lɛ ehiŋ baai lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛwu amɛshi helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ.

english: Why does crop medicine sometimes fail to work even after I have bought and used it on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsofai ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ tsuuu nii eyɛ mli akɛ mihe ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Medicine can fail if it is not applied using the correct technique. Because certain treatments do not remain inside the leaf naturally, poor application prevents the plant from absorbing enough to fight off sickness.
ga: Tsofa baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋaa ni ja tsuuu nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai komɛi ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ ehiɛɛɛ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwu eshi hela.

english: Can bacterial diseases inside my crops be controlled once the plant is already infected?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akudɔ bacteria helai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ tsei lɛ amli pɛ?

english: Yes, bacterial infections can be controlled by using proper treatments like plant boosters that work within the plant to stop bacteria from spreading and destroying the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akudɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni sa, tamɔ tsofai ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli ni tsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ mli koni ekɛtsi helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How does a plant booster actually stop bacteria from destroying my crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsofai ni haa tsei tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ atsĩ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: When applied correctly, a plant booster enters the plant's system and helps it actively control and limit the growth of bacteria, preventing the disease from damaging the leaves and fruit.
ga: Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tsofai ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekudɔɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ adalɛ. Tsi helai ni fiteɔ baai kɛ aduawai lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my crops dry up when the rains stop, and how can artificial watering help?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ gbiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛ lɛ? Ni te nu ni akɛfee lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops need a constant supply of water to absorb nutrients from the soil. When the dry season comes, using irrigation pipes or pumps delivers water directly to your crops so they stay healthy and keep growing even without rainfall.
ga: Tsei hia nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛnu niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ bashɛ Nu shwiemɔ hose loo pɔmp ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha nu aya onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛya nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: What is the simplest way for me to get water from a nearby stream to my farm without carrying heavy buckets?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maná nu kɛjɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli kɛya miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni miwooo baagi ni tsii nɔ?

english: You can use a small motor pump connected to plastic hose pipes. The pump draws water directly from the stream and spreads it across your farm, saving you strength and watering your crops much faster.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsɔne pɔmp bibioo ko ni akɛwo plastic paipi ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Pɔmp lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ faa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ejaraa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Ehaa onáa hewalɛ kɛ nyɛmɔ ni okɛwoɔ onibii amli nu oya kwraa.

english: What time of the day is best for me to water my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is the best time. During midday, the sun is too hot and will dry up the water before your plants can drink it from the soil.
ga: Leebi loo shwane mli Eji be ni hi fe fɛɛ. yɛ shwane mli Hulu lɛ baadɔ tsɔ ni ebaaha nu lɛ agbi dani tsei lɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I hire a tractor to plow my land instead of using my hoe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe trakta koni mikɛtsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii yɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: A tractor plows deeper and much faster than manual labor. Deep plowing loosens hard soil so plant roots can grow deep to find water, while also saving you weeks of heavy physical work.
ga: Trakta baanyɛ atsu nii kɛya shɔŋŋ ni etsu nii oya fe nine nitsumɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ada kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha okɛ otsii babaoo akatsu nii waa.

english: Will using heavy machinery on my land make the soil hard and spoil my crops over time?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa ni ebaafite miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Tractors can press the soil too tightly if you drive them on very wet land. If you only plow when the land is slightly dry, the machinery will loosen the soil without damaging its structure.
ga: Trakta baanyɛ anyɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa tsɔ kɛji okɛ tsɔne kudɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ efɔ waa nɔ. Kɛji akɛ otsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi fioo pɛ. Shishitoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: How can using machines during harvest time help save my crops from spoiling?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkafite?

english: Harvesting machines collect crops quickly in just a few hours. This prevents your mature crops from sitting in the field for too long where rains, mold, or insects can damage them.
ga: Nikpalɔ lɛ kɛ oyaiyeli kpalaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo ko pɛ mli. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ, he ni nugbɔ, ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii baanyɛ afite nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Is it possible for me to plant and harvest crops twice on the same land in one year?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ madu ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ yɛ he kome yɛ afi kome mli?

english: Yes, if you use fast-growing seeds combined with irrigation during dry spells, you can harvest one crop and immediately plant another on the same field in the same year.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ fata nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii kome ni okɛ ekroko awo ŋmɔ kome mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi kome mli.

english: Why is it important for me to clear and prepare my land before the first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni masaa he dani klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ anɛ lɛ?

english: Preparing your land early allows the soil to settle and removes weeds before you plant. This means your seeds can go into the ground at the very first rain and get a head start on growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ejieɔ jwɛi dani aduɔ nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli ni amɛná yitso yɛ dalɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant legumes like cowpea on a field where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa, tamɔ tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ mli tsutsu lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, while cowpeas put natural plant food back into the earth. Rotating these crops keeps your land fertile and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, cowpea lɛ kɛ tsei aniyenii kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nibii nɛɛ ni oootsake lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up tightly on very hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The maize plant rolls its leaves into tight tubes to protect itself from the hot sun so it does not lose too much water through evaporation.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli amɛwoɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa mli koni ekɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni amɛkafite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer gradually gives the maize the energy it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ Kɛ́ okɛ organic loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa fata he lɛ, ebaaha oŋmei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce very thin tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ?

english: When soil is too hard or has too much nitrogen, the plant uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves above ground. Loosening the soil before planting helps the cassava roots expand naturally into large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How does planting plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings help them grow?
ga: dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Te mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Plantain leaves act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade it needs while keeping the soil moist so the cocoa can establish itself safely.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Plantain baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni ekɛhaa kookoo bibioo lɛ bɔ ni esumɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ama shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I stop burning the bush cleared from my farmland before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa tsei bibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ midumɔi amli lɛ ashãa dani madu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic food in the soil and leaves it exposed to dry under the hot sun. Letting cleared plants rot directly into the soil over time enriches the ground with natural nutrients and holds rainwater longer.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaa egbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ha tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ agbo kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo, ni ebaaha nugbɔ nu lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper and garden egg flowers drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔii kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when plants get stressed by extreme hot weather or lack of water in the soil. Regular watering during dry spells helps the plant stay healthy enough to hold onto flowers and produce fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it bad to plant three or four corn seeds together in the exact same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting many seeds in one hole forces the crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Spacing seeds out ensures every stalk gets enough food to grow big, full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛwu amɛtao nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni dumɔwui eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking juices from under the leaves. Spraying early with neem oil or mild soap water protects the leaves from insect damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Mra be mli lɛ ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and lets specific pests build up. Switching to legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients to the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni oha tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi abua amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmãa tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top. Mounding extra soil firmly around the base of the plant gives the roots a stronger grip in the ground to resist wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Shikpɔŋ kroko ni akɛbaabɔle shishi lɛ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground before it is time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yam rot happens when water collects around the tuber in hard soil or when underground pests bite the skin. Planting on high mounds helps excess rainwater drain away, keeping the yams dry and healthy.
