ga: Sweet potato rot baa kɛji nu ebɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ŋmɔ hewolo lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ha sweet potato lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Without tall shade trees or temporary plants like plantains to block the harsh sun, the leaf tissue loses water faster than the roots can drink, causing the leaves to scorch and die.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Leaf tissue lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow from the leaf tips inward when the soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen, which the crop needs to build strong, green food-making leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ kɛyaa mligbɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my crops get more diseases when I plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa helai babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously lets pests and fungal spores that feed on that specific plant build up in the soil, making each new harvest weaker and more vulnerable to sickness.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ edaa lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ hee fɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei baa shi ni helai baanyɛ amɔ amɛ oya.

english: Underground cassava rot usually happens when heavy rains leave standing water in poorly drained soil, suffocating the roots and allowing harmful fungi in the dirt to decay the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. ni oha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy required to grow deep, large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the blossoms fall off without making fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi efoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when daytime temperatures are extremely high, when soil moisture shifts abruptly from dry to wet, or when there are no wind currents or insects to move pollen inside the flower.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bɛ ni baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stunting the plant's growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiiha tso lɛ dalɛ miitsi enaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the fresh leaves, or from a plant virus spread by those insects as they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ mli

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to put fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli dani ahum baa lɛ ji susumɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away loose fertilizer off the topsoil before the crop's roots can absorb it, wasting your investment and washing nutrients into nearby rivers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them survive hot weather?
ga: Mulching around Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ jwɛi yeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dried grass or leaves over the soil acts like a protective blanket that shields the ground from direct sun, keeping the soil cool and trapping moisture so roots stay hydrated longer.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if they are growing a small distance away from them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo pɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds spread roots underground that secretly steal water and plant food from the soil, while their top leaves block light, leaving your main crops starved and weak even if they do not touch.
ga: Jwɛi gbɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkɛju nu yɛ teemɔŋ ni amɛdu niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa. Shi oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ni hɔmɔ aye amɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ ataaa amɛhe po.

english: How do I know if my land is naturally fertile enough to grow maize before I spend money on seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmãa dani mafite shika yɛ dumɔwui ahe?

english: You can check the soil color and texture—dark, soft soil that holds moisture without remaining waterlogged usually has good organic matter. Observing healthy wild plants growing on the land is also a natural sign that the soil is rich enough for maize.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ su kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha. Nɔ ni ha ebalɛ nakai ji shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu shwieee nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Bei pii lɛ, eyɛ nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli. Koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field without tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct equatorial sunlight. Fast-growing shade crops like plantains or bananas act as temporary umbrellas, shielding the young cocoa trees from intense heat and heat stress while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ equatorial hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo banana tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli shade. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks close together so I can fit more plants on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots and leaves fight for limited sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly allows each plant to get enough food to develop thick, heavy tuber roots underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa shishifãi ni mli tse ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow and dropping off even though I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be a sign that the plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the roots are suffocating from too much standing water. Balanced fertilizer and good soil drainage allow the plant to absorb food properly and stay green.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ afee okadi akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ejaakɛ nu lɛ ekã shi tsɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ja kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up and turn sticky during the warm season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck the plant's juices and spread viruses. The sticky substance is waste left by the insects, which attracts soot-like mold and stops the leaves from making food for the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ baa. Nɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ ji jwɛi ni kooloi bibii shiɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ ni haa tso lɛ baa lɛ feɔ niyenii.

english: Why does my crop get burned and die when I pour fertilizer directly against the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmeii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is rich in salts that draw water out of plant roots and stems when touched directly, causing chemical burns. Fertilizer should always be applied in a ring or line a few inches away from the stem so roots can safely suck up the nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛji amɛkɛ amɛhe kpe tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni kɛ tsofa shãa baa Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be fɛɛ be yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai loo ŋtayaai amli 2-3 inches kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How often should I water my cabbage farm during the dry season to prevent the heads from splitting open?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-cabbage ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni yitsei lɛ akagbala?

english: Cabbage needs consistent soil moisture rather than heavy flooding after a long dry stretch. Irregular watering causes the inside of the cabbage head to grow faster than the outside skin, which makes the head burst open.
ga: Kaabaji he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni nu aaawo mli waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ baaha kaaba yitso lɛ mligbɛ lɛ ada oya fe kponɔgbɛ lɛ. ni haa yitso lɛ mli gbalaa lɛ

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from last year's harvest produce smaller ears than certified store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ toi bibii fe dumɔwui ni ahe kɛjɛ shwapoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred hybrid varieties engineered for high yield and vigor in the first generation. Saving seeds from these plants for the next season results in genetic breakdown, leading to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni afee lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei nɛɛ amli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ haa fɔmɔ nii fiteɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the lower leaves of my garden egg plants once they start fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli beni amɛbɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Removing lower leaves near the ground improves airflow around the base of the plant and stops splash-back of soil diseases during rains. It also forces the plant to send its energy and nutrients directly to growing bigger fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Enyɛɔ tsei anɔ hu koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo aduawai wuji ni miida lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crop leaves even when I clear the land completely before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miida oya fe mitso lɛ baai lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jɛmɛ fɛɛ dani midu nii moŋ.

english: Weeds produce thousands of hardy seeds that lie dormant in the soil waiting for sunlight and rain to disturb them. Because weed species are native and naturally aggressive, they germinate quickly to steal nutrients before cultivated crops can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi woɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɛɔ shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni emɛ hulu kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni egba enaa Enɛ ji akɛ, jwɛi ji maŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni amɛfeɔ basabasa yɛ adebɔɔ mli. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ nii dani tso lɛ anyɛ ada.

english: How can I check if the crop seeds I bought at the market are pure and good enough to germinate well before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ he tse ni ehi bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani adu?

english: You can test seed quality by placing 100 seeds on a damp cloth or in a bowl of moist soil for a few days. High-quality seeds will have over 90 to 95 out of 100 seeds sprout healthy shoots, with very few broken or dirty seeds in the mix.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka dumɔwui lɛ ahe okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 100 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. loo yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaná dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fe 90 kɛyashi 95 yɛ 100 mli, ni dumɔwui ni ekumɔ loo muji fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli ni akɛfutu lɛ mli.

english: How do I make sure the grain seeds I save from this harvest do not spoil before the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ efiteee dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baashɛ?

english: Ensure seeds are dried thoroughly until they are hard enough that you cannot dent them with a fingernail. Remove all dirty or damaged seeds, and store the good ones in airtight containers mixed with approved storage powder in a cool, dry place.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛbaafee shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛkagbala ŋmei lɛ. Jiemɔ dumɔwui ni he tseee loo efite lɛ fɛɛ. Ni okɛ dumɔwui kpakpai awo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni akɛ powda ni akɛtoɔ nii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ efutu mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow even though there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are missing a key soil nutrient called nitrogen, or the soil is waterlogged and suffocating the roots. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea usually restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ekoŋŋ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my young crop after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa awo tsei bibii amli beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: The best time for the first fertilizer application is about 2 to 3 weeks after the seedlings sprout, because their roots are now developed enough to take in the nutrients. A second dose is usually given when flowering or fruiting starts.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ ji aaafee otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye niyenii mli hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, akɛ tsɔne ni ji enyɔ lɛ haa kɛ́ fɔfɔi loo yibiiwoo je shishi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and moisture, protecting the young cocoa trees during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad if I put too many maize seeds into one hole when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the growing plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them out gives every plant enough room to build strong stalks and full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ haa tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he akaŋ. He ni ato lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso lɛ shishifã ni wa kɛ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I select the best cassava stems to plant so I get a big harvest of tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu koni maná ŋmei ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Choose mature, healthy stems from the middle section of strong, disease-free cassava plants. Cut them cleanly into pieces that have at least 4 to 6 visible buds or nodes before planting.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 ni anaa lɛ ahi mli dani adu.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat gets too intense, when watering is uneven, or when bees are absent to pollinate them. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Removing weeds early in the crop's growth allows your plants to absorb all available nutrients without competition.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on my farm next season instead of planting maize in the same field again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ

english: Planting groundnuts or beans helps repair the soil after heavy crops like maize. Legumes take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, providing natural fertility for the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts loo beans ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni esaa shikpɔŋ lɛ beni adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Legumes lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni afee adebɔɔ mli babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but very few of them actually turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Cocoa trees rely on tiny insects or human help to move pollen from flower to flower. If pollen isn't transferred successfully, the unpollinated flowers simply dry up and fall off without forming pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei yeɔ kooloi bibii. loo adesa yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛjieɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi lɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ pollen tsɔne lɛ yeee omanye lɛ, fɔfɔi ni pollen bɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: Hand pollination is a technique where you manually transfer pollen from one cocoa flower to another using small tools or tweezers. This ensures that more flowers turn into healthy, full-sized cocoa pods, significantly boosting your harvest.
ga: Hand pollination ji gbɛ ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ onine shwieɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ dɛŋdade bibioo ko loo tweezers nɔ. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi babaoo atsɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha okpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow directly on the main trunk and thick branches instead of at the tips of tiny twigs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ kɛ eniji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e wa ngɛ tso nine nyafii ko nya.

english: Cocoa pods are heavy fruit. The tree naturally grows flowers on its trunk and major branches so the thick wood can support the weight of mature cocoa pods without snapping.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ji aduawai ni tsii. Tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ tsei niji wuji lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, tso ni mli tse lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ kookoo tso ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ ni efoŋ.

english: How does pruning or trimming my cocoa trees help them grow better pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kookoo tsei ni afoɔ loo afoɔ amɛhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary or dead branches, allowing sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree. This reduces humidity that causes black pod disease and lets the tree focus its food on growing healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni egboi lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ aba shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow or dry during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves dry up when the tree lacks sufficient water or shade. Providing tall shade trees keeps the soil cool and moist, protecting your crop from extreme heat stress.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Buu onibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he.

english: How often should I clear weeds from around my cocoa trees?
ga: Esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Shii enyiɛ kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Weeds steal valuable soil nutrients, light, and water from your cocoa trees. Clearing weeds every few months—especially right before flowering—ensures your trees get all the food they need.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jara wa, la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli. Ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ daa nyɔji fioo, titri lɛ dani fɔfɔii baa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ anine ashɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm is producing as many cocoa bags as it should for its size?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ miiwo kookoo kotokui babaoo bɔ ni sa kɛha bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji lɛ?

english: You can calculate yield by measuring the total bags of dried beans produced per acre or hectare. Well-maintained farms with good pollination can produce twice as many bags per acre compared to neglected fields.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu yibiiwoo he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni ajieɔ yɛ acre loo hectare kome mli lɛ fɛɛ ni ooosusu lɛ nɔ. Okwaafoi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie baagi ni fa fe shii enyɔ yɛ acre kome mli. Kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Why are some cocoa pods on the same tree big and healthy while others stay tiny and dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni pods komɛi ji bibii ni amɛgbi lolo lɛ?

english: Pod size depends on proper pollination, water availability, and pest control. Pods that received partial pollination or were attacked by pests like mirids often stop growing and dry up prematurely.
ga: Pod dalɛ damɔ pollination, nu ni yɔɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids lɛ fã ko ewo mli loo amɛtutuaa amɛ lɛ kpaɔ amɛdalɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya.

english: My cocoa trees are getting very old and yield fewer pods; do I need to cut them all down?
ga: Mi cacao tsei lɛ miigbɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Ani ehe miihia ni mafo amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Not always. Old trees can often be revitalized through heavy pruning and side-grafting with improved young shoots, or by gradually replanting seedling varieties alongside the old ones.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be ebaa lɛ nakai. Abaanyɛ aha tsei ni egbɔ lɛ afee ehee kɛtsɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa kɛ afã ni akɛ ŋmeii heei ni asaa amɛhe lɛ baawo mli lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi heei ni aaadu yɛ momo lɛ ahe fiofio lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes black spots on my young cocoa pods, and how does it hurt my crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa? Ni te eeye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Black spots are usually caused by fungal disease (black pod) or sap-sucking insects (mirids/akate). Left untreated, they ruin the beans inside and prevent the pod from ripening properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela (black pods) loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ baa. (Mirid/Akate) Kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii Ebaafite ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I save seeds from my maize harvest this year to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ afi nɛɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It depends on the variety. If you are growing a hybrid variety, saving and replanting those seeds next year will lead to smaller harvests and uneven plant growth. It is better to buy fresh hybrid seeds every planting season.
ga: Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji oodu hybrid henɔi ni oookwɛ nɔ ni ooodu ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni abaakpa lɛ afee bibioo ni tsei lɛ adalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Esa akɛ ahe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why should I buy certified seed from an agricultural agent instead of buying grain from the local market to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe dumɔwui kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ koni okɛdu

english: Certified seeds are specially produced and tested by experts to resist diseases, handle weather changes better, and produce much higher yields than regular grain sold in the market.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni ŋaalɔi kaa amɛkwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ kɛji helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe. Kpeemɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ naa jogbaŋŋ Ni yibiiwoo lɛ fa kwraa fe dumɔwui ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What does it mean when an officer says my crop is a pollinating crop?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ onukpa lɛ kɛɛ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔi pollination?

english: It means the crop needs pollen moved from one flower to another by wind or insects like bees to make fruits or seeds. Because pollen travels, pollen from a neighbor's field can easily mix with your crop.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei he miihia pollen ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii jieɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ koni amɛfee aduawai loo dumɔwui. Ejaakɛ pollen baanyɛ aya gbɛfaa. Pollen ni jɛɔ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afutu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya.

english: Why did my yellow maize cob end up with white seeds mixed inside it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei ŋmɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ?

english: Wind carried pollen from a nearby field growing white maize onto your yellow maize flowers. To keep your seed variety pure, you need to plant different maize varieties far apart from each other.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa pollen kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ ko ni miida lɛ mli kɛyaa oŋmãa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ anɔ. Bɔni afee ni odumɔwui lɛ ahe atse Ehe miihia ni odu ŋmãa srɔtoi lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ.

english: How often do I need to walk through my field to check on my crops after planting?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔji amli koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ agbe naa?

english: You should walk through your field at least twice a week. Regular monitoring helps you catch pests, diseases, or nutrient deficiencies early before they spoil your entire harvest.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ oyale mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Nibii amlipɛimɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni onáa tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ mra. Dani amɛbaakpãtã onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to produce smaller harvests every year when I keep using my own saved seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Be mli ni mikɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ miitsu nii lolo?

english: Over time, saved seeds lose their original strength and can build up seed-borne diseases across generations. Returning to fresh certified seeds restores high productivity.
ga: Beni be hoɔ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amɛshishijee hewalɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli kɛbaa lɛ yɛ yinɔi lɛ amli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ni akɛbaaku sɛɛ aba lɛ baaye abua ni aná yibii babaoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Are insects flying around my crop flowers harmful to my farm?
ga: Kplukai ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ he Ani mi fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ oshara kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Not all insects are harmful. Beneficial insects like bees visit flowers to feed and in the process transfer pollen, which helps your plants form healthy pods, fruits, and seeds.
ga: Oshara bɛ kooloi komɛi ahe. Kplukai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii yasaraa fɔfɔi kɛha niyenii. kɛ yɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ pollen kɛyaa fɔfɔi anɔ lɛ mli Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii, aduawai, kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if a new seed variety brought to our community will actually grow well on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui heei ni akɛba wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can plant the new seed on a small test portion of your farm alongside your usual crops. This lets you observe how it behaves in your soil and weather before planting your main field.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui heei yɛ kaa fã bibioo ko mli. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ daa lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa okwɛɔ bɔ ni efeɔ enii ehaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli dani okɛduɔ yɛ oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli.

english: Why are my neighbor's crops growing faster than mine even though we planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tso lɛ daa oya fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Your neighbor might be growing an improved early-maturing seed variety, or their soil might have different moisture levels and nutrients. Seed variety plays a big role in growth speed.
ga: Okutsoŋnyo lɛ baanyɛ adu dumɔwui ni shwereɔ mra ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Aloo ekolɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ srɔtoi. Dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ tsuɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ ko ni he hiaa he nii yɛ dalɛ oya mli.

english: If I hold onto extra planting seeds in my home until next year, will they still germinate well?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ to ni mikɛdu yɛ shia lɛ, ani amɛbaakwɛ̃ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Seeds lose their ability to sprout if stored poorly. Moisture, heat, and insects weaken seeds over time, so they must be kept in cool, dry, sealed conditions if saved for later.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛtooo jogbaŋŋ. Fɛ̃i, dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni atsĩ naa kɛji akɛ akɛbaatsu nii yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and curling up in the middle of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plants lack key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil or when fall armyworms attack the central shoot, preventing the crop from absorbing food properly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo beni autumn cutworms lɛ tutua ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored beans develop tiny holes and turn into white powder after a few weeks in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔ powda yɛŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni ekɛwo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ

english: Bean weevils lay invisible eggs on the crop before harvest, and once placed in dry storage, the eggs hatch into insects that eat the inside of the beans and leave behind powdery waste.
ga: Bean ŋmei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani akpaa. ni kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni egbi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ powda yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: If I plant cowpeas and maize together on the same piece of land, will they fight for nutrients?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ he kome lɛ, Ani amɛbaatswa amɛhe shi yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he?

english: Cowpeas and maize actually work together; cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil to feed the maize, while maize gives the tall cowpeas a stalk to support them.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa haa tsina ŋmeii kakadaji ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ.

english: Why does my farmland soil become hard like concrete and stop growing healthy crops after a few seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit ni ekpaa tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ yɛ bei fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Repeated burning of farm clearings and heavy rain wash away organic leaves and earthworms that keep soil loose, leaving behind dense soil that roots cannot easily push through.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni agbele nɔ ni ashãa shii abɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsei ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli mlɛo.

english: Why are my maize plants producing tassels at the top but no proper corn cobs this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii yɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ? Shi ŋmãa ni sa bɛ afi nɛɛ.

english: When crops experience extreme heat or dry spells right when flowering starts, the silk threads dry out before pollen can fertilize them, resulting in empty or bare cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ he pɛ kɛkɛ ni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfɔ̃ɔ lɛ, Siliki lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji cob ni nɔ ko bɛ mli loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do my bean seeds rot in the ground when I plant them right after a very heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa waa sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen in the soil to breathe as they sprout; flooded soil drowns the seed and allows rot bacteria to break it down before it can push above ground.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛtsiɔ amɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my harvested maize has gone bad and is dangerous to feed to my family?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ efite ni eye miweku lɛ awui?

english: If maize is stored while still wet, invisible mold grows and releases toxic chemicals called aflatoxins, which give the grain a greenish-black powder, a musty smell, and make people sick.
ga: Kɛji okɛ ŋmãa to be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ, ŋmãa ni anaaa lɛ daa ni ejieɔ tsofai fɔji ni atsɛɔ amɛ aflatoxins lɛ kpo. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Musty ŋmɔlɔ ko yɛ. ni eha gbɔmɛi hela mɔ amɛ

english: Why do my maize grains split open and crack when I leave them on mats in the hot midday sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ fãa ni amɛtswaa kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Drying wet grain too quickly in high heat bakes the outer layer faster than the center can dry, creating tension inside the kernel that forces the outer shell to break.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa ni efɔ lɛ oya tsɔ yɛ la ni mli wa mli lɛ, ebaaha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ ashã oya fe bɔ ni teŋgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbi. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmãa baa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli fãa.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my last maize harvest produce smaller cobs than the original seed I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmeii bibii fe shishijee ŋmeii ni mihe lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds lose their natural strength after the first generation, so replanting saved grains yields weaker crops with smaller cobs compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee jarayeli nibii krokomɛi lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aaadu ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii aba kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and taller than my crop seedlings even when they sprout on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkwɔ fe midumɔwui lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tougher and adapted to poor conditions, allowing them to suck up soil nutrients, water, and sunlight far faster than cultivated crops can.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa jwɛi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong direct sunlight and heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava around them creates shelter and keeps the soil cool until the cocoa trees grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ he fɛɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ mli waa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the maize lacks food, especially nitrogen, or that the soil is too dry. Adding animal manure, compost, or recommended nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and produce good corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛfata he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmei kpakpai.

english: Why is it bad if I drop three or four maize seeds in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in the same spot, the roots fight with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Planting one or two seeds per hole gives each plant enough space to grow strong and yield big ears.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ baawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the middle leaves of my corn plants and chewing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing centers of corn plants. Applying recommended crop protection or putting clean wood ash inside the central funnel early in the morning helps get rid of them.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo mli loo okɛ tso sũ ni he tse fata ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋta lɛ he leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted with the small growth buds pointing upward toward the sky or placed flat under the soil. Planting them with the buds pointing downward makes it difficult for roots to form and delays growth.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋwɛi loo okɛ ohe awo shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ adu ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ shi lɛ, ehaa ewaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baaje shishi, ni ehaa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tuber growing underground. Raising the vines on stakes keeps the leaves clean, catches sunlight, and prevents diseases caused by leaves touching wet ground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ ahe tseɔ, ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ, ni ehaa helai ni baai ni taa hei ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects hiding under the leaves. Spraying the plants with neem water solution or safe pest treatment stops the insects and allows new leaves to spread out flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Ni akɛteeɔ tsei lɛ ashishi ni akɛ neem nu loo gbɛi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwieɔ tsei anɔ Etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa ni ehaa baai heei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: My tomato plants have many blossoms, so why are the flowers dropping off without making fruits?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely between waterings, or when tiny pests attack the flowers. Regular watering and keeping the soil moist helps fruits form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, nu ni oooha amɛ daa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai aba.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm ground better for the next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have roots that trap good air and turn it into food for the soil. Leaving their roots and leaves to decay in the soil feeds the next crop without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni he esa waa ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fite yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, stops the sun from drying out the earth too fast, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition causes the plants to grow tall and thin with small, weak corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ shwiili ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate roots and leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living umbrellas that shield them from the sun and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo tsei ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my cassava yield get smaller every year if I plant it in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the exact same spot year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, causing the land to become weak and producing smaller harvests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewooo yibii babaoo.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my soil stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to a family of crops that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps neighboring crops like maize grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele, ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and getting full of tiny holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu bibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in maize leaves and yellowing are common signs of pest attacks, such as Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the leaves, or a lack of essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe, tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmei ni yeɔ baa, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden changes in hot weather, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium and key nutrients in the soil.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛkpe nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, tamɔ tsakemɔ ni ba trukaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be loo calcium kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: How can I prevent the soil around my vegetable crops from drying out quickly during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables lɛ he lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry leaves, straw, or grass—a practice called mulching—traps moisture in the soil, blocks direct sunlight, and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Ni akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—haa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Tsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni oha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my planted food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni adu lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that adapt quickly to local conditions, allowing them to suck up water, fertilizer, and sunlight much faster than cultivated food crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shihilɛi amli. Enɛ haa amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya fe niyenii ni amɛduɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I prune or trim lower leaves from my pepper and tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Trimming lower, old, or yellowing leaves helps the plant direct its energy into growing big fruits instead of extra leaves, while also improving airflow to prevent damp fungal diseases.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni egbɔ, loo ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni fa fe nine baatsu nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ hela ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do seeds bought from an agro-dealer produce better harvests than seeds I saved from my last crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ wo yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds from agro-dealers are specially selected and treated to resist diseases, handle bad weather better, and produce higher yields compared to seeds saved over multiple harvests.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni atsaa amɛ koni helai akamɔ amɛ. Enyɛɔ ekpeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi babaoo mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why is my maize turning light yellow from the bottom leaves going up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ amli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow big. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base will help the plant recover its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are some of my crop plants staying very short while others right next to them are growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi be kukuoo nɛkɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ shwereɔ waa lɛ?

english: Uneven growth happens when soil nutrients or moisture aren't spread evenly, or when small root pests damage individual plants. Spacing your crops evenly and distributing organic fertilizer across the whole field ensures every plant gets equal food and space to grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ loo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli ejaaa pɛpɛɛpɛ. aloo be mli ni shishifãi bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ Fiteɔ tso fɛɛ tso. Tsɔɔmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ato he ni oja yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ koni tsei fɛɛ aná niyenii kɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara lɛ falɛ kome.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids hidden under the leaves, sucking out the plant's juice. Using neem oil spray or insecticidal soap gets rid of these pests so the plant can grow smooth, healthy new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛtsɔ nu ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark conditions. Pruning overcrowded cocoa branches lets sunlight and fresh air into the farm to dry out the pods and stop the fungus from growing.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kookoo tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni aaafolɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni eha ŋmeii lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy rainwater collects in the soil and cannot drain away, suffocating the tubers. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to run off, keeping the tubers safe and dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli. suffocate the head Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant before turning into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme midday heat or sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil around the plant constantly moist with mulch helps cool the roots so the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ shwane mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛ́ okɛ muji wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my watermelons cracking open on the field before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelons lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛdara kwraa lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack when they absorb a sudden surge of water after being dry for a while, causing the sweet inside to expand faster than the skin. Watering your field steadily and moderately prevents this sudden swelling.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛ́ eŋɔ nu ni teɔ shi trukaa beni egbi be fioo sɛɛ lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe ŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo otsei lɛ amli daa kɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafuu trukaa.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support the weight of a heavy bunch, especially in strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a bamboo or wooden prop takes the weight off the roots and prevents the tree from snapping.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ amli tsiimɔ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso loo tso fiɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni ebaaha tso lɛ akakumɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorching and dying in the bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain alongside your cocoa creates a living canopy that protects the young trees from heat until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo he lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daa waa.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting early while sitting in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ oya beni mitara ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers break dormancy and sprout when the storage area gets too warm and humid. Storing yams in a cool, well-ventilated barn off the ground helps them stay asleep so they keep fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baawɔ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato to ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwɔɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting my maize seeds further apart produce bigger corn ears than planting many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ lɛ haa ŋmãa toi wuji baa fe dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ? Dumɔwui ni abua naa yɛ bu kome mli

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing maize properly ensures each plant gets enough food and light to produce large, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ toi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to make big mounds of loose soil before I plant my yam setts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji agbo ko dani madu sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow large and long underground. Loose, elevated soil mounds allow the root to expand easily without fighting hard, compacted dirt, resulting in bigger and better-shaped yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Gɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni awó nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ muji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni dara ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burning and drying up under the sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct sun. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to protect them from scorching until their roots and branches are fully developed.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akashã lɛ kɛyashi eshishifãi kɛ eniji lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to stay green and grow leaves. The plant takes nitrogen from older leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ baai. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ baai momoi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small, tight bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe bibii bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids hiding on the underside of the leaves. As they drink the plant's juices, they cause the leaf to warp and stop growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ Amɛbaafite baai lɛ ni amɛbaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Without a steady moisture supply, the plant abandons flower production to save its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛji hulutsoo be fɛɛ be bɛ lɛ Tsei hu baakpa fɔfɔii afeemɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When soil stays flooded or waterlogged for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing underground fungi to multiply and rot the crop.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my maize grow so much greener when I plant it on a plot where I harvested cowpeas last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ fe tsutsu lɛ kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa tsina ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other leguminous plants take nitrogen gas from the air and store it naturally in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that stored nitrogen remains in the dirt to feed the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the fruit bunch is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani aduawai akutsei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top. When strong winds come, the weight of the bunch pulls the shallow root system out of the ground unless you prop up the trunk with strong wooden poles.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa lɛ Nine lɛ muji lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ anɔ. kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi ja akɛ tso ni mli wa tsu nii ni akɛfi tso lɛ shishi

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with seeds that can sleep in the soil for years. When you clear land and expose the soil to rain and sunlight, weed seeds germinate instantly and drink up nutrients faster than domestic crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa. Dumɔwui yɛ ni baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Beni ojieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni okɛwoɔ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Jwɛi dumɔwui baakwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛnu niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shia tsei dumɔwui.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works well because maize grows fast and is harvested in about three to four months, leaving the field open for the slower-growing cassava to expand and produce tubers over the rest of the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3-4 mli. Shi ŋmɔji lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni ewo ŋmei yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stems and tiny yields. Giving crops proper spacing creates healthier individual plants and a larger total harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi. Kɛ akɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa baaha tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa babaoo yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava dropping off during the dry season, and does it mean my crop is dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii miigboi?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to conserve water and protect itself from drought. The crop is not dead; it is resting and will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi hɔmɔ naa. Nibii ni adu lɛ gboko lolo. Ehe jɔɔ ehe ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight. When the leaves catch good light, they produce the energy needed to grow large, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la kpakpa Ebaaha hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which causes the plant to focus on growing leafy branches instead of holding onto fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niji ni miida ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ aduawai ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster right after I put fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer feeds any plant growing in the soil without picking sides. Clearing weeds completely before applying fertilizer ensures your crops get all the nutrients instead of sharing them with weeds.
ga: Fertilizer haa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhala fãi. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ naa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ baajara amɛ.

english: Why does my soil become very hard and red after rain, making it difficult for crop roots to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni etsuɔ ​​waa beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ani eha ewa aha tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃?

english: Heavy rains wash away the fertile topsoil and leave behind compact clay that is low in organic material. Mixing in compost or decomposed animal manure softens the soil and helps roots breathe and absorb water.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. ni eshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni efee ekome ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli faaa yɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo futu mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛmuɔ nu

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and showing small holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee bu bibii lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves with ragged holes are usually a sign of insect pests like fall armyworms feeding on the central growing point of the plant, or a lack of nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ buji ni etse lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe okadi, tamɔ fall armyworms ni miitao niyenii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa lɛ. loo nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, usually triggered by inconsistent watering where the plant cannot pull continuous nutrients from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni no hewɔ lɛ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ

english: Why do some coconuts on the same cluster grow big while others drop off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ kuu kome mli lɛ daraa ni ekrokomɛi hu shwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: A coconut tree produces more flowers on a bunch than it can actually feed. The tree naturally drops extra tiny nuts so it can send enough water and energy to mature the healthiest ones remaining on that bunch.
ga: Kokoo tsei baawo fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni abaanyɛ akwɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Tsei jieɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. kpo bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa aba koni ekɛkwɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do fruits on my coconut tree mature at different times instead of all coming out at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yibii ni yɔɔ mi ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shikome lɛ?

english: Coconut trees produce new fruit bunches in continuous stages month after month. While one lower bunch is fully ripe and ready for harvest, new flowering shoots higher up are just emerging.
ga: Kokoo tsei yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ aduawai akui heei daa nyɔŋ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shishigbɛ fã kome ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ moŋ. Shi fɔfɔi heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ miije shishi amɛmiiba kɛkɛ.

english: Why are the coconuts on my trees coming out very small compared to normal ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa kwraa kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni yɔɔ daa lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Coconuts remain small when the tree lacks sufficient nutrients like potassium, suffers from water stress during dry spells, or is crowded by nearby plants competing for soil nutrients.
ga: Kokooi baakã he afee bibioo beni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ potassium, ni nu he haomɔ miipiŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ. aloo he ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ

english: How does the growing of new leaves on my coconut tree affect the way nuts form?
ga: Te baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii tsei anɔ lɛ saa ŋmeii afeemɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Every new leaf on a healthy coconut tree protects and supports a developing fruit bunch at its base. Green leaves act as energy factories, creating the food required for flowers to develop into nuts.
ga: Baa hee fɛɛ baa hee ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ buɔ aduawai niji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ahe ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ. Baai eŋɔlii tsuɔ nii akɛ hewalɛ nitsumɔhe. Ebɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Is it good to cut off lower green leaves from my coconut tree so the nuts get more strength?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooofo shishigbɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli lɛ koni ŋmei lɛ mli awa?

english: No, cutting off green leaves deprives the tree of its ability to make food. You should only trim leaves that have turned completely brown and dry to avoid reducing the tree's fruit yield.
ga: Dabi, baai eŋɔli lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaha tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii. Esa akɛ ofolɔ baai ni efee ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni egbi lɛ pɛ. Bɔni afee ni akaha tsei lɛ ayibii lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do some flower shoots on my coconut tree dry up before opening into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani aduawai lɛ tswaa lɛ?

english: Flower shoots dry up or fail to open when the tree experiences severe heat, extended dry seasons, attack by sap-sucking insects, or a lack of proper nutrients in the soil.
ga: Fɔfɔi ashishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ loo amɛmlijaaa kɛji tso lɛ shɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. be kakadaŋŋ ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ mli Kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuaa loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why does one coconut tree in my farm yield plenty of nuts while another right next to it produces almost nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso kome ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tso kroko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ wooo yibii kwraa.

english: Trees can perform differently due to hidden soil differences, root damage from pests, variations in the seed variety planted, or unequal access to sunlight and underground water.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ afee amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni adu loo hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni anáa lɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: What causes small, young coconuts to fall off the tree before they even grow big?
ga: Mɛni haa akokoobii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: Young button nuts fall mostly due to water shortage during dry periods, poor flower pollination, or insect attacks at the early flowering stage.
ga: Nu ni faaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ titri ni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ laajeɔ. fɔfɔii lɛ amli pollination ni ehiii loo kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ashishijee be mli

english: Does prolonged dry weather cause my coconut tree to stop producing fruit bunches?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa ŋmei tsei kpaɔ aduawai babaoo?

english: Yes, water shortage slows down the emergence of new leaves and fruit bunches, causing the tree to shed young flowers to survive until regular rains return.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni faaa lɛ haaa baai kɛ aduawai heei adalɛ aya hiɛ, ni no haa fɔfɔi bibii lɛ daaa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How long does a coconut tree take before it starts producing its first bunch of fruits?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso woɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ yibii?

english: Dwarf coconut varieties usually begin producing their first fruit bunches within 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties take between 6 to 8 years under proper care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 8 kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce their surface area facing the sun, helping the plant trap moisture and avoid losing too much water during hot dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha ŋwɛi ni kwɛɔ hulu lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: How does planting shade trees help protect my young cocoa plants from dying in the hot sun?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ duɔ lɛ abu mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct heat; shade trees create a cooler environment, shield young cocoa leaves from sun scorch, and retain soil moisture needed for survival.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Buu kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kɛha wala lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rainstorms, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. Using wooden stakes or planting windbreak trees creates a physical defense against strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. make it top heavy Tso tsei ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do yellow spots start showing up on my cassava leaves during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baai anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow spots on cassava leaves are often caused by tiny pests like mites or whiteflies that multiply rapidly in warm weather, sucking sap from the leaves and weakening the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmei baa nɔ lɛ baa. No fɔɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why is it important to plant my seeds immediately after the first major rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting right after early rains ensures seeds get initial moisture while the soil is warm, allowing crops to establish strong root systems before dry spells or heavy downpours occur.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ leebi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná shishijee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni mli wa dani hɔmɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing fruit when the days are very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat sterilizes tomato pollen, preventing fertilization. The plant drops unpollinated flowers to conserve energy until weather conditions become favorable again.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa gbeɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn yellow and drop when water sits in the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Standing water suffocates plant roots by cutting off oxygen, causing root rot and preventing the crop from absorbing essential nutrients from the soil.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds seem to sprout and grow much faster than my crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, native plants adapted to local soil conditions, allowing them to absorb sunlight and water faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ hulu la kɛ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ.

english: If my government-supplied fertilizer arrives late, will applying a double dose make my crops catch up faster?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛmaje lɛ ba sɛɛ Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ toi enyɔ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ oya?

english: Over-fertilizing late in a crop's growth cycle can burn plant roots and damage yields. Fertilizer must be applied in controlled amounts at specific stages to be effective.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akudɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bigger when I plant cowpeas in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa waa kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, providing neighboring crops like yam with natural nutrients for better growth.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmeii, naa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the surrounding soil moist while the cocoa establishes its roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seed immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a heat spell or a long dry gap. Planting too early causes seeds to sprout and then die from lack of moisture before the main rainy season fully begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi kwraa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green foliage and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni etsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their flowers before forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets excessively hot or when plants experience dry soil, which stresses the plant and forces it to shed flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kpe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by these insects.
