ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ

english: What is causing small, ragged holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi kaabaji baa lɛ nɔ

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by diamondback moth caterpillars or leaf beetles eating the leaves, which can be managed by early handpicking or applying neem leaf extracts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ji diamondback loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabe baai amli lɛ baa. Abaanyɛ akwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ nine ni akɛbaatsu nii mra lɛ nɔ. loo okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu atsu nii

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and naturally fall off, and the main stem base expands noticeably.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni tso wulu lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baagbɛ eshwa waa

english: Why are heavy rains washing away the dirt around my newly planted yam mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ muji ni ebɔle wɔhe lɛ kɛyaa lɛ? Mi sweet potato ni midu ehee lɛ?

english: Unprotected soil on yam mounds easily erodes under intense rainfall; planting cover crops or adding mulch around the base helps anchor the soil and protect the seed yams from sunlight exposure.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni abuuu he ni yɔɔ sweet potato gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shishi. Mulch loo mulch ni aduɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebuɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he.

english: Why do my harvested onions start rotting shortly after I put them in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ beni mikɛwoɔ nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Onions rot in storage if they are stored before their necks fully dry out or if they are kept in a damp area without good airflow, allowing fungus to grow.
ga: Sabolai fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto dani tsitsii lɛ agbi kwraa. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Why do my plantain bunches ripen all at once before I can bring them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ shikome dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains release a natural gas as they begin to mature that speeds up the ripening of neighboring fruit, so storing harvested bunches in a hot, enclosed room causes them all to soften together rapidly.
ga: Plantains lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji gas lɛ kpo beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwereɔ lɛ, ni no haa yibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ shwereɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ wo tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni nɔ ko eha nɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛ fɛɛ amɛfee blɛoo oya.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rain patterns keep changing every year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa? Akɛni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ daa afi hewɔ lɛ

english: Rather than planting with the very first light rain, wait until the soil is consistently moist down to your finger's depth for a few days. Planting too early during false rains can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up before the main rains arrive.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baadu nii lɛ, mɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛyashɛ onine mli gbii fioo komɛi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni ji amale mli lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi dani nugbɔshiimɔ titri lɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops wilt and roll up their leaves in the afternoon even when the soil still has some water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the strong sun to prevent water from evaporating too quickly from inside its leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ́ abɔle baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ ji koni nu akajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: My cocoa pods are turning black and decaying, but people in my village say it is caused by a spell—is there a real cause for this?
ga: Mikookoo ŋmɔji lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi. Shi mɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ kɛɔ akɛ ŋmiŋmi ko ji nɔ ni kɛba—ani yiŋtoo diɛŋtsɛ ko yɛ ni ha enɛ ba?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a microscopic fungus, not a spell or bad luck. The fungus thrives in wet, dark environments, so clearing weeds and pruning tree branches to let in sunshine and air will stop the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛ ŋmei bibioo ko mli. Jeee ajwamaŋbɔɔ loo shweremɔ ni ehiii. Fungi yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ duŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei aniji ni afoɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akpa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is running short on soil nutrients like nitrogen. The plant naturally moves its remaining food to the young leaves at the top to keep growing, letting the older bottom leaves fade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ yaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I space my seeds far apart when putting more seeds close together seems like it would give me more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala midumɔwui lɛ amli? Etamɔ nɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaawo yibii babaoo.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak plants with small fruits. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food to produce a larger harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Yam plants make food for their underground tubers using sunlight caught by their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight, which allows the plant to send more energy down to grow a big tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ hulu la ni tswaa ebaa lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii ehaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences shock from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of insects like bees to pollinate them. Keeping the soil moist with mulch helps protect the flowers so they can form peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na shoofeemɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa tamɔ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants spend all their energy growing tall green leaves instead of flowers. Balanced plant food helps the crop switch its energy from growing leaves to growing fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Tso niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds instead of planting seeds saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected to resist common local diseases and withstand dry spells. Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strength over time and usually yield much less crop than the original harvest.
ga: Ahala dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ni amɛte shi amɛwo hɔmɔ shihilɛi. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli. ni bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa lɛ faaa kwraa fe klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ

english: How does chemical fertilizer actually help my crops grow bigger and faster?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛ oya lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer acts like concentrated food that dissolves when wet. The plant roots drink up this nutrient water to build strong stems and leaves much faster than relying only on the natural nutrients already in the soil.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ shi kɛji edɔ. Tsei shishifãi nuɔ nu ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ nɛɛ koni amɛkɛma tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni wa oya fe ni amɛkɛ amɛhe aaafɔ̃ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why do most of us in Ghana only plant crops during the rainy season instead of all year round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔteŋ mɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ be mli pɛ, shi jeee afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Most crops need steady water to germinate and grow. Since many farms rely entirely on rainfall rather than artificial irrigation systems, planting is timed with the rainy season so the soil stays moist naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ pii biɔ nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔji babaoo kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ kwraa fe nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu ni akɛfee lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, atoɔ be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it possible for me to plant and harvest crops three times in a single year on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ madu ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ yɛ afi kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, but only if you use fast-maturing crop varieties, have access to reliable irrigation during dry months, and properly replenish soil nutrients with fertilizer or manure between plantings.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi kɛji akɛ okɛ tsei srɔtoi ni daa oya tsu nii pɛ. Na nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni okɛ niyenii ni sa afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ dumɔ be mli.

english: How can I continue growing crops even after the major rains stop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maya nɔ madu tsei beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa po lɛ?

english: You can practice off-season farming by using water sources like shallow wells, rivers, or simple drip irrigation, and by choosing drought-tolerant crop varieties or quick-maturing vegetables.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu jɛɛhei tamɔ ŋshɔi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, faai, loo nu ni hoɔ ni shwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii kɛtsu okwaayeli ni be lɛ bɛ mli lɛ he nii. kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa loo aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ ni ahalaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops seem to suffer from more diseases during the rainy season than during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni helai yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rain creates high humidity and wet leaves, which are the exact conditions fungi and bacteria need to grow, multiply, and spread quickly from plant to plant.
ga: Nugbɔ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ adara, amɛshwere, ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya kɛjɛ tso kome mli kɛya tso kroko mli.

english: What simple steps can I take to protect my crops from rotting when it rains too heavily?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkafite kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo?

english: You can create proper drainage channels so water does not pool around roots, weed regularly to improve air flow around plants, and space your crops widely enough so leaves dry quickly after rain.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee gbɛi ni sa ni nu tsɔɔ nɔ koni nu akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa koni kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle tsei lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ, ni oha he ni aduɔ lɛ lɛ afee shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni baai lɛ agbi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: Can plant diseases spread from my neighbor's farm to mine through rainwater?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli kɛya shika tsuru tsei amli kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu nɔ?

english: Yes, splashing rain drops and flowing water runoff can carry disease spores and bacteria from infected plants in nearby fields straight onto your crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni jɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ aya onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What are the main stages I need to follow from planting to harvest to keep my crops healthy?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii titrii ni esa akɛ mafee kɛjɛ dumɔ mli kɛyashi kpamɔ mli koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Successful farming involves three key stages: proper land preparation and planting, ongoing crop maintenance (weeding, watering, and disease monitoring), and timely harvesting followed by safe storage.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yeɔ omanye lɛ biɔ nibii titrii etɛ: shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kpakpa kɛ dumɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ (jwɛi ni ajieɔ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, kɛ helai akwɛmɔ) kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ji nibii ni akɛtoɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my plants grow very tall and leafy during the rains but fail to produce good fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai yɛ nugbɔ be mli shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Excess rain combined with too much nitrogen in the soil causes a plant to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of developing flowers and fruit. Heavy rains can also wash away other essential nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fataa he lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa waa lɛ.

english: If I plant crops continuously throughout the year, will my soil become too weak to produce food?
ga: Kɛji midu tsei be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ tsɔ ni ekɛ niyenii baaha?

english: Yes, continuous planting without breaks depletes soil nutrients quickly. To keep the soil strong, you should rotate different crop types—like switching between maize and beans—and regularly add compost or fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni yaa nɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he lɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite oya. koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee shiŋŋ Esa akɛ otsake ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni oootsake. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he daa.

english: Which crops in Ghana are best suited for planting multiple times in a year if I have a reliable water source?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ shii abɔ yɛ afi mli kɛji miyɛ nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ?

english: Short-cycle vegetables like tomatoes, pepper, okra, garden eggs, and leafy greens mature quickly in two to three months, making them ideal for multiple plantings within a single year.
ga: Aduawai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, okra, abɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔi, kɛ ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui babaoo yɛ afi kome mli.

english: Why are some of my cassava plants growing very big while others planted on the same day remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi daraa waa shi ekrokomɛi ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Crops planted at the same time can grow at different speeds due to slight natural variations in the cutting's strength, soil nutrients, or water access in different spots.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ baanyɛ adara oyaiyeli srɔtoi. Enɛ jɛ adebɔɔ mli tsakemɔi fioo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ni anáa yɛ hei srɔtoi

english: Why do suckers growing from the same plantain tree develop into different sizes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ dumɔwu kome mli lɛ daa kɛyaa dalɛi srɔtoi amli lɛ?

english: The mother plantain tree feeds its suckers unevenly, usually directing more nutrients to the first or strongest sucker, causing them to grow at different rates.
ga: Dumɔwu nyɛ lɛ yeɔ eshishifãi lɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be. Bei pii lɛ, amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ haa klɛŋklɛŋ loo nɔ ni he wa fe fɛɛ ni nuɔ nu lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ.

english: Why do tomato seeds taken from the very same tomato fruit grow into plants of different strengths?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tomato henɔ kome mli lɛ daa kɛfeɔ tsei ni amɛhe wa yɛ srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Seeds within the same fruit have natural variations in their energy reserves, causing some to sprout faster and absorb nutrients better than others.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ aduawai kome mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ srɔtoi ni amɛtoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi.

english: How do I select the right seeds from my maize harvest to keep for the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni sa kɛjɛ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli koni mikɛto kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Always choose large, healthy seeds from your strongest plants and separate them from the tiny or weak seeds, as strong seeds carry the vigor needed for a good harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ ahala dumɔwui wuji ni mli wa kɛjɛ tsei ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. ni ogbala amɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui bibii loo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ateŋ Enɛ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha kpamɔ kpakpa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant small or weak yam setts together with my big ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mi-batch ni da lɛ duɔ sweet potato bibioo loo nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ?

english: Large setts sprout aggressively and can easily block sunlight and consume nutrients meant for smaller setts, leaving the small ones weak and underdeveloped.
ga: Mɛi wuji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya, ni hulu lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya. ni amɛye niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha fãji bibii lɛ feɔ fãji bibii ni Egbɔjɔ ni edarako

english: Should I sort my pepper seedlings by size before transplanting them into the field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahala pepper dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ amɛdalɛ naa dani mikɛ amɛ awo he kroko?

english: Yes, sorting seedlings by size and planting similar sizes together ensures that larger seedlings do not overshadow and steal nutrients from smaller ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ato dumɔwui lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ naa ni adu tsei ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe lɛ ekomekomei lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui wuji lɛ akafee nɔ ko ni amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ amli.

english: Is it helpful to separate big seedlings from small ones into different beds when moving them from the nursery?
ga: Dumɔwui wuji kɛ dumɔwui bibii amli gbalamɔ kɛmiiya saatsoi srɔtoi anɔ. Kɛji akɛ oshi gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ ani sɛɛnamɔ ko yɛ he?

english: Separating big seedlings from small ones allows you to give extra care and attention to the smaller group so they can catch up without competing with bigger plants.
ga: Dumɔwui wuji ni oootse kɛjɛ bibii amli lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohaa kui bibii lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ hiɛdɔɔ babaoo koni amɛya nɔ amɛhi shi ni amɛkɛ tsei wuji lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Why is it necessary to pull out tiny extra seedlings when too many sprout close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie dumɔwui bibii kɛjɛ mli be mli ni dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Removing extra or smaller seedlings gives the remaining plants enough room, air, sunlight, and soil nutrients to grow strong and yield better crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni fa fe nine loo ni faaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ naa he ko, kɔɔyɔɔ, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do maize cobs in the same farm row end up with different sizes at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ dalɛi srɔtoi kɛ́ akpa lɛ?

english: Individual maize plants compete for localized soil moisture and nutrients, causing some plants to produce large cobs while nearby ones produce smaller cobs.
ga: Abɛi tso fɛɛ tso kɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu pɔtɛɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: What happens to my smaller crops if I let bigger, faster-growing crops grow right next to them?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji miŋmɛ gbɛ ni tso ko ni da ni daa oya lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ emasɛi?

english: Bigger plants capture most of the sunlight with their larger leaves and drink most of the water, which starves the smaller crops and keeps them from growing big.
ga: Tsei wuji kɛ amɛbaai wuji lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la lɛ babaoo ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ehaaa amɛdara.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because direct heat from the sun burns their soft leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Keeping shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides shelter for young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa he ko ni amɛhiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does using a tractor to plow my land help my crops grow better than just clearing with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ traktɔ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii?

english: Mechanized plowing breaks up packed, hard soil, making it easier for plant roots to grow deep and absorb water and nutrients. It also turns over weeds and mixes them into the soil as organic matter, creating a soft, rich environment for seeds to sprout.
ga: Tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛha tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛ baa mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Etsɔɔ jwɛi hu ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli futuɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ehaa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Yams need loose, deep, and well-drained soil to stretch down and form large tubers. Building mounds provides soft soil for the yam to expand freely without hitting hard ground and prevents excess water from sitting around the seed yam and causing rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛgbala ni efee ŋmeii wuji. Gɔŋ ni afee lɛ haa sweet potatoes ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ shwereɔ oya ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. ni etsĩ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekabɔle Yam dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for green leaf growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the younger upper leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛya baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi, ni ji bibii lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why do I get very small cassava tubers when I plant my stem cuttings close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi bibii waa nɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight each other underground for limited space, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing cuttings properly gives each plant enough room and soil nutrients to form big, healthy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko ni faaa, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ tso lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a family of crops that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground through their roots. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen remains in the soil to naturally feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ he. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I wait for the main rains to settle before sowing my maize seeds in the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ lɛ dani madu ŋmãa yɛ be ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Planting after just one early rain can trap seeds in hot ground if the rain pauses for weeks, causing the seeds to dry out and die. Waiting for consistent rain ensures the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ dumɔwui yɛ hei ni edɔɔ lɛ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat or a sudden lack of water. Under extreme heat or dry stress, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa trukaa lɛ kpe amɛ. Yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛha amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young corn leaves with tiny droppings in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the corn plant during the day and feeds on the soft inner leaves. If left unchecked, it destroys the growing point and stops the plant from developing proper cobs.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni eyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Efiteɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni sa.

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal food, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. When weeds take over, your main crop goes hungry and cannot produce full, healthy yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ ye Oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ nɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye bo ni enyɛŋ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted nearby to protect them from burning and drying out in their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ he yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: How do I know if my soil lacks nutrients before I start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had pale or yellowish leaves, or yielded tiny fruits, your soil is likely low on nutrients. Testing the soil or observing weak weed growth can also signal that fertilizer is needed.
ga: Kɛji onibii ni okɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ewoɔ aduawai bibii lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa loo jwɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal attack that thrives in wet, overly humid conditions. It spreads when trees are too shaded, planted too close together, or not pruned to let air flow through.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo fe nine yɔɔ mli. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ tso lɛ nɔ tsɔ tsɔ. ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo afolɔko mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a natural defence mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves to expose less surface area to the hot sun, which prevents water from evaporating too quickly from inside the leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe fioo. Enɛ haaa nu akajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree when it seems to be growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso niji krokomɛi amli yɛ be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that waste energy and block sunlight. Trimming them allows the tree to focus its strength on growing bigger pods while improving air circulation to prevent disease.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni fiteɔ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa lɛ. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ maa ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni helai akamɔ mɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds very close together so I can get more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This makes all of them grow thin and weak, resulting in a lower total harvest than properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa shi fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding over-fertilization helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ajie ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Cocoa pods are fully ripe when their outer skin changes completely from green to yellow, or from red to bright orange-yellow. Harvesting green pods reduces the quality and flavor of the beans during fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa kɛtee ŋmɔŋ. loo kɛjɛ etsuru nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔŋ-ɔranji ni mli tse nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ni akpaa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ahe fɛo kɛ amɛhe ŋɔɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep roots that absorb water and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early stops them from stealing the food your main crops need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Can I grow cassava and maize together on the same plot of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows fast and is harvested in a few months, leaving plenty of room and sunlight for the cassava to mature slowly later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa gbɛ babaoo kɛ hulu la haa ŋmei lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: How often should I water my tomato crops during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Vegetable crops like tomatoes need steady moisture; watering them deeply every other day helps the roots grow deep into the soil rather than light surface watering every day.
ga: Aduawai tsei tamɔ tomato he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ daa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli jogbaŋŋ daa gbi kroko lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, mo shwie nɔ ɔ nɔ nu fioo daa ligbi.

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to build healthy leaves and big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai agboi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight; they need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to keep them cool while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo.

english: Is it good practice to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows plant-specific pests to build up in the field over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava shows it is mature when the lower stem leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the main stem starts to crack.
ga: Kasava tsɔɔ akɛ eda kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why are small insects attacking my pepper plants, and how can I stop them simple way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua mi-pepper tsei lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ?

english: Pests attack tender leaves for food; spraying a simple mixture made from crushed neem tree leaves and water can naturally repel many common field insects.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa baai bibii koni amɛye niyenii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo Akɛ neem baai ni atswa kɛ nu fee, ni ebaanyɛ eshwie kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Weeds are hardy wild plants that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, which is why clearing them early gives your crops a fair chance.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie lɛ mra lɛ. Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa.

english: Should I cut off some of the extra side branches growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo niji ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Removing the tiny side shoots helps the plant direct all its energy and food into making bigger, healthier fruits instead of growing extra leaves.
ga: Ni aaaŋɔ tso lɛ fã bibioo lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ baai krokomɛi

english: Saved seeds lose their ability to grow if they absorb moisture or get too warm during storage, so they must be completely dried and kept sealed tightly in a cool place.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nyɛŋ adara kɛji amɛmu ŋmɔtɔ loo amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi kwraa ni akɛwo he ko ni mli ejɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize turn yellow and stay small even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɔ shi bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Maize needs key nutrients like nitrogen from the soil to stay green and grow tall. Rain provides water, but if the soil lacks food, the plant cannot grow healthy leaves or stalks without added fertilizer.
ga: Niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmãa. Bɔni afee ni tsei afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara lɛ, nugbɔ haa nu, shi kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ baai loo amɛshishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli.

english: How exactly does adding fertilizer to my farm help my maize produce bigger ears?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni ehaa toi lɛ daraa?

english: Fertilizer acts as concentrated food for crops. It gives maize essential elements like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, which allow the plant to build strong stalks and fill out full, heavy cobs.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni mli wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa ŋmãa nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni wa ni eyiɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so my crops can take it up properly?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer is most effective when applied to moist soil during periods of active growth—typically a few weeks after the seeds sprout and again just before the plants begin to flower.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ miida waa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ otsii enyɔ komɛi asɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Ni ekoŋŋ dani tso lɛ baabɔi fɔfɔi.

english: Why do some farmers harvest a lot of maize from a small field while I get very little from my large land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kpaɔ ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli yɛ be mli ni mi lɛ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa fioo ko nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ wulu ko nɔ lɛ?

english: High yields depend more on crop management than land size. Using quality seeds, spacing plants correctly, and applying fertilizer at the right times allows each plant to yield more maize on less land.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ nɔ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Gbɛ ni ja ni ka tsei ateŋ Ni kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso fɛɛ tso baanyɛ awo ŋmãa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ fioo nɔ.

english: Why do my maize seeds sometimes fail to grow after I plant them in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if the soil is too dry, if they are buried too deep where air cannot reach them, or if the seeds themselves are damaged or poor quality.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he. aloo kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ efite loo ehiii kwraa

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same plot every season lower my harvest over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Maize heavy-feeds on specific nutrients in the ground. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of those nutrients unless you rotate crops or nourish the soil.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nakai niyenii lɛ. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ niyenii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my young maize plants so early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmãa bibii tsei amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from young maize plants before the crops have a chance to grow strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli. Dani tso lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni ekwɛ̃ shishifãi ni mli wa

english: What causes my maize plants to fall over easily when strong winds blow through the field?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize falls over when root systems are shallow or weak. Planting seeds at the proper depth and providing nutrients helps the plant build deep roots and a thick, sturdy stem.
ga: Abɛi baagbee baai lɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo ebɛ hewalɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa ni akɛ niyenii haa lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: Why do some of my maize cobs have missing kernels or empty spots on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ekomɛi amli ŋmeii lɛ elaaje loo amɛhe efee efolo lɛ?

english: Empty spots happen when the tassels fail to pollinate all the silks on the cob, which often occurs if the plants suffer from severe heat or lack of water during flowering.
ga: He ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ tsɔne lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee siliki fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsɔne lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully ready to be harvested for selling as dry grain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmã lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa koni ahɔ̃ɔ akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi?

english: Maize is ready for dry harvest when the husk outer leaves turn completely brown and papery, and the kernels become hard with a visible dark mark where they attach to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni egbi beni ŋmeii lɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni amɛfee tamɔ wolo lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni anaa ni akɛkpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains turn into powder and get full of holes when stored in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ feɔ powder ni eyɛ bu kɛji akɛ akɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those small holes are caused by tiny insects called grain weevils that eat the inside of the maize. If you dry your maize thoroughly until the grains are very hard and store them in airtight bags, the insects cannot survive to ruin your harvest.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ corn weevils ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai bu bibii lɛ baa. Kɛji ogbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, Kplukai nyɛŋ afite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I easily know that my harvested corn is dry enough to put into storage sacks without it rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛwo kotokui amli ni egbooo?

english: You can test your corn by pressing a grain hard with your thumb or biting it. If it leaves a deep dent or feels soft, moisture is still inside and will cause mold; dry corn should feel glass-hard and make a sharp cracking sound when bitten.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ŋmãa lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ ni okɛ oshishifa lɛ baanyɛ nɔ waa lɛ nɔ. loo ŋmãa ni ŋmɔɔ Kɛji ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ba loo enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii yɛ mli lolo ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmeii aba. Esa akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ afee nɔ ni wa tamɔ glase ni efee gbee ni tswaa kɛji akɛ amɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly like sticks during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ tamɔ tsei tsei yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during intense heat as a natural defense to stop water from escaping into the air. It is the plant's way of saving water, but if the leaves stay rolled up early in the morning, it means the crops need water immediately.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni nu akajo foi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu toɔ tsei ahe. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo leebi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia tso lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow very long and thin without making big tubers when I plant them under shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni efeɔ mlɛo ni efeee bulbs wuji beni miduɔ yɛ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Yam plants need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food. When planted in deep shade, the vine stretches high searching for sunlight, using up energy that should have gone into growing a thick, heavy tuber in the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Wein tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛtao hulu la. Ekɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii koni akɛwo bulbs ni mli wa ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the base of a plant usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen fertilizer. The plant takes whatever nutrients are left in its lower leaves and moves them to the top to keep new leaves alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkwɛ baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This feeds the soil naturally and helps your maize grow bigger without needing as much expensive artificial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua o-abele lɛ ni edara ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa afee.

english: Why do caterpillars attack and eat the fresh center leaves of my young maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutua ni amɛye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai heei lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide from the hot sun inside the cool funnel of the plant during the day and feed at night. Checking your farm early in the morning allows you to spot them early and apply ash, neem, or recommended chemicals before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ tsei akutsei ni mli ejɔ mli yɛ gbi mli, ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii gbɛkɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni ona amɛ mra. ni okɛ sũ, neem loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii dani ofite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds kill my young crops so fast if I do not clear them in the first few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi gbeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ oya kɛji mijieee amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young crops are weak and grow slowly at first. Fast-growing weeds steal the sunlight, soil nutrients, and water away from your crops' small roots, effectively starving the crop before it gets a chance to establish itself.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaada blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ni nu shĩɔ tso lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ amli, ni ehaa tso lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ dani enáa hegbɛ ni eda lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the flowers stay attached long enough to grow into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ muji ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my maize crops produce very small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu bibioo kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for root space, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant its own spaced-out hole allows the roots to spread wide and gather enough food to grow large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná shishifãi lɛ ahe gbɛ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebu ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo ni ebuaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn and dry out easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them provides a natural umbrella, keeping the soil cool and moist while the young trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee shade yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and stop producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves, or by viral infections spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves healthy so the plant can produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ mli waa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why does my maize turn light green or yellow and grow very slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni edaa blɛoo waa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer can restore the plant's healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground after harvest, they naturally fertilize the soil for the next crop of maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛbaaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the plants grow very tall stems and green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni kɛlɛ waa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmei tso lɛ baato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants must fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space ensures it gets the nourishment needed to grow large cobs.
ga: Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Esa akɛ tsei ni miida lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni enáa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed for a single strong harvest. If you replant the seeds saved from a hybrid crop, the second generation will yield much less and grow irregularly compared to buying fresh certified hybrid seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha kpamɔ kome ni mli wa. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ hybrid dumɔwui amli lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa shi kwraa ni ebaada yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ akɛto hybrid dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruits during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when temperatures are too high or water is scarce to save energy and survive. Providing consistent water and light mulch around the roots during heat waves helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi lɛ bɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hottest part of the afternoon even if I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Leaf drooping during intense heat is a plant's natural defense mechanism. The leaves fold down to reduce water loss from the sun, and they will perk back up once the day cools down.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ be mli lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni hulu la lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ edɔ.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam tubers are ready when the vine leaves naturally dry up and turn yellow to brown at the end of the rainy season. This shows that the plant has finished moving food into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen nutrients or the ground is waterlogged, which stops the roots from absorbing food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow tall with lots of green leaves but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, or when plants are spaced too close together, the cassava puts all its energy into leaf growth instead of building fat tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha ebaai lɛ akwɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitso ni yɔɔ fɔ

english: Why are my vegetable plants wilting during the afternoon sun even though I watered them this morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ miiho ŋmɛnɛ gbɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha amɛ ŋmɛnɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During very hot afternoons, water evaporates from the leaves faster than the roots can drink it up. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out, usually recovering by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my crops in neat rows instead of scattering seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in rows gives each plant the right amount of space to get sunlight and nutrients, makes weeding much faster, and prevents plants from competing directly with each other.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ená hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ haa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yaa oya kwraa. ni etsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. Planting them refreshes the soil with free fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Tsei nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, which feed on sap and spread plant viruses that stop normal leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni yeɔ tsofa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Enɛ haa baa lɛ shweremɔ ni sa lɛ kpaɔ.

english: Why do my green tomatoes develop dark, sunken rotten spots right at the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, which often happens when soil watering is irregular during hot weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ ejaaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines get brown spots and die off before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early leaf drying is often caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads in warm, wet weather and weakens the vine before the yam tubers can fully grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ kɛ baa lɛ gbimɔ mra. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni eha wain tso lɛ agbɔjɔ dani sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if there are not enough tiny midges (pollinating insects) in the farm, or if the tree experiences extreme drought stress and drops flowers to save energy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji amɛyɛ bibii. Nibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa (pollinators) lɛ faaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ ni naa wa kpe ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwie shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Plantain roots are shallow by nature, but trees fall easily when underground pests like banana weevils or nematodes attack the roots and corm, destroying the plant's support system.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli. Shi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ banana ŋmeii loo nematodes tutua amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Efiteɔ tsei lɛ ayelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there is direct sunlight on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that dry out easily under intense sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them provides living shade that protects the cocoa until it grows stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni enáa hewalɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dried grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating in the heat, keeps the soil cool, prevents weeds from taking over, and slowly breaks down into rich plant food.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la kɛji akɛ edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa ni fiofio lɛ efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy foliage. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's sap, or by a viral disease spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or insect attacks. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from pests helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with tiny yields when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they fight over light, water, and plant food in the soil. Proper spacing allows every plant to get enough sunlight and nutrients to produce big fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei fɛɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Yam leaves need to catch sunlight to make food that grows large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they get full sun and stay safe from fungal rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii beni aduɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it harmful to grow maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ abaadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop every season drains the same soil nutrients repeatedly and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the soil. Rotating crops gives the soil a break and starves out pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be Be lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ hoɔ shii abɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ gbalaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my crops right before a big downpour of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes fertilizer away off the surface before the crop roots have a chance to drink it, wasting your money and polluting nearby streams.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ. Efiteɔ oshika ni efiteɔ faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 and 12 months after planting, which you can tell when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off, leaving a woody stem, or by carefully digging up one root to check its size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ole be ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Tso ni eshwɛ lɛ ji tso. aloo kɛtsɔ shishifã kome ni oootsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my bagged mushroom compost is ready for me to open it so the mushrooms can grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-baagi ni mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ mli lɛ efee klalo akɛ magbele mli koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: When the white fungus (mycelium) has completely spread throughout the dark compost bag and turned it almost fully white, it means the substrate is fully colonized and ready to be opened for mushrooms to sprout.
ga: Enɛ ji be mli ni ŋmei yɛŋ (mycelium) lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmei kotoku ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni eshwɛ fioo ni ebaatsɔ eyɛŋ kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ kwraa, ni efee klalo akɛ abaagbele koni ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my oyster mushrooms need a cool, shaded, and moist room to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oyster ŋmeii lɛ he hiaa he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Unlike green crops, mushrooms do not need direct sunlight to produce food. High moisture and cool shade keep the delicate mushroom caps from drying out, allowing them to grow plump and fresh.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ tsei eŋɔli lɛ, ŋmeii biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ akagbi. Ha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ehee.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop curling up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl during intense heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and prevent water from evaporating out of the plant.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the surrounding shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ hulutsoo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under harsh sunlight. They require taller shade crops like plantains to shield them and keep the surrounding air cool and moist during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo babaoo, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets too hot or water levels in the soil drop sharply, causing stress that prevents the flowers from pollinating and setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ba shi oya. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni tsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkawo ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwo yibii lɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. The corn plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the top to support fresh new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua dalɛ hee.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing huge green leaves above ground but producing very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cassava spend all its energy growing leafy stems above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below ground.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa ŋmei fiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛkwɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: If pepper plants lack water, their leaves wilt and droop during the day; if they receive too much water, their roots suffocate and the leaves turn pale yellow before falling off.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ pepper tso lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse dani amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: How do weeds growing near my cowpea crop slow down its growth?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ahe lɛ aha amɛdalɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil food away from your cowpea plants, forcing your crop to struggle for survival instead of producing strong branches and pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsina tsei amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni ehi shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo niji kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why are small holes appearing on my okro leaves, making them turn brown at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ okra baai lɛ anɔ, ni no haa amɛshishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Small holes mean insect pests are eating the leaves. When leaves get damaged, the crop loses its ability to catch sunlight and produce the food it needs to grow healthy pods.
ga: Buu bibii tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ baai lɛ miiye. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ fite lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛhe hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. This usually happens when the soil is worn out or after heavy rains wash away nutrients.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ejie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my growing tomatoes turn dark and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni midu lɛ shishi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering while the fruit is developing, causing the skin at the bottom to collapse.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo awoɔ lɛ nu be fɛɛ be be mli ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ miida lɛ. Enɛ haa hewolo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall stems but leave me with very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much water or excess nitrogen early in its life, it spends all its energy growing big leaves and tall stems instead of storing food in its underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei ná nu babaoo loo nitrogen ni fa fe nine yɛ eshihilɛ mli mra Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbaa baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii kakadaji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the stem without turning into any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when temperatures are too high or when there is sudden water stress. The plant sacrifices its flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Pepper tsei baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Tsei kɛ fɔfɔii shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Young cocoa pods drop off during a natural process called cherelle wilt. It happens when the tree does not have enough shade, water, or nutrients to feed every pod growing on it.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherel wilting lɛ mli. Ebaa kɛji tso ko bɛ hulutsoo, nu, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my groundnut plant push its flowers down into the soil after they bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers bloom above ground to get pollinated, but the stem then bends downward to bury the growing tip so the actual peanut pod can develop safely hidden underground.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee pollination. Mohu ɔ, tso ɔ shwieɔ si konɛ e pu tso ɔ yi mi nɛ ngɛ wae ɔ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my garden egg plants stop making new flowers during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi heei yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli kɛ́ egbi lɛ?

english: Garden eggs slow down their growth and stop producing flowers during dry periods to conserve water, saving their strength until regular moisture or irrigation returns.
ga: Abɔɔ mli wɔji lɛ daalɛ baa shi ni amɛkpaa fɔfɔii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛbu nu he. Ehiɛɔ ehewalɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves high up toward the sun. Capturing maximum sunlight allows the plant to produce extra energy, which goes back down into expanding the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Hulu la ni anáa bɔ ni aaanyɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ kroko. Enɛ baaku esɛɛ kɛya shi koni ekɛgbala tso lɛ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain trees split into ribbons when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves naturally split along their veins during high winds so the breeze can pass straight through, preventing the main stem from snapping or the whole plant from falling over.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ atsɔ mli. Tsi tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my cowpea plants curling up and covered in sticky black dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ diŋ ehà amɛhe lɛ?

english: Small insects called aphids gather on the undersides of the leaves to suck out sap. They leave behind a sugary liquid that attracts black mold, which blocks sunlight from feeding the plant.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ aphids lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Amɛshiɔ nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar ni gbalaa ŋmeii diji kɛbaa amɛsɛɛ. ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekabote tsei lɛ amli ni eha amɛ niyenii

english: What is a greenhouse, and how can it help my vegetables grow better than planting directly in the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe ni amɛduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: A greenhouse is a plastic or glass shelter that protects crops like tomatoes and peppers from heavy rains, scorching sun, and destructive pests. It keeps temperature and moisture steady, allowing crops to grow faster, suffer less disease, and produce higher yields.
ga: Greenhouses ji plastic loo glase shĩai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ tomato kɛ shitoi ahe, kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi daa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya. helai fioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight and harsh dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava next to them acts like a living umbrella, providing soft shade and retaining soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava, yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaafee tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are some of my pepper seeds failing to grow into seedlings after I bury them in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ dumɔwui beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need a warm, moist environment and must not be buried too deeply. If buried too far down, flooded with too much water, or planted in hard soil, the seed rots before it can sprout into a healthy plant.
ga: Dumɔwui hia shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. ni esaaa akɛ afuɔ lɛ tsɔ Kɛji afu lɛ tsɔ Nu babaoo loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is weak and needs fertilizer before I start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nii dani mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: If your previous crop was pale, small, or grew very slowly, your soil is likely out of nutrients. Testing the soil or observing hard, dusty earth with poor weed growth shows that adding manure, compost, or fertilizer is needed to nourish the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ mli tse, amɛji bibii, loo amɛmiida blɛoo waa lɛ, ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa loo shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni sũ yɔɔ nɔ ni jwɛi ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant cassava in the exact same spot on my land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?
