english: Planting cassava repeatedly in the same spot strips the soil of the specific nutrients cassava needs and allows diseases to live on in the dirt. Rotating with beans or groundnuts gives the soil a rest, fixes nitrogen back into the dirt, and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Kassava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa cassava lɛ. ni ehaa helai hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hejɔɔmɔ. Nitrogen ni akɛbaaku sɛɛ awo sũ lɛ mli ni akumɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: Why do weeds seem to sprout and grow much faster than my planted crops whenever the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants built to drink up rain and soil nutrients instantly. Because they grow faster than crop seeds, you must clear weeds early so they do not steal the water, light, and food your crops need.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni ama koni amɛmu nugbɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya fe dumɔwui. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha amɛkaju nu, kane, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my green maize crops turning pale yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer or is being attacked by pests like fall armyworms. Adding nitrogen to the soil and checking under leaves for caterpillars will help bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-ŋmã lɛ kɛha nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms miitutua lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How often should I water my vegetable crop during the hot dry season to keep it from drying out?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛkagbi?

english: Vegetables need consistent water, typically once a day early in the morning or late in the afternoon during the dry season. Deep watering directly at the roots prevents moisture from evaporating quickly in the midday sun.
ga: Nu he miihia aduawai daa. Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ lɛ shikome daa gbi leebi loo shwane yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ aya oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why should I cut off some of the lower leaves and small branches from my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi kɛ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ pepper tso lɛ mli

english: Trimming lower leaves allows sunlight and air to reach the plant, which keeps fungal diseases from developing. It also forces the plant to send its food directly into growing larger peppers instead of wasting energy on excess leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akaba. Enyɛɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ hu nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii aya ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yam tubers so they do not rot underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Yam tubers are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines on top of the soil dry up and turn yellow. Leaving tubers in the ground after the vine dies exposes them to heat and underground pests that cause rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ mli beni wain tso lɛ egbo sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dying shortly after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile like human babies and suffer from heat shock under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting their tender leaves.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ abifabii, ni amɛyeɔ amanehulu yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I nurse my pepper seeds in a protected seedbed before planting them in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he dani madu yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Tiny pepper seeds produce delicate sprouts that can easily be washed away by heavy rains or eaten by insects. A seedbed protects them during their early growth stage until they are strong enough to survive direct weather conditions.
ga: pepper dumɔwui bibii Ewoɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya loo ŋmeii yeɔ amɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ buɔ amɛhe yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee bei amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo be lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my young crops need shade trees when mature trees grow in open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni edara lɛ miida yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow root systems that cannot drink deep soil water yet. Shade trees cool the ground temperature and prevent the hot sun from scorching young foliage while their root systems develop.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ anu shikpɔŋ nu ni mli kwɔ lolo. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛtsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashã baai bibii lɛ beni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: If weeds grow right next to my young maize from the start, why can't I just clear them later before harvest?
ga: Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ emasɛi Mi-baby corn kɛjɛ shishijee Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mafo jwɛi sɛɛ mli dani akpa?

english: Weeds growing alongside your crops from an early age steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from the crops. This early competition permanently stunts the crop's growth, which cannot be undone even if you clear the weeds later.
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Nɛkɛ mra be mli akaŋshii nɛɛ haaa tsei adalɛ aya hiɛ kwraa. Anyɛɛɛ ajie enɛ kɛji akɛ okɛ jwɛi shwie nɔ sɛɛ mli po.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava and maize together in the same farm at the same time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping them works well because maize grows fast and matures in a few months, while cassava grows slowly at first. Once you harvest the maize, the cassava takes over the extra space without competing for resources.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya ni eshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ shishijee mli lɛ. Kɛji okpa ŋmãa Cassava baaye he kroko ni okɛ nibii ahe akaŋ akaŋ.

english: How do I know when a sick crop can be treated with chemicals versus when I must cut it down completely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni abaanyɛ akɛ tsofai atsa tso ni hela mɔ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ be esa akɛ mafo mli kwraa?

english: Treatments work for insect bites or fungal spots, but viral diseases cannot be cured with medicine. If a tree has a viral infection like Cocoa Swollen Shoot, cutting it down completely is the only way to stop the disease from spreading to neighboring trees.
ga: Tsofafeemɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ahe. Shi anyɛɛɛ akɛ tsofa atsa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ hela ko tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot lɛ emɔ tso ko lɛ, efolɔ kwraa ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do insect pests keep damaging my tomato farm even after I cleared all the old tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yaa nɔ efiteɔ mi-tomato ŋmɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie tomato tsei momo lɛ fɛɛ moŋ.

english: Pests and disease spores often remain alive in the soil long after the crop is harvested. If you plant tomatoes repeatedly in the same spot, the pests waiting in the soil immediately attack the new plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ beni akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ odu tomato yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni miimɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatutua tsei heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling and pale patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by small insects called whiteflies. The disease damages the leaves' ability to make food, resulting in smaller tubers under the ground.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ he ni etse lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If one cocoa tree shows signs of swollen branches, why do I need to cut down the healthy-looking trees right next to it?
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso ko niji efuu Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo kookoo tso ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ? Koni ekwɛ ehewalɛ hu?

english: Viruses often infect neighboring trees through sap-sucking insects before visible symptoms appear. Removing nearby healthy-looking trees creates a safe boundary that prevents the hidden infection from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ nɔ dani hela lɛ he okadii lɛ jeɔ kpo. Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe baa koni helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does my land yield much less maize now than it did when I started farming it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa faaa kwraa fe beni mibɔi okwaayeli afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous farming over many years depletes the soil's natural nutrients. Soil is like a bank account; if you repeatedly harvest crops without adding plant food back through manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted.
ga: Afii babaoo ni akɛtsu nii be fɛɛ be lɛ eha adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ efo. Shikpɔŋ tamɔ shikatoohe akaunt. Kɛji okpa ŋmɔshi nibii shii abɔ Ni okɛ tsei aniyenii fataaa he ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, they end up fighting for the same food, water, and sunlight in the soil. Giving crops proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kome ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã tsei ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves acts like an umbrella. It stops the hot sun from drying out the ground quickly, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: When heavy rain sits in soil that does not drain easily, water drowns the roots by taking away all the underground air. This trapped wetness allows tiny organisms to attack and rot the cassava roots.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo lɛ nɔ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔ nɛɛ haa bɔɔ nii bibii shwieɔ shi. Ebaanyɛ etutua ni efite cassava shishifãi.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and small roots that burn easily under direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them shields the cocoa from direct sunlight until they grow older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ, ebaabu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the plant. Staking allows the leaves to spread out high off the ground, which helps the plant produce bigger tubers underneath.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔɔŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shishi.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat stress or lack of water. Without enough water and steady temperatures, the plant drops flowers to conserve its remaining energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ bɛ Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft, growing funnel of young maize leaves because it offers food and protection from the heat. Catching them early prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhaa niyenii kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Why are my plantain trees easily falling over in light wind before the fruit matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ dani eyibii lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees often fall because tiny pests underground, such as root nematodes or stem weevils, are eating away the roots. Without strong roots anchored in the ground, the plant cannot support the heavy fruit bundle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ahewɔ. ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem weevils ni yeɔ shishifãi lɛ Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on land where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Crops like maize pull a lot of nutrients out of the earth. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts actually take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally restoring soil fertility for future crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Legumes, tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts, gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my crops growing very green and bushy leaves, but failing to produce good fruits or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji waa lɛ? Shi enyɛŋ ewo yibii loo dumɔwui kpakpai.

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer makes plants put all their energy into leafy growth rather than flower and fruit production. Balanced feeding is necessary for a good harvest.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaawo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai Niyenii ni ja he miihia kɛha ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: Is there a specific time in the farming season when I should apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Ani be ko yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer must be applied at specific growth stages when the soil is moist. Applying it at the wrong season or during dry spells prevents roots from absorbing the nutrients and can waste your money.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni esaaa mli loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni eji shika fitemɔ.

english: Why do my crops look scorched and weak after I apply chemical fertilizer to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni egbɔjɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo mli lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer too close to plant stems, using too much, or applying it to dry soil can burn the root system, reducing the plant's vitality instead of helping it grow.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine Aloo nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua tsei ni amɛdara lɛ

english: Why does chemical fertilizer fail to improve my yield even after I apply a lot of it to my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ aha miŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ewo miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: If the soil has lost its natural vitality and organic matter, or has become too acidic, plants cannot absorb added fertilizers. The soil health must be restored first before fertilizer can work effectively.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fite loo eyɛ acid tsɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfata he lɛ. Esa akɛ aku sɛɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has lost its strength and vitality for crop production?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afeemɔ mli lɛ miiho?

english: Signs of degraded soil vitality include hard and compacted ground, water pooling on the surface, weak crop growth despite good rainfall, and low yields regardless of fertilizer input.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ efite lɛ he ji shikpɔŋ ni wa ni edɔ. Nu buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Tsei adalɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi ni ekɔɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he.

english: What steps can I take to restore life back to soil that no longer produces good crops?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni wala aba shikpɔŋ ni wooo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: To restore exhausted soil, rotate your crops, incorporate well-rotted organic compost, grow cover crops, and allow the land time to recover rather than relying only on chemical inputs.
ga: yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ sɛɛkuu mli Tsakemɔ oŋmɔshi nibii. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ afata he. ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ ni ahaa be ni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ moŋ fe ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why does animal manure give off a strong bad smell when I leave it in heaps on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ashishifãi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa waa kɛ́ mishi yɛ ŋmei mli yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bad smells happen when manure is left wet and unmanaged without enough air, causing it to rot improperly. This process loses valuable plant nutrients into the air.
ga: Nɔ ni ŋmei lɛ baa ji kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni efɔ ni akɛtsuuu nii ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteee jogbaŋŋ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ laajeɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Can using improperly rotted organic matter on my farm harm my crops?
ga: Ani nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Raw or poorly decomposed organic matter can introduce diseases, attract pests, generate high heat that damages crop roots, and temporarily steal nutrients from the soil as it continues to rot.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ŋmɔŋ loo ni efiteee jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ hela aba. Egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Ehaa dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni fiteɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ baa. ni ejuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ be mli ni eyaa nɔ efiteɔ lɛ.

english: How long should I allow plant trash and weeds to decompose before planting on the land?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mahã tsei ahe jwɛi kɛ jwɛi lɛ afite dani madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Organic matter should be cleared and allowed to fully decompose into rich compost weeks before planting so that it enriches the soil rather than decomposing while young crop roots are trying to grow.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛfite ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ otsi kome dani adu. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeefite yɛ be mli ni tso bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miitao ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why is it important to align my crop planting strictly with the start of the rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni ekɛ nugbɔ be ni jeɔ shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ akpã gbee lɛ?

english: Planting at the right seasonal time ensures young crops receive consistent water to establish strong roots early, protecting them from unexpected dry periods later in their growth cycle.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ náa nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa mra. Ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ bei ni akpaaa gbɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ mli.

english: Why do insect pests keep coming back to my crops even after I drive them away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mishwie amɛ moŋ

english: Simply scaring or chasing insects off doesn't destroy them. They temporarily hide in surrounding bushes or neighboring fields and fly back as soon as they feel safe because your crops are their primary food source.
ga: Kɛ́ oootswa ŋmeii lɛ loo oshwie amɛ kɛkɛ lɛ, ekpataaa amɛhiɛ. Amɛyatee amɛhe yɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli be kukuoo ko. loo ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli ni amɛfo kɛku amɛsɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛnu he akɛ amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji amɛ niyenii titri.

english: Where do farm insects usually hide their eggs so that I can find them early?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii fɔɔ amɛwuji lɛ kɛtee koni manyɛ mana amɛ oya?

english: Insects hide their eggs on the undersides of leaves, inside stem tissue, or just beneath the soil to protect them from hot weather and predators. Checking beneath leaves regularly helps you catch infestations before they hatch.
ga: Kplukai kɛ amɛwui teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi. stem tissue loo shikpɔŋ shishi koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona helai ni baa amɛnɔ dani amɛfɔ.

english: Why do small flying insects scatter into the air whenever I walk through my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni foɔ lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɔɔyɔɔ mli be fɛɛ be ni matsɔ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Insects scatter as a natural survival instinct when they sense vibrations or shadows. They fly off to hide on nearby weeds or crop leaves and will return to feeding once the disturbance stops.
ga: Kplukai gbɛɔ amɛshwãa akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo su kɛji amɛnu shikpɔŋhosomɔi loo hulutsoo he. Amɛfoɔ kɛyaa ni amɛyateeɔ amɛhe yɛ jwɛi loo tsei ahe baai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni ebaaku esɛɛ ebaye niyenii ekoŋŋ beni basabasafeemɔ lɛ kpa lɛ.

english: If insect pests fly away to another field, will they come back to lay eggs on my plants later?
ga: Kɛji tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ fã kɛtee he kroko Ani amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba sɛɛ mli koni amɛbawo mitsei lɛ anɔ ŋmeii?

english: Yes, insects often migrate temporarily to mate or feed, but adult females will return to healthy, leafy crops to lay their eggs where the newly hatched young will have plenty of food.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, kooloi fãa kɛyaa he kroko be kukuoo ko koni amɛyafɔ loo amɛyatao niyenii. Shi yei ni eda lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli koni amɛyawo amɛwui. Bibii ni afɔ lɛ ehee lɛ baaná niyenii babaoo.

english: Why do I get more pests on my crop plants when my farm is close to the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be mli ni miŋmɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ jwɛi lɛ?

english: The wild bush acts as a natural breeding ground for insects and wild animals. When wild vegetation dries up or when your farm crops begin to flower, these pests move into your farm searching for fresh food.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli he ni kooloi bibii kɛ koo mli kooloi fɔɔ yɛ. Beni koo mli tsei lɛ egbi loo be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ fãa kɛyaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyatao niyenii hee.

english: How can I stop animals from the nearby bush from coming onto my farm to destroy my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni jɛ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ anaa koni amɛkaba miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛbafite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Creating a cleared buffer zone around your farm edges removes hiding spots for wild animals. Keeping boundaries clean and using basic physical barriers or repellents helps deter them from crossing over.
ga: Buffer zone ni mli ka shi faŋŋ ni ooobɔle Oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baaye abua ni ejie hei ni koo mli kooloi kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. Husui ni aaakwɛ koni ehe atse kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii loo shishijee nibii ni tsiɔ mɔ naa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akafo mli.

english: Why does leaving wild bushes and weeds near my field make insect problems worse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni koo mli jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ haa kooloi bibii ahe naagba lɛ mli waa lɛ?

english: Weeds and wild bushes act as alternative hosts that shelter pests when your main crops are harvested. Clearing these areas starves the insects and prevents them from multiplying between planting seasons.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ koo mli tsei bibii tsuɔ nii akɛ hei krokomɛi ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe beni okpaa onibii titrii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie hei nɛɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi lɛ, ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafɔ bii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Do wild animals and insects from the bush behave differently than regular farm pests?
ga: Ani koo mli kooloi kɛ koo mli kooloi feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Bush animals and wild insects tend to visit crops seasonally based on wild food availability, whereas farm-adapted pests remain directly on your crop fields year-round because cultivated crops offer easy nutrient sources.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koo mli kooloi kɛ koo mli kooloi saraa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kɛ bei amli, ni enɛ damɔ koo mli niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Is pest damage on my farm caused by traditional customs or bad luck, or is there a scientific reason?
ga: Kusum loo shweremɔ gbonyo ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Aloo yiŋtoo ko yɛ ni jɛ jeŋ nilee mli?

english: Pest damage is purely biological. Insects and wild animals are driven by natural biological needs for food, water, and safe egg-laying environments, which respond to weather patterns and crop cycles rather than spiritual customs.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli kɛkɛ. Nɔ ni tsirɛɔ kooloi bibii kɛ koo mli kooloi lɛ ji amɛ adebɔɔ mli hiamɔ nii ni ji niyenii, nu, kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaafee amɛshĩa lɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ ahetoo fe mumɔŋ kusumii.

english: How can I tell if damage on my farm is caused by small insects or by larger wild animals coming from the bush?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii loo koo mli kooloi wuji ni jɛ jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ kɛ nɔ ni efite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ba?

english: Insects leave small holes in leaves, chewed stems, or tiny spots of egg clusters, while larger bush animals leave bigger footprints, snapped crop stalks, or whole eaten fruits and roots.
ga: Kplukai shĩɔ bu bibii yɛ baai amli, tsei ni atsɔ mli, loo ŋmeii bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli, yɛ be mli ni jwɛi wuji lɛ shĩɔ naji wuji, tsei ahe tsei ni ekumɔ, loo aduawai kɛ shishifãi muu ni ayeɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Shade plants protect them from harsh heat and keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Spacing cocoa trees about 3 meters by 3 meters gives each tree enough room to spread its leaves, absorb sunshine, and get root nutrients without competing heavily with neighboring trees.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ feɔ aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3, ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa, ekɛ hulu la, ni enáa niyenii kɛjɛɔ eshishifãi amli ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ waa.

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow directly on the main trunk instead of the tips of branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anaagbee lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce flowers on the thick trunk and older branches so that the heavy mature cocoa pods can be supported securely without breaking thin branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ tsei niji momo anɔ. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua kookoo tsei ni edara kwraa lɛ shweshweeshwe ni efoŋ tsei niji bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are some of my small green cocoa pods turning shriveled and black before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni ji So mine lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani ahoɔ lɛ?

english: This is often cherelle wilt, a natural process where the tree drops extra pods it cannot support, or it can be caused by poor insect pollination and lack of nutrients.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ eji hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ ashwieɔ shi. Aloo ekolɛ kooloi bibii ni bɛ ŋmeii kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: How do tiny insects help my cocoa trees produce pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii yeɔ ebuaa mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Tiny insects called midges carry pollen from flower to flower. Without these insects pollinating the cocoa flowers, the trees cannot produce pods.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi amli muji kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Kɛji nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ni shwieɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmeii.

english: Heavy rainfall creates high humidity, which spreads fungal spores causing Black Pod disease. Keeping the farm clear of weeds and pruning dead branches helps air flow and reduces wetness.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo baa. ni gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ eshwaa. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni afo tsei niji ni egboi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi.

english: What causes tiny dark spots on my cocoa pods and young shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa? Yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmɔji bibii lɛ anɔ

english: These spots are usually caused by capsids (mirids), small pests that suck sap from the plant, weakening the branches and damaging the pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, capsids (mirids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsei niji lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why must I ferment my cocoa beans under banana leaves before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee cocoa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ banana baai ashishi dani amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Fermentation kills the bean's seed germ, changes its color to rich brown, and creates the sweet chocolate flavor required by buyers.
ga: Fɛ̃i gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Tsakemɔ su lɛ kɛya ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni ofee tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to dry my harvested cocoa beans directly on the bare dirt ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaagbi kookoo yibii ni akpa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying beans on the bare ground exposes them to dirt, stones, mold, and animals, which lowers the quality grade and reduces the price you can sell them for.
ga: Beans ni agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ haa amɛnaa dumɔwui ni he tseee, tɛi, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi bibii. Enɛ haa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa jara ni obaanyɛ okɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: A fully ripe cocoa pod changes color completely from green or deep red to a bright yellow or orange color, and makes a hollow sound when tapped.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse nɔ. ni efeɔ gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛji akɛ ata he

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides shade and preserves the soil moisture young trees need.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ Aloo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are usually signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems and removing infected plants early helps keep the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ atsu nii ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela akagbɛ eshwa

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. You can prevent it by frequently picking ripe pods, weeding around the trees, and pruning extra branches to let sunlight and air dry out the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni eshɛko ni ooobua naa lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni ofolɔ tsei lɛ amli babaoo koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark powder inside the whorl?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa mli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed on the soft, inner leaves of young maize. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended treatments or neem extract directly into the center of the plants helps stop them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii amli baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii loo neem mli nu lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa amɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves develop yellow stripes and produce small, thin cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves and poor cob growth usually mean the maize plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Applying compost or the right fertilizer at the correct time gives the plant the nourishment it needs to build big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ ŋmeii tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tsei lɛ amli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomatoes often drop their flowers due to excessive heat, irregular watering, or using too much nitrogen fertilizer. Water your plants consistently and use balanced fertilizers to help the flowers turn into healthy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii Okɛ nu awo tso lɛ mli daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa atsu nii koni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds too close together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving them proper spacing ensures every stalk grows strong and produces full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha tsei lɛ fɛɛ adara ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why is it better to buy fresh certified maize seeds every year instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i ngɔ dumɔwu komɛ kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi.

english: Hybrid maize seeds are bred to give high yields in their first planting, but seeds saved from that harvest lose their vigor and produce much smaller yields. Fresh certified seeds guarantee strong growth and higher harvests.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔ mli. Shi dumɔwui ni ahere amɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔ mli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ maa dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ ŋmaa babaoo nɔ mi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry out and break down the stem during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkuɔ amɛshishifãi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water quickly in hot, dry weather. Spreading dry grass or crop leaves around the base of the plant retains moisture in the soil and protects the roots during dry months.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest so they don't become hard and woody?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, ebɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ tso?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. Leaving cassava in the ground for too long makes the roots fibrous, tough, and lower in starch content.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee fibrous, amɛhe wa ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow and dry out so fast when my farmland is very sandy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛgbiɔ oya nɛkɛ be mli ni he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ ji ŋã waa lɛ?

english: Sandy soil is made of large, coarse grains with big gaps between them. Because of this, rain and soil nutrients drain away rapidly deep into the ground before your crops' roots can drink or absorb them.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmaa wuji ni mli edɔ kɛ gbɛjegbɛi wuji ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ oya kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ loo amɛheɔ amɛ.

english: Is pineapple a good crop for me to grow if my farm soil is sandy?
ga: Ani pineapple ji ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa kɛha mi kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji ŋã?

english: Yes, pineapples are very tough crops that store water in their thick leaves and prefer loose, sandy soil because heavy, wet soil can easily cause their roots to rot.
ga: Hɛɛ, pineapple ji tso ko ni wa ni toɔ nu yɛ ebaai ni mli tse lɛ amli, ni esumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ waa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo oya.

english: Why do pineapples seem to handle hot, dry conditions better than many other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni pineapple nyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Pineapples have a special leaf structure that traps moisture and reduces water loss, allowing them to survive and produce good fruit even in hot weather and dry soil.
ga: Pineapple yɛ baai krɛdɛɛ ko ni mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ hiɔ shi ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi po mli.

english: Why do some crops grow very well on my neighbor's land but refuse to grow on mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shi amɛkwɛɛɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Different crops require different soil types to survive. Some plants need soil that holds a lot of moisture, while crops like pineapples do better in light, dry, sandy soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi koni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ ni baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo he miihia tsei komɛi. Yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ pineapple tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni egbi, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How will putting goat manure on my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ too ŋmei ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Goat manure adds essential nutrients and organic matter to the soil, which feeds the plants and helps sandy ground hold onto water for a longer time.
ga: Too ŋmei kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What can I add to sandy soil so my crops do not suffer from lack of food and water?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he koni niyenii kɛ nu akafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Adding animal manure or decayed plant compost creates a spongy layer in sandy soil that traps water and plant food right where crop roots can reach them.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa ŋmei sũ lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ mli shwieɔ shi koni ekɛmɔ nu kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ hei ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Can I put fresh manure from my animals directly onto my crops right after cleaning the pen?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloo ŋmei hee awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ beni mitsumɔ ŋmei lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: No, fresh manure is too strong and hot, which can burn plant roots. It should be allowed to dry out or decompose for a few weeks before applying it near crops.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔtɔ hee mli wa tsɔ ni edɔ. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi Esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbi loo egbo otsii fioo komɛi dani akɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: How can keeping farm animals like goats help me lower the money I spend on my crop farming?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ tooi akwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔ mli nyɔmɔwoo aba shi?

english: Raising animals gives you a free, steady supply of rich natural fertilizer, reducing the amount of money you need to spend buying chemical fertilizers for your crops.
ga: Koolooi akwɛmɔ haa onine shɛɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ daa ni aheee nɔ ko. Enɛ haa shika ni ehe hiaa ni okɛhe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does rainwater disappear so quickly from the surface of my field after a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ laajeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sandy ground acts like a sieve, allowing water to pass straight down into the deeper subsoil instead of holding it near the top layer where shallow roots can drink.
ga: Ŋshɔ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋã. Kɛtsɔ nu lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, ha nɛ e hi he nɛ e kɛ hiɔwe ɔ he nɛ sisije ɔmɛ tsɔ we ɔ. baanyɛ anu

english: Is it better for me to focus only on growing crops, or should I combine crop farming with raising animals?
ga: Ani ebafeŋ nɔ ni hi akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ baama tsei ni mikwɛɔ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ tsei akwɛmɔ kɛ kooloi akwɛmɔ afata he?

english: Combining crops and animals creates a balanced system where animal waste feeds your crops, crop leftovers feed your animals, and you are protected financially if crop prices drop.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ kooloi ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ haa gbɛjianɔtoo ni ja baa. He ni kooloi ashwiei yeɔ onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ yeɔ okooloi lɛ anɔ. Ni abaabu ohe yɛ shika gbɛfaŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara ba shi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct sunlight and harsh heat. Keeping or planting shade trees like plantains creates a cool umbrella that protects young cocoa roots and leaves from drying out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ loo adumɔ haa shade ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii kɛ baai ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow with tiny holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Holes and yellowing in maize leaves are often caused by pests like fall armyworms feeding on the plant, or a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Catching insects early prevents them from destroying the crop leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ tso lɛ loo nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Koolooi ni amɔmɔ amɛ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes twisting up and changing color to pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsake ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Twisted and pale cassava leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small flies. Planting disease-free or resistant stem cuttings stops this sickness from reducing your harvest.
ga: Yucca baai ni etsake ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Niji ni hela bɛ mli loo ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baatsi hela nɛɛ naa koni ekaha okpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my crops grow lots of tall green leaves but give me very small tubers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi ehaa mi bulbs bibii waa kɛ aduawai lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to put all their energy into leafy growth instead of growing food underground or producing flowers. Crops need balanced nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to form big tubers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa baai lɛ adalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo amɛaawo fɔfɔi lɛ, ehe miihia ni Tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasiɔm ni sa. koni efee yitsei wuji kɛ aduawai

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field make the next maize crop grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize there later, the maize uses that natural plant food to grow tall and healthy.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ jɛmɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa kɛ nakai adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why do I end up with a smaller harvest when I plant my seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and grow large.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni etsɔ agbo.

english: How do weeds make my main crops grow thin and weak?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha mitso titri lɛ afee mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds while your crops are still young ensures your main crops get all the food they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: High heat combined with dry soil stresses tomato plants, causing their flowers to drop before fruit can form. Providing shade and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fataa he lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo. Shade ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry out fresh seeds before they sprout. Waiting until the rains become regular ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be kukuoo ko nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No haa dumɔwui heei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting fast in my barn after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mifo mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are cut or bruised during harvest or stored in warm, airless spaces. Handling tubers gently and storing them on cool, raised, airy racks prevents rot from spreading.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ bulb lɛ tsu nii blɛoo ni okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni awo nɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite.

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from heavy fertilizers or animal manure, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stem above ground instead of feeding the roots where the cassava tubers form.
ga: Beni ŋmãa naa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni tsii loo kooloi ŋmãa mli. Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know when my maize is completely ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa?

english: Maize is ready when the outer husks on the cob dry out completely and turn brown, and a tiny black mark appears at the base of each kernel where it attaches to the cob.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmei lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ ŋmei lɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ egbi kwraa ni etsɔ ŋmei. Ni okadii diji bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the afternoon weather gets too hot or when the soil lacks water. High heat prevents the flowers from pollinating properly, so the plant sheds them to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shwane kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why is it better to leave cleared weeds to rot on my field instead of burning them before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaafite jwɛi ni ajie yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni aaashã dani adu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic nutrients and helpful living organisms in the topsoil. Leaving cut weeds on the field allows them to decay, creating natural food for the soil and keeping moisture in the ground.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni afo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi. Efeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I add dried animal manure to the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts as slow-release food for crops. It improves the soil's ability to hold water and steadily feeds the plants essential nutrients throughout their growth.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni ajieɔ lɛ blɛoo kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: What makes my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: During the dry Harmattan, strong winds and intense heat cause cocoa trees to lose water rapidly. The tree drops its leaves on purpose to reduce water loss and survive until the rainy season comes back.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni naa wa haa cacao tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ yiŋtoo ko hewɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my young maize plants have small rows of holes chewed straight through their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the central leaf shoot. They chew through the rolled leaves inside, which shows up as a row of holes as the leaf grows out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai ni abɔle amɛhe yɛ mli lɛ. Amɛjeɔ kpo tamɔ buji ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ beni baai lɛ daa kɛjeɔ kpo lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the hot afternoon heat even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli edɔ po

english: In the intense hot afternoon sun, leaves lose water to the air faster than the roots can drink it up. The plant temporarily droops to protect itself from drying out and will recover in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi yɛ shwane mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. ni ebaahe ejɔ ehe gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell before the real rainy season starts. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the tender young plants will dry up and die from lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do I get fewer grains when I replant seeds saved from my hybrid maize harvest compared to buying new seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ dumɔwui fioo nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ du ekoŋŋ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ahemɔ he lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two different strong parents to give high yields only in the first generation. Replanted seeds lose that special strength, leading to smaller, uneven plants and lower yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi enyɔ ni he wa lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ bibii, amɛdalɛi kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to build healthy green leaves. This often happens in exhausted soils or after heavy rains wash nutrients away, but adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer can restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaha aná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Shi kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpeas in the same field where my maize is growing?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni aduɔ ŋmãa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas alongside maize is very beneficial because cowpeas naturally take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts as a free fertilizer for your maize while giving you two different crops to harvest from the same plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Ejaakɛ cowpea lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa bo ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni obaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is moist right after a light rain, but not during or right before a heavy downpour. Heavy rains will wash your expensive fertilizer away before the crop roots can drink it in.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli loo dani enɛɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie o-fertilizer ni jara wa lɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ.

english: What is eating ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark droppings inside the leaf funnels?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli buji ni ekumɔ lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that hides deep inside the plant's central leaves. Checking your farm early and spraying safe bio-pesticides or diluted neem seed liquid into the leaf funnels will kill the caterpillars.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ateŋ baai amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem dumɔwui amli nu ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ ni oooshwie baai lɛ amli lɛ baagbe kooloi lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying even when the ground has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that blocks the tubes inside the stem so water cannot reach the leaves. Once present, you should rotate that plot with non-solanaceous crops like maize or cassava for a few seasons to starve the bacteria.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni sũ ni tsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Kɛji atsɔɔ lɛ Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa, atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ bei fioo komɛi amli koni hɔmɔ aye helatsɛmɛi lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays in the soil for too long during heavy rains, effectively suffocating the roots. Planting your cassava stems on raised dirt mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating in the heat. It also blocks sunlight so weed seeds cannot sprout easily.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ edɔ. Etsĩɔ hulu lɛ hu naa. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ mlɛo.

english: Cocoa flowers drop without setting fruit if the air is too hot and dry, if the tree lacks water, or if tiny pollinating insects called midges are missing. Maintaining shade trees around your cocoa keeps the air moist and creates a habitat for these beneficial midges.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Midge lɛ laaje. Tsei akwɛmɔ koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha amɛhe Cocoa haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa cacao tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ feɔ shia.

english: Why do I need to clear small shoots from the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ plantain lɛ shishi?

english: When too many young shoots grow around a single plantain tree, they steal water, nutrients, and sunlight from the main stem. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong succession plants, ensuring your main tree produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa ni baaye esɛɛ lɛ ahi shi. Enɛ haa otso titri lɛ baaná dumɔwui wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Yam vines naturally climb up high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large underground tubers. Keeping the vines off the ground also prevents damp leaves from catching soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛbaa lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Wein tso lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai ni mli efɔ lɛ náaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ.

english: Can I do anything useful with the juicy red or yellow fruit attached to my cashew nuts after harvest, or should I just leave it to rot?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ aduawai tsuru loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ cashew ŋmeii ahe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ maha egbo kɛkɛ?

english: The cashew apple—the fruit attached to the nut—is completely edible and can be processed into fresh juice, wine, jam, or dried snacks instead of being left to waste in the field.
ga: Cashews, ni ji aduawai ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ nut lɛ he lɛ, ayeɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ afee lɛ nu hee, wain, jam loo niyenii ni egbi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ

english: How can I process my excess fresh mangoes so they do not spoil when I cannot sell them quickly at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu mango heei ni fa fe nine lɛ ahe nii koni amɛkafee yaka be mli ni minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ amɛ oya yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: You can preserve extra mangoes by drying sliced fruit in the sun, boiling them into jam, or pressing them into juice, which allows you to store them longer and sell them at better prices.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mango ni fa fe nine lɛ ato kɛtsɔ aduawai ni afo lɛ ni oooha egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ. ahoo amɛ awo jam mli loo ashɛre amɛ awo aduawai amli nu mli Enɛ baaye abua bo ni okɛ amɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ kɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What can I make out of fresh pawpaw if I harvest too many ripe ones at the same time?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛjɛ papai heei amli kɛji mikpa papai ni ekwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ be kome mli?

english: Ripe pawpaw can be turned into bottled fruit juice, fruit leather, or jam, while unripe pawpaw can be processed to extract papain, an enzyme used for tenderizing meat.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsake papaya ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ afee nu ni akɛwoɔ tɔ mli, aduawai ahewolo loo jam, yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ atsu papaya ni ekwɛko lɛ he nii koni ajie papain. ni ji enzyme ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛha loo afee blɛoo

english: Why do my cashew trees drop so many of their flowers without forming any fruit or nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ fɔfɔii babaoo ni ewooo yibii loo ŋmeii ko lɛ?

english: Cashew trees often shed flowers due to dry spells, attacks by sap-sucking insects like thrips, or natural flower thinning where the tree keeps only what it has enough nutrients to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be hewɔ. Kplukai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔi ni egbee shi lɛ tutuamɔ. He ni tso lɛ toɔ fãi ni yɔɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eda lɛ pɛ.

english: Why are my orange trees dropping green fruits long before they are ready to be picked?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ woɔ yibii eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ dani eshɛɔ he lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruit mainly when there is a sudden lack of water in the soil, heavy nutrient deficiency, or damage from fruit flies attacking the skin.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii titri kɛji nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ trukaa. Niyenii ni esaaa kwraa loo nɔ ni jɛɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni tutuaa hewolo lɛ mli baa lɛ efiteɔ.

english: Why does my plantain stem die off after producing just one single bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gboiɔ beni amɛwo ŋmei kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed to flower and produce fruit only once in its life cycle; once harvested, the main stem naturally dies so the underground root bulb can direct energy into fresh young suckers.
ga: Afee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Kɛji akpa Tso titri lɛ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ajie hewalɛ kɛya ŋmeii bibii heei anɔ.

english: Is there any practical use for cassava peels after harvesting and peeling the tubers?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ ko ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii yɛ ŋmei ni ajieɔ lɛ he yɛ ŋmei ni akpa ni ajie ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Dried cassava peels can be ground down to make cheap livestock feed for goats, pigs, and sheep, or buried in the soil to turn into rich organic compost.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsɔ ŋmei ni egbi lɛ nɔ afee kooloi aniyenii ni jara waaa aha tooi, tsinai kɛ tooi, loo afu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ koni afee ŋmei ni fa babaoo.

english: Can I turn leftover maize stalks and husks into something helpful for my soil after harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa tsei kɛ ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ koni ekɛye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Dry stalks and husks can be chopped up to mulch around crop bases to retain soil moisture, or layered with animal manure to create nutrient-dense compost for your next planting season.
ga: Abaanyɛ afolɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei kɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ afee muji ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ nɔ koni efee ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and spoil so quickly during transport to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ fee blɛoo ni egbo oya beni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes soften quickly because they release natural ripening gases and generate heat when stacked tightly in deep baskets without ventilation; using shallow, rigid crates keeps them cool and intact.
ga: Tomatoi feɔ blɛoo oya ejaakɛ ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ shwereɔ lɛ kpo, ni ehaa dɔlɛ baa kɛji akɛ ato tsɛnsii ni mli kwɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ amli. Krɛti ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni wa ni akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni adeka lɛ mli ajɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akafite.

english: How do I plant new pineapple crops using the fruit I just harvested from my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔ aduawai ni mikpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli amrɔ nɛɛ nɔ makwɛ ŋmei tso hee?

english: You can cut off the leafy green crown at the top of the harvested fruit, let it dry for a few days, and plant it directly in the soil to start a new pineapple plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo tso yibii ni akpa lɛ yiteŋ ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ. Ha ni egbi gbii fioo komɛi. No sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni oje ŋmei hee shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants are like small babies that burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that act as living umbrellas, keeping the cocoa shaded and moist during its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ abifabii bibii. ni hulu lɛ shãa oya Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it better to grow my yams on high soil mounds instead of flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds loosen the soil so yam roots can spread and grow into large tubers without hitting hard dirt, while also preventing heavy rains from drowning and rotting the tubers.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni sweet potato shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni shikpɔŋ ni wa akatswa amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or compost will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize removes a lot of nutrients from the dirt, but crops like groundnuts put food back into the soil naturally, making the ground fertile again for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi tsei tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I see small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside my maize stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ

english: Those holes are caused by stem borer caterpillars eating the plant from the inside. Planting early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can protect your crops.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nakai bu lɛ baa ji stem borers ni yeɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli lɛ. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get destroyed by tiny bugs inside storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ kpata ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those bugs are grain weevils, which multiply if maize is bagged while still damp. Thoroughly sun-drying your corn until hard before bagging keeps the insects away.
ga: Nakai kooloi lɛ ji dumɔwui amli ŋmeii. Enɛ baagbɛ eshwa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ wo kotoku mli be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa dani okɛwo kotoku mli koni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, when lower leaves begin turning yellow and falling off, and the soil around the stem base starts cracking open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather gets too hot or when soil completely dries out, because the plant drops flowers to save energy when stressed.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛ́ amɛmiihao.

english: Cutting off extra shoots, called pruning, allows sunlight and air to move through the tree to prevent diseases like black pod and helps the tree direct its energy into producing pods.
ga: Nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ pruning. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Koni akɛtsi helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji anaa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ amaje koni ekɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do farmers cover the ground around plants with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai haa he ni amɛtsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot days, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly turns into natural plant food.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye nɔ ni fiofio lɛ etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ haa.

english: Will planting my maize seeds closer together give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in thin stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth, or that water is sitting around the roots for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading a virus that stunts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Ekɛ tsei amli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɔ helai ni tsiɔ amɛdalɛ naa lɛ eshwaa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the daytime temperatures become too high or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells between waterings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na bei ni mli egbi waa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small caterpillars inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu ni mli egbala kɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, an insect pest that feeds on the soft growing tissues inside maize plants.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ.

english: Root rot happens when heavy rains leave too much water trapped in heavy clay soil, allowing fungal diseases to attack and decay the roots.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu babaoo hi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Ha ni fungal helai atutua ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ afite.

english: Covering the ground with dried organic material, called mulching, blocks direct sunlight, keeps the soil cool and moist, and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I plant maize on the exact same farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season, leading to tired soil and an increase in crop-specific pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ, ni ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu yaa hiɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth so they can grow big and expand smoothly downward. High mounds keep the soil loose, improve water drainage, and make harvesting easier.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛdara ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shishigbɛ mlɛo. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ehaa nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo

english: Why are small worms eating the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They hide deep inside the leaves and destroy the growing point of young maize plants if left untreated.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛfiteɔ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my plantain leaves developing dark spots and turning brown from the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This is likely Black Sigatoka disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy seasons and causes leaves to dry up early, reducing the size of your plantain bunches.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛ ji Black Sigatoka hela, ni ji hela ko ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni ehaa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantain tsei lɛ ayibɔ ba shi.

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It usually happens when tomato roots cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering or dry dry-season soils.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni tomato shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but give me tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves on top instead of storing food in the underground roots.
